## A Bird in the Hand

A Bird in the Hand is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You saved Capon from the gallows.

## Acquisition

Complete the For Whom the Bell Tolls main quest. The achievement is tied directly to the quest's conclusion and therefore cannot be missed during a standard playthrough.

## Tips

- After the fallout from the wedding incident in Semine, Henry and Hans Capon are brought to Trosky Castle's dungeons. Upon arrival, events take a turn when it is revealed that Hans is wanted for poaching, a capital crime against the Crown. With Hans facing execution by hanging, Henry must gather evidence to prove Hans' nobility and secure his release. Successfully completing the quest ensures that Hans avoids execution, thereby unlocking the achievement.

## A Good Scrub

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

A Good Scrub is a side quest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Betty, the owner of the baths in Kuttenberg, asked me to help her get the bankrupt business up and running again.

## Walkthrough

### Retrieve the Package

You will enter a decrepit house that allegedly used to be a bath house. With some luck, it can serve the same function once again. Betty asks you to go to Grund to check on a package that should have arrived awhile ago. Arriving at the town's alehouse, you'll see three girls. The wagoner, who was supposed to deliver the "package", is nearby - usually leaning on the wall next to the gate to the alehouse itself. After some back and forth, you'll eventually convince both parties to go to Kuttenberg. Although it's possible to travel independently, it is strongly recommended by the game itself you take the wagon with them.

### Announce the Bathhouse

Back in Kuttenberg, Betty needs you to announce the opening of the bathhouse, now officially called The Kingfisher, to the masses. You'll design the announcement together with Betty, the choices have no real effect beyond exactly what Henry says. As long as you make sure to do the announcement during the day, you'll have no issues.

The quest indicates four spots for you to announce the opening: at each of them, a quick talk action will pop up for you to start shouting the prepared announcement. In a random location out of these four, you'll be confronted by a disgruntled gentleman, who is of the opinion that bathhouses are infested with sin. Subdue the man with your fists or with a smart argument, either way is okay.

### Party at The Kingfisher

Tell Betty that everything is ready. You should probably prepare a Hair o' the Dog potion if you dislike your Henry having a hangover. If you did everything right, you'll get one of the funnier cutscenes in game.

The next morning, you're woken up by one of the bath maids. A city councillor came by for a surprise inspection, and Betty is delaying him. Your job is to clean up the mess from the past night. Gather the tankards and dirty clothes from the floor - none is hidden away too much, but some items are in the bath area and some are in the main area with tables. Clean up your own vomit next to one of the baths. Carry the unconscious guests to the floor above you and the first room on the right. Then put on some decent clothing.

When you finish the cleanup, the city official will check the premises and sign off on their impeccable condition. Talk with Betty to finish the quest.

If you are unable to clean everything up in time, the alderman will recommend the bathhouse be closed and Betty will bid you farewell, locking you out of the subsequent quest with her.

## A Knight's Word

A Knight's Word is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You rewarded the herbwoman for her help as promised.

## Acquisition

To unlock this achievement, you must return to Bozhena, the herbwoman who helped you during the prologue, and repay the 150 Groschen debt you owe her. She can be found at her hut west of Zhelejov.

## Tips

- The act itself is simple: paying back what you owe. However, some may choose a less honorable approach. One method is to create a manual save before approaching her, pay the debt to unlock the achievement, then reload the save to recover the money. This allows you to keep your funds but is not very knightly.

- If you are short on money, note that Hans Capon gives you 150 Groschen at the start of the Back in the Saddle main quest, just before departing for Nebakov. You can use this to settle your debt with Bozhena.

## A Moment of Fame

A Moment of Fame is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Walkthrough

After completing Fight Dirty, Thomlin will tell you that Tobias was looking for you. Talk to him and he’ll ask you to throw a fight so the others will think he is stronger than he is and stop pushing him around.

You can help him by doing so, or offer to train him in unarmed. Whichever you choose will end the quest.

If you offer to train him he’ll become a trainer in turn. Tobias can skill teach at a journeyman level for the horsemanship and houndmaster skills.

## A Pleasant Pastime

A Pleasant Pastime is a task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It introduces the repeating task of archery contests, Kuttenberg Sharpshooters.

## Description

I've got a visit lined up with another Guildmaster, this time Master Gottfried aus Steyr. I hope it'll be a thoroughly pleasant meeting.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Gottfried, who will tell you to talk to his apprentice Bruno out back. He'll take you out of town to a range in an abandoned quarry ran by Carpenter Raven, where you'll enter into an archery wager.

Once there, you'll be approached by a rival, Matthew Hock, who claims ownership of the shooting range. The butchers' guild wants to lease the place permanently. You suggest a bet for use of the space.

Win or lose, use of the space will be allowed.

## A Sketchy Situation

A Sketchy Situation is the 1st quest in the Brushes with Death DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Completing this quest will unlock Shield painting.

## Description

I encountered an older fellow tied to a tree at the edge of the forest, where he was being threatened by wolves. I decided to help him since I wanted to find out how he ended up in such an unfortunate situation.

## Synopsis

Henry comes across a strange man tied to a pole in the forest southwest of Trosky Castle. The man is talking to a painted skull that sits in the ruined campsite in front of him. He greets Henry awkwardly as Henry approaches, saying he wasn’t really doing anything before someone decided to tie him to a tree.

As Henry approaches, a small pack of wolves descend. Once they have been dealt with, Henry sets the stranger free and they are introduced to each other. The man, Voyta, is an artist in the employ of von Bergow. When asked why it seemed he was talking to a skull, he says he likes to talk to it to sort out his thoughts as he sees it as better than talking to himself.

He explains that during a walk in Slatego, he was nearly hit by an arrow from an archery range that had unknowingly been set up right by the road. As an apology, the two who had set up the range invited him over to drink and play some dice. Voyta noticed one of them was cheating and was hit over the head in the ensuing altercation after which he woke up tied to the tree where Henry found him. Voyta also lost a couple of things that are important to him, his brushes and some dice. He asks Henry to go and retrieve them for him, preferably without bloodshed.

The vagrants, one Yura Hawk-eye and Four-leaf Clovis, are camped nearby and greet Henry warmly. He may talk to them and discover they have a different story for how their interaction with Voyta went. Essentially, per Yura, everything matches up until it comes to their sitting in camp together. Yura says that Voyta started acting strangely, even saying that the skull told him he looked like a captain from Kolin who sired a lot of bastards. To top it off, that man’s brother is apparently hunting those bastards down and killing them to secure his inheritance, something that seemed too eerie. When Clovis saw how shaken he was, he hit Voyta over the head and Henry already knows the rest. Henry may then get back the items through peace or force before heading off to return them to their original owner.

Voyta admits he may have omitted certain parts of the story, but is grateful Henry was able to recover his belongings. He gives Henry his dice and offers to paint something on his shield for him.

## Walkthrough

Head to the purple quest marker southwest of Trosky Castle to start the quest. After a cutscene, kill the wolves and then untie Voyta and talk to him. He will give you the rundown of how this mess started, eventually asking you to retrieve his brushes and dice from the men who robbed him, preferably peacefully.

The men who took Voyta’s things are nearby and they will greet you warmly. They are called Yura Hawk-eye and Clovis. Talking to Yura and passing a skill check (easy speech, medium intimidation, or medium might) will open up the opportunity to hear his side of the story.

You can deal with them in a few different ways.

- Win the items back

- Steal the items

- Lie to recover the brushes

- Kill the men and loot the items

Winning the items back may be the most costly as both will ask for wagers for their games, but it is doable. Play dice with Clovis and beat Yura in a popinjay shooting contest and they will wager the items you need. Clovis will take some convincing before he admits he knows the painter, requiring you to pass an easy coercion check or a medium unarmed check. Then, to play for them, you’ll have to pass an easy speech check or a medium intimidation check.

To steal the items you will have to pickpocket the men. You can either count on your stealth or else come back later during the night when they will be asleep.

If you lie to Yura, passing a medium coercion check and then a hard intimidation check, that Voyta was torn apart by wolves, he will hand over the brushes.

If all else fails, you can attack the duo and take the items off their bodies.

However you recover the items, once you have them, head to Trosky Castle to return them to Voyta. He can be found near the top of the Crone past the scribe’s room. He will thank you, unlocking shield painting and giving you his painted dice.

An abandoned barn sits in a field south of Wysoka. What remains is little more than the skeleton of the building, with a broken cart outside. Inside, a straw mattress has been set up and some supplies for thieving are hidden.

## Abandoned beehives

Abandoned beehives is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

This is a hidden loot cache found on the eastern outskirts of Tachov. The trail begins at a lone beehive standing near the tree line, easily spotted from the eastern road leading into Tachov. From there, head into the woods and follow the scattered beehives, you'll be guided deeper into the forest.

Eventually, the trail splits at a fork. To the right, you'll find a broken blacksmith's cart with a bag of materials and some repair kits left behind. To the left lies a sunny clearing with a single beehive that still holds a bit of honey, and an easy-locked chest. Inside the chest is the Survival skill book, Woodsman's Journal II.

## Loot

Inside the chest:

- Leather gloves

- Burgher's shoes

- Chamomile decoction × 2

- Strong Aqua Vitalis

- Woodsman's Journal II

- Groschen × 13

In the beehive:

- Honey × 10

Inside the bag:

- Cobweb

- Fastening material × 5

- Armourer's kit × 3

- Bag of nails

On top of the cart:

- Blacksmith's kit

## Abandoned building

Abandoned building is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. There is also a point of interest by the same name in the Kuttenberg region.

## Trosky

### Description

An initially unassuming abandoned homestead, overgrown with no immediate signs of anything disastrous having befallen it. In the yard are two wild dogs and inside nothing save for a broken jar with a long-forgotten key and an old loaded die.

The key unlocks a chest in the loft, accessible only through a ladder left on the roadside facing wall, since the inside access has rotted away. The contents of the chest suggest that a thief once lived there.

### Description

A long-abandoned camp in the woods of Apollonia. Bone fragments are scattered about. Behind the camp is an overground dugout, inaccessible now, on the other side is a rotted cabin. The area was used at some point as a paddock for keeping horses.

## Abandoned forge

Abandoned forge is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

When Mezholes was burnt, this forge at the edge of the village was left relatively unscathed. The main house and barn have fallen into great disrepair, perhaps showing that the forge had been abandoned long before the village was sacked. Its walls are still strong, however, and the forge itself functional.

A small mercenary band has made camp in the walls, content to sleep in the one room still shelter from the elements and play dice. The band used to be employed by the people of the town and have chosen to stick around despite their former employers being killed or scattered.

## Amenities

- Sharpening wheel

- Dice table

## Residents

- Frentslin Klik

- Joachim

- Beuschel

## Abbot Jan III

Abbot Jan III is a minor character in the game Kingdom Come: Deliverance II and a major character in its DLC Mysteria Ecclesiae.

He was the abbot of the Sedletz Monastery. As abbot of the oldest Cistercian abbey in Bohemia, he was very invested in matters of the country, participating in political disputes and trying to re-establish Sedletz as one of the seats of power. His methods were not universally welcomed by the monks, some of whom viewed his actions as being at odds with the religious vocation.

## Abbot's chambers

Abbot's chambers is a point of interest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

The chambers of Abbot Jan III. Opulent by monastery standards, the room has its own fireplace and desk as well as the nicely carved wooden bed frame. Adjoining the room is a more plain workspace where the abbot keeps his books.

Abbot's chapel is a point of interest in Sedletz Monastery in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The abbot’s own chapel where he prays when in solitude. The painting above the altar depicts the Archangel Michael weighing the souls of the dead and casting those found wanting into Hell. The room is otherwise austere and devoid of decoration or furniture.

## Absolver

Absolver is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

Sigismund’s soldiers are not exactly loving each other. One of them, Thomas of Kolin, would like to discreetly get his hands on a sword belonging to a Cuman called Basan, and I’m supposed to help him.

## Walkthrough

Speak to Thomas of Kolin at Sigismund's camp to start the quest. He will request that you steal a sword from a Cuman called Basan, craft a replica, and give him the original while giving the replica to Basan.

Basan’s tent is white with gold trim and can be found on the east side of the camp behind the tournament combat area. Sneak in and steal the sword from his chest. This can be done day or night depending on his schedule and your stealth and lockpicking skill. If you choose to inform Basan of Thomas's plan, he will seek out and atack Thomas. If Thomas wins the duel and kills Basan, the quest continues as normal.

Once you have the sword, it’s time to craft the replica. If you do not have the necessary materials, you will be able to buy them from the smiths at the camp.

To craft the replica you will need:

Main article: Replica of the longsword "Absolver"

- Deer skin × 1

- Eight-sided sword pommel × 1

- Frankfurt steel × 2

- Horned sword guard × 1

- Iron × 2

With both the original and replica in-hand, you can choose what to do with them. If the replica is at least gold quality you can give either to Thomas and satisfy him. Whichever you choose, give one to Thomas and place the other back in the chest in Basan’s tent to end the quest.

## Ada von Lippe

Ada von Lippe is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. She can be randomly encountered at Camp by the road locations alongside two stablemasters and a hired hand.

## Biography

A shrewd businesswoman, Ada von Lippe specializes in the trading of horses and is willing to overlook... well, "anything" as she puts it. When questioned about her past, von Lippe will reveal little. Asking her if she also sells horses to Sigismund's army, however, will provide more context to her current situation. Having lost two husbands to the war, she cares nothing for kings or titles and places her faith only in coin. Once a noblewoman herself, it is her belief that one day both Sigismund and Wenceslas will be brought to task for their actions by the people and, most importantly, the traders whose business they've affected.

## Adder

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Adder is a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Leszek, better known as "Adder," was a Polish mercenary and member of Dry Devil's band. Very little of his background was known. He only ever spoke in Polish which made him difficult to understand for most people, though his close friend Janosh understood enough to translate for him. His statements implied he could understand Czech just fine and simply refused to speak it. He was renowned for his strength and ferocity in battle as well as his lechery, the latter of which often got him into trouble, especially with married women.

After the Devil's Pack broke up, Adder eventually ended up on his own in Pschitoky, where he was accused of sleeping with the local butcher's wife, Eva. As a result, the locals attempted to lynch him, but he was saved by Henry, who had been seeking out the former members of Dry Devil's band.

Adder happily rejoined his old pals, and took part in their work in the region, including the attack on Maleshov. Later, Adder went with the group to intimidate a visiting legate, who subsequently ran off in fear. Adder caught up to him and, in a fit of anger, headbutted him to the ground. Unfortunately, the legate hit his head on a rock and died.

Following the infiltration of the Italian Court, Adder was stabbed with a dagger by Vauquelin Brabant at Ruthard Palace revealing Brabant's treachery. As he laid dying, he told his comrades to leave without him, and they complied.

## Associated quests

- The Devil's Pack

- Dancing with the Devil

- Oratores

- The Italian Job

## Adept

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Adept is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It's the first quest in the Legacy of the Forge DLC.

## Description

In Kuttenberg, I found a ruined forge, which is historically connected to my father, Martin. I’ll try to take charge of it.

## Walkthrough

You can pick this quest up by travelling to the ruined forge building in the Hoprink district of Kuttenberg, right next to The Hole in the Wall tavern. After following the quest prompt, Henry will talk to a woman named Magdalena the next day and agree to try to restore the forge.

She'll tell Henry to go meet with Master Bushek in order to prove himself to the Blacksmiths' Guild. Bushek will tell Henry he needs to pass a trial to join the Guild, and offers a guide book for Henry to study before the exam (no need to buy this if you're familiar with the blacksmithing mini-game).

### The trial

To pass the trial, you can make only one mistake be it missing one verbal question or forging a silver quality blade. Ideally, to pass with flying colours, you should get all 3 verbal questions correct and forge a sword of gold quality or better.

If you fail, it will cost 200 to retake, but you can do so as many times as needed.

The correct answers to the verbal questions (which are asked in random order) are:

- Are sparks good or bad? - That depends

- What is the final step before finishing? - Quenching

- How can you tell your progress while smithing? - The shape

- What colour shows the metal is at the right temperature? - Straw yellow

- What is the purpose of whistling while forging? - Steady rhythm

### Repair the forge

To unlock the forge street entrance, just run up to it and follow the prompt. This will reveal a spade you can grab that you'll need to clear the rubble away. After entering through the main door, on the table immediately to your left are the keys to the upper floor that you'll need later (if you don't want to pick the Hard lock). From here you can also unlock the gate to the yard.

To access the upper floor, simply run up the stairs in the yard and use the keys you found on the table on the first floor (or pick the Hard lock) to get inside. You'll then need a spade to clear the rubble and take the sacks outside. All the rubble and items you need to clear on the upper floor are in the southern room (the one with the workbench and ladder in it). Once you sweep the floor after clearing all the rubble and items, you'll unlock an owned bed in the same room.

After clearing all the floors, Magdalena will show you the forge management area where you can purchase upgrades and renovations. Buy and equip the shop sign (under House management), then talk to Magdalena again. She'll tell you she needs an old axe of hers repaired, the quest will complete, and you'll automatically begin the next quest Magdalena's Axe.

## Agnes Thrush

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Agnes Thrush is the daughter of Bailiff Thrush and younger sister to Svatya Thrush in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Her upcoming wedding plays a vital role in the first part of the storyline.

## Biography

While she's engaged to the local lord's son, Olda of Semine, she's aware this was only arranged because despite being of nobility, the Semines don't have a lot of money, while Agnes' father does. Despite this, she tries to make the best of the situation with getting to know Olda. However, Olda tends to disappear a lot at night, sometimes for days, without telling Agnes anything about what he's up to.

Agnes thought he'd stop going out as often after they got married, but no sooner had they said their vows, he disappeared once more, upsetting her. When Henry came to comfort her, one of the wedding guests believed he was trying to seduce her and started a fight which turned into a large brawl.

Following the wedding, if von Bergow was informed of her new husband's suspicious activity, she may have been killed along with the other residents of Semine.

## Albich of Uniczow

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Albich of Uniczow (Czech: Albík z Uničova) is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II and a major character in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC.

## Biography

### Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Albich is mentioned during the quest Ars Dimicatoria. After Arne the German suffers injuries during the tournament, he is brought to the Kuttenberg apothecary where Oswald Torwart and Albich tend to his wounds (off screen).

In the main storyline, he appears in the Italian Job quest as one of the participants of the council which Godwin infiltrates posing as the cardinal.

### Mysteria Ecclesiae

Henry receives a task from Peter of Pisek to contact Albich and accompany him to the Sedletz Monastery, where Albich hopes to secure an audience with Abbott Jan III. After finding him tending to a sick woman in one of Kuttenberg townhouses and helping him deal with the thugs harrassing him, Albich agrees to take Henry with him to Sedletz as a bodyguard ('The Royal Physician').

Upon arriving at Sedletz, Albich and Henry learn about a mysterious disease which three people have been infected. Albich immediately sets about tending to the sick; the physician can be found in the monastery infirmary, where he cares for patients. Albich and Henry discover that a mysterious illness is spreading through the monastery. It eventually comes to light that the source of the contamination and a political conspiracy are directly linked to the hostile alchemist Zacharias and secrets hidden within the monastery crypts.

Albich is the reason Henry infiltrates the monastery. As a physician connected to the royal court, he possesses knowledge regarding King Wenceslaus's health. A conspiracy centers on Albich and the monastery's secrets, involving figures such as Abbot Jan III and the alchemist Zacharias, who is at odds with them.

Henry finds Albich lying motionless on the floor of one of the chambers the physician has been poisoned by conspirators. To salvage the situation and carry out Albich’s mission, Henry must steal the genuine medical notes regarding King Wenceslaus IV’s health from the abbot’s chapel.

Albich’s role concludes in the expansion’s final quest. Henry finds him lying motionless on the floor of one of the chambers. Henry’s first objective is to pick Albich up and carry him to the bed, which triggers the final sequence of events: obtaining the king’s medical records, securing the relic, and the climactic duel with Zacharias in the courtyard.

- If Henry convinces Zacharias the records are legitimate

If Henry managed to convince Zacharias that the records are legitimate, he was able to get the antidote from Zacharias following their duel. With its help, Albich made full recovery and then could continue healing the sick. The monastery eventually returned to its normal life and Albich was able to get the recommendation letter from Abbot Jan which would allow him to visit King Wenceslas in his prison.

- If Henry fails to convince Zacharias the records are legitimate

If Henry failed to convince Zacharias that the records are legitimate, Zacharias got angry and destroyed the antidote before the duel. Without it, Albich remained bedridden for a long time and lost his eyesight. He was unable to help prevent the spread of the illness. At the end of the game, Abbot Jan told Henry that the cloister could be dissolved with so many brothers dead and without pilgrims coming in.

### Associated Quests

- The Italian Job

- The Royal Physician

- Anamnesis

- Seek and You Shall Find

- The Time Has Come

## All Fun and Games

All Fun and Games is a hidden achievement introduced in Brushes with Death.

## Description

Hopefully now Stihlau understand there are some things you shouldn't joke about.

## Acquisition

This achievement is unlocked during the Unveiling quest. To obtain it, you must rescue Apprentice Chrudosh from the thieves' gang and return to Journeyman Stihlau afterwards.

## Tips

- You can save Chrudosh using two methods:

- Confront the bandits during the day if you are confident in your combat abilities.

- Alternatively, wait until night and kill the bandits while they sleep.

- Untie Chrudosh and exhaust all dialogue options before telling him to run. For the achievement to unlock, it is essential to hear him mention the girl he fancies and Stihlau - otherwise, Stihlau will not have the relevant dialogue later.

- Return to Kuttenberg and speak with Stihlau, who is usually found at the same work yard as Carpenter Planck. After the conversation, the achievement should unlock.

## All's fair…

All's fair... is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. Speak with Pavel in Wysoka to start the quest. He works for the local cobblers, and sleeps in the small barn behind their home.

## Description

To have a chance with his beloved, Pavel needs help with a local farmer’s son. I offered to help ruin the fellow’s reputation

## Walkthrough

Hired Hand Pavel is in love with Ursula, who will soon marry the respected son of a prominent farmer. He seeks to improve his chances by plotting to frame his rival for theft. Pavel asks Henry to steal personal items from around town so he can plant them on the farmer's property.

### St. Francis medal

Found in a Magpie's nest in the large tree in Bohushka's yard. Knock it down using a ranged weapon or by throwing rocks.

### Father Anthony’s book

Found in the rectory next to Father Anthony's bed. Easiest to sneak in while he is sleeping and take it, does not require lockpicking.

### Ursula’s ma’s rosary

Can be pickpocketed form her during the day.

Found in a hard locked chest in her room at night. The key to it can be pickpocketed from her while she sleeps.

### Bohushka’s ring

Sneak into the old woman’s house while she sleeps and you’ll hear her talk in her sleep about having lost her ring. To find it, steal Poppy seed kalach in her house and eat it; Henry will find the ring with his teeth.

You can talk to her during the day and agree that you're her husband. Doing so you'll get free access to the house and taking bakery won't be considered stealing.

### Vejmola’s new shoes

In the Vejmola house, the new boots can be found in the corner behind the door to the bed room. They may be hard to see at night.

### Return the items

Go back to Pavel and he’ll act a little shady. Press him, and he’ll reveal he actually wants to sell the items so he can make it to Kuttenberg, as he really stands no chance with Ursula regardless. At this point, you can choose whether to give the items to him, refuse to give the items and sell them yourself, or else give him enough money to make it to town and return the items.

- Giving him the items will prompt the task Seeking Justice later.

- To return the items, head to Father Anthony in the morning. He will thank you for returning the “lost” goods and you’ll gain reputation and scholarship experience.

### Objectives

## Alms

Alms is a repeatable task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

Head toward the orange shield, where someone in Kuttenberg will be collecting alms. Simply speak to them to hear what they are fundraising for and then interact with the chest nearby to donate. Each donation will cost at least 1000 , and you will earn blacksmith prestige and reputation.

One unique instance of the task, which will only appear if you've completed the side quest The Mouth of Hell, involves donating 2000 to Father Marian in Old Kutna to restore the local church bell. If you then wait at least three in-game days, return to the area around noon, and wait for the bell to ring, you can activate the on-screen prompt "Look at the bell" to unlock the achievement Voice of the Bell.

After the first iteration of this task, the similar repeatable task Herald of Kuttenberg will also become available.

## Ambrose (hermit)

Ambrose, originally known as Adam and later as simply "the hermit", was a hermit that lived in Apollonia in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Adam grew up around Troskowitz with his brother, Jan, over 30 years ago. However, Jan had unrequited love for a childhood friend, Margaret, to the point that when she married one of Jan's friends, Vashek, Jan didn't handle the rejection well. Adam likely knew of this to a degree, as when Jan's body was found at the base of a cliff, having looked like he committed suicide by jumping off of it, only Adam suspected something else happened and that Margaret and Vashek were hiding it. As such, his brother's body was buried outside of hallowed ground, as those who died by suicide weren't allowed to enter heaven.

However, instead of seeking out any form of revenge, Adam instead left for Prague and renamed himself Ambrose, where he joined the Knights of the Cross with the Red Star. There, he made friends with Konrad and appeared to strive for a very pious life, giving others the sense he was likely trying to find some kind of peace from the life he left behind. He did well and rose so far in the ranks, he was named seneschal, making him just second in rank under the Grand Master. Unfortunately, his principles to live a life without corruption eventually put him into conflict with unscrupulous members and the Inquisition when he discovered the Grand Master had committed treachery, so he disappeared. He headed back home and setup a secluded place in Apollonia, only telling Konrad where he went.

There in Apollonia, he only went by "the hermit" and was known to help people in the area who sought him out. By the time he was one foot in the grave, his old friend Konrad came to see him regarding a dire matter with their corrupt grand master. However, by the time Konrad got there, Ambrose wasn't even able to comprehend his friend was there. In Ambrose's last moments though, he suddenly spoke clearly that he had two final wishes: to tell Margaret he forgave her, but his brother needed to get what was rightfully his, and to retrieve his old sword from where he buried it so he could hold it one last time. However, while Konrad was out retrieving the sword, Ambrose passed away.

## An Old Friend

An Old Friend is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You found Pebbles.

## Acquisition

This achievement is awarded for reclaiming Pebbles, Henry's old horse from the first game who has been stolen during the bandit's ambush. The achievement is tied to the main quest Wedding Crashers, which begins after completing the prologue.

## Tips

- Wedding Crashers is the major quest following the prologue, and it tasks you with finding a way to get to the wedding taking place in Semine. You can progress the quest by choosing one of two approaches: assisting Miller Kreyzl, located southwest of Semine or assisting Blacksmith Radovan in Tachov, north of Troskowitz.

- If you choose to help Radovan, you will be sent south to Semine to locate his missing cart. During this investigation, you will naturally come across Pebbles as part of the questline. This route includes an introduction to Captain Gnarly, who offers to assist with the search.

- Before you can proceed further, you will need a horse. Speak to Groom Ballatay, who can be found near the southwest wall of the stables in Semine. Ballatay offers a grey, older horse listed as a "Cheap horse" during dialogue. This horse is revealed to be Pebbles. You can either persuade Ballatay to give you the horse (the "Be reasonable" option), or purchase Pebbles outright for 160 Groschen.

- If you instead assist Miller Kreyzl, the quest will progress differently, and you will need to find Groom Ballatay on your own to trigger the event.

- Regardless of how you reclaim Pebbles, doing so will unlock the achievement.

## Anamnesis

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Anamnesis is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 2nd quest in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC and the first taking place in the monastery.

## Description

I accompanied Albich of Uniczow to Sedletz Monastery.

## Walkthrough

A plague has come to Sedletz Monastery. Follow Albich and he’ll talk a bit while you walk over to the infirmary. You’ll inspect the ill, pass a hard scholarship check to help with the confessor and Zacharias of Prachatitz, physician to King Sigismund will interrupt.

He is certain there is nothing to worry about with the so-called plague that has the abbot in a tizzy. He introduces Denes Latzkfi, his aide. All three sick folk have the same symptoms, issues of fever and rash leading to bloody diarrhea.

Albich wants you to look into what the patients were doing before they fell ill, to find the source of the miasma that infected them. The confessor is currently the only patient well enough to converse, the others will require acquaintances.

Note: At this point, to get the quest Maddening Pain, you should leave the infirmary immediately. You'll find two people arguing, Maddie and Novice Benedict, talk to Maddie to start the quest. Once their conversation is over she will leave and the quest will become unavailable.

If you’d like a tour, you can find Monk Petromil in the garden, ask him and he’ll show you around.

Stephen, the confessor, is in the infirmary. Speak to him, pass a very hard scholarship check and he’ll understand what you want to know; however, he cannot break the seal of confession. Medium coercion or very hard speech check will get him to give you some information. He will ask for some flowers, as he doesn't want to smell sickness, any 5 will do. He’ll direct you to his cell. In his cell, you’ll also find a decent amount of jewellery and flowers, which you'll find suspicious.

You’ll find Zdenyek outside in the work area, ask him about Blazhena and he’ll tell you he suspects she’s been stealing as food has been disappearing from the pantry. He’ll direct you to her room across from the church, upstairs by the window. Her roommate is called Valerie and she is nearby.

Valerie is offended Zdenyek would lie as she saw him take something from Blazhena’s chest though she doesn’t know what. After taking it, he went down into the cellar. His room is downstairs in the kitchen. Valerie confirms that Blazhena was talking to a monk.

In Blazhena’s room, you’ll find 300 groschen in her chest. In the cellar you’ll find a large amount of water and large amounts of wine poured into tub – Zdenyek is watering down the monastery wine. Confront him and he’ll ask you to talk in private. Getting him to talk in public will require a coercion check. Blazhena caught him in the act and he stole a key from her chest for the monastery cellar which he will offer as payment to keep quiet about the wine.

He’ll beg you not to tell the abbot and you have to choice to report him or not. Keeping him around will allow you to buy lockpicks from him.

The librarian, Crispin, can be found in the library. Talk to him and he will tell you Jaroslav was translating the Decameron and was focused solely on that work with his other duties being given to other brothers. As for who might know him best, Crispin suggests Brother Celestine. Check the book he was translating to find not much progress was made.

In Jaroslav’s cell, you’ll find in his medium locked chest a map - Old cellar plans.

Celestine is usually praying, ask him about Jaroslav and he’ll reiterate what the librarian said. When confronted with how unfinished his work was, Celestine will admit that Jaroslav has been sneaking out at night down into the cellars and may have been meeting with a woman.

Down in the monastery cellars, you’ll find a wine stain that will lead to a locked door. With the key from Zdenyek you can get in. Inside will be a monk called Vojtiech, talk to him and he’ll let you know he’s been writing a book with Jaroslav and Blazhena. While talking to him, you can get him to tell jokes. Listen to all of his jokes to unlock the achievement Survivor. Jaroslav became worried the Decameron would be destroyed, so he hid his translation down in the cellar and decided to write a book inspired by it.

Another monk, Brother Ernest, was involved as well. He is an older brother in charge of building and repairs around the monastery. The room is damp, but not the source of the miasma. Go to check on Ernest to find him deceased in his cell. You’ll find some building plans on his table. Inspect his body and determine he died from the same illness, most likely the first to catch it.

With all the information you can gather right now, head back to the infirmary to update Albich on what you’ve learnt. Pass a hard speech check to lie about the secret scriptorium when talking to the Abbot. After conversation with the Abbot, the monastery will be quarantined, ending the quest.

## Anna of Waldstein

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Anna of Waldstein is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Anna was friends with Rosa Ruthard, the two having grown up together. They were described as being quite close, almost inseparable.

Anna was married to Wenzel Bartosh, after he died, she took over his estates, including Pschitoky, and his family believed she had something to do with his death. Others, like Kunzlin Ruthard, believe she truly loved her husband and would not have done such a thing.

She was a shrewd and business-minded woman, well-connected and smart in matters of politicking. She agreed, with some help from Father Godwin, to support Jobst's plan to raise an army to stand against Sigismind and was killed in the attack on Raborsch.

### Associated quests

- The King's Gambit

- The Feast

- Stained Honour (mentioned)

## Apollonia

Apollonia (Czech: Apolena) is a forest area east of Troskowitz, that consists of an intricate network of sandstone rock formations, with winding paths and underlying caves hiding beneath.

The area itself isn't home to any settlements. Instead, it's a rocky terrain with many nooks and crannies, making it an ideal place people go to to hide from others.

## Codex entry

A local legend says that Apollonia was the daughter of a wealthy landowner who fell in love with a poor boy. Her father was against it, so he arranged for her beloved to be conscripted into the army for seven years, where he lost his life. When Apollonia learned of this, she went mad with grief and left for parts unknown. Her mother later found her, sick and emaciated in a cave in a rock town, which the girl now called home. The girl refused to come home and died in her arms.

This is not a 'town' in the true sense of the word, but a complex system of sandstone rock formations near the Trosky castle and the village of Troskowitz. Many paths wind through the rocks with caves underneath them that historically provided refuge for outcasts and exiles, as well as villagers seeking shelter from approaching armies.

Due to severe erosion of the weathered sandstone, public access has been completely restricted and the site has become a protected nature reserve. Visitors can, however, visit other very similar rock towns that are peppered throughout the so called Bohemian Paradise.

## Apothecary Emmerich

Apothecary Emmerich (Czech: Lékárník Emerich) owns the only proper apothecary shop in the Trosky region.

He lives in Troskowitz with his wife, Gerda, and their two sons, Heinrich and Vuytek.

## Biography

### Early life

Emmerich and his family moved to Troskowitz from the city (presumably Kuttenberg) after Gerda inherited a house from her relatives. Although Emmerich initially planned to sell the property, he came to terms with village life, partly for his wife's sake, as she never fully got used to living in the city.

As the only established apothecary in the region, Emmerich is known to overcharge for his services. As a result, many locals seek treatment from herbalists instead, whom he dismisses as charlatans.

Despite never attending medical school, Emmerich considers himself a properly educated man. He shares an interest in books with Tailor Bartoshek and, together with Scribe Gaibl, frequently studies Latin texts. According to Merchant Jurg Thömel, however, of the three, only Gaibl knows the language.

### Involvement

During Henry's stay in the region, Emmerich and his wife attend the Semine wedding, where he can be seen dancing with her. He jokingly remarks that Gerda, being considerably younger, might be the death of him, yet he continues to indulge her. They enjoy the festivities and joke together about their son Vuytek's bad luck with womenfolk.

He also takes part in the gambling tournament organized by Bailiff Thrush. When Henry approaches him to challenge him to a game of dice, Emmerich says that he has lost his badge. In truth, the badge was stolen by Scribe Gaibl.

### Associated quests

- Wedding Crashers

- The Hermit

## Apple orchard

Apple orchard is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A small apple orchard has been planted in the shadow of Trosky Castle. In the middle sits a small cabin, full to the brim with apples with only a straw mattress on the floor by way of real furniture.

## Apprentice Matthias

Apprentice Matthias is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Matthias worked as an apprentice under Blacksmith Zdimir in Grund. He was thought of by his master to be quite skilled and as such Zdimir would often boast about his skill.

Zdimir arranged for a competition between Matthias and Henry to prove who was the better smith. They were to craft a Competition sword. If Henry's was better, Mattias was offended, assuming he must have cheated. He challenged Henry to a duel, only accepting defeat that way.

## Arm armour/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Arm armour is one of the armour types that Henry can equip in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

There are two categories of handwear: Sleeves, which include pauldrons, couters, and various armoured sleeves, and Gloves, which include gauntlets.

Each of the categories occupies its own designated inventory slot.

## Overview

Sleeves

Sleeves serve as the primary form of protection for the arms. While offering strong defense, sleeves add extra weight and generate more noise, making them less ideal for stealth.

Gloves

Gloves, are protective hand coverings that shield the hands and forearms. They come in various designs, from simple leather gloves to more elaborate armored gauntlets.

## Armiger Hagen Trott

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Armiger Hagen Trott is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Hagen worked under Urso von Morgenstern as a mercenary.

When the group was hired by Vaquelin Brabant, Hagen worked alongside the others to support Zizka’s band, helping to steal a cannon from the Prague militia and make a raid on the village and adjoined fortress of Maleshov. He also provided reinforcements and helped carry the silver stolen from the Italian Court to Ruthard Palace to load it onto wagons.

Ultimately, Brabant’s plan was to have them take off with the silver and betray Zizka’s band. This ploy was found out and a fight broke out in which Hagen lost his life along with most of his other allies.

### Associated Quests

- The Lion's Den

- Dancing with the Devil

- The Italian Job

## Armour/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Armour is a crucial part to surviving fights in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

Henry is able to mix and match various types of armour in order to suit his needs. However, to wear protective armor, the padded pieces have to be equipped first before putting on the respective protective pieces.

## Overview

The armour system in the game follows simple logic:

Coif goes under helmet, gambeson under chainmail and/or chest plate, leg plate can only be worn over quilted hose or padded chausses, and spurs can't be worn without shoes. It is not necessary to put on coat and neck collars before the protective gear. Accessory pieces, such as ring and necklaces, do not contribute towards defensive stats but should be worn to boost charisma.

It is possible to create up to 3 gear loadouts and switch between them at any time, excluding active combat. Unlike slots for consumables, which have to be unlocked via pouches, this mechanic is available from the start.

## Armour types

Armour has the following varieties, which each have a designated section in the inventory - it is impossible to wear two of the same item, and some items occupy two slots, but armour and clothing can be overlaid for maximum effect.

Note: To see the lists of available armour follow the corresponding link in the table.

## Statistics

Each piece of armor offers unique stats that affect Henry's overall attributes. Your choice of gear should align with your playstyle, as some armor types may be better suited to certain approaches than others.

For example, if you want to sneak on someone or go on a stealing spree, it's unwise to done full plate, that would clank with every move.

|
Icon

Stat

Description

|

Stab defense
The level of protection the armour provides against stabs from pointed weapons and other items.

|

Slash defense
The level of protection the armour provides against slash type attacks, such as a swinging sword or saber.

|

Blunt defense
The level of protection the armour provides against blunt type attacks, such as an attack with a mace.

|

Conspic.
Conspicuousness is a measurement of how much you stand out in the world. The higher it is, the more noticeable you are.

|

Noise
The amount and level of sound the armour causes with movement, greatly affects your stealth potential.

|

Visibility
How visible you are, greatly affects your stealth potential.

|

Charisma
Charisma is a measure of how important you look. Peasants will bow to someone they think is a noble.

|

Durability
The amount of damage an item can withstand before breaking. Damaged armour will offer lower protection.

## Codex entry

Armour

In the 14th century, manufacturing capabilities expanded, leading to the production of stronger and often combined armours. Older chainmail armours transitioned to plate armour due to advancements in steel processing and the ability to forge larger pieces of metal on automatic hammers. Soldiers' heads were protected by helmets such as the cervelliere (known as the "iron hat"), bascinets, and helms.

Armours were crafted by armourers or helmet makers, typically from a single piece of hardened plate (skull caps, bascinets) or riveted together from several smaller pieces (cervelliere, sallet). The finest armour of the early 15th century was considered that made in German and Italian lands. "Combined type" armours were used by heavy cavalry - they consisted of chainmail supplemented with plate armour covering the limbs and simpler forms of cuirasses, plate coats, or quilted jackets. Some plate coats and breastplates were equipped with a hook for the knight's spear. If the armour lacked a hook, the spear was inserted into a slot in the shield, which covered the left arm controlling the reins and the lower part of the helmet.

A widely used helmet was the bascinet (sallet) with a distinctly shaped visor nicknamed the "dog snout." Additionally, iron hats with one or two eye slots are frequently depicted in visual sources. Shoulders were protected either by chainmail sleeves or small pauldrons. An indispensable part of the armour was the shield.

—Codex entry: Armour/KCD2

## Arne the German

Arne the Deutsch! The apprentice of Master Menhard, they traveled here together all the way from Frankfurt! But don't think him a foreigner! He's grown to love our city so much, he considers it home! Glory to Arne!

—Fridusch Kumel

Arne the German (Czech: Arne Němec) is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

He's the companion of Menhard of Frankfurt with whom he arrived to Kuttenberg prior to the events of KCD2.

When asked about his past by Henry, he says that he originally worked in a port, loading and unloading ships with fabrics. He can additionally reveal that to be able to afford swordsfighting lessons with Master Menhard, he started stealing some cloths to sell. After being caught, Menhard stood up for him and accepted him as his apprentice anyway, for which Arne appears very grateful. Since then, Arne has been in Menhard's services, learning and trying to make a good name for himself as an honest swordsman.

### Associated Quests

- Ars Dimicatoria

- Kuttenberg Tournament

## Arnold

Brother Arnold, otherwise known shorthand as Arn, is a Knight of the Cross with the Red Star in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Arn, alongside his fellow knights, Sibald, Niclas, and Clesgine, were sent to track down and kill Konrad, a former knight from their order who they claimed was paid by the Inquisition to kill the order's Grand Master, Zdenyek. While disguised as monks, they were eating at the tavern in Troskowitz when they overheard locals talking about the hermit, Ambrose, and how strange apparitions that looked like the works of the devil were afoot, suddenly peaking Arn ans his brothers' interest.

Eventually, Arn's group pieced together the fact that Ambrose was their order's old seneschal, but had passed on and Konrad had secretly taken his place. When they went to find and kill Konrad though, Konrad managed to mortally wound Clesgine and the group retreated back to a safer position.

If one sides with Konrad:

Arn, along with the rest of his fellow knights, were summarily killed in Apollonia.

### Associated quest

- The Hermit

## Arrow-head

Arrow-head is a time-limited task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available for a brief window of time following Speak of the Devil.

## Description

## Walkthrough

After completing Speak of the Devil, head down the road between the Devil's Den and Grund. There will be a random encounter there, starting this quest. If you are fast travelling, it will show as a sleeping man on the side of the road. If you are travelling normally, keep an eye out for him.

The sleeping man is called Karel and he has a distinctive arrow in his head. Speak to him and agree to carry the sacks with him back to his camp. Although this is a bandit camp, they will not be hostile as you are with Karel.

Simply follow him then talk to him once you are in his camp to receive your reward and end the quest.

## Ars Dimicatoria

Ars Dimicatoria is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. After completing this quest, Henry will be able to compete in the weekly Kuttenberg Tournament.

## Description

In Kuttenberg, I met a master swordsman and engaged in a friendly duel with him. It turned out, it’s not that easy in Kuttenberg to practice [sic] the art of swordsmanship, or Schwertkunst, also known by the scholarly name of Ars Dimicatoria.

## Walkthrough

In the market square in central Kuttenberg, a man named Menhard von Frankfurt will call out and challenge you to a duel. He can be found in the northeastern side of the square, outside the door of an armourer (there is an additional armourer and blacksmith directly south of him, and another armourer to the southeast). If Henry accepts, he can duel Menhard and bet 200 groschen on the outcome.

Menhard will insist on practice longswords only with no armour, and is a skilled opponent. He'll regularly parry and riposte your strikes so make sure to use your own ripostes and master strikes to take him out. It won't take many hits to win the fight (or lose) since neither of you are armoured.

Regardless of the outcome of the duel, several angry townspeople and a councilman will approach and demand that Henry and Menhard stop, because the Kuttenberg swordfighting brotherhood has exclusive rights to swordfighting in the city. There are two medium skillchecks Henry can use to get out of this mess and unlock the quest: diplomatically defend Menhard instead of remaining silent during both skillchecks.

Additionally, refuse to pay when the councilman insists that Henry either pay or be caned (Menhard will pay for you - if you win the duel at least, I'm not sure otherwise). After this, the situation will defuse and Menhard will invite Henry to come talk to him at the Emperor Charles tavern.

### Meet with Menhard

At the inn, Menhard and his pal Arne the German have a plan to force the swordfighting guild to duel them - Henry is to steal the guild sword from the guildhall and hang it outside the town hall, so that it looks like a challenge to the Germans.

### Steal the sword

Wait until nightfall (or not, depending on your lockpicking ability) and then make your way to the guildhall in the Hradek district in the southwestern corner of the city, next to the city bathhouse. At night, the locks on the side and back doors of the guildhall are both hard, and the front door is very hard, so if you can't pick them you'll need to sneak in during the day.

The entire first floor is free to roam during the day and the backdoor will be unlocked, but the second floor and up are all off-limits. At night the entire building as well as the courtyard and fighting arena behind it are red trespassing areas.

Go to the second floor, through the first door on the right (the south side of the building, it will have an easy lock on it) where you'll be in a lit hall, and on the right wall will be the sword. Grab it and escape unnoticed. Note that NPCs patrol the building during the day and at night, but there appear to be many more during the day/evening. After midnight, most of the guards go to sleep on the second and third floor.

Now, simply take the sword to city hall, wait until the coast is clear, and hang it up on the southern wall of the building. Once you're done, return to Menhard. The next day, Henry, Menhard, and Arne will go to the town hall to accept the challenge, and the city councilman will declare that a tournament will be held to decide which swordfighting brotherhood remains in the city and reserves the right to teach swordsmanship.

### Join the brotherhood

If you wish to participate in the fight, you must join Menhard's brotherhood. If you won the duel against him earlier, you'll be able to join immediately. Once you accept, Menhard will hold a brief ceremony swearing you in, and then you'll become a member. Afterwards, talk to Menhard again when you're ready for the fight (the game also autosaves for you at this point).

If you did not beat Menhard initially, you will have to duel Arne for the right to become a member. You can duel him as many times as needed to beat him. Make sure you keep the Training longsword equipped or else you will not be able to be armed against him.

### The tournament

Once you're ready, tell Menhard and the tournament will begin. Note: while the other combatants are fighting, you can loot the armourer's tent that the councilman mentions to find several good pieces of armour, and several armourer's kits, blacksmith's kits, and tailor's kits (with the exception of the Magdeburg cuirass, you're allowed to pick them up - it's not theft) before returning to the fight area.

You'll need to win at least one of your two fights before a cutscene plays and Arne is injured. There is a speech check here - if you fail it, you'll need to have won both of your previous fights in the tournament in order to win overall, assuming you win your next 2 fights against Emmerich and Nikolas.

As Menhard is disqualified - it's up to you! Emmerich is a far easier opponent than either Menhard or Nikolas, but Nikolas will parry and riposte well, so play defensively against him and look for master strikes. You shouldn't need more than a few hits to beat any of the opponents, but the same is true in reverse. Once you've won, you'll fast travel to the apothecary where Arne will receive treatment, and you'll need to wait a few days for Menhard to take over the swordfighting hall.

### Conclusion

After a few days have passed, the quest will update and tell Henry to go see Menhard at the fighthall. He'll thank Henry for his help and give him Master Menhart's longsword, as well as offer to teach him a special longsword combo, Oben Abnehmen. Henry will also now be able to participate in the weekly Kuttenberg Tournament. He'll also have complete access to the fighthall, and an owned bed in the loft there. Additionally, Menhard and Arne will now both be available as combat trainers. This concludes the quest.

## Rewards

- Master Menhart's longsword

- Unlocks (and begins) the weekly Kuttenberg Tournament

- Owned bed (inside the Kuttenberg fighthall)

- Fechthalle key

- Oben Abnehmen (longsword combo)

- Unlocks Menhard (master longsword trainer) and Arne (master polearm & heavy weapons trainer) as combat trainers

## Attila (Quest)

For the horse see Attila

Attila is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is available after the main quest Taking French Leave.

## Description

Some gangs stole a horse from Hashtal’s stables. But in doing so the fools made quite a racket. Hashtal caught them in the act and now wants help getting his horse back from them.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Innkeeper Slatchalek in Maleshov to get the tip for the quest. He will point you towards Groom Hashtal.

Note: You can lock yourself out of this quest if you choose the skill checks with Hashtal and fail them.

Talk to Hashtal and he will send you after the horse Attila who has been stolen. The horse thieves are in the woods to the west along the stream on the west end of the search radius.

Mount the horse and ride off back to the Maleshov stables. Hashtal will give you 250 groschen as a reward and will then be unlocked as a skill teacher for horsemanship and craftsmanship.
