## Back in the Saddle

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Back in the Saddle is the 7th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

We finally met with Lord von Bergow, but unfortunately this is not the time for political negotiations. The region is plagued by a group of bandits, and von Bergow is gathering troops to strike against them. He has, therefore, sent us to Nebakov to take the call of arms to the lord there.

## Synopsis

Having recovered from their near miss, Henry and Hans are called into a meeting with von Bergow. He requests a report on what brought them to the point of near execution before turning to business – von Bergow and his allies have been opposed to those of Rattay, so before he can consider rearranging allegiances he needs his bandit problem dealt with. Bergow wants to call all his vassals to Trosky in order to gather enough men to mount a real attack. He wants Henry and Hans to go to Nebakov and send the word to his vassal there – Sir Jaromir Nebak.

Before they leave, Henry wants to know if von Bergow may have seen Istvan Toth among the bandits when he was attacked, as Henry is still certain he saw him at the pond. Bergow, however, says he saw no one who would meet Henry’s description.

Chamberlain Ulrich leads them out of the room, attempting an apology now that he’s aware Hans really is a noble, but Hans is still unwilling to forgive both insult and injury incurred. For Henry, he provides a brief tour of the Trosky Castle grounds, showing Henry to his bed by the forge while Hans finds his own accommodations.

As a gesture of goodwill, von Bergow has ordered a horse and tack to be prepared for Henry along with the return of his things and some clothing – so he won’t go embarrassing the castle. Henry may take the gift horse or stick with Pebbles. Either way, he’s now ready to escort Hans to Nebakov.

On the ride, Henry and Hans talk about various topics from Hans’s near miss to the intricacies of political machinations, having the opportunity to race for a bit. At Nebakov, Hans leaves to discuss the reason for their being there with Lord Nebak while Henry is given over to an adjutant, Michael. Michael first insists Henry have a drink, letting him know part of the fortress is off limits due to ongoing construction but that he has free rein of most of the place for as long as the talks take and there’s plenty of dice to be played.

There are many things Henry may do to pass the time, duelling with Michael, racing Hertel, helping Klara on her rounds to gather herbs, helping various other Nebakov denizens and exploring on his own. Alongside these diversions, Henry may notice a few strange goings on – everyone seems keen to keep him distracted, stories about how the many horses were obtained don’t match up, and he may even spy stolen equipment, a Leipa shield, and even a man in the dungeons claiming to be the real Lord Nebak amongst other things.

Eventually, Hans is finished talks and Henry goes to loop him in. Whether or not Henry caught wind of the suspicious goings-on around the fortress, Henry and Hans leave to report back to von Bergow. They report on the results of talks and their findings. For his part, von Bergow’s men have captured a member of the infamous band; he is down in the dungeons and von Bergow would like for Henry and Hans to interrogate him as he has so far been unsuccessful. He also asks if either of them knows of any strange happenings in the region that might put them on the trail and Henry may report on various topics including one that may be of note – Olda Semine’s suspicious behaviour the night of his wedding.

## Walkthrough

Right after your talk with Otto von Bergow, Ulrich will lead you outside where Hans will immediately accost the chamberlain for nearly getting him killed. He'll then inform Henry he'll meet him at the gates when ready.

If you want, you can follow the chamberlain, who will talk to you a bit about Trosky Castle before showing you to your quarters—a small room near the forge. More importantly, your storage chest is inside, containing all your taken items, and Mutt will be back at your side if you found him. When you open your inventory, you will be given the option to restore your clothing and equipment presets to those you had in place just before the wedding.

When you're ready, go talk to Kabat and he'll tell you the horse tack is prepared, but also that he was instructed to ask whether you'd like to keep your current horse or accept the one von Bergow is offering. You can then check out the nearby horse, Herring and then let Kabat know your choice. If you decline the offer, he'll come up with an idea to secretly sell Herring for some coin and split the profits with you—while telling the lord you accepted the horse. You can agree, refuse, or pass a speech check to ask for more groschen. Either way, he'll then give you some horse tack.

### Meet up with Hans

Note once you set out with Hans, a number of activities will come up later in the quest. As you won't have access to an alchemy bench, it's recommended you have at least a few Saviour Schnapps to save as needed so you don't have to re-load too far out from the last save if you mess up somewhere.

Hans will only set out in the morning (wanting to be back by sunset), so if you're wanting to run around and do other things, keep this in mind that you'll have to wait out time to the next morning if it's too late in the day.

Once ready and during a time Hans is ok with (usually indicated by him waiting just outside an archway/gate area) approach and talk to him. Here you can talk a bit and, if wanting to express any romantic interest, an option comes up in the second conversation. He'll also mention wanting to make good on his promise to repay Bozhena for her kindness, which if you already did Henry will automatically tell him, earning some reputation. If you also did Bad Blood, Henry will likewise mention part of this, earning some more reputation. After that, mount up and follow Hans, responding how you wish.

Outside the castle, Hans will mention needing to let loose for a bit and asks to race, which you can agree to or not. If you agree, you'll race him to the shrine at the crossroads to the southwest of Troskowitz. Note you don't need to stick to the roads either: you can cut across the fields here entirely if you want. If you beat him, he'll reward you with 55 Groschen.

Afterwards, you'll continue riding a bit with Hans, where a couple topics can be discussed before you're given the option to fast travel or continue manually travelling (neither choice will have an affect on available topics). Choose whatever you like, and eventually you'll make it to Nebakov Fortress.

### Nebakov Fortress

At the fortress gate, you're told to leave as Jaromier Nebak isn't accepting visitors. However, Hans will demand to see him as he has a message from von Bergow. You'll eventually be let in where the lord will meet you with some of his men. Small talk is made, notably about the large amount of horses Jaromier has, before he heads off to talk with Hans privately while having one of his men, Michael, shows you around.

-
Michael

-
Klara

-
Zwerk

-
Peltzel

-
Mark

Michael will take you to where their dice player is, next to the kitchens and asks you to join him in eating and drinking. If you do, he'll ask into why von Bergow sent you, where you can choose to answer or not. If you tell him you don't know, he'll try again to see if you can drop any details, which you can oblige or remain firm. Eventually he'll ask if you want to have a friendly duel or not, which you can accept or decline. Note that if you caved and provided some information, right after this you have the option to then inquire about how they have so many horses. Michael will oblige, noting Jaromier had acquired some deceased relatives' lands that he couldn't be given, so they instead gave him a bunch of horses as compensation.

Note if you agreed to duel him and proceed to do so, he is a tough opponent, fighting with a shield. If you best him, he'll give you rowel spurs. He'll then point you to several people at the fortress you can talk to: Klara, Zwerk, Peltzel, and Mark.

Klara is located at her small hut just past the archway to the left of the blacksmith. You can ask her to tend to your wounds, after which you can talk a bit, impressing her with your scholarly knowledge if you pass the check. She'll then ask if you can go along with her to help her out. If you agree, there are two different ways this part will affect later dialogue choices based on how you answer:

- Picking the flirting option will lock out a way to get a little information about the fortress (but the information isn't crucial)

- Noting to explore the fortress will have her provide a little information with a speech check (but the romantic option will still appear if you decide to not ask her for information)

Regardless of choice, she'll lead you out to a field past the horse pastures to gather materials. Keep in mind an auto-save point is made after this choice.

While you walk, she'll ask you to talk to her about your travels, of which you can choose two to talk about. At the field, she'll then request you help her gather some herbs. If you have high enough survival skills, you can further impress her with your knowledge to gain some more reputation before she sends you off to gather marigold, poppy, and sage. These are found throughout the field. Once you have enough, bring them back to her and she'll note she has to reveal something to you, then will lead you further off to a secluded area.

Depending how you agreed to accompany her, the following options may happen:

- If you flirted, she'll go straight to giving you a riddle that can lead to a romantic encounter.

- If you want to decline her advances, choose the "I'm not in the mood for this", though this will cause some reputation loss

- If you didn't flirt, you have the option to ask her what she wanted to tell you (leading to the riddle above) or demand what's going on at the fortress with a speech check.

- If you successfully press for details, she'll confirm that something is going on. However, she wants nothing else to do with you, causing some reputation loss.

Zwerk is the dice player with whom you can use a silver badge. He doesn't give any special rewards or information other than the standard betting amount you picked if you win.

If you head out to talk to the groomer, Peltzel, there will be a villager standing near the trough who'll try to get your attention. If you talk to the villager, he'll make a remark he's going out to get some deadwood (kindling) indicating he wants you to follow him. If you do so, he'll lead you out a short ways where nobody else is around and then warns you something is very off about the people: he hasn't seen Jaromier in ages and it seems some new men are in charge now, claiming to be friends with Jaromier. He'll then see a guard approaching from the distance and will run off before he's spotted. You can then go and intercept the guard, who comes up with some lame excuse why he was out there before telling you you should go back to the fortress.

If you talk to Peltzel, you can try to convince him with a speech check (with medium checks to ask about the horses or that you're interested in them, otherwise hard check for wasting a knight's time) to get him to reveal where the horses came from. Otherwise, you'll have to race and win to get details out of him. Getting him to talk will reveal they got the horses when they took out some bandits, which if you talked to Michael, clearly doesn't line up. You can poke some more at his story, which will get him to stammer and mix up details, locations, and names.

If you choose to race, you'll face off against Hertel and will need to race down the valley, to Nebakov Mill, and back. If you win, Peltzel will give you a Hungarian saddle.

Mark is in the area over the gate and will let you try to compete against him in archery. If you win, he'll reward you with an Old field crossbow.

Note also that if you found the stockpile of ammo, you can question him on this, but he won't provide any details and causes some reputation loss.

### Exploring the fortress

By this point, if you've got information about the horses from both Michael and Peltzel, or talked to the villager, you're likely realizing something fishy is going on. You can either choose to try and explore around some more or continue with various activities. Keep in mind as your time limit is 6 in-game hours at the fortress (after which the meeting will be done and you won't be allowed to continue walking around the fortress interior) you may not be able to do every activity while also figuring out what's going on.

-
Steer

-
Hertel

-
Mikesh and Kozliek

-
Points of interest

Steer is the blacksmith, located right inside the fortress' gate. You can talk shop with him and, with high enough skill, get him to reveal some of the guys are working on something further downhill. When you offer to help though, he'll suddenly become flustered and wave it off and try to direct you to some of the other activities instead.

If you found the surplus of equipment, you can ask him on this, but he won't reveal any information about it.

Hertel is standing guard at a door on the ground floor of the tower, just past the dice table. Talking to him will reveal there's prisoners and understandably, you're not allowed into the area. If you want in, there's a few ways to do this, some more trickier than others:

- Get the keys that are one floor above, in the dining hall in the tower. This area is a private area, so you'll have to sneak in, then quickly sneak through the door right inside to find the keys on the table here and get out. You may opt to carefully do this by opening and closing doors as you go so nobody gets suspicious, but will have to make a careful exit out.

- Rely on lockpicking. Instead of getting the keys, you can try to lockpick the door. However, it's a hard lock and you may get spotted by a patrolling guard, as they frequently pass through the area.

No matter what you choose, you still need to get Hertel out of the way, either by using a medium speech check to get him to leave for a bit or, failing that, go into the kitchen area, use the backdoor here to sneak around and knock him out discreetly. Just be careful of the other guards around.

Once inside, quickly close the door behind you so guards don't get suspicious, then turn to the cells to see the prisoners. Talk to the nearest one and he'll soon reveal he's the real Jaromier: his fortress was taken by surprise by bandits who are now holding him captive there. He'll then beg you to quickly head back to let von Bergow know of the situation. You can try to talk more with him, though you may not have much time if you left a door open or aroused enough suspicion that it puts the bandits on alert (like if they find you stole the keys). However, if you have time, with a hard speech check you can get Jaromier to reveal some details of how the fortress was taken, but will cause some reputation loss. If you likewise question why you should believe him, this will also cause some reputation loss.

This is entirely dependent on actions you took when you were helping out Bozhena during Fortuna. If you convinced them to leave, they'll appear here, behind Klara's hut. Talk to either one and they'll give the same conversation, with Henry remarking he recognizes them from somewhere. If you pick the right one (Rocktower pond) they'll suddenly drop details that re-confirm they're the bandits that were trying to find you, raising further suspicions if you haven't already talked to the prisoner.

Ammo

If you take to exploring around, just past the kitchen area are stairs that go to the right, with a locked door here in this small area. You can lockpick it, but be careful of the patrolling guards, and make sure to quickly close the door behind you so they don't see you snooping. Once in, examine the area near the target to notice they have a ton of ammunition. When ready to leave, try to do so when you don't hear a guard passing by.

Equipment

At the very top of the fortress' tower are some sleeping guards and a lot of equipment which you can examine. You can examine and steal items, just be aware if you get spotted acting suspicious in this area, they may figure out you stole the items here.

Leipa Shield and Pistol

This one's harder to reach since it's in a private area at the far end of the fortress, with a guard at the gate and workers around. Go to Klara's hut, then look at the fence opposite it—you'll see an opening with some fallen posts. Go through and follow the outer wall all the way around to the back of the fortress. There's an opening near a building.

If angled right, you can examine a Leipa shield just inside the building from the fence opening. Note regarding Mutt here: Mutt has a tendency to set the nearby soldiers off, so while they'll focus on him, this can cause complications trying to leave discreetly/without raising any alarms if you want to explore the building here.

If you want to look around some more, carefully enter this restricted building and pick the medium locked door to enter to find a number of things to examine: the equipment, the contraption to the right of the door, and if you pick the medium locked chest, the ammo inside. If you had completed Opus Magnum, Henry's remarks will be different here regarding the contraption and ammo, recognizing it as similar to what Kreyzl's been working towards.

### Reunite with Hans

After six in-game hours have passed, your objectives will automatically update to show that the meeting has concluded. At this point, the entire interior of the fortress becomes a private area, and everyone will tell you to leave. Return to Hans—if you uncovered the truth and found the real lord, Henry will briefly explain the situation and why they need to leave quickly. Otherwise, he won't have anything special to report. Either way, you'll immediately head back to Trosky Castle to report to von Bergow.

- If you didn't find out the truth, Hans will give his report on what "Jaromier" agreed to send. While you can mention the horses, Hans will add that Jaromier hired mercenaries, and that—per his contract with them—it would cost extra to send them out for tasks beyond protecting the fortress. Von Bergow will wonder how the lord managed to afford so many mercenaries, but the conversation soon shifts to another topic: a captured prisoner who was part of the group that ambushed von Bergow.

- If you did find out the truth, you'll instead reveal that the fortress is in the hands of bandits and that Jaromier is their prisoner. While this is certainly alarming, von Bergow sees one silver lining: the bandits have walked themselves into a trap, as he expects the fort can be easily besieged once preparations are made. He'll then move on to the next topic: a captured prisoner who was part of the group that ambushed him.

However, his next issue is a sensitive one: it requires the possible torture of the prisoner, which is usually handled by executioners. As the castle lacks one though, he asks Hans and Henry to do it instead, especially as it's personal to them as well. You can either readily agree (earning some reputation), be against it (loss of reputation), or note you'll try other ways if possible (no reputation change). The three will talk a bit more before von Bergow asks you both if you noticed anything suspicious going on while he was away. Depending how much you've already explored, you may have a long list here but can only choose one (or none). Worthy of note though is remarking that "Young Semine left his own wedding." Important: using this line can cause a very hard speech check in the next main quest if you wish to avoid certain outcomes. If you wish to keep options open and don't think you'll have enough to pass said check, use something else or say nothing.

The conversation will then wrap up, but if you uncovered the truth, von Bergow will tack on one additional thing: a special reward for you that you can claim from Black Bartosch (which will be a weapon of any type along with a few armour pieces). The weapon given will be one of the following based on your pick:

- Longsword - Common longsword

- Short sword - Broadsword

- Axe - Bearded axe

- War hammer - Rider's war hammer

- Polearm - Glaive

## Bailiff (Pschitoky)

Bailiff is a unnamed minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

The bailiff was in charge of the construction of the fort at Pschitoky in the service of Anna of Waldstein.

Due to many different factors, however, the construction was behind schedule and over budget. To check on the situation, Adela of Mnischek was sent to the town to obverse how things were going with her guard Yedlitchka.

As part of the construction he had hired a painter to paint inside the new fortress and had promised him payment in the form of a Lapis lazuli. He came, however, to view the stone as a good luck charm and refused to be parted from it.

The bailiff was enamoured with Adela and wanted to impress her, ignoring her hints that she was not at all interested in him in return. To try and win her over he tried to convince Henry, who had come to gather the payment the painter was owed, to insult Adela and then lose to him in a duel for her honour.

The duel might have gone either way. If Henry refused the duel flat out, he could have instead gathered payment by defacing the finished painting to say that the bailiff did not pay.

### Associated quest

- Stained Honour

## Bailiff Thrush

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Bailiff Thrush (Czech: Rychtář Drozd) serves as the representative of Lord Otto von Bergow in the Trosky region. He is tasked with enforcing the law, managing the daily affairs of the village of Troskowitz, and handling complaints from the local peasantry.

He lives in the Troskowitz's rathaus with his two children - Agnes and Svatya. While he's considered a commoner, he has more money than the local nobleman of Semine.

## Biography

### Associated quests

- Bad Blood

- Battle of the Frogs and Mice

- The Hermit

- The Jaunt

- Wedding Crashers

- Portrait in Red

## Dialogue

(I'd like to report an ambush.)

Henry: "I'd like to report an ambush. Some scoundrels attacked my lord's retinue and killed our men."

Thrush: "That's a serious matter. Where is your lord?"

Henry: "Well, I… He left."

Thrush: "I don't understand why he's not lodging a complaint himself and why not directly at the castle. He has that right as a lord."

Henry: "It's a long story. My lord got very angry and then went missing."

Thrush: "Sorry, fellah, but I'm not sure whether you're making it up or lying to me. But if you're telling the truth, why don't you bring your lord here and we can talk it all over calmly? I'm sorry, lad, but until then, I've got more important things to do."

━━━━━━━━━

(I need to speak with Sir Otto.)

Henry: "I need to speak with Sir Otto."

Thrush: "With the Royal Chamberlain? Are you yanking my official pizzle?"

Henry: "Why not?"

Thrush: "I'd like to talk to him too, boy, but he's still in Prague. He's hardly ever here. Chamberlain Ulrich is in charge of things."

Henry: "And where do I find him?"

Thrush: "Where do you think? Up in the castle."

Henry: "But they won't let me in there."

Thrush: "What do you want me to do about it? That's your problem. I'm not going to put a word in for you. I hardly know you."

━━━━━━━━━

(I'm looking for my friend.)

Henry: "Excuse me, I'm looking for the man who was in the pillory with me yesterday. Have you seen him?"

Thrush: "I can't help you with that, you'll have to find him yourself."

━━━━━━━━━

(Where can I find the local merchants here?)

Henry: "I'd like to buy something. Where can I find some merchants around here?"

Thrush: "If it's tradesmen you're after, most of them live here in the village, of course. Your best bet is to ask our merchant Jurg. He knows everyone. I'm sure he'll help you."

━━━━━━━━━

(What's new?)

Henry: "What's new, Bailiff?"

Thrush: "Hmm, nothing special. Fortunately, Troskowitz is a quiet village. It's peaceful here and the war has avoided us so far, thank God. Just here and there a brawl in the tavern or a neighbour's errant cow. Well, that's how it was until recently, at least!"

Henry: "And what happened?"

Thrush: "What do you think? It started with that nomadic riff raff, theft of hens and sheep, then continued with ambushes on the road! And then the wolves started to come in from the forests on account of poachers killing off their prey. Oh, and then our Master Chamberlain Ulrich, oh my God… But that's no business of yours, understand!?"

Henry: "Aye, I understand, that's your business, Bailiff."

━━━━━━━━━

(Mice quest tip.)

Henry: "What's new in the county, Master Bailiff."

Thrush: "I heard something's going on in Tachov again. Prochek the innkeeper is probably coming up with some mischief to pull on the Zhelejovites. Will they never cut it out! Their bickering is making work for me!"

━━━━━━━━━

(Tip about Zizka.)

Thrush: "I was just visited by one of the local peasants. He said he found more fresh graves behind his field. Just below the village, along the road to Nebakov."

Henry: "What do you mean more? You sound like this isn't the first time."

Thrush: "That we found someone buried here? Don't even ask. I've been digging up bodies ever since that bandit gang started running rampant. Most of them are von Bergow's men."

━━━━━━━━━

(Tip about Sauerkraut Pepa.)

Thrush: "Also… as if it wasn't bad enough that a gang of bandits is rampaging through the region. Now someone's stealing cabbage from the peasants! What a disaster."

Henry: "Cabbage?"

Thrush: "Aye. And the peasants won't stop bugging me about it. I was just visited by a peasant from Schdiar. He's been talking my ears off for God knows how long. Say, do I really have to do this? Do I have the time to look for some moron stealing cabbages?"

## Balthazar

Balthazar is an enigmatic man in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II that can be randomly encountered at Camp by the road locations.

## Biography

Balthazar is a well-spoken but mysterious character who can be found at roadside locations as a random encounter. He appears to know quite a bit about Henry and claims it is because he quietly observes things, with an uncanny ability to listen and remember details for later. A barber & surgeon, he also notes that he has no qualms about assassinating someone when paid to do so. He sells a variety of both potions and poisons.

## Bandit camp

Bandit camp is a location type in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance

Smoke in the middle of the screenshot of the Sasau region map.

Clearing up the bandit camps is part of the quests Ruin, Raiders, and Interlopers.

Bandit and cuman camps in Kingdom Come: Deliverance are usually unmarked. However, their location is easy to see on the background map - there is a smoke coming off of their location.

The camps consist of a few bandits (Ruin and Interlopers) or Cumans (Raiders). The camp leader is very well armed, and there is often an enemy with a bow.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

In the second game, most enemy camps are part of some quests, and in Legacy of the Forge, they are part of the "fetch" questline In the Service of the Guild.

The bandit camps are referenced by names that often didn't make it into the game (with the notable exception of the Kerchak camp), but correspond to names used for the areas.

## Barber Fiala

A fine fellah, with a punch like you've been kicked by an ox, but Dorothy, his wife, has him on a short leash.

—Innkeeper Lawrence

Barber Fiala (Czech: Bradýř Fiala) is the best (and only) barber in the Trosky region, while also acting as the bouncer for his wife's bathhouse in Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn.

## Biography

### Early life

Many years ago before he got involved with Dorothy, Fiala used to be a drunkard and gambled a lot. However, that changed one day after an incident involving Dorothy, Fiala, a pitchfork, and "the arse of one uppity customer." As such, Fiala credits his wife as helping him become a more decent person.

Nowadays, he's a barber though he also helps out at his wife's bathhouse, acting as bouncer to make sure customers behave themselves.

### Involvement

Henry first hears about him during the local brawling tournament, where he holds the title of reigning champion at the Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn. The tournament had been put on hold because Dorothy forbade him from participating - he's the bathhouse bouncer and responsible for looking after the girls, so he can't shirk his duties. Though, as Dorothy admits to Henry, the real reason is that he always wins, and the bruised egos (and faces) of defeated men aren't great for business.

After Henry convinces her that "this time is the last time", he happily rejoins the tournament. Whether he wins or loses, he'll teach Henry what he knows afterwards.

### Associated quest

- Wine, Women and Blood

## Basilard

Basilard is a melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a shortsword.

Note: Basilard can be crafted.

## Description

A short sword that is said to have been given its special name because of its origin. Whether it really originated in the Swiss city of Basel is questionable, but it is certainly a great weapon that can be carried, unlike the sword, even by low-born townspeople.

## Bathhouse owner Dorothy

Bathhouse owner Dorothy (Czech: Majitelka lázní Dorota) runs the bathhouse in Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Dorothy is married to Fiala, who before they got involved, was originally a drunkard and tended to gamble a lot. However, that changed one day after an incident involving Dorothy, Fiala, a pitchfork, and "the arse of one uppity customer." Nowadays, Dorothy runs the bathhouse while Fiala acts as a bouncer, making sure customers behave themselves.

### Associated Quests

- Wine, Women and Blood

- Opus Magnum

## Bathing spot

All three drowned. It sends shivers down my spine.

—Henry's comment

Bathing spot is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

This place can be found along the western shore of the Rocktower pond, at a small pier near the dam, just off the water's edge among the reeds and scattered trees.

It was once a spot where three local hired hands were often seen swimming, but after they stumbled upon the Water goblin's treasure, they all mysteriously drowned.

The bodies are visible without much searching. Two of the hired hands lie partially submerged in the shallow water, while the third is on the shore to the right of the pier.

After discovering the bodies, you can tell Innkeeper Lawrence for additional reputation.

## Loot

On the pier inside the burlap sack:

- Drowner's map

- Fine wine × 3

- Roast duck

- Groschen × 138

On the body farthest from the pier:

- Unlucky die

- Carpenter's Advantage badge

- Groschen × 6.9

## Battle of the Frogs and Mice

Battle of the Frogs and Mice is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It's the culmination after doing Frogs or Mice or both.

## Description

Every year, disputes over the pasture between Tachov and Zhelejov culminate in the men from both villages getting together, arguing, and punching each other in the mouth. But this year, they’ll have a guest from Skalitz to share in the glory.

## Walkthrough

Eventually, you'll see the option to go talk to Bailiff Thrush about the pasture, though he'll be a bit annoyed, as both villages constantly bring it up to him. You can eventually try to convince him settling this once and for all means not having to hear about the pasture any more. If successful, he'll mention Troskowitz's chronicles were documented by the previous bailiff, but in such a weird wording that Thrush can't figure out what it all means. If he grants you access to read it, go find it near where scribe Gaibl normally works, on a podium near the bookshelf.

While reading the text is helpful for context clues on figuring out which tree, what you really need right now is at the very end of the book, where Latin text is written. Remember this text and go ask Gaibl about it. Pick the correct phrase and he'll translate it, revealing the pasture's boundaries between the two villages was marked by an iron nail in one of the three trees. You can read the book for further clues on which tree it is as well.

Hard to see nail, marking the boundaries

Head out to the pasture area and you'll see a few large trees throughout it. The one you want is somewhere in the middle. Note that finding the nail can be difficult as Henry won't automatically get a prompt to view it, so you'll have to carefully look for a rusty brown nail sticking out of the tree on one side (about eye level). As such, it's best to do this when it's sunny out.

After you find it, it'll be noted that the pasture is equally split between both villages. At this point you can leave it be, or remove it and try to move it in favour of one or the other.

Once you've finished with the nail make sure you complete the optional objective to go tell Thrush about it before you talk to either prank giver. If you don't tell Thrush about your discovery the entire effort will have been a complete waste and your only option will be to watch both sides fight over the pasture again.

When you're ready, go to either prank giver and let them know you're ready to head out to the pasture.

People from both villages will meet up and Thrush will appear to finally settle things. Note there's several speech checks here, where you can gain reputation (if you're polite and push for the groups to make up) or loss reputation if you yell at them to listen. If you didn't move the nail, it'll be revealed the pasture is equally split and while neither group is particularly happy about this, this resolves their conflicts and Olbram and Proschek will converse amicably enough, hinting they kind of enjoy still pulling pranks on each other.

Talk to the bailiff afterwards and he'll be thankful that's over. If you ask for a reward, you will lose reputation here, and while he'll give you a skill book, Master's Studies I, this would have been given anyway without asking for a reward.

## Been There, Done That

Been There, Done That is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You've completed most of the game's content.

## Acquisition

This achievement is awarded for completing the majority of the game's content. While the exact threshold is not specified in-game, the achievement is tied to completing approximately 100 quests, including main quests, side quests, and tasks.

A small number of failed quests does not seem to block the achievement, provided the total number of completed quests and tasks reaches the necessary threshold.

## Tips

- When entering a new town or village, speak with the innkeeper and ask about happenings in the area. This will reveal nearby quest givers on the map.

- Complete side quests and tasks as soon as you receive them. Some quests may become unavailable if delayed.

- While fast travelling, stop at events along the road. Certain side quests and tasks are triggered through random encounters.

Although most content remains accessible after completing the main story, there are two points of no return in the game, after which certain quests become unavailable.

First Point of No Return

Occurs toward the end of the Necessary Evil main quest, after interrogating the prisoner and before speaking with von Bergow. A fullscreen warning is displayed at this point. Failing to complete the Demons of Trosky quest before this point will render it inaccessible. If you raid Semine instead of avoiding the assault, you will also miss the following tasks from Gules:

- Canker

- Handsome Charlie

- Johnny the Gob

- Casper

Second Point of No Return

Occurs near the end of the Oratores main quest, when returning to Ruthard Palace. A fullscreen warning is again shown. Quests that may be missed if not completed by this point:

- Ransom

- The Thunderstone

- Hush, My Darling...

- Absolver

- Lost Honour

- Spoils of War

- The Stalker

While Ransom is not technically missable, the remaining quests are. Most of them are tied to Sigismund's camp, and should be completed before reaching the conclusion of Oratores.

Note that this is not an exhaustive list of missable quests - only the most prominent examples.

## Bellatores

Bellatores is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It can be started by talking to Jan Posy of Zimburg, who will be in front of or inside the tavern in Bylany.

## Description

Knights Sir Jan 'Posy' and Sir Miroslav 'Tugbone' of Zimburg were attacked along with their company while travelling to Sedletz Monastery. Miroslav was captured, and Jan is preparing to save him.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Posy and agree to help him, then hop on your horse and follow him to the site where his party was ambushed by the Cumans.

### Robbers

As you arrive at the site of the ambush, you'll come upon a group of men robbing the corpses. Posy fully intends to kill them, and will do so unless Henry intervenes. Regardless of how the robbers are dealt with, you'll next have to search the bodies for a priest who was travelling with Posy's group. Despite his earlier outrage over the corpse robbers, he has no problem with Henry looting the corpses (which you should do, as there's a significant amount of valuable gear here, including Posy's unique polearm, Balshanka). The priest you're looking for is lying dead next to the river, just off the road.

### Find the hideout

After discovering the dead priest, Posy will decide it's time to track down the ambushers and head off into the woods. Eventually you'll come upon a woman named Fiolka. She'll inform you that the Cumans must be holed up in Posy's family's very own abandoned castle nearby. As you arrive at the ruins, the game will save and Posy will tell you his plan, which is very simply just a frontal assault.

### Killing the Cumans

With a Medium speech check you can convince him to wait until night (which is recommended - there are a lot of Cumans you'll have to fight), or alternatively you can offer to do it completely alone during the day. You'll want to buff yourself as much as possible and probably utilize some strong Bane poison if opting for the frontal assault, whether during the day or night, as there's roughly 8+ enemies you'll be facing all at once.

It may be easier to opt to do it alone at night, and just sneak through the camp assassinating the Cumans one by one. Once they're all down, the game will save and Jan will tell you to search the southern part of the ruins for Miroslav. You can use this opportunity to loot the dead, as there's a ton of good gear here. There are also 2 chests in the camp, one Medium and one Hard that are worth looting.

Run down into the ruin on the south side of the camp and you'll see Miroslav sitting there tied up. Untie him and a cutscene will play of him reuniting with his brother. The brothers will reward Henry for his assistance. However, the mysterious item that they were transporting to Sedletz isn't here, and the leader of the Cuman band isn't either. So Posy tells Henry to wait a couple days and then come and find him if he wishes to help them recover the item (this is the Skeleton in the Closet activity). With this, the quest is completed.

## Besieged

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Besieged is the 28th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically at the conclusion of So it begins....

## Synopsis

Suchdol is besieged by the Prague army. If we want to survive, we must prevent the enemy from advancing.

## Walkthrough

Zizka will give you orders to interrogate a prisoner and choose some of your men for a raid on the Praguer camp.

### Choose soldiers for the raid

You'll need to choose which soldiers you send on the raid. Choosing the best soldiers will have the best outcome here, so pick any 3 of Kubyenka, Samuel, Jaroslav, or Janek. You can choose to send Dobrosh and/or Wolfram, but they are not as skilled and it presents more of a risk for them.

Once you've assigned the men, head into the basement and talk to Dry Devil.

### Interrogate the prisoner

Next, you'll need to get as much information as possible out of the hostage before the raid so that your guys know what to burn down. Dry Devil will offer to torture immediately, but if you'd rather get the information without resorting to torture tell him you'd like to at least try talking to the prisoner first.

You'll need to choose the following dialogue options in order to get all the information you need without torture:

- Skill check you are most likely to pass. (medium speech, medium charisma, hard intimidation)

- "Where are your supplies?"

- "Where is your ammunition?"

- "Do you have any siege engines?"

- (Change subject)

- "Is Markvart still commanding the troops?"

- Skill check you are most likely to pass. (medium charisma, hard speech, hard intimidation)

- "Will Markvart survive?"

- "Where did von Bergow go?"

### Start the raid

Now it's time to head up to the battlements and begin the raid.

You’ll need a ranged weapon and some ammunition. Talk to Captain Frenzl and he’ll give you 30 piercing ammo for whichever type of bow you prefer and let you know the stores are running low. You can then speak to the nearby blacksmith and he’ll ask you to find 10 pieces of scrap metal around Suchdol that he can use to make more ammunition.

At the stables next to the smithy, you’ll find a couple of Old horseshoes, a Bag of nails, and a Broken pickaxe. In the inner stables, you’ll find more horseshoes, another bag of nails, and Rusty shackles. That should be enough for the blacksmith, return to him and hand them over for some reputation and an increase to your ammunition stock.

### Cover the raiders

Next, make sure you have a ranged weapon equipped and head to the battlements where Capon is waiting. If you need extra ammunition, there's also a barrel right behind Capon with arrows inside it.

Talk to Capon, who will go over the plan one last time, and then the raid will begin. It is best to use a bow as opposed to a crossbow for the faster rate of fire. You’ll have to take out as many of the attackers as possible, all your allies will be carrying torches to mark them. It is possible for all of them but Dry Devil, Kubyenka, and Sam to die, so you may want to replay this section in that case. There is an autosave when the raid begins.

Once the raid is finished, you can ask Dry Devil a few questions about how everything went, then head back into the castle to give Zizka your report.

He’ll then send you to bed which will conclude the quest, starting Hunger and Despair.

## Beyond the Grave

Beyond the Grave is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. You can talk to Rat in The Hole in the Wall tavern after completing Feast for the Poor to begin.

## Description

Rat needs to get the seal of a dead mine owner from his grave in Sedletz for the Guild.

## Walkthrough

After talking to Rat, head over to Sedletz Monastery and into the ossuary and into the crypt in the middle. The wall you are looking for is to the south of where you can fall into the ossuary from the trap door, next to a pillar, it has some differently colored bricks similar to other walls you can break down. Pull it down and vault inside. The seal is missing, so the gravedigger most likely took it if the empty bottles of brandy strewn about are any indication.

Head to the gravedigger’s house, north of the monastery. You can talk to the gravedigger and ask him about the tomb but all it will do is result in a loss of reputation as he refuses to speak on it. The easiest way to get what you need to go by at night.

The gravedigger keeps the seal on his person so you will need to pickpocket it from him. If you pickpocket the seal from the gravedigger before talking to him, you can confront him about robbing the tomb, but not reporting him for it, this will gain you reputation instead of a loss, and you will keep the seal.

Once you have it, return to the Hole and give the seal to Rat, ending the quest.

## Bird of Prey

Bird of Prey is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

Once Vostatek is home and feeling better, talk to him the next day. He’ll tell you about nearby poachers causing trouble. If you agree to help, you’ll need to track them down.

### Rocktower Poacher

The first poacher is at a path intersection on a hillside north-west of Rocktower Pond. He claims he’s poaching to feed his family. You can ask him about his situation and the ambush he witnessed (the same one you were caught in at the start of the game.) After talking, you can either arrest him or ask what he thinks you should do.

Arresting him will gain reputation with Vostatek. Letting him go will have him mark deer hunting spots on your map. If you use a Speech check, you can convince him to stop poaching. You’ll lose some reputation with Vostatek.

After dealing with him, return to Vostatek and report back.

### Vidlak Poacher

Vostatek will tell you about another poacher hiding north of Vidlak Pond. To gather more information, you can speak to the fisherman's wife and the tanner, who live just west of Vostatek’s house near the bridge.

The tanner explains that people suspect him due to all the hides and carcasses he has, but he insists he’s running an honest business selling hides to Troskowitz. He also mentions a clearing near some deer where the poacher might be.

The fisherman & his wife suspect the tanner but also mention a path behind their house that leads into the forest, marked by Pagan idols. This path leads to Witch’s Copse, a place people fear, and it could be where the poacher is hiding.

Follow the path behind the fisherman’s house, guided by the Pagan idols. You’ll first reach a deer clearing—keep following the idols north. Deep in the forest, you’ll find the poacher’s camp and the poacher himself. This poacher is much more aggressive than the first.

You can use Speech or Dread skills to calm him down, but unless your stats are 15+, he will attack.

If he attacks, you can kill him in combat or knock him out in unarmed combat, then wake him up and send him to the bailiff to be hanged.

If you succeed in the skill check, you can resolve the situation peacefully.

Return to Vostatek, who will be pleased with how you handled the poacher. While your job for him is done, he suggests visiting Varel, who may have more work for you.

Vidlak Poacher Camp Location

### Varel

After you've helped out Vostatek as much as you can with hunting down poachers in his area, he'll direct you to talk to Varel at Nebakov Mill and the gamekeeper responsible for the eastern side of the Trosky region.

Varel will be happy for the assistance, and will first direct you to a poacher in the Slatego forests. He can also suggest you talk to the gravedigger, Ignatius, if he might have seen anything as well.

### Slatego poacher

If you talk to the gravedigger, he'll point to you a path you can try behind the cemetery going into the woods. This path in question would take you straight to the body. Otherwise, if you want to loot around and learn a bit more, head to the unfinished cottage that Varel mentioned. Here you can find a chest that includes a map of game in the area. In particular, note the wolf indication. From here, head to the southwest to find the poacher's camp with nobody around except a wolf.

Around the bed, loot the sack for a knife and then have Mutt track it. He'll eventually lead you to the same path Ignatius noted, where it's discovered the poacher was killed by wolves. You'll have to chase or kill off the remaining ones so you can then loot his body for his knife as proof. Head back to Varel to let him know what happened and he'll then ask if you want to continue. If so, his next request is about a poacher in Lower Semine.

### Lower Semine poacher

If you're already familiar with The Lair, Bonnie can be talked to if she's seen the poachers. This will drastically narrow down the area to search, though it's still a sizeable chunk. The camp in question is almost directly south-southwest from The Lair. As you start to search this area, you'll likely be spotted by at least one of the bandits before you find the actual camp. For the evidence, there's a gutted deer near a large hole in the ground a bit to the northeast of the camp. At the camp itself, three's the hanging carcass and the skin next to the stack of logs.

You won't be able to talk the poachers into being turned in, so you'll have to go about killing instead if you want to do the optional task here. There are 3 bandits, but note one may run off from the area, making it difficult to find them. In such cases, you can wait an hour or so there and they should re-appear at the camp. As proof they're dead, make sure to also loot the Lower Semine poacher's kit off them (usually on the well-armed bandit). Head back to let Varel know you found the camp and, if you killed them off, he'll be glad he won't have to send Bailiff Thrush after them. You can then ask about the ghost poacher.

### Kopanina poacher

If you've completed the quest For Whom the Bell Tolls, this part will be skipped. Otherwise, Varel will explain this particular poacher is very different from the rest: he's a great marksman, but he's very sloppy at cutting up game. He's also clever, having taken to poaching in an ambiguous area that neither gamekeeper knows who's actually responsible for patrolling, making it the least patrolled area. Like the other poachers, Varel will note if you find him, he's to be sent off to the gallows like the rest, or killed if he won't go peacefully.

While the region to search is very large, it's actually closer to the road here, below some rock cliffs (roughly east-northeast of Barnaby's hut). When you find it though, you instead find Hans Capon. Apparently he's taken to poaching to make money, believing he'd be forgiven for his crimes as it was an exceptional situation. You can inquire a bit with him, but he'll only reveal he's been working with a trader in Troskowitz. Eventually, you'll have to figure out what to tell Varel, and Hans will give an excuse, but with a hard speech check, you can try to convince him that won't be enough: he has to stop, otherwise it'll be clear you didn't take care of the poacher. If successful, he'll reluctantly agree. Regardless, he'll give you his poaching kit to help convince the gamekeeper you dealt with the poacher.

Go back to Varel and lie to him about the situation. Note while you can try and tell him the truth, he won't believe you as it sounds so absurd, so just lie instead. Varel, now glad the poachers are dealt with, will reward you with a mix of potions, food, kits, and 80 groschen.

## Objectives

- Ask Varel the gamekeeper about work.

- Find out the truth about the poacher in the Slatego forests.

- Ask the gravedigger about poachers. (Optional)

- Tell Varel about the poacher from Slatego.

- Find the poacher in the Lower Semine forests.

- Ask around in The Lair about poachers. (Optional)

- Find evidence of poaching the camp. (0/3)

- Wipe out the poaching bandits. (Optional)

- Report the Lower Semine camp to the Gamekeeper.

- Find out about poaching in the Kopanina forests.

- Tell Varel about the Kopanina poacher.

## Black

Black is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Black worked as a soldier in the service of Sigismund of Luxembourg. He started a relationship with a woman from Miskowitz called Victoria, though he was not very interested in something serious or long-term.

Victoria fell pregnant and tried to harm herself to end the pregnancy, but was not successful. Henry came to Sigismund's camp to try and find her where he met Black.

Black was in the infirmary due to an upset stomach which was caused by slight poisoning after eating the wrong kind of mushrooms. Henry was able to help him, and Black told him about his relationship with Victoria and the nearby clearing where they used to meet.

Depending on Henry's actions, Black may have chosen to take responsibility for Victoria and their child, allowing them to stay with him at the camp.

## Black Bartosch

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Titles are worthless. A man should earn a name for himself. It's not enough to be born with a silver spoon in your mouth.

Sir Bartoschek of Drahonitz (Czech: Bartošek z Drahonic), also known as Black Bartosch (Czech: Černý Bartoš), is a young knight in the service of Lord Otto von Bergow, acting as his personal bodyguard. He also serves as the swordmaster and combat instructor of the Trosky Castle garrison.

His historical counterpart is Bartholomaeus of Drahonice, a Czech knight, an active participant and a chronicler of the Hussite Wars.

## Biography

### Early life

Bartosch hails from a noble family that traditionally held estates in the Karlstein region. Despite his father's lifelong service to Emperor Charles IV, the family remained neither prominent nor wealthy. Nevertheless, they enrolled Bartosch at the University of Prague; however, he devoted more time to martial pursuits than academic study. When financial constraints forced his departure from university, he "had to do what he does best" and became a mercenary.

Over the subsequent five years, he traveled extensively, training in fencing under renowned swordsmen. He later joined the garrison at Prague's Royal Castle, where victories in two major tournaments brought him to von Bergow's attention. The Royal Chamberlain soon appointed him as his personal bodyguard.

### Involvement

He repaid von Bergow's favor soon after: on the road to Trosky, he saved his life during an ambush orchestrated by Jan Zizka. This allowed von Bergow to reach the castle just in time to prevent Hans Capon's execution. While von Bergow recovered from the wounds sustained in the ambush, Bartosch was stationed at the Trosky garrison as a combat trainer, usually found near the castle's arena.

Before the assault on Nebakov Fortress, von Bergow entrusted Bartosch with the protection of Hans Capon. Amidst the ensuing chaos, Bartosch became separated and was captured alongside another knight, Hermann Littlehead, by Zizka's forces. He later appears to have been freed through the combined efforts of von Bergow and Markvart von Aulitz.

### Related quests

- For Victory!

- The Finger of God

## Historical counterpart

The character is based loosely on a real Bohemian knight and chronicler of the Hussite Wars. A supporter of King Sigismund, he served on the Catholic side in various garrisons before retiring from military service due to illness. He is chiefly remembered for his Latin chronicle, one of the few contemporary accounts of the conflict written by a participant.

Bartholomaeus of Drahonice [Bartošek, Bartossius] ca 1380/1390-1443. Bohemia. Soldier; author of Latin chronicle of the Hussite revolution. Born to a family of lower noblemen. As adherent of Sigismund of Luxembourg during the Hussite revolution he fought on the Catholic side as a member of the garrison of Prague Castle, then of Karlstein.

In 1426 he contracted an eye disease and left military service. His only work is a chronicle of the war years 1419-43, written after 1426, possibly in Karlstein. In 85 manuscript folios he described the war events from the military and economic point of view. The rough text written in bad Latin is valuable for its relatively objective information drawn from his own experience and that of other soldiers.
— Entry from Encyclopedia of the Medieval Chronicle

## Black Horse Tavern

Black Horse Tavern is an inn in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is located in Kuttenberg.

## Description

The inn for the Striped Tonies miners. An average inn, it has a large yard out back where most of the patrons spend their time. The Tonies have an intense rivalry with one of the other nearby mining taverns and their patrons, the All Saints. They have no rooms for rent, but they do have a musician play from time to time.

## Blacksmith's Commission

Blacksmith's Commission is a repeatable task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It becomes available after Henry is fully integrated into the blacksmiths' guild. Most of the tasks involve crafting a specific weapon or performing a quick task for someone around town involving your smithing skills.

## Repeatable Task

### Description

The good people of Kuttenberg and its surroundings have started coming to me to have things forged.

### Walkthrough

Forge whatever item is requested and deliver it to the commissioner. If you are fast enough at forging they may still be in your yard, saving you a trip. In order to satisfy your customer, make sure you give them something of high quality, gold or higher. Sometimes Magdalena will offer these to you directly as well.

If you do not already have the recipe for the requested item, the game will tell you to check with Master Bushek to buy it.

Each day the item requested will rotate from a large list of either swords or axes. After a certain number of completed commissions, they will start routing to Magdalena with the same general story of a wife looking for a blade for her husband who travels with merchants for work.

### Objectives

## Blacksmith's Commission - Forging for an Admirer

### Description

A strange fellow reeking of fish came to me, asking that I show him how to smith.

### Walkthrough

He wants you to make him any sword, short or long; he just wants to watch.

### Objectives

## Blacksmith's Commission - Forging for an Admirer while Drunk

### Description

That odd fisherman who took a shine to my forging and pretended to be my apprentice has visited me again. This time he's been egging me on to show him how I can forge while drunk.

### Walkthrough

He wants you to make any kind of axe. He will provide you with the drink, so as soon as you accept you'll be quite intoxicated.

### Objectives

## Blacksmith's Commission - Legendary Weapons

### Description

A mysterious street vendor approached me with an irresistible offer: a sketch of a legendary sword.

### Walkthrough

Horst of Lishkau will appear up to four times to offer weapons of questionable quality. In the first encounter, he'll offer you the plans to craft a legendary sword, which you can purchase for 600 , but after you forge it, it will turn out to be a fake called Fakescalibur, and he'll give you the money back. In the second encounter, he'll sell you the plans for a fake Durendal called Durendull; this time, he won't have money to compensate you for the disappointing result, but he'll offer you the third weapon free instead. In the third encounter, he'll give you the plans for the powerful Longsword of the Four Evangelists. In the fourth and final encounter, which will only appear if you have a Dragon claw in your inventory from the side quest Dragon's Lair, he'll offer you the plans for the Dragon fang Axe.

### Objectives

## Blacksmith's Commission - Tooth Pulling

### Description

A distraught woman came to me, saying her husband's tooth was causing him dreadful pain and he was too frightened to visit the barber-surgeon. She asked if I, as a blacksmith, would pull it out for him, and I decided to give it a try.

### Walkthrough

Accept the commission and go to the marker. You'll find the wretch up a ladder in the barn. He'll startle and run, chase after him. If you lose him, you'll find him standing in a yard just around the corner from where you started.

Call to him and he'll engage in combat. Beat him unarmed and you'll knock his tooth out. He'll thank you and head on home. Note: sometimes this may cause guards to react as if you’ve committed assault, so be prepared to deal with them.

Afterwards, just head back to the wife and talk to her, she'll thank you for your duty, give you your pay and offer to tell the city about your skill.

### Objectives

## Blacksmith's Commission - Swords for the Guards

### Description

The captain of the Kuttenberg guard asked me to sharpen their dulled swords.

### Walkthrough

The location of the key on the city map (red dot) and in the street (bright spot on the ground).

Go to the town hall cells and talk to the guard. He will tell you that someone who certainly wasn't him lost the key to the chest that holds the swords you're meant to sharpen on the way home from the All Saints Tavern the night before. You can get a Disgusting rag from him to give to Mutt to smell.

You can simply unlock the chest to move forward, but the guard would really rather you get the key; after all, what good is a chest you can't lock? You can give the rag to Mutt and he'll search, but the key you are looking for is in an alley near the north edge of the search radius next to some broken pottery and suspicious stains.

Return to the town hall and open the chest, with the key or by lockpicking. Take the swords from inside and sharpen them. You can do so one by one at a grindstone or by using a blacksmith's kit - the kit will cost 153.3 to sharpen all of them.

Once they are sharpened, talk to the guard and let him know. He'll give you 100 groschen for the job and an extra 50 should you return the key.

### Objectives

## Blacksmith's wife Martha

Blacksmith's wife Martha is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Martha lived in Miskowitz and was married to the blacksmith, Marosh. She met Henry when he visited and asked him to forge horseshoes for soldiers at Sigismund's camp, as her husband refused to work with them.

After he had done so, she requested he give them to Victoria whom she usually had deliver things. Martha was upset to hear that Victoria seemed to have been hurt and was nowhere to be found. She suggested that Farmer Kuba may have had a hand in it, but he turned out to be innocent.

If convinced, Victoria may have returned to Miskowitz and come to live with Martha and her family.

## Blazhena

Blazhena is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Blazhena was a maid working in the granges of the Sedletz Monastery. She roomed with her friend Valerie and was known for her good nature and humour. Because of these qualities, Jaroslav from the monastery invited her to join him and a couple of other monks in writing a book about laughter, inspired by Decameron, in the secret scriptorium in the monastery cellars. While others (namely her roommate Valerie and Monk Celestine) have misinterpreted the interactions between Jaroslav and Blazhena as romantic, Blazhena was simply wanted in the scriptorium for her insight and humour.

One night, she caught her boss, Steward Zdenyek, watering down the monastery wine, which he was doing to make a profit and pay off his debts. Afraid that Bozhena might rat him out, Zdenyek started spreading rumors that she was stealing and asking her coworkers whether they had noticed anything suspicious about her lately. Since she had falled ill with the mysterious illness by the time and couldn't defend herself, this was viewed negatively by the other maids. Zdenyek went as far as going through Blazhena's things (possibly to plant evidence in her chest), finding her key for getting into the monastery cellars in the process.

Despite care provided in the infirmary, Blazhena eventually succumbed to her illness and died.

In the good ending of the DLC, Henry can support Jaroslav's decision to continue writing the book as a way of keeping the memory of Blazhena alive.

### Associated quests

- Anamnesis

## Body armour/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Body armour is one of the armour types that Henry can equip in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

There are five main categories of body armour: Plate, Chainmail, Coats, Gambesons, and Tunics.

There are also two additional categories: Belts and Pouches for quick access to consumables and weapons without using the inventory.

Each category has a dedicated inventory slot, except gambesons and tunics, which occupy the same slot and cannot be worn simultaneously.

## Overview

Plate

The outermost defensive layer, the primary form of protective gear in the game. Plate armour must be worn over a gambeson. It delivers the highest defense against damage, though it is costly, heavy, and loud.

Chainmail

A mid-layer protection garment of interlinked metal rings, usually covering the torso and arms. Worn over the gambeson but beneath plate armour.

Coats

Outer garments such as decorated surcoats and waffenrocks. Coats do not add much protection, but they add charisma bonus. They can be worn over any other type of body armour or on their own.

Gambesons & Tunics

The innermost layer of body armour, occupying the same inventory slot. Gambesons are quilted jackets that provide modest standalone protection and serve as a required base layer for plate armour. Tunics, on the other hand, are lighter cloth garments with little protective value.

Belts

A belt is used to hold weapons, which are then much easier and faster to access. Of course, the amount of things that can be attached to the belt is limited.

Pouches

A pouch can be worn on the belt and usually hold small items such as food, bandages or potions, which are then more quickly available when one wants to use them.

## Bohemia

The Kingdom of Bohemia was a country in central Europe and an electorate of the Holy Roman Empire. In the 15th century, Lands of the Bohemian Crown primarily consisted of the Kingdom of Bohemia, the Margraviate of Moravia, the duchies of Silesia, the Margraviates of Upper and Lower Lusatia, Upper Palatinate and Margraviate of Brandenburg.

It was a landlocked kingdom located southeast of Germany, southwest of Poland, and north of Austria and Hungary. Bohemia together with Moravia and part of Silesia forms the modern day country of Czech Republic.

The events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance take place in a small portion of this land. The accessible area of the game is located in regions between Sasau and Rattay, southeast of Prague.

## History

### House of Luxembourg

The kingdom was established by the Přemyslid dynasty in the 12th century by the Duchy of Bohemia. In 1310 the Luxembourg dynasty began its rule of the kingdom of Bohemia. In 1355 Charles of Luxembourg, the king of Bohemia, became Holy Roman emperor as Charles IV. He strengthened the power and prestige of the Bohemian kingdom. His reign is considered the Golden Age of Czech history. Charles VI is remembered for founding the University of Prague (1348) and for greatly increasing the boundaries and importance of Prague, which he made the capital of the empire. From that time on Prague was a principal center of intellectual and artistic activity in central Europe.

Charles died in 1378, and the Bohemian crown went to his son, Wenceslas IV. He had also been elected King of the Romans in 1376. He was deposed from the Imperial throne in 1400, however, having never been crowned Emperor. His half-brother, Sigismund of Luxembourg, was eventually crowned Emperor in Rome in 1433, ruling until 1437, and he was the last male member of the House of Luxemburg.

### Hussite movement

During the reign of Wenceslaus IV, Bohemia fell victim to disputes between Roman Catholics and the followers of the Bohemian religious reformer Jan Hus, who was burned as a heretic in 1415. Hus's death sparked the Hussite Wars, decades of religious warfare.

Sigismund and the Catholic Church responded to the events with five crusades from 1420 to 1431. However, all these attempts were repelled by the Hussite troops, led by Jan Zizka. Riots broke out in Prague. Hussite Czechs and Catholic Germans turned on each other; many were massacred, and many German survivors fled or were exiled to the rest of the Holy Roman Empire. Wars ravaged the kingdom until compacts were negotiated in 1436 that granted the more-moderate Hussites (known as Utraquists) some degree of religious freedom and reduced the power of the Roman Catholic Church there.

## Economy

Bohemia was among the first countries in Europe to become industrialized. Mining of tin and silver began in Ore mountains in early 12th century. The German hospes had a major role in the industrial development of the kingdom. In the late 12th and in the 13th century the Přemyslid rulers promoted the colonization of certain areas of their lands by German settlers from the adjacent lands of Bavaria, Franconia, Upper Saxony and Austria.

The new settlers not only brought their customs and language with them, but also new technical skills and equipment that were adapted within a few decades, especially in agriculture and crafts. They settled mostly the hills and mountains and started the mine works and high qualities industry such as metal works, weapon industry and beer making. Forest glass production was a common industry for German Bohemians

## Territories

Lands of the Bohemian Crown, also referred to as the Lands of the Crown of Saint Wenceslaus, were a collection of territories bound by feudal ties and subject to the rulers of Bohemia. They did not form a personal union or a confederation, and apart from sharing a common monarch, they had no unified governmental institutions.

The concept of the "Bohemian Crown" was introduced by King Charles IV on 7 April 1348. It referred to the lands inherited from his father, John of Luxembourg: Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia, Egerland, Upper Lusatia, and several fiefs in German territories. In 1370, Charles added Upper Palatinate and Lower Lusatia. According to an imperial decree, the Lands of the Bohemian Crown were to remain an indivisible entity even if the House of Luxembourg were to become extinct.

From the 16th century onward, the Lands of the Bohemian Crown passed into the hands of the Habsburgs and became part of their hereditary domains.

In 1742, following the First Silesian War, Empress Maria Theresa was forced to cede Silesia to Prussia.

In 1918, after the dissolution of Austria-Hungary, Poland annexed the Cieszyn (Těšín) region. The remaining former Bohemian Crown lands that were still under Austro-Hungarian control became part of the newly formed Czechoslovakia.

## Bohemian Graffitti

Bohemian Graffitti is an achievement introduced in Brushes with Death.

## Description

You painted every type of shield.

## Acquisition

You can acquire the Bohemian Graffitti achievement after unlocking the Shield painting mechanic by rescuing Voyta. Namely after returning him his paintbrushes during A Sketchy Situation quest he offer to paint your shields free of charge.

## Tips

- For the achievement you need to paint every kind of shield as follows: Knight, Heater, Pavese and Round/Cuman shield.

- The Cuman shield can be found during random encounters or in Sigismund's camp, while the rest can be purchased in Kuttenberg.

- A kite-type shield is not required for the achievement.

## Bohemian Sniper

Bohemian Sniper is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You killed an enemy with a crossbow shot to the head at long range.

## Acquisition

The Bohemian Sniper achievement is earned by landing a long-range (approximately 30 meters) headshot on an enemy using a crossbow.

A reliable target is Handsome Charlie, a bounty from Gules available in Semine. Around dusk, Charlie can be found sitting alone at the southwest corner of his camp. At this time, other NPCs are usually asleep, and Charlie remains stationary.

Position yourself in the shrubs on the east side of the road, far enough that Charlie appears very small. Save your game before attempting the shot. Aim near his legs to line up the headshot; the bolt should take him down cleanly.

## Tips

- For this achievement you will need a crossbow with high enough damage. The recommended crossbows are:

- Field crossbow: It can be found in the Buried stash west of Pschitoky in central Kuttenberg region. It deals 350 damage and has a faster reload time compared to heavier crossbows.

- Reinforced heavy crossbow: Deals higher damage of 550 points but has a slower reload. It is located in the Abandoned shepherd's dugout southwest of the Devil's Den.

- Decorated field crossbow: Sold by Master Wenceslas in southeastern Kuttenberg, one of the best all around crossbows in the game but it is expensive.

- To make things easier, down a Bowman's Brew beforehand and level up your Marksmanship skill.

- Some long-distance crossbow bolts, like Sharpshooter's bolt or Marksman's bolt, could come in handy.

## Bohemians Rise Up!

Bohemians Rise Up! is an achievement in the Brushes with Death the expansion.

## Description

You were ahead of your time and created the foundations for the state emblem of Bohemia.

## Acquisition

For this achievement you need to paint three Knight shields with the crests of different Crown Lands that make up the Kingdom of Bohemia.

The achievement cannot be unlocked until the Portrait in Red side quest and the Judgement Day main quest have been completed, as the required shield designs only become available afterward.

## Tips

From left to right in the painting menu:

- Bohemia: Barry Indented → Gules → Gules → Historical → Lion Argent

- Moravia: Per Fess → Azure → Azure → Historical → Moravian Eagle

- Silesia: Per Fess → Or → Or → Historical → Eagle Sable

This achievement can be finicky, you may need to try replacing one of the Gules with Bordeaux or Carnation until it registers as complete.

## Bohush

Bohush is a villager from Semine and is involved with Marika in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

After nomads settled into the nearby area, Bohush met Marika, one of the Voivode's children, and soon started courting her, despite his mother's protests, who claimed her son must have been hexed and would never have gotten involved with a nomad otherwise. When things started to get serious, the voivode sent a message to Semine that Bohush should marry Marika or pay. However, this message arrived while Bohush was out with Marika so his mother responded with insults.

Bohush soon learned of this, but got caught up in an escalating conflict where Marika's brothers, Tibor and Gejza, had come to confront the villagers to avenge their family's honour. Unfortunately, things took a turn for the worse when they ran into some woodcutters and Bohush was stabbed, Gejza was killed, and Tibor was taken captive.

Marika managed to find her boyfriend and quickly took him to a hiding spot in Apollonia to recover, though she was limited by what she could gather in the area.

If Miri Fajta is completed and Marika's given the amulet:

Clever like her father though, when Henry found Marika and Bohush and offered to assist, Marika eventually proposed her idea: for Henry to wager the letter against her father's amulet. If Henry won, then the voivode would have to come see her and hand it over to her himself. Henry did so, winning the bet and, as promised, her father met her in the cave with the still recovering Bohush. As they talked, Marika noted the amulet wasn't just for her, but for her and Bohush, to save his life, revealing her plan all along: by saving someone's life as per their custom, they'd become part of the family as well. Realizing the clever plan his daughter just pulled off, the voivode laughed over how she had outwitted him. He then apologized for his earlier, stubborn behaviour and welcomed Marika and Bohush back to the camp.

At the Nomads' camp, Marika's mother, Aranka, provided more healing care to Bohush so that in a few weeks, he'd be back to normal. For her part, Bohush's mother also finally accepted that her son was in love with a nomad.

### Associated quest

- Miri Fajta

## Bolek

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Bolek is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered multiple times throughout his ultimately unsuccessful search for the Holy Grail.

## Biography

The villager named Bolek can be encountered digging at a crossroads in the Trosky region. When questioned, he will tell Henry that he searches for the Holy Grail, believing himself to be on a mission for God after receiving a poem which indicates its location. As with other similar encounters, Henry can ask to see the poem. Unfortunately, the poem is actually just lewd verses, which Henry can comment on. Determined to continue, Bolek is not discouraged and Henry can either point him in the direction of millers or a monastery.

Depending on which suggestion Henry makes, the next time he encounters Bolek he's "disguised" in either a monks habit or in miller clothes. Either way, he will regale Henry with a tale of his unsuccessful quest for information about the grail. Henry can then give him further advice on infiltrating whichever source of information wasn't suggested previously. When Henry next comes across Bolek, the man will be wearing the other disguise and will again have a story about his failure to find more clues about the Grail.

On Henry's final encounter with him, Bolek will be disguised as a miner. When asked about his appearance, he explains that he believes something valuable may be hidden within one of the mines around the Kuttenberg area, and that posing as a miner will help him search without drawing attention. By this point, however, he has abandoned his search for the Grail, believing that quest to be hopeless. Instead, he is now pursuing rumors of a hidden treasure. When questioned about how he learned of it, he reveals that he obtained the information from a knight whom he defeated in a game of dice. Having nothing else left to wager after losing, the knight staked the information itself.
