## Bonnie

Bonnie is one of Miller Kreyzl's hired hands in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Bonnie originally started out in a convent to become a nun, but after realizing she didn't want to give up certain pleasures like alcohol and men, she soon went off to do her own thing, eventually finding she was quite good as a thief. She started working for Kreyzl and became one of his most reliable workers, and probably one of the few that could understand and put up with the miller when he went off on his ideas. She was known to have a soft spot for animals, and had a dog of her own, Sniffer, until he died recently from health complications.

When she was sent on a job with Zinek in Troskowitz, things went wrong and Zinek was taken and thrown in jail for a time. Afraid the guards might have also seen her, she hurried back to the mill and laid low at The Lair. After Zinek was freed, he likewise hid out at the storehouse to keep a low profile, but much to Bonnie's annoyance with all his talking.

If Forbidden Fruit is done:

She soon met Henry, who'd been sent by Kreyzl to ask her about a vital component Kreyzl needed a lot of: saltpetre. Bonnie eventually revealed that the gravedigger, Ignatius, would know where a pit would be, but they couldn't exactly let the gravedigger in on what they needed it for.

If you let her keep the dog:

Bonnie soon learned that on a local farm there was a dog, Monarch, that was being abused by its owner. She in turn set out to retrieve the dog for herself and give it a better home. While in the middle of this process though, Henry found her and informed her the neighbours had secretly requested to Ignatius that the dog be killed as it was a nuisance to them. However, this put them in a conundrum as they still needed the saltpetre location.

Bonnie pleaded with him to let her keep the dog and lie to the gravedigger, and Henry agreed, not wishing to kill it. Glad to have a new dog, Bonnie thanked Henry for his compassion and quickly took the dog with her.

If you turn her in to the Troskowitz bailiff:

Bonnie, Zinek and Miller Kreyzl end up being executed by hanging. Bailiff decides to leave them swinging from the rafters in their own Lair.

### Associated Quests

- Forbidden Fruit

- Opus Magnum

## Booze stash

Booze stash is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. There are five booze stashes around Vidlak forest.

## Description

Gamekeeper Vostatek is no stranger to a bit of drink. As such, along with his shallow graves, he’s stashed alcohol in various places around the woods under his purview. This way, even if his wife or son take whatever he has at home, there’s always more somewhere.

## Locations

Listed below are all booze stash locations in order from north-east to south-west.

### Stone Niche

In a little niche in the stone north-west of Tachov.

Loot

- Schnapps

- Mead

- Strong Saviour Schnapps

### Wolf den

Next to a wolf hunting spot, south-west of the Dug-up corpse. Vostatek has hidden the booze on top of the rocks, a few bottles of fallen to the ground. To get to the stash, approach from the south-east.

Loot

- Drinking water

- Mead

- Wine

- Saviour Schnapps x2

At bottom of rocks

- Strong Saviour Schnapps x2

### Fallen tree rest

South-west of the niche stash, near a fork in the road is a fallen tree where Vostatek has set up a little sleeping spot.

Loot

- Bacon

- Saviour Schnapps

- Strong Saviour Schnapps

### Forest watch

North north-east of the gamekeeper's cabin, east of the Vidlak Pond travel point. On top of some rocks is another stash.

Loot

- Mead

- Schnapps x2

- Saviour Schnapps

### Vidlak Pond lookout

South of the gamekeeper's cabin, near the road around the pond, on the cliff under a tree overlooking the pond. A bench has been set up overlooking the water.

Loot

- Drinking water

- Schnapps x2

- Strong Saviour Schnapps

## Bozhena's hut

Bozhena's hut is a humble wooden cottage located just west of Zhelejov near a small pond and meadow. It is home to the elderly herbwoman, and her daughter Pavlena.

## Description

The hut is tucked away along a winding forest path, southwest of the main road leading toward Trosky Castle, and is surrounded by dense woodland and medicinal plants.

The structure itself is modest - a wooden building with a thatched roof and a small herb garden nearby. Inside, the hut contains an alchemy bench, shelves lined with dried herbs, and a simple bed. Above the main room is the loft, accessible by a ladder near the hearth.

### Related quests

- Fortuna

- Bad Blood

- Miri Fajta

## Loot

- Marksman's kit and Tailor's kit — Found in Bozhena's loft up the stairs, along with a few piercing arrows.

- Bandage — Found on a shelf in the side room near where Bozhena is caring for Hans.

- Marigold, Comfrey, and St. John's wort — You can gather several bundles from the herb garden outside.

## Broken wagon

Broken wagon is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The roads of Trosky are treacherous. It may not be uncommon to find broken wagons on even the most easy of roads but the beautiful cliffs of Trosky present an elevated risk to travellers.

Over the side of a drop between Semine and its mill, one such example can be found. It’s clear the wagon broke long ago, as it is half-eaten by grass and leaves. There are signs that it was attacked when it fell of the cliff. Its various goods have been strewn about down the side of the hill and next to it lies a locked chest holding the only goods that survived.

Side note: In close vicinity to the broken wagon more than 40 Belladonna and more than 80 Herb Paris can be gathered.

## Loot

- Silver cross with insignia

- Fine wine x6

- Perch x12

- Prayer to Saint Wenceslas

## Brother Morticius

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Brother Morticius is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Brother Morticius lived and worked at Sedletz Monastery as the keeper of the mortuary and ossuary.

Brother Morticius was a blind monk who spoke in rhyme and asked Henry to help clean the monastery's ossuary by gathering and tidying the bones there into three pyramids. When Henry finished this work, Brother Morticius was nowhere to be found.

The gravedigger then mentioned to Henry that Brother Morticius had been dead for years.

Brother Morticius could then later be found in Miskowitz where he revealed he wasn't really Morticius but his grandson - a poet and wayfarer. He claimed that his grandfather must have been so bored keeping the ossuary that he stepped out and had a bunch of children all over the region. Monks didn't tend to have much to leave to their offspring, but his grandson had his old habit, something he used to have a bit of fun from time to time.

As his promised reward, the not Brother Morticius offered to teach Henry about poetry.

### Associated quests

- Thou art but dust...

## Brunswick's dagger

Brunswick's dagger is a stealth-specific melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, included as part of The Lion's Crest DLC pack.

## Description

A dagger worthy of a true knight. Its shape is perfectly suited to cut right into a gap between armour.

## Acquisition

Brunswick's dagger can be is obtained as part of the DLC's treasure hunt quest. The riddle told by Scribe Gaibl in Troskowitz points to the Chapel in the rocks, located in the forest north of Trosky Castle. You find the dagger inside a chest buried beneath the stone cross.

## Trivia

- This is the so-called bollock dagger. The name is derived from the phallic shape of the hilt (the two lobes of the guard combined with the shape of the grip) and the 14th century warrior's propensity for wearing the dagger directly in front of the girdle.

- Another term, coined by Victorian-era historians in an apparent effort to downplay the sexual connotation of the dagger's form, is the kidney dagger.

- The dagger first started appearing on continental effigies around 1300–1350, and has one of the longest usage periods of any of the five main types of medieval daggers.

## Brushes with Death

Brushes with Death is the first major story expansion for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Announced on 16 January 2025 alongside two other expansions, Legacy of the Forge and Mysteria Ecclesiae, it was released on 15 May 2025 for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. It is included in both the Expansion Pass and the Gold Edition.

The Brushes with Death DLC introduces a new quest chain, centered on Master Voyta, an eccentric artist that can be found in the Trosky region. To start the questline, you must first complete the main quest For Whom the Bell Tolls and gain access to Trosky Castle.

## Description

Help a mysterious artist uncover his enigmatic past and unleash your creativity in shield painting. Henry encounters a quirky painter, who draws him into a web of intricate plans, pushing his skills to its limit in finding solutions.

In a series of quests - spanning both maps of the Kingdom Come: Deliverance II world - Henry must find, persuade (and sometimes eliminate), a host of familiar and unfamiliar characters to help his new friend complete the most important painting of his life. Discover the answers to the many questions that surround this mysterious character. Who and what is he? How does he know so much? And why does he carry around a painted human skull?

In addition to new quests, Henry can also gain brand-new shield designs for his work, with over 100 unique designs and colour combinations to choose from.

## Features

- A new storyline taking place in both the Trosky and Kuttenberg regions.

- The option to create your own unique designs on any shield you choose.

- New unique weapons and armour related to the mysterious painter's story.

## Quests

- A Sketchy Situation

- Source of Inspiration

- Chiaroscuro

- Portrait in Red

- The Night-Mare

- Stained Honour

- Man Proposes

- God Disposes

- Root of Evil

- Unveiling

## Buresh of Krakovitz

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Master Buresh of Krakovitz is a nobleman from Moravia and the owner of a smelting operation in Grund.

## Biography

Buresh worked with Mint Master Ulrich Vavak to operate a large silver siphoning scheme. He directed his underling, Volkmar to intimidate Foreman Fett from the Horschan mine to continue the work, skimming ore off the top and cooking the books to make it appear like less ore was coming to the smelter than actually was.

This ore would be smelted with the rest, then diverted again to a secret mint in an old mined-out shaft not far from Grund. At the secret mint, using legitimate dies, Buresh oversaw the minting of new groschen to go right into the conspirators' pockets. This scheme was discovered when Henry came to investigate on behalf of Christian of Pisek in an effort to gain the help of Kunzlin Ruthard in rescuing Hans Capon from Ruthard's old estate, Maleshov.

Buresh tried to bribe Henry to keep the secret safe, fleeing if the offer was rejected. He may have kept the work going under Christian later, merely changing who was pulling the strings.

## Burgrave Hashek of Kozle

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Hashek of Kozle is a burgrave in the service of Otto von Bergow in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Hashek is von Bergow's right hand man, being in charge of Trosky Castle's garrison and helping to enforce his lord's orders as necessary in the Trosky region. He was travelling with von Bergow and their men, including von Bergow's page, Albert, when they were suddenly attacked by a large group of bandits. The bandits ruthlessly cut down everyone, including maids that were part of the caravan and Albert as he tried to protect his liege. Hashek managed to pull together the remaining men and von Bergow, but the bandits, realizing their surprise advantage was gone now, fled. Hashek and the rest managed to find a straggler, who tried to hide in the woods due to an injured leg. Taking him prisoner, the group headed back to Trosky Castle to interrogate him.

However, interrogations were considered unclean work, and as such, only executioners could do such. Having no executioner at the castle though, Hashek and his men simply tried to beat information out of the prisoner, but with no luck.

If Olda's name is revealed in Necessary Evil:

After learning of Olda's involvement in the ambush, on von Bergow's orders, Hashek gathered his men and set out for Semine to confront and arrest Olda Semine. On arrival, Jan Semine refused to hand over his son and tried to plea with Hashek to let his son live. However, Hashek, wanting revenge for what happened to his people, refused any such request and demanded Jan hand over Olda now or blood would be shed.

If one sides with Semine:

Hashek and his men were killed off by Semine and his guards with the help of Henry and Hans. Realizing von Bergow would likewise kill them if he learned the truth, Henry and Hans lied and told the lord that Hashek fell while heroically covering their retreat.

If one sides with Hashek:

Hashek and his men, with the help of Henry and Hans, cut down all of Semine's guards. Hashek then ordered everyone in the keep to be killed, while he let Jan stay alive just long enough so he could watch as his son killed before him. The burgrave then sent Henry to find Olda. However, having a feeling Henry might not be so keen to turn in Olda, secretly followed him as he went to find their target.

If Olda is turned in:

Hashek made his presence known, approving of the fact that Henry was standing firm and arresting Olda. However, still set on revenge, Hashek went against his lord's orders and killed Olda instead.

If Olda is allowed to leave:

Hashek made his presence known and forced Henry to duel him to the death over trying to let Olda escape. Having no choice, Henry killed Hashek and then the rest of his men so von Bergow wouldn't learn of the truth. Realizing von Bergow would likewise kill Henry and Hans if he learned of this, Henry and Hans lied and told the lord that Hashek fell while heroically covering their retreat.

### Associated quests

- Necessary Evil

## Burnt down camp

For the location in the Kuttenberg region, see Burnt down camp (Kuttenberg).

Burnt down camp is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

### Description

The ruined campsite is located south of Tachov village, a short distance from the road. From the looks of it, this was once the resting place of a musician, or perhaps an entire troupe, judging by the scorched remains of various instruments scattered about. Among the debris, you can spot the charred frames of a couple of lutes, a flute, a horn, and a battered tambourine.

A little downslope from the main camp lies the blackened corpse of a man, with a flute jammed down his throat and a hunting horn stuck where no horn should be.

## Loot

|

Around the camp:

- Apple

- Burgher's hat

- Onion × 3

- Smoked cheese

- Smoked chicken

- Smoked hare meat

- Wine

In the burlap sack:

- Common bolt × 12

- Copper × 2

- Fastening material × 3

- Wolf fangs

## Burnt down camp (Kuttenberg)

For the location in the Trosky region, see Burnt down camp.

Burnt down camp (Kuttenberg) is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

## Description

A poacher's camp, now ash and ruin. It was destroyed along with the rest of the forest in a fire. Smoke still smoulders in its fire pit. The poacher himself seems to have fled in an attempt to wait out the fire, but was ultimately unsuccessful. His corpse can be found at the Burnt down trap.

## Loot

- Hunting cap

- Cooked apple x4

- Cooked cabbage x4

- Cooked garlic x4

## Butcher (Pschitoky)

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Butcher is a unnamed minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

He lived and worked in Pschitoky as a butcher alongside his wife Eva.

One night, his wife went home with a man called Adder whom the butcher assumed must have seduced her. He rallied a few other townspeople to capture Adder and attempt to hang him from a tree outside the town. Henry interrupted their lynching and saved Adder.

The butcher may then have been killed either by Henry or by Adder. He may also have returned home, shaken.

### Associated Quest

- The Devil's Pack

## Butcher Bashka

Aye, I saw you, but I ain't bothered, you know. You didn't rob me, because if you did I'd cut your thieving hands off on the spot!

Butcher Bashka (Czech: Řezník Baška) is Troskowitz resident meatman. He lives on the edge of the village with his wife Milena.

Besides legitimate trade, he acts as a fence for local poachers.

## Involvement

When Henry and Capon part ways after their stint in the pillory, Bashka can be asked about Capon's whereabouts. He is cagey about it and avoids giving a straight answer. It seems he has already had some dealings with him, likely related to Capon's poaching, as he remarks that Capon is no fool and will find Henry himself if he wants to see him.

Another hint that he is selling the poached game comes from Tailor Bartoshek. Bashka ordered from him a jacket fit for a king, even though he is not even attending the upcoming wedding at Semine.

When Herbwoman Bozhena's daughter Pavlena goes missing, he is one of the few Troskowitz residents who can be asked about it. Although he responds in his usual cagey manner, this time it seems he is telling the truth and genuinely knows nothing about her disappearance.

## Butcher's wife Eva

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Butcher's wife Eva is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Eva lived and worked in Pschitoky alongside her husband, the butcher.

Her husband was often cruel to her even going so far as to hit her from time to time and jealously guard her. One night, she returned home from the tavern with a man called Adder who was well-known as a seducer. She claimed that Adder had been too drunk and nothing happened between them, but her husband could not be convinced. He rallied a few of the local men and took Adder out of town.

Eva told Henry this when he arrived in Pschitoky looking for Adder.

## Bylany

Bylany is a village located south-west of Kuttenberg.

## Codex entry

A settlement 1.5 km southwest of Kuttenberg built along Bylanka creek.

According to archaeological findings, the history of the local settlement dates back to the New Stone Age (about 4,000 BC). The first written mention of the village is from 1143, when Miroslav of Zimburg donated it to the Sedletz Monastery. The village later passed from the monastery into private hands and often changed owners.

Near the village is the Spring of St Adalbert (pramen sv. Vojtěcha), which supplied the whole of Kuttenberg through wooden pipes, starting in the Middle Ages.

To this day, massive slag heaps lie in the village along the Bylanka creek. These are remnants of medieval mining, when surplus and waste material from nearby mines was deposited here.

## Bynyek

Bynyek is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Bynyek was the elder and de facto leader of the village of Bohunowitz. He lived there alongside his daughter, Sovka.

Bohunowitz was often accosted by Sigismund's soldiers who were stationed nearby at Opatowitz and Sigismund's camp. He was required, along with his neighbours, to prepare food to be requisitioned for use by the soldiers on pain of death and destruction.

To avoid starving to death, Bynyek stashed some valuables in a nearby plague grave.

One day, a couple of soldiers came to the village as an advance party to warn them that the larger force was coming for their supplies. The villagers were fed up with their poor treatment and one of them, Vitek, led an attack on the two soldiers, killing them and becoming heavily injured himself. The villagers then hid the bodies and hoped for the best.

When the soldiers led by Captain Puta arrived for the supplies, Bynyek spoke with Henry as the village's voice. Above all, he wanted his village's continued survival.

If conflict broke out between the soldiers and the villagers, Bynyek fought valiantly.

### Associated Quest

- Spoils of War

## Cabbage cave

Cabbage cave is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The small cavern nestled in the rocks of the Trosky region is located along a winding path south of the Lower Semine Mill, near the middle of the southern lake.

The cave entrance is marked by a trail of discarded cabbage heads leading off the forest road into a rocky outcrop. Right outside there's a wooden cart overflowing with stolen cabbage.

The cave's interior is dim, illuminated by a single lantern. Inside, there's a makeshift fermentation workspace where Pepa, the cabbage thief, crafts his signature sauerkraut.

## Calvaria axe

Calvaria axe is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It was introduced in the Legacy of the Forge expansion and can be crafted.

## Description

A light, well-forged battle axe on a long haft, shaped after the weapons used by Turkish riders. The axe head is fitted with a wide edge for smashing enemy skulls, which is where its Latin name originates. On the field of Kosovo, it is said, the heathens stacked two towers of Christian heads, between which the victorious Sultan's army marched for a whole day.

## Acquisition

Can be crafted, the sketch can be found during the quests Sinners of Kuttenberg and In the Service of the Guild.

## Camp by the road

Camp by the road is a type of encampment in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. They are spread around along the side of various roads in both the Trosky region and the Kuttenberg region.

A Camp by the road will be indicated on the map by the icon.

## Description

Camps along the side of the road where various wayfarers will set up for the day or night. Many of those who camp there are friendly and open to speaking with strangers about who they are, where they came from, and where they are going. Many will also be open to buying and selling goods, playing dice, sparring, or having a shooting competition.

Occasionally less friendly bandits will camp in the same locations, warning those who might ride by to keep walking lest things turn violent.

## Canker

Canker is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Canker was a member of Gules's gang in the Trosky region. He was called Canker because of his rotten attitude and general unpleasantness. His mode of operations was to dress up as a travelling monk and place himself by the side of the road with his men hidden in the woods to attack travellers as they stopped and offered him some alms.

He was killed by Henry as part of his efforts to help Gules rid the world of his former compatriots.

## Canny Shooter

Canny Shooter is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You won the miners' competition on the highest difficulty.

## Acquisition

The Canny Shooter is unlocked by participating in any Popinjay archery contest on the highest difficulty setting.

## Tips

- Although the achievement description states that it must be completed during the miners' archery competition (presumably as part of a side quest), it actually unlocks during a standard Popinjay contest found throughout the Kuttenberg region.

- Ironically, winning the miners' archery competition does not appear to unlock the achievement.

- You can unlock the achievement even when some shots miss the target, as long as all 11 birds are hit in total between both participants and you are in the lead.

Gnarly is the Semine captain in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

Gnarly has been a soldier for Semine since he was young. While starting out as a soldier, he always had a gnarly club with him, refusing to use anything else. This in turn caused Jan Semine's grandfather to nickname him Gnarly and it stuck ever since.

## Captain Puta

Captain Puta is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Puta was a soldier in the service of Sigismund in the Kuttenberg region.

Part of his responsibilities was to requisition supplies from nearby villages, namely, Bohunowitz. The villagers were required to prepare supplies for the soldiers, but Puta thought they were hiding resources to try and trick him.

On one such excursion, he brought along Henry and had him take charge gathering supplies and looking for hidden stashes. After returning with the supplies, he turned in those necessary for survival and sold the rest for a profit.

He had not much sympathy for the plight of the villagers, not hesitating to slaughter them all if he found out they had killed a couple of soldiers earlier or if they refused to hand over sufficient supplies. He could also have been killed in turn, if the villagers revolted.

### Associated quests

- Spoils of War

## Captain Thomas

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Captain Thomas is in charge of Lord Otto von Bergow's security in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

While on an expedition to rout some bandits that had been active in the region, Thomas and his group came across Henry, Sir Hans Capon and their retinue who had just arrived from Rattay to deliver a letter to the lord of Trosky Castle.

Thomas was sceptical as to their identities and their motive in being in the area, as they were ostensibly on opposite sides of the ongoing greater conflict between supporters of King Sigismund and those of King Wenceslas IV. He looked over the letter they carried and advised them to make camp, as the castle would be closing without him or von Bergow being present.

Thomas was then gravely injured in an ensuing skirmish with the bandits and was moved to the chapel at the top of Trosky castle, as the physician was absent as well. He had a terrible fever and was given up for gone; however, Henry was able to help him recover. Thomas was able to leave the tower with the help of Henry and his sister Adela so that he could vouch for Capon's identity and save him from hanging.

Although Thomas was not taken as a credible witness due to his delirium, Capon would be saved when von Bergow arrived moments later, himself having had a run-in with the bandits.

Thomas was later able to return to his regular duties.

### Associated Quests

- Easy Riders

- For Whom the Bell Tolls

## Cardinal Pozzo

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Cardinal Pozzo is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Cardinal Pozzo was sent from Rome to Kuttenberg as a papal legate to adjudicate the dispute between the Sedletz Monastery and the Brotherhood of Corpus Cristi. With his retinue, he lodged at the vineyard north of Kuttenberg, where he was ambushed by the members of the Devil's Pack who wanted to convince him - by force, if neccesary - to help them infiltrate the Italian Court.

One of his bodyguards however managed to stab Kubyenka with a knife, causing enough distraction to help the legate escape. In the following pursuit, Cardinal Pozzo fell off his horse and was then inadvertedly killed when Adder headbutted him to the ground and he bumped his head on a rock.

Godwin then posed as him for the meeting of the disputing church factions at the Italian Court.

### Associated quests

- Oratores

- The Italian Job (posed as)

## Carrot on a Stick

Carrot on a Stick is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

Stanislav is a shepherd that needs help with a ram that ran off into the woods when wolves appeared, instead of to safety with the rest of the sheep. However, said ram will only follow with a carrot, which he'll give you.

If you already assisted Siegfried during Mutt, you'll likely recognize this as being Ignatius. If Ignatius died in the Mutt quest, it is named Ernie instead. Head out to the spot to the east to find him, safe and sound. You'll need to then lead him back to the sheep pen, but wolves will try to attack as you take him home. If you only manage to scare them off, they'll periodically continue to stalk and eventually attack while you make your way back.

Back at the pen, lead Ignatius into the pen, then go let Stanislav know he's safely back.

## Casper (quest)

For the bandit see Casper

Casper is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

A few days after completing Johnny the Gob, Gules has left the toughest for last: a bandit named Casper.

## Description

## Walkthrough

Gules will warn you the reason he left Casper for last: he's even made Gules wary of him in the past with how tough he is, and even has some scars from Casper's ring when Casper would pick fights. He's also learned Casper has setup camp in the very rocky region of Apollonia, making any approach difficult.

Casper's camp is in the northern part of Apollonia, with quite a few bandits roaming around. If you want to take a stealth approach, come here around midnight, when most if not all of them are asleep. With high enough stealth and a dagger, you can quietly go around to each sleeping bandit and kill them quietly. Note there may be one or two patrolling bandits, like one sitting around a fire. These you'll want to take out first as they're more likely to hear/see you if you kill a sleeping bandit nearby. Otherwise, taking a direct confrontation can be risky with the large amount of bandits.

Once they're dead, loot Casper's body for his ring to take back to Gules. If you also want to get at their loot, make sure to get the keys for the two chests in this camp as well.

Head back to Gules who'll be glad it's over with now, though he'll admit there's no going back as he's considered a traitor among any bandits left. He'll also reward you with 95 Groschen. You can also ask to keep the ring or not. After this task is complete, Gules can then become available to teach several skills.

## Objectives

## Cat woman

Cat woman is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Out in the hills of a dried up mine lives a woman who has surrounded herself with only the company of cats. She is wary of strangers, and especially hates dogs, but is not hostile. She simply wants to live her way and not be bothered.

Although willing to tolerate guests, she's not afraid to deal with dogs quite harshly should they come sniffing around.

If you examine the burnt remains of a cottage just to the southeast of the Cat woman's hut, as well as the barn full of cats across the road from her, you'll be able to ask her how the cottage came to be burned down.

## Cave under Trosky

Cave under Trosky is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

There is a Cave in Apollonia that leads deep through the earth underneath Trosky Castle and its environs. Though most of the caves are no more than passageways, one opens up into a large opening. There are carvings on the walls and signs that people have used this spot as a hideaway.

Underneath a treacherous opening in the rock that goes to the surface is a skull lying on top of a key which unlocks a nearby chest in the water.

## Chamberlain Ulrich

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Ulrich von Schaumberg is the chamberlain of Trosky Castle in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

He was left in charge of the castle while Lord Otto von Bergow was away. However, he was still restricted by his role as chamberlain, namely that only the lord could sentence others to death.

With the lord away, and an increasing number of bandit attacks in the area, Ulrich ended up closing off the castle to any visitors unless they were a royal messenger. As such, when two vagrant looking men approached the gate, with one claiming to be a noble and a messenger but missing said message, Ulrich had them turned away.

Following a brawl at Olda Semine's wedding, he almost had Hans Capon executed for poaching but was stopped last second by von Bergow's arrival back at Trosky Castle. With Captain Thomas still being ill, von Bergow gave the command of his force to recapture Nebakov to Ulrich.

On the way there, his force got ambushed and he ended up getting shot by one of Zizka's men, mere seconds after Hans Capon managed to pull him out from under his horse. He is then shot and killed regardless of Capon's aide.

### Associated Quests

- Wedding Crashers

- For Whom the Bells Tolls

- Demons of Trosky

- For Victory!

## Chiaroscuro

Chiaroscuro is the 3rd quest in the Brushes with Death DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Things are never quite black and white with Voyta, but that may just have changed… He’s missing a binder for his paint and has asked me to find him a basilisk egg. Apparently, its yolk has magical properties.

## Synopsis

Voyta has finally decided what he would like Henry’s help with. He takes a swig of his mysterious potion, claiming it is for courage when Henry asks what it is. It turns out Voyta is running out of paint and he wants Henry to find him some ingredients to make more. Not just any ingredients, however, he wants a basilisk egg to use for mixing.

The catch? Basilisks don’t lay their own eggs, they hatch when a toad broods an egg laid by a black cockerel. Voyta has heard a rumour of such a black cockerel in Semine in the yard of a man called Slavek. He suggests Henry head there and ask around. As for toads, there are plenty of them near Zhelejov.

With that information Henry starts his search. In Semine, the farmer Slavek is reluctant to talk about it but, after some convincing, he tells Henry he did in fact have such a cockerel, but since it was such a runt he put it down and took it to the woods. Thankfully, one of its eggs is still intact and Henry is able to continue on to find a place to set it to be brooded.

The toads are plentiful in Zhelejov, as promised, and Henry is able to find a place to put the egg. After waiting a day, Henry goes back to check on the egg and finds it changed.

Voyta is so eager to receive it he neglects to thank Henry properly, though he apologises for that when prompted. He has no coin, but gives Henry a ring of his by way of payment. He also requests privacy for when he cracks open the egg, must to Henry’s regret. He isn’t expecting the paint to have any special qualities, exactly, telling Henry it’s all about the story – having patrons honoured to have such exotic materials used to decorate their walls.

Voyta tells Henry he’d like to leave Trosky but he has something important he must finish first, someone he needs to meet. He asks Henry to meet him the next day when he should be done with mixing the paint.

## Walkthrough

Head over to Trosky Castle and talk to Voyta. He’ll give you your task to find a basilisk egg as well as a hint of where to start your search, Semine and Zhelejov.

Head to Semine, and talk to Slavek. He’ll play dumb, so you’ll have to pass an easy speech, easy domination, or easy coercion check to convince him to talk. He’ll direct you to a waste pile on the edge of the woods. You’ll have to hop over his fence to get there but it’s essentially in a straight line south. There will be a wild dog guarding the area which you’ll have to take out. Once it’s dealt with, look for the cockerel to the right of the entrance facing in; the egg will be just behind it.

Next, go to Zhelejov. Listen for the toads and you’ll find a suitable place for the egg on the east side of the water just below the inn next to a tree.

Now comes the hard part, waiting. It will take 24 hours before the objective updates, but proximity will be a factor as well. The easiest way to ensure the toads do their thing is to leave the area completely and do other tasks until it updates. If you have nothing else to do, be sure to go at least as far as the inn and then wait for the duration of the time. Sleeping may not move time forward as you’d expect. One Henry remarks enough time has passed, head back to the nest to pick up the basilisk egg.

All that’s left is to return to Voyta and give it to him to end the quest.

## Christian of Pisek

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

If there's one thing I've learnt about silver, it's that it's got one special property - it never stinks!

Christian of Pisek (Czech: Kristián z Písku) is the steward of the royal mint in the Italian Court and the main ally in Henry's investigation against the mint master - Ulrich Vavak.

Christian is a brother of the former mint master and lord of Suchdol, Peter of Pisek.

## Biography

In his quest to free Hans Capon, Henry's path led to an investigation into Ulrich Vavak's scheme to steal and counterfeit the king's silver. He was aided by Christian of Pisek, Vavak's direct subordinate. Christian wanted the Mint Master office for himself, but Vavak secured it first thanks to his connection with King Sigismund. As a result, Christian had a personal interest in seeing the investigation succeed.

He and Sir Kunzlin Ruthard started the investigation but it was left to Henry to carry it through. With the password provided by Ruthard - "via argentum" - Henry proved his allegiance and Christian shared what little he had uncovered so far. Though his findings were limited, he promised Henry his full support, laid out a plan for further investigation, and provided a letter of safe conduct to access the mines.

Later Henry and Christian discussed the outcome of his investigation among the miners and it became apparent the trail of stolen silver lead to the smelting operation in Grund. Christian wrote a letter to the smelter's owner Buresh of Krakovitz, introducing Henry as a wealthy nobleman interested in starting his own smelter. He also advised Henry on how best to approach the cautious Buresh.

After uncovering the criminal network the Royal Mint Master has created, through which he diverted a part of the royal share to the secret mint, Henry returned with the evidence to Christian. The steward was astonished by the audacity of the scheme and proposed that they continue to make use of it. Everything would stay the same only there would be a change in the management. Henry could choose to accept or refuse the offer.

If Henry accepts the offer:

With the mutually beneficial arrangement agreed upon, Henry became several hundred groschen richer and gained an influential ally.

If Henry refuses the offer:

Christian cursed Henry, and they parted on rather bitter terms.

## Associated quests

- Via Argentum

- Oratores

- The Italian Job

## Christopher Oderin

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Christopher Oderin is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

### Early Life

Christopher was the second son born to Martin Oderin, after his older brother Godwin. Godwin was much older and left the household before Christopher was born, leaving in his wake nothing but stories and expectations.

Godwin was not considered by his father to be a good son, so Christopher not only had to hear of all his brothers misdoings but had to rise above them in his father's eyes - a tall task, as his father was not easily impressed.

### Involvement

Christopher was present at his home during the meeting of Wenceslas IV supporters at Raborsch. As Godwin was there as well, Christopher took the opportunity to challenge his older brother to a duel for their father's honour.

Later during the evening, Otto von Bergow and his men attacked Raborsch where Christopher was targeted. If saved, he was gravely injured and brought to Suchdol to recover. Upon recovering, he left with his father and the other assembled lords for Podebrady to send word to Jobst of Moravia that Jan Zizka's group had been successful in stealing Sigismund's silver from the Italian Court.

### Associated quests

- The King's Gambit

- The Feast

- Civitas Pragensis (dependent)

## Civic Duty

Civic Duty is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is mutually exclusive with The Spark.

## Description

To follow the law, or break it?

## Walkthrough

Once you have started Feast for the Poor, talk to Bailiff Andreas Plümel and report the Guild to him. He will ask you to keep tabs on them and report to him intermittently.

After each Guild quest, you can report to him their movements and earn 30 groschen per tip. The final report you can make is during The Spark at which point the two quests become mutually exclusive.

If you’d like to complete Civic Duty, complete The Spark up until you are meant to bring the black powder to the mine. Upon delivery, instead of going in, run away. This will fail The Spark but allow you to report to the bailiff one final time that the Guild has been dealt with, netting you a final reward of 150 groschen. Later, when passing by the Kuttenberg gallows, you can see that Rat, Chenyek and 2 other Guild members were swiftly hanged.

## Civitas Pragensis

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Civitas Pragensis is the 26th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically at the conclusion of The Italian Job.

## Description

Sigismund has pulled out of the country and is heading back to Hungary. The theft of the silver from the Italian Court turned out to be the last straw. This is a victory worth celebrating!

## Walkthrough

Talk to Zizka, then head down to send the former hostage lords and Rosa off. As you go, you can check in with Janosh and Dry Devil who is sitting with Katherine, Samuel, and Peter of Pisek. With them, you can toast to your victory and talk a little about their future plans.

Once done in the inner bailey, you can head out to see the lords off. You can talk to most of the people assembled getting ready to leave for Podiebrad, saving Kunzlin Ruthard for last as speaking to him will trigger their departure.

As they leave, Kubyenka will appear having been freed by Erik to send a challenge to Henry. You can then choose whether to accept it or not. You can ask your comrades of their opinions regarding whether you should accept or not as well. Duelling Erik is optional. If you would like to skip it, you can decline, which will trigger the end of the quest and the immediate start of the next, So it begins...

### Duel Erik

If accepting, prepare yourself for battle and talk to Zizka and the guard to be let out of Suchdol. Erik is a difficult enemy, however, you have an opportunity at the start of the duel to pass a medium coercion check and lower his stats a little by taking Zizka’s advice and provoking him.

Once the duel is complete, the same cutscene from if you declined it will play and the quest will end, starting the next, So it begins....

## Codex entry: Jitka of Kunstadt

This article is about the Codex entry. For the character, see Jitka of Kunstadt.

Main

Localization

Jitka of Kunstadt is a Characters codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Trivia

- The betrothal of heirs of Kunštát to the heirs of Lipá followed a long tradition. The man who arranges the marriage in the game, Boček II of Poděbrad, was himself married to Anna Eliška of Lipá, a daughter of Jan Ptáček's guardian Jindřich of Lipá. And their grandson, Jiří of Poděbrad, the later Bohemian King, would marry his son Viktorin to Markéta Ptáček, Hynce Ptáček's daughter and Jan's granddaughter.

- There could be multiple reasons for Jitka receiving a dowry from Jan Ptáček in 1408: Dowries could be regathered with the husband's death or the dissolution of the marriage, or in such cases where the husband had been found guilty of mismanaging it. The most probable explanation, however, might be that dowries were often paid on credit and therefore received in the form of instalments over several years. So Jan Ptáček might just have taken some time to pay off his.

## Codex entry: Murals

Main

Localization

Murals is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

A large part of the population was illiterate during the Middle Ages. Therefore, art was a tool for education and communication among different layers of society. For this reason, preserved works of art are among the best sources of information about the medieval period. Wall paintings, whether sacred or profane, often reveal very detailed information about the lives of our ancestors.

While religious paintings focused primarily on spreading piety and humility towards God, secular painting represented cultural and historical moments of local history. Among the most popular motifs were allegorical scenes from the Bible, images of court life or knightly legends, and we also encounter portraits of saints (mostly patrons of the given communities) or significant clergy. The paintings also include events such as the founding of buildings, coronations of rulers, or the granting of city rights.

Figures were most often depicted in contemporary or slightly archaized clothing, even if the scenes depicted were perhaps hundreds of years old. The depicted architecture typically contains characteristic Romanesque or Gothic elements and is enriched with a number of symbolic floral and animal motifs.

Large-scale murals often came into being with the contribution of multiple artists, whose styles were visibly inspired by the works of contemporary masters of this or that region, as evidenced by similarities in themes, as well as the composition or colorfulness of the paintings.

## Codex entry: Noble Marriages

Main

Localization

Noble Marriages is a Society codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Trivia

- Marriages were, in most cases, no contracts made between two loving individuals, but between families and lineages, in which each of them hoped for their child to profit from this union as best as possible. After all, "nullum sine dote fiat coniugium", no marriage shall be without a marriage gift, was common medieval (church) law, and so one central part of this reciprocal profit was the dowry.

- Dowries would come in the form of the dos, the dowry itself, typically paid by the bride's family to the spouse, and the donatio propter nuptias (gift on account of marriage), the counter-dowry that the spouse's side gave to the bride. In early medieval times, the sum of both dos and donatio was about equally large, but over time this balance shifted, so that by the 13th century the counter-dowry was would not exceed half or even a quarter of the dowry.

## Codex entry: Old silver mining

Main

Localization

Old silver mining is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

The minerals mined in the Kuttenberg belts, primarily galena, sphalerite, and chalcopyrite, were characterised by a low silver content, making its smelting a rather challenging process.

Work in the smelters was continuous. Furnaces with open spouts for easier handling of metal were used, or more often, those with closed spouts for better temperature regulation. This refinement process was described in great detail, for instance, in Agricola's illustrated work from 1556.

The medieval process of silver extraction consisted of four stages. Almost every step had to be repeated several times to achieve the desired result. The raw material's structure and composition changed from the form of rocks and solidified slag to molten silver with lead impurities and finally to a solid "loaf" of pure silver. The primary goal was to remove unwanted impurities and reduce the ore's weight to a minimum.

The final phase - silver refining through the addition of a specific amount of pure lead and the separation process (cupellation) - was known as far back as antiquity. Silver was melted with lead in a so-called cupellation bowl, where unwanted mixtures of other metals were separated through air oxidation.

## Codex entry: Ore tax

Main

Localization

Ore tax is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

The word urbura comes from the German Urbuhr and means yield or revenue. This term refers to a form of tax, a tribute that miners paid to the monarch in kind, in extracted resources, in exchange for the right to mine metals within the territory of the Kingdom of Bohemia.

According to mining law, it was literally the monarch's share of the profit from metal mining. Urbura was expressed as a portion of the mined metal, which was mostly used for coin production. The collection of urbura was overseen by royal officials known as Urburers. The amount of urbura was determined based on shares and depended on the quantity of ore extracted.

## Codex entry: Popinjay Shoot

Main

Localization

Popinjay Shoot is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

It was a shooting competition to celebrate Pentecost (Whitsun), involving shooting with bows, crossbows, or guns at a live bird tied to a pole, later replaced by a wooden bird. The church criticised this custom and found it offensive because it was held on the feast of the descent of the Holy Spirit, whose symbolic representation in the Holy Trinity is precisely a bird: a dove.

## Codex entry: Ringen

Main

Localization

Ringen is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

A type of unarmed combat known as Ringen (from the German Ring Kunst, meaning art of wrestling) is one of the oldest martial systems widespread in medieval Europe.

In an effort to defeat the opponent, the wrestler did not rely so much on brute strength as on a combat strategy that used the whole body, aiming to throw the opponent off balance and bring him to the ground. Kicks, holds and strikes with fists or the edge of the hand were often aimed at the joints. Attacks on the eyes or finger-breaking were also not uncommon.

Ringen was taught in swordfighting schools, where medieval masters placed great emphasis on comprehensive schooling in combat. One of those who wrote extensively about refining Ringen techniques was Johannes Liechtenauer, the master of one of the most prominent swordfighting schools of the late Middle Ages, located in Nuremberg.

## Codex entry: Silver mining

Main

Localization

Silver mining is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

Silver mining in Kuttenberg (Kutná Hora) began in the late 13th century and reached its peak during the 14th and 15th centuries. Research around the town has identified 14 to 15 previously exploited vein zones.

At various times, there may have been at least 20, but more commonly 50 or even up to 200 independent mines along these zones. Around the year 1400, silver was mainly extracted in four to five mining zones, known as Oselský, Rejzský, Kuklický, Grejfský, and partially Rovenský. The landscape around Kuttenberg was thus intersected by hundreds of mining corridors and typical clearings appeared due to extensive deforesting in the area.

The first independent mine owners, and later the monarch, were unable to ensure the smooth operation of such extensive mines, so parts of them were leased for a share of the extracted ore. Approximately 20 to 30 miners worked in a single mine, while around 700 to 1200 individuals contributed to overall silver production during this period.

In addition to the miners themselves, many other workers processed the ore and performed various support tasks on the surface. This included operating and maintaining mining equipment, arranging material transport, and the work of craftsmen such as potters, charcoal burners, rope-makers and others. Each master of these trades had their assistants. Transporting people and materials to and from the mines required a large number of horse-drawn carts, stabling facilities and, of course, people to care for the animals.

Skeleton in the Tavern is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

Anyone who has ever visited the tavern frequented by Kuttenberg's poor, bearing the unflattering nickname of Hole in the Wall surely noticed a local peculiarity: a skeleton sitting at a table.

We borrowed it from the book Staré / Nové kutnohorské pověsti (Old/New Kuttenberg Tales) by Jitka Jelínková, who wrote that there used to be a gambling house in the Lower Town, where miners would go to drink and gamble. But the miners' wives would not stand for it, so they hatched a secret plan. They bought a skeleton from the executioner's assistant and hung it in the gambling house in the closet where the cards were kept. They hoped this would scare the men and make them give up their habit forever.

But instead, the drunk men pulled the skeleton out of the closet, sat it at a table and began to drink with it. To their dismay, the skeleton came to life as midnight struck and started to actually drink its beer while thrashing the inn.

For our purposes, we have taken the liberty of borrowing the first part of the story.

## Codex entry: Synagogue

Main

Localization

Synagogue is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

The Jewish prayer hall, used for religious services as well as for social and educational gatherings, is known in Hebrew as a "house of prayer" and in Yiddish as a "school." It serves the Jewish community as a center for both spiritual and social life. It is typically oriented towards the east (towards Jerusalem), with the eastern wall housing an ark that contains the Torah scrolls. In the center of the synagogue is a raised platform called the bimah, used for leading prayers and reading from the Torah. In Orthodox communities, there are separate spaces for men and women, but in most Jewish congregations, the space is mixed.

Jews celebrate their holy day on Saturday (Shabbat), but prayers are conducted every day.

One of the oldest Gothic synagogues in Europe is located in Prague (the Old-New Synagogue).

## Codex entry: Thunderstone

Main

Localization

Thunderstone is a General codex entry in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

Numerous folk tales mention the “thunderstone” – an object that supposedly falls to the ground along with lightning during a storm. Sometimes it falls immediately; other times it appears only after seven days, months, or even years. Its size is said to depend on the strength of the lightning, the depth it burrowed into upon impact, and the manner in which it later surfaced.

This led to various popular beliefs about it, which, however, had little basis in reality. In fact, “thunderstone” referred to various prehistoric stone tools or different types of stones notable for their unusual colour, shape, or unique location in the landscape.

The thunderstone was reputedly believed to bring abundant crops and to protect fields from lightning, hail, and pests. One custom stemming from pagan traditions was, for example, placing a thunderstone into seeds at sowing time.

The stone, however, had not only a magical but also a practical function. It was used to mark territorial boundaries and served as a safeguard for clearly defined territory. Sometimes it could even become part of tools or weapons.

## Collapsed mine

Collapsed mine is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A once-used mine collapsed unexpectedly. Not all the miners were lucky enough to escape, one can even be seen in the rubble. Along the bend in the stream near the former opening to the mine is a small campsite and a fish trap.

- Silver nuggets

### In trap

- Perch

- Cheap wine

- Kuttenberg bread

- Nighthawk

## Combat Training I

Combat Training I is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

While the second part of this quest is given by Bara, this one is typically done first on meeting Tomcat.

## Description

Bara the Beggar told me that in the gypsies’ camp by Rocktower Pond, there’s a showman named Tomcat who performs various feats of strength and is even good with weapons. It sounds unlikely, but maybe I could learn something from him.

## Walkthrough

Tomcat is located at the far end from the entrance into the Nomads' Camp, at the fenced fighting ring. You can talk to him about a few things, but when ready, you can ask him to show you a few moves.

## Objectives

---

## Combat Training II

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Combat Training II is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

This quest is given by Bara in Troskowitz if you talk to her about the nomads in the area.

## Walkthrough

Tomcat is located at the far end from the entrance into the Nomads' Camp, at the fenced fighting ring. You can talk to him about a few things, but when ready, you can challenge him to a duel.

After you successfully defeat him, he'll walk you through the tutorial on learning master strike.

## Objectives

- Defeat Tomcat in a duel.

- Learn the master strike from Tomcat.

- Attack Tomcat.

- Counter the attack from below.

- Counter the attack from the side. (0/2)

- Perform a master strike for real. (0/3)

---

## Common longsword

Common longsword is a melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

Note: Common longsword can be crafted.

## Description

The longsword is a perfectly balanced lethal weapon. Its price is not small, because only a master of his craft can forge a thin yet flexible blade! The longsword is not meant for the heat of battle, but for swift swordplay.

## Conciliation cross

Conciliation crosses are similar to shrines, in the respect that Henry can pray at them. Their primary reason is not orientation, but penance for the people who had the crosses erected. Nevertheless, the crosses often served as important landmarks too.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance

- Drahomira has a conciliation cross erected during Restless Spirit

- A cross, presumably for Father Simon's lover, can be seen while looking for him in the forest during A Man of the Cloth

- Many crosses carry the names of Kickstarter backers of the game. Reading 90 names grants you the achievement Pilgrim.

### Codex entry

Conciliation crosses, or merely stones with a cross engraved into the surface, were erected in places where tragic events or important historical events in the life of the community or the country had occurred; they were closely linked to criminal law – a symbol of admission of guilt and a plea for forgiveness. The conciliation cross embodied repentance by the perpetrator of a crime, built at the culprit's expense. In addition, conciliation crosses marked the boundaries of estates and municipalities.

—Codex entry: Conciliation Crosses

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Conciliation crosses appear in the game, but they are not as prevalent nor commonly shown on the map.

### Codex entry

Conciliation crosses, or simply stones with a cross carved into their surface, were erected in places where tragic events or important milestones in the history of a given municipality or country often occurred, and were closely related to criminal law – they were meant to be a symbol of admission of guilt and a plea for forgiveness. A conciliation cross was a penance for a crime committed, erected by the repentant culprit at his own expense. In addition, conciliation crosses also marked the boundaries of estates and communities.

—Codex entry: Conciliation Crosses (KCD2)

## Confessor

Confessor is a hidden achievement introduced in Brushes with Death.

## Description

The painter told you everything.

## Acquisition

The Confessor achievement can be unlocked after finishing two optional quests - Man Proposes and God Disposes.

## Tips

- First you have to finish the Man Proposes quest. After that the next quest will become available.

- Then during the God Disposes quest Voyta will send Henry to visit his old friend's grave. Clean it up, pray for his soul.

- Return and learn the entire story of Voyta's past.

- You do not need to dig up the grave to get the achievement, but doing so will get you extra dialogue.

- If you confront Voyta about what you saw in the grave. It is important to choose the dialogue option that express your Henry's desire to know the truth. The other choice will only make Voyta more upset without prompting him to open up.

## Confessor Stephen

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Confessor Stephen is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Stephen was an older monk who worked at Sedletz Monastery as a confessor. In this role, he received confession from other monks as well as any lay people in the monastery for work.

In this capacity, he received confession from some of the workers who were repairing the floor in the main church of the monastery. The sin confessed was one of thievery, as the workers had broken into the crypt and were robbing the bodies there in search of a man who was said to be buried there with a special relic. The confession came with some goods that had been taken from the dead, which Stephen stored in his cell.

Not long after, Stephen fell ill and was moved to the Monastery infirmary for treatment. Of the three initial patients brought there, Stephen remained lucid the longest. He was able to speak with Henry who was working with Albich of Uniczow in a medical capacity and let him know to look in his room for a clue, though he could not disclose what had been confessed to him.

He also asked if Henry would bring him some fresh flowers, as he loved to have them near by even in good times and did not want to have to smell sickness and medicine. Unfortunately, Stephen was unable to hold out long enough for a treatment and died not long after from the illness.

### Associated Quests

- Anamnesis

## Crime/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Crime plays a central role in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, with the same general consequences for committing crimes, such as killing innocents, stealing, breaking and entering, harming people or domestic animals, or generally being a disturbance to the peace.

Be mindful that villagers are capable of deducing you likely committed a crime if you were seen in the area that the crime happened.

For instance, if you break into someone's home and steal an item, but someone saw you at one point during it, people will realize you likely stole the item in question and they'll report you, even if you ran off. Likewise, if you're not seen at all, it's more unlikely they'll realize it was you, unless a lot of crimes have been committed lately after a stranger (that is, Henry) showed up in the area.

### Stolen goods

Stolen goods can be sold, but only through certain circumstances. For instance, it's very unlikely you'll be able to successfully sell an item you stole in one town to someone in the same town, as they'll likely recognize it as stolen property. Depending on your reputation, the trader might either have the guards called on you, simply refuse to buy it, or will buy it but at a reduced value. Those who don't recognize it as stolen will pay the normal value like if it was a regular, non-stolen item.

### Pillory

If you are known to have committed a crime, the guards will either force you to talk to them, or attack you on sight, depending on the severity. Even if they attack you, you can use the option of talking to them by giving yourself up.

With sufficiently high Dialogue stats, or some perks like Drunken Fool or Fundamentals of Law, you can persuade the guards to simply let you go. However, unlike other speech checks, even the "positive" ones cause a small reputation hit. Alternately, you can accept your punishment.

Depending on the severity of the crime, these are the possible punishments:

- a fine

- the pillory

- a whipping at the whipping post

- branding

- execution by hanging - game over

All the other punishments can be avoided by paying a fine, and it is even possible to get a list of the crimes you are being punished for.

Once you have been branded, any crimes that would have normally resulted in a branding get you executed instead while the debuff Freshly Branded is active. In hardcore mode, this effect of the debuff is permanent.

### Other consequences

Any crimes committed, even if you weren't caught, cause people to be more suspicious. Other NPCs will randomly warn you of the unsafe environment, guards will start harrassing people at the gates, and they are also more likely to randomly search you.

With the perk Criminal Element, you get a permanent +2 bonus on Coercion, Domination and Intimidation if branded. If only Ma saw you now, she probably wouldn't be very happy.

## Crypt

|

That’s one hell of a bloody pit.

|
- Henry's comment

Crypt is a point of interest in Sedletz Monastery in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The crypt beneath the church of Sedletz monastery is reserved for abbots and a handful of older nobles who were buried there long ago. Due to its limited space and capacity for burials some of its former residents were moved to the ossuary or the outer graveyard.

It features high vaulted ceilings with minimal decoration, with alcoves for each coffin. The coffins themselves are engraved often with the name and/or arms of the person inside, along with Latin prayers and the date of their death.

There are plenty of cobwebs and places where water seeps in occasionally. It is not a place that is opened up very often and one section has been completely sealed off. During repairs on the church, the floor gave way and opened into the crypt. Some of the workers took advantage of this, going into the crypt and prying open some of the graves in search of riches.

## Loot

- Torch

- Crypt map

- Filthy parchment from the crypt

## Csaba Molnár

Csaba Molnár is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Csaba serves as a royal jailer for King Sigismund and is recognised as Hungary's strongest man.

He guards the captive lords Kunzlin Ruthard, Martin Oderin and Botschek of Kunstadt at the Italian Court. Csaba cares about their comfort and conveys any concerns they have to his superiors, such as Jerome Naaz.

Csaba bars the doorway to the chamber of King Wenceslas, where the prisoners are being held, when Adder and Janosh Uher try to free them. He shows no fear, being the strongest man in Hungary and claims that even though outnumbered, he would still fancy his chances. However, he is also willing to discuss matters peacefully if necessary.

If Henry is present, Csaba can either be provoked into a fight or calmed into a conversation.

If a fight breaks out, Csaba, though courageous and formidable, will ultimately be defeated. However, if he is persuaded to talk things out, he worries about losing his reputation as the strongest man in Hungary and fears that he might lose his job as a jailer. Still, he considers that at least he would no longer spend his days overseeing prisoners, allowing him to lead a more peaceful life back home with his wife. Csaba promises to delay sending his report about what happened to King Sigismund, who is at Sedletz Monastery, until dawn.

## Associated quest

- The Italian Job

## Cuman Jasak

|

Bad here, but every other place badder.

|
- Jasak on life in Sigidmun'd Camp

Cuman Jasak is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be first encountered along with Vasko's Cumans and later on his own at Sigismund's Camp.

## Biography

Jasak was part of Vasko's band of Cumans who deserted Sigismund's army and camped close to the Nomads' camp near Semine. Unlike Vasko, he didn't speak any Czech at the time, and had to rely on Henry's help with talking to one of the bathmaids he was interested in.

However, as he had nowhere to go after deserting and struggled on his own in Bohemia, he eventually concluded that he'd be better off returning to the army and parted ways with Vasko. The Cuman leader, Chertan, had him punished by caning, which Jasak gladly accepted as it was a low price to pay for the previous desertion.

## Cumans

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Cumans (Kunok in Hungarian) were a Turkic nomadic people who hailed from the Pontic-Eurasian Steppe and later the Kingdom of Hungary. Serving the Hungarian crown as mercenaries the Cumans were key participants in King Sigismunds Invasion of Bohemia from 1402 to 1403.

## History

Prior to their settlement in Hungary the ancestors of the Cumans lived further east in the Pontic-Caspian steppes. Known as the Cuman-Kipchak Federation. It was a tribal polity comprised of 16 tribal groupings organised in a decentralised pan steppe federation. Each tribal grouping answered to a Khan who was a hereditary ruler from one of the Cuman noble houses.

They eked out a simple semi-nomadic lifestyle on the vast wilderness rearing large herds of Sheep, goats and cattle for sustenance and trade with their neighbours the Kievan Rus and Hungary. They also practiced routine border raids into these neighbouring lands to secure plunder, livestock and slaves.

Their frequent border raiding and fearsome combat prowess earned them a reputation as demons and heathens by the christian peoples they menaced. Despite their reputation the Cuman-Kipchaks were highly sought after mercenaries by Kieven and Hungarian rulers, for their battlefield skill as pathfinders and light cavalry. Conversly the Cuman-Kipchaks were considerably cheaper to hire than other mercenary forces. Rather than demanding large sums of coin for their services. The Cuman-Kipchaks were more than happy to plunder what they needed as payment. Though this often resulted in brutal scenes of slaughter, rape and pillaging wherever they went. Further contributing to their reputation in Europe as a savage heathen horde.

Eventually the Cuman-Kipchak federation met its end at the hands of an even more fearsome adversary. In 1237 the Mongol Empire arrived in Eastern Europe and systemically destroyed the Cuman-Kipchak federation.

Fearing for the survival of his people Khan Köten organised a vast refugee train of 7 tribes and fled across the Carpathian Mountains and further into Eastern Europe. In 1239 after two years of migration the fleeing Cumans arrived at the borders of the Kingdom of Hungary. The ruler of Hungary at the time King Bela IV admitted the Cumans into his realm and settled them in the Great Hungarian Plain. In exchange for their asylum in Hungary Khan Köten and other Cuman tribal leaders signed the Royal Charter of 1239 which decreed that the Cumans would recognise the authority of the Hungarian Crown, convert to Christianity and when called upon serve the King of Hungary during wartime.

## Invasion of Bohemia 1402 - 1403

When King Sigismund of Luxembourg invaded Bohemia in 1402 following the deposition and abduction of his half brother King Wenceslas IV he brought with him a force of Cumans to serve as his vanguard.

As Sigismund marched across Bohemia seeking to put down the rebellion instigated by the abduction of their King. He unleashed the Cumans upon the land and gave them free rein to attack and plunder the estates of lords loyal to his half brother Wenceslas.

Across Bohemia the Cumans embarked on a campaign of rampaging and pillaging, sowing discord and chaos wherever they went. Their brutality and battlefield terror proved to be a double edged sword for Sigismund. On the one hand his Cumans successfully tied down the Loyalist Lords seeking to oust him from the kingdom and on the other the rampant devastation left in their wake served to demonise Sigismund in the eyes of the Czech people whom increasingly came to view him as a foreign conquerer seeking to control and plunder Bohemia for his own ends.

In march of 1403 King Sigismund launched a suprise raid on the town of Stříbrná Skalice also known as Silver Skalitz. The town was held by the Royal Hetman of King Wenceslas, Sir Racek Kobyla whom was a staunch supporter of the deposed king and contributed great funds to the Loyalist Resistance seeking to force Sigismund out of Bohemia. The raid was lead by a vanguard a Cuman horsemen who breached the town walls and promptly instigated a sack of Skalitz. Massacring the towns inhabitants and setting many buildings ablaze in the process.

However the Cumans failed to breach Skalitz Fortress and settled in for a siege intending to starve Racek and his garrison out. Thankfully for the besieged defenders a storm rolled in during the night forcing the Cuman besiegers to retreat to their tents and wait out the torrent. This break in the siege enabled Racek and his garrison to mount a nighttime escape to the nearby stronghold of Rataje nad Sázavou or Rattay on Sasau.

Throughout the remainder of Sigismunds campaign in Bohemia the Cumans were deployed as scouts and light cavalry. Ordered to conduct lightning raids on estates and settlements resisting Sigismund. However as Sigismunds foothold in Bohemia began to falter coupled with news of a rebellion lead by Ladislaus of Naples fomenting back in Hungary, Sigismund was now firmly on the backfoot. By July of 1403 Sigismund withdrew from Bohemia taking his Cumans along with him. Though many returned to Hungary to aid their king in putting down the rebellion, some bands of Cumans remained behind in Bohemia to continue marauding, primarily motivated to procure as much plunder before returning back to Hungary. Anti marauder operations in Bohemia continued well into December of 1403, by then the last of the Cuman bands had either been destroyed or slinked back over the border into Hungary.

## Events of Kingdom Come Deliverance

Sack of Skalitz - March 1403

The Cumans make their first appearance during the prologue of Kingdom Come Deliverance, where they appear outside the walls of Silver Skalitz accompanying King Sigismunds army. Lead by Markvart Von Aulitz the Cumans surge into Skalitz easily overcoming the towns defences and begin Sacking Skalitz. During the chaos of the raid Henry witnesses the deaths of both his mother and father. Watching as Markvart Von Aulitz slashes his father Martin from behind while leaving his mother to be butchered by the Cumans.

Henry is forced to flee Skalitz and get to Talmberg in order to warn them of the attack. Before he departs Skalitz he saves Theresa the Mill Wench from a group of Cumans attempting to violate her, before stealing a horse and riding towards Talmberg. Hot on his heels are a group of Cumans who ride after him shooting arrows as they do so. Henry narrowly makes it to Talmberg as the Cumans close in behind him however they are repelled by the Talmberg garrison and are forced to retreat.

Battle of Pribyslavitz - May 1403

## Equipment

As a population primarily devoted to cavalry attacks, Cumans are usually equipped with very light, colourful and comfortable clothes. They also wear Lamellar armours and bizarre pointed helmets. In battle they often used scimitars, bows, and circular wooden or metal shields.

### Weapons

The main weapons of the Cumans were the recurved and, later, the composite bow (worn on the hip with the quiver), the javelin, curved swords, mace, and heavy spears for lancing. Due to European influence, some of the later period Cumans wielded war hammers and axes.

- Common sabre

- Cuman bow

- Cuman metal shield

- Nicopolis sabre

- Wooden Cuman shield

### Armour

For defence they used a round or almond shaped shield, short sleeved mail armour, consisting of commonly alternating butted and riveted rows, Lamellar armour (iron or leather), leather cuirass, shoulder spaulders, conical or dome shaped iron helmet with a detachable iron or bronze anthropomorphic face plate (gold for princes and khans), and at times a camail suspended from the helmet, consisting of chain or leather. The armour was strengthened by leather or felt discs that were attached to the chest and back. The items suspended from the belts were a bow case with bow, a quiver, and a knife.

## Curiosity Killed the Cat

Curiosity Killed the Cat is a hidden achievement introduced in Brushes with Death.

## Description

If you hadn't poked around, Libor wouldn't be swinging.

## Acquisition

The Curiosity Killed the Cat achievement is unlocked during the Man Proposes quest. You need to reforge the madman's sword from the dugout and then convince him to keep it.

## Tips

- During the quest when the madman calms down a bit you'll have an opportunity to question him. After that he'll give you the Madman's broken sword.

- Reforge it (repairing it with the blacksmith's kit doesn't count) and return to the dugout. Convince the madman to keep the sword by picking the dialogue option with the skill check.

- Leave the dugout, wait at least 24 hours, and return. The deed will be done. Now reload and keep the sword, you monster.

- It is important to note that if you tell Voyta about his friend’s fate, you will not be able to start the God Disposes quest. This will lock the Confessor and Rest in One Piece achievements.

## Damsel in Distress (KCD2 quest)

Damsel in Distress is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It unlocks after the main quest Via Argentum and can be tipped from the baker in Bylany.

## Description

The old miller locked his wife in a shed and apparently went to fetch an axe. It’s time to teach him a lesson in manners!

## Walkthrough

Head to the Rabstein mill, as you approach you’ll hear a woman calling for help from inside the shed. Unlock the door and talk to her and she’ll tell you her husband has been treating her increasingly poorly of late, escalating to locking her in the shed and going to fetch an axe. She wants you to help protect her.

She will direct you to the woodshed back behind the mill. Head over there and look around, but no one is there. Run back to the shed to find the miller and a guard dumbfounded at how the woman got away. It turns out the woman was lying, rather than his wife, she was a thief.

They blame Henry for letting her get away. You’ll have to pass either a hard speech, domination, or intimidation check or else pay a 500 groschen fine. Once that’s done the quest will end.
