## Dancing with the Devil

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Dancing with the Devil is the 23rd main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. You can start it at any time after finishing The Lion's Den by speaking with Zizka at Devil's Den.

## Description

After lengthy preparations, the time has come to show Otto von Bergow that he's not untouchable, even behind the walls of his Maleshov Castle.

## Walkthrough

### Get ready

As the objective suggests, make sure you are ready to fight. Once you talk to Zizka and confirm you are ready, there will be combat with no way to replenish supplies. When you are ready, talk to Zizka and let him know you are ready.

He’ll then invite you to a meeting in the evening to discuss the plan in detail. You’ll have one last chance to stock up here as you have the choice to wait with him until evening or come back, depending on the time of day. In the evening, Zizka will go over the plan.

After a cutscene, you’ll have the opportunity to choose whether to go with Dry Devil’s plan to burn Maleshov and take no prisoners or to go against it. The main gameplay difference in both routes is the number of defenders in the fortress once you break in. It will also affect NPCs’ conversations with Henry and his ensuing nightmare.

### The Town

Burn Maleshov

Agree to burn the village or else lose to Dry Devil and the group will set the fires. Head into the fray and kill the villagers who have not fled. Any cowering villagers can be told to run into the woods.

Once the village is cleared, talk to Zizka, then wait for the soldiers to come out from the fortress to check on the town. Defeat them, then talk to Zizka again to get your next orders. From this point, the objectives align, get into the fortress.

Save Maleshov

If you would like to leave Maleshov in one piece, during the conversation, choose to say you don’t want the village burnt, your family died in such an attack, and you’ll duel the Devil for it. This will initiate combat, you have to win the duel to avoid torching the village.

Infiltrate the fortress

Afterwards, you’ll have to sneak over the walls of the fortress and open the gate for the others. Janosh will carry the ladder, follow the group and you’ll be directed to go over first.

Note: Successfully infiltrating without being spotted after saving Maleshov will net you the achievement No Good Deed.

### The Fortress

Once over the wall, head to your left and down the stairs. There are two guards posted at the gate. You’ll have to toss a couple of stones to get their attention and then sneak past. You can also take out the guards by stealth, through sneaking around the battlements. Once you open the gate, combat will initiate. After a few moments, the rest of the men will arrive.

Keep fighting until the bailey is clear. Archers will then take aim at you from the inner bailey. You can exchange fire with them using any ranged weapon, but the segment is timed. After a couple of minutes, a cutscene will trigger. Next, clear out the remaining defenders.

Once the inner bailey is clear, head over to talk to Hans and Zizka about your next steps. Don't worry about looting enemies yet, as there will be ample time once the quest is over. The defenders still inside will throw rocks at you if you get too close to the tower. Regardless of your input, they’ll attempt to parley with von Bergow. It turns out, he has Rosa captive!

### Rescue Rosa

If you are looking to get the best reputation with Rosa, you’ll want to try and rescue her. Choose the following:

- Let’s make a deal

- Any skill check (If you pass, von Bergow will capitulate, so pick one you think you’ll fail if you’d like to go into the tower)

- I refuse to put Rosa in danger

- I’ll try to rescue Rosa

- Yes, I’ll do it!

After insisting, you’ll be prompted to head into the tower yourself. Go inside and fight your way up, after you defeat everyone inside, von Bergow will capitulate.

### Force von Bergow to Surrender

If you say you’ll burn the tower, von Bergow will capitulate immediately, but Rosa will be upset with you for risking her. This will not lock you out of her romance, but it will affect her reputation and mood.

Once von Bergow surrenders, a cutscene will trigger and the quest will end, starting the next Oratores.

## Objectives

If Maleshov is burnt

If Maleshov is saved

If either

If rescuing Rosa

## Danemark Mill

Danemark Mill is a mill located northeast of Maleshov and southeast of Bylany.

## Codex entry

The Danemark Mill was built above the Vrchlitz river during the economic growth of Kuttenberg, possibly even earlier than the 15th century.

It deserves to be remembered and immortalized in the game, mainly because it is the last surviving Middle Age building among many similar ones in the area. It can be viewed today having undergone an 18th century reconstruction and no longer serves as a mill.

Who knows, perhaps the longevity of this building was due not only to its owners, but also to the spirits of the first settlers in the area. Traces of prehistoric settlement, dating back to the early Eneolithic period (4,400 and 2,000 BC), have been found on the rock above the mill.

## Dead horse

Poor horse. It wasn't killed by the dog, someone must have mistreated the animal so badly it died.

—Henry's comment

Dead horse is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The body of a horse can be found north of Semine keep, just below the rocky outcrop where the Vantage point is located. Nearby, a wild dog can be seen digging around, drawn by the carrion.

The area by the outcrop shows signs of struggle, with a patch of trampled earth, blood splattered on the rocks, and a pair of lost horseshoes. It appears the horse bolted from there and collapsed in the grass not far away.

You can learn what happened by asking around at the Semine stables. Ballatay, the stablemaster, explains that one of their horses went missing after a groom lost control of it. Henry can point out that the animal was clearly mistreated and the groom must be lying.

Ballatay is furious at the news and promises to have the groom whipped and driven out. He rewards Henry with some Groschen and offers to teach him something about handling horses for his trouble.

## Demons of Trosky

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Demons of Trosky is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

Immediately after starting Back in the Saddle and after being shown your quarters, Ulrich will go to his next location in the castle, where he can then be talked to. Ask him if needs any assistance around the castle and he'll mention they're being plagued with demons. Eventually he'll give you the choice between two different waters, but your choice here won't affect anything. He'll also direct you to talk to two of the cooks, Manyeta and Bertha, as well as the blacksmith, Osina. As this will require you to go to all areas of the castle, Ulrich will give you almost complete access to the entire castle while you have this task (except the dungeon, which is always off limits).

Note that if you want to do a little less running around, if doing Opus Magnum, you can do those steps in tandem here.

### Talk to the cooks

The cooks are in separate kitchens, with Bertha in the Crone's tower and Manyeta in the Maiden. Both of them though will remark that you need to sprinkle the special water at the fireplaces in the opposite tower from them, as that's where the "demons" are coming from. While Bertha will try to give you a crazy ritual and both will note you should do it at night, neither of these are needed: Henry will automatically sprinkle the water and it can complete just fine during the day.

Crone's tower

- Kitchen, separate fire from the food pot

- Fireplace on next floor above the kitchen

- Fireplace in Erazim's room (first landing/left door after the stone staircase in the castle)

- Room above the alchemy bench

- Room at the very top of the stairs/tower, around the banister

Maiden tower

- Kitchen, separate fire from the food pot

- 2 floors up from the kitchen, in the room where Hans yelled at the chamberlain (has 2 opposing doors and a third door near the green one that goes into the room you met von Bergow in)

- From the room above, go into the room where you met von Bergow in to find a fireplace here

- Next floor up, go directly through the door here from the stair's landing (where a guard is typically standing) and fireplace is on the right wall

- From the above room, continue further into the room and go through the door on the right. This new room's fireplace is against the right wall (shared wall with the other fireplace).

After clearing both towers, report back to the cooks to confirm the fireplaces are treated for reputation gain.

### Talking to Osina

Osina will direct you to a supposed location below the guardhouse, which turns out to just be the guards' privies. Go back to talk to him about this and he'll tell you he realized he got the location wrong right after you left and directs you to a location in the Maiden tower instead. However, this location also turns out to be yet another privy.

Return to the blacksmith again where you can confront him about this and choose to stop bothering with him (noting he's making a fool of you) or try to persist by getting an actual location (asking where the demons are). If you try again, he'll then point you to a location in the Crone tower. However it's yet again, a privy. At this point when you confront him, you can either ignore him or fistfight him. Just be careful if fistfighting at a high level, as usually one punch is enough to make him yield.

### Return to the chamberlain

Return to Ulrich to let him know the results. Note that even if you fought with Osina, this won't cause any reputation loss, as Ulrich is just happy you took care of the issue. You'll then gain some reputation here, along with boosts to survival, vitality, and scholarship skills and some physical rewards (a golden cup, golden chalice, and 55 Groschen). This will also remove your privileges to move around the castle freely, so be careful after this what areas you access going forward.

## Objectives

- Talk to Manyeta.

- Banish the devils from the Crone's side of the castle. (0/5)

- Talk to Bertha

- Banish the devils from the Maiden's side of the castle. (0/5)

- Talk to Osina.

- Find the devils according to the blacksmith's directions.

- Return to Osina.

- Return to the chamberlain.

## Denes Latzkfi

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Denes Latzkfi (Lacković) (Czech: Dénes Lackfi) is a minor character in the Kingdom Come: Deliverance II expansion Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Biography

### Early life

Born into the noble Lacković family in Zadar, Dalmatia, Denes grew up at the court of his uncle Stjepan Lacković, a powerful local ruler with estates in Croatia, Dalmatia, and Slavonia. The family has however become embroiled in the power struggle between Sigismund of Luxembourg and Ladislaus of Naples over the rule in Croatia, siding with Ladislaus. During a meeting of the representatives of nobility with the king, Sigismund had members of the Lacković family and their supporters killed in what has become known as the Bloody Sabor of Križevci. Following the massacre, the surviving members of the Lacković family lost their properties, social standing, and power, and Denes entered Sigismund's services, using the Hungarian variant of his name Latzkfi to distance himself from his family.

According to Denes himself, he hoped to fix the reputation of the family which had been tarnished by his uncle's "betrayal" of Sigismund. Additionally, he wore black "as a sign of shame for his family", and vowed not to wear anything else until he had regained the king's trust.

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

At Sigismund's court, Denes served multiple courtiers, eventually becoming the aide and bodyguard of the royal physician Zacharias of Prachatitz sometime in 1401. Alongside him, he travelled to the Sedletz Monastery which Sigismund chose as his temporary residence in Bohemia. There, he worked as Zacharias' aide, and after the breakout of the mysterious illness, he was additionally tasked with taking care of the supplies for the patients by Zacharias. This however resulted into an issue with Cellarius Julian, who refused to give any extra supplies to those being treated in the infermary.

When the first workmen who were looking for Boleslav Bavor's grave at Sedletz on Zacharias' orders became sick with the mysterious illness, Denes was tasked by Zacharias to help Herbalist Joachim keep the situation under control. He borrowed books for Joachim in the Monastery library and forced him to perform medical procedures. After the two workmen died and the illness spead among the monks of the monastery, Joachim panicked and tried to get rid of the bodies by dragging them to a shed by the flour store and setting it on fire. However, the two bodies were recovered by Brother Elijah and could be examined by Henry, who realized the two bodies were the two missing workmen. Angry at Joachim for failing to cure the men and committing arson which only attracted further attention, Zacharias sent Denes to silence Joachim.

Henry found Denes and Joachim arguing in Joachim's hut. Before he could properly intervene, Denes stabbed Joachim to death and then turned against Henry. Henry however managed to kill him in their duel.

### Associated Quests

- Silent Witnesses

- To Dust you Shan't Return

- Our Daily Bread

## Deserter Chief Vladimir

Deserter Chief Vladimir (Czech: Velitel dezertérů Vladimír) is a former soldier of the Prague militia who abandoned his post in favor of collecting pearl mussels along local rivers.

He can be found at a camp by a river stream south of Danemark Mill in the Kuttenberg region, accompanied by his former comrades-in-arms, now fellow bandits: Bohumil, Maresh, and Zbyshek.

## Involvement

During the search for the ingredients for Master Voyta's decoction, Henry comes across Vladimir's camp. The deserter chief leads a small group of bandits who have been camping by the stream for some time, sifting through mussels in search of pearls to sell or trade.

When Henry arrives, the situation can be handled in several ways. He can reason with Vladimir, convincing him to share a single pearl since there are plenty to go around. A successful persuasion allows Henry to take one from the river without a fight. Alternatively, Henry can intimidate him into giving it up or purchase the pearl directly.

If negotiations fail, a fight breaks out. If he survives the encounter, Vladimir and his gang remain by the stream for a while longer, continuing their search before eventually moving on.

### Associated quest

- Root of Evil

## Devil's Den

Devil's Den is a tavern located at the northernmost part of the map, north of Horschan.

## Codex entry

The Devil's Den is still today one of the smallest settlements in the Kuttenberg region. Unfortunately, no records of its appearance in 1403 have survived, but in the 16th century, the infamous Devil's tavern stood on its site, where the lowlifes of Kuttenberg often gathered, and which served as a model for our Devil's Den.

The name of the settlement and the tavern comes from a legend, according to which, devils were said to come out of the local mines and fly over Kuttenberg at midnight. They were only driven from their dens by water, which later flooded the mines.

We also learn about the dark character of the former inn from the memoirs of Mikuláš Dačický: 'Michal', a messenger of the mining authority, killed the innkeeper Št'astný with a spear in the Devil's tavern near Kuttenberg, where there was a den of rogues and whores. They were fighting over some gloves.'

## Dice/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Dice, also known as Farkle, return once more as a mini-game in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is a two-player game played with a set of six-sided dice. Players compete to reach a target score before their opponent by rolling dice and banking points across multiple rounds.

The game's random nature can be influenced by special loaded dice and badges that modify gameplay rules.

The game is played at dice table in taverns, camps, and various settlements,

## Rules

### Choosing dice

The game is played with six dice. The default dice are all the same colour and perfectly fair. You may choose to replace up to six of these with special dice from your inventory before starting the game.

### Course of the game

You start the game by rolling all six dice. In the bottom right corner you can see the available actions:

- Help: Open the help screen with instructions and valid die combinations.

- Hold die: Select scoring dice you want to keep. You gain points for them at the end of your turn.

- There is always a chance to roll a bust - a situation where none of the rolled dice score any points. In this case, your turn immediately ends and your opponent takes their turn.

- Score and continue: Roll the remaining unselected dice. You can keep rolling until you run out of dice. This option is greyed out until at least one scoring die is selected.

- A special case occurs when all dice rolled during the current turn are scoring dice and no dice remain on the table. In this situation, you may roll all six dice again, and any points scored are added to the total accumulated during the current turn.

- This can continue multiple times, but if you subsequently roll a bust, you lose all unbanked points earned during that entire turn.

- Pass / Score and pass: End your turn. If you have selected scoring dice, the points from those dice are added to your total score. If you have not selected any scoring dice, no points are added.

- Give up: Immediately forfeit the game. Your opponent wins and you lose your wager.

The art of dice is to finish your turn and score your points before you bust (get a roll where not a single die scores). The first player to reach the score goal is the victor. You can see all point information for the current game in the bottom left corner.

### With a badge

Dice badges are items introduced in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Each badge offers a unique effect, such as improved rolls, additional rerolls, or modified scoring rules, and can be equipped before a game begins.

If you and your opponent have a badge of the same level (tin, silver or gold), you can make use of them during your game. Every badge has a different property that affects the rules of the game.

## Probability of a bust

A graph of the probabilities of a completely bust dice roll, dependent on the number of dice you're rolling.

The probability of a completely failed throw is already very low with fair dice and can be nudged into effective impossibility with an appropriately chosen set of weighted dice. On the initial throw, bust probability is 3,9%. With five dice, it's 7,7%., four is 15,7% likely to end in a bust, three dice fail in 27,7%, two bust at still less than half at 44,4%, and finally a single die will bust 66,7% of the times.

## Dicer Filip

Dicer Filip (Czech: Kostkař Filip) is the resident cook at the Troskowitz tavern. He can usually be found behind the dice table where the tavern's veranda turns the corner, near the side wall.

## Involvement

Unlike the ever-busy Betty, he rarely concerns himself with the daily running of the place. Instead, he spends much of his time idling about, playing dice with the local drunkards and chatting with the tavern's regulars.

Every suggestion of work makes him grumble. When the Cumans came to the tavern, his only concern was whether he would have to leave the dice table to cook for them.

## Dicer Lucia

Dicer Lucia is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Lucia lived in Miskowitz and once had a husband. Sometime ago, he died in what was ruled by the local authorities to have been an accident while washing laundry. He was found drowned by a washing spot with soap shoved in his mouth. She claimed, however, that he never would have done any washing of his own volition, but nevertheless treated his death as an accident since that was the official ruling.

She enjoyed playing dice, seeing it as one of the few sins allowed for women, as they weren't allowed to drink, fight, or whore like men were. Her husband had been in debt due to his own dicing and she mentioned to Henry that she figured that someone must have gotten sick of him.

Following her husband's death, Lucia was able to take up dice and live a much freer life.

### Associated Quests

- The Master's Game

## Dicer Martin

Dicer Martin is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Martin had travelled broadly in his time, visiting Germany and Hungary. As a dice player, he met Henry when the young man was playing dice throughout Kuttenberg on behalf of the local blacksmiths' guild.

Due to his travels, Martin considered himself a bit of an expert in profiling blacksmiths and mentioned that he though Henry's hands were too small for such work. In fact, his hands must have been the smallest north of the Alps and south of Warsaw, something that confused Henry as he had always thought of his hands as being a normal size.

When asked what he lived on while travelling, Martin took the question to mean how he stayed alive, to which he told Henry about how he used to forage for food. When Henry then tried to clarify he meant what he did as a tradesman, Martin replied that he would never eat a tradesman as he preferred cooked meat to raw.

## Dicer Yara

Dicer Yara is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Yara saw himself as a dicer first and foremost, worthy of pride in and of itself as a way to earn money.

When approached by Henry to play dice with Henry acting as a representative of the Kuttenberg blacksmiths' guild, Yara was not impressed. He didn't want to play, since he saw the wager as lopsided- at best he would win money, while Henry could win both money and glory.

Since things were so naturally uneven in his eyes, he wanted a larger wager than would normally be paid for, though Henry refused. The only other thing he'd play for would be world peace, or at least a chance to forge something at Henry's forge. Neither would be hit lot, however, as Henry would only play for money.

## Die Another Day

Die Another Day is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

As Godwin, you saved your brother.

## Acquisition

To unlock the achievement, you must ensure that Godwin's younger brother, Christopher Oderin, survives the massacre at Raborsch during the main quest The Feast.

## Tips

- During the main quest The King's Gambit, Henry attends a council meeting in Kuttenberg Town Hall to learn more about Sigismund's plans. Partway through the quest, control shifts to Godwin in the northwest of the region.

- This quest transitions directly into The Feast, which culminates in a large-scale skirmish at Raborsch. After retrieving the wine from the cellar, the objective will change to "Defend Raborsch!" with an optional objective: "Protect your brother" - referring to Christopher.

- To unlock the this achievement, ensure that Christopher survives the battle. He can be found near the base of the stairs leading to the courtyard, wearing green. Stay close and help eliminate any enemies targeting him. If Christopher survives the encounter, the achievement will unlock.

## Ditrich Katz

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The world has changed, friend. War has changed.

—Ditrich Katz to Musa

Ditrich Katz is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He is the Prague militia commander at Sigismund's camp near Kuttenberg.

## Biography

Katz was the commander of the Prague forces in the service Sigismund in the Kuttenberg region.

He became good friends with the camp's physician, Musa of Mali, and often tried to entice him drink and gamble, though Musa would always refuse due to his steadfast adherence to his religious beliefs.

His second in command was Stephen Crow, who one day brought a possible enlistee, Henry to Katz for approval. Katz sent Henry in search of a missing charter and the soldiers who had disappeared with it. When Henry was successful, Katz suggested they drink in celebration.

Their merrymaking was interrupted by a commotion outside, the Cuman commander, Chertan, had been stabbed and left for dead. Musa tried to heal him, but in vain, he was poisoned and died. The commander of the camp, Grozav of Borumlaca, suspected Musa, but Katz was certain it could not have been him. Not only had Musa been with Katz and Henry at the time of the stabbing, but he would have no reason as a healer to inflict injury.

In order to prove Musa's innocence, Katz put Henry on the case and retired to his tent, sick from drinking. A couple of days later, the king's justicar, Stibor of Stiborzitz, arrived to mete judgement. Katz defended Musa and, with Henry's help, was able to clear his name.

Finally, with the charter and Musa's situation resolved, Katz was confident the Prague forces could move out for Sedletz with the cannon in-hand. Henry then reported this movement to his allies, and the party was ambushed.

Katz survived the initial ambush and may have been spared, although he also felt a commander should go down with his men and was just as accepting of an honourable death.

### Associated Quests

- The Lion's Den

## Divine Messenger

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Divine Messenger is the 10th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

It's been quite some time since Radzig and Hanush last heard from Henry and Capon... Let's hope that has nothing to do with the big battle that just took place in the region.

## Synopsis

Godwin Oderin arrives in the Trosky region, having been sent by Hanush and Radzig to check in on Henry and Hans. He rides at a gentle pace, but speeds up when he comes across the makeshift burial mounds of the former companions to the two men he’s been sent to find.

In Zhelejov, he talks with the innkeeper of the Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn, musing about the path his life has taken to bring him here. He’s lost the position at his parish, claiming gossip and hearsay did him in even though he may admit he’s done his fair share of sinning. It’s worked out well then that his local lords have sent him here. Lawrence catches Godwin up on the happenings in the area and directs him towards Nebakov Mill. He believes Henry and Hans were most likely killed; two witnesses from the mill – Anna and Kuba – saw the attack and said no one made it out alive. Kuba was injured and Anna is with him holed up in the barn at the inn to recuperate.

Godwin heads over to ask them if they are certain Henry and Hans were killed. Anna describes the whole sordid affair for him, how she and the other millworkers were locked in the barn in the evening only for morning to bring carnage. She and Kuba tried to make a break for it but Kuba was shot by an arrow, forcing them to hide until things calmed down. Kuba mentions the bandits took some captives, so not all the enemy men were killed in battle. Anna confirms that Henry and Hans were among those taken captive and that they were hanged. When Godwin refuses to believe this, Anna crumples, she can only say what she saw but she supposes it’s not impossible she could be wrong. As Godwin goes to leave, he speaks a Latin phrase and Anna asks him to bless Kuba for a swift recovery. He may do so or else disabuse her of the notion that his words carry any weight.

With all the information he can hope to find gathered, Godwin makes for the battlefield. As he gets closer, he remarks to himself about the strategy used by the bandits, hiding in tree cover, using wagons to block the road, all in all a decent operation – if bloody. Closer to the mill, Godwin runs across some looters doing what they are wont to do. He may leave them be or else take it upon himself to give some of them justice by the sword.

At the mill, Godwin is stopped by a member of the band who initially mistakes him for one of the looters they’ve allowed to comb the forest. Godwin insists he isn’t a looter and rather he’s looking for friends of his. He explains he’s a priest, although he doesn’t look like one and asks to be brought to his commander to confirm if his friends are among the dead. The guard brings him to Erik, the man in charge of dealing with the aftermath.

Erik asks many of the same questions, and Godwin reiterates that he’s here looking for friends of his. Godwin asks Erik for details of the attack, not even knowing which parties were involved. Erik says he thinks it highly unlikely anyone survived and suggests Godwin check the burial pit for them. However, Godwin reveals one of the men he’s looking for is a noble and gives their names. At this, Erik confirms the captain did, in fact, take a few prisoners with him though Erik claims not to know who.

More looters arrive and Erik dispatches them with Godwin’s help. Erik is impressed by Godwin’s skill and asks after Godwin’s past to which Godwin obliges, telling him a little about his time spent as a fighter. Erik agrees to take Godwin to see the captain since he’s proved his mettle. Along the way, Erik asks more questions of Godwin’s purpose before initiating a race up to the fortress.

Regardless of who wins, Erik calls for the gates to be open and presents Godwin who needs to meet with the captain. Michael, who meets them, says the captain is with some captives – a good sign for Godwin’s chances – and Erik insists he be called.

Zizka arrives, bandaged and bloody, complaining to be called away from his duty. Erik introduces Godwin along with the name of the man he’s come to seek – Sir Hans Capon. Zizka finds it a funny coincidence, turns out he just had an interesting talk with the very same Capon… and Istvan Toth. This makes Erik nervous, certain the jig is up. Zizka asks him to wait in the tower so they can have their own conversation, leaving him to finally speak with Godwin.

Godwin gives his praise for Zizka’s scheme with the ambush, something that Zizka finds surprising to hear from a priest. They continue their back and forth, with Zizka eventually confirming both Hans and Henry are alive and well. Godwin demands he be allowed to see the boys to make sure they are as well as Zizka says, but Zizka denies him, neither willing to trust the other. Godwin can’t make heads of why the boys would be helping von Bergow with anything and Zizka imagines Godwin could be anyone on any side.

Suddenly, a cry come from within the fortress – rebellion! Godwin takes advantage of Zizka’s distraction to grab hold of him, keeping a dagger to his throat. Zizka meanwhile, points one towards Godwin’s abdomen – a stalemate. They bond over both having fought against Turks and release each other. Zizka promises that if Godwin helps him now, he’ll let the boys go. So help Godwin does.

Once the rebels are taken care of, Zizka mentions that Hans had told him Istvan and Erik were spies and this only proves he was right. With a start, he realises they’ve lost sight of Erik and rushes for the cells.

Sometime earlier, Henry and Hans are thrown into a cell. The door opens and in walks Istvan. As soon as Henry lays eyes on him he starts hurling insults and asking after the sword. Istvan pretends not to know him, telling Zizka he must be raving, but Henry’s mention of Istvan’s loyalty to Sigismund perks Zizka’s ears enough that he tells Hans to elaborate. Istvan tries to wriggle out of it, but the facts line up and Zizka is uncertain enough now that he orders Istvan to be held as well. It’s then that he’s asked to come to the gate to speak with Godwin.

Now stuck together, Henry berates Istvan some more while Istvan mocks him in turn. Nebak is less than impressed with his new cellmate, but Istvan explains that it’s thanks to him the true lord of the fortress is even still alive, that they are on the same side despite Istvan’s involvement in taking the fortress in the first place – all in service of taking Zizka down from the inside.

Erik bursts in, fresh off being dismissed by Zizka at the gate and rushes to let the able prisoners out. He gives Istvan his sword, Henry sword, and Istvan wants to take Henry out, but Erik says there’s no time, they have to go right this minute. They escape, leaving Henry and Hans alone in the dungeon, frustrated and confused.

The next time the door opens it’s Godwin who enters, overjoyed to have finally found the boys. He greets Henry with an embrace and unlocks their cell. Back up top the trio and Zizka watch as the other former prisoners ride away towards Trosky.

With things calm for the moment, it’s come time to straighten the story out. Zizka details his providence and who he works for – Jan Sokol and Margrave Prokop, Jobst’s brother. The situation amongst brothers is difficult, but this means all the men present are on the side of Wenceslas. Godwin wonders how it is that Henry and Hans, then, could have ended up working for von Bergow and Henry explains it all started with their being ambushed by Zizka’s band at the pond – a tragedy of errors.

More explanations follow: Zizka is here on orders to make things difficult for von Bergow as one of Sigismund’s most powerful supporters, he mistook Henry and Hans’s company for being in league with von Bergow from the start since their meeting with Captain Thomas was friendly, but he claims not to have known Katherine when he saw her at the pond and he refuses to name the source that warned him in time to set up the ambush at the mill. Henry explains Istvan’s past in the Sasau region and his own personal history and Godwin explains how he came to be sent to Trosky.

The next order of business is how to leave. Now that von Bergow has been beaten and embarrassed, he’ll be sure to try again and with aplomb, possibly even bringing in reinforcements from others in the League of Lords. Tentatively, they all plan to return to Rattay as Jobst is still afield.

Godwin treats Zizka’s wound, saving his eye from infection. Henry apologises for causing the injury in the first place, but Zizka knows it was his own fault for removing his helm during their duel.

## Walkthrough

Immediately after you gain control over Godwin Oderin, you can walk around to talk to others at the inn, but they won't have much to say as they all use the same general dialogue.Head into the barn area to find Dorothy praying over two survivors from Nebakov Mill: Anna and Kuba.

Talk to them and Anna will tell you how they were rounded up and locked into a barn before they heard the fighting break out early the next morning. When the two tried to flee, Kuba was injured, so the two hid in the area to wait it out. While they waited, they saw the bandits take some captives, though when you reveal you're looking for Henry and Hans, she believes they were hanged as they were part of von Bergow's party. When pressed though, she'll admit she's not entirely sure if they were actually hanged or not as she only saw it from a distance. As Godwin prepares to leave them be, he'll speak Latin, revealing he's a priest and Anna will ask that you bless Kuba. If you do so, she'll then give you a commemorative ring as thanks.

### Check out the ravine

When ready, head to the side of the inn where your horse, Bibiana, is waiting and head out to the ravine. Note the game will prevent you from trying to get too off course, so just stick to the main path and instructions Lawrence gave and you'll eventually reach the ravine. As you ride down the same path the army went, Godwin will make some remarks on what he sees/how the ambush was set up. Eventually you'll hear voices up ahead and find the source: a few opportunists looting the dead. You can talk with them a bit and as long as you don't try to tell them off, you can pass through without issue (or choose to fight them if you wish - Godwin is an extremely strong swordsman).

Continue following the path around the cart that blocked Henry's path earlier (it's been moved aside so you have room to stay on your horse here), and head towards the mill. A guard posted here will initially mistake you as one of the looters you met and tell you off, until you explain you're a former priest and looking for your friends. He'll bring you to Erik, the one in charge of disposing the bodies. Erik will give Godwin the rundown of what happened, but more importantly he'll eventually reveal their leader did take some people captive, but he's not sure of their names. However, you'll be interrupted by the looters you ran into earlier: apparently they've gotten too greedy and want to take all the loot for themselves now (or they're angry about you killing their friends back in the forest). Erik will then ask you to assist and, in return, he'll take you to the prisoners to check for your friends.

### Nebakov Fortress

After the fight, true to his word, Erik will then take you with him to the fortress. He'll talk with you a short bit before opting to have a quick race to the fortress. You can easily beat him by cutting through the bushes (instead of following the path all the way around) and then going towards the marker around the campfire to win. After a short conversation, you'll be introduced to the captain, with a now bandaged eye thanks to Henry. On revealing you're there for Hans, the captain will send Erik to the tower to talk in private later, noting he had an interesting chat with Hans and Istvan earlier.

Chat with the captain, but eventually the conversation will turn sour regarding ransom. However, just as the captain tries to dismiss you, his men will call out that there's a rebellion going on, distracting him and allowing Godwin to put a dagger to the captain's throat. The captain will chuckle, revealing he likewise has a dagger aimed at Godwin's abdomen. After the two reveal they both fought Turks, they'll release each other and the captain will agree to let Hans and Henry go if Godwin helps them fight off the rebels.

Head into the fortress and help kill off the rebels past Klara's hut. Talk to the captain again, who'll reveal Hans' intel was right: von Bergow had spies - Istvan and Erik - infiltrated his men. Suddenly realizing those two were left alone while they dealt with the rebels, the captain will immediately make for the prison cells.

### Encounter with Istvan

Zizka turns on Istvan

The game will then cut to what happened a little bit earlier, where Hans and Henry were thrown into a prison cell just as Istvan appeared. On recognizing him, Henry will yell at Istvan, revealing in front of the captain that Istvan works for Sigismund, and Hans will likewise back this up. Istvan will try to deny these allegations, but piecing together how Istvan was trying to avoid the battle earlier, the captain will realize the two are telling the truth and will have Istvan thrown into Jaromier Nebak's cell. After a quick scene where the captain's name is revealed as Zizka, he'll leave and you'll be in control of Henry as you confront Istvan.

Jaromier will initially wonder why he shouldn't strangle Istvan right there, but Istvan reveals he was meant to be the lord's rescuer and the only reason they kept the nobleman alive, rather than off him as Zizka wanted to originally. Istvan says he infiltrated the group on Otto von Bergow's direct orders to gain Zizka's trust so they could eventually put an end to him once and for all. However, Zizka had locked down the fortress the night before they ambushed the army, so Istvan wasn't able to sneak out to warn von Bergow. After a little more dialogue, Erik will break in, knowing their ruse is up, and release Istvan and Jaromier, but prevent Istvan from killing Henry as there's no time. The trio will then run off.

### Talking to Zizka

A short time later, Godwin appears and releases Hans and Henry, and the trio will join Zizka as they watch over the ramparts as Istvan, Erik, and Jaromier flee to Trosky Castle. The group will then talk at length, with Zizka formally introducing himself and how you and Hans ended up assisting von Bergow. You'll then be able to talk to him further about how Istvan and Erik joined, why his group attacked you at the pond and about Katherine (though he denies knowing her), the ravine attack, and about Semine. Zizka will then note the group needs to leave soon, as no doubt von Bergow will retaliate as soon as he can. The group will decide it's best to head back to Rattay while Godwin will ask to take a look at Zizka's injured eye so it doesn't cause further complications when they're on the road. After a short scene of Godwin addressing it, the quest will end and immediately go into the next main quest.

## Do Good to All People

Do Good to All People is an achievement introduced in Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Description

You helped the people of the monastery.

## Acquisition

The Do Good to All People achievement can be obtained by successfully finishing three out of four of these:

- Maddening Pain – at the start of Anamnesis, after speaking with Albich in the infirmary, step outside. You will see two people arguing; immediately talk to the girl, Maddie, as she will walk away if you take too long. To complete the task correctly, give her the Anti-inflammatory potion.

- Our Daily Bread – after finishing Anamnesis, speak to Zacharias and then Denes to start this quest. You must complete all objectives, including the optional ones, for the quest to count.

- This is also when you can earn the Ostraconophobia achievement.

- Foreseeing Evil - during Prevention or Our Daily Bread you'll have to talk to Librarian Crispin to access the library. Don't pick any of the skill checks, rather say you'll help him. You'll then need to give him herbs. If you already have them, don't give them to him right away, instead say you'll get some. That unlocks the task.

- Help Monk Vincent – at any time after Anamnesis and before entering the crypt in Silent Witnesses, you can find Brother Vincent in the monks' quarters above the library. Unlock a locked door with food placed outside it or speak with the monk through the door. Exhaust all dialogue options, then choose to pray with him. After praying, finish the conversation by asking if he feels better.

- You may also give him a potion, but it is not required.

## Trivia

- The achievement's title references Galatians 6:10, where the apostle Paul encourages Christians to live by the Spirit and do good to others: "Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers." (NIV)

## Dragon's Lair

Dragon’s Lair is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is a timed quest.

## Description

Rumours have started spreading about a mythical creature in the Kuttenberg region. Is there any truth to them?

## Walkthrough

Speak to Monk Slava in Bylany to begin the quest. You can find him east of the fast travel point, usually sitting under a tree. He has an urgent message for the abbot who is currently visiting the church outside Kuttenberg but cannot leave town to deliver it, so he wants you to handle it. It turns out, that dragon bones have allegedly been discovered and Slava wants the abbot to be aware and advise on how to handle it.

When you arrive at the church, you’ll find the abbot in conversation with a man called Gerhard. Talk to the abbot and deliver the message, and he will tell you to collect the bones and bring them to Slava so they can be destroyed. On the way out of the church yard, Gerhart will give you a counterproposal – give the bones to him for a monetary reward.

Head back to Bylany to get the location of the bones. After speaking to Slava a man called Leopold and his cronies will appear. If you can pass a very hard speech or presence check, you can put them off the hunt, otherwise you’ll have to fight them and then deal with them later on.

Slava doesn’t know the exact location but he will tell you where to find the man who found them. His name is Vashek and he can be found working around Bylany. Talk to him and then either pass a hard intimidation check or give him 200 groschen and he’ll give you the full description of where he went on the trip where he found the bones.

You’ll have to follow along with the directions he gave starting from the woodcutters’ camp southwest of Bylany. As you find each landmark, Henry will speak about it, updating the search area and leading you to the next. There will be a few other people on the trail and they will be hostile, so watch for them as you go along.

Finally, you’ll find the bones at the end of a stream west of Bylany, between Wysoka and Maleshov. If you did not deter him earlier, Leopold will appear along with a band of mercenaries. There are a few ways you can proceed from here.

You can betray one group and side with the other. Siding with Leopold will result in him backstabbing you and you will have to kill him. Siding with the mercenaries may allow you to take one of the three bones but depending on checks you may also have to kill them after.

You can broker a deal and split the bones amongst the three groups. This will require a couple of medium speech checks, but if done properly can allow you to bring the bone you have to Gerhard for his reward.

You can also just take on both groups and take them out to have all the bones to yourself.

Once you have the bones, you can decide whether to return them to Slava or Gerhard. If you have all three bones, you will be able to satisfy both Slava and Gerhard, with a medium speech check. Lie to Slava and say you have given him all the bones while only giving him a couple and then rush over to Gerhard to give him the rest.

Giving all the bones to Slava will result in a large reputation gain across the region. Giving any of the bones to Gerhard will net you some groschen.

## Drunkard Jezhek

Drunkard Jezhek is a Troskowitz resident in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

While Jezhek owns a small home in Troskowitz, it's about the only thing he has to his name. He's known for being the village's drunkard and doesn't really contribute to anything, leading to no sensible woman wanting to marry him. Consequently, he came up with the idea of getting Pavlena to agree to marry him thinking she would be easy pickings, as she had been forced into exile when her mother, Bozhena, was run out of town. However, Pavlena was smarter than this and immediately dismissed him as well.

Despite him having a rather abrasive personality, Betty and many others agree that Jezhek is all bluster: first sign of a fight and he'll cave.

## Dry Devil

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Sir Hynek of Kunstadt and Jaispitz (Czech: Hynek z Kunštátu a Jevišovic), better known to his friends and enemies as the Dry Devil (Czech: Suchý Čert), is a infamous robber knight and the leader of a mercenary band called the Devil's Pack.

His historical counterpart is a Moravian nobleman of the same name, who became famous as a robber knight during the Moravian Margrave Wars.

After the Battle of Suchdol and after the war he stayed with Zizka and planned to go wherever he went.

## Biography

## Codex Entry

Originally named Hynek Jevišovský of Kunstadt, he was a fierce and fearless soldier who became famous as a robber knight during the Moravian Margraviate Wars, in which he repeatedly raided Austria in 1401 and 1402, continuing even after the first capture of the Bohemian king in Vienna.

Only after the escape of King Wenceslas IV did the Austrian Duke Albrecht lose patience and so in 1404 he marched on Znojmo with 12,000 soldiers supported by another 12,000 soldiers of Sigismund of Luxembourg. However, the Dry Devil knew about the campaign. When the enemy troops stood in front of the town, it was already fortified and with substantial help from his friend Jan Sokol of Lamberg he repelled the attack. It should be noted that a dysentery epidemic, which had spread among the enemy to such an extent that both enemy nobles were infected, also contributed greatly to this. Albrecht IV of Austria even died of the disease.

And so the Dry Devil continued to pillage and plunder. Eventually, however, even Wenceslas IV ran out of patience and had Hynek imprisoned in 1407. He was soon released, but did not enjoy his freedom very long, for he died in 1408.

## Trivia

- The historic Dry Devil is distantly related to Hans Capon on his mother's side, as well as to his future wife, Jitka of Kunstadt. He and Jitka come from the same noble house and his mother is the member of the lords of Lichtenburk, a branch of the Ronov family. It's unclear if the version of the Dry Devil featured in the game shares this relation or not.

- It is said the honorific the "Dry Devil" was given to him for his tall and thin physique, his dry temperament, and for the devilish manner in which he persecuted his enemies.

## Déjà Vu

Déjà Vu is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You defeated Capon during practice. Again.

## Acquisition

The Déjà Vu achievement is unlocked during the prologue of the game, as part of the main quest Easy Riders.

## Tips

- After meeting the patrol outside Trosky, Henry, Hans Capon and his retinue make camp near a lake. During this sequence, you'll participate in a combat tutorial that ends with a sparring match against Capon. To unlock this achievement, you must defeat him in that duel.

- The achievement is missable, but there is an autosave just before the fight, allowing you to reload if necessary.

- To win, focus on using perfect parries and ripostes, and manage your stamina carefully. It's best to play defensively - wait for Capon to attack, then counter with a riposte aimed at his unguarded side. Going on the offensive too aggressively can leave you winded and vulnerable to his counters.

## Easy Riders

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Easy Riders is the 2nd main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Me, Sir Hans Capon, and our armed escort are on our way to Trosky Castle to deliver a message to the lord there, Sir Otto von Bergow. Von Bergow is the most influential man in the League of Lords, and our task is to try and enlist his support in the resistance against King Sigismund and rescuing King Wenceslas from captivity. Everyone is counting on us: Sir Hanus of Leipa, Margrave Jobst of Moravia and my father, Sir Radzig Kobyla.

## Synopsis

Henry and Sir Hans Capon arrive in the Trosky region with the rest of their company members; Oats, Tankard, Konrad, and Nicolas of Rattay. Sir Hans is in good spirits, excited to get away from the “hellhole” that is the Sasau region and have some fun. Henry on the other hand, doesn’t see how much fun they could possibly have when theirs is such a simple task – ride to Trosky, deliver a letter, and then return home. The company spot Trosky Castle in the distance, marvelling at its grandeur and riding on.

The company rides towards the castle, Henry and Sir Hans discuss what they hope will be in store for them, with Henry either playing along or being a wet blanket. After some time, they come across a company sent from Trosky Castle led by von Bergow’s captain – Thomas. Thomas is suspicious of the armed strangers, as he says there has been a lot of banditry in the region of late.

Sir Hans shows him the letter to prove their identity and purpose in the region, but Thomas replies that their being sent by Sir Hanush of Leipa implies that makes them enemies. Henry can defuse the situation, explaining that they have come to put those differences aside and end hostilities.

Thomas calls off his men, apologizing for his cold demeanor, but emphasizing that the bandits operating in the area have caused them much strife. He suggests the company make camp, as it is too late in the day for them to reach Trosky Castle before nightfall and he and his company must finish the job they were sent to perform and thus cannot vouch for them.

Sir Hans decides they should set up camp at a nearby pond, saying the bandits would most likely be keeping their heads down with Thomas’ patrol combing the woods. Once camp is made, Sir Hans will ask Henry to deal with his dog.

Once Mutt is happy, Hans challenges Henry to a duel so they can stretch their limbs after a long journey. Regardless of the outcome, the fighters have worked up an appetite. The company eat their meal and chat around the fire, bantering with each other, reminiscing, and discussing what they might do while in the region.

After the meal, Sir Hans insists that he and Henry take a bath in the pond. Some of the members of the company aren’t too keen on their campsite – what with the bandits about, but Sir Hans insists he won’t let any of them bring down the mood. With help, Sir Hans strips down and has a mug of wine.

Henry follows him into the pond, a little wary that it might be too deep since he can’t swim. Sir Hans hears some women singing down the shoreline and decides to investigate, with Henry in tow. As they approach the women, the sound of horses and shouting disturb them.

It turns out, the bandits aren’t so worried about Thomas’s patrol after all. The campsite is under attack and Henry and Sir Hans can do nothing but watch as their comrades are slaughtered. In the group of bandits is a familiar figure all dressed in black, Sir Istvan Toth, who steals the letter meant for von Bergow.

Henry spots one of the women from the pond being attacked by a few of the bandits and he shouts to divert their attention. A fellow bandit on horseback arrives and tells them to leave her alone, even going so far as to kill one of them when he won’t let her go. He nods and she runs off, while the remaining men are told to go after Henry and Sir Hans.

Henry and Sir Hans are able to swim away, but Henry is hit in the back by one of their arrows. Sir Hans pulls out the arrow, and the pair attempt to escape from the bandits on the other side of the pond. They sneak past some of the searching bandits, heading into the rocks, eventually being separated.

After reuniting with Sir Hans, Henry is attacked by a bandit. The two fall over a cliff in their fight. Although the bandit breaks his fall, Henry is greatly wounded and sees his dead father, Martin, having a short chat with him about mortality, glory, and how Henry needs to see things to the end. Hans wakes Henry and they set off again into the woods.

## Walkthrough

After the cutscene, you will automatically ride alongside the company, any dialogue options can be chosen and they have no great affect on anything.

As part of the interaction with Thomas, you can choose Henry’s starting stat buffs and playstyle:

- Soldier: likes nothing more than to have a weapon in his hand and wear a strong suit of armour; he is also infamous for his short temper. (combat skills)

- Adviser: prefers to solve things using his knowledge, sharp tongue and a kind word. (speech skills)

- Scout: likes to hide in the shadows and solve tasks silently, undetected and by stealth. (stealth skills)

Note: The choice of this starting playstyle will give you a head start on experience for the related skills, but will not hamper growth in any others. That being said, speech is always good to focus on in the early game, if you would like to resolve certain quests peacefully.

Whichever you choose, Thomas will then ask why he should trust you, prompting your first Persuasion attempt. In order to succeed you must choose the option that corresponds with the playstyle you chose in the earlier dialogue:

- Soldier: Charisma or Might

- Adviser: Speech or Charisma

- Scout: Charisma

After the discussion with Captain Thomas, the company will set up camp and Sir Hans will complain about Mutt’s barking and you must call him to heel.

If you would like to get him something to eat, speak with Oats and ask him for scraps. Oats will refuse, as Mutt has been getting into their supplies on his own. He can either be persuaded to give Henry a sausage or else be willing to trade it for a ring he lost at dice to another company member, Tankard.

For persuasion, your options are:

- Speech: We’ll get food at Trosky – fail, reputation loss, Oats will keep the sausage

- Charisma: I’ll bring you something from the nobles’ feast – success, reputation gain, Oats will give Henry the sausage

- Intimidation: You wouldn’t want Mutt to bite you – success, reputation loss, Oats will give Henry the sausage.

Tankard can be found at the dice table behind the pot. You will have to beat him at dice to win the ring. Once you have the ring, return it to Oats and, as promised, he will give you a sausage to feed to Mutt.

Speak with Sir Hans again and he will challenge you to a duel, starting the combat tutorial. (Note: If you are able to beat Sir Hans in the duel you will unlock the achievement Déjà Vu.)

After the duel, go by the fire to prompt some conversation. Some of the conversation will prompt further attribute experience.

Sir Hans will then insist that he and Henry bathe, once in the water, crouch down to sneak and follow Sir Hars through the reeds towards the washing women. One of the women is doing laundry, toss a stone to her left and she will leave to investigate, allowing you to sneak past.

Once on the other side of the pond, the bandits will be looking for you. Follow Sir Hans and do what he tells you to until eventually he will have to stop and regain his energy. He will ask you to scout ahead. There are two ways you can go, one is a dead end which Sir Hans will direct you towards and the other is the way out. Following either will eventually prompt you to return at which point you will find two enemies instead of Sir Hans.

If you went to the dead end, wait until the bandits return to searching and head to what is now your left. If you went to the exit, crouch to the side until the searching bandit passes you and then follow behind him at a crouch. Follow Sir Hans again until being attacked by a bandit.

Regardless of the outcome of the battle, you will fall from the cliffs, ending the quest.

## Emperor Charles Tavern

Emperor Charles Tavern is a tavern in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is located in Kuttenberg.

## Description

The Emperor Charles Tavern serves mainly the merchant class in Kuttenberg. It is run by a wine connoisseur, Havel, who is also a member of the Kuttenberg city council. It has a small outdoor section in the front though its main space for patrons is just inside. It has a large number of rooms for rent which can be found on two upper floors, each with their own kitchen, and an attic where workers sleep. Out back is another outdoor area though it is not as frequently used.

## Enneleyn

Enneleyn is a well-travelled courtesan currently residing in the Nomads' Camp in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Enneleyn's full history is unclear, though she was said to have travelled all over the continent, serving as everything from a concubine to mistress to a companion, and been offered extravagant gifts for her services, including an estate. She was also no stranger to unusual clients.

By 1403, she ended up in the Trosky area and went to Dorothy's bathhouse in Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn for work, but on noting how much payment she required, was turned away, which irked her.

Later, she was approached by Henry with a proposition for a job - to pretend to be a noblewoman and seduce the local chamberlain and steal a book from him on behalf of Miller Kreyzl. Enneleyn accepted, although she was initially offended by the low nature of the task, she was also intrigued by the rumours of the chamberlain's taste for something apparently unspeakable. She requested Henry to bring her a nice dress and perfume so she could look the part, along with some wine to mix with a sleeping potion.

Enneleyn then attended the wedding at Semine Fortress and took to her job, being escorted by the chamberlain and accompanying him. At some point during the event, he told her what he proposed to do and she was so disgusted by it that she changed her mind and slipped away from him.

She found companionship in another wedding guest, one Hans Capon, and went to talk with him in private. The pair were interrupted by Henry who had been sent by the chamberlain to find Enneleyn. Enneleyn reiterated her conviction to sever ties and end the job, giving Henry the ring the chamberlain had given her as proof she no longer wanted anything to do with him.

After the wedding, she returned to the Nomads' camp.

### Associated quest

- Opus Magnum

- Wedding Crashers

## Enough!

Enough! is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available as soon as you get to the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

The lads from Miskowitz are training in fistfights after the incident with the Praguers. Maybe I could learn something too.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Innkeeper Zdeslav in Miskowitz and ask him about the fights to start the quest. He will tell you not to mention them to the bailiff. If you do, you’ll have to pass a speech check to convince the bailiff you’ll end the fighting and will then require intimidation checks to start each fight. Otherwise, just speak to each fighter to challenge him.

First up is Ventza, he is usually found around the tavern or the pond. He is a fairly easy fighter to beat, as he doesn’t really counter and will give up quickest.

Next is Paskal, he will counter, so it’s best to clinch with him if you have decent clinching or focus on kicking, as he is weakest against them.

Finally, challenge Marcus. Marcus is the most difficult of the three and will also counter. He may be pushed into a corner to try to avoid countering but he may take a few tries if your unarmed is not very strong.

Once you’ve fought all three, head back to the innkeeper to finish the quest. He'll give you 60 and beer.

## Erik

Erik is the captain of the bandit army in Vranik and Istvan Toth's second-in-command.

He serves as a secondary antagonist in Kingdom Come: Deliverance, and a main antagonist in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Stats

### Kingdom Come Deliverance

|

|
Erik

|
10-12

9-11

13-15

## Biography

### Early Life

Erik's parents were murdered by Sir Istvan Toth during a raid in Moravia, who took Erik into his retinue and, in his words, became more of a father to him than his real father had been. Erik learnt sword-fighting and became more confident under Toth's tutelage, eventually becoming his right-hand man.

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance

Erik led the bandit camp at Vranik under Istvan. He welcomed Henry into the group following The Die is Cast after the latter received a good word from the recruiter Kozliek. Erik then sent Henry to Vanyek for a sword fighting lesson and Istvan arrived at the hideout.

Erik and Istvan captured Henry and revealed Istvan's plan to help King Sigismund conquer the region by undermining the local lords and terrifying the populace, ensuring he would be richly rewarded once Sigismund became the undisputed King as well as the secret of Henry's parentage. Erik and Istvan then left Henry to be tortured by their lackey, Udo.

Henry later escaped, returning the following evening with the combined forces of Sir Divish, Sir Radzig, and Sir Hanush. During the assault on Vranik, it became clear that neither Erik nor Istvan were there. The attackers realised they have been led into a trap and Istvan had taken the majority of his forces to take Talmberg Castle, where Lady Stephanie and later Radzig were taken hostage, beginning the Siege of Talmberg.

Erik led an attack on the siege camp and was taken prisoner. He was then interrogated by Henry and Hanush. Following the interrogation, it became clear that Erik was Istvan's lover and thus a valuable hostage, giving them the opportunity to try an exchange. This attempt was rejected by Istvan who nevertheless swore he would harm his hostages if Erik was harmed.

Erik remained in captivity for the remainder of the siege. When the trebuchet built at the siege camp destroyed Talmberg's portcullis, allowing the regional forces to storm the castle, Istvan agreed to an exchange of hostages as he no longer stood a chance of holding out. Erik was exchanged for Lady Stephanie and taken with Istvan and Radzig to Skalitz where Radzig was released and Erik and Istvan left the region.

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Erik went to Trosky with Istvan following the Siege of Talmberg, infiltrating Jan Zizka's band at the behest of Lord Otto von Bergow. After the ambush on Nebakov Mill, Erik was tasked with disposing the bodies in the area. He met Godwin in the course of those duties while the priest was looking for Henry and Sir Hans Capon. After being assisted with looters, Erik agreed to take Godwin to Nebakov to check if his friends were among those taken prisoner.

When it was revealed that Henry and Hans are indeed who Godwin was looking for, Erik was dismissed by Zizka and told they would speak later as Zizka had just had an interesting conversation with the prisoners. Knowing that the ruse was up, Erik went to the dungeon and freed Istvan and Lord Jaromier Nebak before anyone other than Zizka was informed of their treachery and the three rode off to Trosky Castle.

The next morning, Erik returned to Nebakov with von Bergow, Istvan, Nebak, and Sir Markvart von Aulitz and the Prague militia to besiege the fortress. The attack forced the defenders into the tower where they faced a salvo from a cannon, ending the battle. Henry, Hans, Godwin, and Zizka were taken prisoner and Erik returned with them to Trosky Castle.

Istvan interrogated Henry and eventually learnt information concerning Margrave Jobst and Liechenstein including their locations and why they met with the Sasau nobles. Istvan took this information to Erik and tasked him with delivering it to von Bergow at Maleshov.

A while later, news reached Maleshov that Istvan had been killed. This news greatly affected Erik, sending him into a spiral and making him vow to get revenge. He travelled back to Trosky and swore on Istvan's grave that he would kill Henry.

With a lust for Henry's blood, Erik wanted to find Liechtenstein as he would know of Henry's whereabouts. With this in mind, he carried out a pogrom on the Jewish Quarter of Kuttenberg on von Aulitz's orders. He ordered his men to leave Henry to him, but Henry was able to escape with some of the surviving members of the town's Jewish community and gave Erik the slip.

Erik was then tipped off that Henry would be at the Italian Court in Kuttenberg, attempting to steal the royal silver. Although he did not much care for preventing the robbery, Erik very much wanted to seek out Henry and so lead the assault on the Court. He offered Zizka safety and freedom for everyone else involved in exchange for Henry's life.

This offer was not taken up, and so the assault began in earnest. Erik and his men were able to break into the court where he came face to face with Henry. Erik was able to injure Henry but Musa of Mali intervened, knocking Erik over the head and saving Henry's life.

Zizka and his group were then able to escape the court with the silver, but Erik's men were hot in pursuit. Erik himself went to Ruthard Palace, hoping to cut them off, but they were already gone by the time he arrived. He was able to catch up with them on the road as they fled towards Suchdol, injuring Musa and taking Kubyenka captive.

The other men most likely would have killed Kubyenka, as he was not worth any real ransom, but Erik freed him with one stipulation - that he bring a challenge of a duel to Henry at Suchdol. Erik then waited in the remains of Sigismund's camp for Henry to arrive.

If Henry did arrive, Erik fought madly and the fight was fairly even. Eventually, they were interrupted by the arriving Praguer army who had come to attack Suchdol. Recognising things were now looking dire for his comrades, Henry disengaged from the fight and ran back as fast as he could, leaving Erik laughing madly in grief and mocking him.

## Executioner Heinz

Executioner Heinz is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He is a famous executioner from Kuttenberg.

## Biography

He was hired by the townspeople of Rattay to execute three notorious criminals, which aggravated their own local executioner, Hermann. To be denied the right to execute the murderers was insulting, and so Hermann enlisted the help of Henry to embarrass his rival.

Henry would either sabotage the rope, tongs, and/or sword used in the executions, publicly humiliating Heinz, or tip him off to Hermann's tricks, giving him enough time to correct and replace his implements.

Later, having suffered embarrassment due to the failed executions in Rattay, Heinz returned to Kuttenberg and lost his confidence. He later asked Henry to forge him a sword using lucky talismans to break his supposed curse and regain said confidence.

## Exodus

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Exodus is the 21st main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically at the conclusion of The Feast.

## Synopsis

Sigismund has decided to finish the Jews of Kuttenberg for helping Liechtenstein. We have to stop him and save as many people as we can.

## Walkthrough

After agreeing to head to Kuttenberg, Kubyenka will appear with a wagon, late to the party. Get on the wagon and head off for the city. You can talk to everyone a little bit before Kubyenka will initiate fast travel.

Follow Samuel and then Liechtenstein through the underground to get to the Jewish Quarter. You’ll come out in the King Solomon. Head upstairs and take out the enemies inside. Then head out to meet Samuel.

Follow him again and he’ll ask you to get his mother from her house to your left, you’ll have to enter from around the side. Once there, speak to her and the next phase will trigger. Follow her to the backyards. You’ll need to take out some attackers, if you have a ranged weapon you can do so from where you stand otherwise you’ll have to run up the ramparts to get them with a blade.

Keep following Sara, along the way if you are fast enough, you may be able to save a couple of people. Eventually, she’ll stop a the house closest to the synagogue. Head inside and fight off the enemies there and meet back up with Samuel.

Erik’s men will break down the gate and you’ll have to fend them off. This battle section is timed, just keep fighting until the next cutscene triggers.

The aftermath

Once you’ve escaped town, you’ll have the opportunity to talk to Sara about Martin. You can talk to a few people around as well including Rabbi Jehuda, Samuel, and Liechtenstein. After speaking to Sara, the quest will end, starting The Lion's Den.

## Face to Face

Face to Face is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You finally met Markvart von Aulitz.

## Acquisition

The Face to Face achievement is unlocked during the main quest Reckoning. While Henry has previously encountered Markvart von Aulitz during The King's Gambit the achievement refers to a specific and optional encounter much later in the game.

## Tips

As part of Reckoning, Henry is tasked with infiltrating Suchdol village to acquire horses so you can ride for the reinforcements. However, there is a hidden, non-essential objective that triggers the achievement: locating von Aulitz inside the tavern at the center of Suchdol, on the east side of the main road.

To reach the tavern stealthily:

- Approach from the outskirts on the eastern side of the village.

- Enter through the barn located behind the tavern.

- Eliminate the two guards near the campfire to the east. One will periodically patrol west, allowing for isolated takedowns.

- Proceed through the barn and deal with the two guards stationed outside the tavern.

- One guard holds the key to the tavern door, but it can also be accessed via a very hard lockpick.

Once inside the tavern, proceed through the door on the left. This triggers a long cutscene in which Henry comes face to face with von Aulitz, unlocking the achievement upon completion. Successfully sneaking into the tavern without alerting guards increases the chance of triggering the event smoothly.

## Fancy Fighting

Fancy Fighting is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You killed an enemy with a combo.

## Acquisition

Successfully killing an enemy using a combo will unlock the Fancy Fighting achievement.

## Tips

- There are various weapon combos in the game that Henry can learn across Bohemia. Henry begins with a few "natural" combos, but more advanced techniques can be learned from trainers for a fee.

- Combos can be trained in fighting arenas found throughout the game. The first one you're likely to encounter is located at the Nomads' Camp.

- Once you have mastered a combo, wait for an enemy who is either low on health or unaware of your presence, and then execute the combo.

- The higher your skill with a specific weapon type, the easier it becomes to perform combos.

## Farmer Matthew's pitchfork

Farmer Matthew's pitchfork is a melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a polearm.

## Description

A pitchfork left here by farmer Matthew. Everyone in Tachov knows that wherever Matthew and his pitchfork go, merriment follows. It seems Matthew may have gotten a bit too merry, as he left his pitchfork behind.

## Acquisition

The pitchfork can be found stuck in the piles of hay located in an open-sided barn directly behind the Tachov tavern. It is the solitary barn that the path goes through, not the one attached to the tavern building. The pitchfork can be simply taken from the hay, with no need to steal it.

## Farmer Slavek

Farmer Slavek is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Slavek lived in Semine and worked as a farmer. After his rooster Boniface died, he found a replacement in a young black rooster. This rooster was small and stunted and Slavek didn't think much of it until it started laying eggs. Worried about rumours and the risk of someone seeing devilry in it, Slavek killed the rooster and put it on the waste pile in the woods, as it wasn't even big enough for soup.

He ran into Henry while Henry was in Semine looking for such a rooster in the hopes of finding a basilisk egg for Master Voyta of Trosky Castle.

### Associated Quest

- Chiaroscuro

Smil lived and worked in Bohunowitz as a farmer.

His village was often targeted by the soldiers in the service of Sigismund who were stationed nearby in Opatowitz and Sigismund's camp. These soldiers forcibly requisitioned supplies from the village.

## Feline Affection

Feline Affection is a hidden achievement introduced in Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Description

You repeatedly interacted with a cat. Aren't you worried Mutt will know?

## Acquisition

The Feline Affection achievement is earned by interacting with the cat in the Sedletz Monastery library on three separate occasions. The cat can always be found sitting on a shelf in the far-left corner of the library as you enter. A "Kitty kitty…" prompt will appear in the lower-right corner of the screen.

## Tips

- The cat does not always appear in the library – generally, you have a chance to see it as quest objectives are completed.

- If you miss an interaction, you can always return to the monastery for 300 Groschen and find the cat again.

## Field infirmary

Field infirmary is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The infirmary of Sigismund's camp, where illness and injury alike are treated. It is made up of two large tents placed next to each other with canvas for privacy and to give the appearance of different rooms for different purposes. There is a section for surgery with two tables stained with blood and shelves for supplies, a section for convalescence with simple bedrolls laid on the ground, and a section for more peaceful things.

Outside the infirmary tents are basins full of dirty and bloodied water. Further back from the infirmary proper is the residential tent of its main healer, Musa of Mali, and his alchemy supplies for making medicine.

## Fight Dirty

Fight Dirty is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

Thomlin Bruthans founded a fight club in Horschan. If I manage to beat the loca goons, I could get a nice reward.

## Walkthrough

In Horschan, talk to Thomlin Bruthans, you’ll find him working in the south end of the village during the day. He’ll invite you to the fight club in the region where you’ll have to beat three villagers in unarmed combat.

Each combatant will wait his turn by the pig pen that serves as a fighting ring if you would like to do them in one go. With the exception of Stanley, who may beg off for a while.

Tobias is not very interested in fighting and should be a relatively easy match. Tuma is also easy and will tap out before a knock-out. Stanley is the hardest of the three.

Once all three are defeated, head back to Thomlin and he will let you know about a few other fighting circles in the region.

## Objectives

## Flagellum Dei

Flagellum Dei is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It was introduced to the base game with patch 1.3, through the free Horse Racing update.

## Description

You scored 150 points in the mounted archery competition.

## Acquisition

You can unlock this achievement after finishing the Horses for Courses quest. In the Trosky region, visit the Nomads' Camp and speak to Horse handler Mikolai and Bibrek the Archer to initiate the quest.

To progress, you must first complete three mandatory competitions set by Bibrek. Afterward, you can challenge him to additional competitions, each increasing in difficulty.

## Tips

- You don't have to score 150 in a single competition. You actually just need 150 cumulative points across all mounted archery competitions. The difficulty of the competition doesn't matter either, you can chose Easy, Hard or Tengri.

## Trivia

- The achievement's title comes from the Latin phrase "Ego sum Attila flagellum Dei", which means "I am Attila, the scourge of God".
