## For Victory!

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

For Victory! is the 9th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Beginning it will prevent you from completing Demons of Trosky.

## Description

The time has finally come to deal with the bastards that ambushed us by the pond and killed our friends. It won't be long till we attack their lair and make sure none of those whoresons escape justice!

## Synopsis

As night falls and preparations are made, Henry and Hans head to the banquet being hosted by von Bergow. The feast is underway when they arrive, and they are called over to the head table by Chamberlain Ulrich. Salutations are given and von Bergow orders wine to be poured; the woman doing the pouring is none other than Katherine. Bergow talks politics and plans. Once he details the strategy for the upcoming attack, Katherine leaves to get more wine.

Henry socialises with the other attendees, most of them intent on talking about the mishaps of his mission so far. Hans is not feeling very much like doing the same and begs off to go to bed fairly quickly. As part of socialising, Henry may play a trick on a visiting knight, play some dice to pass the time, and have a fling to close out his night.

Before he can do that though, he has some duties to fulfil. Namely, fetching wine and armour for Hans. Osina is out of supplies, all he can provide are the leftovers no one who came by before them wanted though he may be willing to provide better services after some persuasion or a little palm greasing. When Henry goes to the kitchen to look for Katherine, he’s told that she’s nowhere to be found. The cook doesn’t mind doing the job though, since it’s for Hans. All she asks is that Henry help out a little while she does so, the spice chest needs to be unlocked.

In the morning, Henry hands over the provisions to Hans and the party sets out towards Nebakov Fortress. Hans seems optimistic, sure that Nebakov is not impressive enough a fortress to withstand any large-scale attack, joking with Henry that the fight might even be over by the time they get to the battle lines. They meet up with the chamberlain at the gates and are told Black Bartosch has been assigned to keep Hans out of harm’s way.

The company heads out watched closely by residents of Troskowitz, fortunes finally reversed for the former vagabonds. Sometime later, in the woods near the Nebakov Mill, Hans complains about having been taken for a ride last time they were down this way. The chamberlain calls him pathetic, sure his bravado covers up fear of dealing with the bandits. Suddenly, bangs are heard and men start falling from their horses – they’re under attack!

The bandits fell a tree and Henry falls from his horse. Hans helps him up, the chaos of battle unfolding around them. They fight their way through bandits, trying to keep moving forward along the road. A ways ahead, the chamberlain gets stuck under his horse. Hans is able to free him, but he is shot and dies soon after.

Eventually, they are able to fight their way to the mill itself. Here, Hans is injured by a bandit and falls to the ground, losing his helm. Henry takes down the bandit and checks on Hans before realising the two of them are surrounded. The bandit leader calls off his men, admonishing Henry for his foolishness when Henry intends to face them alone to protect Hans.

Since he’s open to talk, Henry takes advantage, throwing his own harsh words back. Henry’s insistence on the depravity of ambushes and the worthiness of full-on combat convinces the bandit leader to take him on one-on-one. He proposes a duel, if Henry survives he can keep his life – something that amuses the other bandits.

Henry wins, the bandit leader only spared thanks to the quick intervention of his men. He’s impressed by Henry’s show and Michael lets slip his real name – Zizka. He asks Henry if Henry believes so deplorable a man as Henry thinks he is will keep his word as his men restrain Henry.

The battle over, the bandits string up some of the men from Trosky and leave the field.

## Walkthrough

Note that after you talk to Hans to attend the evening banquet here, you'll be locked in; you won't be able to do other side quests and you'll lose access to the Trosky region for a while, so only talk to him when ready to move forward with the main storyline.

Once it's evening (20:00), go talk to Hans and you'll attend the banquet with him. As you talk with Otto von Bergow and Ulrich, you'll notice Katherine is also there, serving wine. You have a speech check that you can answer, or choose to remain silent. Eventually von Bergow will reveal his plan: to attack Nebakov Fortress at dawn the next day, with Ulrich leading the assault on account of Captain Thomas still being ill and von Bergow expecting an important visitor to arrive.

Ulrich will then reveal his idea: a frontal assault, which obviously sounds like a bad idea and Hans will voice his disagreement. You can choose to remain silent or back Hans up on this (if you speak up, Hans will thank you later for some reputation gain). Regardless, von Bergow will insist he trusts Ulrich to handle the assault just fine and will dismiss you to enjoy yourselves.

### Mingle with guests

At this point, you can talk around with other guests at the banquet. With von Bergow, you can discuss the situation a bit more but nothing else comes of it.

-
Bushek and Hanko

-
Hans

-
Jezhek and Olbram

-
Bartosch

-
Widow Johanka

-
Hermann Littlehead

You'll likely be immediately flagged down to the right by Bushek Dub and Hanko Goathead, who discuss the ambush at the pond. Eventually Hanko will invite you to play him at dice, when you can agree to for 110 .

Hans meanwhile is standing off to the side of the other table, away from the rest and will call to you to talk to him. He'll reveal he's not happy with the chamberlain, or the feast for that matter as it's all just for show and not actually getting anything done. Answer him how you wish before he advises you not to drink to be ready for the fight tomorrow, before he heads off.

Knights Jezhek and Olbram are standing between the two main tables and can be talked to to learn von Bergow paid a lot for something called the "Finger of God." However, neither has a clue what exactly it is, though he got it from Prague. They'll then remark how von Bergow seems to be doing well despite the war going on.

Black Bartosch is standing behind the table with Ulrich and von Bergow. As he's on duty, he can't drink, but will gladly discuss politics and the guests with you. Note if you want to have a fling with him, you need to ask about the local girls, after which he'll insinuate he'd prefer Henry's company, then pass a medium speech check. If you accidentally selected that option but don't want any romance, you can back out by noting you'd rather not. Otherwise, let him know you'd like to meet up later that night with him. When you've done all you've wanted for the night, return to him to let him know and they'll spend the night together and cut to the morning.

Johanka is a young widow and noblewoman seated between Father Nicodemus and Erazim at the table opposite von Bergow. Note that accepting her advances for a fling will end the party. If you wish you have the fling, it's easiest to wait to engage in conversation with her until you've done all other objectives. If you don't wish to have a fling with her, or you don't mind turning her down once, feel free to talk to her at any time.

She'll have a a speech check that has a medium, easy, and hard option, respectively. Continue your story how you wish until it turns to the bailiff, where you should then pick "The Bailiff was right to punish us" as she'll then invite you to escort her outside for a bit. There, she'll be glad you got her away from the old men and then opens up the option to have a fling or not.

Hermann Littlehead is standing at the other table. When you talk to him, he'll reveal he wants to play a joke on another knight there, Florian, to get even for an earlier prank Florian pulled on Hermann. If you agree, he'll instruct you to go get Florian's ring, which is in his quarters in the Crone tower and off limits.

If you do this, it's relatively easy, just bear in mind that it's considered a private area from the scribe's chambers and up, and there are two guards who patrol around there. Florian's chest is in the first room on the very top floor, against the opposite wall. Loot it for the ring and then head back to the feast with it and let Hermann know. He'll then direct you to present it to the young woman on Florian's right, Adleta of Straz.

Talk to Adleta and tell her it's from "a shy friend" to set off the older woman on Florian's left, Mareta of Bor, who'll call out Florian for cheating. Go let Hermann know the deed is done and he'll reward you with a Weak Saviour Schnapps and The Strength of the Knight III.

### Get the armour

Go see Osina, who's working late in his forge. He'll tell you he has nothing left, as the other knights already cleaned him out earlier. With a medium speech check, you can get him to cough up a weapon and some armour for Hans. Otherwise you'll need to pay him or find another way to get the items. If you got the items, he'll give you a common longsword, Saxon plate legs, Noble's gauntlets, Saxon bascinet, and Smooth cuirass.

### Get the wine

Head into the Maiden tower kitchen and talk to Manyeta about where to find Katherine to get the requested wine. At Katherine's name, Manyeta will insist she'll get it herself, as Katherine seems to have disappeared. While she does though, she'll ask you to unlock the herbs chest which, like the spice one, gets stuck a lot. This medium-locked chest is in the kitchen, in the small corner near some shelves and a table.

Once unlocked, let Manyeta know and she'll give you the wine for Capon.

### Go to sleep

Once you've done all you've wanted for this quest's objectives, either go to your own bed next to the forge or, if you're opting for a fling with Bartosch or Johanka, approach them with the right dialogue, which will then cut to the morning.

### Marching out

Marching out

The following morning, go talk to Hans, who'll automatically be given the wine. For weapon and armour though, you'll have to select all the pieces you want to give him (if you want to keep the gear from Osina, have a few cheap pieces on hand, as Hans has his own custom armour and weapon he will use regardless). Once everything is handed over, go mount up and follow him out, where you can give your own input on a couple points before they meet up with Ulrich and Bartosch at the gates. A cutscene will then play out as the army heads out for all the region to see, and into the ravine forest area. Before setting out, make sure you clear as much inventory space as possible and bring a few Artemisias with you as there is a ton of gear to loot during the next part of the quest. You'll also probably want some Aqua Vitalis, Buck's Blood potion, and maybe some Painkiller brew for all the fighting ahead.

All smiles

### Ambush!

As Ulrich talks with you and Hans, a sudden blast is heard, killing a soldier in front of you and knocking down a tree behind you, preventing any retreat that way. Hans will eventually help you back to your feet, and you'll then have to help fight off bandits to try and get to Ulrich. When you find the chamberlain, he's pinned under his horse and Hans will try to get him out. However, no matter what you do here, Ulrich will be killed. With no other choice, continue to follow Hans down the path, taking out bandits as you go.

Note, there's a LOT of valuable gear and groschen to loot here with no penalties if you can do so quickly (Hans can die if he gets too far ahead, failing the quest) -- prioritize looting named Knights that have fallen. There should be 3 named knights right when you regain control after the ambush cutscene that all have extremely high quality loot and roughly 100 groschen each.

Save Hans!

Eventually you'll reach a spot where the bandits blocked off the road further south so instead, crouch and follow the dirt path to the right to and go under the fallen tree. More bandits will be waiting at the top of this side route. Past them, you'll drop down a ledge here where Hans is crouching and the game will autosave. Further on, several more groups remain, including several archers near the mill. After they're dead, continue to follow Hans until you reach a small stream cutting across the road for another cutscene where Hans gets knocked out briefly and the bandit leader approaches, remarking they'll get a nice ransom for Hans.

The duel

Eventually the leader will duel you to test your mettle. After a few hits, Henry will slash the man's left eye, causing another cutscene where the other bandits step in to prevent you from killing their leader before they proceed to hang some of the soldiers from a nearby tree.

### Godwin

A small cutscene plays out with Godwin, who's now arrived in the area. After a short conversation with the innkeeper Lawrence at Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn, he'll be directed to where the massacre occurred, as well as some people he can talk to that escaped from the mill before cutting to the the next main quest to find Henry and Hans.

## For Whom the Bell Tolls

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

For Whom the Bell Tolls is the 6th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is a timed quest that picks up immediately following Wedding Crashers.

Note: due to the time limit, no access to your normal gear, and thus no way to do manual saves, you'll have to plan or make use of auto-saves well here to make the most of your items.

## Description

Me and Sir Hans finally got to Trosky, but it certainly didn't turn out the way we expected. Capon was accused of poaching and is facing the gallows. Luckily, Captain Thomas is in the castle - he saw our letter and knows we're messengers from Rattay and not just some vagabonds. But Thomas is lying wounded and feverish in the chapel in the Maiden Tower.

## Synopsis

The morning after the wedding, Henry and Hans find themselves in jail in the Trosky Castle jail. Hans feels the walls are closing in on them, anxious to be in a less dark and cramped place, but the guards won’t bother responding. Henry, for his part, is less fussed. Hans apologises for his recent behaviour, and asks what Henry’s been up to since they parted ways. The two talk about their respective times since their last conversation until the guards talking interrupt them. Captain Thomas, it seems, is in a bad way; he was attacked and struck by fever and the castle physician away with its lord.

Sometime later, the guards finally turn their attention to the wayward messengers. Guard Kroupa says there’s work for Henry while keeping Hans in the cell. When Hans complains, insisting he be allowed to talk to the ailing captain, Kroupa replies he should want to talk to God – Hans is set to hang for poaching. The bells of Trosky rings out, twelve more, Kroupa says, and the priest will come for Hans.

Henry’s been given a much lighter sentence, all he has to do to make amends is work off his debt. It seems no one at the castle believes Hans when he says he’s a noble – they all think him mad. Kroupa advises Henry the best he can do is pray for his lunatic friend and pretend not to know him. As for the captain vouching for them, no one wants to hear anything with his life on the line; Thomas has been moved to the chapel at the top of the Maiden tower to be closer to God in what may be his final hours. As a not so honoured guest, Henry is not allowed entry into any portion of the castle, least of all the summit of its towers.

All Henry can do for now is what’s told of him, work until there’s no work left for him. He’s to start by hauling sacs of charcoal and once that’s done, the blacksmith Osina should have some work for him along with some work down by the scaffolding in the outer bailey.

Henry is able to gain access to the castle, either by helping Chamberlain Ulrich and receiving permission or by sneaking in through a well. Once inside, he makes it to the chapel and talks with Thomas’s sister, Adela. Thomas needs something to treat his fever.

Henry can make a tonic for Thomas or else find one in the Crone Tower, if he hasn’t already. When he gets to the surgeon’s work room, Henry finds Katherine there looking through the surgeon’s things. She is still quite reticent, unwilling to talk about herself, but may let Henry know where he can find some ingredients he needs. The tonic gets Thomas on his feet, and he is carried down the tower supported by Henry and Adela just as the final bell tolls.

Hans is brought to the gallows, with most of the denizens of Trosky having come out to watch. The chamberlain speaks to the crowd, insisting again that Hans is mad and impersonating a noble or else delusional enough to believe he is one when he clearly is not. As Hans is placed on the gallows, Henry tries to stop the execution, Thomas in tow.

The chamberlain is not willing to listen, insisting that Thomas is delirious and even if he were to vouch for Hans his testimony could not be counted on. Hans is somewhat emboldened by the display, calling out again that he’s a noble and this punishment is unlawful. Guards restrain Henry and the executioner is just about to kick the log Hans is perched on when there comes a commotion at the gates – von Bergow has returned.

Although injured, he insists the hanging at least be delayed until he can look into Hans’ claims of nobility.

## Walkthrough

The two will talk a bit, with Hans mustering up an apology for his behaviour back in Troskowitz. Note: the conversation here is slightly different if you found him prior to Wedding Crashers or not, but overall has no change on the outcome here - Hans had been poaching, which is a crime punishable by death.

Kroupa will take you out to a wagon and directs you to your first job: haul charcoal sacks up to a shed. You can try to plead for Hans' case, and while he'll ignore this, he will reveal some crucial details: Thomas is in the chapel at the very top of the Maiden tower. You can ask him more on this and other things before getting to work.

You have 12 in-game hours to save Hans from execution. At his point, you'll need to work relatively quickly/without too much meandering. However, if you're a completionist/like to get as many optional objectives done as possible, you'll still be able to do that with time to spare. If, however, you want to get through quickly, make sure you're adept at thievery, alchemy, and scholarship and/or survival. Henry will remark each time the bell tolls, noting which number it is so you know how much time you have left.

### Charcoal sacks

For the sacks, you'll need to take three of them to a shed all the way up the hill. Depending on your stats, this can be done relatively quickly, but you may notice on your initial way up the hill, Vuytek is there, trying to work off his punishment as well. However, he's instead fruitlessly trying to pick up yet another woman, this time Magda. You can intervene to tell him to get back to work and, if you really want to get at it, reveal the truth to Magda that he's working off his punishment. Otherwise, you can try and be nice and lie. If you reveal the truth so that Magda gets mad at Vuytek and leaves, Vuytek will likewise get mad at Henry, and no matter what is said there, he'll promise to find you later to fight this out. However, he won't do it during this quest, so you don't need to worry he'll jump you during any of this.

After completing the sacks, you'll then have the option for the other two jobs Kroupa mentioned: helping at the gallows and talking to the blacksmith.

### Blacksmith

Talk to Osina, whose workshop is near the charcoal shed (which you passed by whilst dropping off the sacks). He'll task you to go make a horseshoe that Kabat needs, giving you safe access to the inner bailey.

In the inner bailey, you can get the materials you need out of the chest in the forge and craft the horseshoe. Depending on perks you have enabled, this might actually net you some lockpicks without needing to buy/steal them.

### Kabat

Talking to Kabat will reveal he used to live a slightly less than honest life beforehand. Fortunately, he hasn't quite left that behind and can sell lockpicks, but unless you're able to go around and pickpocket for money or stealthily steal items to sell him, this may not be a good option to get them. However, what he does need help with is recovering a rosary that Father Nicodemus took off of him.

Nicodemus wanders around in the area past the charcoal shed, going from sitting on a bench to standing at the ramparts. If you're good enough at pickpocketing, you can try to get the turquoise rosary off him that way. Otherwise, he'll want you to play dice but you have to cough up 20 groschen as your wager. If you succeed in getting it, bring it to Kabat and he'll give you 3 lockpicks in return. Alternatively, giving it to Jarek leads you directly to Thomas, but this option skips most of the quest.

### Gallows

Head down to the gallows and find Kolda, who's sawing away at a log. He'll ask you to go get his axe and sharpen it. The axe is across the area, in a chest in a shed near a sharpening wheel. Once retrieved and sharpened, bring it back to him. Arrguing for Hans' innocence will do nothing to convince him, but if you talk to him about the other topics and he'll reveal someone in the past, Binyek, made it into the chapel once by climbing down from the courtyard's well. Of course, the guards have since cut off climbing down this well, but you can jump in if you want to try that route, though this isn't the most optimal and can lead to an injured leg.

### Cook Fanka

After you've finished with the sacks and got Osina's job to go make horseshoes, go into the courtyard and you'll see a woman, Fanka, standing near the blacksmithing forge. Talk to her and she'll reveal she needs help with a stuck lock on her spice chest, and the blacksmith has still not helped her with it, so it's kept getting stuck for three years. You can say you will help her, but you'll need tools first to do so if you haven't already found some. Note you can find some without asking the stablehand, say you'll help Fanka, then return and ask the blacksmith and he'll still give you some lockpicks. Once you get the lockpicks from him, an auto-save will occur here.

Once you have some lockpicks, let her know and follow her to the chest in the kitchen area. It's an easy lock so even those without much skill should be able to open it for her. She'll thank you and offer for you to drop by the kitchen when you want, allowing you access to talk to the chamberlain who's there.

### Chamberlain

Once you've gained access to the kitchen, you'll hear Ulrich complaining while looking in pain. Approach and remark on his health issues. With a medium speech check you can convince him you know how to diagnose and he'll let you try. You are then given 4 topics to ask, 2 easy checks ("what have you tried" and "I'll examine you, sir") and 2 medium ("describe the pain" and "What's your lifestyle?"). You can do all 4 if you want to get a full overview. If done right, Henry will confirm Ulrich has stomach ulcers and can be treated with a new diet, while temporary relief can be given with a Digestive potion. However, you don't have the tools to make the potion, so he'll grant you access to the Crone Tower where the alchemy bench is. This also creates an auto-save here.

Once you have the potion in-hand (see crone tower section below), go back to the chamberlain and give it to him, and eventually you can ask him to give you access to the chapel without issue. Note after this quest, you can approach him later about this and he'll properly thank you with 25 .

### Gaining access to the Crone tower

From the inner bailey near the forge, if you go right and up the stairs, you'll find a small kitchen with a guard standing watch at the stairs on the far end. He can easily be persuaded to let you by, by bringing him food or by letting him know you have permission from the chamberlain (if you have it already) and he'll let you go up.

Go all the way up the stairs to a red door. Open it to find a small hallway with two closed doors on opposite sides and go through the right one to find none other than Katherine snooping around. With medium speech check, you can convince her to help you out and she'll reveal there are chests in the other room that contain some things you could use, but they're hard locked.

Note even if you weren't able to examine/help the chamberlain, one item you still need for Thomas is in this tower: the fever tonicum potion. One is found in a chest in the scribe's quarters, by his bed. The other is in one of the hard locked chests mentioned above. If you're not able to lockpick these, you can instead brew one. To do so, you'll need to steal the Physician's journal that's on a shelf in the room with the alchemy bench and read it, which will then add the fever tonic recipe to your list. All the ingredients needed are in the chest that Katherine was poking around in which is locked by an easy lock. Note: this journal will disappear after this quest, so if you want to get it for the recipe, you have to do it during this quest.

### Gaining access to the Maiden tower

Once you've gained permission to access the chapel by the chamberlain, you can come up here without issue. If you didn't gain lawful access though, there's only one guard so you can try and distract them from behind by throwing a rock. Note that while you can take the well route into this tower if you couldn't help the chamberlain, this will only lead you into the dungeons/right next to where Hans is, requiring you to still have to sneak all the way up.

Head all the way up to the top of the tower and enter the room here to find Adela, Thomas' sister, trying to treat him. If you already picked up the fever tonicum, Henry will automatically give it to her and a cutscene will play out to end the quest. Otherwise, you need to go retrieve or make one for her.

### Talking to von Bergow

Despite your best efforts, Ulrich won't listen and will try to have Hans hanged. However, just as he's about to do so, von Bergow arrives, wondering what the hell is going on and stops the hanging before he collapses off his horse.

After a short time, and in better clothes, von Bergow will formally welcome Hans and Henry with a slightly embarrassed chamberlain. After a discussion about the current political climate and issues, von Bergow will note he isn't up for discussing if he's open to changing which king he backs until he's dealt with troubles going on in his own region. As you've likewise had issues with bandits in his area, Hans and Henry volunteer to help, so von Bergow will ask you to go to Nebakov Fortress to have Jaromier Nebak supply aid.

## Forbidden Fruit

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Forbidden Fruit is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It immediately follows after completing Materia Prima for Kreyzl.

## Walkthrough

Go talk to Bonnie, who's on the other side of the river from Lower Semine Mill, at The Lair. If you want to earn a little extra reputation, be sure to bring at least one fresh herb for her. She'll talk with you, opening a way to talk a bit more about your lives and earn further reputation, otherwise you can choose to bypass this and get straight to business.

She'll eventually reveal Kreyzl needs a lot of saltpetre and as they've already scoured the whole area and taken what they could find, this only leaves one last option: getting it from pits with carcasses. However, they don't know where the local gravedigger, Ignatius, buries such bodies, so you'll need to go talk to him. She'll also suggest you bring him some fresh meat to gain his favor.

### Skipping Ignatius (Option A)

You can do the entire quest to find the pit. Or, it's directly east of Ignatius' graveyard. Past the sheep pen, next to the road that passes the graveyard and the pen.

### Helping Ignatius (Option B)

While you can give him fresh meat, in the end you'll still be dragged along to help him out before he'll show you the pit's location. If it's not at the right time (early in the morning), he'll offer you some reading material in his outhouse and some money to rent a place to sleep in Troskowitz if needed. Once it's around the right time, go talk to Ignatius and go sit on the wagon. Note: you won't be able to access your horse's inventory (including moving stuff over) until you are taken to the pit, so be sure you have enough space to not become encumbered or other ways to mitigate it as you'll be hauling around a few sacks.

As you're riding through the area, Ignatius will discuss Kreyzl and his shady hired hands before making his first stop at an unmarked abandoned hut. He'll then send you in to retrieve the deer carcass and bring it back to the wagon for him. There will be a wolf here before you can enter the hut. Note also the room you need to get to has a very hard lock, so unless you're able to lockpick it quickly, instead head back outside and to the side of the hut is a fence with some barrels. Climb up and then over the fence, walk around the outside here, and through the window into the locked room to find the carcass. Pack it up and bring it back to the wagon, only to find Ignatius dealing with some would-be avengers.

The men will note they were stolen from by a couple thieves that were seen in the area, Scruffy and Dunger, aliases used by Bonnie and Zinek. You'll have an easy speech check here to convince the men to leave without issue, otherwise you'll only be able to attack them.

After that, get back on the wagon and Ignatius will go to the second stop, explaining they're picking up a couple dead pigs that, despite superstitions, sounds like they were poisoned. At the place, the woman will talk a bit to Ignatius about it, while also dropping hints about the third stop (a dog that's been annoying everyone in the area). If you want to do the optional step here to find the source of the infection, head towards the house and then walk up the small path on the other side going north into the forest. When you find the stream, follow it northeast a short ways and you'll find the source: several dead deer in the water. To save a little running back and forth, go back to the pig pen and bag up and carry one pig back to the wagon, then let Ignatius know of the source. An hour will pass as you both take care of that, allowing you to then go back and get the last pig and talk to Ignatius to let him know it's done.

There's approximately 30 Belladonna in a close proximity to the left side of the wagon, so be sure to use this opportunity to grab it before mounting up on the wagon.

Get back on the wagon a third time, and Ignatius will fill you in on the last task, but this one isn't about hauling a carcass. Rather, it's to kill a dog that's been bothering everyone. You can try to refuse, but Ignatius will hold it over your head he won't reveal the location of the pit unless you do so. That said, if you don't want to kill the dog, there's a way out of it without having to find the pit on your own.

Reaching the final stop, head to the marker to find the dog isn't in the shed. You'll soon hear barking coming from the northeast. Head that way and towards the lone tree across the road to find none other than Bonnie with the dog in question. You can explain that you were sent to kill the dog and she'll get upset, saying she'd like to keep the dog after her last one died. She'll also explain she saw how Veisar treated the dog the last time she was in the area. If you don't want to kill Monarch, you can agree to let her keep him and she'll be happy and quickly takes him away.

Head back to Ignatius and, if you let him go, you can try and lie that you killed him. If you pass the medium speech check, he'll be convinced you did the job and approve. He'll then take you to the pit, where you'll have no choice but to taste it to make sure it's saltpetre, much to Ignatius' amusement. He'll also give you Knacker's gloves for assisting him.

In the open hole, you should see a prompt to taste it on one of the walls. After tasting and confirming it's saltpetre, you can talk to Ignatius to head back to the cemetery, though he'll request you help him bury the newest carcasses, taking two hours.

Head back to Kreyzl to let him know the location and he'll reward you with 85 Groschen and As Quiet as a Cat II. He will then lead right into the next quest, Opus Magnum.

## Objectives

- Find the saltpetre pit and taste it to see if there's actually saltpetre in it.

- Talk to Bonnie.

- Visit the gravedigger.

- Accompany the gravedigger on this rounds.

- Follow Ignatius to the wagon.

- Find the carcass in the ruined farm.

- Bring the carcass to the wagon.

- Protect Ignatius from the farm hands.

- Talk to Ignatius.

- Follow Ignatius to the wagon.

- Find the source of infection. (Optional)

- Clear the carcasses from the farms.

- Talk to Ignatius.

- Follow Ignatius to the wagon.

- Take care of the greengrocer's dog.

- Talk to Ignatius.

- Return to the miller.

## Foreman Fett

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Don't tell me one of the yackers shat all over the outhouse in the yard again?

Foreman Fett (Czech: Předák Máslo), or head gaffer, as he called himself, was a miner working in the royal silver mines near Horschan.

He was responsible for maintaining discipline among the other foremen and their crews. In addition, his duties included counting the corves of ore extracted and recording the totals in the record books.

Fett was appointed head foreman after his predecessor, Kercher, fell down a shaft.

## Involvement

Henry met him during the investigation into Ulrich Vavak's scheme for stealing and counterfeiting the King's silver. By questioning every foreman of the three miner shifts about how many corves of silver ore they extracted on a specific day - he found out that the amount Fett recorded in the books is false. When pressured, Fett admitted to the fraud.

As soon as he was made the head foreman, a person from Grund's smelting works approached him. He made it very clear if Fett didn't cooperate, he could suffer an "accident", just like his predecessor. They agreed that Fett would underreport a portion of the extracted ore and use the extra groschen from the smelting works to pay the miners and his accomplice, ore merchant Hermann.

The fraud had been ongoing for at least half a year - beginning around the time king Sigismund arrived and Vavak became the mint master. Henry ultimately put a stop to it, but not before promising that Fett and Hermann wouldn’t face punishment for the capital offense, provided they remained silent to avoid alerting bigger players - namely, the mint master himself.

In the end, he met his fate on the slag pile with a broken neck. Christian of Pisek suggested that it was likely Hermann had told someone that the scheme had been uncovered, and Fett paid the price for it.

### Associated quest

- Via Argentum

## Foreman Frank

Foreman Frank (Czech: Předák Franta) is a miner, who works in the royal silver mines near Horschan. He leads the first mining shift of the day.

## Involvement

Henry has a chance to meet him during the investigation into Ulrich Vavak's scheme for stealing and counterfeiting the king's silver. The task of uncovering the conspiracy begins with questioning members of the three miner shifts about how many corves of silver ore they extracted on a specific day - the Feast of St. Petronilla.

Before revealing any useful information, Frank demands Henry to bring him some beer for wasting his time. After bribing him with the beer or money or intimidating him, Henry learns that Frank and his crew yielded 36 corves of ore on the day of the feast.

## Foreman Paul

Foreman Paul (Czech: Předák Pavel) is a miner, who works in the royal silver mines near Horschan. He leads the second mining shift of the day.

## Involvement

Henry has a chance to meet him during the investigation into Ulrich Vavak's scheme for stealing and counterfeiting the king's silver. The task of uncovering the conspiracy begins with questioning members of the three miner shifts about how many corves of silver ore they extracted on a specific day - the Feast of St. Petronilla.

Pavel is seemingly nowhere to be found, but his crew reveals that he’s usually at the lowest level of the mines, praying for a young miner - a member of his crew - who died the day before the feast. Pavel later explains that the deceased miner was his nephew, whom he had raised since boyhood after his sister passed away. The young man hadn’t even completed a full week on the job before the accident, and Pavel blames himself for his death.

When Henry asks for the information he needs, Pavel only requests that he pray with him for a while. Afterward, he reveals that his crew mined 30 corves of ore on the day of the feast.

## Foreman Samko

Foreman Samko (Czech: Předák Samko) is a miner, who works in the royal silver mines near Horschan. He leads the last mining shift of the day.

## Involvement

Henry has a chance to meet him during the investigation into Ulrich Vavak's scheme for stealing and counterfeiting the king's silver. The task of uncovering the conspiracy begins with questioning members of the three miner shifts about how many corves of silver ore they extracted on a specific day - the Feast of St. Petronilla.

Before revealing any useful information, Samko challenges Henry to a dice game. After beating him, bribing him, or persuading him, Henry learns that Samko and his crew mined 34 corves of ore on the day of the feast.

### Associated quest

- Via Argentum

## Dialogue

Are you Foreman Samko?

Foreman Samko: Aye, I am. And who's askin'?

Henry: My name is Henry. Steward Christian sent me to you.

Henry: I'm a student from Prague, and I'm writing a treatise on miners and mine operations.

(Chose "student" cover story.)

Henry: My family runs mines, so I came here to gain experience.

(Chose "nobleman" cover story.)

Henry: I'm his nephew, he wants me to learn about his work.

(Chose "nephew" cover story.)

Foreman Samko: Why should I care? Divvent ye see we're off graft?

Henry: Sir Christian told me to ask about anything that interests me. And that you'll tell me.

Foreman Samko: Ah, sonny… I'm so tired, I haven't even got the strength for a gabbing. I wouldn't mind havin' a game of dice but. Miners' rules. Then I'll tell ye everything. What do ye say?

Let's play Miners', then.

Henry: Alright, let's do it. I don't think I've played Miners' with a real miner before.

Foreman Samko: See, kiddar? There's a first time fer everything. Let's crack on, let the groschen roll!

(After finishing the dice game.)

Foreman Samko: Great game, sonny.

Henry: Now will you tell me what I want to know?

Foreman Samko: Aye, ask away.

What is the work of a miner about?

Foreman Samko: Aye, that's a good question, marra. Mostly about howking, any yacker will tell ye that. But proper rest is even more important than graft. Yer as weak as a midge without it.

How do you rest?

Henry: So how do you rest?

Foreman Samko: Depends. Some have a kip, some a swally, some go whoring. As for me, I play dice.

How do you mine ore?

Foreman Samko: Either we're on hard rock and then no one's hewing shit, or we're hewing something soft and then it goes grand. Only then there's not much silver in the ore and you've got to smelt the shit out of it.

How much do you make?

Henry: How much do you make doing this?

Foreman Samko: Don't even get me started. The chink's bad and it's getting worse. Half a groschen a corf is nowt.

How much did you mine on the feast of St. Petronilla?

Henry: How many corves did you mine on, say… the feast of St. Petronilla?

Foreman Samko: I can tell you exactly. All the yackers were working and we were getting along nicely. We managed to howk thirty-four corves without skimping on hyem-time! First time in ages, that was.

Henry: That's all I need to know.

Foreman Samko: If ye need owt else, feel free to drop by.

## Forge Waffenrock

Forge Waffenrock is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Legacy of the Forge DLC.

## Description

The tournament organiser, Fridusch, suggested I should have a waffenrock made with my forge’s emblem and take part in the tournament wearing it.

## Walkthrough

After speaking with Fridusch Kumel and pledging for the tournament, head to the tailor’s near the Town Hall and ask for a blacksmith’s waffenrock. Master Tuchmacher will be able to make it for you right away for 300 groschen, non-negotiable. Once you pay for it, you’ll wait an hour for him to be done.

When he’s finished, you’ll receive the Waffenrock of Henry's Forge, ending the quest. Now, you’ll be able to earn prestige in the tournament by wearing the waffenrock while you compete.

## Fortuna

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Fortuna is the 3rd main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, immediately following Easy Riders.

## Description

Me and Hans Capon managed to flee from the raiders who attacked us at the pond. We found refuge that night with Bozhena, and old herb woman living nearby. She took care of me, but Sir Hans got worse during the night. Now I have to get my strength back and then help Bozhena care for Sir Hans, if at all possible.

## Synopsis

Henry is losing strength, the injuries he’s sustained while escaping the bandits catching up with him. Sir Hans supports him as they wander the woods in search of help. Along the way, Henry sees many images of his past and his fears – a massing army of Cumans headed by Sigismund and von Aulitz, an approaching rider cutting him down, the slaughter and razing of Skalitz, Bianca’s body, his father sending him off with the sword for Sir Radzig, his parents being cut down. Hans is distraught, worried that Henry will succumb to his wounds.

Hans spots a light in the distance which turns out to be a small cottage with an old herbwoman inside. At first she mistakes the men for her daughter, Pavlena, before Hans explains they need help. A bandit appears, having managed to follow them. He rushes in to attack and Hans hits him over the head with a jug before kicking and grappling with him on the floor. Henry tries to reach for the sword, but the bandit manages to get to it first and Hans tackles him through the doorway and Henry loses consciousness.

In his dreams, he sees his parents again, reliving the attack on Skalitz, his subsequent escape to Talmberg, and the stand-off there with von Aulitz. He is woken by the herbwoman; she is relieved he’s conscious as he was in dire condition through the night. Henry is barely well enough to get up, but Hans suffered an injury grappling with the bandit and requires some healing himself.

The herbwoman tells Henry to get bandaged and set right and she gives him her name – Bozhena. She prays for Hans while Henry does as he’s told before checking in on Hans. Bozhena has some of the medicine she gave Henry left, but Hans’ fever is too high for it to be of any use; Henry needs to gather the herbs and brew a chamomile decoction to lower it, as Bozhena’s eyes are too poor to do it herself. She’d also appreciate it if he could take care of the, now dead, bandit in her yard.

Henry may bury the bandit by the creek and gathers the herbs. Upon returning from fetching the herbs, Henry hears Bozhena’s dog barking – two strangers, Mikesh and Kozliek, have arrived. Henry can talk them down, lying and saying they have come to the wrong place or else dispatch them with violence. Either way, Bozhena will be shaken. She asks Henry who he really is and why the bandits are so dogged in their search for him, and is pleased if he tells her the truth.

Hans is more stable, but he requires the decoction in order to improve further. Henry brews it with Bozhena’s help and she puts him to bed saying he won’t miss anything and he could really use the rest to recuperate. In the night, Henry has another nightmare, focused again on the attack on Skalitz, the stolen sword, and its current bearer – Istvan Toth.

The next morning, Henry is awoken by Pavlena, now home. She tells him Hans is awake and as lively as ever and the two discuss Henry’s dreams. Hans is as relieved that Henry is up and about as Henry is about him, now they can finally finish their duty, but first some light conversation. Hans asks that Henry regale the women with his heroic deeds, in saving Hans’ hide, and Henry in turn thanks him for repaying the favour. However, they do have a mission to complete so they can’t sit around all day. They thank Bozhena again for her service, vowing to pay her back once things are put to rights.

They head off in fine spirits, no longer in immanent danger and eager to get back to a sense of normalcy. When they get to Trosky Castle, tired from their long walk, they find the gates closed. The master is away, and the guards have been advised not to let anyone enter. Dressed in rags as they are, Henry and Hans don’t make a very imposing pair and the guards would rather toss human waste on Hans than hear him out. The ruckus attracts the attention of the castle chamberlain, but he is not impressed either, claiming that Sir Hans Capon is dead and his body was found alongside that of his company, so the two must be lying. To add insult to injury, the man who could vouch for them – Captain Thomas – was also waylaid by bandits and is in a delirium.

Thoroughly dismissed, Henry and Hans have no choice but to head to the nearest village – Troskowitz.

## Walkthrough

The quest begins as Henry is carried through the woods by Sir Hans, barely conscious. Along the way, Henry hallucinates, and Hans asks what he’s seeing. The responses don’t affect anything.

After a few minutes, Hans brings Henry to a hut, and a series of cutscenes play. Henry later wakes up inside, where a healer named Bozhena has been tending to him. However, due to his injuries, Henry has lost most of his skill points from the fall and must regain them gradually throughout the rest of the game.

Hans is resting, recovering from a beating he took during a bandit attack on the healer’s hut. Meanwhile, Bozhena gives Henry a few tasks to get back on his feet: stop your bleeding, wash up, and eat something.

Open your inventory and use 4 bandages to stop the bleeding. You already have them on you. Right in front of your bed is a pot of food. Interact with it twice to fill up. Step outside and use the water tub just in front of the house by the stairs to clean yourself off.

Head back inside and speak to Bozhena. You’ll get a few dialogue options. Here’s how they play out:

First Dialogue Choices:

- “I know about herbs” → *Fails* (Reputation-)/may succeed if survival buff was chosen in the initial stat choices

- “How do I recognise the herbs?” → *Bozhena explains*:

- Sage = Purple blossoms

- Chamomile = White petals with a yellow centre

- “Lethean potion is dangerous, isn’t it?” → *No effect*

Second Dialogue Choices:

- “I think I can manage” → *Success* (Reputation+)

- “You’re right, I don’t feel great” → *No effect*

To bury the body, find the spade just ahead of you and pick up the body. Follow the compass indicator, dig a hole, and bury the bandit once you reach the indicated area.

To get to the meadow, head up the path to your left, behind the cottage. Continue to follow the path until you see a dead tree, the herbs should be just ahead to your left.

When you come back to the cottage, some of the bandits will be there: Mikesh and Kozliek. There is an axe just to your right, leaning against a log with which you can arm yourself. If you didn’t bury the body, they will attack you on sight. If you did, however, they will tell you they have been sent on behalf of von Bergow and are looking for the men who ambushed ‘some knight’s company’ the night previous.

You can tell them your true identity, initiating combat, or you can tell them they don’t seem like von Bergow’s men and then lie that they are looking in the wrong place at which point they will leave peacefully. If you deal enough damage to the leader, Mikesh, they will run away. You can give chase and kill them or else let them go.

Note: They come up in a few quests later in the game, so it is recommended to handle things peacefully with them.

Once they have been dealt with, go talk to Bozhena. She will ask after your identity, feel free to tell her the truth as it will improve your reputation with her. She then asks that you brew the potion for Hans and that you bury the bodies of the bandits, if they did not willingly leave. Instructions for the chamomile decoction can be found here, although Bozhena will walk you through it if you tell her you don’t know how.

After brewing the potion, you may be asked to bury any bodies you haven’t already or else be sent to bed. Bozhena is right, there’s nothing to miss, so sleep until morning. In the morning, speak to Hans and head out for Trosky castle, ending the quest.

### If bandits attack

## Trivia

- In one of Henry's hallucinations, he sees a closed gate, to which Hans responds "Don't worry, my name will open any gate." Ironically, soon afterwards they will get into trouble for not being able to get inside Trosky Castle.

## Fragile Delivery

Fragile Delivery is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II as part of the Legacy of the Forge DLC. It introduces the repeatable donation quest Alms.

## Description

Magdalena gave me some eggs for the priest at St James’ in Kuttenberg.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Magdalena, and she will give you a Basket of eggs to deliver to St James' church, the one closest to your forge. Head there and talk to the priest.

He will be grateful for the eggs and ask that you donate 1000 groschen to the church building fund, as it will reflect well on your honor. The donation box is behind him; donate the groschen to end the quest. If you do not have enough groschen to do it in one payment, the quest will remain active until you give an overall donation of 1000 groschen.

## Biography

Franta was the son of the cook who worked for Ulrich Vavak. The morning of the meeting, he went to the market to pick up his livery and took with him the certificate he would need to get into the event.

He was approached by Henry, who wanted to take his place and work the meeting instead. Franta was able to be convinced and handed over the necessary clothes and document.

## Fresh Air

Fresh Air is an achievement introduced in Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Description

You finished DLC3.

## Acquisition

## Fresh clearing

Fresh clearing is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Along the road heading west of the Lower Semine Mill is a small clearing, so freshly cleared that the axe is still in a stump and one of the trees is only partly cleared. To the unassuming traveller nothing would seem out of place.

## Friendly Bout

Friendly Bout is a repeatable task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Introductory Quest

### Description

Master Mathias and the rest of the guild sometimes hold fencing bouts for fun, and since I'm new to the guild he challenged me straight away.

### Walkthrough

Accept the duel with Master Mathias von Saaz, and you'll be led to the fighting ring behind the Hole. This will be a regular one-on-one duel, so be sure to change into your best fighting armor. Your opponent will give you a chance to make any changes you need before initiating combat.

Win or lose, you will gain some blacksmith prestige and a bit of groschen.

### Objectives

## Repeatable Task

### Description

Fighting your place in the smiths' guild takes a bit of proving, so it's time for another friendly duel.

### Walkthrough

Various people in Kuttenberg would like to duel and/or train with you, either with swords or unarmed. NPCs who ask you to fight with them will have a skill check at the end of the bout; passing the check will earn you increased reputation and blacksmith prestige.

### Objectives

## Friendly Bout - Unarmed Sparring

### Description

I met a bloke who likes to settle things the old-fashioned way, fists only. Can't see any reason to turn him down.

### Walkthrough

After fighting the hired hand, he will fall unconscious. Treat him using a bandage and any strength Marigold decoction. He will ask you to vouch for him to his wife whom he promised he had quit fighting. Go with him and you can lie to uphold his story, tell the truth, or try a hard speech check to flatter his wife.

The flatter option, when successful, will paint the hired hand as having defended her honour and she'll give you 150 groschen.

### Objectives

## Friendly Bout - Duelling the Owl

### Description

I met a strange knight. Calls himself George, known as the Owl, and he's a great lover of duels. I'll try to prove myself a worthy opponent.

### Walkthrough

In front of your forge, you'll see a beggar digging. Talk to him and he'll challenge you to a duel for the rights to put up a shelter there. Once you accept, he'll reveal himself to be a travelling knight. He fights with axe and shield.

He will then later appear with the DLC repeatable quest marker in various taverns or inns along the road and challenge you to a duel each time. Defeating him three times will get you the Owl's Claw sabre and the Owl shield. Losing to him on the third duel will still get you the Owl shield.

### Objectives

## Friendly Bout - Miskowitz Guard

### Description

I ran into a guard with a halberd, so I challenged him to a friendly duel. After all, I don't get the chance to fight a halberd every day.

### Walkthrough

In Miskowitz, duel the guard with the halberd after paying him 50 . Win or lose, a townswoman will approach and tell you her people are under attack. Follow the woman, and she'll lead you to her caravan currently under attack by bandits. Kill the bandits, then speak with the woman. She'll give you the option to receive a reward of 150 ; declining it will earn you reputation and speech xp.

### Objectives

## Frogs

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Frogs is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

This side quest is essentially a number of pranks that two rivaling villages try to pull off on each other, with it accumulating to who owns a pasture that both settlements use. See Mice for Tachov's pranks and Battle of the Frogs and Mice for the pasture outcome.

## Walkthrough

Note that this quest can get lengthy depending if you want to do all possible objectives before settling the pasture dispute. You also have the option to rat out the one asking you to pull the prank to the other, though in turn this just has them offer their own prank in turn. As you can do all pranks without revealing to either quest giver, rating one out would only give some reputation (which can easily be earned anyways by doing the pranks).

### Maypole

For pranks, Old Olbram in Zhelejov is tired of Tachov making fun of him and their bullying, so he asks that you steal Tachov's maypole, or more precisely, just the wreath on top to take them down a peg.

For this objective, you'll need to ask around Tachov and learn they closely guard it, with Henik always on guard duty at night. You can then learn from the innkeeper Prochek that he wants someone to beat Henik up a bit because he's dating the innkeeper's daughter, Manka, and gives you ideas on how to provoke Henik. You can also learn from Manka that she's still secretly seeing Henik but it's difficult to find time to be alone together. With that, you have three options:

- Goad Henik into a fight and defeat him, making him storm off

- Offer to take Henik's shift that night so he and Manka can go on a date, then steal it. This will piss off Henik when he realizes you stole the wreath, though not enough to call any guards if you talk to him after the deed.

- Set a date for Henik and Manka, but do not steal Maypole, instead go to Maypole, wait during night. In the morning you can talk to Manka to hear how glad she is and next day you can sneak behind Henik knock him unconscious and steal Maypole

Note once you're ready, you'll need an axe and do it at night to cut the wreath down. Climb up the pole and chop it down, then go pick up the wreath from the ground and head back to Olbram with it, who'll be pleased.

If you do it without getting caught, Olbram will reward 45 Groschen. If you also beat up Henik, Olbram will give an additional reward of 25 Groschen.

### Livestock

For the next prank, Old Olbram wants the sheep in Tachov chased out of the pasture into the forest. To do so, Herdsboy Alshik cannot be present to watch over them. It will be around noon when Alshik takes a lunch break and his snack can be spiked with a Laxative for Alshik which would make him sick, giving you the time to chase off the sheep. Once Alshik acquires his lunch, he'll return to the pasture to eat there. If you successfully spike his lunch, Alshik will make a run to the nearly place to vomit. Old Olbram also suggested that you ruin their laundry that they lay out in the pasture. The best way to do so is by chasing the sheep through the laundry.

Complete this without getting caught and Old Olbram will reward 45 Groschen.

## Objectives

- Steal the maypole from Tachov.

## Gallant Huntsman's Kit

Gallant Huntsman's Kit is a downloadable content pack for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, released on 4 February 2025 alongside the base game.

Initially, it was available exclusively through the Expansion Pass and could not be purchased separately, but it has since been released as a standalone DLC.

## Description

Hunting Season has started… and you don't want to miss it! Tracking down those who murdered your parents - or stalking game in the forest - you can now look the absolute part with the Gallant Huntsman's Kit.

Whether you're sporting St. Hubert's hunting cap, firing bolts at your quarry with Artemis' crossbow or looking dapper in Nimrod’s famous hunting coat, this full costume hunting garb is a 'must have' for the aspiring ranger.

## Acquisition

After the DLC has been downloaded, its content becomes available in the shared stash once it is unlocked. The unlock occurs after completing the introductory questline, with the final requirement being the Laboratores quest.

Players who meet this condition receive a pop-up notification. This appears either immediately upon finishing the required quest or, if it was already completed, upon the next login after purchasing the DLC. The message displayed is:

Your premium items have been successfully added to your shared stash. Enjoy your new gear and happy adventuring!

## Content

- St. Hubert's hat

- Master huntsman's hood

- Nimrod's coat

- Master huntsman's gloves

- Master huntsman's hose

- Master huntsman's boots

- Artemis' crossbow

- Hunting bolt × 30

## Gamekeeper Vostatek

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

When you shoot a deer and it doesn't make a sound, you know you did a good job. It didn't suffer, you know?

—Vostatek

Gamekeeper Vostatek (Czech: Lovčí Vostatek) is the huntsman in service to the Lord of Trosky, Otto von Bergow, in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Vostatek was considered one of the best huntsmen in the area, and thus was named Lord von Bergow's gamekeeper. As such, he took orders from the lord, which sometimes sent him out for days at a time. As a result of his position, his family lived in a cabin in the area that was reserved for the lord's huntsman.

Despite this, he was also a known drunkard, which his son, Vitek, had little respect for and openly showed his disapproval in his father's behaviour regardless of who might be around to hear it.

Unfortunately for Vostatek, his position didn't come without certain moral dilemmas. While he'd typically been asked by von Bergow to take care of some already dead bodies, which he'd take deep into the woods for wolves to finish off, about two years before Henry arrived in the region he was asked to kill someone: a girl no more than 15 years old. Fearing he couldn't refuse a lord's direct orders, Vostatek carried out the killing, but discovered right after she was pregnant and realized she had likely been carrying the illegitimate child of Jan Bergow, Otto von Bergow's son. The gameskeeper informed his wife what had happened, but continued to be haunted by the girl's senseless death for years.

### Associated quests

- Lackey

- Troubadours

- Wedding Crashers

- Bird of Prey

## Gejza

Gejza was one of the Voivode's children and brother to Tibor and Marika in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

While Tibor and Gejza were close, Gejza was a known hothead, quick to pull a knife out on anyone who poked fun at him. Unfortunately this worked against him when his father sent a message to Semine that Bohush should marry Marika or pay, but was in turn sent only insults back. Seeking to avenge his family's honour, Gejza took it upon himself to confront the village. He, along with Tibor, went to confront Bohush, not realizing he didn't send the insults. Unfortunately, things took a turn for the worse when they ran into some woodcutters and Bohush was stabbed, Tibor was taken captive, and Gejza was killed. His body was then tied up to a nearby tree as a warning to the others to not come to the village or else.

## Associated quest

- Miri Fajta

## Gerda

Gerda (Czech: Gerta) is the wife of Apothecary Emmerich. She lives in Troskowitz with her husband and their two sons, Heinrich and Vuytek.

She can usually be found at the apothecary's yard, keeping the place tidy or tending to the herb garden.

## Biography

### Early life

Gerda and her family moved to Troskowitz from Kuttenberg after she inherited a house there. Originally from the village, she never became accustomed to life in the city. She enjoys walking in the woods and gathering herbs and mushrooms, so she found the slower pace of rural life much more agreeable.

### Involvement

During one of these outings, while gathering roots near the conciliatory cross by the road to Tachov, she stayed out until after dark. When she reached home, she realised she had forgotten her knife and went back for it. There she saw an apparition that sprang up as if from the ground in front of her. Terrified, she turned and ran, but at one point looked back and saw a dark figure darting across the field toward Apollonia.

The encounter left her so shaken that she was not herself for several days. When Henry starts to investigate the incident as part of his search for the hermit's sword, Gerda fears he will laugh at her, much as others in the village had done. Henry can reassure her, persuade her to recount what she saw, and promise to share whatever truth he uncovers, giving her some peace of mind. The mysterious figure ultimately proves to be knight Konrad, carrying out the dying wish of his friend, Ambrose, who lived in Apollonia as the local hermit. The conciliatory cross concealed the hiding place where Ambrose kept mementos from his past.

Later, Gerda attends the Semine wedding with her husband. The two can be seen dancing. Emmerich struggles to keep up with his younger wife, yet despite his grumbling he continues to indulge her. They enjoy the festivities and joke together about their son Vuytek's bad luck with womenfolk.

### Associated quests

- Wedding Crashers

- The Hermit

## Biography

Goatskin was a petty thief and would-be spy who lived in Kuttenberg. He was not very well-liked and had few peers willing to interact with him. He was a regular of The Hole in the Wall for some time, and was well known not to ever have much money. He did, however, have a girlfriend called Lousy Mary who worked for the City bathhouse.

At some point, he was approached by Samuel and recruited to do some spy work on his behalf, keeping tabs on the comings and goings of certain nobles in the city. This work paid him well, much better than anything else, and Goatskin began bragging to the crowds at the Hole that he was working for someone very rich and powerful.

When word of this bragging reached Samuel, he sent some of his other allies to teach Goatskin a lesson and Goatskin was beaten by the group and subsequently went into hiding. Although he much more careful not to be seen, Goatskin still needed a way to make money, so he returned to his roots – robbing rich Germans and other patrons of the city bathhouse.

One such patron was Master Schindel, a visiting scholar from Prague. From him, Goatskin stole an Astrolabe and a book on astronomy. These things he hid in a cache in the Kuttenberg underground which was marked on a map of his own making. However, hard up for cash, he sold this map to another thief called Angel.

Eventually, Goatskin was found by Henry who was looking for him in order to find John II of Liechtenstein. Goatskin had heard the name a few times when speaking with Samuel, but could not say if it was in a good or a bad way.

Henry may have offered Goatskin a place to hole up at the Devil's Den, promising him safety should he mention Henry’s name, which Goatskin would accept. Otherwise, Goatskin remained in Kuttenberg trying to stay low.

### Associated Quests

- Into the Underworld

- Master Schindel's Toys

## God Disposes

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

God Disposes is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 8th quest in the Brushes with Death DLC.

## Description

The painter asked me to visit his dead friend Voyta’s grave and say a prayer for him, since nobody had done so in a while.

## Synopsis

The painter Voyta would like Henry to go to the grave of the dead Voyta and pray for him, as no one has done so for years. The grave is far away and not even consecrated, since Libor and the painter had to bury Voyta themselves.

In their youth, the three boys found a tree with three trunks near Mesoles which the painter took as a sign that it was meant to represent the three of them, and it’s there they buried Voyta. As for the prayer, the painter Voyta just wants to be sure Henry will pray for his soul, as he was one of the best people the painter knew, and that he hasn’t given up on the painter.

The painter wants Henry to go on his own, scared of checking on the state of the grave himself. He’s hopeful he might go there some day soon though, if all is well.

Henry goes to look for the grave, eventually finding it with the help of the directions given by the painter. The grave is in a terrible state, overgrown and in a mess. Henry cleans the grave, pulling the weeds and freeing the grave of debris. On the tree, Henry spots three carved initials, R, V, and L.

Once the grave has been cleaned, Henry prays as promised. Henry may also dig up the grave, revealing the buried Voyta is missing his skull.

With his promise fulfilled, Henry return to Kuttenberg to speak to the painter. The painter tells Henry he feels bad for not going himself, but reiterates his intention to do so when the time is right. The painter asks Henry about the initials, though he still maintains he doesn’t remember his true name. In fact, he doesn’t even want to remember.

The trio, it seems, had growing pains. As they got older, the painter devoted more and more of his time to his art, Libor was the son of the bailiff and had to deal more with his father, and Voyta had no one else until Burkhard showed up. The painter had never really shared his artistic inclination with Libor, though he had shown Voyta a bit of his work.

After joining up with Burkhard, Voyta became a changed person, having nothing to talk about except who he’d robbed or beaten in the rare times his friends found time to meet up with him. The painter blames himself, having been so focused on his art that he felt Voyta was only wasting his time.

They once got into a terrible argument over it and though the painter can’t remember the details of it, he remembers a specific insult he gave where he called Voyta a dirty drunken thief. The altercation spurred Voyta and Libor into wanting to get rid of Burkhard. They had planned to use Libor’s father to get it done, but wanted to meet with Voyta first. They told him to pack his things and meet them at the tree, but when they got there he was on the ground, being fed on by wolves.

The painter sent an unconsolable Libor to get a shovel. When Libor left, the painter realised Voyta was still breathing though he couldn’t talk or move. When Libor returned, he and the painter argued over whether Voyta could be saved or not, the painter wanting to put him out of his misery. In the end, Libor struck the final blow and the two of them buried Voyta where he laid.

Henry weighs in on how culpable he feels the painter is. If he dug up the grave, Henry mentions that Voyta was missing his skull. Although the painter is upset that Henry would do such a thing, he admits he eventually dug up the grave and took Voyta’s skull which he now keeps with him as his muse.

He can’t explain exactly why he did so, just that he felt that Voyta was calling him and he had the feeling he had to do it. The painter thanks Henry for all he’s done so far and Henry then leaves him to his work.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Voyta after completing Man Proposes to start the quest. He’ll ask you to find the real Voyta’s grave and say a prayer.

Head towards Burnt Mezholes. Once you’re there, Henry will remark on the landmarks you’re meant to look for. Go east along the stream Voyta described to the edge of the woods, then take a sharp right. Near the middle of where the woods curve, you should be able to spot a dead tree with three trunks. Inspect the tree to find the grave below it.

Interact with the grave to clean it and then say a prayer. Once the prayer is done, you can dig up the grave, doing so will get you more information from Voyta later but is not required to get Confessor. You’ll have to commit, as Henry will be reluctant to do so.

Once you’re done, return to the painter Voyta in Kuttenberg to finish the quest. At this point, if you are able to get him to tell you the full details of his past you’ll earn the achievement Confessor.

## Godwin

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Godwin Oderin (Czech: Bohuta Oderin) is a supporting character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and protagonist in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He was the former parish priest of Uzhitz and lived with his concubine in the rectory of the Uzhitz Church. He is one of three protagonists of Kingdom Come: Deliverance - Stories Untold, serving as the main protagonist of Oratores segement.

Godwin is Martin Oderin's son and Christopher Oderin's older brother.

## Biography

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance

Although deeply religious, he was also considered odd for a priest. He was a skilled sword fighter, having fought as a mercenary and his concubine lived with him openly in the presbytery, despite being forbidden by their vow of chastity. (It was not unusual for a priest to have a "housekeeper", similar to the situation with Father Simon and Mary). As it was, Godwin was hesitant to talk about his past, and had settled down to enjoy the simple pleasures - wine, women and mass.

According to the nobles in the area, Father Godwin was the younger son of a noble family, and in his youth he was taught swordplay, as well as developing a taste for the sins of the flesh. With the eldest inheriting the family estate, it was common for younger sons to enter the priesthood. A gentleman would be insulted by the idea of doing any job fit for a commoner, and by giving one of their own to God's service, his family could be confident of receiving divine blessings - in addition, a priest could depend on the church and his parishioners to keep him well housed and fed, a luxury afforded to few in that time period.

Father Godwin shares his house with the visiting Vicar when he was searching for heretics in Uzhitz, and Henry sought his help banishing a ghost who was haunting a widow in Ledetchko. Godwin pointed out that the Bible says the dead will not walk the Earth until the day of judgement, and suggests that it was in fact the widow's conscience that was haunting her, not a spirit. As it turned out, he was right, and making peace with her past was the solution to the widow's woes. Father Godwin was concerned with the souls of the three women dabbling in witchcraft, and asked Henry to investigate. He was horrified when he heard of the lives lost in the ensuing confusion, warning Henry never to let the devil tempt him, and to pray for forgiveness.

Later, he refused to break his vows by giving Henry information about Lubosh during the Neuhof investigation, describing the criminal as merely a lost soul - although he did promise to try and think of a loophole to convey what he knew. That evening, the two would converse about Henry's past, and the corruption of the Catholic church, while drinking heavily - until the irate Bailiff had them thrown out of the tavern, prompting a fight between Henry, Godwin and the guards.

Godwin and Henry spent the remainder of the night in a drunken stupor, ringing the church bell and having sex with his concubine, while Henry bed the local alemaid. The next morning, the hungover priest was horrified to realize he was due to give a sermon, and begged Henry to do it on his behalf. If Henry did not go through with it, Father Godwin would refuse to help him again, and Henry would need to get his information elsewhere (see the quest Mysterious Ways). However, if Henry performed the mass, he would praise the younger man for his skill, saying he would make a good priest, before giving him some vital information about Reeky.

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

After Hans Capon and Henry disappeared on their mission to Trosky several months later, Godwin was "celebrating" his removal from the clergy by the Bishop when he finds himself visited by Sirs Hanush and Radzig. Due to his unique skillset as both a priest and a mercenary, he is asked to travel there and quietly inquire as to their whereabouts. Hearing from the locals about the ambush near Nebakov Mill, Godwin heads to the battleground and searches the carnage for signs of either young man.

While there, he is able to infiltrate the mercenary band occupying Nebakov Fortress and eventually meet Captain Zizka. Having already been impressed by Henry's courage and skill, Zizka is convinced to release his prisoners once Godwin helps him repel a minor uprising among the mercenary band. Realizing that both Istvan Toth and Erik were double agents the entire time, and that he is on the same side as Hans Capon and Henry, Zizka agrees with Godwin's recommendation that the group travel to Kuttenberg.

After the battle of Nebakov, Godwin, Henry, and Zizka were taken to the dungeons of Trosky, while Hans Capon was captured by Otto von Bergow. Upon escaping Trosky, Godwin went to Rattay to inform Radzig and Hanush of what had happened; he gave Henry a ring and told him that, should he ever find himself in trouble, he should seek out Martin Oderin and present the ring to him, as Martin Oderin would provide assistance.

## Trivia

- Godwin enjoys the sermons of Jan Hus, has a common law wife and he even urges Henry to help the extremist heretics in Waldensians. He represents the common clergy, disillusioned with the teachings of the Catholic church, that will later find their footing with the Hussite movement.

- Godwin's likeness is modeled after the father of the game's director Daniel Vávra.

- Godwin's backstory in KCD2 slightly differs from KCD1 - in both cases he has a brother, but Godwin is younger in the first game and older in the second one.

## Gravedigger Ignatius

Gravedigger Ignatius (Czech: Hrobník Ignác) takes care of the Troskowitz cemetery and the region's dead.

## Involvement

Ignatius had been the town's gravedigger for almost 40 years, seeing his job as a passion and not something everyone was cut out for. However, his job came with a heavy societal cost: despite doing what was considered a necessary labour, because he handled dead people and animals, he was considered unclean and not even allowed to hang out at the tavern. He didn't appear to be treated with disdain though, as Bailiff Thrush paid him well in money and goods.

## Gregorius

Gregorius is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered at Camp by the road locations.

## Biography

Gregorius was a wayfarer who travelled selling various goods, including some that were purported to be holy relics capable of leading to the intercession of a saint.

He spoke Latin and preached about the oncoming Day of Judgement which could be avoided by the purchase of one of his goods. If accused of doing no better than selling indulgences he would become upset and claim that he wasn't really selling anything only offering the opportunity for people to exchange a few groschen for a saint's intercession.

## Grindstone

The Grindstone is a device used to maintain bladed weapons in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It can be used an an alternative to the Repair Kit, allowing you to hone the weapons yourself. One can be found in every smithy. In order to sharpen a weapon, it must be held at a correct angle (at which bright sparks and no smoke come out of the weapon) while the wheel is turned.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance

In Kingdom Come: Deliverance, sharpening at a grindstone is the only way to remove the bloodied visual from your weapon.

### Notes

- Dulling a blade instead of sharpening it is useful in Money for Old Rope.

- With the perk Rusty Edge, a damaged weapon can poison your opponents.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

In Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, grindstones are an important part of Blacksmithing. After the minigame creation, weapons are at 70% condition, and need to be sharpened to 100%. Henry will comment on the weapon being at 100% with lines such as:

- "All right, done!"

- "That's one sharp blade!"

et cetera.

### Notes

- The perk Razor-Sharp grants a damage bonus to weapons sharpened at a grindstone, even if the weapons are later repaired only with Blacksmith's kit.

- Sharpening a blade at a grindstone removes poison from the blade.

## Biography

Hashtal lived and worked as a groom at the stables near Maleshov. He owed a great debt to Maleshov's former owner, Kunzlin Ruthard, due to Ruthard having paid a great sum to bury Hashtal's father.

Due to this existing debt, he was asked by Henry to prepare horses so that Henry could escape with Hans Capon from Maleshov Fortress without causing a ruckus. Hashtal was willing to help and prepared the horses as requested.

Later, von Bergow's favourite horse, Attila, which was under Hashtal's care, was stolen by horse thieves. He was worried that the thieves would use Attila for food rather than try to sell him due to his distinctive appearance and connection to the new owner of Maleshov. He thus asked Henry to help recover the horse. With the horse returned, both their lives were saved.
