## Groschen Must Flow

Groschen Must Flow is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You spent ten thousand groschen.

## Acquisition

The Groschen Must Flow achievement is unlocked by spending a total of 10,000 Groschen throughout the game. Purchases can include armour, weapons, services, or even horses - the latter being among the most expensive items available.

## Tips

- While 10,000 Groschen may seem like a large sum early in the game, it becomes far more manageable by the time you reach the Kuttenberg region.

- Looting valuable weapons and armor during quests and encounters is the most efficient way to amass wealth. Once Henry and his horse reach maximum carry capacity, head to Kuttenberg, where numerous merchants have enough coin to buy your surplus goods. This is more practical than selling in Trosky, where trader funds are more limited.

- Once your cumulative spending reaches 10,000 Groschen, the achievement will unlock.

## Grozav of Borumlaca

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Grozav of Borumlaca is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Grozav was the commander of Sigismund's forces in the Kuttenberg region. He was a nobleman, though an impoverished one, as he had to resort to borrowing large sums of money from another commander in the camp, Chertan.

Despite commanding a large number of men on the king's behalf, Sigismund was not fond of him. Grozav's unpopularity with the king combined with his gambling debts and general antagonsitic behavior has led to his authority as camp commander being weak. This can be noticed in remarks heard around the camp: Henry can overhear an argument between Grozav and the camp blacksmith, who demands pay for his services (which Grozav is reluctant and most likely unable to grant); Katherine mentions that Grozav fell out with half the Royal Court and has been holed away in the camp as a form of punishment, and both Katz and Crow comment with disdain on the type of mercaneries that Grozav takes on.

Grozav seemed aware of the way he was viewed by the camp's inhabitants and King Sigismund. When Henry questions him, he can admit the existence of his debts and lament that ever since he had to sell some of his land, everyone at the court started treating him like a leper. Additionally, he is certain that the king appointed him as the camp commander only to have him to blame for any potential trouble.

Following Chertan's death, Grozav was removed from duty or else killed and replaced by Stibor of Stiborzitz.

### Associated quests

- The Lion's Den

## Grund

Grund (Czech: Grunta) is a village located northwest of Kuttenberg.

## Codex entry

The village was founded by miners sometime in the mid-13th century, when silver ore began to be mined in the area. In the 1270s, according to records, 300 miners and their families were already permanently settled on the nearby Kuklík hill. Legends say that when King Přemysl Otakar II of Bohemia went to battle and needed horses for his army, he took 500 of them from Kuklík alone, which interrupted mining for a while and the miners had to leave.

Under Wenceslas II, new silver veins were discovered, which attracted new miners. The village began to expand and the German name for it became 'Grunt in Mariae' (Valley or Mine of the Virgin Mary, abbreviated to Grunta in Czech). In addition to residential houses, infrastructure for processing the extracted ore also began to appear, as well as facilities for sorting, crushing or smelting. The waste from mining was enormous, so the remaining tailings and slag began to be exported around the area and new landforms were created.

In the village there is also the Church of the Visitation of the Virgin Mary. Already in records from 1305 it is written that it was delapidated, so it is not surprising that in 1367 a new church was built by local miners and townspeople of Kuttenberg.

The mining and smelting premises operated here intermittently until the 15th century, when silver reserves were almost exhausted (it is estimated that 80% of the ore was mined here in less than three centuries).

## Guard Adalbert

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Guard Adalbert is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Adalbert was a soldier in the Prague forces under Ditrich Katz in the service of Sigismund. He worked as a guard in the military's camp in the Kuttenberg region.

He was on duty when the commander of the Cuman forces, Chertan, was attacked and was one of the first to arrive on the scene. As such, he and the other guard, Radovan, were considered suspects but both were subsequently cleared of suspicion.

Once the murder was solved, the Prague forces left the camp en route to Sedletz with their cannon. Along the way, the group was ambushed by Jan Zizka and his men and Adalbert was subsequently killed.

## Guard Radovan

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Guard Radovan is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Radovan was a soldier in the Prague forces under Ditrich Katz in the service of Sigismund. He worked as a guard in the military's camp in the Kuttenberg region.

He was on duty when the commander of the Cuman forces, Chertan, was attacked and was one of the first to arrive on the scene. As such, he and the other guard, Adalbert, were considered suspects but both were subsequently cleared of suspicion.

Once the murder was solved, the Prague forces left the camp en route to Sedletz with their cannon. Along the way, the group was ambushed by Jan Zizka and his men and Radovan was subsequently killed.

### Associated quests

- The Lion's Den

## Guild longsword

Guild longsword is a melee weapon and a quest item in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

Note: Guild longsword can be crafted.

## Description

The guild longsword is a magnificent weapon crafted to celebrate the founding of the Kuttenberg swordfighting brotherhood. It was subsequently adopted as their emblem. The master swordsman, who leads the brotherhood, wears it at his side only on ceremonial occasions. Most of the time, it adorns the great hall of the Kuttenberg swordfighting house.

## Crafting

Main article: Sketch - Guild longsword

- Broken guild longsword × 1

- Fastening material × 1

- Toledo steel × 2

## Acquisition

- The Guild longsword plays a major role in Menhard von Frankfurt's questline. Henry is tasked with stealing it during the Ars Dimicatoria side quest and later reforges it in Mark of the Brotherhood.

- You can make the same sword later for yourself, as the sketch doesn't call for any unique materials.

## Guildsman Janek

Guildsman Janek is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Janek worked as an apprentice saddler in Semine. He heard a rumour that nomads had a special magical horseshoe they could use to let horses run even up sheer cliffs. He wanted to get a hand on such horseshoes so that he could guarantee himself a victory in an upcoming horse race.

He asked Henry to look into the rumours. Henry was able to find out that the horseshoes were not actually magic, but simply spiked to allow for better traction on rocky ground. Janek was grateful for Henry's help and used a pair of Spiked horseshoes to win the upcoming race. He split his winnings with Henry as further thanks.

### Associated Quests

- Miri Fajta

- Magic horseshoes

## Gules

Gules is a nobleman turned bandit in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Despite being a noble, Gules came to lead a group of bandits in Apollonia. However, this didn't come without issues with some, like Handsome Charlie, trying to get the rest to turn on Gules. When he learned of this, Gules ran Charlie out of the group. Despite this, Gules' right hand man, Johnny the Gob, proved to be a loyal friend, never once betraying him.

At one point, Gules was working with two young men, cousins Franzi and Ventza, to steal a bunch of goods from the blacksmith in Tachov. The two cousins eagerly went and apprenticed to the blacksmith, who was preparing a large order for an upcoming wedding in Semine.

However, the cousins then got a rash idea to not just steal from the blacksmith, but also try to run off with the goods for themselves. Gules caught onto this though and he and his bandits found the cousins and cart. Gules then had Ventza tied up while he talked it out with Franzi. Around the same time, he learned of an attack on an entourage at Rocktower Pond, so he sent Johnny with 7 of their best men to check if anything of value was left behind.

If The Jaunt is completed:

Unfortunately for Gules and his men, the missing cart hadn't gone unnoticed and Jan Semine set out with Captain Gnarly and Henry to find it. The trio soon found and attacked Gules' bandit camp, taking Gules captive alongside the two cousins. The three were then taken to Semine, where their fates would be decided. As Gules was a noble though, he couldn't be hanged, so Jan simply took him on as a guard for the town.

### Associated quests

- The Jaunt

- Canker

- Handsome Charlie

- Johnny the Gob

- Casper

- Wedding Crashers

## Hammer and Tongs

Hammer and Tongs is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

If you ask me, Zdimir the blacksmith boasts about the skills of his apprentice, Matthias, a bit too much. He even suggested we make a bet on who can forge the best hunting sword. The winner gets both weapons and a nice pile of groschen on top.

## Walkthrough

In Grund, talk to the Blacksmith Zdimir to start the quest. He bets that you won’t be able to forge a sword better than his apprentice, Matthias.

He will give you the necessary materials to forge the sword, what you want is the Competition sword, it is functionally identical to the regular Hunting sword but specific to this quest:

Main article: Competition sword

- Fastening material × 1

- Scrap metal × 1

- Steel × 2

Once you’ve forged the sword, give it to Zdimir for inspection. In order to win the bet, it must be of gold quality or higher. Zdimir will admit that your sword is indeed better and hand over your winnings. If the Legacy of the Forge DLC is installed, he will also suggest you present yourself to Master Nicholas Krondel in Kuttenberg.

Matthias, however, will not be so gracious. The apprentice will not want to admit his loss or hand over his sword. To get it, you can either pass a medium intimidation check or duel him for it. Once he hands over his losing sword, the quest will complete.

## Handsome Charlie (quest)

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

For the bandit see Handsome Charlie.

Handsome Charlie is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

After completing Canker and a few in-game days have passed, Gules will be ready with the next gang that needs to be dealt with.

## Walkthrough

Gules will point you to Handsome Charlie, who as his name implies, really cares about his appearance, and will ask for his hat as proof. Gules is none too fond of Charlie either, owing to having caught Charlie trying to turn the others against him, so Gules ran him off. However, sources indicate he's holed up with some charcoal burners. As these people may not be fully aware of what mess they're caught up in, Gules will note you can try to avoid others being killed by challenging Charlie to a duel, though this is up to you.

The location is way to the northwest. Note entering this area is considered a privacy area and the charcoal burners will warn you off. Talk to one to try and convince them to take you to Charlie. Doing so, you can then challenge Charlie to a duel using either option. If successful, you'll only need to fight and kill him. Once he's dead, make sure to loot him for his hat.

Back in Semine, Gules will be glad to hear it's done, though he doesn't have much in the way of reward owing to Jan Semine not having much to give for it. In this case, you can ask for the hat if you want. Regardless if you take it or not, the quest will complete.

### Outcomes

While that completes the quest, if you spared the charcoal burners, when you later return to Gules (likely for the next task he has), he'll give you 125 Groschen from them as thanks for not killing them.

## Objectives

- Kill Handsome Charlie.

- Bring Gules Charlie's cap.

## Hangman's Halter Tavern

Hangman's Halter Tavern is a tavern in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is located in Kuttenberg.

## Description

A happening tavern at the edge of Kuttenberg’s large open market. The front offers a large seating area with a tent overtop. Inside are multiple rooms on the ground floor for patrons to eat and drink. Upstairs is also mainly open patron areas, though they have one room to rent with multiple beds. The attic is accessible only by ladder and it is where the workers sleep, for the most part.

The cellar is mainly empty, with some wine barrels and game animals hanging for butchering. There is an entrance to the Kuttenberg underground there as well.

## Hans Capon

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Audentes fortuna iuvat - fortune favours the brave!

Hans Capon (Czech: Jan Ptáček), formally known as Sir Hans Capon of Pirkstein, is a young bohemian nobleman and the heir to the town of Rattay, raised under the guardianship of Sir Hanush of Leipa.

He is a prominent supporting character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and a returning character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, where his role is significantly expanded. Though immature and arrogant at first, Hans gradually evolves throughout the events of both games. His relationship with Henry of Skalitz serves as a central thread of the second game. He is a possible love interest in the second game.

His historical counterpart is the Bohemian nobleman Jan Ptáček of Pirkštejn.

## Biography

### Early life

Hans Capon was born sometime around 1383 as the only son of Jeschke Capon of Pirkstein and Hedvika of Dauba, both members of the noble Ronov family. As the heir to the towns of Rattay and Polna, Hans came into his inheritance at a young age following the death of his father. Since he was still too young to rule at the time, his estates were placed under the care of his uncle, Sir Hanush of Leipa.

Growing up in wealth and comfort, Hans grew into a spoiled and arrogant young nobleman. He enjoyed the luxuries of his station, such as fine food, strong drink, and the attention of women, far more than the responsibilities that came with his title. Sir Hanush often, and very loudly, expressed frustration at his ward's immaturity, doing his best to guide Hans toward becoming a more capable ruler. But Hans had little interest in politics or religion, complaining during sermons and often shirking lessons in governance.

Despite his carefree exterior, Hans was not ignorant of the world around him. He kept up with political events and was particularly animated in discussions concerning the ongoing civil war. Still, his reckless and flamboyant personality often undermined any serious ambitions others may have had for him.

### KCD

Hans first crossed paths with Henry when Henry returned to Rattay after having attempted to bury his parents. Hans was visibly irritated by Henry being rewarded and taken into Sir Radzig Kobyla's service, despite having disobeyed orders and losing Sir Radzig's sword. Sir Radzig, however, defended Henry, explaining that a man who had lost everything should be rewarded for his loyalty rather than punished further.

Hans protests Henry's promotion

Hans observed Captain Bernard putting Henry through basic combat training. He mocked Henry's "sloppy technique" before casually wandering off to the archery range to practise. Later, when Henry and Bernard joined him at the range, Hans and Henry exchanged sharp words. Bernard threatened to throw Henry in the stocks for insubordination, but Hans proposed an archery competition, then a sword fighting match, to test their skills.

Later, Henry, now serving on the town watch, was tasked with closing taverns for the night. This put him in direct conflict with Hans, who refused to obey orders from a commoner. Their confrontation escalated into a brawl, which was broken up by Sir Hanush. Disappointed in both of them - Hans for his conduct as a noble and Henry for disrespecting one - Hanush sent them on a joint hunting expedition, hoping the experience would teach Hans leadership and Henry humility.

Hans mocks Henry when he attempts to shut down the tavern

During the trip to the Talmberg woods, Hans forced Henry to jog beside his horse, in a poor show of power. On the way, he admitted his behaviour at the tavern was inappropriate, though he maintained that Henry was also in the wrong for challenging a nobleman. As it turned out, he was annoyed that Henry was rewarded for disobeying a direct order, when Hans was punished for merely putting so much as a toe out of line, and so overreacted. That evening around the campfire, Hans asked about Henry's past, especially the attack on Skalitz, and decided to get him drunk when Henry hesitated to speak. They talked about Hans' life as a nobleman, and he revealed that his main reason for going hunting was just to get away from overbearing Sir Hanush and his lectures. He also explained that Sir Hanush was overseeing his estate and education until he came of age - a decision delayed due to King Wenceslas's imprisonment and the inaction of his father's council.

Hans learns you can't hunt boar with arrows

The following morning, Hans bet he could shoot more hares than Henry by midday. Later, the two set out to hunt a wild boar. Despite Henry's warning that boars should be hunted with spears, Hans wounded the animal with an arrow and recklessly gave chase on horseback, with Henry following close behind. They became separated, and by the time Henry found the young lord, Hans had accidentally ridden into a hidden Cuman camp and been captured. Henry defeated the attackers and helped Hans return safely to Rattay. Back in town, Henry was formally accepted into Sir Radzig's service as a reward for rescuing the nobleman, while Hans was ordered to bed to recover. After this incident, Hans began treating Henry with greater respect, shifting from cruel mockery to more good-natured teasing about his lowborn status.

Hans stumbles right into a Cuman camp

A recovering but bored Hans invited Henry to join him at the baths for a few days in order to have some fun with Klara, a beautiful bathmaid, and even admitted Henry had been right - hunting boar with a bow and arrow was not the best idea. At the baths, a drunken Hans first goaded Henry into stealing some of Sir Hanush's finest wine (though he didn't expect him to actually go through with it) then sent him to pick flowers for Klara in the middle of the night. While Henry was away, Klara's jealous lover, Archie, attempted to drown Hans, believing he was sleeping with her. Fortunately, Henry returned just in time to save him, and the two continued drinking merrily until the sunrise.

Later, Henry heard rumours about Sir Hanush holding the tourney and asked Hans about it. He was dismissive at first, considering it mere entertainment for common folk. However, he was clearly troubled and confessed that, after another dressing down from Sir Hanush about neglecting his duties, he told him he had been training a new page. Unfortunately, that wasn't strictly true but Hans had a masterful idea: if Henry entered the tournament, he could show off all the skills Hans had "taught" him, and both would earn Sir Hanush's praise.

Henry and Hans in the baths

Some time later, when Henry went to visit Hans, he gloomily revealed that Sir Hanush learned about the misadventures in the baths and had demanded their presence. Hans insisted on lending Henry some of his fine clothes for the occasion, since as his squire walking in rags would reflect poorly on Hans. During the meeting, Hanush reprimanded them for their careless behaviour and reminded Hans that his people labour to ensure he was well fed, scolding him for his ingratitude. He threatened to send Hans to his mother in Polna to be married off if he could not mend his ways and prove himself worthy to rule.

An opportunity soon arose, when Sir Bernard's cousins feuded over control of a fortress. Sir Hanush sent Hans and Henry along with Captain Bernard to settle the matter peacefully. However, Hans was eager to prove his worth and boasted about dealing with the bandits directly. Despite Hanush's instructions to avoid bloodshed, once Baron Wolflin of Kamberg refused to surrender, Hans ordered his men to attack, even engaging the renegade nobleman in single combat.

Sir Hanush admonishes Hans and Henry

As tensions in the region came to a boiling point, Sir Robard proposed a stealth mission to liberate hostages, including Lady Lady Stephanie and Sir Radzig, from occupied Talmberg; Hans volunteered at once. He scaled the walls beside Henry and a group of raiders, sneaked through the keep, and helped eliminate enemy guards. During the withdrawal he was shot, ignominiously, in the backside by a Cuman archer, forcing Henry to haul him back over the ladder. Hans laughed off the injury, bragging that the scar would impress the ladies.

Despite the wound, Hans remained in good spirits and recovered swiftly. He even participated in the final assault. He joined the storming party on the western wall, but objected loudly when Sir Hanush agreed to let Istvan Toth leave in exchange for the hostages. Toth agreed to give Lady Stephanie back immediately, but would not release Sir Radzig until he reached Skalitz to ensure his own safety. Hans mounted up with Henry to pursue the traitor to the border of the fiefdom. There he left Henry and Radzig to their reunion and galloped after Toth with a handful of retainers.

Shortly after, Hans and Henry were invited to the meeting of the local noblemen with Margrave Jobst. To determine the loyalty of Otto von Bergow, a known supporter of King Sigismund, Jobst proposed sending envoys with a letter. Hans immediately volunteered to ride to Trosky Castle to question von Bergow himself and, naturally, he insisted Henry accompany him.

### KCD2

(incomplete section)

Hans and Henry relax at camp.

Hans' story resumes in KCD2 exactly where it left off. Hans, Henry, and their company resume their journey to Trosky Castle. Their party is intercepted by Captain Thomas who informs the group that the area is full of bandits. Hans decides to have everyone rest for the night as Trosky is still a day away. He engages in a training fight with Henry and later insists that they bathe at the pond beside camp, despite everyone saying it's a bad idea.

While Henry and Hans bathe in the pond Hans hears female voices nearby and insists he and Henry go investigate. As they tread water and search for the women, a group of bandits attack the party members still on land. Hans watches on in horror as all his companions beside Henry are slaughtered. Hans and Henry remain hidden in the reeds but Henry exposes them in an attempt to save Katherine.

An unconscious Hans recovers in the herbwoman's hut.

Hans and Henry attempt to swim away from the group of bandits lead by Žižka and Istvan Toth. Henry is shot through the shoulder in the process and Hans removes the arrow, causing severe bleeding. Hans navigates himself and a delirious Henry through the dark and away from bandits, all while unclothed with no weapons. Eventually Hans brings them to Bozhena's hut and begs the herbwoman to help Henry. As she begins to treat Henry a bandit emerges and attacks Hans who is pulled outside and to the ground. Hans finds a nearby bucket and bludgeons the bandit to death, but not before he is stabbed through the stomach.

An unfortunate occurrence at the castle gate.

For the next few days, Hans remains comatose on the floor of Bozhena's home. With Bozhena and Henry's help he recovers. Bozhena gifts them clothes and money to get them to Trosky. After an arduous journey, Hans and his page make it to Trosky castle. As they appear raggedy and have no entourage, they are not believed to be nobles. Hans insists the guards retrieve Von Bergow but they refuse. He continues to cause a scene and gets a bucket of waste dropped onto him. The Chamberlain appears and informs everyone that Sir Hans Capon is believed to be dead after the attack. Hans and Henry are turned away.

Hans and Henry in the pillory.

During Fortuna Hans and Henry visit the Troskowitz inn to discuss what to do next. They hear about a local wedding that Von Bergow will be attending and decide they need to find a way in. They agree about needing money but Hans refuses to work saying it goes against the will of God for a noble to work. Hans starts a fistfight while Henry was attempting to move flour sacks for Innkeeper Betty. The fight escalates and the two are arrested and put in the pillory. While stuck in the pillory Hans and Henry exchange heated words and Hans admits to feeling like his life went downhill since meeting Henry. The moment he is released from the pillory Hans runs off.

Hans is next seen at the Semine wedding now clean and dressed in his signature colors. During the wedding he takes place in the swordplay tourney. He also plays a role in the final stages of Wedding Crashers, but his role depends on how the player attended the wedding. If you attended via Miller Kreyzl he will be drinking with Enneleyn above the dice room. If you attended via Blacksmith Radovan he will be against the barn with information about the lost sword.

After the wedding takes place and Von Bergow is a no show a drunken brawl breaks out, and Hans defends Henry despite their previous animosity. The brawl escalates to a full-on fight and the catchpoles are called. Hans and Henry are taken to Trosky Castle and await punishment.

Hans awaits the twelfth toll of the bell.

Hans and Henry have a catchup and a heart to heart in a jail cell below the castle where Hans apologizes. He also tells Henry he got by in the time they were apart by poaching, which is a capital crime. Guards come to retrieve Henry for labor and tell Hans that he is to face execution. Hans spends the next few hours in the dark contemplating his death that will be brought upon the 12th toll of the bell.

As the bell rings the final time, Hans is brought from his cell and paraded to the gallows. The hangman's noose is put around his neck even as a frantic Henry and Captain Thomas try to explain that Hans is a noble and therefore cannot be executed. The Chamberlain announces Hans' crimes to the gathered crowd and beings to motion for his execution. At the last moment, Von Bergow bursts through the castle gates and interrupts the execution saving Hans.

Hans finally gets his audience with Lord von Bergow who believes he truly is Lord Capon and drops all charges against him. He and Henry attempt to get von Bergow to side with Sir Hanush and Wenceslas but von Bergow refuses to discuss the matter until several other problems are fixed first. Von Bergow sends Hans and Henry to Nebakov to address the rampant bandits in the area and gather forces. During the journey to Nebakov, Hans expresses his appreciation of Henry and jokingly calls him his guardian angel. Upon arriving to Nebakov fortress Hans is called to have a private meeting with Jaromier Nebak, the head of the fortress and a vassal of von Bergow. As Hans attends his meeting Henry discovers that the fortress has been taken over by the very bandits they set out to catch and the real Sir Nebak is imprisoned beneath the castle.

Hans and Sir Nebak, actually Žižka, share a toast after the false lord promises to send infantry and cavalry to von Bergow's defense. After the meeting Henry informs Hans of what he discovered beneath the fortress and the two ride back to Trosky to inform von Bergow. Sir Otto is delighted to have found the location of the bandit headquarters and hosts a feast for his allies with a plan to sneak attack the dawn after the feast.

At the feast Hans once again asks the Chamberlain and Lord von Bergow to reconsider their stance on the war and siding with Sigismund. He also offers to lead the charge against Nebakov after disagreeing with von Bergow's idea of sending the Chamberlain. Von Bergow denies allowing Hans to lead saying that the fight will be extremely easy. He also refuses to parley with Hans and insult him for not knowing when to compromise and focusing on the wrong problem. Hans decides to retire early for the night, requesting Henry retrieve his armour and sword for the upcoming fight.

Early the next morning the journey to attack Nebakov fortress takes place. Hans and Henry ride beside the Chamberlain as their combined forces venture through the woods around Nebakov. Despite all allies feeling this will be an easy battle, Henry and Hans express concerns to eachother about underestimating an enemy. As the Chaimberlain berates them a large tree is felled behind the party and an ambush against them begins.

An injured Hans is protected by Henry.

In the ensuing battle many of Hans' allies fall. Even after he manages to free him from under a horse, the Chamberlain still perishes. Hans leads Henry away from the bloodbath only to stumble into another. As they attempt to make their escape Hans, who is wearing a helmet but no coif, is struck directly in the head with a morningstar at close range. He falls to the ground, the force of the blow knocking off his helmet and severely concussing him. Henry is successful in slightly awakening Hans, but Hans is still incapacitated after taking the hit. A group of bandits surround them and move to kill. The bandits, however, are stopped by their leader, Žižka, who recognizes Hans and believes he could get a good ransom from him. As Hans is unable to defend himself or even stand, Henry stands in front of him telling they bandits if they want Hans they must get through him.

Žižka admires Henry's courage and challenges him to a duel, saying he will let both Henry and Hans live and walk away if he is defeated. Henry is able to defeat Žižka, but Žižka refuses to let them leave and abducts them back to Nebakov fortress. At the fortress, Hans is thrown into the dungeon below along with his surviving allies.

Hans refusing surrender.

After the misunderstandings are cleared up and a battle is clearly on the horizon, Hans and Henry become allied with Žižka and prepare for Von Bergow's siege on Nebakov. Hans plays dice with Henry and reminisces about his life so far. When the battle begins and several large armies appear, including Von Bergow, Istvan Toth, Markvart Aulitz, and other Sigismund forces. They offer the option the surrender but Hans and his allies refuse.

During the battle at Nebakov, Hans protects the gate area until a retreat is called. Once reaching the castle tower he and his fellow fighters discuss the next steps until the Finger of God is shot off, destroying the tower. Hans is crushed beneath rubble and unable to free himself, leading to him being caught by enemy forces. The other surviving members of Žižka's band are hauled off to Trosky, but Hans is brought as a hostage to Maleshov fortress. While imprisoned in Maleshov, Hans was confined to one room and continued to develop fear of enclosed spaces.

During Taking French Leave Hans, as well as Brabant, are rescued by Henry who snuck into the castle via an underground tunnel. Hans, due to his newly developed claustrophobia, refuses to enter the cramped tunnel so the group must fight their way out. After fighting through the courtyard, stealing horses, and fleeing Hans is finally free from his imprisonment.

Hans enjoys his newfound freedom, for a short while.

Almost immediately upon leaving Maleshov, Hans is whisked away by Sir Radzig and Sir Hanush to accompany them to a meeting of Wenceslas supporters at Raborsch. During The Feast Hans is unwillingly betrothed to Jitka of Kunstadt. Upon learning this information, via Hanush and Infront of a huge crowd, he becomes distressed and proceeds to drink heavily. Another battle then takes place with Žižka and Godwin fighting at Hans' side. Henry shows up during the last leg of the fight and invites Hans back to the Devil's Den where Hans chooses to reside for the foreseeable future. Hans joins the Devil's Pack and helps create a plan to attack Sigismund's forces.

Prior to The Lion's Den, Hans takes Henry on a hunting trip to liven his spirits. During the trip the encounter a band of Cuman soldiers, similar to the Prey quest in the first game. The two fight off and kill the bandits before deciding to head back to the Devil's Den.

### Romance

The following contains spoilers for Kingdom Come Deliverance II.

In Kingdom Come Deliverance II, Hans becomes a possible major romance. Despite being a major companion throughout the first game, Henry could not romance or flirt with Hans until the second. Other than Black Bartosch, Hans is the only male romance option.

The player has many opportunities to express care and concern for Hans that are not romantic. Nonsexual intimacy such as hugs and shoulder pats happen as well. The first opportunity to flirt with Hans takes place directly after the main events of For Whom the Bell Tolls. The player is given the option to comfort Hans and express concern over his would-be fate. Hans expresses gratitude.

The next time when it is possible to flirt with Hans is during Taking French Leave by telling him you will 'manage it together'. After completing several steps and rescuing Hans, another romance dialogue option will appear. During The Italian Job another romance dialogue is present.

The main romance scene takes place during Hunger and Despair. Henry can go to Hans' room and say goodbye before leaving Suchdol. Henry can sit with Hans and listen to him telling a story about the Arthurian knights Lancelot and Galehaut, in which a knight loses his partner and dies from grief and sorrow. Hans admits that if Henry dies he too would be so beside himself in grief that he might die as well. Hans wishes he could save Henry for once.

Hans tells Henry about the knights he feels mirror them.

After selecting the Kiss Him dialogue option you get the main romance cutscene. Henry places his hand on Hans' and promises to return to him then gets up and begins to leave. Hans grabs him by the arm and pulls him into a kiss.

A surprised Henry pulls away and heads to the door while a distraught Hans apologizes. Henry thinks for a moment before locking the door and turning back around to kiss Hans. Henry and Hans sleep together, and the romance route is completed.

Before Judgement Day is completed, Hans will speak with Henry about his upcoming wedding to Jitka of Kunstadt and mentions he and Henry's previous intimacy here.

Jan Ptáček (Hans Capon)

1388? – 1419

(Sir Hans Capon)

The underage son of Jan Ješek Ptáček and Hedvika of Dauba. After the death of his father, his family, the Lords of Leipa - his uncle Jindřich (Henry), his son Hanuš (Hanush) and his brothers, became his guardians. Young lord did not take possession of Rattay (and hereditary estate in Polna) until 1412. Soon afterwards he entered political life and he held positions in the provincial offices.

After the imprisonment of Master Jan Hus he signed a petition in his defence, but during the Hussite wars he was initially on the side of the League of Lords against the Hussites in a few minor battles (in 1419 he took part in a battle against the Hussites at Knín), apparently due to the influence of his close neighbour Lacek of Kravař of Šternberk. There are no records indicating he took part in the war later. His son was Hynek Ptáček, who achieved high office in the Kingdom of Bohemia, becoming Royal Hofmeister and Mince[sic] Master.

—Codex entry: Jan Ptáček

Jan Ptáček (Hans Capon)

1388(?) - 1419

young Lord Capon (Jan Ptáček)

Son of Ješek Ptáček and Hedvika of Duba. After the death of his father, Jan Ješek, the Lords of Leipa (uncle Henry, his son Hanush and his brothers) became his guardians.

After the imprisonment of Master Jan Hus, he signed a petition in his defence. In the Hussite wars, however, he initially sided with the League of Lords against the Hussites in a few minor battles (in 1419 he took part in the battle against the Hussites at Knin), apparently due to the influence of his close neighbour Lacek of Kravař from Šternberk. There are no records indicating he took part in the war later.

He was the Lord of Rattay and Polná. He acquired Rattay from his guardians only in 1412. He held positions in the provincial offices and his son was the famous Hynek Ptáček.

Unlike his historical precursor, however, we took the poetic license of making Hans Capon a twenty-year-old man in our game.

—Codex entry: Jan Ptáček/KCD2

## Hanush of Leipa

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Your graces, I have to tell you in all seriousness, that this land of ours is in the shit. Deep, fucking shit.

Sir Hanush of Leipa (Czech: Hanuš z Lipé) is a main character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and a side character in Kingdom Come:Deliverance II.

He was the acting Lord of Rattay in 1403, and was a distant relative and regent of the young Sir Hans Capon.

He is based on the real-life figure of the same name (see below for codex) and his coat of arms are two crossed branches on a golden field.

## Biography

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance

Heir of the Ronov family, Hanush was the son of Henry III of Leipa, who had ruled Rattay since 1388 on behalf of the young lord Hans Capon. When Henry of Leipa also passed away, the care of Hans and of Rattay fell to Hanush. Although Hans refers to him as "Uncle", the codex states that they are some sort of distant cousin.

He was a good friend of Sir Radzig Kobyla, Lord of Skalitz and of Sir Divish, Lord of Talmberg, and knew Radzig well enough to know his secret, and even poke fun at him for it. Following the razing of Skalitz in 1403 by King Sigismund of Hungary, Hanush provided shelter to the newly displaced refugees of the village, including Sir Radzig, offering them the lower castle of his city as a temporary home.

In contrast to the more quiet and serious Sir Radzig, Hanush is depicted as boisterous and jovial in attitude, with a penchant for martial combat. He is quick to joke but also has a bad temper, switching from laughing to yelling in a matter of moments. When Hans gets into strife during Keeping the Peace, and later in Next to Godliness, Hanush has no problem disciplining his ward, and warns him that a Lord is only a Lord so long as the people accept him - and the people will not accept a drunken, spoilt lout. To that end, he will even send Hans away to live with his mother, rather than allow him to rule incompetently.

Hanush and his ward, Hans Capon

Like most of that era, he was a religious man, and attended church in the evenings, although there is no love lost between him and the local Friar. He does appear to be quite fond of his nephew, despite their differences, displaying sincere gratitude to Henry when he saves Hans' life in The Prey. He prefers battles and hunting to peaceful diplomacy, and cannot read (as he explains, why bother learning when he has a scribe?).

However, he takes his role as acting ruler of Rattay very seriously, and seems to genuinely care for his subjects, becoming enraged when finding out about the slaughter at Neuhof that kicked off The Hunt Begins.

Hanush rages at Hans and Henry

He is also skilled in politics, dispatching Henry in Waldensians to assist the visiting Vicar in finding heretics - or, ensuring he does not find heretics, as the case may be, as such an event could spell trouble for Hanush. However, this stems from his belief that there are no actual heretics in his region, and he will rail at Henry if he assists the Waldensians in their escape attempt. During Baptism of Fire, he sends some of his troops to assist in the attack on the bandit camp, but does not fight himself.

Shortly after Pribyslavitz is cleared of bandits, Sir Bernard receives word that the bandits have continued their attacking, even launching a raid on Merhojed. He suspects that these attacks are to show that the bandits are still strong, and that they will continue to plague the area.

Hanush is furious, but brightens when Master Tobias arrives, bearing the chest of gold coins that was recovered at the Pribyslavitz camp. Unfortunately, the engineer reveals that the coins are all forgeries. Hanush is livid at being duped, however Sir Radzig is able to deduce that the forger must have access to a forge, skilled craftsmen, and a source of materials - an important clue in finding whoever is behind the attacks.

Forgeries? Kurva!

Sometime later, he will summon Henry and Sir Hans as part of Clothes Make the Man, where he rails at his ward for his immature behaviour, and at Henry for encouraging it. However, he decides to give his layabout nephew one last chance to prove himself, by helping Sir Bernard track down his renegade cousin Baron Wolflin of Kamberg in Robber Baron.

Henry may visit Hanush during The Die is Cast to tell him, along with Radzig, that he has learned the location of the bandit camp. While Hanush is excited at the prospect of Henry infiltrating the bandits and getting more information to sway the battle, Radzig is hesitant, warning Henry not to take any unnecessary risks.

Henry later returns, bloody and bruised from his torture at the hands of Erik and Sir Istvan Toth, now revealed to be the masterminds behind the bandit attacks. Henry is able to report that they have over one hundred men, far more than the forces of Sir Divish, Hanush and Radzig put together. Henry reveals that Istvan told him something else - that his father was not Martin the blacksmith as he'd always believed, but that he is the illegitimate son of Radzig himself.

Hanush laughs as Henry reveals he knows Radzig's secret

Hanush is amused by the turn of events, as he had long since known about their relationship, and praises Henry for his balls. However, his attention quickly turns to what should be done about the massive bandit army, and decides that their only chance of victory is to launch an immediate attack on the bandits, while they still have the element of surprise.

That evening, in Payback, the Lords launch their assault on Vranik (after a rousing speech from Hanush) and are able to defeat them. Much to Hanush's frustration, there is no sign of Istvan or Erik. Henry searches the homestead and finds a clue, a letter (which Hanush can't read, as he's illiterate), which mentions that Istvan will "soon succeed in seizing the castle".

At that moment, the soldiers drag up a bandit that they've captured alive, who laughs at them and mockingly asks which castle they left unguarded. As Divish realizes with horror that Istvan has taken his men to Talmberg, Hanush kills the laughing bandit with a swift blow from his mace.

Hanush leads the attack on Vranik

The men launch a desperate attack to try and breach the castle before the enemy can pull up the drawbridge, but Istvan appears holding a knife to Lady Stephanie's throat, and revealing he has also captured Sir Radzig, who had raced ahead. Sir Hanush is in favour of a siege, but Sir Divish is adamant this should be the last resort. Sir Robard of Talmberg proposes that someone sneak into the castle, and Henry is the first to volunteer.

Sir Hanush and Sir Divish commanded the building of a trebuchet in order to retake the castle, Henry recruits the military engineer Konrad Kyeser to build the trebuchet. After they finish the construction they destroy the portcullis of the castle which results in the gate being opened and the lords storm the castle killing Istvan's soldiers. With Istvan cornered, Sir Hanush conducts an agreement to let Sir Istvan leave safely in exchange for Lady Stephanie and agreeing to drop off Radzig at Skalitz. Hanush and the other lords are visited by Margrave Jobst of Moravia. Together they the discuss the current state of Bohemia. Jobst explains to the lords that King Wenceslas IV of Bohemia invited his younger half-brother King Sigismund to rule in his place while he enjoyed his luxurious life. However, when King Wenceslaus realized he would be nothing but a puppet he refused to cooperate so Sigismund decided to abduct the King. Hungary has gone into revolt against Sigismund so the lords decide to form an alliance with the king's allies to peacefully put an end to the civil war. Hanush and Jobst compose a letter for Lord Otto von Bergow, then entrust it to Hans Capon to deliver, with Henry acting as a bodyguard.

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

After Hans Capon and Henry failed to return from Trosky, Hanush and Radzig visited Godwin in Uzhitz so that he could set out to find out what had happened to the pair.

Upon his return, Godwin informed Hanush and Radzig that Hans had been captured by Bergow and that they were being taken to Kuttenberg. A meeting of Wenceslas’s supporters was also scheduled to take place near Kuttenberg, so Hanush, Radzig, and Godwin set off for the region.

Hanush was present at the gathering of Wenceslas's supporters in Raborsch, but by a stroke of good fortune, Hanush left the assembly before the evening massacre. Together with his men, he was part of Jobst’s army, which liberated Suchdol from the control of the Prague militia.

## Codex entry

Years: ? - 1415

Following the death of Heinrich III of Pirkstein in 1402, Hanush of Leipa became the guardian of the former's son, Hans Capon and thus the acting governor of the surrounding region. He completed the construction of Pirkstein, its fortifications and the local church of St. Matthew, which contains a shrine to his family.

When Sigismund of Luxembourg invaded and burned Skalice (Skalitz), the town's Burgrave, Racek (Radzig) Kobyla, and the survivors of the raid found refuge with Hanuš. Hanuš subsequently took action against scattered groups of brigands and Cumans.

His relationship with the king was peculiar to say the least, judging by often contradictory sources - it appears that in 1410 crown forces descended on the town of Rataje (Rattay) in Hanuš' domain, probably after he became a robber baron and rebel, who may also have participated in the siege of Jihlava in Moravia. Nevertheless, in 1414 he became a Provincial Marshal and dwelt together with his wife Markéta of Šternberk (Sternberg) at Špilberk in Brno.

## Hanush's sword

Hanush's sword is a unique melee weapon and a quest item in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

## Description

The longsword is a perfectly balanced lethal weapon. Its price is not small, because only a master of his craft can forge a thin yet flexible blade! The longsword is not meant for the heat of battle, but for swift swordplay.

## Acquisition

At the end of the Judgement Day main quest, Sir Hanush remarks that his brand-new sword became dull during the battle. Henry offers to sharpen it for him. However, it must be returned to him and cannot be acquired without using console commands.

## Hardcore Henry II

KCD

KCD2

Hardcore Henry II is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It was introduced to the base game with patch 1.2.4, through the free Hardcore Mode DLC.

## Description

You finished the story in Hardcore mode.

## Acquisition

To earn the Hardcore Henry II achievement, start a new game in Hardcore Mode and complete all story missions. When beginning this playthrough, you must select at least three negative perks from the ten available.

## Tips

- To save time, you can combine this with the Hardcore achievement Against All Odds, which requires completing the game with all ten negative perks selected.

## Trivia

- The name of the achievement is probably a reference to the Russian-American film Hardcore Henry (2015), written and directed by Ilya Naishuller. The name is also shared with an achievement from the first game.

## Hardcore Mode/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Hardcore Mode is one of three free content updates for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Announced on 16 January 2025, it was released on 15 April 2025 with patch 1.2.4.

It adds an optional game mode that implements a variety of mechanics designed to increase difficulty and immersion.

## Description

A new immersive game mode in which navigation, survival and combat are more difficult and more realistic. At the start of Hardcore mode, you also have to select at least three negative perks which further modify the games difficulty in different areas.

## Features

Henry, setting forth towards new lands by Hans Capon's side, isn't the lad he used to be. His adventurous life has taken a toll on him.

You will lose:

- The compass and location indicator on the map - carefully observe your surroundings to find your way around, or you can ask the locals for directions.

- The attack direction indicator in combat - you'll have to pay close attention to your opponent's movements as well as the position of your own weapon.

- Your mind, and likely even your life.

## Changes

The changes are as followed:

- You must pick at least 3 negative perks the game provides you.

- Auto-saves from non-major quests are disabled; saving only occurs if you drink Saviour Schnapps, sleep, go to a Bathhouse to heal, after major events during main quests or save and quit.

- Combat is much deadlier for you and enemies abuse their greater numbers more often.

- Feints are less effective at fooling enemies.

- Items purchased from traders are much more expensive.

- You'll sell items at worse prices.

- Trades are not as willing to haggle less gold for buying items.

- Repairing at vendors will cost significantly more.

- Eating from pots provide less nourishment.

- You cannot fast travel.

- You cannot see where you are from the world map, you must deduce your location from what you see around you.

- The crest of a town doesn't appear on your arrival into said town

- The rabbit under the compass is removed, so you won't know you're being pursued or attacked and have to use sound queues to determine your situation.

- The top bar doesn't show compass directions, You'll have to deduce your direction with structures and paths in the area against the map.

- Points of interest such as vendors or quest markers will only appear once you get close enough.

- The bar in the bottom screen is removed, as such, you'll have to rely on visual clues to determine the following:

- HP (screen turns red when low, can still be seen in the Inventory tab).

- Stamina (screen turns blue when low).

- Enemy HP (limping, staggering etc. determine how low the enemy is).

- Horse Stamina (horse will rear it's head and whinny when stamina is low).

- When engaging in combat, the combat "star" that displays where your attacks are directed will never be visible, therefore you must be able to tell according to visual cues of your arms when holding weapons.

- Additionally, the green shield for Perfect Blocks are no longer shown during combat (except during encounters with wolves, clenches and takedowns).

- The blue swords that appears for counterattacks is also not present in combat (only appearing once again during encounters with wolves, clenches and takedowns).

- Perfect blocks/dodges and riposte windows are more unforgiving.

## Negative Perks

## Hare

Hare is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Hare was a member of the band headed by Karel Arrowhead. After Karel's death, he went with Pasha to the Devil's Den to find someone to help retrieve the arrow that had lodged itself in Karel's head from his corpse.

Henry agreed to help and met with Hare after having gotten the arrow back. Hare started leading him towards their current camp but stopped partway there to ask if Henry would give him the arrow instead of giving it to Pasha. Pasha, he claimed, was not as good a leader as Karel had been and would only lead the band to ruin, as it was even his idea to take the job that killed Karel.

Henry then had the choice to do as he asked, or refuse. If he gave over the arrow, Hare thanked him, telling him he saved a lot of lives by doing so and swearing he'd repay Henry some day. If Henry refused Hare either cursed him and ran or else tried to fight him for the arrow and was killed.

### Associated Quest

- The Magic Arrow

## Head armour/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Head armour is one of the armour types that Henry can equip in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

There are five categories of headgear: Helmets, Coifs, Collars, Hoods, and Caps.

Each has a dedicated inventory slot, except helmets and caps, which occupy the same slot and cannot be used simultaneously.

## Overview

Helmets

Helmets are the primary form of protective headgear in the game. They provide the highest level of defense against melee and ranged attacks.

Caps

Caps (or hats) share the same inventory slot as helmets, so both cannot be equipped simultaneously. They are primarily cosmetic, offering limited protection but providing higher charisma bonuses.

Coifs

Coifs are close-fitting headgear made of padded fabric or chainmail. They can be worn alone for light protection, but a coif must be equipped first in order to wear a helmet.

Collars

Collars protect the neck and lower face, often integrating with chest or shoulder armour. In gameplay, they serve as an additional layer of defense, slightly reducing damage from strikes to the upper body.

Hoods

Hoods are soft, fabric-based headgear that, similar to caps, provide minimal protection and grant additional charisma bonuses. While many NPCs wear their hoods raised, Henry's only hood with this feature is the Cutpurse's hood.

## Heater shield

Heater shield is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It is held in the off-hand and classified as a shield.

## Description

A shield made of wooden planks glued together and covered with thin rawhide. These shields are usually decorated with the coat of arms of a lord, noble family or city.

## Heavy crossbow

Heavy crossbow is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as the ranged weapon type.

## Description

The heavy siege crossbow is used for shooting soldiers defending castle walls. The strong iron limbs have a considerable draw weight, therefore a hand crank must be used to load it. A bolt fired from this weapon can easily tear through plate armour.

## Heavy mace

Heavy mace (Czech: Palcát těžký) is a blunt‑type melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It can't be crafted.

## Description

A mace with steel flanges is a formidable weapon, yet it is still nimbler than a simple axe. It can crush and break bones even through quality plate armour.

## Heinrich

Heinrich is the son of Apothecary Emmerich and Gerda. He lives in Troskowitz with his parents and his brother, Vuytek.

He can be found in the apothecary's yard, either leaning against the shed with the alchemy bench or tending the herb garden.

## Biography

### Early life

Sometime in the past, his family moved from Kuttenberg after his mother inherited a house from her relatives. Since then, they have been living in Troskowitz, where Heinrich apprentices under his father.

### Involvement

When Henry and Capon appear in the village tavern, he can be seen at the same table as Svatya Thrush and Farmer Bourek, drinking with them, although he does not join the conversation about the upcoming wedding. When the argument between Svatya and Hans escalates into a brawl, he jumps in to help and can be promptly knocked out.

Later, when Vuytek takes offence at the Cuman Vasko and his band eating in the tavern and antagonizes them, Heinrich is at his side, ready to fight. How the situation plays out depends on whether Henry sides with the Cumans, the villagers, or manages to calm both parties down. If Henry sides with the Cumans, there is a chance to knock Heinrich down a second time.

While his parents and brother are at the Semine wedding, he stays at home.

### Associated quests

- Laboratores

- Invaders

## Inventory

Note: Character inventories are divided into Equipment, which includes items currently worn or actively used, and Possessions, which can be pickpocketed. Equipment is typically stored in the character's bedside chest overnight.

There are a total of 6 items in Heinrich's inventory.

| ItemCategory

| Equipment

| Tunic Body

| Simple hose Legs

| Simple shoes

| Possessions

| Walnut kolachFood

| Door and chest keysUsable

| Groschen × 4.5

## Trivia

- Like his father, Heinrich uses German voice lines, unlike Vuytek and Gerda. Taking Doubravka's comment at the Semine wedding into account, this could imply that Heinrich is Emmerich's son from a previous marriage and Vuytek is Gerda's by her first husband, with both parents becoming widowed before they married.

## Heirloom sword

Heirloom sword is a melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

## Description

The sword stolen from the blacksmith's family on the way to Kuttenberg. Besides the owner's maker's mark, the sword seems rather unremarkable, but it's of immeasurable value to the blacksmith's family.

## Acquisition

Finding the Heirloom sword is part of one variation of the repeatable activity In the Service of the Guild.

## Henik

Henik is a minor character living in Tachov in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Unlike most in Tachov, Henik's family wasn't originally from the area. Instead, his parents arrived shortly after a plague and settled into a vacant farm in town and eventually had three sons: Pena, Rudlen, and Henik. However, after their father died, Pena left, and after their mother passed away, Rudlen likewise left, leaving Henik alone. Despite both his older brothers saying they would return in a year, neither did and Henik was left wondering what happened to them.

When Henik started dating Manka, Manka's parents greatly disapproved of the relationship, believing Henik would just follow in his brothers' footsteps and leave the town one day. To them, this meant if the young adults ever got married, Henik would likely take Manka with him and thus they'd never see their daughter again.

Despite Manka's parents' adamant declarations that the relationship between Henik and Manka was over, the young couple were still secretly seeing each other when they could find the time. They were not particularly careful all the time however, as one time they went to a dance in Troskowitz and Manka's parents found out and were furious over it.

### Associated quests
