## Henry of Skalitz

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Next time, I won't run. I'll never run away again. I'll find the one who did this to you. I remember his face. I'll find him.

Henry (Czech: Jindřich) - commonly called Hal (Czech: Jindra) by his friends and locals of Skalitz, or occasionally Henry of Skalitz (Czech: Jindřich ze Skalice) - is the main protagonist of Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He travels with his horse and Mutt (dlc). He also appears in Kingdom Come: Deliverance - Stories Untold.

Henry is the illegitimate son of Radzig Kobyla.

## Biography

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance

Henry lived in the tranquil village of Silver Skalitz, training to be a blacksmith under his father, Martin, at their forge. In between lessons, he'd often go about horsing around with his friends - Fritz, Matthew, and Matthias - while wooing Bianca, the local alemaid and his sweetheart. He eventually began learning the basics of warfare and sword fighting in secret with Vanyek, much to his mother's disapproval.

Henry and his father finished making a masterwork sword for their liege lord, Sir Radzig Kobyla. Henry soon learnt that, in addition to being a skilled swordsmith, his father had some talent in sword fighting as well. Henry longed to venture into the world, so he asked his father to teach him how to defend himself, but Martin refused, preferring that he settle down with a nice girl, learn his blacksmith's trade, and keep away from trouble.

However, this peaceful life was soon to be interrupted. In 1403 a Cuman army commanded by Markvart von Aulitz, one of King Sigismund's lieutenants, attacked and destroyed Skalitz as revenge on Sir Radzig for sending valuable silver and his continuous loyalty towards King Wenceslas IV, Sigismund's deposed half-brother and the rightful king of Bohemia.

A helpless Henry watches as his parents are murdered

Both of Henry's parents were killed in the attack along with most of the other villagers. Henry managed to escape the slaughter, stealing a horse and riding to Talmberg to warn Sir Divish of the attack. During his journey, he may have been able to distract some Cumans from raping and assaulting Theresa, a local miller girl. He was later injured by a Cuman arrow before arriving at his destination.

Once in Talmberg, his wound was treated and he was put on guard duty, as Divish and his captain of the guard, Sir Robard, were wary that Talmberg might be the next target for the approaching army. Luckily, the survivors of Skalitz managed to escape and flee to Rattay, passing by Talmberg on the way south. Sir Radzig was relieved to see Henry alive and commanded Divish to keep him confined in Talmberg castle, forbidding him from returning to Skalitz, which by now was surely swarming with bandits.

Henry mourns his dead parents, and vows revenge

The next day, Sigismund, hot on Radzig's tail, assembled his army outside Talmberg, but thankfully decided to move on in search of his prey, convinced by Divish that they had not seen the escaping refugees. Henry took the opportunity to escape the castle, and headed back to Skalitz to bury his parents.

There, among the smouldering ruins of the town, he saw the bodies of many of his friends and neighbours, including Bianca and his parents. Henry tearfully vowed to bury them and begged their forgiveness for being a coward. Henry searched for a shovel and stumbled across Zbyshek, who was trying to loot the corpses. After a confrontation, Zbyshek ran off, but left behind his shovel. Henry returned to his parent's bodies, but was interrupted by Zbyshek, who had returned with a group of scavenging bandits, led by the powerful and brutal Runt.

Henry faces off against Runt while Zbyshek watches

Runt, taking a liking to the exquisite sword Henry still carried, beat him up and was about to kill him with it, when Theresa appeared, followed closely by Sir Robard and some of the Talmberg guards. They chased off the bandits and Theresa took Henry to her Uncle Peshek's mill in Rattay, where she nursed him back to health over several weeks.

Once recovered, Henry requested a meeting with Lord Radzig, asking to be sworn into his service, in order to learn how to fight, kill Runt and recover the sword, sparking. Radzig was at first hesitant to make a squire from a blacksmith, but relented and ordered Henry to undergo basic training with Captain Bernard in. During this time, Henry met Hans Capon, the future governor of Rattay, and the two struck up a rivalry.

Henry goes hunting with Lord Hans Capon

Bernard then ordered Henry to join the local watchmen on evening patrol. While on duty, Henry attempted to close the local tavern, and got into a fight with Sir Hans, who was less than pleased to be ordered home by a commoner. The fight was interrupted by Sir Hanush, Hans' guardian, who was disgusted by the two young men's comportment. To ensure Henry learnt his place and Hans learnt his lesson, he ordered them to go on a hunting trip together.

While on the trip, the two men learnt a bit more about each other, and both became a bit more respectful, further cemented when Hans was taken prisoner by two Cumans, and Henry was able to save him and ensure his safe return to Rattay. Having now earned the respect of the nobility, Henry was officially accepted into Sir Radzig's service. However, at that moment Captain Bernard arrived to tell them that there had been a raid on the local Neuhof stud farm, and Henry was asked to accompany the captain in opening an investigation.

Henry surveys the slaughter at Neuhof

Once at the farm, they were horrified to learn that nearly all the horses had been slaughtered, along with many of the people. Henry investigated and confirmed that the raiders came from the north, and that Runt was among them. He became suspicious that a stableboy named Ginger might know more than he's letting on, after discovering he had fled the farm.

As it turned out, Ginger was innocent, but because he recognized one of the bandits, he ran away, terrified that they would come after him. Henry dispatched Ginger's pursuers, and Ginger gave him a lead - a man from Uzhitz with a limp. After some more investigation, Henry learnt the limping man was called Lubosh, and headed off to Uzhitz to track him down. However, he arrived too late, as Lubosh had been brutally murdered.

Henry seeks help from Father Godwin

At first, Henry was dismayed, but managed to discover that Lubosh had been spending a lot of time with the local cleric, Father Godwin. Although the priest stated he could not break his vows to tell Henry what he needed to know, they agreed to meet at the local tavern and try to work something out. The two discussed the corruption of the church and drank heavily into the night. The next morning, they awakened hungover and Godwin promised that if Henry performed that day's sermon, he would tell him all he knows about Lubosh. Alternatively, Henry would have the opportunity to speak with the local Bailiff. Either way, he would set off in search of his new lead - Reeky from Ledetchko.

Eventually, Henry was able to track Reeky to a cave near Ledetchko. If he got there in time, he could have savedd Reeky from the bandits who were out to kill him and gain some valuable insight into the Neuhof raid, but if he took too long he would have found Reeky beaten almost to death, and could do nothing more than ease his passing.

Henry is confronted by bandits while searching for the Neuhof gang.

Henry set off to find the next member of the gang, Timmy, tracking him to a windmill south of Merhojed. There, Henry was confronted by four bandits, led by Morcock, and could have either told them where Timmy was, sent them to Rattay while he found Timmy himself, or else killed them. In any event, he would learn the vague location of the bandit camp, and further investigation would reveal them hiding at Pribyslavitz.

Henry was tasked with infiltrating the camp, and may have taken the opportunity to sabotage the food and arrows in preparation of the upcoming battle. While there, he was able to confirm that Runt was holed up inside the crumbling church. Along with Sir Radzig and Sir Bernard, Henry took part in the attack, wiping out the Cuman and bandit camps before turning their attention to the church.

Henry defeats Runt while Sir Radzig and Sir Bernard approach

Runt fled up to the steeple with Henry in hot pursuit. At first, the bandit commander did not recognize him, until Henry began to demand the sword. The two finally fought as equals, and Henry was able to overpower him, repeatedly demanding the sword and becoming more enraged as Runt laughed at him. Henry continued beating Runt's head against the ground until he was no more.

Sir Bernard and Sir Radzig congratulated Henry on his first successful battle, and looked over the remains of the camp, where their troops were finishing off the last of the enemy. Overcome by the sight of the slaughter, and the turmoil of emotions he felt now that Runt was dead, but the sword was still lost, Henry was promptly sick. Bernard advised him to put the day behind him, but Henry vowed to never forget what had transpired.

Henry is made Bailiff of Pribyslavitz

With the From the Ashes DLC installed, a short time after the raid, Henry was appointed the new Bailiff of Pribyslavitz, and was tasked with rebuilding and managing the village. If he was successful in this endeavour, Henry was promised a share of its income for five years - not just a tidy sum, but more importantly, a huge step up in the social world for a blacksmith's son.

Sometime following the raid on Pribyslavitz, Henry learnt the bandits were still conducting raids, and the nobles discovered that a chest of coins recovered from the church were counterfeit. Hearing that the villagers of Merhojed had captured a bandit, Sir Radzig dispatched Henry to interrogate him. The bandit revealed that Runt took his orders from a man they called "The Chief", and he was due to rendezvous with a merchant named Menhart in order to collect another chest of counterfeit coins.

Henry and Sir Radzig share a quiet moment

Henry met again with Sir Radzig to report what he had uncovered. The two enjoyed a quiet moment on the lookout point near Talmberg before Henry questioned why such terrible things happen - what was the point of it all? Sir Radzig responded that life is a trial, and the more problems you overcome, the better a man you will be. He gave Henry approval to pursue Menhart, telling him "good luck, son."

Henry tracked Menhart to Rovna, but found only an empty wagon and some dead guards. He discovered that the local charcoal burners looted the wagon, but did not attack it, and questioned a Mercenary they had rescued, who told Henry the wagon was attacked by a knight. Henry eventually discovered that the knight was named Ulrich of Passau, and he was also seeking the counterfeiters. With or without Ulrich's assistance, Henry managed to find the head counterfeiter, an impoverished knight named Sir Jezhek, and placed him under arrest.

Henry and Ulrich confront the counterfeiter

Jezhek revealed that he was hired in Sasau, and put in charge of minting the counterfeit coins by a young foreigner called Erik, who in turn took his orders from an unknown Hungarian nobleman - the Chief. Henry set off in search of the bandit recruiter, hoping it would finally lead to the man behind it all. Following several potential leads, he eventually learnt that the bandits had a secret meeting place - the church of Sasau.

Once there, Henry was confronted by a bandit named Kozliek, who turned out to be the recruiter. Kozliek gave Henry a test - find and kill the last remaining member of the Neuhof gang, Pious, who turned tail and ran when the robbery turned into a massacre. Pious, as it turned out, had taken vows at the Sasau Monastery and became a novice monk.

Henry takes his vows as 'Brother Gregor'

In order to infiltrate the order, Henry tracked down a nobleman named Karl, who was unwillingly being forced to join the same order as Pious. Together, the two conspired to obtain the writ needed for Henry to access the monastery while posing as Karl. The ruse was a success, and Henry was given the name 'Brother Gregor' after becoming a novice monk.

Thus began Henry's new life in the cloister, as he tried to figure out which of the four novices was Pious. After some time in the Monastery, he was able to determine that Pious had taken the name Brother Antonius, and seemed to sincerely repent his actions. After deciding what to do with Pious, Henry met up with Kozliek again and learnt the location of the bandit camp - Vranik.

Henry learns the truth about his father

Before setting off to Vranik, Henry visited Sir Radzig and Sir Hanush, to tell them of his plan to infiltrate the bandit camp. Hanush was enthusiastic but Radzig hesitated, telling Henry not to put himself at risk. After tying up some loose ends, Henry arrived in Vranik, where he was able to gain entry and speak to the captain, Erik. However, he quickly discovered that Sir Istvan Toth, carrying Sir Radzig Kobyla's sword, was the true mastermind behind the plan, but Istvan captured him before he could escape to warn Radzig.

Istvan ordered his lackey to beat Henry, and told him of his plan to secretly help King Sigismund claim the throne of Bohemia, and be rewarded with Lordship over the Sasau region - he gloated that even the combined forces of Divish, Hanush and Radzig couldn't stop him now. He finally revealsed the secret everyone had kept from Henry his whole life. He was not the son of Martin the blacksmith but the illegitimate son of Lord Radzig Kobyla.

Istvan taunted Henry, telling him the reason Radzig never told him of his true parentage was because he was ashamed of him. Henry vowed to kill Istvan with the sword, but the traitorous Lord laughed it off and promised to give him the chance. He left his lackey to beat Henry senseless, intending on holding him to ransom. However, Henry was able to escape, with the help of Zbyshek, and make it back to Rattay.

Henry attacks Vranik

There, he revealed to Radzig that he knew the truth of his parentage. Radzig promised that they would talk about it later, as they had to plan for the upcoming battle, and Henry raced to Talmberg to tell Sir Divish that the armies were preparing to assemble.

Divish agreed to immediately round up his troops and march to Vranik. That evening, Henry joined the army in an all-out-assault on the camp - but there was no sign of Istvan or Erik, only a letter which mentioned that Istvan would "soon succeed in seizing the castle". At that moment, the soldiers dragged up a bandit that they had captured alive, who laughed at them and mockingly asked which castle they left unguarded - and Divish realized with horror that Istvan had taken his men to Talmberg.

Together with the three Lords, Henry raced to Talmberg, but it was too late - they had infiltrated the castle, and taken Lady Stephanie captive. The men launched a desperate attack to try and breach the castle before the enemy could roll up the drawbridge, but Istvan appeared holding a knife to Stephanie's throat, and revealed he has also captured Radzig, who had raced ahead. Henry and the rest were forced to withdraw as Talmberg burnt around them. Outside, they discussed what their plan should be to rescue Stephanie and Radzig. Hanush was in favour of a siege, but Bernard suggested sending someone to sneak into the castle at night to release the hostages. Henry, of course, volunteered, along with several others including young Sir Hans Capon.

The stealth mission was ultimately a failure, as Henry and his comrades were detected, but they managed to flee before any harms befell them or the hostages. The assembled armies then prepared to lay siege to Talmberg, and Henry completed various tasks to improve the morale and capabilities of the camp, as well as enlisting the help of Konrad Kyeser, the renowned siege machine designer who was currently in Sasau.

After many days of building, a trebuchet was completed, and after several attempts to fire at Talmberg's main gate, the walls of Talmberg were struck, and Henry and the assembled armies of the lords attacked once again. Once they reached the central courtyard of the castle, Toth was confronted by Hanush and the other Lords. Hanush eventually promised Toth that, if he left Sir Radzig safely in the nearby countryside, and the other hostages safe as well, then his men would be given safe passage to do so and a small head start.

Henry waited reluctantly as Toth rode out into the countryside with his father still captured. He questioned those around him as to why Hanush had let Toth go, rather than just trick him and capture them all when they emerged from the tower. Hanush and the others explained that a lord's word is a powerful thing, and that it must be adhered to, otherwise Toth would have never trusted Hanush in the first place. Shortly afterwards, Henry rode out with Hans Capon and some other men to pick up Sir Radzig. They found him standing safely in a meadow outside Skalitz. Sir Hans charged off after Istvan Toth, stating that now that Toth had released Radzig, the traitor was considered fair game.

Sir Radzig and Henry stood and admired their surroundings, exchanging some heartfelt words, and discussing all that had happened, before heading back together. After their return to Rattay, Henry, Sir Radzig, Sir Hanush, Sir Divish, Sir Bernard, Sir Capon, and Sir Robard were visited by Jobst of Moravia. Jobst came to request an alliance with them to stand against Sigismund's invasion of Bohemia and restore King Wenceslaus to the throne. Henry and Hans Capon were sent to Trosky Castle to deliver Lord Otto von Bergow a letter to inquire whether he sought to continue to support King Sigismund.

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Henry begins his adventure immediately following the events of the first game. Serving as squire to the knight Hans Capon, Henry is sent alongside Hans on a mission commissioned by Margrave Jobst, Radzig, and Hanush to Trosky Castle, the seat of Otto von Bergow. Their task is to gauge the political stance of this powerful feudal lord.

The journey quickly turns into a disaster. Henry and Hans Capon fall into a brutal ambush set by bandits. They are severely wounded and stripped of their gear. Henry and Hans Capon were healed and cured by the herbalist Bozhena.

After being separated and then reunited while held captive by von Bergow, Henry and Hans are forced to carry out tasks for him; von Bergow sends Henry and Hans to confront alleged outlaws in Nebakov.

In Nebakov, it turns out that the bandits are not mere outlaws but the armed wing supporting the imprisoned King Wenceslaus IV. Henry and Hans briefly join forces with Žižka in Nebakov. At the same time, Henry and Hans Capon cross paths once again with their arch enemy, Istvan Toth.

After the Battle of Nebakov, Henry, Godwin, Žižka are taken to the dungeons of Trosky, while Hans Capon is captured and taken prisoner by Bergow. After escaping from Trosky, Henry first traveled to Suchdol with Žižka and Katherine; there, Henry met Peter of Písek and once again encountered Jobst of Moravia, with whom he conversed.

Upon arriving in Kuttenberg, Henry met Katherine at the Hangman's Halter Tavern in the market square to learn what information she had gathered about Liechtenstein; she told him about Goatskin, a spy, who frequented a tavern called "The Hole" in the Hoprink district. He obtained the information about Goatskin's whereabouts from Chenyek. Goatskin, in turn, led him to a certain Samuel, who, as Henry would later learn, only let him see John of Liechtenstein because of Henry's sword, carrying the markings of the blacksmith Martin.

Henry could therefore warn Liechtenstein that Sigismun's men are looking for him, and also ask for his advice on freeing Hans Capon from Otto von Bergow, regardless of Jobst's plots. John pointed Henry in the direction of the Ruthards. Kunzlin Ruthard had recently his estates taken from him, and the Maleshov fortress was given to Otto, making it a likely prison of Capon. Ruthard agreed to help Henry, in exchange for Henry getting dirt on Ulrich Vavak, the royal mintmaster. With the help of Christian of Pisek, Henry uncovered Ulrich Vavak's operation. With powerful blackmail material, Vavak was forced to agree to Kunzlin Ruthard's demands, who, in turn, allowed his daughter Rosa to let Henry in on a secret passage into the fortress.

After freeing Hans Capon from Maleshov, Henry took him along and then acting on the orders of Radzig and Hanush traveled to Kuttenberg to learn more about Sigismund’s plans for the council.

After discovering in Kuttenberg that Sigismund had ordered his henchmen to confiscate the property of the local Jews, Henry rushed to Ratibor to warn his allies; there, he met Samuel who turned out to be Martin’s illegitimate son and, after alerting Samuel and Jehuda, set out for Kuttenberg with them, Liechtenstein, and Kubyenka to save the Jews and Sara.

The The Devil's Pack decided to take revenge on Otto von Bergow for the pogrom. It was time to go on the offensive. For that, they needed an advantage. Someone suggested that one such advantage would be the superior firing power of Finger of God, the very weapon that turned the tide during the battle of Nebakov.

At the camp near Opatowitz, acting on information from Katherine, Henry approached the Praguer captain, asking to join the detachment. Corporal Stephen Crow allowed Henry to speak with the captain, Ditrich Katz, who allowed Henry to join, if he found out what happened to a unit that carried precious letters. Henry, possibly with the help of a wounded member of the unit, Myshek, learned about the unit's whereabouts and found out the soldiers weren't ambushed, but that they defected. When Henry obtained the precious documents from the deserters and returned with them to the camp, Katz allowed him to join the Praguer militia.

In the middle of the night, while Henry, Katz, and the camp doctor Musa of Mali were still celebrating Henry's success, Stephen Crow told them that someone stabbed the commander of the Cumans, Chertan. Henry, being the only one who wasn't currently trying to sew Chertan back up, had alibi for the time, and was sober, was the only candidate for the principal investigator of the attack. Unfortunately, Chertan died on Musa's operating table, apparently of poisoning. The camp commander Grozav of Borumlaca immediately accused Musa of the murder. This complicated the plan to steal the Finger of God - it wouldn't be moving to Sedletz until after the trial was concluded.

To Henry and Katz, that accusation was obviously false, as it didn't make sense for Musa to finish the job of the attacker, he didn't have a murder motive, and on top of that, he was a doctor. After thorough investigation, Henry found some suspects, and Sigismund's justicar, Stibor of Stiborzitz was moved by his arguments to convict the person Henry pointed his finger at. The accused, however, refused to be taken prisoner and died in the resulting fight. After the trial, Grozav of Borumlaca was removed from the post of the camp commander (replaced by Stibor of Stiborzitz, and Ditrich Katz ordered the move to Sedletz. Because Henry informed Zizka through Katherine of the exact time, the retinue was ambushed, and the Finger of God taken. With it, it was easy to take Maleshov, although the last cannon ball tore the weapon apart. Otto von Bergow was taken hostage.

Brushes with Death

Legacy of the Forge

Mysteria Ecclesiae

## Henry the Bruiser

Henry the Bruiser is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You beat the best brawler around.

## Acquisition

To unlock this achievement, Henry must defeat one of the two regional fistfighting grandmasters in Trosky or Kuttenberg. Each region hosts its own underground brawling circuit, culminating in a final showdown with a champion. In Trosky it's the Herbalist Barnaby, and in Kuttenberg it's the Gravedigger Frantishek.

## Tips

To begin the Trosky fistfighting circuit, speak with Miller Kreyzl at the Lower Semine Mill to start the following tasks:

- Melee at the Mill - Initiates the regional brawling questline.

- Wine, Women and Blood - Enter the fighting ring via Innkeeper Lawrence at the Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn (you can bypass the entrance fee by speaking with Kreyzl).

- Best for Last - After defeating all opponents, return to Lawrence to challenge the regional grandmaster, Barnaby, a herbalist in northeastern Trosky.

While defeating Barnaby grants no special rewards beyond the achievement, it does complete the region's brawler arc.

To begin the Kuttenberg fight circuit, speak to Thomlin Bruthans in Horschan. Additional tasks include:

- Fight Dirty - Start the brawling side quest.

- Enough! - Available from Innkeeper Zdeslav in Miskowitz, this task opens access to another set of fighters.

- Teeth in the Bag - Initiated by Innkeeper Mole at the Hole in the Wall inn in southeastern Kuttenberg.

- Nail in the Coffin - After completing the previous tasks, return to Mole, then proceed to the cemetery in the northwestern Kuttenberg at night to face Frantishek, the gravedigger and grandmaster of the region.

Defeating Frantishek not only unlocks the achievement, but also rewards Henry with the Shoulder Throw combo from the Unarmed combat skill tree.

## Henry the Matchmaker

Henry the Matchmaker is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You brought Victoria her sweetheart. Against his will.

## Acquisition

This achievement is tied to the Hush, My Darling… side quest. To begin the quest, speak to Innkeeper Zdeslav in Miskowitz and inquire about any local happenings. He will direct you to Martha, the blacksmith's wife. It is strongly recommended to complete this quest immediately after starting it.

Eventually, the quest will lead to Sigismund's Camp, where you must find Black, Victoria's lover, in the infirmary. Treat his food poisoning using a Digestive Potion and avoid provoking him during the conversation - when he complains about Victoria, choose "Alright. I'll tell her." Then knock him out and carry him to Victoria's camp in the woods east of the main road.

At Victoria's location, speak to her once to trigger initial dialogue, then speak again to prompt Henry's line: "You wanted your soldier? Well, here he is!" A cutscene will play, followed by a short conversation. Once the quest concludes, the the achievement will unlock.

If Viktoria does not acknowledge Black the first time you speak to her, select "Hang in a while longer, I'll be back." and then talk to her again.

## Tips

This achievement is highly missable due to several conditions:

- The quest appears to be time-sensitive - if left too long, Victoria may die before the quest can be completed.

- It must be completed before the second point of no return during the Oratores main quest in Kuttenberg.

- A specific dialogue choice is required in order to carry Victoria's lover to her.

## Herald of Kuttenberg

Herald of Kuttenberg is a repeatable task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

Magdalena heard that Fridusch Kumel wants to talk to you, most likely about financing the Kuttenberg Tournament, as the city council recently reduced their support. She'll flag you down. Talk to her, and she'll tell you to find Fridusch. He can usually be found at the tournament grounds near the large bathhouse during the day or at the Town Hall. Talk to him, and he'll ask you to sponsor the tournament.

Agree to contribute, with the following options. You'll receive more blacksmith prestige for paying larger amounts.

- Peasant's contribution (300)

- Blacksmith's contribution (500)

- Noble's contribution (1000)

- Imperial contribution (2000)

- Papal contribution (3000)

Fridusch will thank you for the contribution and suggest you get a waffenrock made by the tailor Tuchmacher with your maker's mark on it to wear during the tournament as a competitor, allowing you to earn blacksmith prestige while competing. This ends the quest and starts the task Forge Waffenrock.

This task will now also start appearing in the DLC's daily repeatable task rotation. It will be marked on the map as a donation task, similar to Alms, and will follow the same loop as the introductory quest, with Fridusch asking for a contribution and your reward scaling with the amount you provide.

## Objectives

## Herbalist Barnaby

Herbalist Barnaby (Czech: Kořenář Barnabáš) is a reclusive man living north of Trosky Castle, in a modest forest hut surrounded by a small herb garden with only his dog for company.

## Biography

### Early life

Growing up, Barnaby was taught all about herbs and alchemy by his very strict grandmother, who would constantly test him on all the knowledge she was teaching him and slap him on the ear if he made a mistake. This relentless teaching method paid off though, as Barnaby was able to commit to memory every recipe and being able to eyeball ingredient amounts instead of having to measure it out.

When he was younger, he worked as a hired hand in Troskowitz and where a girl, Sarah, took an interest in him. However, Barnaby had no interest in her and told her straight away. When Sarah complained to her brother though, her brother figured out Barnaby was gay and used this as an excuse to gather some of his friends and attack Barnaby. Realizing they'd otherwise beat him to death, Barnaby managed to fight them off. However, everyone else in the area viewed Barnaby with disdain.

In turn, Barnaby took to living a solitary life, away from everyone in the woods north of Trosky. Despite knowing the dangers of living in isolation, he does enjoy the solitude it gives and, likely due to his appearance of being poor, unscrupulous people in the area leave him alone. Villagers in the area though don't even try to hide their dislike of him, but come running to him for assistance each time they have a cut or medical issue. While this bothers him with their attitude, he takes it in stride that at least they don't threaten to burn his home down.

### Associated quest

- The Best for Last

## Herbalist Joachim

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Herbalist Joachim is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Joachim was the herbalist living in a hut at the estates of the Sedletz Monastery. Despite not having formal education, Joachim was very knowledgeble in the field of healing and medicine, which earned him respect and friendship of the Kuttenberg apothecary Oswald Torwart. Torwart claimed to have learned a lot from Joachim and often visited him; when they couldn't meet in person because of Torwart's busy schedule, they at least exchanged letters.

Joachim had also met Albich of Uniczow during his previous visit of the monastery.

When the first workers who were opening graves in the crypt on orders of Zacharias of Prachatitz became sick, Zacharias blackmailed Joachim into taking care of them in secret in his hut. Despite Joachim's efforts, he was not a physician and lacked the experience needed to cure the men. When they died, Joachim wanted to get rid of their bodies (since they were infected, and he didn't want to leave them to rot in his house). For that reason, he dragged them into the shed by the flour store and set it ablaze.

However, thanks to Brother Elijah's timely rescue of the bodies from the fire, Henry was able to eventualy figure out where did the bodies come from and come to the hut.
By that time, however, Zacharias' lackey Denes Latzkfi had arrived to get rid of Joachim. After a short argument over the dead men and the arson, Denes stabbed Joachim to death before himself being killed by Henry in a duel.

### Associated quests

- To Dust you Shan't Return

## Herbarium/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Herbarium as it appears in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

The Herbarium is one part of the alchemist's bench in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It serves as a detailed catalog of all herbal ingredients you've discovered. Each entry provides the name of the herb, a short description, its known effects, and clues where it can be found in the world.

All entries are available automatically from the start of the game.

## Belladonna

Atropa

Beware this plant! For its great toxicity it is unsuitable for the apothecary and even a small amount if used badly can bring death! It induces shakes and chills, the body is gripped by convulsions and strange visions. Some old wives know other uses too, but the medical arts have no use for belladonna in cures.

- It grows in clearings and in leafy woods, but it is best not to seek it at all.

- Very poisonous!

Main article: Belladonna

## Chamomile

Matricaria

Dispels all manner of sickness, as well as quieting fever and women's monthly pains. In an infusion it is good to soothe the stomach as well as evil thoughts, but combined with the wrong herb induces sleep too deep. For better and quiet sleep it is well to drink a weak infusion before bed.

- Most often it is found in fields and fertile land.

- Strengthens agility and speech and induces hunger.

Main article: Chamomile

## Comfrey

Symphitum

Called also Black Salsify, it is the best remedy for broken bones, swelling and bruising and aids as well against internal pains from the bones. It is used for health and resilience, but it also drives away horses and big animals.

- Grows most of all on banks by water and in ditches around fields.

- Greatly helps the health and stamina, but induces fatigue.

Main article: Comfrey

## Dandelion

Taraxacum

Drinking it drives the urine strongly and thus purges the body. It is used for prevention of various ailments. It strengthens the endurance of the body under stress and in a syrup drives away colds in long winters.

- Grows everywhere as a weed, but mostly on grassy slopes and meadows it is to be found.

- It strengthens vitality and stamina.

Main article: Dandelion

## Eyebright

Euphrasia

A miraculous herb for all ailments of the eyes and sight. In a compress it relieves inflammation, in suitable combination it improves agility and dispels night gloom from the eyes. He who desires to have sharp eyes should drink regularly a tonic boiled from Eyebright.

- Grows on pastures and heaths and in all places where there is light enough, as well as wet ground.

- Increases agility and speech.

Main article: Eyebright

## Henbane

Hyoscyamus

For immediate relief from pain and for anaesthesia before medical treatment in which the flesh must be cut, for it kills pain and puts the body in a state of torpor. It is not recommended for picking or using by lay folk for its toxicity, which even the beasts recognize and are wary to approach it.

- It grows in sunny and warm places, especially on dung and rubble.

- A strong poison, yet it increases vitality.

Main article: Henbane

## Herb Paris

Paris

In old wives' recipes it is said to be a protection from sickness, and in the apothecary against the headache. It is not recommended for lay folk to pick or use it, for it is poisonous and induces nausea and sleep, though rarely does the poisoning end in death, unless it be with other poisons mixed.

- It may be sought in deep woods.

- Reduces stamina, induces sleep and lowers health.

Main article: Herb Paris

## Marigold

Calendula

Good against cramps, inflammations and ulcers, against many skin blemishes and fungus, good for bathing and ointment as well as a medicinal drink. It helps women against monthly pains and restores regularity to them. Placed on a wound it speeds recovery. It is sometimes mixed with other greens in a drink to arouse love desire and the affection of the opposite sex.

- Grows where the earth is fertile - on rubble piles and dung and abundantly too in pastures.

- Raises health and vitality.

Main article: Marigold

## Mint

Mentha

He who mulls wine with mint and drinks it in the morning cannot that day be intoxicated by any other drink.

- It is rarely found in nature, but rather alongside houses and in gardens cultivated.

- Improves speech and dispels fatigue, but increases hunger.

Main article: Mint

## Nettle

Urtica

Take pounded nettle leaves and place them on a wound and the bleeding will stop at once. Also chopped and steamed it provides a tasty meal that dispels hunger. It should not be mixed with certain herbs, for then it may cause cold shivers. Its burn and sting are good against ache of the joints.

- It can be found abundantly by water, on the edge of woods and in the furrows of fields.

- Improves health, but lowers speech and vitality.

Main article: Nettle

## Poppy

Papaver

A herb that is beautiful to look upon, but treacherous for the body, which is often brewed for little ones and for the sick. Brewed correctly it will put anyone to sleep and immerse them in dreamless darkness, to awake with head left empty. Boiled with the tooth of a wild boar it is said to help the hunt.

- It is found abundantly in fields and furrows as a bothersome weed.

- Brings fatigue and reduces stamina.

Main article: Poppy

## Sage

Salvia

An aromatic herb for fumigation and brewing potions of all kinds, it drives away insects as well as evil spirits. Too much inhalation induces prophetic dreams. Whoever drinks sage shall have less headache after alcohol, whoever drinks too much shall become dull-witted. Whoever drinks it in moderation and brewed in the right combination shall gain strength in battle.

- Can be found in pastures and on hillsides.

- Improves strength and vitality. It reduces speech.

Main article: Sage

## St. John's wort

Hypericum

St. John's wort, the king of all medicinal plants, purifies the blood and dispels dropsy and kidney stones. Whoever brews it in wine arms himself against all alcohol, whoever brews it in oil prevents decay of meat. It is good also for stamina and sharp eyes, it unties the tongue and dispels foul moods. When used too often it loses its effects on the body.

- It is most fond of leafy woods, glades and clearings.

- Improves agility as well as stamina, but somewhat takes away strength and vitality.

Main article: St. John's wort

## Thistle

Benedictus

Thistle is a miraculous medicine against various ailments and plague especially. In water it gives relief from pain and poisoning and in ale restores the appetite. In wine it dulls a man's wits and should not be thus imbibed.

- It grows in roadside ditches, in clearings and where there is relief from the sun and rather shadow gathers.

- Adds stamina, reduces speech.

Main article: Thistle

## Valerian

Valeriana

The name "Valerian" means "to be healthy" and truly it helps against all ills - pains as well as impure influences. It is known as a panacea for various ailments and an additive to drinks that arouses loving desire and summons lovers. Hung in the house it protects against lightening and properly prepared helps in the hunt.

- To be found on forest paths, in mires and peat bogs and everywhere that ground is damp.

- Renews health and energy, but lessens strength.

Main article: Valerian

## Wormwood

Artemisia

Whoever suffers from fever and headache should put on his head at night a bandage dipped in it. It helps also against chills and dizziness when drunk in an infusion. For increasing strength it is good to lessen its bitterness by the correct addition of other herbs, though with others it has sometimes detrimental effects.

- Abundant grows on roadsides and in fields.

- Greatly increases strength and dispels fatigue, but lowers speech.

Main article: Wormwood

## Herbwoman Bozhena

Herbwoman Bozhena (Czech: Kořenářka Božena) is an elderly herbalist and former midwife who lives in a secluded hut in the woods west of Troskowitz, along with her adopted daughter Pavlena.

In her old age, she has become nearly blind and relies heavily on her daughter for daily tasks.

## Biography

Bozhena used to be a midwife living in Troskowitz, helping the town's women as needed, just like her mother before her. At one point, she was assisting a young woman during labour, but who died shortly after giving birth to a baby girl. With the father not around either, Bozhena ended up taking in the baby, naming her Pavlena, and raising her as her own.

While Pavlena was really young, one fateful night Bozhena was called on by another villager, Jakesh, to assist his wife, Ludmila, who'd been in labour for several hours already. However, he had sent for assistance too late and Ludmila ended up giving birth to a stillborn baby boy before she herself died from the exhaustion. Bozhena could only helplessly stand by but Jakesh, not realizing his son had been stillborn, accused Bozhena of having damned his son for not christening him before death, and letting his wife die. He riled up the rest of the town and they drove Bozhena out of town.

Bozhena was then forced to live in isolation with her daughter in a small hut out in the forest, making due with what they could forage from the land. As Pavlena grew older, she took to making baskets to sell in town to help out, as at least the villagers didn't blame her for what happened.

Years later, two badly injured men, Hans Capon and Henry, burst into her cabin in the middle of the night. As Hans begged her to save Henry, an armed man appeared and attacked. Despite his own injuries, Hans managed to kill the thug, but was also badly wounded in the process. Acting quickly, Bozhena did her best to heal them both and managed to save them. After the two were well enough to continue travelling, they thanked Bozhena and Pavlena for saving them and their hospitality. Bozhena then gave the men some food and money as they set off for their destination. Grateful, Henry can later return to repay his debt.

However, there was still clear animosity from Jakesh against Bozhena and, while he never wished for Pavlena to be hurt, his drunken rants about Bozhena caused some of his hired hands to try and scare Pavlena to get at Bozhena. When Bozhena learned of this, she finally had enough of Jakesh and wished for something to be done about him as otherwise she and Pavlena would never know peace.

If Henry manages to convince Jakesh to stop targeting Bozhena:

Bozhena thanked Henry for his assistance in helping with Jakesh.

If Henry denies helping them:

Pavlena gets executed by hanging and Bozhena hangs herself in her hut.

### Associated quests

- Fortuna

- Bad Blood

## Herbwoman Vlasta

Herbwoman Vlasta is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Vlasta lived outside of Miskowitz with her late husband Peter, as his career as a poacher necessitated easy access to the woods. After his death, she decided to stay there on her own, saying that it would be less painful to be where they had shared their life than alone anywhere else.

Locals would often come to her for herbs and decoctions and even the tending of wounds. As such, she was greatly affected emotionally by the presence of pillaging soldiers in the region and developed a dislike of them strong enough that she helped supply a small group of local rebels who were working to steal and undermine the soldiers.

### Associated quests

- The Peasants' Revolt

## Hic-Hic-Boom

Hic-Hic-Boom is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Making gunpowder while drunk isn't a very good idea.

## Acquisition

The Hic-Hic-Boom achievement is awarded for failing to make the gunpowder while drunk.

## Tips

- You must first obtain the Recipe for Lead shot gunpowder. It can be acquired through several methods:

- Reward for completing the side quest Opus Magnum for Miller Kreyzl.

- Purchased from the Apothecary in southern Kuttenberg, near the Emperor Charles Tavern.

- Found in the evidence chest during the main quest Via Argentum.

- To craft the gunpowder, you'll need the following ingredients, all of them are available at the Kuttenberg apothecary:

- Sulphur × 1

- Saltpetre × 1

- Charcoal × 1

- Before attempting the recipe, consume a large amount of alchohol to become intoxicated. Around five bottles should suffice, depending on your alcohol tolerance. Henry must reach the second stage of drunkenness, indicated by heavy screen sway and blurred vision (beyond 50% of the negative intoxication phase).

- There is an alchemy bench in the back room of the apothecary. Follow the recipe incorrectly to trigger the achievement. A minor mistake is sufficient, such as boiling each phase for 1 turn instead of the correct 2 turns. The goal is to fail the potion, but not so severely that the brewing process halts prematurely.

- If performed correctly a message will appear: "Making gunpowder while drunk was not a very good idea." At this point, the achievement will unlock.

## High Noon

High Noon is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You shot a gun-wielding enemy with a gun.

## Acquisition

Firearms become available during the main quest The Finger of God, shortly before the final battle in the Trosky region. This quest is also when Henry first receives a Pistole.

The High Noon achievement is highly missable, as there are only a few specific moments throughout the game where enemy firearms are present and can be countered in kind. These opportunities typically occur during major story battles where you are tasked with defending a position.

## Tips

- While there are multiple points in the story where the achievement can be earned, due to heavier enemy armour in the Kuttenberg region, it's recommended to attempt this achievement during the Trosky portion of the game.

- The most reliable opportunity is during The Finger of God, when defending the castle walls.

- During the objectives "Defend the castle" and "Knock down the ladders," position yourself on the battlements.

- Look for an enemy shooter standing behind a wooden fence on the far left side. This opponent wears little to no armour, making him an ideal target. A single accurate shot with the Pistole is often sufficient to defeat him. Once the enemy is killed with a firearm, the achievement will unlock.

- At Rabstein Mill ruin (north of Old Lhota in the Kuttenberg region), there is a hostile NPC called "Alchemist." In close quarters, he will choose melee combat, but if given enough distance, he will switch to a Hook gun, making it a good opportunity to obtain this achievement.

## High Toll

High Toll is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

Kuttenberg innkeeper Geldstück is having problems with a group of Sigismund’s soldiers who have ensconced themselves on the road between Kuttenberg and Grund, collecting tolls from merchants. He asked me if I could do something about it.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Innkeeper Franz Geldstück at the Iron Eagle to start the quest. He will let you know that a group of soldiers have set up a toll along the road to Grund and have been causing local merchants a lot of problems. He wants you to get them to move on, whatever it takes.

You can take them out head-on or by stealth, but you can also deal with them diplomatically. To do so, approach during the day and speak to the soldier guarding the road. Pass a medium presence check and he’ll allow you to read the writ.

It turns out, the writ is for a very different road, and the men are here illegally. At that point, you can send them away peacefully or else initiate combat.

If you are unable to convince the soldier to show you the writ, and you do not want to slaughter the group, you will have to steal it. Approach at night and pickpocket the writ from an NPC called ‘Royal Customs Officer.’

Once you have the writ, return to Geldstück to complete the quest and collect your payment.

## Hired hand Franzi

Hired hand Franzi is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Most of Franzi's past isn't clear, though one day his cousin, Ventza, worked with Gules to see about stealing from Tachov's blacksmith and enlisted Franzi to help out. To pull off their plan, the cousins apprenticed to him and worked for about a month before they were sent with a loaded cart to take to a wedding in Semine.

However, they suddenly got the idea to try and take the goods for themselves, cutting out Gules. Gules learned of this though and managed to find the cart and cousins. Owing to Ventza having saved Gules' life though, Gules only had Franzi tied up while he confronted Ventza.

If The Jaunt is completed and Ventza surrenders:

Unfortunately for Gules and his men, the missing cart hadn't gone unnoticed and Jan Semine set out with Captain Gnarly and Henry to find it. The trio soon found and attacked Gules' bandit camp, taking Gules captive alongside the two cousins. The three were then taken to Semine, where their fates would be decided. Being a commoner, though not having committed egregious acts, Semine put him to work as a hired hand. However, as part of his punishment, Franzi had to give up all of his possessions as penitence. Despite this, he felt life was pretty decent at Semine as he had a roof over his head and enough food to eat.

### Associated quest

- The Jaunt

## Hired hand Ota

Hired hand Ota is a hired farmhand and brother to Straw in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Ota worked as a hired hand under Jakesh in Troskowitz along with his brother Straw. The two wanted to be in the good graces of their employer and after hearing the older man rant and rave about the Herbwoman Bozhena and her alleged mistreatment of his late wife and son, the brothers decided to take matters into their own hands.

To get revenge on Bozhena, they decided to ambush her daughter, Pavlena. However, they were surprised by the presence of her man, Roman a local woodcutter. Straw panicked and hit Roman over the head with a rock, killing him. He then tried to bury Roman to hide what had happened while Ota took Pavlena to a hiding place in a nearby gorge.

Ota was holding Pavlena captive when Henry came to the gorge in search of her. He was either convinced to let Pavlena go, in which case she killed him, or he killed Pavlena and then was killed by Henry in turn in the ensuing fight.

### Associated quest

- Bad Blood

## Hired hand Stanley

Hired hand Stanley is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Stanley worked on the farm under Thomlin Bruthans in Horschan and participated in the fighting ring there. Thomlin described him as having a big mouth and the strength of two men.

He thought of Tobias, called Darling by most, as an idiot and and easy target for ridicule. At one time, he went to Darling’s place in Grund, scared the horses there, and beat Darling’s dog, Beda, causing the dog to become afraid of strangers.

He also thought it was quite fun to lie to Darling and trick him into getting drunk, even one time goading him into trying to capture the moon out of the water by telling him it was a silver platter, which resulted in Darling nearly drowning.

He could fight with Henry when Henry came through Horschan. After losing, Henry could tell him to go easy on Darling.

### Associated quests

## Hired hand Straw

Slavobor, better known as Straw, is a hired farmhand and brother to Ota in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Straw worked as a hired hand under Jakesh in Troskowitz along with his brother Ota. The two wanted to be in the good graces of their employer and after hearing the older man rant and rave about the Herbwoman Bozhena and her alleged mistreatment of his late wife and son, the brothers decided to take matters into their own hands.

To get revenge on Bozhena, they decided to ambush her daughter, Pavlena. However, they were surprised by the presence of her man, Roman a local woodcutter. Straw panicked and hit Roman over the head with a rock, killing him. He then tried to bury Roman to hide what had happened while Ota took Pavlena to a hiding place in a nearby gorge.

Henry would investigate Pavlena's disappearance on her mother's insistence and confronted Straw. Depending on his actions, Straw could have been killed immediately or taken to Bailiff Thrush to face punishment either for murder or accidental killing.

### Associated Quest

- Bad Blood

## Hog

Hog is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Hog, whose real name is Chrudosh, is a member of the Kuttenberg Guild. Usually found at The Hole in the Wall tavern, Hog explains that he was a guardsman who lost his position when Sigismund took over the city. He then turned to a life of crime to get by, but wasn't very good at it. He was in a pillory when he was found by Chenyek and Goliath. The pair gave him a job and taught him how to steal properly. He describes himself and Rat as the "main workforce" of the Guild, meaning that they do whatever Chenyek tells them to.

Hugo lived in Troskowitz where he looked after pigs and often took them to the nearby forests to forage. One day, he lost track of one of his pigs when he came across Henry who let him know his pig was eating the dead body of a murdered man in the woods.

## Hole in the Wall

Hole in the Wall is a tavern in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is located in Kuttenberg.

## Description

Kuttenberg’s most infamous tavern, a veritable den of ill repute. Those in the region will say its name is apt, but although that may be true for the quality of goods and likelihood of losing your purse, the tavern is quite large. It consists of the tavern proper as well as a large yard and barn with chicken coop. The barn hosts a fighting ring as well, where some of the regulars will place bets and fight for entertainment.

The Hole in the Wall’s most famous regular is a skeleton called Hugo which sits in the main drinking area and has done so for longer than most anyone can remember. Along with him, the tavern is also home to a self-styled thieves’ guild, led by Chenyek, who see themselves as righteous thieves. Under Chenyek, they focus on local supporters of Sigismund and champion the poor.

## Home Sweet Home!

Home Sweet Home! is an achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You completed the reconstruction of your smithy.

## Acquisition

To earn the Home Sweet Home! achievement, you must restore every upgradeable section of your new Forge, obtained during the Adept quest.

Focus on purchasing all Garden upgrades, which unlock the functional features like journeyman buildings.

## Tips

- Reaching Prestige level 15 is required to make all essential upgrades available.

- You don't have to purchase all the options. Selecting the lowest-tier upgrade for each slot is sufficient. As long as every slot has at least one upgrade applied, the trophy will unlock.

## Hook gun

Hook gun is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as the ranged weapon type.

## Description

A hand cannon, unlike a pistole, is a much more massive weapon. The barrel is fitted with a hook on the underside, which serves to wedge the weapon behind an obstacle and limit recoil when fired. This piece has a barrel made of wrought iron and therefore does not last as long as guns cast in bronze. It is therefore recommended to shoot with a smaller powder charge. Up close, this gun cracks knights in metal like thrushes snails on a rock.

## Hop field

Hop field is a point of interest in Sedletz Monastery in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A large field where hop plants are grown and the hops they produce are stored and processed into beer. The field has its own well and walls and there are two main buildings used with the hops. The storage building is in the middle of the field, storing not just hops but straw and upstairs is a table and chest. In the south-eastern corner of the field is a building for processing the hops where the beer kegs can also be found.

### Associated Quest

## Horschan

Horschan (Czech: Hořany) is a village located northwest of Kuttenberg and west of Grund.

## Codex entry

The settlement on the border of the Kolin and Kuttenberg regions was likely inhabited since ancient times. In the 1970s, a borehole discovered a prehistoric granary with remains of pottery of the so-called Knovíz culture (8th-6th century BC).

Regarding preserved records, Horschan is mentioned in 1299, when Wenceslas II handed it over to the Sedletz monastery and Markvart Šik of Kuttenberg. In 1437, Sigismund of Luxembourg (by then already Emperor) pledged the village to the 'Hussite King', George of Podiebrad.

- Drying rack

## Horse Racing

Horse Racing is one of the three free content updates released for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It was released on 16 May 2025 through patch 1.3 alongside the Brushes with Death expansion.

## Description

Prove your riding and shooting skills and settle the feud between two nomads. Take part in mounted archery, where good aim and quick observation win the day, or take off in a cross-country race to test your horse's stamina and knowledge of the Trosky region.

- Experience a swift and perilous new adventure

- Access to new activities: mounted archery and cross-country horse racing

- The opportunity to gain two unique perks and horse tack

## Overview

In the horse racing events, you face off against three challengers on a range of routes that increase in difficulty. These checkpoint-based tracks wind through the landscape.

Mounted archery challenges require you to ride along a set path and shoot targets from horseback. To succeed, you'll need to maintain accuracy while in motion and score enough points before reaching the finish.

The activities are available at the Nomads' Camp located west of Zhelejov. Find Bibrek the Archer and Horse handler Mikolai, who oversee the competitions. Speak with them to begin the questline.

## Achievements

There are a total of 2 new achievements introduced in the Horse Racing DLC.

|

Boneworks

10

|
You helped the executioner, knacker, and ossuary guardian.

|

Flagellum Dei

10

|
You scored 150 points in the mounted archery competition.

## Horse races

Horse races is a repeatable task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It becomes available after the completion of Horses for Courses.

## Description

Mikolai is testing my riding skills and knowledge of the region.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Mikolai in the Nomads' camp to start the quest. You can only run one race an in-game day.

Choose from 10 different courses, each named for the landmarks it encompasses. They will be listed in increasing order of complexity. Once you choose one, you can also pick its difficulty: simple, honest, or tough. In the tougher races, the other racers will take more shortcuts and have better top speeds. Once you select your course and your difficulty, you’ll have to put up the stake for the prize which is also determined by the chosen variables.

Run the race and then take your prize. The checkpoints will be marked by a smoke signal and you will have to pass through the decorated gate to clear each one.

A successful win will net you some Horsemanship and Survival experience as well as the prize pot.

### Semine

Ride straight ahead towards the smoke, being careful to avoid falling into the pond. Turn around and race straight back to the finish.

Objectives

### Semine, Schdiar, Zhelejov

Ride straight ahead towards the smoke, being careful to avoid falling into the pond.

From there, turn to your right and ride towards the homestead north of Nebakov Mill.

Once you pass through the second checkpoint, turn left and race towards Zhelejov, you’ll have to go through the green, so approach by the road if you don’t have great handling and you are not competing on a harder difficulty.

Finally, head back to the starting point from the green in Zhelejov it should be in front of you.

Objectives

## Horse tack/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Horse tack is a type of equipment that Henry can equip his horse with in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

Each piece of tack affects the horse's stats, sometimes negatively. These decreases can be balanced with other tack.

There are four categories: Bridles, Saddles, Torso armour, and Horseshoes.

## Overview

Bridles

Bridles offer some defence for horses, but their primary purpose is to increase stamina and speed.

Saddles

Saddles offer greater defence than bridles, but their primary purpose is to increase a horse's carrying capacity. With an increased carrying capacity, saddles can also lead to a decrease in maximum speed relative to the amount of extra capacity they provide.

Torso armour

Torso armour for horses is separated into caparisons and breeching. Both, however, provide similar bonuses namely an increase to armour, stamina, and courage with a decrease to maximum speed and carrying capacity.

Horseshoes

Horseshoes offer no increase to armour but increase maximum speed.

## Horseman's pick

Horseman's pick is a blunt-type weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It can be crafted.

## Description

The horseman’s pick is a light riding ace with a spike. Used correctly, it’s a good friend in a pinch. Its sharp point can cut through armour, its blade through any shield.

## Craft Usage

Main article: Sketch - Horseman's pick

- Fastening material × 1

- Frankfurt steel × 1

- Iron × 2

## Horses for Courses

## Description

Apparently, it was possible in the nomads’ camp to take part in horse races. I went there to find out more and maybe earn a few extra groschen.

## Synopsis

Bibrek and Mikolai are fighting over the dedication of an altar near the Nomad Camp. Each claims it for his own under the name of Karachin for Bibrek and Zamur for Mikolai. Henry must complete their challenges and prove himself in the sports of horseback archery and horse racing in order to earn their respect and then he can resolve the dispute.

Henry can claim the altar for either side, or for both.

## Walkthrough

Speak to either Bibrek or Mikolai to begin the quest. Each will tell you about his preferred sport and ask that you accompany him to an altar to pray before beginning. No matter who you choose, the other will appear at the altar and claim ownership. They will then set up challenges for you to complete for each of their chosen sports.

### Horse Racing

You must win all three races to complete Mikolai's segment.

First race - Straight ahead to the checkpoint (Semine Pond) and back

Second race - Again to Semine pond, then east to the Schdiar farm, northwest to Zhelejov, and back west to the starting point

Third race - First checkpoint is back in Zhelejov, then continue northeast to the Quarry below Trosky, and south to the Troskowitz cemetery. Continue south to the Slatego farm, then west back to the starting point.

Notes: Pebbles with the Good Old Pebbles perk and the Final Stretch perk is almost guaranteed to win as long as you don't get lost.

### Horseback Archery

You have to match or beat Bibrek's score in each of the three courses to complete his segment. There are three types of targets, all with different point values. You do not need to hit the highest value targets every time in order to win, they are smaller and harder to hit.

Round Targets - 1 point each, the largest and easiest to hit

Straw Dummies - 3 points, skinny but taller

Buckets - 5 points, smallest of them all

Notes: It is best to set your horse to follow the course automatically at the default speed. It is possible to slow down near targets, but this can open you up to running out of time as each course has a time limit. You will gain a points bonus at the end of every run, so your score does not need to be as high from shooting as you might expect.

### Resolution

Once you have completed all six challenges, return to either quest giver and tell him you are ready to make your judgement. Each will offer you a special piece of horse armour if you decide in his favour. You can choose whichever you fancy, but in order to acquire both you must pick the following dialogue options:

- To both!

- First of a Thousand and Tooth

After completing the quest, the full range of races and archery courses will be open to you.

## Hunger and Despair

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Hunger and Despair is the 29th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically when you wake from your rest at the end of Besieged.

## Description

Losses and a lack of food are taking their toll on the defenders of Suchdol. Everyone is hungry, and with each passing day, the Praguers are getting closer to the walls.

## Walkthrough

### Find food for Capon

Starvation has all but set in a few weeks into the siege. Hans will ask you for a morsel of food which you can then search for. If you’d like, you can talk to him again and insist you’ll find nothing, which will automatically end the segment.

You can ask your allies if they’ve seen any food anywhere, but most will have nothing but anecdotes. The stablemaster of Suchdol will mention a stash of alcohol he hid so he won’t die sober, but he’s not willing to share with just anyone.

Talking to the stablemaster will also give you the option to ride the horse Boudica, whose owner has fallen, to keep her healthy. She is in the stable, all you need to do is mount her and then ride around the outer bailey a few times and then back to the inner stables. Talk to the stablemaster after returning her and he’ll give you some moonshine. Alternatively, you may brew some moonshine at the alchemy bench. You can then give this to Capon, or have it for yourself.

After you ask Janosh for food, Dry Devil will call you over with a proposition. He wants to kill and eat Mutt. You can agree to do so, but this will truly kill him and you will not have access to a dog in the post game. If you agree, the Devil will brew Man's best soup and give you two portions. If you don’t want him to kill Mutt, you’ll either have to pass a hard speech or intimidation check, or else beat him in a fist fight. If you have sent Mutt home before The Italian Job, there will be some other, nameless dog in the fortress you can eat instead.

At the inner gate, you’ll find Kubyenka, Godwin, Sam, and Musa together discussing food. Musa knows of a man who once made soup from shoes. The best would be sheep leather, and Kubyenka noticed Gerta wearing such shoes. You can find them in her room in a chest, you can also convince her to hand the key to her chest over with a very hard speech, or hard intimidation check (the domination check will fail).

In front of her room will be a guard, if you do not have the key from her, pass a medium speech check to lure him away. Bring them to Musa, and he’ll make Shoe soup.

Once you give Capon some food, the next section will start.

Lent

If you are going for the Lent achievement, any of the soup options will lock you out. Even if you do not eat them and only keep them in your inventory, it will count as having eaten meat.

All you need for Capon is some kind of food. You can give him the moonshine from the stablemaster or else you can look for some wine in the fortress.

### Protect the fortress

First, a funeral. Godwin will say a prayer, pick any you like. Then, immediately following, an attack will begin. As always, the first step is to knock down as many ladders as you can.

As before, some of the men in your company can die, so feel free to reload if you are not as efficient with the ladders on the first go. After the ladders are down, you’ll have to break into the tower where some enemies have holed up. Bash down the door, take out the enemies inside, then deal with the next wave of ladders on the other ramparts.

If you head down and focus on the tower, your allies may be able to deal with the walls themselves. If not, once you clear the tower, head back up and clear the walls. The battle at the back will be won, but the outer bailey will be lost.

Someone needs to send word to Jobst to send reinforcements. Henry of course will volunteer.

### Get ready to leave

Now it’s time to prepare for stealth and say your goodbyes. Should you be romancing either Katherine or Hans, this will be the climax of that arc, so make sure you go and talk to them, but only once you’re ready for time to pass. Katherine will be down by the infirmary while Hans will be in his room. Before you leave the room, Zizka will want to talk to you about Katherine, where he’ll explain her backstory and reason for being with the group.

Around the fortress, you’ll find all your other allies and you can say goodbye to them as well. When you’re ready, head to the ramparts if you haven’t been put there already following a romance scene. The next cutscene ends the quest and starts the next, Reckoning.

## Hunting the Werewolf

Hunting the Werewolf is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

After completing Carrot on a Stick and The Lost Sheep, you'll be directed to talk to another shepherd, Natan, who's also been having problems with losing sheep. When you go talk to Natan, he'll mark on some unusual issues regarding his missing sheep and suspects a werewolf as the cause.

Head to the crossroads he mentions to find a broken arrow in the tree stump and some blood on the ground. If you have Mutt, he can be used to track down the dead sheep. Otherwise, you'll have to try and follow the bloody trail that goes off from here.

Eventually you'll find the culprit: some vagrants had been snatching and killing the sheep. Unfortunately, they're not up for much conversation, so you'll have to fight them enough to get them to surrender or scare off so you can examine the dead sheep on the rock to confirm what happened to it.

With that, go back to let Natan know what was really killing his sheep and he'll reward you with 1 Wolf ear, Weak Saviour Schnapps, Schnapps, 25 Groschen, 3 Bandages, Bread, 2 Cooked onions, and an Even die. He'll also point you to the hunter that'll buy the ears off of you.

If you go back to Natan without killing or knocking out the bandits, Henry and Natan's dialogue is slightly changed, and Natan only gives Henry with Beer, 6 Groschen, Wolf ear, Weak Chamomile Decoction, Apple, Bandage, and 2 Carrots.

## Objectives

- Track down the werewolf

- Explore the vagrant camp

- Go back to Natan.

## Hush, My Darling…

Hush, my Darling… is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is a timed quest.

## Description

The wife of the Miskowitz blacksmith, Martha, is looking for horseshoes. But is there more than meets the eye here?

## Walkthrough

Speak to the Blacksmith's wife Martha in Miskowitz and she will request you forge two sets of Horseshoes, as her husband refuses to do work for Sigismund's camp. If you need materials or the recipe for them you can speak to the husband, pass a hard speech check to have them provided for free, or else purchase them.

Once the shoes are forged, return to Martha and she’ll ask you to give them to the girl who usually does deliveries, Victoria. Her house is south of the smithy and when you get there you’ll find it empty with lots of blood in the hearth room.

If you want to skip directly to where she is, you can, but the game will expect you to search. Go back to Martha and let her know what you found. She will suggest you check at the war camp and with a local farmer, Kuba who had his eye on Victoria.

The farmer is usually nearby in the village, he doesn’t know anything and repeated interrogation will make him hostile. If you want you can fight him or leave him alone and believe his story. You can also pickpocket Victoria's scarf from him for Mutt to track.

Next, head to Sigismund’s camp. If you ask around, you’ll be directed to the smithy in the middle of the camp. There, the blacksmith will tell you about a soldier called Black with whom Victoria usually hangs around.

Black is currently in the infirmary. To get anything out of him, you’ll have to treat him. Passing the survival checks will determine that he ate something bad and requires a Digestive potion. Once he has that, ask him about Victoria. He will tell you you can probably find her in a field not far from the camp.

At this point, you can choose a few different ways to approach things. Passing skill checks can convince Black to step up and take responsibility for Victoria, allowing you to send her back to the camp later.

There is a unique ending if you knock Black out and physically take him to her, this will unlock the achievement Henry the Matchmaker. However, this route can lock other objectives in Sigismund’s camp, as you will almost certainly have to kill some of its inhabitants to take him as it is considered assault and kidnapping.

Victoria will be in the clearing Black indicated. Talk to her and you may be able to convince her either to go back to the camp, if previously you convinced Black to take her, head to the Devil’s Den or back to Martha’s in Miskowitz.

There are no real tangible rewards for this quest and the ending has no trickle-down effect on anything else (unless you had to kill a few guards in the camp). So choose however you will.

## Trivia

- This quest seems to be inspired by the famous Czech novel The Grandmother. In it, a village girl called Viktorka (Czech diminuitive from Victoria - in the Czech translation, the female protagonist of this quest is also called Viktorka, not Viktorie which would be the corresponding translation to Victoria) falls in love with a soldier known as Black Hunter (for his mesmerizing black eyes) and runs away from home to follow him wherever his regiment might go. She is later found homeless, living in a cave in a forest after going mad from the love or obsession over Black Hunter, and it is subsequently revealed that she fell pregnant, had a baby, and probably killed the said baby by throwing it into the river.

## Ignatius (sheep)

Ignatius is a ram that belongs to Siegfried in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

According to Siegfried, Ignatius is a rather stubborn ram, making Siegfried unsure whether the ram is the stupidest one he's ever met or the brightest.

If Siegfried is approached about trying to find Mutt, he'll tell you of a local pack of wolves that a stray dog has been seen with. He'll then lend you Ignatius if you ask for bait to get the pack to come out. Note that Ignatius can die to the wolves if you don't quickly get their attention on you instead. Otherwise, if he survives, he'll make his way back to his owner, who'll be pleased as he's still rather fond of the stubborn ram.

Sometime later though, Siegfried ended up selling the ram to Stanislav, and likewise caused issues for the herder.
