## Ill Repute

Ill Repute is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. You can pick up the quest by talking to Betty after finishing A Good Scrub.

## Description

The city council is going to vote soon to choose which baths in Kuttenberg to elevate to City Bathhouse status, which means it won't have to pay high taxes. As might be expected, Betty's Kingfisher bathhouse doesn't have much chance because Adam, her biggest rival, is bribing councillor Jerome Naaz to award him the title.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Betty at the Kingfisher about her troubles after having completed A Good Scrub to start the quest. Henry has an idea of how to help her, turn Adam’s prized guest against him to guarantee her better odds at being named the Municipal Baths and avoiding a tax that would force her to close. This is a time-sensitive quest and will progress differently if you delay.

First, you’ll need to learn about Councillor Naaz’s preferences from the women who work for Adam. Head over to the other bathhouse and talk to the girls to get information. Lousy Mary won’t know anything and will suggest you speak to the others.

- Katchka, following a very hard Charisma or Presence check or some groschen will tell you they once had to change a tub for Naaz on account of a flea infestation along with the location of the councillor’s special tub.

- Little Lida will request a dress (get the most expensive Noblewoman's Cotehardie) for her information and if given one will tell you they use a special fragrant oil for the councillor which Adam keeps locked in his room.

- Hanka from Prague will suggest you speak to Mary, as Lousy Mary doesn’t know anything it’s Meaty Mary you want.

- Meaty Mary won’t tell you anything unless you can pass a very hard speech or hard charisma check. Then, she’ll let you know that the councillor has his own special cask of wine and is allergic to chamomile.

To make sure Naaz has the worst time possible, you’ll want to steal the oil, plant a flea-ridden rag, and mix in some chamomile to the wine. If you already have a chamomile decoction on you or your horse, the only thing you’ll need to leave the bathhouse for is the fleas.

Talk to a few beggars around town, although rude, one will offer some info for 31 groschen. They’ll tell you about a blanket in the Cobblers’ Quarter so infested with fleas you can tell at a glance. The blanket can be found in a rubbish heap behind the largest tent in the encampment. Open the sack behind the large tent and loot the Flea-ridden blanket.

To obtain a chamomile decoction you can purchase one or else craft one.

Once you have everything you need, head back to the bathhouse. Upstairs, to your right you’ll find Naaz’s tub. When no one is looking, sprinkle the fleas both in the basin behind the tub and the chest next to it.

The wine is in the pantry also on the same floor, to the left of the stairs enter an easy locked room then go to the door to your right where you should find the casks. Interact to pour the chamomile in.

To steal the oil, you’ll need to head to Adam’s chambers in the attic. In the same room behind the easy locked door, head up one more level. Go through the door at the top of the stairs and then to your right. Inside a very easy locked cabinet again to your right you’ll find the Foreign fragrant oil, steal it.

Return to Betty and give her the good news. She has an idea for another councillor you could get on her side – Tuchmacher. The tailor had a row with Betty some years ago and may hold a grudge, but if you can help him with his problems, maybe they can reconcile.

If you delay dealing with Naz, he will ride out of town and you can't ruin his experience with the bathhouse.

Tuchmacher’s shop is just west of the Town Hall near the grocers across from the butcher’s. When speaking to him, avoid mentioning Betty at first. He had a quarrel with Sir Jan of Lesztin and needs someone to stand for him in a duel.

To the rules of the duel, Lesztin will be fully armed and armoured while you will only be allowed padded and mail armour (no plate) and a commoner’s weapon – either a mace or hunting sword. The duel will happen in the morning, so if you are later in the day you’ll have to wait though you can wait alongside Tuchmacher. When you’re ready, agree to head out.

You can pass a very hard speech check to have Lesztin remove his plate. Otherwise, Lesztin is better armoured than you but he is not a skilled swordsman. Play defensively to avoid getting hit and aim for his head, he should go down in a few hits depending on your skill with the weapon you chose. Since you cannot be armoured, consider buffing with potions.

Once the duel is over, talk to Tuchmacher to confirm the results and then return to Betty once more. Now all that’s left is to wait for the vote and hope for the best. It will take three in-game days, so feel free to run off and do other things until the objective updates.

When the council has convened, head back to Betty to hear the verdict and end the quest.

## In Vino Veritas

In Vino Veritas is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Talk to Casper Rudolf just north of the Fountain on Vintners' Street to receive the quest.

## Description

Kuttenburg burgher Casper Rudolf decided on a risky undertaking. Hoping to capitalise on the wine-growing revival under Charles IV, he bought some land on the hillside below St Barbara's Cathedral and planted a vineyard there. It soon became clear, though, that his wine couldn't compete with the wine made by the Sedletz Monastery. Casper suspects that the monks' wine-making process has some secret, and my task is to find out what it is.

## Walkthrough

Casper can be found hawking his wine outside of the Trader's shop just north of the Fountain on Vintners' Street in Kuttenberg.

### Study Casper's book on wine

Casper lent the book to his "friend" Adleta Mannlicher. Head to the marker in southeast Kuttenburg where you'll find a garden open during the day. You can either wait and try and catch Adleta on her way to the garden, or if she is already there, her brother Hugo Mannlicher will be standing guard. He can be convinced to let you in with a very hard charisma check or a medium craftmanship check. Alternatively, you can duel him and if you win he will leave. There are a few ways to get Adleta to give you the book. You can pass a very hard speech check, or a medium scholarship check. Alternatively, you can suggest becoming "friends" as well. You can pass a hard speech check to recite her a poem, while the other two options will lead to you bringing her flowers as a gift. It seems that dried herbs will not work, but there is plenty of fresh marigold that can be picked. Once you've succeeded, she will give you the book. You can ask for a kiss as well, but she will refuse regardless of the dialogue choices.

### Make an impression on Havel the tavern keeper

Regardless of whether you chose to retrieve Casper's book, head to The Emperor Charles tavern and speak to Innkeeper Havel. You will need to make a good impression to get the secret out of him, so wear your best charisma gear. He will ask you where you are from, and you can pick any of the options. He will then suggest you taste some wine together. There will be four tastings, with the first three being medium drinking checks and the final one being a hard drinking check. If you fail the check, you will lose reputation, but if you skip the check you will not. Passing the check gains reputation. If you succeeded in making an impression, there will also be a final, fifth, tasting with a medium drinking check. You can skip all the drinking checks as long as you answer the questions correctly that he asks in between tastings. The answers that gain reputation are:

- That's not a suitable gift.

- Steinberger/Vin Santo/Avignon (Germany/Italy/France)

- It's missing ginger.

- They chose the food well!

### Search Havel's office

If you failed to make an impression, the quest will update telling you to search Havel's office for his ledger. The ledger can be found on the third floor, in the room left of the top of the staircase in a hard locked metal chest. The key can also be found on Havel.

### Tell Casper about the results of your investigation

Regardless of whether you learned the secret from the ledger or Havel himself, return to Casper. He will give you 55 , and you can pass an easy speech check to request more money at the end of the quest. Regardless, he will tell you that you will need to go and find out the secret yourself. You can optionally return Adleta's book to him if you acquired it at the start of the quest. If you didn't retrieve it already or tell him you no longer need it, he will ask that you still retrieve it so that he can sell it to pay off some debts. You can either accept or refuse, saying you've done enough for him already. It does not seem to matter whether the book is returned.

### Get hired at the vineyard

The vineyard can be found north of Kuttenburg. You can talk to the recruiter there who will hire you without any requirements, starting the task Under the Straw Hat. This task is only available during this side quest.

### Find the monastery's secret

Whether you got hired or snuck in, the monastery's secret can be found in the central building. The secret you are looking for is behind a medium locked door in the cellar off the kitchen in the central building. The cellar will be considered trespassing regardless of whether you got a job, and the central building will be a private area at night time as well. The sulphur wicks can be found in the chest at the back of the locked cellar room. Additionally if you would like to complete the optional objective of retrieving seedlings for Casper, they can be found in the back yard behind a very hard locked door off the courtyard or on the other side of the kitchen. The garden will also be considered trespassing.

### Take the monastery's secret to Casper

Once you have the sulphur wicks and optionally the seedlings, return to Casper. He will reward you with 225 if you passed the earlier skill check, and an extra 55 if you acquired the seedlings as well, completing the quest. Completing the quest will also end the Under the Straw Hat task.

## In the Service of the Guild

In the Service of the Guild is a repeatable task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It becomes accessible once Henry is fully integrated into the blacksmiths' guild. Investigations will appear as part of the daily guild task rotation, sending you to deal with various matters on behalf of the other guild members.

## Repeatable Task

### Description

Guildmaster Klaus Eichner chose me as a partner to investigate the theft of our guild's goods and deal with matters no one else should know about.

### Walkthrough

The repeatable task will have Klaus Eichner send you to one of thirteen bandit camps to retrieve one of twelve sets of items stolen from the guild; the locations and items are randomly selected from the available options with each instance of the task. For items that aren't quest-specific (e.g., seals and documents), you can obtain copies of the target items by other means and turn them in as well, but it's likely simpler (and more lucrative) to loot the items from the relevant chest in the bandit camp as directed. If a usable crafting sketch is one of the target items, reading it will cause it to disappear from your inventory and make it impossible to return that copy to Klaus; however, if you'd like to learn the recipe while still readily completing the task, you can give him the unread sketch to complete the task, then pickpocket it from him afterward.

In each instance of the task, find the bandit camp within the marked search area (you'll know you're in the right area when you remark on the smoke of a nearby campfire), loot the target items from the correct locked chest in the camp, and return them to Klaus for a reward of groschen and blacksmith prestige.

Possible locations:

- Derelict farmhouse northwest of Pschitoky

- Sparse forest west of Old Kutna

- Forest spur north of Bylany

- Forest spur north-northwest of Grund

- Forest east of Danemark Mill

- Forest west of Danemark Mill

- Forest south-southeast of Burnt Mezholes

- Forest south-southwest of Burnt Mezholes

- Forest east-northeast of Maleshov

- Forest northeast of Wysoka

- Forest northeast of Raborsch

- Rabstein ruin northwest of Old Lhota

- Opatowitz

Possible items and related quest journal entries:

- Milanese cuirass, Milanese gauntlets, and Milanese plate leg armour

Two days ago, a wagon carrying expensive armour for a noble customer was ambushed. Guildmaster Eichner doesn't consider this a routine robbery, but so far, he does not know if the trail leads anywhere further. He has already obtained reports on where the stolen goods might be. I promised him I would look into the stolen shipment. It's Milanese armour - a cuirass, plate legs and iron gauntlets.

- Noble's bascinet, Noble cuirass, and Noble's plate legs

Two days ago, an armourer’s order for a wealthy noble went missing. The lad transporting it disappeared, and the noble has already made it known that he received nothing. Guildmaster Eichner found out where the apprentice was last seen and suspects that local bandits might be behind it. He asked me if I could look around the area and try to recover the lost armour. It’s nobleman’s armour – a helmet, cuirass and plate legs.

- Battle longsword, Broad longsword, Duelling longsword, and Knight's longsword

Yesterday, some unknown bastards managed to stop and rob a wagon carrying an order of first-class blades for an important lord. Fortunately, he does not know yet; Guildmaster Eichner learned of the ambush from the driver, who made it out unharmed. Klaus Eichner also obtained other leads pointing to where the robbers might be hiding. The missing items are four different longswords of excellent quality - a battle longsword, duelling longsword, knight's longsword, broad longsword.

- Bitumen of Judea, cinnabar amalgamate, gum arabic, and mastic

Once again, someone robbed a merchant's wagon carrying expensive alchemical ingredients meant for welding, alloying steel, and decorating weapons. Not only is this an irreplaceable loss, but it's also delaying important orders. Fortunately, Eichner already has a small lead on where the trail leads. He asked me to investigate it, and if possible, recover the ingredients. The items are: gum arabic, bitumen of judea, mastic, and cinnabar amalgamate.

- Toledo steel x10

A guild wagon carrying the finest Kuttenberg steel was ambushed on the road. The Guildmaster does not yet know who might be behind it but has found out where the stolen goods might be located. He asked me to investigate the matter and, if possible, recover the goods, ten bars of Toledo steel.

- Heirloom sword, golden cross ring, scapular with aperture, silver ring, and women's brooche

On the road to Kuttenberg, some bastards robbed the family of a respected master blacksmith. For Guildmaster Eichner, it's a matter of honour to protect our guild's members, and he asked me to help him with that. He already has some suspicion about where the stolen family valuables might be if the bastards haven't already sold them off. The items are: a family heirloom sword, a lady's brooch, a silver ring with a gem, a gold ring with a cross, and a scapular with a little window.

- Blacksmith's apprentice certificate, Sketch - Basilard, Sketch - Lingua belli longsword, and Sketch - Shell hunting sword

Not far from town, there was a robbery that Guildmaster Eichner takes very seriously. Some bastards laid in wait for a freshly apprenticed blacksmith's journeyman. The poor lad fortunately survived, though quite beaten, but he lost his apprenticeship certificate and sketches, which every master blacksmith guards with his life. Klaus Eicher wants to uphold his promise to protect guild members and asked me to help. He found out where the bastards are camped, and I agreed to try to recover the stolen documents. These are: the apprenticeship certificate and three blacksmith recipes.

- Orphan's inheritance, Sketch - St. George's sword, and lavish rosary

Near Beneschau, some gang raided a forge and is now supposedly roaming near Kuttenberg. The heirs are orphans, and though it was not one of our guild members, Guildmaster Eichner would like to uphold the guild's reputation for restoring order. If those cutthroats have settled somewhere nearby, it is only a matter of time before they cause more trouble. I promised Eichner I would look for the orphans' property. It concerns the orphans' goods, a rare blacksmithing recipe and an ornate rosary.

- Master blacksmith's seal ring, silver cup, silver brooch enamelled, and silver cross with insignia

On the road to Kolin, bandits ambushed one of our members and took his signet ring and some family silver. The master fortunately got away alive. Guildmaster Eichner of course does not want to let this slide, lest anyone think we cannot protect our own. He asked me if I could look into it. He has obtained an unconfirmed report of roughly where they might be camped. I should recover the stolen master’s signet ring, a silver cross with insignia, a silver enamel brooch, and a silver goblet.

- Blacksmith's guild seal and tongs

Messengers carrying new sealing marks for sacks of goods to the forge were ambushed. The Guildmaster has already learned it was likely a coincidence, but he knows where to look for the bastards who did it. He asked me if I could recover the two stolen marks.

- Guild seal letters x3

Yesterday our mounted messenger was ambushed and had important letters stolen. Guildmaster Eicher found out some details and thinks he knows where the bastards might be. He asked me to handle the rest and track down the stolen letters. All three letters bear the guild seal.

- Stolen guild die x2

Yesterday on the road to town, an experienced carter went missing. Besides other goods, he also had old guild dies from a closed forge. If they fell into clever hands, they could be used for great harm. Guildmaster Eichner has already learned more about the ambush and has a lead. He asked me to handle the rest and recover the stolen guild dies.

### Objectives

## In the Service of the Guild - Warlock's Riddle

### Description

Guildmaster Klaus Eichner has chosen me as a companion in the search for the stolen guild goods and the handling of troubles no one else should know about.

### Walkthrough

Location of the stash the riddle points to, as seen from the central road of the map, from Kuttenberg, riding east on horseback.

Bushek needs your help with a sensitive matter. A job he was supposed to finish was interrupted due to accusations of sorcery concerning the man who ordered it. He wants you to finish the delivery.

Go to the inn west of Kuttenberg and go upstairs. The room you want to search is the third from the door, just before the end of the hall. You'll remark the door is jammed. Kick open the door to see the remnants of some strange ritual.

On the bookshelf to your left, you'll find a book and a strange riddle. The riddle reads:

Were I Peter, I'd behold the holy towers, at least as many as the Master of the Art hath planets. Then I'd fall to the west, end my flight there, to the place of petitioners, where my Saviour guards His treasure.

You're looking for an unmarked wayfarer shrine on the road to Kuttenberg. It will be nearby east of the inn, hidden a bit off the road on a small hill. Look behind the shrine to find a cache; loot the cache and return to Bushek.

When handing the quest item over to Bushek, select "I don't want anything" during the dialogue to get the Sketch for armourer V.

### Objectives

## In the Service of the Guild - Betrayed Bandits

### Description

Guildmaster Klaus Eichner has another case, though it's quite peculiar. Klaus had tried this time to protect the transported goods by sending two different wagons, and while one carried steel plates, the other held just rocks in the chest. Despite this careful preparation, someone still ambushed and looted the right wagon. The guildmaster can't explain it, as he'd spoken to no one about the plan. He asked me to take up the investigation and try to find out more about how it happened, and meanwhile retrieve the stolen plated steel.

### Walkthrough

The closest fast travel point is Old Lhota. The camp is west-northwest from there near the stream closer to the west edge of the search radius. When you get there, however, all the bandits will be dead, and the goods are nowhere to be found. Keep heading west along the stream, and you should hear a dying bandit calling out.

Talk to him and try to heal him. To do so, you'll need to tie the wound off. If you can tend to him, he'll tell you his band was betrayed and he has a map and ring on his belt. He'll ask you to bring the ring to Anna, the alemaid at the All Saints Tavern. If you are unable to tend to him, he'll die without telling you anything, and the quest will update to indicate you'll have to find a new lead; simply loot him to find the map.

The map leads to the nearby Rabstein ruin to the east. If you want to hand the ring to Anna (shown as "Innkeeper Anne" in game), do so before heading to the ruin. You can ask her about the Solomon that Ondra mentioned, and though she doesn't know the name, she'll mention Ondra worked for a man called Eichner.

At Rabstein, the cache is inside the ruin itself, which is guarded even well into the night. Once inside, go up the ladder to find a very hard locked chest to your left with the goods inside. If you arrive at night, the alchemist will be sleeping next to it, and you can pickpocket him for the keys if need be. Return to Eichner with the goods.

### Objectives

## In the Service of the Guild - Silent Partner

### Description

Guildmaster Klaus Eichner chose me as a partner to investigate the theft of our guild's goods and deal with matters no one else should know about.

### Walkthrough

Talk to Eichner, who will reveal he's learned that Solomon is none other than his brother, Olbert. Offer to go with him, and you'll fast travel there immediately. It's best to let Klaus handle most of the talking at first.

The goods, it turns out, have been for Sigismund's allies, and Olbert sees that as a betrayal of the King Wenceslas. Pass an easy prestige check to insist that Klaus stay on as guildmaster. After this opening, pass a very hard charisma, coercion, or speech check or a hard intimidation check to confirm why he should agree.

He'll then send you to check some evidence hidden in an abandoned adit southwest of the Kurzhim gate. Head to the building in the search area and you'll see a horse, indicating Olbert's men are there as well.

Note: To unlock the achievement Silent Partner, you must finish the rest of this quest without killing anyone. Also, a letter looted from one of the enemies in this section reveals they are in the employ of the brother of Vavak the Mint Master.

Head inside, where two enemies are in the first area, one of whom is patrolling. Knock them out and head left to go deeper in. Go left and down the ladders until you reach the shaft, where you'll find a couple more guards. Go left and then left again, which will take you to a room with boxes. Loot the first chest for recipes, pick up Master Mathias's dagger, and grab the goods (including a copy of Sketch for armourer I) from the chest behind, then return to Eichner's shop to end the quest.

### Objectives

## Inn by the Oak

Inn by the Oak is a tavern in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is located east of Kuttenberg.

## Description

The Zur Eiche (referred to most Bohemians as Inn by the Oak, Tavern by the Oak, or simply The inn near Old Kutna) is a tavern on the road from Pschitoky to Kuttenberg. Being a short distance from the city itself but not under its direct oversight, it is perfect for people who are not exactly welcome within the city.

## Amenities

- Dice table x 2

- Lodgings

## Traders

- Innkeeper Helga Schelm

## Residents

- Arne the German (dependent)

- Dice player Halama

- Halama's wife

- Jan of Suchotlesky

- Menhard von Frankfurt (dependent)

## Associated Quests

- The German's Treasure

- Ransom

- Post Scriptum

- Ars Dimicatoria (dependent)

## Note

Given that it's nowhere near the road to Old Kutna as some characters will claim, it's possible that two inns merged during development, or the location of this inn has been changed. Whatever the reason, this must be the only inn with consistently inconsistent naming.

- Zur Eiche - given its owner is german, highly logical. Menhard and Rat use this name.

- Inn/Tavern (by) The Oak - used by Menhard, Laszlo, and Henry during conversations with them.

- Old Kutna Wagoners' Inn - name used in the game files and quest logs during The German's Treasure.

## Innkeeper Betty

You want some advice? Here's some for free. I catch you fighting here again and I'll spank your bare arse like a brat!

Innkeeper Betty (Czech: Hospodská Běta) runs the only tavern in Troskowitz with some help from the cook Filip. She's known as the local gossip and gladly will share what she knows with any willing soul.

Surprisingly she's a skilled dice player to boot. Some say she waters down her beer, but no one's brave enough to tell her that to her face.

## Biography

### Associated quests

- Laboratores

- Invaders

- The Hermit

- Opus Magnum

## Dialogue

Any news here?

(Lackey quest tip.)

Innkeeper Betty: If it's work you're looking for, you could stop by our local huntsman. He has a cottage near the Vidlak Pond. His wife is always complaining that Lord von Bergow runs him off his feet, so I reckon he wouldn't turn down a helping hand. If you ask me, though, he spends more time drinking than he does hunting. But I wouldn't want to argue with Zlata about it.

(Wild woman's hut location tip.)

Innkeeper Betty: Have you heard about the divozhenka of Semine?

A divozhenka?

Henry: What divozhenka?

Innkeeper Betty: You haven't seen one yet? A divozhenka is a wild woman of the forest, an ugly, disfigured creature. You can find them deep in the woods or caves, where they make their ointments and gather magic herbs. Sometimes they hurt people, sometimes they help them.

I haven't.

Henry: No, I haven't heard that.

Innkeeper Betty: In the rocks below Semine lived a divozhenka. It's been a few years since she appeared here, but until now, people have been getting along with her. The locals would sometimes even go to her for various magical salves and decoctions. But now they say she put a spell on one man and seduced him. A married man! And it happened now of all times! When the young Semine is going to get married!

Where did she live?

Henry: Where did the divozhenka live?

Innkeeper Betty: Between the Rocktower and Lower Semine Ponds. It's said she's got a little shack in the rocks there.

(If Wild woman's hut is yet undiscovered.)

Innkeeper Betty: You shouldn't go there.

Henry: Why not?

Innkeeper Betty: It's the Semine people. They were worried she might put young Lord Semine under her spell. Especially now… because of the wedding. So they took care of her.

(If Wild woman's hut is already discovered.)

Henry: I know where it is. I've been there. I found a poor dead woman there.

Innkeeper Betty: That's her!

She must have fooled me.

Henry: She must've fooled me. At first glance, she looked just like an ordinary woman. How did she die?

She was an ordinary woman.

Henry: Horseshit. There wasn't anything witchy about her. Who did that to her anyway? What happened to her?

Innkeeper Betty: It's the Semine people. They were worried she might put young Lord Semine under her spell. Especially now… because of the wedding. So they took care of her.

## Dialogue

When asked whats new around here?

Well ... Zdimir, our blacksmith, had one too many a while back and told me some curious things.His wife was having an affair with Thomlin Bruthans from Horschan. But then she sent her Zaimir to rough Thomlin up.I've no idea how things are between them. Strange thing is, Zdimir's a big fellah, but Thomlin still beat the shit out of him.Don't mention it to Zdimir, though, he was all upset about it. But you could ask Kona, his wife. You might find out what's really going on there. And I also know Zdimir the blacksmith finally got himself a new apprentice. Heh! He was cursing for ages that he couldn't find anyone who could hold a hammer properly.Maybe he'll be satisfied now.I also heard there are some disputes among the miners ... ... I don't know what it's about, but I heard it has something to do with their traditional
archery contest.If you're interested, go and see the foreman Vlach in the Black Horse tavern.And that's about it.

## Innkeeper Lawrence

Innkeeper Lawrence (Czech: Hospodský Vavřinec) runs the Wagoners' Inn outside of Zhelejov with his wife, Marie. Along with food and drink, he also puts on regular brawling tournaments to keep the locals entertained.

## Background

The idea for now well-known in local circles fist fighting tournament actually came about more by accident than design. One day, Lawrence and Miller Kreyzl were arguing over who had the tougher hired hands. A few locals joined in, and before long, it turned into a regular tradition. Now Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn is the unofficial fighting ring of the region.

### Associated quests

- Divine Messenger

- Frogs

- Troubadours

- Sheep among Wolves

- Wine, Women and Blood

## Dialogue

(Bird of Prey quest tip)

Henry: "Excuse me, I'm looking for a friend of mine. He's not from round here, but…"

Lawrence: "Let me guess: a dirty ruffian who ain't got a groschen to his name but acts like he owns the bloody place?"

Henry: "He was here then?"

Lawrence: "Aye, he was. He was larging it up good and proper, but then he found some lads who paid his bill… unfortunately."

Henry: "What do you mean by that? Why unfortunately?"

Lawrence: "Because they're right ruffians who are always up to no good… But still, birds of a feather, eh? In the end they left like best pals, but I got no idea where they went."

━━━━━━━━━

(Lackey quest tip)

Henry: "What's going on around here, innkeeper?"

Lawrence: "Hmm. Vostatek, Lord von Bergow's gamekeeper, is a regular here. He might have some work for you. He's got a cottage near Vidlak Pond, so if you know your way around the woods, you could go and offer him your help. I hope he hasn't started drinking somewhere else, he's my best customer!"

━━━━━━━━━

(Water goblin's hut location tip)

Lawrence: "You're not going to believe this, but two local lads claim they found a water goblin's treasure."

Henry: "You have a water goblin here?"

Lawrence: "It would be a wonder if we didn't, with all the ponds around. He's got a hut nearby. If you follow the right bank of the Rocktower Pond, you'll find it hidden in the reeds."

(Location discovered.)

Henry: "I've already seen it, I just had no idea a water goblin lived there."

Lawrence: "Joke all you want, but sometimes you can hear him cackling there, the slimy devil."

Henry: "And what did they find there? Are you sure they didn't make it up?"

Lawrence: "I thought so too, at first. They're foolish lads, so I wouldn't be surprised. But then they ordered wine, and paid with silver! Their purse was jingling with groschen!"

Henry: "Would you happen to know where I could find these lads?"

Lawrence: "They often swim at the other side of the Rocktower Pond. There's a pier there by the dam, that's their spot."

(Location discovered.)

Henry: "I am afraid I've got bad news. I found the lads, but they were dead. They drowned."

Lawrence: "Christ almighty! I told them they should've returned the treasure! Those poor lads… Such foolishness. Thanks anyway. I'll let the Troskowitz gravedigger know, he'll bury them."

━━━━━━━━━

(Wolf pack location tip)

Lawrence: "Recently, a bunch of charcoal-burners who have their kilns on the hill above the Kerchak Pond came here to have a beer. I started talking to them and they told me they almost didn't make it."

Henry: "Why?"

Lawrence: "They said a pack of wolves came after them."

Henry: "Aren't wolves afraid of people?"

Lawrence: "That's what I thought too. It's strange."

Henry: "Did they tell you where it happened?"

Lawrence: "In a gorge above the Rocktower Pond. They noticed the wolves watching them from the rocks. If you climb up those rocks, you'll be able to see the whole pond from there."

Henry: "Did they tell you how large the pack was?"

Lawrence: "They mentioned three wolves, but God knows if that's all of them."

━━━━━━━━━

(Frogs quest tip)

Lawrence: "By the way, old Olbram from Zhelejov keeps complaining about the Tachovites. If you go and see him, I'm sure he'll tell you more about it. But… well… He takes a bit of getting used to though."

Henry: "Oh? What do you mean?"

Lawrence: "You'll see… I mean… hear."

## Innkeeper Prochek

Prochek runs the tavern in Tachov alongside his wife, Voyka, in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Prochek and his wife appear to have lived in Tachov their entire lives. Prochek also appeared to act as the village's speaker regarding a pasture dispute with a neighbouring village, Zhelejov, as everyone had forgotten how it was divided between the two communities, with each village thinking it was rightfully all theirs. This had led to both Prochek and Zhelejov's representative, Old Olbram, to constantly pull pranks on each other.

Meanwhile, Prochek and his wife both disapproved of another villager, Henik. Their dislike grew when their daughter, Manka, started dating Henik, as Prochek and Voyka believed Henik would follow in his brothers' footsteps and leave the area (taking Manka with him if they got married). This disapproval was so great that Prochek was fine with giving information needed to others to provoke Henik into a fight so he could be beaten up.

### Associated quests

- Mice

- Battle of the Frogs and Mice

- Wedding Crashers

## Biography

Voyka and her husband appear to have lived in Tachov their entire lives. As such, she and her husband were biased against another villager, Henik, as his parents weren't from the area and had since died while his brothers left and never returned. This in turn caused them to greatly disapprove of him when the couple's daughter, Manka, started dating Henik.

Voyka seemed to firmly believe they got Manka to stop seeing Henik, though in reality the two were still secretly seeing each other.

## Innovator

Innovator is an achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You've acquired all the new weapons and armour from your journeymen.

## Acquisition

For the Innovator achievement you need to find eight sketches in total, have the workers at your forge create them and finally purchase these items from them.

### Building and Recruiting

- In order to be able to actually create the items from the sketches, you need to unlock two workshops and recruit two journeymen to work them. The two workshops are the Armourer's shelter and the Foundryman's shelter.

- These are naturally done while progressing towards the Home Sweet Home! achievement but you should prioritize these as soon as you have some sketches, to save you some time.

- The two journeymen you need are Standa the Fly (armoursmith) and Apprentice Pushko (weaponsmith). Both are recruited as part of the expansion's storyline, in the quests Martin's Dream and Old Plans respectively.

### Finding the Sketches

In total, you need to collect eight sketches: Armourer I–V and Caster I–III. These can appear randomly during the Sinners of Kuttenberg or In the Service of the Guild activities, and you may find duplicates of the same sketch. However, there are also some guaranteed methods to obtain each one:

- Armourer I is found in the chests at the objective location during In the Service of the Guild – Silent Partner quest.

- Armourer II OR Armourer III are given as a reward for the first In the Service of the Guild quest; Rewarded for completing the Sinners of Kuttenberg – Ragman's Dream quest (depending on which of the sketches you got previously).

- Armourer IV is found in the camp chest after completing the last quest in the Kuttenberg Sharpshooters questline.

- Armourer V is rewarded for picking the dialogue option "I don't want anything" at the end of the quest In the Service of the Guild – Warlock's Riddle.

- Caster I is rewarded for completing the quest Sinners of Kuttenberg, Ragman's Dream.

- Caster II is found in the small chest at the objective location during In the Service of the Guild – Silent Partner quest.

- Caster III is purchased from Carpenter Raven after completing the Kuttenberg Sharpshooters questline.

### Crafting the Items

Once you have all the required sketches, give them to your journeymen and wait one in-game day for the items to be crafted. Remember that you need to purchase each item, so depending on your haggling skills, you may need an additional 13,000–15,000 for all items.

In total, you should have eight items:

## Interesting site

KCD iconKCD2 icon

Interesting sites (also called Points of Interest) are minor locations found throughout Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. These spots are scattered across the landscape and can be discovered while exploring the world. They rarely tie directly into the main story or major quests, but they encourage exploration, offer loot, small environmental stories or easter eggs.

When discovered, an Interesting site is marked on the map. In Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, the perk Explorer marks all points of interest on the map regardless of if they have been visited or not.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance

There are over two hundred locations marked as "Interesting site" in the first game. None of these spots have unique names or individual descriptions.

## Into the Underworld

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Into the Underworld is the 16th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

It was obvious it wouldn’t be easy to find Sir Hans. There was someone here who could help me, though; John of Liechtenstein, who’s spying for Jobst in Kuttenberg. But there was no sign of him, and unfortunately I knew why. If anyone could have told me what happened to sir Hans, it was Liechtenstein. But how can I find him? Kuttenberg isn’t only big, it’s pretty dangerous by all accounts.

## Synopsis

Now that the Dry Devil is freed, Henry can head to Kuttenberg and look for Katherine. Zizka mentions she was looking for work at the Hangman’s Halter, a tavern in the city. When Henry meets her there, Katherine tells him her lead – one of the other workers at the Hangman’s Halter has a sweetheart who frequents a less than reputable establishment and one of the regulars there recently started throwing around a lot of coin. The man is called Goatskin and he’s usually not one of means, to add to the suspicious influx of coin, he’s also apparently been bragging that he got all this coin spying for a rich lord.

Katherine does not want to go anywhere near the place, so she asks Henry to look there for this Goatskin. The place is aptly named The Hole in the Wall and it’s in the rougher part of town. Once there, Henry asks around after Goatskin, but no one is willing to divulge any information at first. In order for them to do so, he has to gain the confidence of a man called Chenyek.

Henry may be able to win over Chenyek through their initial conversation or he may have to do a bit of legwork to earn the man’s respect. If Chenyek wants to test Henry, he suggests Henry go find a man called Goliath and challenge him to a fight. After the fight, Chenyek is impressed by Henry’s mettle and is willing to tell him what he knows about Goatskin.

Goatskin hasn’t been seen around the tavern in a few days, though he used to be a regular. It turns out, before he stopped coming some men showed up and beat him. Chenyek doesn’t know who they were but he says some of them were certainly Jews, something he finds odd, since they usually keep to their own and don’t get mixed up in things. Chenyek think it might’ve been concerning Goatskin’s big mouth, repeating the rumour Katherine heard, though no one at the tavern believed it. All Chenyek can say regarding where he might be now, is that Henry should check his usual working area, between Hradek and the Horse Market, after dark. There are a couple of watering holes in the area, the bathhouse and the Black Horse tavern.

The innkeeper at the Black Horse confirms that Goatskin operates in the area, but says he stays away from the tavern, as they don’t have German customers. It seems Goatskin has a penchant for robbing German merchants, something Henry may use to his advantage to set a trap to find him. He suggests Henry check the bathhouse, not only do they get many German patrons, but apparently one of the women who works there has been seeing Goatskin.

Goatskin’s girl is called Lousy Mary, and she’s not well-liked by her coworkers. Henry may be able to convince her to tell him where Goatskin is holed up. Otherwise, he’ll have to lure Goatskin out using one of the bathhouse’s German guests, Udo. Either way, Henry finds Goatskin and interrogates him. Goatskin says he never told anyone anything and he’s willing to swear to a man called Samuel on it. Henry doesn’t know who that is, but Goatskin assumes he must have been sent by him; he’s reluctant to talk as he promised Samuel that he wouldn’t talk about anything any more. Henry convinces Goatskin to talk, and hears that he was, in fact, spying for a couple of weeks, that Samuel is the man who hired him, and that the name Liechtenstein did come up a few times, though Goatskin isn’t sure if it was in a good or bad way. Samuel, he says, can be found in the Jewish Quarter, either outside the synagogue or the King Solomon tavern.

Henry heads over there and speaks to Samuel, telling him directly he’s looking for Liechtenstein. He’s reluctant to answer, but he may be willing to tell Henry what he knows as long as Henry helps him out with a problem none of his people can deal with. Samuel tells Henry that there’s a group of antisemites he’s gotten wind of conspiring in the city. He needs Henry to infiltrate their meeting and report back with whether or not they are making any concrete plans to try something.

When Henry arrives at the meeting spot, however, he is met by some of Samuel’s men who try to ambush him. Win or lose, Samuel intervenes, assuming Henry is working for Sigismund. He only relents upon seeing the maker’s mark on Henry’s sword, then agrees to take him to Liechtenstein as long as Henry is blindfolded.

Samuel and his men lead Henry to see Liechtenstein in the basement of the King Solomon. Liechtenstein is happy to see Henry and wants to know what brought him here. Henry catches him up to speed, focusing on the most pertinent information – warning Liechtenstein that Sigismund knows he’s in Kuttenberg and wanting to find Hans.

Liechtenstein mentions that Sigismund recently confiscated property from some of the noblemen in Kuttenberg who were opposed to him. One such property was given to von Bergow, Maleshov Fortress. It stands to reason, that that is where Hans is being held. A fortress means no usual assault will work, so Liechtenstein suggests Henry use stealth.

The fortress’s former owner, Kunzlin Ruthard has a house in Kuttenberg. If Henry were to pay him a visit, and convince him they have shared interests, then there’s a decent chance he would help Henry find a way in.

## Walkthrough

### Talk to Katherine

Henry is tasked with finding John II of Liechtenstein, who is believed to be in or around Kuttenberg. Go meet up with Katherine at the Hangman's Halter. Her lone lead so far is a shady character named Goatskin who is a regular at a tavern called The Hole in the Wall.

This house if ill repute can be found in the southeast area of Kuttenberg, called Hoprink. Once there, speak to a man named Chenyek. You can earn his respect with a speech check, but if you fail, then you'll have to beat a lackey of his called Goliath in a fist fight first. Once you've got Chenyek's confidence, he will tell you he knows Goatskin but hasn't seen him in a few days, ever since a few Jewish thugs came and beat him up. He urges you to check the southwestern district of the city where Goatskin normally robs drunks at night.

### Find Goatskin

Visit the bathhouse just inside the southwestern gate of the city, and talk to Bathhouse Mistress Beata, who will inform you she's very familiar with Goatskin because he keeps robbing their German patrons. This will give Henry the idea to set a trap for Goatskin (you can do so by enlisting the help of Udo, the last remaining German regular of the bathhouse). If you don't want to deal with Udo, you can wait a few days and eventually the quest will update, telling you to go back and talk to Katherine again. When talking with her, Henry reveals that he knows the general area where Goatskin is, and that he's been robbing the area, but that he can't find him. She suggests asking around the bathhouse or tavern in that area, or flashing some coin at the bathhouse to make himself a target. If Henry is dressed nicely she will compliment his looks, saying that it'll do.

Asking around the bathhouse will reveal that Goatskin has a sweetheart there. Her name is Lousy Mary and she can be found around the bathhouse doing her duties or resting. Talk to her and you may be able to convince her to reveal to you where Goatskin is hiding. If successful, she will direct you to a barn nearby with a characteristic hole in its gable.

Set a Trap

Visit the city bathhouse at night, and find Udo there, who is extremely drunk. Play dice with him if you like (for 150 groschen). You can either keep playing with him until he runs out of money. Alternatively you need to pass a skill check to convince him to leave. Once he does, follow him out and eventually he'll be ambushed by Goatskin. Talk to Goatskin and pass 2 skill checks to convince him to help you. If you can't pass the second (hard) skill check, you'll need to pay him 150 groschen to talk. He'll tell Henry that he was hired by a guy named Samuel, who seems to be important over in the Jewish district, and he has heard the name Liechtenstein mentioned, but can't remember if Samuel liked or disliked him.

Find Goatskin's Hideaway

To access the barn, you have to head into the yard of the house a few doors down from it, go into their barn and across the buildings against the wall. Once you come out into another yard, climb up into that barn and find Goatskin's hideout. If he isn't there, just wait until he comes home.

Talk to Goatskin and pass 2 skill checks to convince him to help you. If you can't pass the second (hard) skill check, you'll need to pay him 150 groschen to talk. He'll tell Henry that he was hired by a guy named Samuel, who seems to be important over in the Jewish district, and he has heard the name Liechtenstein mentioned, but can't remember if Samuel liked or disliked him.

### Talk to Samuel

Now Henry needs to meet with Samuel, who will either be standing outside the Synagogue in the Jewish quarter during the day, or inside the King Solomon Tavern at night. Samuel is suspicious of Henry's motives, and you'll need to convince him to talk to you with an easy skill check, or money if that fails. He'll tell Henry that he needs him to infiltrate a group of antisemites that meet somewhere in the mining district so that Henry can warn Samuel before they perform any violent acts against the Jews. In exchange, Samuel agrees to tell you what he knows about Liechtenstein.

### Infiltrate the antisemites' meeting

Go to the meeting place and wait for the meeting to start (around 10pm) or else head there after dark. Turns out, it's a trap! Two Jewish armoured fighters will be waiting for you, and you'll have to fight them. If you lose, you'll be knocked down and Samuel himself will put a dagger to your throat, assuming you to be one of Sigismund's spies. If you win, Samuel will stop Henry from harming his men and Henry will oblige.

Henry will have Sir Radzig Kobyla's sword with him at this point, and Samuel will notice the "M" engraved on the blade and decide to trust you. He'll then throw a bag over your head to hide the way and take you to meet none other than Liechtenstein himself, who's apparently hiding amongst the Jews in Kuttenberg.

### Conclusion

Liechtenstein will recognize Henry immediately and greet you warmly, letting you know you're now in the basement of the King Solomon tavern. You'll then have a conversation with him and Samuel discussing your prior exploits in Trosky and Nebakov. Henry will have the option to admit that Godwin gave away Liechtenstein's location under torture, but this will have no consequences.

Ultimately, the group will realize that Capon is being held at Maleshov Fortress, which was recently taken from its prior owners, the Ruthards, and given to Otto von Bergow by Sigismund. Henry will be tasked with meeting Sir Kunzlin Ruthard to devise a way to break Capon out of the fortress without causing a ruckus, ending the quest.

## Invaders

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Invaders is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

After giving Betty some time to not be upset at Hans and Henry for getting into a fight (usually a few in-game days), go back to the tavern and you'll see a prompt of some Cumans at one of the tavern's tables outside.

Note that this will trigger a situation where you can either try to help Betty out or ignore it/run off. If you do the latter though, returning to the tavern later will have Betty a bit annoyed you didn't come by to help earlier, as a brawl broke out between some locals and the Cumans, but still start the quest regardless.

If you spotted the group and go talk to Betty, she'll still want to serve out food, but is afraid of them, so asks you to do so and warns to please not start anymore fights. Go talk to the group, to learn only one of them speaks your language, Vasko. He'll eventually request smoked sausage and bread, which are available in the tavern's kitchen, on the table near the fire pit and window.

Go back out and serve them the food, where you can then talk to Vasko a bit more. No matter what though, one of the locals at the next table, Vuytek, will make snide remarks at the Cumans to the point you'll eventually be met with a hard speech check. If this is done early on, you may not have a way to ease tensions, resulting in the locals wishing to fistfight the Cumans. You'll then be asked whose side you're on, but even if you try to answer neutrally/ask them to stop, this just makes the locals hostile to you, dragging you into the fight regardless. After the fight, the Cumans will leave without eating/paying.

Even if the fight was avoidable, Betty won't be too upset at you. However, this will prompt you to find where they're camping to inform them it's best they don't return to Troskowitz. Note also if the Cumans were forced to fight, the food they ordered will be left behind on the table that you can take without stealing.

You can ask around other villages for where they are, or just find them directly. At the Nomads' Camp, Aranka will inform you they're just next to their camp, down a pathway to the west.

### Cumans' camp

Head over to find and talk to Vasko, who depending if you were friendly enough with/didn't side against, will be somewhat welcome to seeing you. If you're amicable enough back, Vasko will eventually talk you into drinking. Take him up on the offer, though keep in mind there's a few drinking speech checks here that can cause a slight reputation loss if you don't have enough levels in it. You can ask him about a number of topics after the first drink, where if you then ask about love, eventually he'll mention one of his comrades, Jasak, is smitten with one of the nomads, but as they don't speak each other's language, it's been difficult to bridge that gap. You can then offer to help, leading to a small interlude where Jasak will lead you to the bathmaid in question.

### Helping Jasak

During the initial conversation, she'll question if you're drunk, but this can be passed with a relatively small skill amount in drinking. Otherwise, admitting it, or failing, will result in some reputation loss. After that, a number of timed speech checks will appear where you try to translate for Jasak. While you can pass some of the checks, some aren't as great as others (like even if you succeed in saying he'll do anything for her, she'll remark how he can't even help bring buckets of water). A simple approach to wooing her (with successful checks) would be:

- He says you're beautiful.

- He said you two should go out together.

- He'd like to get together with you. (requires around 17 skill)

After that, she'll agree to go out with him, only for her to get annoyed at seeing another nomad lurking around who won't leave her alone and he likely overheard you. Sure enough, he'll confront you immediately with yet another timed speech check. If you're successful in this, it'll avoid a fight and get him to leave.

### More drinking

Return to Vasko where, if you were successful, he'll offer to drink some more. If you agree, time will pass to nighttime. You can then prod him some more about Silver Skalitz, but he'll push that off to later. You can ask him about other topics before being sent with Jasak to fetch some special moonshine that the woodcutters make. Follow along, where you can make remarks as Jasak talks. He'll eventually start singing and you can choose to respond back to each line. If you do, you'll gain a little reputation for each unique line (if you're on top of the prompts, he'll repeat the lyrics in full twice before he collapses.)

After Jasak collapses, continue further past him to see a strange dog. Ask it for advice and choose whichever option you like. Afterwards, go slightly to the south-southwest where the new quest marker is pointing to find the moonshine's hiding spot and loot it for the odd moonshine. Head back to the cumans' camp, where you'll see Jasak has disappeared from the trail. However, back at camp you'll see he returned safe and sound. Talk to Vasko, who'll remark that seeing the talking dog was likely an important sign and message to Henry. Eventually, Henry will try to voice that he's good in other skills outside of drinking, which you can then choose from.

Note however that some can lead to uncomfortable mentions and reputation loss if you don't pass them (like mentioning horsemanship, Henry can fail this and bring up when he escaped Skalitz and accidentally insults the listening Cumans). After picking two of them (even if you failed at one), you can continue mentioning skills or say you're the best. This leads to Henry declaring he can swim before it cuts to him standing on some logs out in the middle of the water, unsure how to get back with Vasko crying out to you to not fall off and be careful. Simply move enough to fall off and it'll cut to Henry back safe and sound on dry land.

At this point, you can finally get Vasko to talk to you about what happened at Skalitz and he'll divulge what he knows: namely, they didn't touch any women in the village, and his group didn't see when Henry's parents were killed, though they did kill some that day. You can then ask more details about Vasko's past and home country. If you get to the point where he mentions other Cumans in the area, you can press him about this and he can give you locations of them on the map, but warns you they're not friendly like his group.

Eventually Troskowitz will come up, where Henry warns Vasko to not return there for his own safety. He'll then offer yet more to drink. If you agree and fail, Henry will throw up, right on Vasko's shoes. With the speech check, you can succeed or fail for a bit of reputation gain/loss, but regardless Vasko agrees they won't return to Troskowitz and offers skill training to Henry if he comes back to visit. At this point, Henry will then suddenly switch to their language for a bit before time skips forward to morning and a very drunk Henry.

### Return to Vuytek

Head back to Vuytek where you can tell him how you dealt with the cumans, either by killing them or talked to them to not return (lying if you pick the option you didn't actually do). If you let them live and pass the speech check telling him this, he'll take your word and reward 25 Groschen.

## Iron Eagle Tavern

Iron Eagle Tavern is a tavern in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is located in Kuttenberg.

## Description

A German tavern, just off Kuttenberg’s pig market. Most of its common area is located upstairs, with just a few tables along the entrance and a yard outback. An adjacent yard hosts hops plants. Unlike most of the taverns in the city, it has no seating out front, most likely because of the smell of the nearby pig pens.

There are no rooms for rent in the tavern itself, though the innkeeper occasionally lets out a bed in the hayloft. The cellar is quite full with wine, fruits, and other storage. It has a through-connection to the Kuttenberg underground. The attic is only accessible by ladder, where most of the staff sleep, though the owner has his own suite behind the public area on the upper floor.

## Istvan Toth

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The stronger dog fucks the bitches.

Istvan Toth (Czech: Ištván Tóth) is a Hungarian nobleman, spy and loyal servant to King Sigismund. He plays a pivotal role in the raid on Skalitz and the death of Henry's parents.

He serves as the main antagonist of Kingdom Come: Deliverance, and a major antagonist in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

In Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2, set in 1403, Istvan Toth dies atop the Baba tower in Trosky when Henry pushes him out of a window.

## Biography

### Early life

Istvan was born in Banat on the border with Hungary; his parents were both killed by Turks, leaving him an orphan. He dedicated his life to revenge, which eventually brought him to Nicopolis where he saved King Sigismund’s life earning himself a title and service. Sometime later, when conducting raids for Sigismund, he orphaned Erik, who would grow into one of his most trustworthy men.

### Kingdom Come Deliverance

In 1403, shortly before Sigismund’s attack on Skalitz, Sir Istvan met with the local lord, Sir Radzig Kobyla, where they admired a particularly fine sword that had just been made by the local blacksmith, with the help of his son and apprentice Henry.

Sir Istvan departed the village almost immediately after, in time for the attack to begin. After the army moved on, Istvan sent Runt and his gang, to loot anything that remained in the village.

Sir Istvan visits Sir Radzig at Skalitz

There, Runt and the others came upon Henry. He had returned to Skalitz to find his parents’ bodies and to bury them. Runt beat and almost killed the young man, but was chased off by the timely arrival of the Talmberg guards, but not before having stolen the sword which he would later give to Istvan.

After the raid on Pribyslavitz, Istvan surveyed the carnage of the battle, and swore revenge. He told his attendant it was time to put the next part of their plan into action. Henry later managed to successfully infiltrate the bandit camp at Vranik, where he found Istvan meeting with Erik, the bandit commander, carrying the magnificent sword.

Istvan's lackey knocked Henry out and tied him up, allowing Istvan to finally reveal what he's been up to. Together with Sigismund, they have been working to undermine the local lords - Divish, Hanush and Radzig - and terrify the local people in order to bring the region to its knees. Once Sigismund becomes undisputed King of Bohemia, he will turn over administration of the region to Istvan.

Istvan takes Talmberg

Istvan then revealed that he knew something about Henry that everyone had kept from him – that Henry was the illegitimate son of Sir Radzig. Istvan then departed, leaving Udo to beat Henry senseless, confident that Radzig would pay a handsome fee to secure his son's safety. Unfortunately for Istvan Zbyshek, a former citizen of Skalitz and tired of the bandit life, helped Henry escape, and the young men fled to Rattay, where Radzig and Hanush decided to launch an immediate attack, together with Divish.

However, once they had stormed the camp and wiped out the bandits, they realized that neither Istvan nor Erik were there, and that they had been led into a trap - Istvan had taken the majority of his men to capture Talmberg. Istvan gained entry by telling Lady Stephanie that his men were injured, and murdering her guards when she let them in to treat their wounds.

By the next morning, Divish and the other Lords had arrived and began to attack Istvan's men, but Istvan threatened Lady Stephanie to get them to back down. Istvan captured Sir Radzig and shot Divish during the skirmish. He then retreated into the castle, ordering his men to fire burning arrows and set the outer bailey of Talmberg ablaze to drive out those trying to take it back.

The siege of Talmberg began, with Istvan resisting while the combined regional forces built siege camps. Istvan refused an initial attempt to exchange hostages after Erik was captured following an attempted rebuff to destroy the trebuchet that was being built. The trebuchet eventually dealt enough structural damage that the regional forces were able to retake much of the castle and Istvan lost his advantage. He then agreed to an exchange of hostages, Erik for Lady Stephanie, keeping Radzig as collateral to ensure his own escape. Istvan set Radzig free outside Skalitz and left the region with Erik.

### Kingdom Come Deliverance II

After the siege of Talmberg, Istvan rode to Trosky Castle with Erik where they were tasked by Otto von Bergow to infiltrate Jan Zizka's group. He was present for the ambush on Henry and Hans Capon’s company and made off with Hanush and Radzig's letter to von Bergow.

Istvan’s true allegiance was revealed to Zizka following the ambush at Nebakov Mill when Henry and Hans were imprisoned by Zizka in Nebakov Fortress. Istvan was then imprisoned with Henry, Hans, and Lord Nebak. He was freed by Erik and they fled to Trosky Castle on horseback. The next morning Istvan returned alongside Erik, von Bergow, Markvart von Aulitz, and the Prague militia. After a brief siege, the defenders were forced to retreat into the keep, which was then destroyed by the Finger of God cannon and Zizka, Henry, Hans, and Godwin were taken prisoner.

Bergow travelled to Maleshov taking Hans as a hostage, leaving Istvan in custody of Trosky with the rest of the prisoners. Under torture, they revealed that John II of Liechtenstein was in Kuttenberg. Istvan promptly dispatched Erik to deliver that information to von Bergow. The prisoners were freed and Henry sneaked up the Crone Tower, seeking out Sigismund's orders and Istvan. Istvan was alone in his room when Henry made it up the tower. Istvan was confronted by Henry and after an altercation Istvan was pushed out of the window, where he fell to his death.

## Italian Court

For the codex entry, see Codex entry: Italian Court.

Italian Court is a location in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is located in Kuttenberg.

## Description

The Italian Court was the centre of groschen minting in Bohemia. It was also used as a neutral meeting place for ecclesiastical and other such disputes, as it was also used for royal residency. The complex consisted of inner walls, with minting stations around the outside of a large inner courtyard.

The court has its own kitchens, staff, and guard. It also hosts the royal treasury, a large armoury, and the royal library and living space.

## Jack of All Trades (achievement)

This article is about the achievement. For the perk, see Jack of All Trades.

Jack of All Trades is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You have successfully completed every mini-game.

## Acquisition

The Jack of All Trades achievement is unlocked by successfully completing all seven mini-games available in the game. Most mini-games are encountered naturally during the main story or side quests. Below is a list of all seven mini-games and how to access them:

- Dice - Found at most taverns and inns throughout the game. Look for tables with dice cups to initiate a game.

- Lockpicking - Common throughout the game. Locked doors and chests appear everywhere, and you will likely have hundreds of lockpicking attempts during your playthrough.

- Pickpocketing - Introduced during the side quest Materia Prima, which is obtained from Miller Kreyzl. Completing the tutorial part counts toward the achievement.

- Alchemy - Performed at alchemist's benches. First encountered during the main quest Fortuna. You'll need basic ingredients and a recipe to brew potions.

- Blacksmithing - Available at smithies in most towns. Interact with an anvil to forge items. Blacksmithing also appears in quests such as helping Radovan access the Semine wedding. Recipes and materials can be purchased from local blacksmiths.

- Weapon sharpening - Sharpening wheels are typically found near smithies. This mini-game also features in several quests.

- Archery contests - Scattered across Bohemia. Notable contests include:

- With Vitek at Vostatek's lodge, west of Tachov.

- At the archery range below Trosky Castle.

- With Kubyenka at the Devil's Den in the Kuttenberg region.

## Tips

- You don't need to win every mini-game, you only need to complete each one successfully once for it to count toward the achievement.

- Most activities are accessible early in the game, but Popinjay archery contest requires progression into the Kuttenberg region.

## Jan Posy of Zimburg

Jan Posy of Zimburg is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

At the tavern in Bylany, Henry can come across a knight named Jan Posy of Zimburg. Sir Jan is looking to recruit someone to help him rescue his brother Miroslav from a band of Cumans who attacked them on the road. When questioned, he is a bit dodgy about the details, but divulges that he has recently become Lord of Zimburg after the death of his father, and that his company was carrying valuable cargo. If Henry agrees, this will begin the quest Bellatores.

Sir Jan - or simply "Posy" as he suggests Henry call him - is a practical man with no cares for politics or loyalty to such notions. When asked whether he supports Sigismund or Wenceslas as king, he simply scoffs at the notion that someone must choose either. Although quick to anger, Posy will listen to sound advice and restrain himself when necessary.

Eventually Posy will divulge more information about his company and their cargo. He mentions that a priest, Father Stephen of Sedletz Monastery, was among them and was carrying something quite valuable. This is later found to be a relic - The Zimburg Reliquary - which holds the remains of Posy and Miroslav's father. Their company and Father Stephen were carrying it to the monastery when they were ambushed.

Following the completion of the Bellatores quest, both brothers can be found at the ruins of Zimburg.

### Associated quests

## Jan Semine

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Jan Semine (Czech: Jan ze Semína) is an old nobleman of modest means. He's the current lord of Semine village, the owner of Semine fortress and a vassal to Otto von Bergow.

## Biography

When Henry first arrived in the region, Semine was about to become a place of a grand affair (at least by local standards). Jan's son Olda was set to marry Agnes Thrush, the daughter of Troskowitz bailiff. Semine was once a wealthy family, but their glory days were gone. Sir Jan hopesdto improve his fortune with the generous dowry that Thrush was offering for his daughter.

Despite being a noble, Sir Jan served alongside his soldiers, even as he was getting up there in age. In turn, he had a good relationship with his estate's captain, Gnarly, with the two occasionally having caused a bit of mischief at taverns, like one time in Jitschine 15 years ago.

## Jan Zizka

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

War is a nasty business. And it's better to have your head on your neck and your foe on his knees than the other way around.

Jan of Trotznov, better known as simply Zizka, is a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

Before the Hussite Wars, Zizka fought as an outlaw in a bandit group. He was wanted by Heinrich III von Rosenberg, and served as a mercenary. At the time of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, Zizka serves as the leader of his own group of outlaws.

## Biography

Zizka first met Henry and a wounded Hans in the Bohemian Paradise when Zizka's group massacred Henry and Capon's men. One of Zizka's men tried to rape Katherine but Zizka saved her and killed the man when he didn't obey his orders to stop.

He engaged in a duel with Henry after the battle of Nebakov Mill. Henry managed to injure his left eye. The eye was eventually saved by Father Godwin. Afterwards, Zizka, with the help of Henry, Hans Capon and Godwin, attempted to defend Nebakov fortress from Otto Von Bergows forces. The defense fell from the 'finger of God', and Zizka, Hans, Henry and Godwin were captured and taken to Trosky castle. From there, Zizka was severely tortured and managed to escape with the aid of Katherine.

After travelling to the Kuttenberg region in search of allies of Wenceslas, Zizka with the help of Henry gathered together Dry Devil's old band in order to continue guerrilla warfare against Sigismund's allies.

## Codex entry

One of the most famous and controversial figures in Czech history. The man who became the face of the Hussite uprising.

Unfortunately, only the last six years of his life are thoroughly documented. We know that he lost an eye in his youth and that in 1408, Zizka served in the sabotage unit of a certain Matthew the Leader and made a living as a bandit in the service of various nobles. According to some leading Czech historians, the activities of his band had more of a political than a material character.

From existing records, we know that when he was later arrested and sentenced, King Wenceslas IV granted him a pardon. There is a theory that at least part of his activities might have been carried out at the behest of someone from the king's entourage.

His most famous historical period follows the outbreak of the Hussite uprising when he took command of the rebel forces and earned a reputation as a brilliant strategist and an undefeated military leader who led the Hussites from victory to victory.

## Possessions

- Zizka is initially seen wearing a short cuirass, a tan padded gambeson, decorated brigandine chausses and pauldrons, leather gloves, and wears a German-style Bascinet with houndskull klappvisor and mail aventail.

- He carries a longsword, as well as his signature mace.

## Jan of Suchotlesky

Sir Jan of Suchotlesky is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Sir Jan of Suchotlesky was a Bohemian knight and the brother of Peter of Suchotlesky. In 1403, he sought to secure his brother's freedom from the forces of Sigismund of Luxembourg, primarily through enlisting the assistance of Henry of Skalitz.

In 1403, Sir Jan's brother, Sir Peter, was taken captive by forces under the command of Sigismund of Luxembourg. His captor, the Hungarian commander László Farkas, demanded a ransom to secure his safe release. While traveling near Danemark, Jan was attacked by Cumans and suffered several injuries. He subsequently sought refuge at the Old Kutna Wagoners' Inn, west of Kuttenberg. There, Jan encountered Henry, who tended to his injuries. Unable to negotiate personally, Jan entrusted Henry with a letter intended for László Farkas and requested that he arrange Peter's release.

Upon arriving at Sigismund's Camp, Henry could discover that Peter had already died in captivity. His remains had been placed upon a cart near the camp bathhouse, despite Farkas continual demand of payment for his release. When Henry returned with news of Peter's death, Jan was devastated and resolved to avenge his brother. He asked Henry to recruit additional fighting men before confronting Farkas at the proposed ransom exchange.

### Possible Outcomes - Ransom

If Henry supports Jan: Jan and his allies confront László Farkas and his Cuman soldiers. Following their victory, Jan rewards Henry with x125 Groschen and allows him to take Peter's Sword as a token of gratitude. He nevertheless wishes to retain the remainder of his brother's possessions.

If Henry betrays Jan: Henry may instead accept Farkas' offer and turn against Jan during the confrontation. In this outcome, Jan is killed, and Henry may claim Peter's weapons and armor without further incident.

Sir Jan of Suchotlesky's ultimate fate is therefore determined by the player's choices.

## Janek

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Are you mad? You can't go back!

—Janek to Henry of Skalitz as he attempted to save his parents

Janek is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He was formerly a guard in the castle of Sir Radzig Kobyla in Skalitz, alongside Jaroslav. Defender of Suchdol in KCD 2.

Janek is the acquaintance of Henry of Skalitz.

Janek is best and close friend Jarosław's.

## Stats

## Biography

### Kingdom Come: Deliverance

He appeared to be familiar with Henry and went drinking with him at the local tavern from time to time, but did his duty and did not allow any unauthorized people to enter the castle.

During the attack of King Sigismund of Hungary in 1403, he attempted to herd as many of the villagers into the castle as possible, and was horrified when Henry turned back to try and save his parents. He called out after him, telling him to come back, but had to turn his attention back to helping the other escaping villagers.

In that evening's tempest, Janek was able to sneak out of the castle and flee with his liege Lord Radzig Kobyla to Rattay, where he was ordered to patrol the castle of Pirkstein.

### Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Janek travelled to the Kuttenberg region with the retinue of Sir Radzig Kobyla, and was eventually stationed at Suchdol Fortress together with Jaroslav. They partook in a bet to see whose beard would grow the fastest during the period they were away from home.

Janek and Jaroslav volunteered to be members of Henry's company during the siege on Suchdol.

## Janosh Uher

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Janosh Uher is a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Janosh originated from around Trenčín (Trencsén in Hungarian) in modern-day Slovakia (then part of Kingdom of Hungary). When he found himself imprisoned and in danger of being executed, he lied about being a cook to save his life. He was then locked up in a castle in Győr, where he learned to actually cook well from a Serbian cook. After the cook had died, Janosh escaped and got to Bohemia, where he got by as a petty criminal. He eventually joined the Dry Devil's band of mercenaries known as the Devil's Pack.

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

For the Bishop, see Inquisitor Jaroslav.

Jaroslav is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He was formerly a guard in the castle of Sir Radzig Kobyla in Skalitz, alongside Janek. Defender of Suchdol in KCD 2.

Jarosław is the acquaintance of Henry of Skalitz.

Jarosław is best and close friend Janek's.

## Stats

|

|
Jaroslav

|
18

16

11

## Biography

### Kingdom Come: Deliverance

Jaroslav appeared to be familiar with Henry and went drinking with him at the local tavern from time to time, but did his duty and did not allow any unauthorized people to enter the castle. Whenever there was a disturbance in Skalitz, he and the other guards knew it to be caused by Henry, Fritz and Matthew and they would be tasked to punish them.

During the attack of King Sigismund of Hungary in 1403, he attempted to herd as many of the villagers into the castle as possible, and was horrified when Henry turned back to try and save his parents.

In that evening's tempest, Jaroslav was able to sneak out of the castle and flee with his liege Lord Radzig Kobyla to Rattay, where he was ordered to patrol the castle of Pirkstein. He was very pleased to see Henry again, and answered many of his questions regarding the attack.

### Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Jaroslav travelled to the Kuttenberg region with the retinue of Sir Radzig Kobyla, and is eventually stationed at Suchdol Fortress together with Janek. They partook in a bet to see whose beard would grow the fastest during the period they were away from home.

Jaroslav and Janek both volunteered to be members of Henry's company during the siege on Suchdol.

## Jeshek of the Order

Jeshek of the Order is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Jeshek joined the Order as Ritterbrüder Ludolf was travelling through Bohemia. Along the way, the Order stopped for shelter at Sedletz Monastery and set up camp there temporarily. While there, he sparred with another recent recruit, Slavek, and the two were mutually injured.

Jeshek claimed that Slavek had been running his gob, insulting Jeshek’s mother, and so Jeshek lost his temper a little and jabbed him – politely – in the shoulder. Slavek, on the other hand, claimed that he was pounced by Jeshek out of nowhere and was only defending himself. Since Jeshek went for his legs and ribs at full force, Slavek went high and smacked him on the head.

The two spent most of their time in the infirmary recovering from their injuries engaged in banter with each other over who was at fault for the injuries and whether it was fair.

When Henry came over to check on them, they asked for him to settle their dispute – happy to have his opinion as the tiebreaker. They wanted him to know there were not really any hard feeling between them. Despite their heated exchange, they were glad to be in the infirmary together and thus didn’t have to deal with Ludolf. They also requested that Henry tell Servant Brother Karl no harm was done and they were not seriously injured, if Henry happened to see him.

## Jewellery/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Jewellery is a type of equipment that Henry can wear in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Wearing jewellery increases charisma, which influences social interactions and can make persuasion and haggling more favorable.

There are two categories of jewellery items: Rings and Necklaces. Each category corresponds to a specific equipment slot, allowing to wear one item from each category simultaneously.

Paradoxically, brooches and spectacles are also classified under the necklace category, with Spectacles granting an additional hidden bonus to the Scholarship skill.

## Overview

Necklaces

Necklaces have high noise and conspicuousness, making Henry more easily noticed by NPCs. Necklaces are best equipped when maximizing charisma is crucial.

Rings

In comparison, rings often have zero noise stat, which makes them more viable for use during stealth while maintaining some charisma.
