## Jewish Quarter

Location on map. The only entrance is at the gate between King Solomon and the merchant.

The Jewish quarter is an area within the Kuttenberg city walls. There is a rumor going around the city that John of Liechtenstein is spinning his webs of plots from somewhere inside.

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

## Codex Entry

At the time of our game, Jews were not allowed to settle permanently in the vicinity of the silver mines, but still, there was a community in the town. It was said to be located on the site of the present-day Ursuline convent, north of the town centre.

Otherwise, the Jews tended to concentrate around the town outskirts, and the separate district as we show in the game never existed. The Kuttenberg synagogue was not built until 1881.

## Characters

The town has special names for unnamed NPCs, not found anywhere else in the game. They entirely replace the usual "Townsman," "Townswoman," "Villager," "Nobleman" etc names. The only unnamed NPCs in English (or your language setting) are the gentile city guards, which occasionally wander to and from through the guard towers.

- Baleboste - female, housewife

- Bekerin - bakeress (single occurence)

- Beker - baker, male (single occurence)

- Meydl - unmarried woman

- Naar - male youth or servant

- Shenkerke - innkeep (female) (single occurence)

- Shnorer - beggar (probably single occurence)

- Shpayzkremer - grocer (single occurence)

- Shteynshneider - stonecutter (single occurence)

- Soykher - merchant

- Tov Ho-ir - male, community guard

## Jezhek of Holohlavy

Jezhek of Holohlavy is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered.

His arms are a black raven sinistre with a ring in its mouth on a yellow field.

## Biography

Sir Jezhek of Holohlavy was a knight who lost his belongings in a duel with another knight by the name of Zavish of Garbow. The duel was instigated when Jezhek tried to stop Zavish from razing a village. He ran into Henry on the road and attempted to mug him, but was persuaded (by word or by force) to allow Henry to help him regain his honour. He asked Henry to retrieve his armour and horse and bring them to him where he was staying at the Pschitoky Wagoners' Inn.

He was grateful to Henry on the return of his belongings and associated dignity.

### Associated quests

- Lost Honour

## Jitka of Kunstadt

Jitka of Kunstadt (Czech: Jitka z Kunštátu) is a young moravians noblewoman, betrothed of Hans Capon.

## Codex entry

Future wife of our Hans Capon, the daughter of Erhart the Elder of Kunstadt and Jitka of Medritsch.

Father Godwin arranged the marriage of Hans Capon and Jitka of Kunstadt with Botschek of Kunstadt during a meeting of the lords who support Wenceslaus. He had a son named Hynce with Jitka, later nicknamed the “King of East Bohemia”, a tireless organiser of the Bohemian political scene and a predecessor of the Hussite king George of Podiebrad.

Otherwise, all we know about Jitka of Kunstadt is that in 1408, Hans Capon granted her a dowry of 60,000 Prague groschen.

## Joachim

Joachim is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered.

## Biography

Joachim first approaches Henry believing him to be someone named Hans. Joachim met Hans at one of the local taverns and was eventually convinced to lend him money so that he could purchase items in Kuttenberg, then sell them for higher prices in Germany. Although Joachim is reluctant to believe that Henry isn't Hans, he eventually accepts that the two men simply look very much alike.

He can later be met again and will explain that Hans was eventually caught using the same scheme on at least three other people, as well as being mixed up in other nefarious schemes. As a way to recoup his financial losses, he is willing to sell Henry numerous items.

## Jobst of Moravia

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

We have to put a stop to this senseless war!

—Jobst to the Lords of Skalitz-Sasau

Jobst of Moravia (Czech: Jošt Moravský) (c. 1354 – 18 January 1411), is a supporting character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He is Margrave of Moravia and cousin to both kings.

## Biography

### Events of Kingdom Come Deliverance

According to Sir Jezhek of Ronow, Jobst conspired against his family and had him declared illegitimate as punishment for his father Vincent's refusal to side with him during a war. Jobst tore down Jezhek's family castle in Ronow rather than fight with Vincent's vassals over it, leaving Jezhek impoverished and shamed. This would directly lead to him joining the bandit army and later taking control of their counterfeiting operation.

Following the siege of Talmberg, Jobst appeared along with a member of his Council, Sir John II of Liechtenstein, in Rattay on Sasau where they gave the local lords information on the circumstances of King Sigismund's conquest in Bohemia and King Wenceslas's kidnapping. He then began to plan with the lords on what the next course of action was to defeat Sigismund and free Wenceslas from captivity.

He and Sir Hanush composed a letter addressed to Otto von Bergow, one of the prominent lords in favour of Sigismund, asking whether his allegiances could be changed in reaction to Sigismund suffering setbacks in Hungary.

### Events of Kingdom Come Deliverance II

## Codex entry

1354 — 18. 1. 1411

Coat of arms Jobst of Moravia

Jobst of Moravia was Margrave of Moravia from 1375 and Elector of Brandenburg from 1388; he also held the throne of the King of the Romans, although he did so for a mere 15 weeks until his death (1410-11). He was the son of John Henry of Luxembourg and the nephew of Emperor Charles IV. He achieved his standing in Europe due to military and political intrigues, aimed primarily against members of his own dynasty, particularly Wenceslas IV, against whom he rebelled along with the Moravian forces in the so-called Margraviate Wars.

He initially supported Sigismund of Luxembourg's efforts to seize the Bohemian crown, but in 1403 he began opposing him and together with Albert IV, Duke of Austria, took part in a rebellion against him. His previous support for Sigismund was probably motivated more by self-interest — it ensured him future influence as long as it seemed that Wenceslas would be deposed and Sigismund, or even Jobst himself, would take his place. His campaign against Wenceslas won him and other nobles many privileges. Then, in 1402, when the situation changed, he rebelled against Sigismund and was even instrumental in liberating Wenceslas from captivity. We don 't know whether the change was due to cunning or conscience, but to the end of his life he remained surprisingly loyal to Wenceslas IV.

Towards the end of his life he even stood against Sigismund in the election of King of the Romans, and won. He didn't enjoy the crown for long though, and died shortly after.

Jobst was not only politically astute, but also a very thrifty governor - many rulers, including Sigismund himself, were financially indebted to him. In his day, it was said that it was Jobst, and not either Wenceslas or Sigismund, who was the true uncrowned sovereign of Bohemia. At the time our game takes place, however, he was in debt up to his ears.

## Johannes von Gelnhausen

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Johannes von Gelnhausen is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

He can be met wandering around Kuttenberg, where Henry of Skalitz can strike up a conversation with him. Johannes is currently writing a codex on the legal matters around mining. He will also offer Henry a commentary on the political situation, namely on king Charles IV's strengthening of the Church's position, its estates, and how a war larger than the current one is likely to start in the next few years.

## Codex entry

Main article: Codex entry Johannes von Gelnhausen

Johannes von Gelnhausen was a lawyer, mining scribe and archivist of the imperial chancery.

As the second-born son of a German noble family, he went to study and before 1365 he secured the post of mining scribe in Kuttenberg. In the following years, he served the most powerful men of his time and travelled throughout the empire with the imperial court of Charles IV. Later, as an expert in both types of law, he led the office of Bishop John of Neumarkt in Olomouc and subsequently was a city scribe in Brno until 1389.

It was only towards the end of his life that he created his seminal work known as the Gelnhausen Codex. An illuminated legal treatise for the mining town of Jihlava, Johannes made full use of his experience here, taking inspiration from the Mining Code of Kuttenberg, Ius regale montanorum.

## John of Liechtenstein

Sometimes all you need to do is send the right man to whisper the right words… into the right ears.

Sir John of Liechtenstein is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He is a member of the House of Liechtenstein, a powerful Austrian noble house with estates in Moravia and Austria.

The Liechtensteins have been put at odds with King Sigismund of Hungary and Croatia, and have allied with Margrave Jobst of Moravia. Sir John is a member of Jobst's Council.

John of Liechtenstein is the acquaintance of Henry of Skalitz, Hans Capon, Samuel's, Godwin's.

## Biography

### Events of Kingdom Come Deliverance

John appeared with Jobst in Rattay following the siege of Talmberg and informed the local lords of the circumstances of King Sigismund's war and King Wenceslas IV of Bohemia's kidnapping. Jobst then informed the lords of the next course of action to defeat Sigismund and free Wenceslas from captivity.

Jobst and Sir Hanush composed a letter addressed to Otto von Bergow, a prominent lord in favour of Sigismund, inquiring after his continued loyalty in the face of Sigismund's troubles in Hungary. John was sent to Kuttenberg to act as Jobst's eyes in the region.

### Events of Kingdom Come Deliverance II

It isn't known how John of Liechtenstein gained the support of the Jewish Quarter residents. By the time Henry of Skalitz got to the city, John had already obtained enough information and allies to point him in the direction of the Ruthards, knowing that Hans Capon is likely to be imprisoned at their old fortress of Maleshov. John of Liechtenstein was able to secure funding for Jobst's army from the Jews in Kuttenberg, and with the help of Godwin, he managed to gather crucial support at the meeting of King Wenceslas's supporters on Raborsch during The King's Gambit.

After the meeting was ambushed by Otto von Bergow and his men, John of Liechtenstein found out from Henry of Skalitz about a planned attack on the Jewish Quarter and insisted on coming along so he could secure his documents from falling into the wrong hands during Exodus. Apparently feeling guilt for what had befallen the people who protected him, he rode with them as protection to Kolin.

## Associated quests

Kingdom Come Deliverance

- Epilogue

Kingdom Come Deliverance II

- Into the Underworld

- Via Argentum

- The Feast

- Exodus

## Codex entry

1386 - 1412

A member of the Council of the Moravian Margrave, Jobst of Luxembourg, who, as one of only a few Moravian Lords, did not fight against the King alongside Jobst. The Liechtensteins were a wealthy family, owning estates in the Styrian and Lower Austria regions from the 13th century onwards, their main seat being Mikulov (Nikolsburg). The Liechtenstein Princes were in close alliance with the Habsburgs and Luxembourgs. In the war against Sigismund, John of Liechtenstein supported Wenceslas, helping to rescue him from captivity, but by so doing fell out of favour with the Austrian Dukes, who confiscated his estates around the Danube River and took him prisoner. After the death of Wenceslas, the Liechtensteins aligned with Sigismund.

## Johnny the Gob (bandit)

Johnny the Gob was a bandit and Gules' right hand man in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Johnny and Gules had a longstanding camaraderie, having saved each other countless times. Even rarer was the fact that Johnny never tried to betray his friend, something Gules saw too often with other bandits in their gang. Despite this, Johnny always had the feeling, likely due to Gules being of nobility, that they'd one day be on opposing sides.

One day, they got word an entourage had been attacked at Rocktower Pond. Wanting to see if anything of value had been left behind, Gules sent Johnny along with 7 of their best men to check it out. Johnny arrived in time to see some of the men that had attacked still there before they soon left. Wanting to check it out, Johnny sent a few of his men to follow to see where they went, concluding they had a camp up in the nearby cliffs.

If Johnny the Gob is completed and he was spared:

Johnny was soon after approached by Henry, who he tried to attack before listening to Henry explain he didn't wish to kill him, as Gules asked him to be spared. Realizing that Jan Semine finally caught Gules, he thanked Henry for sparing him and was thankful to his old friend for still trying to look out for him. As part of their ruse though to make sure Jan didn't find out they deceived him, Johnny agreed to disappear from the area.

## Johnny the Gob (quest)

For the bandit see Johnny the Gob (bandit).

Johnny the Gob is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

Like before, a few in-game days after completing Handsome Charlie, Gules will have information for the next target. However, this one is more sensitive in nature: he's sending you after Johnny the Gob, Gules' former right hand man and someone who's never betrayed Gules.

Gules will ask you to spare his friend if you can, though it'd go against Jan Semine's orders, and bring his shield back as proof. You can agree to try or not.

The camp itself is where Henry and the rest originally setup their ill-fated camp, though this time with 7 bandits roaming around. If you want to spare him, Johnny likely won't listen right away, so you'll need to take out most if not all his men before he concedes. Note that depending on your stats/weapon, you could end up accidentally killing him too quickly (if you were wishing to spare him) so it's best to switch to unarmed and weaken him enough to get him to finally talk.

Talking to him will also give you a little bit more information on the ones that attacked your group, marking a guard patrol on your map. You can visit this area separately, though not much is gained from it other than confirming it's the ones who attacked you.

Go back to Gules who'll be relieved you let his friend live. Like the previous tasks, you can ask to keep the shield or not. The quest will then conclude.

## Objectives

- Break up Johnny the Gob's gang.

- Bring the Gob's shield to Gules.

## Judgement Day

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Judgement Day is the 32nd and final main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically following Last Rites Pt. 2.

## Description

I'm going back to Suchdol at the head of Jobst's army, by the side of my father Radzig Kobyla and Hanush of Leipa. The time has come to break the siege, liberate my friends and deal with the treacherous Praguers once and for all!

## Walkthrough

### Liberate Suchdol

Reinforcements have arrived! Fight through the remaining Praguer forces to liberate Suchdol. Once all the enemies in the outer bailey are dealt with, you’ll have to get into the inner bailey.

An ally will flag you down, follow him around the moat and up the side. He will be killed by Lamprecht von Prag, whom you will then have to duel. He's a solid swordsman, but there is an autosave. Head into the tower behind him after he's dealt with, to your right will be the portcullis control. From there, head down to the inner bailey and finish off the final wave of enemies.

With that, Suchdol is free!

Hanush will mention a new sword he got that dulled during battle, which you can offer to sharpen for him. Take it over to the grindstone behind you and fix it up for him while he talks to Hans.

You can also catch up with your allies around the fort. Once Hanush is ready, head over to him and return the sword. After talking to Hanush, you can speak with Hans as well. Then go to find Radzig.

### If Sam died

The Praguers left Sam hanging at the bottom of the walls. You’ll have to go and take him down and prepare him for transport to his family in Kolin.

### Finish up in Suchdol

If von Aulitz was not found or else spared, you’ll also have the objective to go find him in the town.

Finally, you can go and speak to Radzig which will end the quest and the main questline! Radzig will most likely give you his sword back, making it now Henry's longsword.

Note: When speaking to Henry's parents in his dream. If you select that you want to settle down, Henry will refuse the sword and Radzig will keep it.

## Karel Arrowhead

Karel Arrowhead is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Karel was the leader of a small band of bandits in the Kuttenberg region. He did his work as a bandit with the ideal of only taking as much as was necessary and avoiding greed. His fellow bandits respected him not just as a strong man but a wise one as well. One time, during a raid, he was hit in the head by an arrow loosed by a member of his band, Pasha, which miraculously did not kill him but became lodged in his forehead, giving him his nickname.

After the incident with the arrow, his companions thought of him as a sage chosen by God and thought of the arrow as possessing magical protective properties.

He met Henry along the road by chance when Henry stopped, mistaking his sleeping form for a corpse on the side of the road. He enlisted Henry's help to carry some sacks back to his camp, chatting along the way about life.

Sometime later, Karel was killed in a botched raid and buried outside of Sedletz Monastery. He was not allowed burial within the graveyard, as the gravedigger, Lenyek took him for a sorcerer as no normal man would be able to survive with an arrow in his head.

## Katherine

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Katherine (Czech: Kateřina) is a charming, extraordinary woman, a skilled spy and a great asset in the rebellion against Sigismund.

In dialogue, Katherine is critical of Jan's friendship with the Dry Devil, as well as war and fighting in general.

Katherine is an optional love interest for Henry. She is the in-game representation of women in war, inspired by the many Katherines in the life of the historical Jan Žižka.

## Biography

### Associated quests

## Codex entry

The brave and determined helper of Jan Zizka of Trotznov is mostly just a fictional character, although women bearing this name played important roles in Zizka's life.

The first Katherine was probably his mother, although this is not certain, as other sources name her Johanna. We know more about the second Katherine. In the provincial land-registry books we learn that Jan Zizka married her and acquired a farm in Čerejov as a dowry. They even had a daughter, although her name is unknown.

After Katherine's death, Zizka married… yet another Katherine. Again, we do not know anything about her, except that Zizka inherited her property after her death.

In view of the importance of this name in the life of this great figure of Czech history, we decided to interpret the character of Katherine in our own way.

## Klara

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Klara is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Klara was a healer who worked in the service of Jan Zizka at Nebakov Fortress.

She tended to the wounded when they returned from battle and minded the fort. When Henry and Hans Capon came to the fortress at the behest of Otto von Bergow to gather his allies in the region, Klara tried to distract Henry from being able to snoop around the fortress and find out their sham.

She took Henry to the nearby woods and asked him to help her pick herbs needed for healing decoctions. She then tried to seduce him to waste more time which he may have accepted. If he was suspicious of the fortress already he may have threatened and scared her.

Later, Henry joined with Zizka and stayed at the fortress. Klara recruited him to help her tend to the most recently wounded. That night, she sought comfort with him as she was nervous about the inevitable battle that awaited them.

Following the successful attack on Nebakov by the Prague forces, Klara was hanged.

### Associated quests

- Back in the Saddle

- The Finger of God

## Klaus' Introduction

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Klaus' Introduction is the 4th quest in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Guildmaster Klaus Eichner summoned me. It seems being a guild member involves not just pleasant dice games, but other duties as well. I just hope I haven't broken some important ordinance.

## Walkthrough

Go to Klaus' shop and meet with him. He'll ask if Martin really is your father, and telling the truth here doesn't seem to have any negative consequences. Klaus will ask you to recover some documents that were stolen by bandits that have been ambushing the guild's wagons. Depending on how you say you will deal with the robbers, Klaus will give you the following supplies:

- Direct approach:

- Strong Aqua Vitalis

- Strong Dollmaker poison

- Ambush:

- Improved wounding arrow x10

- Improved wounding bolt x10

- Strong Dollmaker poison

- Poison:

- Strong Bane poison

- Long pourpoint - black

- I don't know:

- Weak Marigold decoction

- Weak Dollmaker poison

- Wounding bolt x8

- Wounding arrow x8

The robbers can be found west of Kuttenberg, nestled at the edge of the forest where the northern edge curves. The documents are in a Medium locked chest at the back of the camp behind the second campfire. Deal with the bandits how you will (or else sneak past while they sleep), gather the documents, and return to the city.

Note: In the chest with the necessary documents is Sketch for armourer III; take that as well, as it will be useful later and is needed for the Innovator achievement.

Klaus will thank you for your service, though he will remark he's a bit worried you were only able to find two documents when he expected more. After talking with Klaus, you'll become a full-fledged guild member and unlock daily Guild Activities. This will complete the quest and automatically begin the next, Martin's Dream.

## Knight shield

Knight shield is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It is held in the off-hand and classified as a kite shield.

## Description

A battle shield made of wooden planks joined glued together and covered with raw cowhide. Usually its outer side is decorated with the coat of arms of the lord or other symbol by which the warriors can recognize each other in the heat of battle.

## Knight's axe

Knight's axe is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It can be crafted.

## Description

A knight's battle axe. A dexterous weapon that can pierce good armour or crush the bones underneath with its spike. It also has a pointed tip to finish off tougher opponents.

## Crafting

## Knight's longsword

Knight's longsword is a melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

Note: Knight's longsword can be crafted.

## Description

Original long swords have a slightly wider blade and a pronounced groove for durability. They are not weapons for decoration, but noble blades to uphold knightly honour and family tradition.

## Knight's war hammer

Knight's war hammer (Czech: Kladivo rytířské) is a blunt‑type melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It can't be crafted.

## Description

The war hammer is considered by many to be as noble a weapon as the sword, since it is used where there is no room for swordplay and hard blows need to be dealt. The war hammer is therefore designed to penetrate armour and crush bones in the heat of battle.

## Kolin

Kolin is a city just north of the area of the Kuttenberg region where the second half of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II takes place. It is mentioned offhandedly by a couple of NPCs as Horschan is on the road to the city. The north gate of Kuttenberg is also called the Kolin gate due to the direction towards there.

Kolin played an important role after the Conquest of Kuttenberg, when the miners who defended the city had to march to Kolin and kneel in the mud in front of Sigismund of Luxembourg.

The majority of the population of the Jewish Quarter is assumed to have moved there after the events of Exodus. After the heist on the Italian Court during The Italian Job, the wagons of silver were supposed to be driven to Kolin.

## Characters from Kolin

- Rupert of Kolin

- Pavel of Kolin

- Benesh from Kolin

- Thomas of Kolin

## Konrad

Not to be confused with: Konrad (hermit)

Konrad (Czech: Konrád) was a soldier in the service of Hanush of Leipa.

He, alongside Oats, Tankard, Nicholas, and Henry of Skalitz, was assigned to accompany Hans Capon in delivering a message from loyalist lords to Otto von Bergow.

## Involvement

Konrad rode out of Rattay as part of Hans Capon's escort. He appears to have been an old friend of Tankard, even though the latter was always cheating him at dice. The two ended up in a brief spat with some locals at the last tavern where the group stopped, after Tankard, drunk out of his mind, tried his luck with the innkeeper's daughter.

During their stay at Rocktower Pond, Konrad helped Capon out of his armour and was the most enthusiastic about the training match between Capon and Henry.

Not much is revealed about him, aside from his fondness for women and heavy weapons, though he was among those slaughtered in the bandit ambush.

### Associated quests

- Easy Riders

## Konrad (hermit)

Not to be confused with: Konrad (retainer)

Konrad was a former Knight of the Cross with the Red Star turned fugitive in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Konrad joined the Knights of the Cross with the Red Star at least 20 years ago in Prague, and where he met a fellow knight, Ambrose. The two became good friends to the point that when Ambrose discovered their Grand Master had committed treason, he informed Konrad, who helped out his dear friend. However, despite Ambrose being second in rank just behind the Grand Master, this caused them problems and as a result Ambrose went into hiding, only telling Konrad where he was.

Konrad likewise had to escape the Order's wrath when he started looking into suspicious murders and convict releases, that accumulated into an archbishop's death. When he found out there were corrupt knights in the Order that led to this, he informed the Grand Master, Zdenyek. However, Zdenyek was in on it and so sought to have Konrad killed as well. Konrad fled, though he was forced to kill a couple of his fellow knights in his escape.

Even though Ambrose was living in seclusion in Apollonia, his friend still held the rank of seneschal, so Konrad sought him out as he was the only one that could convict the grand master. However, when Konrad arrived at his friend's hut, he found Ambrose was one foot in the grave and couldn't even comprehend Konrad was there. In his last moments though, he suddenly spoke clearly that he had two final wishes: to pass on a message to a widow in Troskowitz named Margaret, and to retrieve his old sword so he could hold it one last time. As Konrad was out retrieving the sword though, his friend passed away.

With nowhere else to go in the meantime, and wishing to at least fulfill his friend's dying wishes, Konrad took on his friend's guise of being the hermit. However, this caused locals to wrongly suspect something sinister was going on as they could have sworn the hermit's health had been frail but was suddenly back to normal again, saw weird sightings of a black horse and rider go through at night, and seen a strange figure at a cross, leaving it slanted, all of Konrad's accidental doing when he got to the area.

## Konrad of Vechta

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

This article is about the character. For the codex entry see Codex entry: Konrad of Vechta

Konrad of Vechta is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He is the royal mintmaster of the currently imprisoned king Wenceslas IV. He currently lives in Poděbrady.

## Biography

Konrad had a career as a priest before he was made Royal Mint Master. He would later be replaced by Ulrich Vavak and was bitter about having lost the post, though he did not expect he would ever get it back even if the crown were to change hands again.

He attended the meeting of powerful supporters of Wenceslas IV at Raborsch. Although he was there, he was on the fence as to where to place his allegiance, as he was worried about his future prospects.

He was taken hostage when the meeting was attacked by Otto von Bergow and held in captivity at the Italian Court in Kuttenberg. Following Zizka's successful robbery of the Court, Konrad was freed and went with the other former hostages first to Suchdol and then to to send news of the success to Jobst of Moravia.

### Associated quests

- The King's Gambit

- The Feast

- Civitas Pragensis

## Kubyenka

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Kubyenka is a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

### Early Life

Kubyenka was a petty bandit, having no real other skills or ambition. At some point he worked as a guard for an artillery. Eventually, after having become a master marksman following years of practice killing with the bow, he became a member of the Dry Devil’s band. His years of alcohol abuse had made it so he had to be perpetually drunk to avoid his hands being too shaky to shoot. He travelled with them for a long time, growing a sense of camaraderie amongst them.

Sometime later, Dry Devil was captured after a botched raid in Kuttenberg and the group was disbanded. Kubyenka found himself at the Devil's Den where he spent his days drinking and gambling while ostensibly trying to come up with a way to save Dry Devil or find a new group to join. As part of this search, he heard about locals in Miskowitz who were rallying against Sigismund’s occupying force, but ultimately did not seek them out.

### Involvement

One day at the Devil’s Den, Kubyenka was drinking and gambling as usual, but got himself into a bit of a sticky situation. The people he owed wanted to make good on his debts and were planning to take him out when Zizka and Henry appeared in the nick of time.

Kubyenka got them up to speed on the situation after being saved and gave Henry some information on where to find his former comrades since they had dispersed. He worked with Henry to gather some gonnes from the old campsite to set up a trap so they could free Dry Devil when he was being transported to Sigismund's camp for a more spectacular execution than Kuttenberg could provide. This trap was successful, though Dry Devil sustained an ally-inflicted injury, and with the leader free the group could be reassembled. His general routine did not change after that, but with Dry Devil’s group mostly back together, he was active in their plans.

When Zizka and a few of their allies went to Raborsch for a meeting of Wenceslas supporters in the region, Kubyenka was initially left behind, but went to join the party when he realised he was missing out. He was too late to join the festivities, as the gathering had been attacked by von Bergow’s men, but was able to bring Henry, Samuel, Rabbi Jehuda, and John II of Liechtenstein back to Kuttenberg in an attempt to protect the city’s Jewish population from a pogrom led by Erik. Kubyenka was somewhat reluctant to help, but did so since he was there and with the group.

Afterwards, he went back to the Devil’s Den and was involved in planning the raid on Maleshov following the appropriation of the Finger of God from the Prague militia. Due to his previous experience near artillery, Kubyenka was assigned to the cannon along with Brabant who himself claimed to have a great familiarity with the weapon.

The first shot they fired missed, the second was on-target, but the cannon itself broke and exploded causing both Kubyenka and Brabant to suffer from short-term deafness. Following the raid on Maleshov, Kubyenka moved to Ruthard Palace along with the rest of the group in preparation for the infiltration of the Italian Court to steal the royal silver.

Kubyenka’s role in the scheme was as part of the reinforcements alongside Zizka who would arrive once the people who had infiltrated the court managed to clear the way. The mission was initially quite successful until Brabant and his hired men tried to make off with the silver. In the ensuing chaos, everyone had to flee the city and Kubyenka’s horse was shot and he was left behind, believed by the others to be dead.

Rather than killed, however, Kubyenka was taken hostage and moved to Sigismund’s camp where he was freed by Erik so that he could send a message to Henry at Suchdol that Erik wanted a duel with him. Janosh was quite happy to see Kubyenka and he was able to slip back into life with the group at Suchdol.

After the remaining Praguer troops attacked Suchdol and a siege began in earnest, Kubyenka volunteered to be part of a company headed by Henry along with Samuel and a few others. As part of Henry’s company, Kubyenka participated in regular guard shifts and siege manoeuvres. During the siege, Kubyenka and Samuel became decent friends often eating or drinking together when provisions were available.

As the siege dragged on, food became much more heavily rationed before eventually running out. Kubyenka discussed options and wishes with a few of the others, admitting he noticed the wife of Suchdol’s captain wearing nice lambkin shoes. Kubyenka continued to protect the fortress with his allies until Henry was able to gather reinforcements and break the siege.

With the siege broken, Kubyenka celebrated heartily and returned to normal service in Dry Devil’s band.

## Kunzlin Ruthard

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Kunzlin Ruthard is a wealthy german nobleman and mine owner from Kuttenberg. His daughter is Rosa Ruthard.

## Biography

### Early Life

Kunzlin Ruthard rose from his original status as a wealthy burgher to that of a noble knight through the acquisition of Maleshov and a lot of negotiation with Charles IV. This elevation lead to tension between his house and the older noble houses who viewed him as not truly one of them, including Ulrich Vavak.

He had two children, a son, Ventza, and a daughter, Rosa. Their mother died sometime when Rosa was young.

During the siege of Kuttenberg, he wanted to negotiate with Sigismund and avoid things coming to armed conflict which he knew would eventually lead to an excuse for Sigismund to seize property in the city. His son, Ventza, disagreed with him and wanted to prove that the Ruthards were knights in more than just title and went off to fight against Ruthard's wishes. This culminated in a battle where it appeared to the Kuttenberger's chosen leader, a Frenchman who Ruthard said showed up out of nowhere and claimed all kinds of fanciful things, that the trebuchets were undefended and an assault was sent on them. This turned out to be a trap, and Ruthard rode out as soon as he heard to try and help his son, who had been sent on the attack. Unfortunately, when he arrived, the fighting was over and Ventza was among the dead. This battle became to Ruthard his own self-described hardest battle, despite him never having raised arms in it.

### Involvement

Kunzlin was involved in a mine dispute with the current Mint Master Ulrich Vavak, due to his loyalty to Wenceslas, while Vavak had been appointed to his current role following Sigismund's takeover of the town. Kunzlin had reason to believe that Vavak was up to no good and wanted a way to find proof of these wrong doings.

One day, Henry came to Ruthard Palace looking to have the Ruthards help him in freeing Hans Capon from their former estate, Maleshov. Kunzlin then took the opportunity to offer his help to Henry in exchange for Henry finding dirt on Vavak.

Henry was able to find ample proof that Vavak had been embezzling money from the royal mines and Kunzlin asked for Rosa to give Henry information on how to slip into Maleshov undetected.

He later went to Raborsch for a meeting of Wenceslas supporters in the region. He wanted a direct plan of attack for taking back the city and did not want to sit idly by and wait for something to happen. That evening, he was taken hostage when Otto von Bergow attacked the meeting and was held in the Italian Court.

Jan Zizka and his men freed Kunzlin along with the other lords who had been taken hostage when they came to the Italian Court to rob Sigismund of the silver being held there. Following his release, Kunzlin went to Suchdol with the other lords and Rosa and then to Podiebrad to send news of Zizka's success to Jobst of Moravia.

## Codex entry

In this case, Kunzlin Ruthard is a fictional character inspired by two different persons of the same name.

The Ruthards descended from an old branch of minor Bohemian nobility who settled in Kuttenberg and gained substantial wealth there; this led to the family’s promotion to knighthood. In 1364, Kunzlin Ruthard bought the Maleshov fortress from the Sedletz Monastery and added “of Maleshov” to his family name. He died sometime around the year 1376. His descendant Wenceslas Ruthard then sold the fortress in 1407.

Another Kunzlin Ruthard had an altar built at the so-called Ruthard Chapel in the Tall Church in Kuttenberg.

## Kuttenberg

For the codex entry, see Codex entry: Kuttenberg/KCD2.

Kuttenberg (Czech: Kutná Hora) is a city that appears in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Situated on the eastern side of the region that takes its name, Kuttenberg, is the largest and most populous accessible settlement. It houses multiple guilds and is the seat of the Royal Mint which is housed in its Italian Quarter. It also has a large mining operation spreading out father into the region as a whole.

The city is large enough to be split into multiple districts, mainly named for the occupations of the inhabitants or the goods sold there. In the north is the Czech quarter, Merchant Quarter, and the Jewish Quarter. The centre of the village is mainly markets, vendors, and the Town Hall. In the south-west is the Hradec Quarter and Horse Market. While the south-east boasts the Italian Court and Mint where all valid Groschen is minted. Outside the inner walls to the south-east is the poorer Hoprink district and gallows. To the south, along the river are workers’ houses and sawmills leading out into the rest of the region.

Below the city, is a network of tunnels referred to as the Kuttenberg underground. These tunnels not only traverse underneath the city but offer access to many different shops and buildings. They are well-used by smugglers and other unsavoury folks.

At the end of 1402, it was attacked by Sigismund and subsequently taken over by his rule. Many of the local ruling families lost access to their holdings as a result and either left the area or were forced into their town homes. A portion of the city’s outer wall was breached in the siege as well, and it is still in the midst of being reconstructed.

All in all, Kuttenberg is a veritable hub of activity and there is always something happening there.

## Kuttenberg Sharpshooters

Kuttenberg Sharpshooters is a repeatable task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A man cannot spend all his time at the forge. Sometimes he needs to get out among people and share a moment with fellow masters and journeymen.

## Repeatable Task

### Walkthrough

Talk to the person who is ready for a contest. Equip the type of bow they want to use and head out to a contest. These can be regular targets or popinjay. Win or lose, you will gain blacksmith prestige, and you have the opportunity to put up a wager as well.

### Objectives

## The Sharpshooters of Kuttenberg - Yaroslav

### Walkthrough

This task, given by Apprentice Yaroslav, will start the same as the rest, but once you arrive at the quarry, you'll find Raven missing.

Head toward the targets to find a bloodstain and Master Raven's hat. Signal Mutt to search using it, if he has the ability. Otherwise, follow some wagon tracks south a few steps and you should spot Raven's quiver. Keep following the road south and you'll find another bloodstain that veers to your right off the road. When you go right, you should be able to hear Raven wailing in pain.

It turns out he was robbed. You can offer to treat him and he'll initially refuse, but he'll accept if you offer again. The robbers went behind him to the west. Head into the woods, and you'll find a couple of bandits sitting by a tree. You can call out to them, but they will become hostile. The crossbow is in the sack against the tree.

Once you have the crossbow, return to the quarry. If you'd like to keep the crossbow, you can lie and tell Raven you didn't find it. Returning it to him will get you reputation and a discount at his shop. Then you can finally speak with the apprentice and end the quest.

### Objectives

## Kuttenberg Sharpshooters - Valihora

### Walkthrough

This task, given by Butcher Valihora, will start the same as the rest, but once you arrive at the quarry, you'll find Raven under attack by a group of bandits.

You'll have to fight the bandits off. They will initially all be shooting at you from the top of the quarry. If you aren't feeling confident with the bow, feel free to approach the quarry wall, causing them to come down the ladders to fight you in melee.

Once they're dealt with, talk to Raven. He'll mention they wanted money from him in the past. If you pass a very hard speech check, he'll admit he borrowed money from them to start a workshop, and even though he's paid it all back, they won't leave him alone. He hopes now that you've dealt with most of them, the situation will be resolved going forward.

### Objectives

## Kuttenberg Sharpshooters - Two Brothers

### Walkthrough

This task is given by Master Gottfried aus Steyr in his shop in western Kuttenberg. He'll tell you Raven has refused to go to the shooting range at the quarry since the bandit ambush, and he'll suggest you speak with him to convince him to return.

Go speak with Raven in the southern outskirts of the city. Regardless of which option you choose (one involves a very hard speech check), he'll explain he and his older brother Brada started a bandit gang to earn coin to set up a carpentry workshop, but the runaway monk Koniash joined and urged them to murder amid the chaos of the war. Raven borrowed money from his fellow bandits and left to establish the workshop, expecting Brada to join him after Raven paid back the debt through his brother, but someone betrayed the transfer location to Bailiff Andreas Plümel, and Brada was caught and hanged. Koniash then convinced the gang Raven had betrayed his brother for the coin (which Raven believes was instead confiscated by the bailiff), assumed leadership over the bandit operation, and started threatening Raven. Raven finally gives you a message from Koniash threatening to turn Raven over to the bailiff if he doesn't return the silver (spelled "silber" in the message). Further conversation will reveal both the location of Brada's capture in the forest east of Bylany (known as Wolf Rock, where you can optionally find the hidden stash of 800 Raven gave Brada in some brush at the base of a tree) and the area southeast of the Pschitoky Wagoners' Inn hosting Koniash's gang.

To unlock the hidden achievement Two Brothers, first go to the Kuttenberg town hall and speak with the bailiff. His location won't be designated by a quest marker, but he should be in his office upstairs in the back courtyard, accessible through the door to the right of the stocks. Do not choose the option "I'm here to report the bandit Raven!" Instead, ask about Brada's arrest to receive the anonymous report that had tipped off the bailiff to his location (with the report also including a reference to "silber"), then ask about the coin to confirm the bailiff did not find any in Brada's possession (by this point, you may have already found the money hidden at Wolf Rock; see above).

Proceed to the marked bandit camp southeast of the Pschitoky inn. When confronted by Koniash or one of his bandits, quickly use the on-screen prompt to "talk" to be led into a conversation with the renegade monk. To unlock the hidden achievement, choose the option "I know who turned Brada in!" followed by "Leave Raven be." This will cause Koniash to agree to leave both you and Raven in peace (to avoid your revealing the truth about his betrayal of Brada) and the bandits to peacefully return to the camp, unlocking the achievement. You may then optionally loot the Sketch for armourer IV and a few crafting materials from the medium-locked chest in the back of the camp.

Regardless of whether you resolved the situation with Koniash peacefully through either blackmail (as described above) or paying the 800 debt or through violence (either before or after unlocking the hidden achievement), return to Raven and confirm his freedom from the threat. If you choose the option "Give me what you've got.", you'll receive 500 , while asking for nothing will make Raven available as a skill trainer. Either way, you'll earn reputation and blacksmith prestige and complete the quest. (You won't have the option to return the 800 you found at Wolf Rock, so if you found that stash and didn't hand it over to Koniash, you can keep the coin.) If you then wait at least one in-game day, you'll be able to trade with him again to purchase the Sketch for caster III.

### Objectives

## Kuttenberg Tournament

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

The Kuttenberg Tournament is a repeatable task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It's unlocked after completing the side quest Ars Dimicatoria.

## Walkthrough

You can compete in the tournament weekly by signing up with Menhard von Frankfurt after completing Ars Dimicatoria. You can compete in any combination of 3 separate disciplines: longsword, short sword and shield, or free combat. Free combat allows fighters to use any of their own weapons and armor, so a good weapon and heavy armor is recommended. The entry fee is 100 per category of fight, plus an optional 105 if you wish to skip time until the tournament begins. Note, you must show up to the tournament area between 6-10am on the day of the tournament or you'll be disqualified!

If you have the Legacy of the Forge DLC, be sure to wear your Waffenrock of Henry's Forge when you compete for extra blacksmith prestige!

## Kuttenberg gallows

Kuttenberg gallows is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

## Kuttenberg longsword

Kuttenberg longsword is a unqiue melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

## Description

A beautiful sword of the highest quality, the ultimate master weapon! It was made by Enderlin, a swordsman from Kuttenberg, as a copy of the sword of the Kuttenberg swordfighting brotherhood. For the greater glory of Kuttenberg, Master Enderlin then donated it as a reward for the winners of the Kuttenberg Tournament.

## Acquisition

- The Kuttenberg longsword serves as the reward for winning the Kuttenberg Tournament.

## Trivia

- The inscription on the blade, Dimicatores de Montibus Cuthnis, translates to from Latin to "Fighters from the Mountains of Kuttenberg," or more simply, "The Fighters of Kuttenberg."

- Montibus Cuthnis is the ablative plural form derived from Mons Cuthna, a historical Latin name for Kuttenberg. The earliest known reference to Kuttenberg under this name dates to 1289.

- Presumably, it serves as the formal Latin title of the swordfighting brotherhood of Kuttenberg. Medieval guilds and fraternities often adopted Latin names or mottos to convey prestige, tradition, and civic pride.

## Laboratores

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Laboratores is the 4th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, immediately following Fortuna.

## Description

Me and Capon finally reached Trosky, but since we look like beggars, the gate guards didn't believe we were messengers and wouldn't let us in to see von Bergow. We ended up in a tavern in Troskowitz. Now we have to rack our brains and figure out what to do next.

## Synopsis

Henry and Hans arrive in Troskowitz, somewhat clean (but still a bit reeky). They stop at the inn for drinks and food and the innkeeper, Betty, is not so impressed with the looks of them. She asks them if they have any money and Hans reluctantly hands over what Bozhena was able to provide for them before they left her home. It’s not enough for anything but a bowl of gruel, but Hans insists she bring them the very best and all will be settled later.

The biggest obstacle in front of them is a lack of money, without groschen they can’t get very far. Henry suggests they can earn some money doing odd jobs, something Hans finds ridiculous as it would surely take too long and there could hardly be even a decent tailor around. Going back to Rattay is just as unfeasible; it would be a disgrace. Henry is optimistic, but Hans blames himself for the whole fiasco and feels responsible not only for their current situation but the deaths of their comrades.

Betty returns with their food and Hans is less than impressed, gruel it is. Betty insists he should be grateful, there’s meat in it after all and it’s worth more than they paid her. To settle the bill, she intends to put them to work.

While eating, Henry spots a familiar face – the woman from the pond who was nearly assaulted by the raiders. Hans is excited, she could vouch for them and end their woes. She asks Betty for a pitcher of wine, claiming she’s been sent from the castle and her name is Katherine.

Henry approaches, stench first, and is not so politely asked to wash off before even thinking about speaking to a woman. While he does so, Katherine updates Betty on the situation at the castle. Captain Thomas was attacked by bandits and badly injured, and the whole situation has made von Bergow so worried he’s forbade any soldiers from leaving.

Henry tells Katherine he’s seen her before, but she insists she doesn’t remember him. When he insists in turn that they saw each other by the pond, Katherine claims never to have been anywhere near any ponds of late. She continues to deny their meeting, saying maybe Henry mistook her for someone else if he continues to badger her. Betty returns with the wine, and Katherine leaves back towards the castle. Henry grabs her, trying one last time to implore her to vouch for them. A rider rushes by, distracting them, and Katherine advises Henry he won’t get into the castle and even if he could the man who just rode by was a royal messenger – von Bergow is preparing to leave. She does give Henry one nugget of hope, there’s a local wedding coming up soon and von Bergow is set to attend.

Once Katherine leaves, Betty tells Henry what he needs to do to work off the debt – carry some sacks of flour off the delivery cart and into the inn’s stores, something that should be quick work for two strapping young men. Henry can ask her for more details about the wedding, since the groom is the son of a vassal of von Bergow’s, Semine, the lord of Trosky is sure to be there, just as Katherine said. Young Semine is being married to the daughter of Bailiff Thrush of Troskowitz, Agnes. Unfortunately, Betty has no way to help Henry get there too, however, a couple of the invited guests are at the inn currently and she directs him their way.

Henry returns to Hans and brings him up to speed. When the topic turns to the work Betty has asked of them, Hans is insulted. Hauling sacks does not befit a man of his station, even impoverished as he is. If anyone were to see him, word could get around once everything is cleared up and he’d lose what little face he has left. Henry is frustrated, not understanding why he can’t just do a bit of work for once but Hans informs him of a little divine law called The Three States of Man.

Society, he explains, is divinely ordered into three groups: Oratores – priests who pray and commune with God, Laboratores – the working peasants who labour for their betters, and Bellatores – the warriors who protect the flock. Hans, as a noble, belongs to the latter group and there’s no way any of the three can mix – it just goes against God!

There’s no convincing him, so Henry hauls the sacks on his own. In reward, Hans insists that as soon as they get some gear together he’ll help find Mutt, ignoring that that doesn’t quite fit under his purview as a Bellator either. While Henry works, Hans strikes up a conversation with another patron – Svatya, the bailiff’s son.

Hans and Svatya turn to discussing the ambush at the pond. Svatya insists the whole thing was the fault of the men who were killed, something that upsets Hans. Hans boasts that he’ll forgive Svatya’s offence, if he apologises… and invites him to the wedding. Svatya rebuffs the posturing saying the only way he could get in would be by making himself useful to the blacksmith or the miller. Henry tries to intervene, but emotions are already too high, Svatya turns to mocking Hans, and his name. Whether Henry tries to calm both parties down or defends Hans, a fight breaks out.

Eventually, the town guard show up to break up the brawl, arresting Henry and Hans and putting them in the pillory. Once there, they turn to infighting, each blaming the other for their predicament as the townspeople hit them with rotten produce.

The next morning, as the man arrives to set them free, von Bergow rides past. Hans is set free first, and while Henry is still immobile, he leaves fed up with the fight they had and the situation they’re in he decides he’ll do it alone.

## Walkthrough

After the cutscene, head to the trough to wash yourself and then talk to Katherine. Once she leaves, Betty will put you to work. Talk to Hans and he’ll refuse to do work that’s beneath him, so off to the cart it is. You’ll have to carry the sacks into the inn’s pantry and place them on the board so they don’t spoil.

The cart is just to the north-east, next to the inn’s back gate. Carry the sacks into the inn, heading straight and then into the second door on the right. The boards are at the back of the room. Do this three times, and Hans will start a fight with Svatya.

Fight Svatya and his comrades, unarmed, until the guard shows up to disperse the brawl.

## Lackey

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Lackey is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

This can be found either in relation to the Mutt side quest, or by coming across Zlata at her family's cabin. She'll note that her husband, Vostatek, has been out for an abnormally long time and she's got a bad feeling he's in danger.

## Walkthrough

After agreeing to help find her husband, head out to the marker and when in range, you should start hearing a man yelling for help from a tree that has several wolves around it. Kill or scare off the wolves, then let the huntsman know it's safe. He'll jump down, only to hurt one of his ankles. You can entertain him in conversation for a bit, but eventually you'll need to pick him up and carry him to his hideout to get his horse, Pepik.

Vostatek will direct you which general direction and landmark to look for at each step before eventually finding his camp, but no horse. Unfortunately he knows this means poachers in the area took Pepik, so he'll ask you to go get his horse back and kill the poachers if you want an extra reward.

Follow the trail and items to the camp further up the hill, but be warned: at low levels, this can be a tough fight if you just charge in, with about 5 regular poachers and 1 with a shield. If having difficulties, try to catch each bandit when they're alone and out of eyesight from the rest to knock them out from behind and hide the body. Keep in mind that if you want the extra reward, you have to make sure to kill all the poachers so either kill them as you go or make sure you remember where you dropped any unconscious bodies as the quest won't update with individual markers for them.

Pepik is further into the camp, near where the shield bearing poacher tends to sit. You'll just need to simply mount up and ride Pepik back to Vostatek's camp to complete this part.

Once back with Pepik, Vostatek will be happy, even more so if you killed the poachers. You can then agree to go with him right back to his home or let him go alone/see him later. Once you return back to Zlata, she'll be relieved to see her husband is safe (with Vitek not so much), and some speech checks will appear here regarding Vitek. Regardless, you'll be rewarded (80 Groschen if you killed the poachers) and a new bed to sleep and save in the stables by the house. Vostatek is also unlocked as a skill teacher.

## Lamprecht von Prag

Lamprecht von Prag is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Lamprecht is a soldier in the service of King Sigismund and the self-proclaimed best swordsman in all of Bohemia.

Lamprecht is encountered at Suchdol during the final stages of the siege. Having already killed several loyalist soldiers attacking the walls of the castle, he challenges Henry to an honourable duel, declaring himself the best swordsman in the kingdom.

Lamprecht typically expresses his satisfaction that Henry has returned to Suchdol so they can compete against each other, especially since other soldiers have spoken highly of Henry's swordsmanship skills. However, if Henry wins the Kuttenberg tournament, he will bring up the victory and ask whether Henry is as skilled in real combat, since he would love to cut the throat of a noble bastard.

Lamprecht is slain by Henry.

Lamprecht was first mentioned by Black Bartosch when Henry of Skalitz first arrived at Trosky Castle following the arrest after the wedding brawl at Semine.

## Landowner Jakesh

Landowner Jakesh is a farmer in Troskowitz in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

At one point, Jakesh married Ludmila and had three daughters together. As his wife had very easy births to the point she'd given birth before the midwife could even arrive, when she was pregnant with a fourth child, Jakesh felt there was no need for a midwife. However, after hours of being in labour, he was asked to call on the town's midwife, Bozhena.

However, he had sent for assistance too late and Ludmila ended up giving birth to a stillborn baby boy before she herself died from the exhaustion. Bozhena could only helplessly stand by but Jakesh, not realizing his son had been stillborn, accused Bozhena of having damned his son for not christening him before death, and letting his wife die. He riled up the rest of the town and they drove Bozhena and her adopted daughter, Pavlena, out of town.

Five years passed, and while Jakesh harboured no ill will towards Pavlena on account of her having been a young child that fateful night, he still despised Bozhena and would rage about her when drunk. One day, while out with two hired farmhands of his, brothers Straw and Ota, he went into another one of these rants, not realizing the brothers would take it to heart and try to act on it to gain Jakesh's favour.

Bozhena wished for Henry to kill Jakesh in retribution for having been responsible for the abduction of her daughter and the death of her daughter's man. Henry may have done so or he may have been able to convince the two to reconcile wherein Jakesh would give Bozhena some money as compensation for the horrible misunderstanding.

### Associated quests

- Bad Blood

## Last Rites

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Last Rites acts as the prologue and 1st main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Suchdol is besieged by the Praguers.

## Synopsis

The fortress of Suchdol is under siege, its defenders on the side of King Wenceslas IV are holding out against the forces of Prague in support of King Sigismund. The siege is not going well for the defenders, they won’t be able to hold out much longer.

Out into the gun smoke and mud steps Godwin, kitted out in armour and ready for battle, except he's forgotten a weapon. Hans Capon arrives, helping a wounded Suchdol soldier, and greets Godwin with a sense that they may not survive this battle. Godwin assures him they will before a trebuchet blast lowers the drawbridge, allowing the attackers to move in closer.

Sir Hans gives Godwin the crossbow once used by the injured soldier he was helping, telling him to "Make it count." before heading to his own position, starting the quest. Godwill will defend the fortress to the best of his abilities, but the onslaught is too great. Hans is shot in the shoulder and the call comes to retreat into the tower.

Suchdol is overwhelmed, and all hope seems lost...

## Walkthrough

As Godwin, head up the stairs in front of you and use your crossbow to fend off the attack. Once the situation is under control, you will be asked to move and help at the gate where the attackers are trying to get in. This attack will be repelled with the help of your crossbow, gonnes of the Suchdol defenders and some fire from above.

After the gate is dealt with, Dry Devil will ask you to draw your sword and follow him. He will lead you over to the back ramparts where enemies have managed to get a foothold with their ladders. Fight off the Prague soldiers and knock down the ladders using a polearm. Knocking down the ladder will end the quest.

## Last Will

Last Will is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is available following Ars Dimicatoria.

## Description

An old widow is looking for someone to stand for her in a duel.

## Walkthrough

Ask Menhard if he has any work for you. He will tell you there is a matter that could use a swordsman but that he cannot risk getting involved in. Talk to Widow Gerda to start the quest, she is usually near the sword hall and plays dice there. She needs you to act as her stand-in in a duel to settle her late husband’s dispute with a man called Radmil.

Radmil can be found at the cobbler’s during the day usually in the workshop behind the store front, talk to him to challenge him to the duel. He’ll ask you to throw the fight since he needs to money to open his own shop. If you want to throw the fight and receive payment for doing so, you’ll have to pass a hard charisma check. No matter what you choose here, confirm the duel and the weapon you want to use.

Head back to Gerda and let her know and she will take you to the duel site. Radmil by his own admission is not a fighter, defeating him should be relatively easy. Just be careful not to kill him, as he will go down in only a couple of hits. If you want to throw the fight, the easiest way to do so would be to leave the duel grounds.

Speak to Radmil to confirm the result and settle the debt.

Should you win, Gerda will give you 250 and a bed at the Hangman’s Halter. Should Radmil win, if you convinced him to pay you he will give you 175 otherwise, he will give you nothing.

## Lay Brother Elijah

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Lay Brother Elijah is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Elijah was a young lay brother at Sedletz Monastery. Although content enough with a semi-cloistered life, he kept a stash of Hidden booze in one of the monastery’s fish ponds so that he could always have a swig when he felt like it.

One night, when going out for a drink, Elijah noticed a fire had started in the flour store of the monastery. He ran over to see what had happened, and noticed two bodies inside. Without much thinking, he leapt in himself to take them out, only realising once he had gone in that they were already dead.

This upset him greatly, and after he was freed of suspicion of arson, he got himself blind drunk and hid in the cellars so he didn’t have to think about what he had seen. He had wanted to do something good for once, but felt humiliated and defeated that he was so desperate to help what turned out to be no one living.

When Henry came asking around looking into who had started the fire, Elijah was reluctant to talk but felt more cooperative after sobering up. He admitted that he saw himself as nothing more than a coward and a drunk. Henry reassured him that his deed was not in vain, as the bodies could hold important clues that would have otherwise been destroyed.

### Associated Quests

- To Dust You Shan't Return

## Lead ball

Lead ball is an ammo item in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A lead ball. It rattles a little in the barrel, but at least it's easy to load. Even the best plate armour can't stop it up close!

## Crafting

Main article: Recipe for Lead shot gunpowder

- Charcoal × 1

- Saltpetre × 1

- Sulphur × 1

## Lefty

Lefty is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He will supply Henry with Black arrows in exchange for Raven feathers at a rate of 1 arrow for 1 feather.

## Biography

Lefty lived in Pschitoky and considered himself to be a great arrow maker, but sadly a very poor shot which earned him the nickname 'by-blow' from others in town.

He greatly enjoyed the process of making arrows and would spend his days in the woods outside the village doing just that, while also failing to make proper use of them.

Even though his arrows were special, he had no qualms with sharing them and making some for anyone who would give him the proper materials to do so. Truly, he wanted someone to be able to shoot them properly for once.

## Leg armour/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Leg armour is one of the armour types that Henry can equip in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

There are four categories of footwear: Cuisses, Hose, Shoes, and Spurs.

## Overview

Cuisses

Metal plates that protect thighs in battle. Cuisses are the main form of leg protection in the game.

Hose

Leg coverings used under armor or for casual wear. They come in two subtypes - simple and padded. The padded hose is necessary to equip cuisses.

Shoes

Everyday footwear ranging from sturdy boots to jester shoes. They deteriorate fairly quickly, but some Craftsmanship skill perks can significantly reduce the stamina cost of sprinting.

Spurs

Metal attachments for boots used to control horses while riding. Spurs don't provide significant defense but give a boost to Horsemanship skill.

## Legacy of the Forge

Legacy of the Forge is the second major story expansion for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Announced on 16 January 2025 alongside two other expansions, Brushes with Death and Mysteria Ecclesiae, it was released on 9 September 2025 for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. It is included in both the Expansion Pass and the Gold Edition.

## Description

Return to Kuttenberg and put your blacksmithing skills to the test to acquire and repair a legendary burned-down forge, where your father, Martin, spent his youth as an apprentice. Establish your own home in the heart of Kuttenberg, designing the forge itself as well as its surroundings and your very own private quarters, with the ability to customize and furnish to aid your gameplay.

Venture down memory lane and learn of your father's legacy as a blacksmith, revealing a part of his life that has remained hidden—until now. Uncover the mystery of an ambitious masterpiece your father once worked on and follow in his footsteps to complete it. Become a forge master and build upon your new blacksmith prestige, helping the people of Kuttenberg with sword crafting, armor-smithing, and some more quirky requests.

In addition to new daily quests, Henry will unlock the ability to earn cash, enabling a brand-new home customization system with over 100 million combinations to personalize your forge, private quarters, and its surroundings. Once decked out, your forge becomes a place to return to and call home.

## Features

- Henry's very own home – Personalise your forge, private quarters, and its surroundings with brand new design features, allowing you to build a unique home with a customisation system that offers over 100 million combinations.

- Continue Henry's journey of discovery – Return to Kuttenberg and venture down memory lane. Meeting acquaintances of your late father, turning strangers into allies in a meaningful pursuit to achieve your family's legacy. Uncover part of your father's life that has remained hidden - until now.

- Enhance your blacksmithing skills – Rise through the ranks to become the master of Kuttenberg's blacksmith guild, taking on blacksmithing commissions that will bolster your reputation. Unlock unique blueprints for new armour and weapons all while helping the people of Kuttenberg with sword crafting, armour-smithing and some more quirky requests.

## Lent

Lent is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You finished the game without eating meat or killing any animals.

## Acquisition

The Lent achievement is unlocked by completing all main questline without killing any animals, wild or domestic, or eating any meat. While the achievement is relatively straightforward, it can be particularly challenging due to the frequency of hostile wildlife encounters.

Requirements:

- No animals killed - Best to avoid engaging with animals entirely. This is especially difficult in the Trosky region, where wolves are a frequent threat. If attacked, it is possible to drive them off by lightly wounding them; however, care must be taken to ensure they do not bleed out after fleeing. Always check your statistics afterward to confirm no kills were registered.

- No meat eaten - Avoid all meat products, including cooked meat, dried meat, sausages, and meals that may contain meat. Honey is your best friend during this walkthrough.

## Tips

- Save frequently, especially before areas known for wolf encounters.

- Run from wolves or use stealth to avoid them entirely. Do not rely on companions or NPCs to kill them, as this may still count against your stats depending on the situation.

- Check your progress using the in-game statistics menu:

- Player → Statistics → Combat → Animals killed

- Player → Statistics → General → Meat eaten

## Trivia

- In Christian tradition, Lent is a 40-day period of fasting. It commemorates the 40 days Jesus spent fasting in the desert, and it’s traditionally observed by giving up certain luxuries or habits, including meat, as a form of spiritual discipline.

## Lights Out

Lights Out is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You slit the throat of an enemy who was looking for you.

## Acquisition

The Lights Out achievement is unlocked by silently eliminating an enemy while they are searching for you - indicated by the white rabbit icon appearing at the top of the screen.

How to perform the stealth takedowns:

- Equipped in order to perform a silent kill.

- Attract attention by:

- Throwing a stone while crouched ( by default).

- Making a deliberate noise (such as walking over a noisy surface or interacting with objects).

- Commanding Mutt to bark.

- Wait for the enemy to investigate the disturbance.

- Once the enemy begins searching (white rabbit icon), sneak behind them.

- Hold to perform a stealth takedown.

## Tips

- The main quest Storm (the final quest in the Trosky region) provides an ideal opportunity to earn this achievement. During the escape sequence through Apollonia, the area is dark and populated by isolated patrolling enemies - perfect for a stealth takedown.

## Like Old Times

Like Old Times is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is only available during The Lion's Den, after you exhaust all conversation options with Hans.

## Description

Lord Capon wants to go hunting.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Hans during the day at the Devil's Den after speaking with the group and deciding on a plan of action during The Lion's Den. He will invite you out on a hunting trip. Agree and immediately follow him outside. Whistle for your horse, as the hunting spot is a long way away. After some initial conversation, you may opt to fast travel to the site or enjoy the view.

Follow Hans and he’ll lead you to a hunting camp he scouted during his solo rides. Along the way you can speak to him. When you get there, however, you’ll find the camp inhabited by a band of Sigismund’s soldiers. Talk to Hans and you’ll have the opportunity to pick a strategy.

- Talk to them - You tell Capon these people are not worth dirtying his sword with. All of the conversation consists of timed options, so be quick. First are medium Dread check and a hard Survival check, followed by hard Strength or Dread check. If you pass both skill checks and don't stay silent for the third conversation prompt, they will run away. Failing even one of those checks will cause them to engage with you.

- Engage - There's five of them, but they are easier to beat than ordinary bandits because you have backup.

- Quiet dispatch - You suggest you'll get rid of them on your own. Hans begrudgingly agrees, but you'll lose rep with him. He will join in an ensuing fight if you raise the alarm.

- I'd rather not get involved - Hans will insist the soldiers are animals and you should get rid of them. After that, you still have a chance to change your mind, as Hans doesn't want to engage them on his own. If you insist on not getting involved, you lose reputation with Capon and the quest immediately ends. Killing the soldiers afterwards doesn't matter for the outcome of the quest.

Whatever you choose, deal with the soldiers. Once they’ve left or been killed, talk to Hans again to finish the quest. You'll have the opportunity to return with him to the Den or else stay at the camp.

## Lingua belli longsword

Lingua belli longsword is a melee weapon in the Legacy of the Forge expansion, categorized as a longsword.

Note: Lingua belli longsword can be crafted.

## Description

This weapon hails from your own forge. A light, well-balanced long blade, sturdy not only thanks to the steel used but also the double fullering technique. It's the sharp tongue of war, Lingua belli, which proclaims the truth of he who wields it.

## Crafting

Main article: Sketch - Lingua belli longsword

- Acidum chloridum × 1

- Coloured gold × 1

- Eight-sided sword pommel × 1

- Horned sword guard × 1

- Sheet steel × 1

- Tincal × 2

- Toledo steel × 2

## Acquisition

- The sketch for the Lingua belli longsword has a chance to be obtained during the Sinners of Kuttenberg or In the Service of the Guild repeatable activities, though the chances of obtaining a specific sketch are random. After that the sword can be crafted as many times as you desire - the sketch doesn't call for any unique materials.

## Trivia

- The Latin phrase lingua belli literally translates to "the language of war."

## Lion's roar Kilij

Lion's roar Kilij is a melee weapon in the Legacy of the Forge expansion, categorized as a shortsword.

Note: Lion's roar Kilij can be crafted.

## Description

A single-edged Turkish blade resembling a sabre, but thanks to its widened tip, it strikes with far more force. The pommel bears the image of Aslan, the lion symbol of ancient kings, for only they were said to have brought him down. This kilij seems fit for one of the bey sipahis, the cursed captains of heathen knights.

## Crafting

Main article: Sketch - Kilij, Lion's roar

- Acidum chloridum × 1

- Coloured gold × 2

- Dogfish skin × 2

- Enamel powder × 1

- Exotic wood × 1

- Jasper × 2

- Toledo steel × 2

## Acquisition

- The sketch for the Lion's roar Kilij is unlocked by completing the Sinners of Kuttenberg activity and following its storyline to the end. After that the sabre can be crafted as many times as you desire - the sketch doesn't call for any unique materials.

- Another can also be obtained illegally from the Scribe Vetter's house. It can easily be found during Martin's Dream, in the same area as the Heart of the Astronomical Clock.

## Trivia

- A kilij (from Turkish kılıç, literally "sword") is a type of curved, single-edged saber that originated with Turkic steppe cultures and was later refined by the Ottoman Empire. It was highly effective in mounted combat and became a symbol of military prowess and status throughout the Ottoman Empire and beyond.

- A signature feature of the kilij is its yelman (or false‑edge), a flared portion near the tip of the blade designed to boost cutting force and allow limited back‑cuts. The kilij's design influenced other sabers across the world, including the Persian shamshir, Mameluke sword, and later European cavalry sabres.

- The sipahi mentioned in the description were professional cavalrymen deployed by the Turks. Sipahi units included the provincial timarli sipahi, which constituted most of the army, and the salaried regular kapikulu sipahi, or palace troops. They were the cavalry equivalent of the Janissary household infantry force.

## Little Nary

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Little Nary was a mercenary, a bodyguard and a right-hand man for the owner of smelting operation in Grund, Buresh of Krakovitz.

## Biography

Sometimes before 1403, Little Nary was hired by a nobleman Buresh of Krakovitz. He was tasked to accompany his employer at all times on account of his morbid fear of being threatened. It is likely, he hired Nary after he joined the mint master Ulrich Vavak's scheme for stealing the king's share from the silver mines.

Little Nary was killed following an altercation with Henry when the latter came to investigate allegations of embezzlement and fraud.
