## Longsword of the Four Evangelists

Longsword of the Four Evangelists is a unique melee weapon in the Legacy of the Forge expansion, categorized as a longsword.

Note: Longsword of the Four Evangelists can be crafted.

## Description

A beautiful long sword with engravings of the four evangelists - Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. According to tradition, each has a supernatural attribute. Matthew is depicted as an angel, Mark as a winged lion, Luke as a winged bull and John as an eagle.

## Crafting

Main article: Sketch - Longsword of the Four Evangelists

- Acidum chloridum × 1

- Enamel powder × 1

- Frankfurt steel × 2

- Iron × 2

- Weapon stub × 1

## Acquisition

- The sketch for the Longsword of the Four Evangelists can be learned by buying a Weapon stub⁠⁠ from the travelling merchant Horst of Lishkau during the Blacksmith's Commission repeatable activity. He'll sell you a broken weapon three different times, and the third of those purchases will be this one.

## Trivia

- The inscription on the blade, Ferrum ferro acuitur, comes from the Latin Vulgate translation of the Bible, specifically the Book of Proverbs (Proverbs 27:17). The full verse reads: Ferrum ferro acuitur, et homo exacuit faciem amici sui. In English, this is usually translated as, "Iron sharpens iron, and one person sharpens another."

## Loretz

Loretz is a location in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It's the vineyard north of Kuttenberg.

## Residents

- Administrator Jerome

- Cardinal Pozzo

- Olbert Eichner

## Associated quests

- In Vino Veritas

- Oratores

- In the Service of the Guild

## Codex entry

Loretz

Whether Loretz was already standing at the time of our game is not clear, as the first written mention of it dates back to 1418.

It's unlikely that vineyards surrounded the fortress, as they were still a hot novelty in the Lands of the Bohemian Crown at that time, but beer was brewed there. From sources dating back to 1544, we learn that Zdislav Zvířetický of Wartenberg bought the local hop farm with malt house and brewery. In 1593, the production of beer called Kumperské was documented, in 1680 Konvent beer, from 1899 it was Dačický lager and the "health beer" Mincmistr.

Loretz Municipal Brewery in Kuttenberg has changed owners several times during its history, but beer has been brewed here, with minor interruptions, to this day.

—Codex entry: Loretz

## Note

The in-game place is a vineyard. The real life Loretz, however, is famous for its beer instead.

## Lovers' spot

Nice. It's almost like the place I used to visit with Bianca.

—Henry's commentary

Lovers' spot is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

This is a quiet clearing south of Troskowitz village, that a pair of sweethearts once chose to steal away for a romantic tryst. The clearing sits on the bank of a small forest pond, shaded by trees.

A blanket lies spread on the ground alongside a picnic basket, inside of which rests a bouquet of flowers. A pair of discarded garments is strewn nearby, and in the pond itself, a couple of beer jugs bob in the water, cooling in the shallows.

Something must have frightened the lovers off in a hurry, as they left without their belongings or even their clothes.

Loyza lived and worked in Miskowitz as a hired hand. One night, he interrupted Janosh Uher who was trying to rob his employer's shop. There was a struggle, and Loyza was seriously injured while Janosh was taken into custody and put in the town's pillory.

He's the former Kuttenberg city scribe, who has been forced to leave the job after he had apparently gone mad during the investigation of the murders of young women in the city. Lumir used to be the scribe, but as he bitterly notes, now he's just Lumir the Madman.

For many long years he was a scribe for Andreas Plümel, a former bailiff of Kuttenberg. As the bailiff was busy settling trivial quarrels of rich men, Lumir started dealing with the problems of the common folk who came to the Rathaus. As he himself claims, he was quite good at it.

## László Farkas

László Farkas is a Hungarian baron and minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

László was in the service of King Sigismund and stationed at his camp in the Kuttenberg region.

He was a profit-motivated man, eager to take prisoners and ransom them back to their families. Following a battle, he captured Sir Peter of Suchotlesky who later died of fever. Rather than risk losing the ransom, László neglected to tell Peter's family he died, choosing to continue negotiations as if everything was normal.

Peter's younger brother, Jan of Suchotlesky came to the region to arrange for his brother's return. He enlisted the help of Henry and sent him to the camp to get László's terms. László was unmoved, even if Henry discovered his omission, and insisted the ransom payment be received - for Peter's corpse if not his life.

At the handover, László tried to bribe Henry to come over to his side, as Jan could not offer him as fine a reward. If Henry accepted, László would give him all of the late Peter's belongings as a reward. If he refused, László would be slain.

## Maddening Pain

Maddening Pain is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC after The Royal Physician, during Anamnesis.

## Description

I met the steward’s peculiar wench Maddie. She was writhing in pain and clutching her belly, as if the Devil himself were dancing in there. At the infirmary they panicked instead of helping her.

## Walkthrough

Outside, you’ll find Maddie experiencing terrible pain in her abdomen. She’s certain it’s not a woman’s issue, but the monks won’t help her. Ask her some questions about her symptoms and offer to help. You’ll offer to get her something from the infirmary.

Talk to Benedict to put in a good word for her, he won’t know how to help but will suggest looking in the library and asking Albich in the infirmary.

If you speak with Albich, he will advise that he thinks he knows the proper treatment and will give you the Recipe for Anti-Inflammatory Potion.

You can ask Zacharias as well, he’ll recommend a combination of drinking, movement, and rest, which you'll find confusing and contradictory, but he'll insist that women's bodies are just naturally confusing like that.

You can ask the librarian for books on women’s matters, but he doesn’t know them specifically, though he suggests taking a loot around the library. The book you want is called The Rose Garden, it can be found on the second bookshelf to the left from the library entrance.

Inflammation in the lower passages will describe Maddie’s problem, the suggested treatment is a decoction against inflammation. Upon reading, you will learn the recipe automatically, if you did not already learn it from Albich :

- AquaAquaWater base

- Nettle × 1

- Valerian × 2

- Ginger × 1

Grind the nettle, then add to the cauldron. Using the bellows, boil for one turn. Add in the valerian, then boil for two turns. Grind the ginger and add to the cauldron. Finally, pour out the potion.

All the ingredients can be found in the monastery gardens, save for ginger which can be found in the alchemy room of the infirmary.

Once you have the potion, any strength will do, go and talk to her. Hand it over to her; she’ll drink it and thank you effusively, ending the quest.

## Objectives

## Maddie

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Maddie is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Maddie was a young woman who worked at Sedletz Monastery. She often helped out around the sties, but did all kinds of menial labour elsewhere outside the cloister as well.

One day, Maddie felt a terrible pain in her abdomen after having sat on some cold stone steps and went to the Monastery infirmary to seek treatment. Initially, Novice Benedict at the infirmary dismissed her symptoms as a “womanly issue” but she insisted she would have known if it had been that. She had tried all kinds of remedies for the pain, garlic rubs, prayers, hanging upside-down from a ladder, all to no avail.

Henry happened to be nearby and accepted Maddie’s request for help. In the end, he was able to determine she was suffering from an inflammation and gave her a potion for proper treatment. The treatment worked almost instantaneously and she was overjoyed and grateful.

Later, Maddie fell ill with the mysterious illness that swept the monastery and its grounds. She was brought to the infirmary not long after the lockdown began, and was eventually able to make a full recovery.

### Associated Quests

- Anamnesis

- Maddening Pain

## Madman's longsword

Madman's longsword is a unique melee weapon in the Brushes with Death expansion, categorized as a longsword.

Note: Madman's longsword can be crafted.

## Description

The sword belonging to the madman from the dugout that Voyta sent me to. The engraving on the blade reads: Confiteor Deo Omnipotenti.

## Crafting

Main article: Sketch - Madman's longsword

- Fastening material × 1

- Frankfurt steel × 3

- Madman's broken sword × 1

## Acquisition

- The Madman's longsword can be obtained during the Man Proposes side quest. After defeating the Man from Dugout, accept the broken sword from him. Once you have it, the weapon can be reforged.

- If you are after the Curiosity Killed the Cat achievement, reforge the sword, convince the madman to take it back, wait a few days, and then visit him again. You will be able to pick up the sword from the scene.

## Trivia

- The inscription on the blade Confiteor Deo Omnipotenti translates from Latin to "I confess to Almighty God."

- It is the opening of the traditional Confiteor prayer, in which the person acknowledges their sins and asks for forgiveness. It is typically recited during the Penitential Act at the beginning of the Roman Catholic Mass.

## Magdalena

Magdalena is a major character in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. She lives in Henry's forge in Kuttenberg and is the widow of its former master.

## Biography

Magdalena was born just outside the walls of Kuttenberg and lived in the city all her life. As a young woman she met a blacksmith named Shkoda and the two were quickly married. They were not blessed with children, as Magdalena had difficulty bringing a child to term, but lived happily together until Shokda's death.

After her husband's death, there was a fire in the house, and Magdalena began living out of only a couple of rooms, letting the house and forge go into disrepair. She lived off of selling eggs and a small stipend from the blacksmiths' guild.

Years later, she met Henry whose father, Martin, had apprenticed under Shkoda at the forge in his youth. Henry was eager to revitalise the forge and helped to bring it back to its former glory. Magdalena helped by selling some of the goods he made to locals as well as through her usual activities.

One of the other former apprentices, Standa the Fly, returned to the forge as well and the two became quite close, initiating a romantic relationship.

## Magic horseshoes

Magic Horseshoes is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

## Walkthrough

Head to the saddler’s in Semine and talk to Guildsman Janek to start the quest. He’s heard the nearby nomads have magic horseshoes they use and wants Henry to make some for him so he can use them during a race for the saddler.

Travel to the Nomads' camp and talk to Mikolai. He can usually be found near the horses during the day. If you can pass a horsemanship check he will tell you it’s no magic, just horseshoes with spikes to get footing on rock. He will give you the recipe and all that’s left is to forge them for Janek.

If you are unable to pass the skill check, you’ll have to find the shoes in the camp. They can be found in a sack next to where Mikolai sleeps. Loot the Spiked horseshoes and hand them over to Janek. You can also find spiked horseshoes at the Shared Altar if you completed quest Horses for Courses. He will give you some money for the shoes and tell you to come back a few days later after the race to split the winnings, should he win.

The quest will automatically update once enough time has passed. Go back to see Janek and he’ll give you an additional 80 as your share of the winnings, ending the quest.

## Maleshov

Maleshov (Czech: Malešov) is a village which is located at the southernmost part of the map, slightly southwest of Bylany. it is overlooked by the Maleshov fortress. The village has its own lake, which serves both as a source of water and a defensive barrier on one side of the fortress itself. Aside from the fortress, the village also has its own wooden guard tower on its east side.

To the east of the village lives groom Hashtal, who cared for horses under Kunzlin Ruthard and later took the same duty when Otto von Bergow was given the fortress together with the village by Sigismund of Luxembourg.

Northwest of the village, you may find the Madman's dugout.

## Traders

- Archery master

- Bathhouse proprietor

- Innkeeper Slatchalek

- Trader

## Amenities

- Smokehouse x 2

- Drying rack x 3

- Dice table

## Associated quests

- Dancing with the Devil

## Codex entry

The name of the village is derived from the legend of a wealthy Kuttenberg burgher named Malesh (Maleš), who founded a woodcutter colony here to supply the nearby silver mountains with charcoal.

The first mention of the village dates back to 1303. The fortress is first mentioned in 1359, when Purkard of Maidberk sold his village to the Sedletz Monastery which subsequently passed the village onto the Ruthards, a patrician family from Kuttenberg, in 1364. When the family was enobled in the early 15th century, they began to call themselves the Ruthards of Maleshov. They did not enjoy the fortress for long, however, because in 1411 it was given to the king's supporter, Martin Kladný of Těchlovice.

The area around Maleshov is steeped in history. For example, in 1421, Martin Kladný defended the fortress against an army of Praguers, that wanted to install its own Mint Master in Kuttenberg. Maleshov became an important fortress especially during the Hussite Wars in 1424.

Today, the remains of the fortress include a five-story tower with Gothic windows and remnants of late Gothic fortifications making it a favourite destination for the Warhorse team.

—Codex entry: Maleshov

## Man Proposes

Man Proposes is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 6th or 7th quest in the Brushes with Death DLC, concurrent with Stained Honour.

## Description

I wanted to learn more about the painter, but instead of telling me, he sent me to some dugout near Maleshov. He said I should take a look around, take in the atmosphere, then come and tell him what I saw.

## Synopsis

Voyta is finally ready for Henry to learn some of the truth of his past, with some cajoling. There are things in his past Voyta has never really told anyone, but he has an idea of how to get them across. He sends Henry in search of an abandoned dugout north-east of Maleshov. He wants Henry to take a look around there and then come back so they can discuss what Henry will have seen.

The dugout, however, is not as abandoned as Voyta made it seem. There’s a man living there who isn’t very happy to have visitors. Henry is eventually able to calm him down and talk to him. His name, it seems, is Libor and he seems half-mad. He talks to himself in the third person and speaks disjointedly. Through his odd manner, he asks if Henry knows Voyta… but then insists that Voyta is dead, killed by Burkhard.

After a while, Libor assumes Henry must have come for a broken sword of his and insists he take it. The sword, he says, makes him confused and he thinks it would suit Henry more. Since he’s here, Henry decides to look around as Voyta suggested he do. The roof of the dugout is quite rundown and must have been that way for decades. There’s a noose tied in the tree out front and a broken wagon behind it that must’ve been nice at some point and a scarecrow has been set up in an anthill which reminds Henry of his own youth.

Henry may reforge the sword and force Libor to take it back, resulting in Libor hanging himself and grief from Voyta.

When he returns, Henry tells Voyta all the things he saw and Voyta opens up a little. The scarecrow, it seems, is called Hugo after the skeleton in The Hole. Voyta and his friends made him when they were young, as they’d always wanted to see the Hugo in town, though it was too far to visit. The wagon was borrowed without permission from a local farmer. Voyta and his friends used to drag it up the hill and ride down in it until they crashed it and broke it.

Voyta is surprised to hear that someone was living there, but he wants to hear what he said. When Henry explains, Voyta is evasive at first saying he’s sure that Burkhard has killed many men with the same name as him. Henry pushes and Voyta admits that he used to meet up at that dugout with his two childhood friends – Libor and Voyta.

After Voyta died, our Voyta took his name. As for the name he was born with, he claims to have forgotten it. The painter feels responsible for his friend’s death. The real Voyta had joined with Burkhard and Libor and the painter tried to get him to stop. When Burkhard found out, he made an example out of Voyta for anyone who might try to betray him.

It’s a lot of information for Henry to take in all at once, but Voyta still has one more favour to ask of him.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Voyta and ask him about his past to start this quest. He will direct you to a dugout north-east of Maleshov. Head there and talk to the man who lives there. The way your conversation goes will have implications for later in the quest.

He will initially be hostile,you can surrender to him or else subdue and and allow him to surrender and he will speak with you. Ask him about himself and he will give you his broken sword.

For the achievement Curiosity Killed the Cat. You can reforge the sword and make him take it back using a hard speech check. After having done so, he will hang himself in a few days, getting the achievement:

Main article: Madman's longsword

- Fastening material × 1

- Frankfurt steel × 3

- Madman's broken sword × 1

If you would like him to live, you can investigate the dugout. The areas you can investigate are the noose on the tree outside, a plate with a wolf's heart inside the dugout next to the bed, two wooden swords on top of a barrel inside the hut, the dugout’s rotting roof, a wolf's pelt near the rotting roof, a broken wagon behind the tree, a scarecrow on an anthill, and the latrine behind the dugout.

With that, you can head back to Voyta in town, you’ll have to pass an easy speech check to get some more specific details about how he got his name. Finally you’ll learn something about his past, ending the quest.

Note: If you tell Voyta that Libor hanged himself, Voyta will refuse to talk to you for two in-game days.

## Man's Best Friend

Man's Best Friend is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You found and saved Mutt.

## Acquisition

The Man's Best Friend achievement is unlocked by completing the side quest Mutt, which allows Henry to reunite with his loyal canine companion.

While regaining Mutt may seem straightforward, the quest is long and can be especially challenging for lower-level players. Nonetheless, Mutt provides valuable support in combat and is worth recovering as soon as possible.

## Tips

The quest becomes available shortly after the prologue, once the open world is fully accessible.

To complete it, follow these steps:

- Speak to Herbwoman Bozhena and ask her about Mutt.

- Find and assist Siegfried, the shepherd located north of Tachov.

- Talk to the fisherman at the southern shore of Vidlak Pond, far west of Tachov.

- Visit Zlata at the Gamekeeper Vostatek's lodge, east of the Vidlak Pond, and begin the side quest Lackey.

- Complete it and then speak to Vostatek again to ask about your dog.

- Travel to the eastern cliffs near the riverbank west of Semine, just east of the bathing spot below Rocktower Pond. A cutscene will trigger upon approach, reuniting Henry with Mutt.

Or simply head down to the endpoint and pick up Mutt, that works too.

Note: During the cutscene, Henry will be ambushed by a pack of wolves. If you are pursuing the Lent achievement (which requires not killing or eating animals), flee the area the moment the cutscene ends, Mutt will follow you.

## Mandelina von Grolle

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Mandelina von Grolle is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

She married her husband Gotzlin von Grolle as a young and pious girl. She quickly became disillusioned with her marriage, as he revealed himself to have an inclination to drinking and eating good food. Sometime later, her son, Hendl von Grolle, was born. When he achieved adulthood, she swore to protect his immortal soul from the same fate as his father's. She, her servant Servant Thaddeus, and perhaps his predecessor, killed, or tried to kill every woman who would threaten her son's piety.

When Henry of Skalitz came to Kuttenberg, he was tasked to investigate a murder of a friend of a friend. He, Katherine, and Lumir connected the murders to the von Grolle household.

Depending on Henry's success in the investigation, Mandelina continued to protect her son's immortal soul by killing innocent women around Kuttenberg, was sent to live out her days peacefully in the countryside, or was killed by Katherine in a confrontation.

### Associated quests

- The Fifth Commandment

## Manka

Manka is the daughter of the innkeepers in Tachov in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Like most, Manka grew up in her hometown and her parents expected her to live out her days there. When Manka became involved with Henik though, this greatly upset her parents, as they believed Henik would be just like his brothers and one day leave the town and never return. Despite her parents being adamant that the relationship was over, Manka secretly still saw Henik when they could find time to be alone together. They were not particularly careful all the time though, as one time they went to a dance in Troskowitz and Manka's parents found out and were furious over it.

## Margaret

Margaret is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Margaret appeared to be a career criminal who often used her status as a young woman to her advantage in duping those around her into believing she was more docile than she truly was.

She tried to rob a local miller and was captured by him. He placed her in his shed to keep her contained until he could fetch the catchpole, but was set free by Henry whom she told she was an abused otung wife of the miller's and she was afraid he was going to kill her. Upon being set free, she ran off, leaving Henry with the bag.

Sometime later, Margaret found her way to the Pschitoky Wagoners' Inn where she was living as a beggar trying to get her next score. There she met Henry again and told him she needed money to support a friend of hers along with that friend's young baby who would suffer without her.

In order to get money for them, she wanted to rob a rich burgher in Kuttenberg and told Henry that said burgher had murdered his first wife to take a younger wife with a larger dowry. This story turned out to be a fabrication, something Henry may or may not have discovered. She convinced Henry to help her with the scheme to extort the burgher and later attempted to lull Henry into a false sense of security to steal money from him as well.

After dealing with Henry, she went back on the road.

### Associated quests

- Damsel in Distress

- Victimised

## Marika

Marika is a young Romani woman and the only daughter of the leader of the nomads who recently made camp in the Trosky region.

The voivode notes that out of his three children, Marika is the one most like him and, if she'd been a boy, she'd have been the one to inherit his position as leader of their clan. However, Marika notes she herself doesn't want that even if she could be voivode (or a voivode's wife).

## Biography

Despite being a nomad, Marika felt trapped by regularly moving instead of perhaps one day settling down, having a family, and not travelling ever again. While her brother, Tibor, understood this, their father didn't take Marika's wish for a permanent home seriously.

When her father set up camp in the area, Marika ran into a local boy from Semine, Bohush. The two started dating, despite Bohush's mother's disapproval. Meanwhile, Marika's father eventually pushed that the two needed to get married or Bohush should pay, as was their custom, so he sent such a request via a messenger to Bohush.

However, Bohush and Marika were actually out together that day, so instead the messenger ran into Bohush's mother, who immediately laughed off the proposal and insulted the voivode. In turn, Marika's brothers, Gejza and Tibor, set off into town to confront the villagers for their insults while Bohush was there.

Things suddenly took a turn for the worse and in the commotion, Gejza was killed, Tibor taken captive, and Bohush stabbed. Marika managed to find her boyfriend and quickly took him to a hiding spot in Apollonia to recover. However, to try and help protect them, when she ran away from the Nomads' Camp, she also took a letter of safe conduct that was in her father's possession in case she'd need a bargaining chip.

If Miri Fajta is completed and she's given the amulet:

Clever like her father though, when Henry found her and offered to assist, she eventually proposed her idea: for Henry to wager the letter against her father's amulet. If Henry won, then the voivode would have to come see her and hand it over to her himself. Henry did so, winning the bet and, as promised, her father met her in the cave with the still recovering Bohush. As they talked, Marika noted the amulet wasn't just for her, but for her and Bohush, to save his life, revealing her plan all along: by saving someone's life as per their custom, they'd become part of the family as well. Realizing the clever plan his daughter just pulled off, the voivode laughed over how she had outwitted him. He then apologized for his earlier, stubborn behaviour and welcomed Marika and Bohush back to the camp. Marika made it clear though that when the nomads decided to pack up and leave again, she'll be allowed to decide for herself if she wanted to stay or go with them.

### Associated quest

- Miri Fajta

## Mark of the Brotherhood

Mark of the Brotherhood is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is available following Ars Dimicatoria.

## Description

Menhard would finally like to lead the Kuttenberg swordfighting brotherhood as he should, but to do so he needs to get the guild sword back.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Menhard at the sword hall and ask him what he’s doing next. He’ll ask you for help getting the guild sword back from Emmeram, as he finds it too awkward to go himself.

You’ll find Emmeram at his shop during the day, the butcher’s near the town hall. Talk to him and he’ll tell you he actually doesn’t have the sword any more – he threw it in the rubbish in anger after losing the duel, which he greatly regrets.

Said rubbish can be found just outside the city walls through a small gate a block west of Ruthard Palace. There are three bushes in the area to check, each guarded by a wild dog. The first is just to your left as you pass through the gate, the next is downhill from there, and the third is to the right of the second. The sword will not be in any of them, unfortunately.

Return to Emmeram and confront him. He’ll relent and give you the sword – in two pieces. You have to opportunity to fight him if you wish.

Alternatively, you can pickpocket the sword from him.

Regardless, with broken sword in-hand, go see Menhard. To repair the sword they’ll need a blacksmith and Menhard happens to know one, you! As such, you'll have to craft a new guild longsword, the recipe will be available to you automatically.

Main article: Guild longsword

- Broken guild longsword × 1

- Fastening material × 1

- Toledo steel × 2

If needed, you can purchase crafting materials from the various armour and sword smiths in town. Once you have all the materials, head to the nearest forge to make the new guild sword then head on back to Menhard again.

Hand the sword back over to Menhard to end the quest.

## Marksman's hook gun

Marksman's hook gun is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as the ranged weapon type.

## Description

The hook gun is a much more massive weapon than the handgonne. The barrel is fitted with a hook on the underside, which serves to wedge the weapon behind an obstacle and limit recoil when fired. This particular piece is cast from bronze by a master gunsmith, therefore can be fired repeatedly without breaking.

## Acquisition

One can be found at the Locked dugout point of interest north-west of Old Kutna.

## Markvart von Aulitz

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

I am Sir Markvart von Aulitz, I come in the name of Sigismund of Luxembourg, King of Hungary and Croatia, to restore order in the name of his brother, King Wenceslas IV.

—Markvart to Sir Divish of Talmberg

Sir Markvart von Aulitz is a main character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance, and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He is a German noble in the service of King Sigismund of Hungary. His actions directly cause the events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance. In KCD 2, Markvart died in 1403; the Prague camp.

He serves as a major antagonist in Kingdom Come: Deliverance, the DLC A Woman's Lot, and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

In KCD 2, Markvart dies alone as a result of a neck wound sustained during the earlier siege (succumbing to his injuries that very night).

## Biography

### Events of Kingdom Come Deliverance

After King Sigismund of Hungary kidnapped his half-brother Wenceslas IV and forced him to abdicate, he invaded the Kingdom of Bohemia at the head of a massive army, composed mostly by mercenaries such as Cumans. One of his most trustworthy men was Markvart, who led the attack on Kuttenberg.

Later, in the spring of 1403, King Sigismund launched an attack the settlement of Silver Skalitz, either because of the wealth found in the surrounding silver mines, or because the Lord of Skalitz, Sir Radzig Kobyla, who remained loyal to King Wenceslas, instead of swearing fealty to Sigismund.

Markvart attacks Silver Skalitz

Once again, the attack was led by Markvart, who, together with a Cuman cavalry squadron, broke down the gates of Skalitz and began slaughtering all the inhabitants. Among the victims of the slaughter were Henry's mother and father. Martin was killed by Markvart's own hand upon seeing his men having trouble in dealing with him, and Martin's wife was overwhelmed by the Cumans while Henry watched in horror.

With the village destroyed, Markvart and the Cumans mercenaries approached the Skalitz Castle, where Sir Radzig and a few citizens managed to take shelter. Luckily for Radzig, a storm blew in, and the enemy were forced to set up camp, waiting for the storm to pass before they could begin their siege. Radzig and the survivors managed to escape from the castle without alerting the enemy.

Divish negotiates with Markvart

The following day, finding Skaltiz castle empty, Markvart put it to the torch and set off through the Skalitz-Sasau region in pursuit of Sir Radzig. He brought the army to nearby Talmberg, where he and Lord Divish had a polite but tense exchange. He asked Lord Divish if he was loyal to his new King, Sigismund, and Divish tactfully replied that he had no wish to become embroiled in affairs that would not benefit him.

Markvart was not exactly pleased with this answer, and questioned him as to the location of Radzig, who he claimed was a traitor using the King's silver to fund an insurrection. Divish lied and claimed they had not seen the refugees, while knowing they had passed by and continued south to Rattay in the hope that the acting Lord there, Sir Hanush of Leipa, could give them shelter.

Markvart looks back as the army moves past Talmberg

Markvart did not seem to believe Divish, but recognized that he was correct in saying that only a fool would abandon a defensible castle like Skalitz to hide in an indefensible location like Talmberg. In addition, Talmberg had nothing of value, and Divish was evidently not going to make trouble for the new King.

Sigismund and Markvart ordered the army to move along, much to the relief of the people. As the army set off in search of its prey, Markvart looked over his shoulder to Talmberg, where Henry was looking back at him.

### Events of Kingdom Come Deliverance II

Markvart and his troops brought the Finger of God cannon to Trosky at the behest of Otto von Bergow, the lord of the region. This delivery came at a time when von Bergow had discovered that the bandits who had been tormenting his men for so long were holed up at Nebakov Fortress. Markvart lead his troops there to assault the fortress which was successful, allowing them to take Hans Capon hostage and leave Henry, Jan Zizka, and Godwin to Istvan Toth's interrogation.

Markvart went to Maleshov with von Bergow and their hostage where they started to discuss their next moves. The major force of him men congregated at Sigismund's camp near Opatowitz, where the cannon was stored. Sometime later, news reached them that Toth had been killed and the captives had escaped. This news greatly upset Toth's right-hand man Erik, sending him into an emotional spiral which Markvart commented on as being a shame.

Markvart then left Maleshov to go to Kuttenberg for the city council meeting which would also be attended by Sigismund. He was a silent observer for most of the meeting, only speaking up once the council had adjourned and the only people left in the room were he, Sigismund, and the wait staff, including Henry in disguise. In this more intimate meeting, Markvart spoke to Sigismund about plans that had been uncovered regarding a meeting of dissenters at Raborsch as well as concern regarding the city's Jewish population's support for Wenceslas. Sigismund then gave consent for an attack on both groups.

Marvart then remained by Sigismund's side until news came that there was a rebellion in Hungary and the king would have to return to reclaim his own throne. The vast majority of Sigismund's troops left the region with him, while Markvart lead the remaining Praguer forces towards Suchdol where the Wenceslas supporters had congregated following their infiltration and heist of the Italian Court where they managed to steal the royal silver. He was accompanied by von Bergow, who had recently freed himself from captivity in Suchdol and Vauquelin Brabant who had recently betrayed the Suchdol defenders while still in Kuttenberg.

Along with von Bergow, Markvart approached the walls of Suchdol to attempt a parlay. The defenders were unwilling to negotiate, knowing that they would not be able to get a good outcome that way. They were so against talking that Dry Devil, heavily inebriated, interrupted talks by shooting Markvart in the chest with a crossbow.

Having suffered this injury, Markvart had to return to his post in the former tavern of Suchdol for treatment while von Bergow left the area. This left Brabant in charge while Markvart convalesced. His injury was quite severe, and he did not respond well to the treatment that was available to him. This left him hobbled and feverish, waiting to die.

Weeks into the siege, he may have been visited by Henry who had escaped from the besieged fortress in an attempt to send word to their allies. Markvart remembered him from Skalitz, offering condolences for the loss of his parents and reiterating that war has no good choices. He expressed to Henry his feeling of battle as a necessary evil and his own want to remember those whose lives he'd taken. At the end of their conversation, Markvart asked that Henry kill him, not wanting to die of illness and from his injuries when he could die a more noble death.

This request may or may not have been granted. Either way, Markvart did not survive the night.

## Codex Entry

Sir Markvart von Aulitz

1360/70 - 27 December 1402

He was the Hetman or Governor of Prague, who, much like those members of the nobility disgruntled with the reign of Wenceslas IV, saw in Sigismund of Luxembourg a better potential King.

His motivation, however, had more to do with money and power - nothing was to come his way from Wenceslas, while helping Sigismund promised a better position in the future. Therefore, it was not difficult for him to change sides and in 1402, at the call of King Sigismund, he joined the siege of Kuttenberg and the surrounding area as the leader of the Prague troops.

He died from an arrow wound sustained during the siege of Suchdol, a fortress defended by the Kuttenberg mint master, Peter of Pisek.

For the purposes of our game, however, we postponed his death for a year.

—Codex entry: Sir Markvart von Aulitz (KCD2)

## Martin's Dream

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Martin's Dream is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It's the 5th quest in the Legacy of the Forge DLC.

## Description

I’m trying to find my father’s friend, the former journeyman, Standa the Fly, to learn more about the repair of the Kuttenberg astronomical clock.

## Walkthrough

After helping Klaus Eichner with the guild documents, he’ll tell you that last he heard Standa was working at the Horschan mines as a blacksmith, giving you your first lead.

### Find Standa

Head to Grund or Horschan and go towards the mines. You can ask the blacksmith working there if he’s Standa (he’s not); he will tell you that Standa now works as a regular miner after an injury made him give up the forge.

The miners' living space is just north of the forge. You’ll find Standa sitting near a fire on the northern edge of the camp. Talk to him and he’ll tell you he owes money to one of the mine guards, Leech. The guard says if he won’t pay late interest he’ll break Standa’s arms. He wants you to deal with the guard for him.

Leech patrols the area. Talk to him and ask after Standa. You can ask why he’s fleecing Standa, pay the debt of 2400 , with a very hard speech check get him to forget the shoddy interest, pickpocket the contract off of him and bring it to Standa, or simply kill him. You can also challenge him to a horse race which will earn you the achievement Racing the Leech, but you will bet 500 . Once you deal with Leech, he will give you the promissory note and promise to leave Standa alone in future.

Head back to Standa and let him know the good news. Upon learning you’re the new master of Shkoda’s forge, he’ll insist on travelling to see Magdalena to apologize about the past. You can ask him about the clock, but he’s not ready to talk yet. You can fast travel with him back to the forge to continue the quest or else tell him you’ll meet him there later.

### Head to the forge

Either fast travel back immediately with Standa or else head to the forge when you are ready to continue. After a conversation with Magdalena, Standa can join the forge as an armourer with an invitation, and will direct you to recover the clockwork heart of the broken clock, now in the possession of a burgher called Vetter.

Vetter works near the Rathaus, last door on the gallery in the courtyard, and lives opposite.

Note: Although you can send Standa away, he is very useful to have around. Upgrade your forge to have an armourer’s station and you’ll be able to give him recipes found in In the Service of the Guild for extra revenue.

### Get the heart

Head to the Rathaus scribe shop and talk to Vetter. You can offer to purchase the mechanism for 7000 or you can try to tell him its true purpose. A very hard speech check allows you to try and tell him it’s the work of the devil which will cause him to offer it to you for 3500 .

To convince him of the mechanism’s true purpose you can try a hard craftsmanship check or a very hard speech check. Passing the craftsmanship check will lower his price to 3500 . Passing the speech check will get him to give it to you for free.

If you are unable to pass any of the checks, and are unwilling to pay up, you can steal the heart from him. It’s kept in his home, upstairs. Head up to his bedroom on the right and you should see it on a cabinet near the windows. Note: the entire upstairs is considered a private area, so it is best to head in at night and with stealth.

Alternatively, the Adorned Axe can be traded for the the heart, gained in Trosky during the The Axe from the Lake task. If you stole Rikonaris' sabre after completion of The Voivode's Curse, also in the Trosky region, you can also exchange it.

Once you have the heart, head back to your forge. If you want, you can tell Standa about it, but this won’t affect much. Place the mechanism on the table next to the forge, it has the sketches for the rest of the clock repair on it as well, ending the quest and beginning Old Plans.

## Master Menhart's longsword

Master Menhart's longsword is a unique melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

## Description

Long sword of the swordmaster Menhart from Frankfurt. According to his own words, he received it from his teacher the day he became a sword master. The weapon itself honours both the bearer and the maker. Truly a masterpiece!

## Acquisition

- Master Menhart's longsword is obtained as a reward for completing the side quest Ars Dimicatoria. To earn it, you must side with Menhard von Frankfurt through to the end.

## Master Nary

Master Nary is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Nary was named Emanuel after his paternal grandfather. He liked the name and thought it was a shame that he had forever been saddled with the nickname he is known by.

The nickname Nary was earned initially because of the strong family resemblance between him and his brother, Vashek. They were always mistaken for each other and Vashek got fed up and grew a beard. This didn’t help entirely, however, and one night they came across a drunk who stopped them in the street to loudly proclaim he was seeing double. The drunk then noticed the beard and started screaming that he wasn’t seeing double after all as one man was hairy and the other, nary.

From that day on the name stuck, so much so that even Vashek started to be called Vashek Nary. More than that, their cousin started being called Little Nary as well.

He lived in Kuttenberg and worked as a judge for Popinjay shoots in the shooting range in Hoprink on the south-east end of the city.

## Master Schindel

Master Schindel is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Schindel was an academic based in Prague. He had many students all over and came to Kuttenberg on a visit. He was well-connected, staying with the city’s main scribe, Vetter.

One day, he visited the City bathhouse and while he was bathing, some of his prized possessions were stolen by a thief called Goatskin. Schindel was understandably upset, complaining to the owner of the bathhouse, Adam, and threatening to go to the city council if the situation could not be resolved.

Eventually, thanks to the combined effort of Adam and Henry, Schindel’s things were able to be recovered. Schindel was grateful to Henry, and let him know what the recovered items were and how they worked. He also offered Henry a strange note one of his students had given him, as he felt he did not have time to go running around town for no reason.

## Master Schindel's Toys

Master Schindel's Toys is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is only available during Into the Underworld.

## Description

A scholar named Johann Schindel was apparently robbed by Goatskin. If I get back his possessions, he’s sure to reward me.

## Walkthrough

During Into the Underworld, when at the City bathhouse looking for information on Goatskin’s whereabouts, speak with Bathhouse Madam Beata and then Bathhouse owner Adam. Adam wants to find Goatskin due to Goatskin’s propensity for robbing his customers. One such customer was Master Schindel – a visiting scholar from Prague who went straight to the city council with his complaint. Adam wants you to recover the stolen goods and save his reputation.

The next step is to find Goatskin, which overlaps with Into the Underworld. Once he’s been found, talk to him and ask about Schindel’s things. He will direct you to the Kuttenberg gallows where you’ll find a hanged man called Angel. In his inventory is a Map of Kuttenberg underground. This map will point to a hideout, indicated by the drawing of a goat’s head.

Make your way there, any entrance to the underground will connect, at the indicated spot you’ll find a tipped-over barrel with the goods inside. The items are an Astrolabe and the Livre du ciel et du monde.

Once you have the stolen goods, return them to Master Schindel. He will be in the house of Scribe Tietz Vetter, not far from the location of the cache. Hand them over and he’ll thank you, rewarding you with 225 groschen and a mysterious note written by one of his students.

## Master Voyta

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

With brush and paint, I bring beauty to where there was only emptiness.

Master Voyta (Czech: Mistr Vojtěch) is an eccentric painter from Kuttenberg, whom Henry encounters during his travels in the Trosky region. He is the central figure of the Brushes with Death expansion.

Though initially appearing as a peculiar artist muttering to a painted skull, Voyta reveals himself to be a troubled but earnest man haunted by past guilt and a desperate need for meaning in his work.

## Biography

### Trosky

Henry stumbles upon Voyta tied to a tree in the woods near the Trosky Castle, muttering to a painted skull and under threat from wolves - an encounter Henry narrowly prevents. After the rescue, Voyta introduces himself as a painter commissioned by Otto von Bergow to complete a variety of artistic work. He explains that he had gone for a walk to enjoy the scenery and clear his head, but was nearly struck by an arrow. The men responsible apologized and invited him to their camp, offering him wine to calm his nerves and suggesting a game of dice. However, one of them turned out to be a cheat. When Voyta confronted him, the other man struck him on the head. He later awoke tied to a tree. After recounting the incident, Voyta asks Henry to retrieve the set of brushes and dice that the pair stole from him.

Investigating the camp Voyta directed him to, Henry discovers that two wanderers, Four‑leaf Clovis and Yura, are responsible for the attack. When questioned about the incident, they claim that they tied up Voyta not because of the dice game, but because of the unsettling things he said. According to them, Voyta told Yura that someone was going to murder him, and that his painted skull had revealed this to him. Disturbed by the warning, Yura panicked and Clovis struck Voyta on the head. They insist they meant no real harm and assumed someone would eventually find and free him. Henry then retrieves the stolen brushes and dice and returns them to Voyta at his workshop in Trosky. If confronted about the discrepancy in his story, Voyta admits that he may have said something troubling, as he was not in the best state of mind at the time, and the two men overreacted. Brushing the matter aside, he rewards Henry with his personal set of dice for recovering the paintbrushes and offers to paint his shield free of charge whenever he wishes.

Voyta's speaking with the skull

Intrigued by the eccentric painter, Henry asks if Voyta needs any further help. Voyta reveals that his lifelong wish is to create a painting so profound that his name will be remembered for generations. To achieve this, he is searching far and wide for a source of inspiration. He believes one such source could be an old shrine dedicated to the pagan god Veles. However, Voyta does not know the shrine's location and asks for Henry's help in finding it. He suggests speaking to an old woman named Kvyetoslava, who may know where it can be found. He tried to find the shrine himself but couldn't get anything out of her on account of her failing memory. With Kvyetoslava's help, Henry eventually locates the hidden shrine and brings Voyta there. He spends many hours painting at the shrine while Henry dozes off under a nearby tree. However, once the painting is finished, Voyta does not appear convinced that it is his long-sought masterpiece. On the contrary, he seems more troubled than inspired. The place, he says, spoke to him of the shrine's history, of Veles and of the underworld. He departs for his workshop, but not before asking Henry to visit him again soon - he has other work for him in mind.

When Henry visits him later, Voyta reveals that he wants to attempt something unconventional: to create a paint using an egg no one has tried before, a basilisk egg. Henry is skeptical, but Voyta persuades him to pursue it, if not for the reward, then at least out of curiosity. Henry eventually procures the egg, laid by a black cockerel and brooded by a toad. Upon receiving it, Voyta quickly dismisses Henry, explaining that he needs peace and quiet for the delicate process. When prodded, he admits he does not expect the paint itself to be miraculous. What matters to his potential clients is the story behind it.

Voyta's drawing at Veles's shrine

The next time Henry visits Voyta, the painter asks him to examine a sword he recently purchased with the last few groschen he had. He even admits to painting a lewd picture above the local blacksmith's bed as part of the payment. Voyta explains that he is now ready for the final task he must complete in the Trosky region: a duel to the death. He reveals that he has planned to confront and fight a bandit named Burkhard, an old acquaintance from his past, in order to find peace of mind. When Voyta discovered that Burkhard was in the area, his first instinct was to flee. However, while attempting to leave the region, he was nearly struck by an arrow - revealing that his earlier tale about taking a peaceful stroll was fabricated. Ever since, he has been plagued by an overwhelming voice in his mind whispering, "Burkhard must die! He must die!" The voice has haunted him to the point that he can no longer sleep, eat, or focus on his art.

If Henry presses him further, asking why he is only now confronting Burkhard after knowing him for so long, Voyta confesses that he had already tried turning to unchristian methods to rid himself of the torment. The shrine and the egg were never about artistic experimentation, but rather a desperate attempt to silence his inner demons. At the shrine of Veles, he prayed not only to the pagan god, but also to the Devil, after feeling abandoned by the Christian god. And the basilisk egg was part of a ritual he performed, along with a prayer to the Devil. Voyta sincerely apologizes to Henry for leading him on.

Voyta's "Judgement Day"

But despite his efforts, the burden remains. With no other recourse, he believes that an honorable duel is the only way to put an end to the torment. Henry, however, objects, pointing out that there would be nothing fair about such a duel - Burkhard is a seasoned fighter, while Voyta's real skill lies in painting. Henry offers to face Burkhard in his place, and after some hesitation, Voyta agrees. His only request is that Henry spare Burkhard's gang. Voyta explains that Burkhard often recruits young, aimless men who lack direction. They are not truly evil, only lost, and Voyta knows this from personal experience he refuses to tell about. After Henry deals with Burkhard, Voyta does not feel the sense of relief he had hoped for. He is genuinely proud if Henry chose to spare the gang, though visibly saddened if they were killed along with Burkhard. Once again, Henry tries to get Voyta to open up, but Voyta deflects his questions. He says he would feel more comfortable speaking freely at home and invites Henry to visit his workshop in Kuttenberg.

### Kuttenberg

Unfinished masterpiece

Sometime later, fate brings Henry to Kuttenberg, giving him the opportunity to take Voyta up on his invitation. Voyta is glad to see him and excitedly shares news about his latest commission - an altar for the Sedletz Monastery. The abbot recently received a Saint Vitus relic from King Sigismund and intends to redesign half the chapel for it. Voyta believes this could finally be his chance to create a true masterpiece. Unfortunately, his joy is short-lived. Bellissimo, a former friend and now a rival, appears and arrogantly boasts that he managed to steal the commission right out from under Voyta's nose. As Henry investigates, he discovers that Bellissimo agreed to paint the altar for free, offering his work in exchange for absolution from the monastery for his many sins. Determined to reclaim the project, Henry and Voyta come up with a plan: to convince Bellissimo that the Devil himself has come to claim his soul. Henry gets Bellissimo drunk enough to fall for the ruse, while Voyta crafts a terrifying costume and transforms Bellissimo's workshop with torches and visions of Hell. The trick worked - Bellissimo was thoroughly shaken, and in the end, the commission was returned to Voyta.

While Voyta continues work on his opus magnum, Henry helps him wrap up the commissions he previously started. Voyta takes care of a simpler task himself, collecting payment for a signboard he painted for a local armourer. However, he sends Henry to resolve a more complicated matter. The bailiff of Pschitoky has refused to pay the agreed price for the decoration of a newly built fortress, which was a valuable lapis lazuli stone, the source of the finest blue pigment. In the meantime, Henry continues encouraging Voyta to open up about his past, and this time, he succeeds. Before discussing it, however, Voyta asks Henry to visit an old dugout northeast of Maleshov, a place that once meant a great deal to him. There, Henry encounters Libor, an old friend of Voyta's. Libor is barely lucid and clearly traumatized by what happened to their mutual friend.

When Henry returns to Voyta, the painter is visibly surprised - he truly expected the dugout to be abandoned. With a heavy heart, he finally opens up about his past: the name "Voyta" was never his. It belonged to the friend who was killed long ago, and he took it as his own out of guilt and grief, feeling personally responsible for what happened. He asks Henry for another last favor - to visit his friend's grave and say a prayer for him, since it's likely been neglected for years. Voyta admits he cannot bring himself to face it yet, but hopes that if Henry describes how it looks, he might find the courage to go himself one day.

The painted skull

The grave turns out to be overgrown and unkept. To honor the memory of the real Voyta, Henry clears the weeds and offers a heartfelt prayer for both the dead man's soul and the painter's. At this point, Henry may choose to dig up the grave. Inside, he discovers that the body is missing its skull, which is the very one the painter has been speaking to. He also finds a carving on a nearby tree with the initials "R+V+L". The "V" stands for Voyta and the "L" for Libor, so the painter's real name must have started with an "R." When Henry returns, the painter admits that so much time has passed he no longer remembers what the "R" stood for, and asks Henry to continue calling him Voyta. If Henry confronts him about the disturbed grave, Voyta is furious at first. However, if Henry presses further, he confesses that he was the one who dug it up long ago and has carried the skull with him ever since, believing that his friend had been calling to him.

With the truth out in the open, Voyta's mental state begins to deteriorate. He now trusts Henry enough to ask for help with something more personal: gathering ingredients for a Mandrake decoction. Years ago, he bought the recipe from a wandering herbalist, and it's the only thing that seems to quiet the inner voice that torments him. Meanwhile, Voyta's masterpiece nears completion - only the face of Saint Vitus and the wooden altar figurines remain. The figurines should have been finished long ago, but with Voyta still unwell, Henry offers to check in with the carpenter responsible for them. After tracking down the final statuette, Henry returns it to Voyta.

### Finale

As the painting nears its end, Voyta slips into a strange, unsettled mood. The decoction has helped, but not by much. He finds himself conflicted about the very goal he has spent his life chasing. Part of him wants to honor the real Voyta's memory, but another part fears the inspiration for the painting came not from within, but from the Devil. In a fit of paranoia, he even begins to question Henry's motives - what if Henry was sent by the Devil too? Henry manages to calm him down, at least for the moment. Still uncertain, Voyta asks for Henry's opinion: what should he do with the painting? Henry now has two choices.

If Henry encourages Voyta to finish his work:

Voyta's finished masterpiece

Voyta turns back to his work while Henry goes to fetch the monks from the monastery. By the time they return, the face of Saint Vitus is finally complete. This time, however, Voyta draws inspiration not from the skull of his dead friend but from Henry himself. The help and support Henry has given him have allowed Voyta to confront, if not silence, the guilt that has haunted him for years. The voice of his old friend is still there, but it has quieted.

With a sense of peace, Voyta hands the finished painting over to the monks. He tells Henry that he knows it will not bring the real Voyta back, but he wanted to create something in his name. It was his way of giving his friend more time in this world, and in a way, it worked. Now that the burden has lifted, he hopes to live a little for himself. What he enjoyed most while working on the painting was all the places it took him, and he hopes to keep traveling. He mentions Rychnov as a possible next destination.

At last, Voyta is ready to part with the skull. He asks Henry to return it to the grave and grant his friend eternal rest. When Henry reburies it, laying the skull where it belongs, the painter is deeply grateful: "Thank you again, my friend. You saved two Voytas from eternal damnation."

If Henry convinces Voyta to destroy it:

Voyta's masterpiece, destroyed

At first, Voyta is appalled by the mere suggestion. But Henry argues that Voyta spent his whole life chasing a grand masterpiece, only for it to destroy him. All Henry sees when he looks at the painting is Voyta's suffering. Eventually, Voyta gives in. The two leave the city and burn the painting together. They sit by the fire and watch it turn to ash.

Voyta admits that he does feel lighter, and the voice of his dead friend has gone quiet - for now. Still, he worries about what might happen in a year or a decade. Despite that, he decides that hiding away in his workshop is behind him. He wants to spend more time among people, especially after seeing how much good it did him to be around Henry. Notably, he still keeps the real Voyta's skull.

## Trivia

- Voyta has a deep affection for cats. At his home in Kuttenberg, he cares for three named Adela, Agnes, and Daniela. He also enjoys the company of several cats that live in the loft of Trosky castle, where he has set up his workshop.

## Master of Masters

Master of Masters is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You beat Zavish in three disciplines.

## Acquisition

The Master of Masters achievement is unlocked by defeating Zavish of Garbow in three different combat disciplines: polearm, one-handed weapon with shield, and longsword. Zavish can typically be found at the dice table in Sigismund's camp, located west of the Field chapel.

## Tips

- Before you can challenge Zavish, you must first start the side quest Lost Honour. This quest is triggered through a random encounter called, which may occur during fast travel or travelling between Horschan and Miskowitz during daylight hours. During this encounter, you'll meet Jezhek of Holohlavy.

- You can either pass a speech check or defeat Jezhek in combat (causing him to surrender).

- Afterward, offer to help him, which will begin the side quest Lost Honour.

- This quest is easily missable. Additionally, because it is tied to Sigismund's camp, it must be completed before the second point of no return in the Oratores main quest in Kuttenberg. Failing to complete it before then will lock you out of the achievement unless you reload an earlier save.

- During the Lost Honour quest Henry needs to pass a speech check with intimidation or warfare, after which Zavish will propose a three part duel. Stealing the armour and horse will lock you out of the achievment.

- It is recommended to save between duels and apply poison on your polearm, short sword and long sword.

## Master of the Blacksmiths' Guild

Master of the Blacksmiths' Guild is an achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You passed the Trial and became a Master blacksmith.

## Acquisition

The Master of the Blacksmiths' Guild achievement is obtained during the quest Adept, once you pass the trial to be accepted into the blacksmithing guild. It is tied to the story progression and can't be missed.

## Tips

The Verbal Test

- What's the final step before completing a piece? - Quenching

- How can you tell you're making progress while forging? - By the shape

- Are sparks while forging good or bad? - That depends

- What colour is a properly heated workpiece? - Straw yellow

- Why do blacksmiths whistle while they work? - To keep rhythm

- What is the motto of the Blacksmith guild? - Good work at a fair price

- What does the craft of forging resembles? - Act of creation

The Practical Test

- After answering the questions you'll be given materials and the sketch for the Blacksmiths' guild longsword. Making one of the ⁠ Medium quality is enough, you don't need to be absolutely perfect.

## Master's handgonne

Master's handgonne is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as the ranged weapon type.

## Description

A handgonne is a firearm that uses gunpowder to shoot small pieces of metal or stone. A thick metal barrel with a handle is attached to a wooden stock, similar to a spear, for example. Fire through the powder stopper detonates the main charge in the barrel and shoots the projectile out. It is fired by a lit cord, a red-hot iron wire or in a worst case scenario, a burning stick. This handgonne has a barrel forged from iron and is therefore less durable than those cast from bronze. Any living being hit with this weapon is sure to no longer be living.

## Masterpiece

## Description

You finished Brushes with Death.

To unlock the Masterpiece achievement complete the Unveiling quest.

## Materia Prima

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Materia Prima is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It's given by Kreyzl if he's sought out for assistance to gain access to the wedding.

## Walkthrough

After talking to Kreyzl at his mill about a job, he'll assign you to carry a number of sacks from the barn to the wagon. The sacks are in the open barn area to the west, right next to the locked chest. As Henry carries each one, he'll make quite a few remarks that something is off here and that the bags are awfully heavy for flour. Eventually, it'll cut to where one of the bags rips, revealing small, black, metal pebbles, just as Kreyzl approaches if you're done.

Realizing the cat is out of the bag, he'll reveal it's part of something he plans to experiment with, but he needs help stealing something for his plans. If you're up for it, agree and he'll ask you to steal a document from the Rathaus in Troskowitz. You can then ask him about how to do the job, and he'll point you to recovering some of his inconspicuous clothes from the bathhouse at Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn as well as ways to practice lockpicking, takedowns, and pickpocketing with one of the hired hands.

The chest if you want to practice is in the barn near the sacks and will automatically re-lock each time you unpick it, allowing one to build up a low lockpicking skill fast without issue. For takedowns and pickpocketing, go talk to Hensel, who'll take you to the same location in the barn to practice on him.

### Prep work

Go to the bathhouse, where you can either snoop around or talk to Dorothy about Kreyzl's clothes. If you talk to her, you can offer to buy them or persuade her to give them to you by either implying the clothes are cursed or offering to be loud publicity for her laundering services. If you want to steal them, sneak upstairs to find the chest here, above the building's entrance. You'll find a number of clothing items as well as a few miscellaneous things.

If you want an easier time figuring out how to find the document, go to Zinek in the stocks in Troskowitz or across from the mill to ask him about it. He'll reveal it was confiscated as the guards mistook it as stolen property and likely still in the locked chest in the guard house. You'll either need to try lockpicking it or pickpocket a guard for the key. Zinek will tell you about the key he used and subsequently lost while being held in the cell right in front of the target chest (if you pick it up, Kreyzl will ask for it along with the document).

### Get the document

Once ready, head out to guard house's underground. Going through the house itself takes a while. From the outside can be tricky as a guard stands here at the stairs that go down, though he will occasionally move from it, sometimes giving just enough time to sneak down. Alternatively, you could just drop down. Behind the locked door in the middle of the stairs is a hidden book on strength. Another guard is in the room at the bottom, though throwing a couple stones will be more than enough to access either the lost key or the chest. Remember to hold E to empty out the chest and close it. On occasion, the door here may already be left open, allowing one to sneak in without issue. Be careful leaving to not get caught, and make your way back to Kreyzl.

Kreyzl will be happy you got it, though he'll get lost in thought as he goes on about alchemy and golems. It'll then complete the quest before going into the next one: Forbidden Fruit. He'll also reward you for both getting the document and the sacks you carried, including the skill book, As Quiet as a Cat I.

## Objectives

- Carry the sacks of flour to the wagon.

- Obtain some thieves' clothing.

- Practice lockpicking.

- Practice takedowns and pickpocketing.

## Matthew the Collector

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Matthew the Collector is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Matthew was a member of the Dry Devil's band before Dry Devil was taken into custody in Kuttenberg. Following the break-up of the band, Matthew found a group of men to follow him and set up raids along the roadsides, pretending to be a royal tax collector and extorting people for their money or their lives.

At some point, he stole a valuable book from Sedletz which was reported across the region. The bailiff of Miskowitz, Crux, put a bounty on his head, requesting that whoever fulfilled the bounty bring him the book as proof.

Eventually, Henry came looking for him to ask if he was interested in returning to Dry Devil’s side now that he had been freed. Matthew was not interested in the slightest, having found a better situation where he was in charge and making a lot of money. Nothing could convince him to return.

Henry could then let him go, or else kill him. Either way, the book could be recovered and given to Crux. Matthew was willing to part with it in exchange for getting the bailiff off his back.

Afterwards, he returned to his usual routine. If left alive, Henry could visit him for pointers regarding his best-honed skills.

## Menhard von Frankfurt

Menhard von Frankfurt is a master of the longsword.

## Stats

### Kingdom Come: Deliverance

|

|
Menhard of Frankfurt

|
1

1

16

## Biography

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance

Menhard appears as a semi-regular fighter in the Rattay Tourney.

### Events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

The master swordsman was given a charter by King Wenceslas IV to travel to Kuttenberg to establish a swordfighting guild and teach the art of the longsword. Menhard was to stay in the city for three years, being paid an ample amount of gold until he selected one of the fellow fighters to lead the guild, after which he could return to Frankfurt. But before Menhard arrived, Wenceslas was imprisoned and a swordfighting brotherhood had already been established by Emmeram and Nicholas.

Menhard petitioned the town council about his charter, but it was rejected. Feeling wronged and that the decision was not just, he began with his companion, Arne, standing in the city market square in front of Boris's armour shop and challenging anyone worthy to face him in a longsword duel to prove who was the true master. This is where Henry met him.

At the conclusion of the duel, councillor Fridusch Kumel, along with Emmeram and Nicholas, angrily interrupted, stating that Menhard had no right to conduct swordfighting within city limits, as the brotherhood were the only ones to have that privilege. A confrontation commenced with Menhard challenging Nicholas, as the best fighter, but he was stopped by Fridusch. After the stand-off was diffused, Menhard invited Henry to discuss their business further at the Emperor Charles Tavern.

It was decided that Henry would steal the guild sword from the current brotherhood and post it at the Town Hall so that Menhard could challenge them to a duel for the rights to the operation of the brotherhood. Menhard and his group won the duel after a close call with Arne taking a head injury, and was finally granted the rights he was promised by the king.

## Mercenary Berta

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Mercenary Berta is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Berta worked as a mercenary in the employ of Urso von Morgenstern. Along with his employer, he came to the Devil's Den and participated in the ambush to steal the Finger of God from the Prauger forces.

Later, he also participated in the attack on Maleshov to capture Otto von Bergow where he was grievously injured. After the battle, he was taken to Suchdol along with the others. Despite being treated by Katherine, he succumbed to his wounds a day later.

- Dancing with the Devil

## Mercenary Lardy Peter

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Mercenary Lardy Peter is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Peter worked under Urso von Morgenstern as a mercenary.

When the group was hired by Vaquelin Brabant, Peter worked alongside the others to support Zizka’s band, helping to steal a cannon from the Prague militia and make a raid on the village and adjoined fortress of Maleshov. He also provided reinforcements and helped carry the silver stolen from the Italian Court to Ruthard Palace to load it onto wagons.

Ultimately, Brabant’s plan was to have them take off with the silver and betray Zizka’s band. This ploy was found out, and a fight broke out in which Peter lost his life along with most of his other allies.

### Associated Quests

- The Lion's Den

- Dancing with the Devil

- The Italian Job

## Merchant Jurg Thömel

Here in the village we don't care much for outsiders. If any do come, they better behave.

Merchant Jurg Thömel (Czech: Kupec Jurg Thömel) owns the general store in Troskowitz. He is the village's only full-time trader, as most others are craftsmen selling their own wares.

Thanks to his work, he's familiar with just about everyone in the village and can introduce Henry to the area.

## Involvement

Jurg Thömel lives on the farm to the left of the village rathaus together with his mother and the daughters from his late wife. He frequently travels as far as Turnov to purchase supplies, which he then brings back for the villagers.

A few days before Henry and Capon arrive in the region, he was returning with goods for the upcoming wedding at Semine. The groom’s father had ordered delicacies and spices for the wedding feast, while Tailor Bartoshek asked him to bring expensive fabrics for the occasion.

Unfortunately, on the way back his horse was spooked and the wagon tipped into the pond. Although he managed to salvage part of the cargo, the rest was lost. When Henry asks about it, the merchant is still angry about the loss.

Naturally, he was invited to the Semine wedding. There he can be seen chatting with his closest neighbour, Apothecary Emmerich, and even takes part in the duelling contest organised by Captain Gnarly. Although even during the competition he tries to pick up gossip, particularly how much old Semine paid for the wedding.

## Mesoles

Mesoles (Czech: Mezholezy) is a raided and abandoned village located southwest of Kuttenberg.

## Codex entry

A village 5 km southwest of Kuttenberg.

The first written mention of the village is from 1384, and then another from 1445, when the village was sold to the Sasau Monastery. Otherwise, all we know about the village is that in 1932, there were 192 inhabitants and the village had two inns and two blacksmiths, while in the earlier times, we have mentions of only 45 inhabitants.

## Mice

Mice is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

This side quest and its counterpart is essentially a number of pranks that two rivaling villages try to pull off on each other, based on a years-long feud over who owns a pasture that both settlements use. See Frogs for Zhelejov's pranks and Battle of the Frogs and Mice for the pasture outcome.

Note that this questline can get lengthy depending if you want to do all possible objectives before settling the pasture dispute. You also have the option to rat out the one asking you to pull the prank to the other, though in turn this just has them offer their own prank in turn. As you can do all pranks without revealing to either quest giver, rating one out would only give some reputation (which can easily be earned anyways by doing the pranks).

## Walkthrough

As part of their ongoing feud, Innkeeper Prochek in Tachov has a plan for pranking Old Olbram in Zhelejov, but he needs your help to pull it off. Olram, the largest landowner in Zhelejov, owns a prize white bull that is his pride & joy. Prochek wants you to paint the bull a different color - any color will do. The bull is quite large, so he also recommends you sedate it with something first and points you to Blacksmith Radovan for a potion that should do the trick.

Radovan is usually found at the forge across the road from Prochek's inn. If you inquire about the potion and you've already helped him around the forge, he'll give you the recipe for the Lullaby potion. Otherwise, it can be purchased. You'll need three potions to properly sedate the bull.

For the paint itself, you'll need to see Tailor Bartoshek in Troskowitz. When you ask about him dying his own fabric, he will offer to sell you the last of his black pigment for 60 groschen. Alternatively, you can strike up a conversation about the fine art of pigments. Listen to his entire monologue and he'll recognize you as a fellow artist, thus giving you the dye for free.

Travel to Zhelejov to find the target of your upcoming artistry. Olbram's place can be found on the northwest side of town. During the day, the white bull can be found grazing in the pen behind the barn but is usually accompanied by hired hands. At night, the bull is put to rest in the barn and a guard is posted. Wait until late afternoon/evening and find the watering trough inside the barn. Pour your lullaby potion into it. It will take a few hours to sedate the bull, so wait until after dark to come back.

As for the guard, you can try distracting him by throwing stones or having Mutt bark. Otherwise, you can sneak into the house and go upstairs to the attic where you'll find access to the barn that way. Once you're in the barn, the bull will be curled up next to the water trough and you can begin your masterpiece. Afterwards, you can leave by cutting through the attic or by simply running out past the startled guard.

Return to Prochek in Tachov for your reward, and a chance to begin the quest Battle of the Frogs and Mice. If you haven't done Olbram's pranks yet in Frogs, you may want to complete that before continuing, as the Battle quest will resolve the questline.

## Objectives

- Speak with Innkeeper Prochek to learn of his prank on the people of Zhelejov

- Obtain 3 Lullaby potions

- Obtain pigment

- Drug the bull's water trough

- Paint the bull

- Return to Prochek for your reward
