## Miller Kreyzl

Miller Kreyzl (Czech: Mlynář Krejzl) is a miller in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

He can first be met in Troskowitz when first visiting with Hans. After that, he'll be at his mill to the far south.

Kreyzl runs a mill in the area, though others, namely Radovan, will note right in front of Kreyzl that millers are rather shady and to be wary around them. At least when it comes to Kreyzl, Radovan turns out to be correct in this: while Kreyzl runs a mill, he also secretly has employees that he takes on and trains as thieves.

## Biography

Kreyzl's father ran a mill, saving up what they could to put towards Kreyzl's future and, when he was old enough, his mother sent him off to study in Prague to become a preacher. However, it cost money not only to attend a university but to afford housing and food, so Kreyzl quickly learned to steal to make ends meet. While in school though, his mother passed away and, with Kreyzl getting fed up with how closed-minded the classes were in sticking strictly to religious ideologies and refusing to branch out of them, eventually packed his bags and left before the school could kick him out over their differences.

After that, he returned home, where his father merely noted "I knew you'd be back" and soon set his son to work in the mill. However, his thirst for knowledge never left him, especially when it came to alchemy and exploring all its uses. While he eventually took over his family's mill, he continued to dabble in alchemy and soon learned by accident a method of making explosive powder.

Wishing to find a way to get the mixture right again, he eventually enlisted the help of several others, like Zinek and Bonnie, but they were still not able to get the ratios right and ended up using all the saltpetre they could find. However, Kreyzl then learned that a monk many years before him had actually learned and perfected the powder and included it in his book, Lightbringer's secret. Even better was the fact a copy of the book was at Trosky Castle. However, knowing he wouldn't be allowed to just go in and ask for it, Kreyzl needed someone to help obtain it.

If you turn him in to the Troskowitz bailiff:

Bonnie, Zinek and Miller Kreyzl end up being executed by hanging. Bailiff decides to leave them swinging from the rafters in their own Lair.

## Millstone quarry

Millstone quarry is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

An old quarry by the road. Although no longer in use, some of the millstones it produced remain at the site. An enterprising local has even hidden some goods behind one. The nearby mossed over shed has rotted, but a chest remains in good shape. A trail of millstones leads off into the woods, revealing an even better stash.

## Miner Anton Kaspar

Miner Anton Kaspar (Czech: Anton Kašpar) is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Anton was a miner in Kuttenberg, working at the St. Anthony pit. He was a good shooter and as such represented the Striped Tonies at the annual popinjay competition between the Kuttenberg miners. Alongside Franzi, he was tasked with getting the St. Anthony's standard consecrated at three Kuttenberg churches before taking the pitman's oath - a tradition that Henry was invited to partake in by Foreman Vlach as thanks for his help finding the standard during Yackers 'n' Fash.

He was from a well-established mining family in Kuttenberg that used to own a house in the city. His father had, however, spent all of their money on the opening of a new mine shortly before King Sigismund's conquest of the city. The miners, fearing that Sigismund's would cancel the concessions, which would lead to them losing any profit, refused to work on the shaft. When the news reached Anton's father, he had a stroke and died soon after, leaving Anton practically penniless for the time being. This change of fortune affected Anton's love life too - his sweetheart, Tess Linhart (who had already been betrothed to him), now seemed unattainable as her father, rich burgher Linhart, looked for a better match for her. Anton, however, kept seeing Tess and seemed very fond of her, despite forgetting to get her a birthday present in the quest Striped Tonies.

### Associated Quests

- Striped Tonies

- Popinjay Shoot

## Miners' crossbow

Miners' crossbow is a unique weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as the ranged weapon type.

## Description

A beautifully decorated and masterfully made crossbow for the traditional popinjay competition. Everyone would love to have one, but this one is mine now.

## Acquisition

- The only way to obtain the Miners' crossbow is through the Popinjay Shoot quest in Kuttenberg, which requires winning an archery contest against a group of miners.

- Be sure to save your game beforehand and use a quick-firing crossbow, as the contest can be challenging on your first few attempts.

## Miri Fajta

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Miri Fajta is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Walkthrough

### A Missing Daughter

Head to the Nomad Encampment on the eastern shore of Rocktower Pond and you'll eventually be told that their Voivode (chieftain) wishes to speak with you. He will explain that his only daughter, Marika, is missing and that his wife, Aranka, foretold that you would come and help them. If you're willing to help, examine Marika's tent behind her mother's wagon. Unless you can pick the hard chest found there, the only item of interest is Marika's scarf.

The Voivode mentioned that Herbwoman Bozhena knows something, but wouldn't talk to them because she doesn't like Romani. If you're already on Bozhena's good side, and especially if you helped her out during Bad Blood, then she should be more willing to talk to you. Bozhena will inform you that Marika and her lover from Semine, a young man named Bohush, arrived at her hut one night with Bohush bloodied & beaten. While she went to gather herbs for them, they left and she does not know where. However, Marika had in the past spoke of a cave she discovered in Apollonia.

Without much else to go on, you must head to the area and explore. Once in the immediate area of the cave, you'll be prompted to use Mutt if you have him again. With a high enough Houndmaster level, you can give Mutt a sniff of Marika's scarf and he'll lead you to where they're hiding.

### A Family Torn Asunder

In person, Marika will tell you quite a different tale than her father did. It seems that Marika and Bohush became smitten with each other when the nomads travelled through Semine. When the Voivode found out, he sent a messager to Semine demanding that Brohush either marry Marika or pay sufficient compensation for her treatment. Unlike her people, Marika liked the idea of settling down in one place. Fearing that her family would demand the two join them as nomads, she convinced Bohush to run away with her and marry in secret. Voivode's two sons went to Semine to search for her, but unfortunately the brothers started trouble when they encountered Bohush, beating him and thus leading to Marika's rushing him to Herbwoman Bozhena. Now Marika says that she needs help from her mother, but she will not leave Bohush's side. She also says that she will not return to the nomad camp unless her father sends or brings his amulet as a sign of protection for them both. When you bring this proposal to the Voivode, he confesses, but cannot give you the amulet until his two sons are returned home. He has learned that one was killed by a group of local woodcutters, while the other is being held captive in Semine.

### Finding Tibor

Head to Semine village where you can ask around for information on Tibor. You'll eventually be pointed to the saddler's area. The saddler won't give you any new information, so instead ask a housewife or hired hand, who'll tell you he's in the back of the stables, but it's always guarded. However, there's a very obvious flaw here: the other side of the stables has a window you can climb through and is right where Tibor is. If you want to be discreet, use this window and untie him. You can also convince a hired hand to tell you where the key to the door is. Once you free Tibor, he'll climb through the window and head off into the woods nearby. Follow him and he'll explain a bit about what happened before telling you the location of Gejza's body, which he requests that you bring to his favourite spot.

### Get Gejza's body

His body was tied up by the local woodcutters to a tree. While you can try to be sneaky and untie it, if you have decent speech check, you can convince the woodcutter foreman to let you reclaim the body. Once you have it, carry him through the woods to where Tibor is waiting. Just note that this can be quite a bit of a walk.

At the spot, place him down and Tibor will talk a bit before cutting to him with his parents there to put Gejza to rest. After a short prayer, the family will thank you and then have you travel to the Nomads' Camp to discuss with the Voivode about the amulet. He'll explain he can't give up the amulet because it provides magical protection and without the letter Marika stole when she ran off, he'd be trapped. It turns out the letter in question was a letter of safe conduct for the nomads, so he wants you to retrieve it.

While you can certainly get the letter and not care about Marika and Bohush, if you want a good outcome for everyone to reunite, talk to Aranka about it and she'll tell you her husband can't refuse a bet, and will be the only way to try and get the amulet. You can also learn this from Marika by talking to her about it.

### Return to Marika

Go back to Marika, only to discover some wolves have gathered around the hideout. Kill or scare them off, then go in to talk to Marika. She'll reveal the letter is her only safeguard against them discarding Bohush and herself. If Aranka wasn't already asked about the amulet, Marika will reveal her father can't resist a wager and to bet the letter she has against the amulet. However, she has one demand about the letter: if she gives it to you, you need to promise not to simply hand it over to her father.

The letter itself is hidden in a tree at a nearby spring well. Head out to it and at the start of the spring, look to the south to see a tree with a larger trunk than the others around it and sort of by itself. The letter is hidden on the north side of this tree that's facing the spring.

### Wager with the Voivode

When ready, head back to the Voivode to wager the letter against the Voivode personally delivering the amulet to his daughter with his blessing. If you don't care about trying to repair the family, just give him the letter. Simply giving the letter though (or losing it in the wager) will mean Marika will not return home and the tone in camp is more somber.

During the wager, Henry can speak to Aranka for assistance, who will offer potions to sabotage Tibor. To do this, Henry needs to ask Voivode to wait before each round and then speak to Aranka. Henry only needs to win two rounds; if you only win one of the first two rounds, the third will be the tiebreaker.

### First Round: Horse Racing

Tibor's horse is extremely fast with high endurance. Only the swiftest of horses could have a good chance of winning the race, such as Pebbles with the Good Old Pebbles perk.

During the race, check the map to see where the next check point is so that Henry doesn't get lost. Taking the wrong turn guarantees that Tibor wins.

Optionally, Henry can use a potion from Aranka to drug Tibor's horse, making it slower.

When the race ends, speak to Tibor who will offer some tips on horseriding, increasing the Horseriding skill.

### Second Round: Fist Fight

Tibor is moderately difficult to beat. Potions can be used to increase the chance of beating Tibor. Optionally, Henry can use a potion from Aranka to sabotage Tibor, making him weaker. Once the fight ends, Voivode will complain that Henry cheated, even if Henry didn't use Aranka's potion or his own.

### Third Round: Dice

This time, you're playing dice with the Voivode himself. He plays somewhat riskily and isn't hard to beat as he frequently busts on his turns. Once you win the wager, he's upset that you outsmarted him, but also respects that you're crafty enough to win.

### Ending

After you’ve won, the Voivode will travel with you to Marika’s hideout. He gives Marika and Bohush the amulet at Marika’s insistence, making Bohush part of the Voivode’s family. After reluctantly apologizing to them, the Voivode receives the letter of safe conduct and admits that he has learned from this event. Afterwards, a cutscene of a party in the camp plays.

## Miroslav 'Tugbone' of Zimburg

Miroslav 'Tugbone' of Zimburg is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Miroslav was the brother of Jan Posy of Zimburg. After the death of their father Albrecht, they expected to inherit the family estates. Their widowed mother however considered them to be too young and inexperienced and preferred to have her brother-in-law, Predbor of Zimburg, rule over them. To prove their worth, the two brothers vowed to deliver the Zimburg reliquary (with the remains of their father) to the Sedletz Monastery.

On the way there, however, their company had been ambushed by Cumans, their men killed, and Miroslav himself captured and taken hostage to the camp the Cumans made in the ruins of Zimburg, ironically, the ancestral home of the Zimburg family.

Following his rescue in the quest Bellatores, Miroslav can be found alongside Jan in the ruins of Zimburg.

### Origin of the nickname

When asked by Henry about the nickname 'Tugbone', Miroslav is reluctant to answer. Jan Posy however insists on sharing the story, and is keen on telling Henry himself: when they were little, the brothers were taught reading and writing by a prioress from the abbey. One morning, she caught Miroslav in his chamber - as he puts it - "playing with his hobby horse" (with Jan Posy using the self-explanatory euphemism "tugging his bone", hence 'Tugbone'). She never returned after the incident. Miroslav is understandably embarassed but Posy encourages Henry to tell this story to whomever he likes because he finds it hilarious.

### Associated Quests

- Bellatores

- Skeleton in the Closet

## Miskowitz

Miskowitz (Czech: Miskovice) is a village located in the central part of the map on the main road west of Kuttenberg, southwest of Pschitoky and northwest of Bylany.

## Codex entry

The first mention of the village can be found in 1309, when it belonged to Nechval and Peškov of Miskowitz. In 1358, part of the village was taken over by the Skalitz monastery. Until 1805, Miskowitz was enclosed by three gates, but it is not known for sure whether there was a wall between them.

The fortress in the village stood since time immemorial and the first written mention dates back to 1419, when it belonged to a Kuttenberg burgher Vaněk Píšek.

The area surrounding the village is rich in water and the spring of St. Adalbert, which supplied Kuttenberg in the Middle Ages, can be found here.

## Miskowitz Blacksmith

Blacksmith is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Dialogue with his wife will reveal that his name is Marosh.

## Biography

Marosh lived and worked in Miskowitz as a blacksmith. He was not fond of King Sigismund and refused to do any work for those associated with him, even with his forge's relative proximity to Sigismund's camp in the region.

Due to this, his wife, Martha would sometimes ask others, like Henry, to do the work Sigismund's men had requested of her husband and have a local girl, Victoria, deliver the goods.

## Monastery cemetery

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

A bit neglected, but otherwise a nice place for one’s final rest.

Monastery cemetery is a point of interest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Behind the small infirmary church is an inner graveyard. This yard was used to bury monks as well as patrons of the monastery who were not permitted burial in the crypt.

Not nearly as large as the outer monastery graveyard nor as sacred as the crypt, the infirmary graveyard has fallen into a bit of neglect. Vines and grass grow over many of the graves and none are especially well-adorned. Just simple headstones with at most a coat of arms to mark the body below.

The knight Boleslav Bavor was moved to this smaller cemetery to make room in the crypt for other bodies. He was moved here along with the relic he brought back from the Holy Land.

## Monastery infirmary

Monastery infirmary is a point of interest in Sedletz Monastery in the Mysteria Ecclesiae expansion of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It serves as your homebase during the expansion.

## Description

The infirmary of Sedletz Monastery is a large room wherein the sick and injured of the monastery are housed for their treatment and convalescence. The beds are separated by sheets of cloth to afford some measure of privacy while each alcove has a keyhole window for fresh air and sunlight.

At the north end of the building, wash basins are set up. The walkways and walls are lined with stations for making bandages and poultices. At the south end, there is an alchemy workshop and living quarters.

|

Monastery kitchen is a point of interest in Sedletz Monastery in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Next to the church and library, the kitchen is the most important room of a monastery, keeping the monks from absolute hunger. Sedletz’s kitchen is rather dark, with no windows, so oil lamps and cooking fires provide the only light.

Herbs and onions hang to dry. The walls are lined with jars, baskets, cookware, and dishes. One table is dedicated to making bread, while another is dedicated to broths and vegetables, while yet another is dedicated to the dirty dishes. In the middle of the room are the main cooking stations, though the bread oven is against the eastern wall. Between the door to the cellar and the dining room is a large scale.

## Monk Athanasius

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Monk Athanasius is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Athanasius was a monk at Sedletz Monastery, having been there for some time. When the monastery was locked down following a plague scare, he stayed confined to the dormitory with his fellow brothers.

Athanasius noticed, however, that one brother was missing, an older monk called Constantine. This made him worried, as he knew following the abbot’s orders was the safest thing.

When Henry came to the dormitory on his rounds on behalf of Albich of Uniczow, Athanasius asked him to look for Constantine believing him to have wandered away. He gave Henry a physical description and let him know that Constantine was known to spend a lot of time in the garden.

Athanasius was then informed by Henry that Constantine had in fact been in the gardens and wished to remain there, feeling more at ease and better protected in the fresh air. Athanasius wanted Henry to convince Constantine to return to the dormitory, which he may have done.

Regardless, Athanasius was relieved to know that Constantine was all right and was grateful for Henry’s help.

### Associated Quests

- The Last Wish

## Monk Constantine

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Monk Constantine is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Constantine was one of the older monks at Sedletz Monastery. He had a great love for nature and enjoyed spending time gardening. In his youth, he lived a more exciting life even in the monastery, having become quite well-versed in sneaking out.

When the monastery was put under lockdown due to a plague scare, Constantine snuck out and went to stay in the gardens rather than stay cooped up in the dormitories with the other monks. He saw no difference in waiting to die in his old age or from illness inside or outside, so why not at least do it in a place he loved. With permission from Herbalist Joachim, he stayed there with relatively little issue.

Eventually, he was visited by Henry who had come to seek him at the behest of another monk, Athanasius, who had been worried for the older brother. Constantine asked Henry to let him stay, and to bring a message to Athanasius that he was just fine, which Henry may or may not have agreed with.

In the end, after the lockdown was lifted, Constantine focused on restoration efforts with the other brothers, helping the convalescing sick and cleaning up.

## Monk Vojtiech

Monk Vojtiech is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Vojtiech was a monk in the Sedletz Monastery. When Jaroslav finished the translation of Decameron and hid the finished book in the monastery cellars, he started working on his own book, and invited fellow brothers Vojtiech and Ernest as well as maid Blazhena to help him. They would meet in secret in the cellar, writing the original work or debating and telling jokes and humorous anecdotes.

After revealing the reason behind their meetings to Henry, Vojtiech asked him not to tell the abbot, fearing that they would all be expelled from the monastery.

## Mounted archery

Mounted Archery is a repeatable task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It becomes available following the completion of Horses for Courses.

## Description

Bibrek puts my riding and archery skills to the test.

## Walkthrough

Diagram of the tracks by their names.

Talk to Bibrek in the Nomads' camp to start the quest. You can run multiple courses in a given in-game day.

The first time you speak with Bibrek regarding the courses, he will give you a map that tracks the different routes available. You can look it over to familiarize yourself with them.

Choose from three difficulties: Easy, Hard, and Tengri.

There are then 6 basic courses to choose from: The Cowrie, The Stirrup, The Torque, Hounskull, The Sickle, and The Wineskin.

There is one additional course only available at the Tengri difficulty – The Earring. Once you select your difficulty and the course shape, you can place a wager.

To pass, just like in Horses for Courses, you’ll have to score more points than Bibrek's set minimum. The minimum number of points is determined by the course and the difficulty you chose. Tell your horse to follow the track and then shoot the targets as you ride past them. The courses are timed, so if you miss something, it is better to keep moving forward.

Each successful course will earn you Horsemanship and Marksmanship experience as well as twice your wager.

## Murdered flautist

My God! He looks terrible! And why does he have a flute in his ear?

—Henry's commentary

Murdered flautist is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The body can be found just outside of Troskowitz, among the trees past the field beneath Trosky Castle. The poor fellow looks like he was beaten to a pulp, with a flute grotesquely jammed into his ear.

His belongings are scattered around, untouched. The attackers didn't seem interested in taking anything. Judging by the state of the body, he's been lying there for some time. A trail of blood and a discarded axe lead from the road to the scene, suggesting he was ambushed and dragged off the path.

If you report the body to Bailiff Thrush, he'll tell you the man was a musician who went missing some time ago. The flautist used to play at the Troskowitz tavern. His music was fine enough at first, but he played on and on until folk grew tired of it. Seems like someone finally lost their patience.

Thrush will hand over a few groschen to Henry for bringing him the news and will arrange a burial for the musician.

## Musa of Mali

Musa of Mali (Czech: Musa z Mali) is a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He was a physician running the infirmary in Sigismund's camp. In addition to this profession, he called himself "a scholar and an explorer" in the first encounter with Henry. Musa, due to his religion, didn't drink, much to Ditrich Katz's dismay. His greatest vice was a deep appreciation for women's beauty.

## Biography

Originating from Timbuktu, Musa studied law in Cairo and medicine in Granada, before traveling to Venice. When in Venice, he joined an expedition heading for India but it was attacked by pirates. Musa was, however, saved by the warship of Sultan Bayezid I. who - upon learning of Musa's education and experience of living among Europeans - started using him as a translator for meetings with foreign envoys. After some time spent in the Sultan's services, Musa left with envoys from Hungary for King Sigismund's court.

Despite being highly educated and well-traveled, Musa's skill wasn't appreciated at the court, much to his dismay. Instead of being named the king's personal physician and counsellor, he was sent away with Sigismund's army to Bohemia.

Musa viewed this arrangement as a great injustice and did not shy away from vocalizing his criticism of King Sigismund in front of Henry.

He was sent on behalf of king Sigismund for a trivial meeting at the Italian Court, where two Christian clerical orders fought over their spheres of influence. This meeting was disrupted by armed robbers who imprisoned everyone present and stole the silver in the royal coffers within the Court.

When the attackers got distracted by Prague militia with Erik as its commander, Musa and the others used the chaos to escape. However, Musa noticed that one of the attackers was Henry and decided to change sides as a result. He escaped with the Devil's Pack to Suchdol, where he and Katherine took care of the wounded during the following siege.

After the liberation of Suchdol, he recovered in Devil's Den.

### Associated Quests

- Ransom

- The Lion's Den

- The Italian Job

## Codex entry

Musa of Mali

The travelling scholar Musa, who often has more respect for a pretty bathmaid than a powerful nobleman, may be a fictional figure, but his origins, name, and even character are based on real people.

The first of these is King Mansa Musa, ruler of the Mali Empire, who lived in the early 14th century. Musa contributed significantly to the spread of Islam across North Africa and the Middle East and to the development of the city of Timbuktu, where he built a mosque and university that still stand today. According to modern estimates, Musa was the richest man in history, with a fortune estimated at the current equivalent of 500 billion dollars.

Our other model for Musa is Ibn Battuta. An Arab scholar and one of the most important travelers and cartographers of the 14th century. He spent nearly thirty years on the road, during which time he covered much of the then known world. He visited countries of North Africa, the Middle East, India, China and Europe, surpassing all of his contemporaries in the scope of his travels. At the end of his life, he dictated his experiences in the travelogue Rihla (Journey).

—Codex entry: Musa of Mali

## Mutt

KCD

KCD2

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

No one's a match for you and me, eh?

—Henry

Mutt (Czech: Vořech), more famously known as "Good Boy" Mutt, is the sidekick of Henry via the Houndmaster skill, which was introduced with the A Woman's Lot DLC.

## Biography

Originally, Mutt was the dog of the Skalitz butcher prior to the Sack of Skalitz. He avoided detection by Sigismund's Cuman hordes, but at the cost of the butcher's life. For days afterward, Mutt never left his master's side, even as thieves and robbers picked the remains of Skalitz clean.

When Henry returned to bury his parents, he encounters Zbyshek attempting to loot Mutt's late owner while flailing a shovel towards Mutt who loyally stands his ground. After driving the looter away, Mutt will remain at the butcher's side until Henry begins the process of burying his parents; the dog comes to comfort the forlorn youth and spurs him to finish his task. However, when Runt and his thugs confront Henry, they spook Mutt and run him off, but he returns when the cavalry arrives.

After Henry woke up at the Rattay Mill, he could find Mutt wandering around the mill or following Peshek. If the A Woman's Lot DLC is installed, Henry could ask Theresa regarding Mutt's presence at the mill. She would confide that when they evacuated Henry from Skalitz after Runt's attack, they brought Mutt with them and he took up residence at the mill, much to Peshek's annoyance; the miller constantly threatened to skin the dog for fur and meat, even when Mutt brought a hare from the woods. If Henry agreed to take him along, Mutt became a recruitable Sidekick and would be able to heed specific commands from Henry.

If you have a question but want to skip searching through the entire page, see Common Q&A.

## Brief Tutorial

## Interaction

Henry can interact with Mutt through a multitude of dialogue choices and commands. When interacting with Mutt with the corresponding button/key, you will be greeted with the following dialogue choices:

- Food

- Henry will feed Mutt with meat-type items from his inventory. Performing this action after praising Mutt can raise his obedience and the Houndmaster skill faster when done at regular intervals. This action will end the dialogue and Mutt will begin to eat whatever Henry just placed on the ground.

- Feeding Mutt spoiled food will lower his obedience so feed him food that is above 50% (Smoked sausages, Bacon, Salami are great options as they spoil very slowly).

- Henry will say: "Look what I've got for you! You'll love this!".

- Praise

- Henry will begin to compliment our good boy :). Praising is affected by recent events and actions (e.g. praising him after you two successfully took down a bandit, or after he brings you a hare) and it will raise his obedience and the Houndmaster skill, especially when done after said events and actions and at regular intervals. You can continue dialogue after this action, but praising continuously will have less effect than praising him every once in a while. This will also give a slight bonus to feeding him when done in the same conversation.

- Henry will say: "Good boy! That's my boy!" or "There's a good doggie! That's my boy!" or "Good fellah! That's my boy!"

- Hunt game!

- Unlocked by the Hunt Houndmaster skill, Mutt will, by default, chase after and instantly kill rabbits. He will then pick up the carcass in his mouth and set it down at your feet. Selecting the Hunt game! action will change his State, but we will get to that later.

- Henry will say: "Let's hunt something, eh? Hare!"

- Seek!

- Mutt will begin searching for chests and sometimes corpses and animal carcasses. He will hover around you, as if in a Free state, but will sniff the ground more often. Once he finds something, he will sprint to it and continue to bark until you investigate or use the Heel command. His level of obedience and your Houndmaster skill level will determine the radius at which he is able to detect things as well as whether or not he will actually detect it.

- Henry will say: "Let's see what you can sniff out here. Seek!"

- Stay!

- Mutt will sit, lay, or stand around his current location—he may take a few steps before heeding the command. During this state, Mutt's obedience does not decrease faster through neglect but will decrease all the same. To summon Mutt, use the Heel command and he will instantly teleport nearby, no matter the distance, and return to your side.

- Asking Mutt to stay before a fight can be beneficial: Mutt wont blindly rush into battle and he can the be called on a specific enemy with the Sic! command if needed.

- Henry will say: "Wait here for me. Stay!"

- Other commands.

- Aggressive!

- Unlocked by the Sic Houndmaster skill, Mutt will, by default, attack nearby enemies with or without your knowledge. This is useful when you are unable to micromanage Mutt during a fight, but can prove dangerous to Mutt's obedience level if he bites more than he can chew and if repeatedly attacked by an enemy.

- Henry will say: "No one's a match for you and me, eh?"

- Heel!

- Just like the key bind, Mutt will follow you closely and wander a small radius around Henry.

- Henry will say: "Here, heel!"

- Free!

- Mutt will follow you freely, wandering a larger radius around Henry, but following within sight.

- Henry will say: "Come along, free!"

- Go back to the mill!

- Mutt will return to the Rattay Mill where you can retrieve him later. While at the mill, his obedience will not decrease but will be reset to the default. You will be unable to interact with him after sending him home and he will teleport to the mill once you look away or get far enough away from him. He will begin following Peshek around as he did before recruiting him. To return him to your side, you will need to speak with Theresa again.

- Henry will say: "Back to the mill! Home!"

- (Back)

- (End dialog)

## Command Button

- Microsoft Windows/PC: X key

- PlayStation Triangle button

- Xbox - Y button

## Commands

Henry has only one button to command Mutt with on all devices (see above). These commands will be discernable by the dog head symbol next to the command along with directions on how to activate it on the bottom right corner of the screen. Using commands will not change Mutt's state (e.g. using the Hunt command will not change Mutt's state from Free to Hunting).

- Sic!

- During one on one combat, the Sic command can be overpowered, as it will keep an opponent still and occupied for you to land a fatal blow, but please note that the Sic command should only be used while attacking / under attack by three or less enemies! Read more below!

- Unlocked by the Sic Houndmaster skill, this command is available while hovering over a person, whether or not an enemy. It can be activated from a very far distance as long as visual contact with the target is established. Mutt will sprint over to the target and activate a arm-biting animation where he will keep the target occupied and in place. After the target breaks free, Mutt will begin repeatedly bite them until you activate the Heel command, the target dies, Mutt's obedience hits zero, or the target gets far enough away from Henry. Be warned, this command will be seen as a crime when done to civilians or non-enemy human NPC's. After, Mutt will return to what his current state makes him do, e.g. if in a Hunting state, he will resume hunting and wont become aggressive.

- PLEASE NOTE that Mutt can easily become overwhelmed when in the presence of many enemies, especially multiple hostile dogs. The Heel command will not break him free if being mauled by another dog or if he is in between hostile humans who are attacking him. The best way to save Mutt from running away due to low obedience is to run away (preferably on horse to get away from the enemies) and to use the Heel command, as it will teleport him to you and out of harm's way. The Sic command should only be used while attacking / under attack by three or less enemies—especially at low Houndmaster skill levels—any more and the access enemies will switch aggro from Henry to Mutt and will hammer on the poor thing until he runs away (see notes).

- Heel!

- Though this command will not automatically prompt in any case, holding down the command button while no other commands are prompted on the screen will activate the Heel command. This commend does not change Mutt's state and will only make him come closer to you.

- Hunt!

- Unlocked by the Hunt Houndmaster skill, this command is available while hovering over an animal, with the exception of other dogs. It can be activated from a very far distance as long as visual contact with the animal is established. Like the Sic command, Mutt will sprint over to the animal and attack it until you activate the Heel command, the animal dies, Mutt's obedience hits zero, the animal gets far enough away from Henry (which is significantly further away than with the Sic command), or Mutt becomes tired. After, Mutt will return to what his current state makes him do.

- Fetch!

- Unlocked by the Hunt Houndmaster skill, this command is available while hovering over a rabbit carcass. It can be activated from a very far distance as long as visual contact with the rabbit corpse is established. When activated, Mutt will pick up the rabbit carcass and drop it at your feet. Mutt will automatically carry out this command when he is in the Hunting state. Note that this command cannot be used on anything that isn't a rabbit carcass.

## Stats

Mutt will have two stats which are affected by your actions and the Houndmaster skill. Both can be seen in the Dog tab of Sidekicks.

- Sense of Smell

A dog can sniff out enemies even when they're out of sight. If you take good care of your dog and are experienced in handling it, it will identify foes at a greater distance. The distance at which it can identify a foe increases with your level of Houndmaster skill.

- In-game Description

Certain perks with the Houndmaster skill, along with leveling up the skill, will increase the distance in which Mutt can detect enemies. Note that only after the Sniffer perk will Mutt be able to warn Henry of nearby foes.

- Obedience

Your dog's obedience affects his behavior. If it's low, he won't always heed your commands or may even run off. If it's high, on the other hand, your dog will be more effective and will obey your orders willingly.

- In-game Description

Despite the in-game description, Mutt will not randomly run off when his obedience is above zero. Though, the moment it hits zero, he will run away from Henry and will not return with the heel command. His dog head icon will also dissapear, but in most cases will not (see bugs). After a minute or two, Mutt will eventually return with default obedience. He will continuesly bark and sprint towards you until he reaches your side. Feeding and praising Mutt will raise his obedience amount, while increasing your Houndmaster skill will rise his default level of obedience—the set amount of obedience he returns with after he either runs away or after you retrieve him after being sent away.

## States

Mutt will have multiple states which can be changed at will through interaction. Under the Dog tab of Sidekicks, Mutt's current state will be seen under Current command.

- Hunting

- Triggered by selecting Hunt game! while interacting with him. Using the Heel command in this state will not change his state to At heel and will instead drop the rabbit carcass or stop chasing an animal and immediately return to you. Mutt will resume hunting after a few moments.

- Waiting

- Triggered by selecting Stay! while interacting with him. Despite using the Heel command to summon him, Mutt will enter a Free state.

- Aggressive

- Triggered by selecting Aggressive! while interacting with him. Using the Heel command in this state will not change his state to At heel and will instead stop attacking enemies to return to your side. But be warned, after returning to you, he will immediately begin attacking enemies again depending on whether you are under attack and their distance.

- At heel

- Triggered by selecting Heel! while interacting with him. This state and the Heel command are not related and cannot be triggered through said command. Using the Heel command will only make him get closer to you for a moment before returning to the At heel state wandering distance.

- Free

- Triggered by selecting Free! while interacting with him. Using the Heel command in this state will not change his state to At heel and will only make him get closer to you for a moment before returning to the Free state wandering distance. Using the Heel command while in this state may free him from being stuck or teleport him to you if he isn't catching up to you while you are running or on a horse.

- Searching

- Triggered by selecting Seek! while interacting with him. Using the Heel command will cause him to stop barking at a container (or whatever he sought out) and return to you, or to stop searching for a few moments before returning to his search. If you use Heel this to make him stop barking at whatever he found, he will usually return to whatever he found a minute or two later, continuing to bark until you investigate.

## Trivia

- The dog's Czech name literally means "Nut" or "Walnut", but otherwise it is slang term with nearly the same meaning as his English name, describing street crossbreed dog.

## Common Q&A

- Question: How do I recruit Mutt?

- Answer: Mutt is only recruitable after buying the A Woman's Lot DLC. Once you have that downloaded, speak to Theresa at the Rattay Mill and chose the dialogue option involving Mutt.

- Question: Where is Mutt located?

- Answer: Mutt is located at the Rattay Mill near Rattay. He will be wondering around the grounds or following the miller, Peshek. If he is not there or is missing, see bugs.

- Question: What can/does Mutt do?

- Answer: Mutt is a Sidekick and is able to be commanded and interacted with by Henry. He can hunt animals, attack enemies, and sniff out treasures if you command him to do so! The measure of his abilities and what he can do solely depends on your Houndmaster skill level and perks.

- For more, click the word you wish to know more about: Interaction - Commands - Stats - States.

- Question: Will recruiting Mutt begin A Woman's Lot's questline?

- Answer: No, the A Woman's Lot's questline will initiate once you select the dialogue choice with the corresponding DLC icon to the side of the option. Mutt's recruitment dialogue choice does not have that icon, and will not affect the DLC or its questline whatsoever.

- Question: Mutt ran away! When will he come back, where did he go, and why did he run away?

- Answer: Mutt will return to Henry after a few minutes, so don't worry, you wont have to track him down or return to the Rattay Mill to recruit him again! He will run away once his obedience level reaches zero. Mutt being attacked by you, an enemy, or a hostile dog will lower his obedient level, while praising him and feeding him will raise it. You cannot follow him once he runs off, as he will despawn once far enough away from you or after he leaves your field of view. For more, see stats.

## Bugs

- During the fourth main quest Awakening, Mutt may become bugged/stuck along the way to Rattay or somewhere within Skalitz during the opening scene. This bug is rare in the vanilla game but is commonly triggered while using mods. The only known fix is to remove the mods and reload before the particular scene.

- After selecting the Food option while interacting with Mutt, a bug may occur where he does not eat the dropped food but will walk over to it and look either to the left or the right indefinitely until you pick up the food or use the Heel command. Moving to a different location, fast traveling, or reloading will fix this.

- When Mutt runs off after hitting zero obedience, his dog head marker will often not disappear and will remain where he despawned on the minimap and larger map until he returns.

## Mutt (quest)

Mutt is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

After you're able to start roaming the world by yourself, this quest will become available to try and find Mutt.

## Description

I should find out what happened to my loyal friend Mutt and take care of him

## Synopsis

Mutt has been missing since Henry fell over the cliff while escaping the bandits. He figures heading back there will be his best bet in finding clues as to Mutt’s whereabouts. When he gets there, he finds a man looking over the body of the bandit who broke his fall. Once the looter is dealt with, Henry spies a half-eaten deer carcass, maybe a sign that Mutt really had been there… but he’s nowhere to be seen, so Henry assumes someone must have taken him in.

Since Bozhena’s is nearby, Henry decides to start there. Unfortunately, Bozhena has seen no sign on him, she has an idea of where a dog might like to go though – fishermen leave scraps and taverns do too. There also happens to be a pack of wolves by Semine, she suggests it’s possible he’s gone feral and joined them as well.

Henry follows her advice, asking around. The tavernkeeper at Zhelejov says he hasn’t seen any dogs around for a while but he echoes Bozhena’s comment about a wolf pack in the forest. He says a shepherd boy, Siegfried has been complaining that his sheep are being eaten by them. When Henry asks about anyone else having come across dogs recently, the tavernkeeper mentions a tale he heard from a poacher who mentioned seeing a deer taken down by a pack of wolves and dogs together.

The fisherman hasn’t seen a dog either, but he’s heard the same story from Siegfried, plus a few extra complaints about the gamekeeper, a good lead as any. The only other dog-related news he has was that he heard howling one night, of a large pack of wolves.

Siegfried certainly has wolf problems. He wants Henry to deal with them, as they keep threatening his sheep. Henry can leave some bait for them in the form of raw meet or a ram on loan called Ignatius. Either way, Henry deals with the wolves, no sign of Mutt, but one happier shepherd. Siegfried mentions that Henry can try asking the gamekeeper about his dog, although the gamekeeper might be a drunk, he can probably still tell the difference between a dog and a wolf.

Henry asks the gamekeeper about Mutt as well, and may even help him out of a tough spot if he hadn’t already. The infamous wolf pack, he says, has been causing issues for everyone around Semine, but he finds it hard to believe a regular mutt would have joined up with them. He tells Henry he’s likely to see them most active around dusk by the rocks above the pond.

Henry finds what seems to be a wolf den in the area the gamekeeper pointed to, and digging in the dirt, a very familiar dog! The pair are happy to see each other, but their reunion is interrupted by the very wolves who live in the den coming out. Henry and Mutt are able to fend them off and catch up.

## Walkthrough

Note this quest will have you running all over the place and doing additional steps to locate Mutt. You can either do them for additional reputation and rewards or simply see if you can locate him without all the legwork.

### Quick method

Head out to the spot where you need to find what happened to Mutt. This is the same spot where you last saw him attack a bandit and you fell off the cliff. Here, you'll find a vagabond checking over the dead bandit's corpse. Deal with him, then inspect the dead bandit and then the deer corpse near the path, which will give the next objective to find him.

From here, you just now need to head south of the Nomads' Camp to find the wolves' den. You know you'll have found it when a cutscene starts as you get close and you're reunited with Mutt, only for a pack of wolves to come out. You can either fight them off or flee with Mutt to complete the quest.

### All objectives

If you don't mind doing the legwork and learning more about some of the people in the area, you'll be directed all around the place, from Bozhena to the lord's huntsman, Vostatek, and a herdsman in the area, Siegfried, most of whom have additional things they need help with.

## Mutt/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Mutt is Henry's dog he had adopted after the sack of Skalitz. In Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, he runs away during the quest Easy Riders and Henry will need to find him in the Mutt quest if he wants to reunite with his four-legged best friend. The skill Houndmaster grants Henry more control over Mutt, and additional perks to quality of sleep,charisma or dialogue stats when accompanied by him.

## Interaction

Three interactions have their own reserved buttons:

- Praise lets you pet Mutt

- Sic lets Mutt know to attack enemies or animals. Note that if Mutt's Obedience is too low, he might ignore the command.

- Heel calls Mutt to your heel from the Stay and Free states

The others hide behind a chat menu:

- Feed opens up a menu with meats to offer Mutt. Open the menu preferably on a flat surface, as various dried meats will roll downhill while Mutt watches them.

- Commands

- Track - Some quests are significantly easier if you have Mutt track the scent of a quest item. Those quests are: Miri Fajta, The Stalker, The Fifth Commandment, and Blacksmith's Comission - Swords for the Guards.

- Send home - Mutt will be waiting at the Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn, Devil's Den, or Henry's Forge, depending on the region Henry is currently in.

- Behavior

- Free is the default state of Mutt, who will stay within a few meters of Henry.

- Heel works exactly the same as the heel command in real life - Mutt will stay closer. He will also ignore any attacking enemies.

- Stay again works exactly as it should in real life. Mutt may accidentally give away your position if you accidentally sneak up on a bandit camp with him. He can be called back again with the shortcut for Heel, or a long press of the same button that calls your horse.

## My Shoes!

My Shoes! is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

While you were passed out drunk somebody nicked your shoes.

## Acquisition

The My Shoes! achievement is unlocked by getting so drunk that you pass out and wake up missing your shoes.

- Empty your inventory into a stash chest, keeping only:

- A single pair of shoes or boots equipped.

- At least 10 bottles of strong alcohol, such as Schnapps.

- Create a manual save before proceeding.

- Drink all 10 bottles of Schnapps in quick succession.

- After a short time, Henry will enter the second phase of drunkenness and pass out.

- Time will fast-forward approximately eight hours.

- If successful, you will wake up to find your shoes missing, and the achievement will unlock.

## Tips

- It is best to attempt this in a densely populated area.

- The result is randomized. If your shoes are not stolen, reload the manual save and try again.

- This achievement can be obtained if your shoes are stolen while unconscious at any time, it does not require being drunk; if you get into a brawl and lose, there is still a chance to obtain this achievement.

## Myshek

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Myshek is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Myshek was a soldier serving Sigismund of Luxembourg. Together with six fellow soldiers, he was sent with a cart to the Sedletz monastery to deliver a letter to the king who resided there at the time. The group had however decided to desert and take refuge in an abandoned building in Old Lhota. Myshek didn't like this idea and refused to join them. Afraid that he'd rat them out to their commander Ditrich Katz, the other soldiers decided to get rid of him, stabbed him and left him for dead.

A peasant found him unconscious on the road and brought him back to Sigismund's camp. There, he was cared for by Musa of Mali.

## Mysteria Ecclesiae

Mysteria Ecclesiae is the third and last major story expansion for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Announced on 16 January 2025 alongside two other expansions, Brushes with Death and Legacy of the Forge, it was released on 11 November 2025 for PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S.

It is included in both the Expansion Pass and the Gold (Royal) Edition.

## Description

Join Henry as he assumes the role of assistant to Sigismund Albicus, a renowned healer with ties to King Wenceslas himself. Tasked with a clandestine mission within the monastery's ancient walls, Henry finds himself entangled in a web of intrigue (and a deadly mysterious plague) where each faction harbors its own hidden motives.

Explore an all-new location, the fascinating Sedletz Monastery, and meet its elusive inhabitants. A sudden epidemic has hit the area, and it's imperative to find the origin. Guide Henry across a rich cinematic quest that will test your deductive and sleuthing skills alike; discover a new outfit, weapon, potions and books, and master your way through to solve the mystery. Careful though, there's more here than meets the eye…

## Features

- Unravel a Deadly Mystery – Unravel the mysteries shrouding Sedletz Monastery as you interact with its inhabitants and uncover their hidden agendas. Engage with a variety of factions, each with their own motivations, and shape the course of events with your decisions.

- Explore a New Location – Traverse the historically accurate Sedletz Monastery's diverse areas, gradually unlocking new sections as you solve mysteries and uncover hidden secrets.

- Grow your Henry further – Discover a new outfit, weapon, potions, and books, expanding Henry’s knowledge and abilities to new horizons.

## Quests

- Maddening Pain

- Our Daily Bread

- Prevention

- Seek and You Shall Find

- Silent Witnesses

- The Last Wish

- The Royal Physician

- The Time Has Come

- To Dust You Shan't Return

## Nail in the Coffin

Nail in the Coffin is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It becomes available once all other regional fighters have been defeated in unarmed combat. You need to complete the following Tasks:

- Teeth in the Bag

- Enough!

- Fight Dirty

## Description

At the cemetery in Kuttenberg, I could meet the strongest fighter around. Maybe it’s a superstition, maybe I’m going to fight for the title of grandmaster.

## Walkthrough

Head to the northern cemetery in Kuttenberg and talk to Gravedigger Frantishek. He’ll reveal it truly is he who is the best fighter in the region, not a ghost, having honed his skills out of necessity.

You can talk to him during the day and he’ll request you come by a night so no one will see the two of you causing trouble. You’ll have to wait or go do other things, as there’s no way to force him to skip time.

By night, you’ll find him most likely leaning against his house just east of the churchyard. Talk to him at night and he’ll accept your request to fight. He is a very skilled fighter, play defensively. When you beat him, he will reward you with a new combo; the Shoulder Throw.

## Nameless spring

Nameless spring is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

At the head of a small stream, surrounded by mossy stones and greenery hides a small spring, so small it doesn’t have a name. This picturesque setting is not entirely safe, however, as thieves have made a camp for themselves nearby.

Located on the wooded trail from Herbalist Bozhena's hut and Zhelejov, about halfway between them.

Next to the water sits a basket with dangerous herbs inside, left there by the one who was foraging them. The herbs themselves both grow nearby.

## Nebakov Fortress

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Nebakov is a small fortress in the Trosky region. It's an ancestral seat of Jaromier Nebak, the vassal of Otto von Bergow in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

The fortress was located in what was considered an ideal spot: on a cliff to see who was approaching through the valley, with only one way in and out. However, the place was taken by surprise one night by a large group of bandits, with most of the guards killed off while its owner was taken captive and held in the fortress' prison.

However, instead of asking for ransom or making it known about their presence, the bandits pretended they were the guards and that Jaromier wasn't accepting visitors, taking over the fortress as their new base.

## Codex entry

The castle was likely built at the end of the 13th century on a promontory overlooking Nebak pond, surrounded on all sides by steep cliffs and water. To construct the fortress, the rock beneath it had to be manually hewn away and levelled, which was a relatively complex process for its time, given it was a small noble castle of little significance.

According to archaeological research, it had a three-part layout with a courtyard and a fortified keep, connected to other parts of the complex by a bridge spanning a rocky moat.

The first mention of the castle in historical sources only appears in 1455. The castle burned down at the end of the 15th century and from 1538, it has been described as abandoned and in ruins. From the fortifications, only the ramparts, moats and notches in the rock have been preserved to this day.

We endeavored to reconstruct the castle in the game, so that its appearance aligns as much as possible with archaeological findings.

## Necessary Evil

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Necessary Evil is the 8th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Who are all the people involved in the ambush of von Bergow and where are the bandits hiding out?

## Synopsis

Having received their mission from von Bergow, Henry and Hans leave to get started on the captive bandit. Hans isn’t too keen on torture, but they need to get into von Bergow’s good graces to stand a chance of bringing him over to their side in the long run. The captive is strung up in the dungeons, von Bergow’s men already having worked him over in an attempt to get information out of him.

The captive is still quite spirited at first but either through force or the powers of persuasion, Henry is able to get a kernel of information out of him. Namely, where their hideout is (if Henry didn’t already know), the not so helpful first name of their leader, confirmation that Toth is indeed with them, and the name of a helper in the region – Olda Semine. With that information comes a dilemma, whether they should inform von Bergow of young Semine’s involvement and risk the people of Semine or stay quiet.

Henry may leave out young Semine’s involvement with the bandits, something that von Bergow may question if he was told the groom had left his wedding, but still may be convinced those events are unrelated. Henry may also, however, be unable to convince von Bergow or else choose to report on the findings in full at which point von Bergow will order Burgrave Hashek to head to Semine to deal with the traitor along with Henry and Hans.

Hans thinks von Bergow is overdoing things, he himself not so keen on exacting revenge for the near miss they had despite the casualties they suffered. It’s not his decision to make, however, so they have no choice but to depart when Hashek is ready.

On the way to Semine, Hashek makes talk with Henry asking after his knowledge of Semine and the horror of the ambush they suffered at the hands of the bandits holed up in Nebakov. The gates are closed when they arrive, but orders to have them opened are heeded, though everyone inside seems ill at ease.

Hashek is wound up, unable to hide his disdain as he demands Olda be brought out, accusing old Semine of hiding him and conspiring against von Bergow along with him. Both sides insist on the other’s guilt until Semine cracks under pressure, fearing for his son. He admits he knows where the bandits may be found and offers to tell Hashek as long as Olda can be spared. Hashek is not moved, threatening to destroy the place if Olda isn’t turned over to him at once.

As tensions come to a head, Henry again is left with a choice. He may side with Semine or with Hashek and, which ever he chooses, a fight breaks out. When the dust settles, Semine is burnt either in retribution or to hide the trail of the fleeing survivors.

The next morning, Henry and Hans (and possibly Hashek) report back to von Bergow, shaken from what has transpired. Regardless of what happened the prior evening, von Bergow will hear that Semine and his men attacked, Olda was killed, and Hashek ordered the fortress to be razed.

## Walkthrough

Note that as soon as you talk to Hans, this quest will start with you having to go down to the prison, so if you want to do other things, handle that first before talking to Hans.

If you waited before talking, Hans will eventually make his way to just outside the torture chamber to wait. Discuss with him the situation then, when ready, interact with the torture chamber to start.

### Interrogation

Depending on your speech check stats and if you already discovered part of the truth at Nebakov Fortress in the last main quest, you can get all the information you need without laying a hand on the prisoner. To do this route, talk to him, where you can eventually choose to respond you're not a traitor, view tongs, or slap him. Regardless what you choose, you then have three questions:

- Ask where his band is hiding

- Ask who their leader is

- Ask about Istvan

If you ask about Istvan first, you won't get any details initially, so wait on that one (you get a chance to repeat the question later though if you do ask it first). The first two questions have hard speech checks to get him to reveal information (or require you to reveal you already know about Nebakov). With Istvan, you'll need to pass a medium speech check for him to tell you what he knows. You can try to ask about the sword as well, but won't get any details on that.

The next two questions, you can ask if someone's helping them and about your ambushed group. Again, you'll need to pass a medium speech check if you want to avoid torture. Regardless how you get the information though, he'll reveal the name: Olda. However, the prisoner will warn you if you reveal this to Otto von Bergow, von Bergow will likely have Semine attacked and innocents will be killed. If you ask why they ambushed you, he'll just reveal his sentiments about killing people during war: there are no innocents and especially those he views are on von Bergow's side. You can argue against this or not, but it won't provide anything to change outcomes later.

Afterwards, you'll talk to Hans for a bit before getting to the big dilemma: if you should reveal Olda or not. Note that what you pick here won't actually set your choice yet, which is done instead when you go talk to von Bergow.

### Inform von Bergow

When ready, go talk to von Bergow about what you discovered. Here, you'll then have to make the choice if you want to keep quiet about Olda or not. If you choose to keep quiet, note that if you had mentioned Olda having left his wedding in the last quest, you'll have to pass a very hard speech check here to convince him you made a mistake (otherwise if you didn't mention him in the last quest, no speech check is required). If you choose this route, you won't have to go to Semine, where a bloody fight will break out regardless who you side with. The achievement Silence is Golden is related to keeping quiet here. The rest of the topics you can discuss without issue, such as Nebakov and Istvan. The quest will also end here and go immediately into the next.

Attack on Semine

If you instead inform Von Bergow that Olda is involved, or failed to convince him Olda's not involved, he'll then question if others in Semine were aware. While you can try to say you don't think so, even if you pass the speech check, this will not have any bearing on the final outcome in Semine. After discussing everything, he'll then order Hashek to get his men ready to confront Semine. At this point, you can either wait around/go do other things, or go talk to Hans and wait with him until Hashek is ready to set out.

When the time is right, Hashek will order everyone to mount up. Follow him out the side gate where he'll call out to his men to also ride out. Settle in for a long ride, where Hashek will talk to you for a bit, opening the way to ask him what exactly happened when his group was ambushed. Eventually, the group will arrive at Semine's gate and a cutscene will play out before they're let in. Hashek will argue with Semine and Gnarly regarding Olda, though it soon becomes clear Hashek is out for revenge for what happened to his people and won't consider Semine's pleas to let his son live. Note while you have a few interjections, your choice doesn't lock in until the final one, where Heshek will ask who's side you're on. At this point, you'll have to either side with Semine (saying nothing is going to burn) or with Hashek ("I'm on your side").

-
Side with Hashek

-
Side with Semine

If you side with Hashek, you'll have to kill all of Semine's guards there, including Gnarly and Tuma. When they're all down, Hashek will task you to find Olda, while he lets Semine survive long enough so he can watch his son be killed. While you can argue with Hashek here, you'll have no choice now but to find Olda while the rest of the men kill everyone in sight. Head up into the tower where you'll see Agnes be killed right before your eyes. Head all the way to the top to confront Olda. You can discuss with him a bit on why he did the things he did, where he'll make remarks that he considers von Bergow a traitor and that Olda still stands firmly with his views that he was helping the people in the area.

At this point, you can either confirm you're arresting him to stand trial or let him go. If you re-confirm you're turning him in, Hashek will appear, revealing he had been hiding around the corner to make sure you weren't going to turn on him. However, Hashek will refuse to take Olda back to face trial, and instead kills him. If you choose to let him go, Hashek will still appear, though this time mad at your decision and will force you to defend yourself from him. You'll then have no choice but to kill Hashek and all his men. The conversation will then turn to talking to Jan and Olda like if you'd sided with them before (but with a lot more dead).

After the cutscene, ride back, where you can talk a bit with Hans about all that transpired. Once it's morning, go report to von Bergow. While Hashek gives his report, you can interject a few times to call out his brutality, for which von Bergow will admonish Hashek. Otherwise, you can remain silent. The quest will then wrap up.

If you side with Semine, a fight will break out, and you will need to kill Hashek and his men. After they're all down, Semine will argue with Olda a bit over his actions, and you can then ask Olda why he ambushed von Bergow. Eventually though, the conversation turns to the fact you'll need to hide that you helped kill Hashek and all his men. No matter what you answer here (cover tracks or use the attack on Nebakov as a distraction), the group realizes they have no choice but to set their estate on fire while Semine and Olda flee the area. After Semine Fortress is put to the torch you will ride back with Hans, with a quick discussion on what occurred.

In the morning, report to von Bergow, who'll soon ask where Hashek is, and he'll be informed he died during the attack. It's best in this case to let Hans do all the talking. Note at the end of the conversation, you have an option to say you killed Hashek, but this only leads to a special game over: you'll see a short cutscene of Henry being in prison and then hanged. Afterwards, the quest will end here to go into the next main quest.

## Nero

Nero is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered at Camp by the road locations in the Kuttenberg region alongside two unnamed mercenaries.

## Biography

Nero was a mercenary specialising in finding wanted people, usually debtors or thieves, but occasionally errant lovers. He and his group were called “stalkers” by those who hired them thanks to their perseverance and propensity for always getting their man. He considered himself to be a “problem solver” who could deal with the messes other people were unable or unwilling to clean up.

His group consisted of himself, a man called Whip who was an executioner’s son, and a man called Hoofpick who joined them after having worked on a farm which had burnt down leaving him unemployed.

Nero was travelling through the Kuttenberg region on the hunt for an unknown man who had knocked up the daughter of the man who hired them, one Young Lady Adler. He treated each man he came across as a possible suspect, insisting they prove their identity at first meeting before being at all forthcoming.

He was skilled with both bow and crossbow and was happy to partake in shooting competitions with anyone passing by who was willing to spend the time (and even better if they were willing to put up a wager).

## Nicholas of Rattay

Nicholas of Rattay (Czech: Mikuláš Ratajský) was a young soldier in the service of Hanush of Leipa.

He, alongside Oats, Konrad, Tankard, and Henry of Skalitz, was assigned to accompany Hans Capon in delivering a message from loyalist lords to Otto von Bergow.

## Involvement

Nicholas rode out of Rattay as part of Hans Capon's escort. He had never traveled beyond his hometown but wished to do so, which is why he asked Oats to put in a word for him.

His task was to take care of the men's horses and gear. He viewed the whole ordeal as an "adventurous expedition" and was looking forward to seeing more of the world.

Despite being a little worried, he believed Capon to be responsible and sensible when it comes to important things, and that clever folks could always come to an agreement.

He was the first among the Capon's men to fall in the bandit ambush.

## Nikvard Libak

Nikvard Libak was a lord who resided in Trosky Castle in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Despite being of nobility, Nikvard was known to be rather reclusive and tended to go off and do his own thing, leaving some like Erazim to wonder if the nobleman ever used his chambers in the castle.

He'd also taken a liking to Otto von Bergow's maid, Regina, and tried to court her, much to the maid's annoyance. When she tried to dissuade him from continuing to try and court her she suggested it wasn't proper for a noble to have an affair with a maid he instead took this to mean she was referring to him being too old for her. As such, when he was helping the scribe sort some new books, he borrowed one that contained odd alchemy ideas, Lightbringer's secret, in the hopes he could find something in it to make him younger.

However, while he appeared to find something to help him, it also caused him to have horrible digestive issues and having to go to the bathroom frequently. He sought out one of the castle's cooks, Bertha, to discreetly make him something for this, making her swear to not tell another soul in fear of the local maidens finding out.

## Nimble Fingers (achievement)

This article is about the achievement. For the perk, see Nimble Fingers.

Nimble Fingers is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You picked the hardest lock.

## Acquisition

The Nimble Fingers achievement is unlocked by successfully picking a Very Hard lock. One of the easier Very Hard locks can be found in an abandoned, overgrown village southeast of Troskowitz, near the road to Schdiar Farm.

It's possible to open this lock at around level 14 of Thievery skill with a bit of patience and minimal loss of lockpicks, though success at lower levels is also possible with a bit of practice.

## Tips

- Quickfinger potion temporarily raises your Thievery skill, making difficult locks more manageable.

- Unlocking perks like Tool Master (greater lockpick durability), Silent Fiddler (quieter lockpicking), Locksmith (Thievery boost during lockpicking), and Hustler (increased Thievery and Stealth experience from selling stolen goods) is also useful.

## No Good Deed

No Good Deed is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You saved Maleshov without getting caught.

## Acquisition

This is a missable achievement obtained during the main quest, Dancing with the Devil. It involves stopping the Dry Devil's crew from razing Maleshov and then infiltrating the fortress undetected.

## Tips

- At the start of the quest, outside Maleshov, the Dry Devil plans to lead his crew in a direct assault on the village. To prevent this, challenge him to a duel. Upon defeating him, you will assume command and initiate a stealth-based approach instead.

- The second requirement is to reach the main gate of Maleshov without being detected or triggering the alarm. One effective method is as follows:

- Climb the outer wall to enter the village.

- Descend the stairs and enter the building on the left.

- Stealth kill the guard near the ladder, then climb it.

- Sneak past the sleeping guards upstairs and drop down onto the battlement on the far side.

- Turn right and wait for the patrolling guard on the ramparts to face away. You may eliminate him, but it is optional.

- Wait for the two gate guards to separate. One usually patrols nearby while the other stays at the gate.

- Time your movement carefully, sneaking behind the lone guard on the stairs when the patrolling guard walks away.

- Alternatively, you can throw stones or other distractions to reposition the gate guards if necessary.

- Approach the gate and open it without alerting anyone.

- Once the gate is opened stealthily, the achievement will unlock.

## Nomad Karol

Nomad Karol is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered at Camp by the road locations alongside three nomads.

## Biography

Karol and his group of Romani nomads can be encountered by Henry at a random roadside camp. He is glad to meet Henry and, if Miri Fajta has been completed, will comment that he has heard of Henry. In gratitude for Henry helping his people around Trosky, he will offer to sell his goods at a substantial discount. Henry can also ask for his fortune to be told, but Karol will tell him that only his wife, Maria, can do such things and she has left for the village to get goods. Henry can also invite Karol to play dice, but the nomad will decline on account of his promise to Maria to stay away from gambling.

## Novice Benedict

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Novice Benedict is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

### Early life

Benedict was born the youngest of five siblings, though one died when they were young. Eventually, both of his brothers left their home to find work elsewhere and his sister was married, leaving him the only child at home to care for his parents. He felt sticking by them was the right thing to do, so he did, caring for them as they became ill until the day they passed.

This experience, he saw as introducing him to his true calling – tending to the ill and infirm. He joined up as a novice at Sedletz Monastery when it became clear he could not join the military and his family had no money left following his sister’s wedding to support him. Two years later, though still a novice, he practised medicine at the Monastery infirmary. He enjoyed reading alchemical texts most of all, as they furthered his learning.

He was generally pragmatic and not over-emotional, becoming detached in times of medical stress which helped him in emergencies. He was quite happy with life in the cloister, thriving in such a structured environment, eating in the same place from the same dishes, praying at the same times every day, and sleeping in the same bed every night.

### Involvement

Benedict was working in the infirmary as usual when Albich of Uniczow along with Henry came to the monastery to speak with the abbot. He had been tending to three ill people who had all been suffering from the same mysterious illness with the help of Zacharias of Prachatitz and Denes Latzkfi.

The cause of the illness was unknown, and all they could do was try to figure out its source and how best to treat it. Benedict deferred to the older, more famous physicians and worked to keep the ill comfortable.

While Albich was getting settled, Benedict was flagged down by one of the outer monastery workers, Maddie, who was suffering from abdominal pains. He was nervous to help her, not being very familiar with “womanly issues” and had no real advice for her. Although he didn’t know how to treat her, he knew the library would have some relevant information.

Later on, Albich’s room was ransacked while no one was around. Benedict, however, did not notice anything suspicious, having been too focused on his patients at the time.

Benedict continued to treat the ill, helping to disseminate the cure once one was found.

### Associated Quests

- Anamnesis

- Maddening Pain

- Silent Witnesses

- The Time Has Come

## Oats

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Ah, Christ! Will I ever live to see his young Lordship finally grow up?!

—Oats about Hans Capon

Oats (Czech: Voves) was an old soldier and a cook in the service of Hanush of Leipa.

He, alongside Konrad, Tankard, Nicholas, and Henry of Skalitz, was assigned to accompany Hans Capon in delivering a message from loyalist lords to Otto von Bergow.

## Involvement

Oats rode out of Rattay as part of Hans Capon's escort. As the oldest and most experienced member of the group, he was responsible for the supplies and cooking, even though his skills in that regard were questionable. He had been in the service of Sir Hanush for many years and had known Capon since his childhood, accompanying his liege often enough that this was far from his first task of delivering an important message. His prior experience navigating the area with Sir Hanush was the reason he was assigned to Capon's entourage.

Oats appears to have been the only one of the men, aside from Henry and Capon himself, who had a clear sense of what their mission entailed and of the political situation surrounding it. Although he did not know the contents of the letter, he correctly surmised that the lords wished to sound out von Bergow's position on the conflict and the possibility of an alliance. He was skeptical that a truce with Sigismund could be achieved at the current stage of the war, yet he still hoped the conflict might be contained and not descend into full civil war. In his view, fighting Cuman mercenaries was one thing, but Czechs fighting Czechs was quite another.

During the stay at Rocktower Pond, Oats prepared supper for the men while Henry's dog, Mutt, begged nearby for scraps. He could be persuaded to give the dog the last sausage from the supplies, either on the grounds that they were meant to restock at Trosky Castle anyway, or in exchange for his wedding ring, which he had lost to Tankard in a dice the previous day. Later he warned Capon that the open campsite isn't safe for bathing, but Capon ignored his concerns. Oats was killed in the ensuing attack along with the rest of the company, though he was the last to fall.

### Associated quests

- Easy Riders

## Inventory

Note: Character inventories are divided into Equipment, which includes items currently worn or actively used, and Possessions, which can be pickpocketed. Equipment is typically stored in the character's bedside chest overnight.

## Trivia

- Oats knew Capon from the latter's childhood and, despite Capon's carefree attitude, believed he had a good heart.

- He appears to have known Theresa and Miller Peshek. He admired Theresa for saving Henry but considered her uncle a crook.

- In the ambush cutscene, it is shown that the bandits who killed Oats were Adjutant Michael and Kozliek. The latter attacked him from behind while he was distracted by the former; after Oats fell to his knees, Michael run him through with a sword and Kozliek finished him off.

- Oats' shield can be found later at Nebakov Fortress during Back in the Saddle main quest.
