Old Kutna was a mining settlement and likely one of the original settlements associated with silver mining even before the establishment of the town of Kuttenberg in the late 13th century.

It was located on the north-western edge of today's town, as evidenced by records dating back to 1369, and subsequent archaeological surveys, that uncovered the foundations of several buildings. In addition, the Church of All Saints still stands here, originally a Romanesque chapel rebuilt in Gothic style and later rebuilt many more times, so that the only remaining element of the original building is a relief of an angel bearing the town's coat of arms.

## Amenities

- Indulgence chest

- Drying rack

## Residents

- Father Marian

- Taras Mura

- Vladimir

## Associated quests

- The Mouth of Hell

- Post Scriptum

## Old Lhota

Old Lhota is a small homestead in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A very small village north-west of Maleshov; it boasts a few buildings, pasture, and a lumber mill. Its sole non-mill worker resident, Crazy Victor, makes a living from fishing. His fish traps can be found in the stream. There is a large number of poppies in the vegetable beds. Victor did not always live alone, but the other residents have since died. The grave of his child is still well-tended.

### Associated Quests

- The Lion's Den

## Old Olbram

Olbram, otherwise known as Old Olbram, is an elderly man living in Zhelejov in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Olbram lived and worked in Zhelejov as a farmer. He lost most of his teeth and as such spoke with an impediment.

He owned a prize white bull called Arnoshtek that was so valuable that he had his hands watching on guard around the clock so no one would try to steal or otherwise pull pranks on it due to the ongoing feud between his village and Tachov.

## Old Plans

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Old Plans is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 6th quest in the Legacy of the Forge DLC.

## Description

I continue in investigating other components needed to repair the Kuttenberg astronomical clock.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Magdalena and ask her about the clock. She’ll suggest you to to Bailiff Andreas Plümel to let him know your intentions. Head to the town hall and do just that. The door you want should be open and is just past the pillory.

Note: To move to the next objective you will require a certain amount of Prestige, otherwise the bailiff will be reluctant to let you work on something so sensitive. You will have to raise your prestige to level 13. You can do this by completing guild activities, the daily quests that spawn around town.

He'll tell you that there's only one person still alive that ever saw the clock in its original state, Fabrizio 'de Dondi, and you should go talk to him. With a Very Hard speech check, you can also convince the bailiff to give you a reward if you succeed in repairing the clock.

Go see Fabrizio, who will tell you what he knows with a Medium Scholarship check or a Hard Charisma check. If you succeed, he'll say you need: an astrolabe (which you already have - the heart of the clock), a precise set of weights, and a master locksmith.

Return to Magdalena and ask her about the documents she was looking through. It turns out, she's found the schematics for the precise set of weights you're looking for. She also knows of a locksmith in town that might be able to help, Master Prokop Eldris, the gunsmith who runs the foundry in the Hoprink district. When you go speak to Eldris, he will say he's currently unable to help as his apprentice, Pushko, has gone missing and he's too swamped to take on new work. You'll have to go track him down.

### Find Pushko

Head to Grund and talk to the local priest there. The priest will tell you that Pushko came and did his job well, but then lost all his money and Eldris' horse, Bentlie, playing dice with the woodcutters. The priest then saw him walk towards the forest with some rope. Henry will assume this means Pushko went to end his own life. There will be a large search radius, head through the forest until its very southern edge where you'll see Pushko waiting to ambush the woodcutters so he can steal the horse back and run off, wanting to use the rope to trip them. Since that's a terrible plan, you tell him you'll go talk to the woodcutters yourself and get the horse back.

### Get the horse

You can get the horse back with a Very Hard speech or intimidation check, by paying 1000 , or by beating the foreman in a game of dice (you'll need to bet 500 ). Once you've got the horse, return to Pushko and head back to Kuttenberg. After briefly covering for Pushko to Eldris, talk to Pushko about casting the weights for you. Here you'll have the option to invite him to work for you directly as a foundryman at the shop, and if you invite him he'll cast the weights for free.

Note: Like Standa, Pushko is very useful to have around, so it is recommended you bring him on as your own caster though it is not necessary. If you dismiss him, you will not be able to hire him at a later time.

### Cast the weights

Whether you invite Pushko to work at your shop or not, bring him the schematics to get him to begin casting the weights you need for the clock. He'll let you know it'll take him roughly a full day. Return to Pushko to pick up the weights when they're ready and the quest will complete.

## Objectives

## Old Raven

Old Raven is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You found the true Lord of Nebakov.

## Acquisition

This is a missable achievement unlocked during the main quest Back in the Saddle, which takes place at Nebakov Fortress in the southern part of the map. Although everything initially appears normal at the fortress, Henry quickly grows suspicious, triggering optional objectives that uncover the truth behind the situation.

## Tips

As part of the quest, there are two optional objectives:

"Find out more about the Nebakov horses"

- Speak to Adjutant Michael during the sit-down scene and ask where the horses come from.

- Speak with Groom Peltzel, who can be found near the stables. If you fail the speech check when pressing him for more details, he will challenge you to a horse race. Winning the race will grant the necessary information.

- Completing this sequence will resolve the first optional objective and unlock the second.

"Explore the fortress"

- Enter the main tower of the fortress, the jail key is located in a room opposite the entrance. Be cautious, as this area is marked as trespassing.

- Climb to the upper floors of the tower and examine the suspicious suit of armour. Again, this area is restricted, so sneak carefully.

- The entrance to the jail is beneath the main building, a guard is stationed at the outer door. Convince the guard that Lord Jaromier is looking for him. This requires passing a charisma or speech skill check. Or use the tunnel entrance on the far side of the camp to sneak up behind the guard.

- Unlock the jail and speak to the true Lord of Nebakov. Doing so will unlock the achievement.

## Olda of Semine

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Olda Semine is the son of Lord Jan Semine in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Being the son of a noble, Olda was expected to take over his family's land and estate. As such, his father kept him on a short leash, trying to teach him how to manage the estate. He was also trained in combat by Gnarly, and while others, like Tuma, acknowledged that Olda was highly skilled, he had yet to compete in a tournament—largely because his father didn’t want him running around all over the place.

By 1403, Olda was engaged to the local bailiff's daughter, Agnes Thrush, a union that quickly became the talk of the town. The wedding was a grand event, drawing many notable guests, including Otto von Bergow.

## Associated quests

- Wedding Crashers

- Back in the Saddle

- Necessary Evil (Optional)

Olina is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Olina lived in Troskowitz with her family. Her father was Jakesh, who ran a local farm while her mother died from complications related to childbirth of a younger sibling.

## Opatowitz

Opatowitz (Czech: Opatovice) is an abandoned village located north of Sigismund's Camp.

## Codex entry

As the name suggests, the village probably owes its foundation to the abbots (opati) of the nearby Sedletz Monastery, who from the 13th century tried to colonise this inhospitable and sparsely populated region. The first written mention of the village dates back to the latter half of the 14th century, when it belonged to the Kuttenberg burgher Jan Glenc.

The farmstead of Opatowitz was founded sometime during the 14th century by the monastery, which subsequently supported it until it was sold to another wealthy Kuttenberg burgher, Wenceslas Bartosch (Václav Bartoš), in 1379.

## Amenities

- Abandoned building

- Burnt down house

- Drying rack

- Enemy camp

- Hidden chest

- Scholar's spot

## Residents

- Gamekeeper Bohunyek

## Opportunity

Opportunity is a unique melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a shortsword.

## Description

The sword worn by Vauquelin Brabant. He sought opportunities all his life, but the window for him has closed for good.

## Acquisition

- Opportunity can be obtained during the Reckoning main quest. Stay hidden, toss a rock near Brabant to alert him, wait for him to draw his sword, then kill him from afar.

## Opus Magnum

Opus Magnum is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

I stole a document from the Rathaus for Kreyzl and after tasting nitre, I had the feeling regular food would never taste the same. What's next? The miller wanted to get his hands on some kind of alchemy book from Prague which, as chance would have it, has found its way to Trosky Castle.

## Walkthrough

Right after turning in Forbidden Fruit, Kreyzl will give the next thing needed to attend the wedding - a woman that will help with distracting the chamberlain of Trosky, Ulrich. It doesn't really matter if she's a simple woman as he'll also give you a list of items to get to make her stand out and get the chamberlain's attention.

### Finding a companion

You'll be directed to talk to Dorothy at her bathhouse in Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn. However, none of her girls are willing to go with the chamberlain having had bad experiences with him in the past. Dorothy will then direct you to someone who came by, Enneleyn, who might be up for it instead.

Enneleyn is usually near the entrance into the Nomads' Camp. She is clearly well-travelled and experienced in dealing with all sorts of clients. She'll take offence to being told she's basically meant to distract/seduce the chamberlain, but will relent and agree to the job. You can also warn her what the bath girls said, but she'll take it in stride and even become slightly curious about Ulrich now and his peculiar tastes. However, just in case, she always carries a sleeping potion around, but she needs wine for it. You can offer to give her some or try to tell her there will be wine at the wedding.

If you also already obtained everything, you can go straight to giving her each item (dress, perfume, and wine). The next quest/wedding won't start though until you let her know you're ready, so you can give her all these items without worry if you want to finish up other things first.

### Getting the dress

The piece you need, Tyrol brocade cotehardie, is sold by Bartoshek, the tailor in Troskowitz. However, it's about 245 Groschen so if you don't want to spend this kind of money, you'll have to find another way to obtain it.

You can break into his shop during the night and steal it from his shop inventory chest.

### Getting the perfume

To get the perfume, you can either talk to Emmerich first or go talk directly with Betty. In any case, the innkeeper bought the last few bottles the apothecary had and she doesn't really want to part with them. You can try to pass a hard speech check to convince her she doesn't need them, offer to buy it for 499 Groschen, try to steal it, or just go make your own.

If you want to make your own, Emmerich sells the recipe and most of the ingredients are readily available in his garden, with a nearby alchemy bench.

### Getting the wine

If you opted to get Enneleyn wine, she's not picky and will accept any version for this.

### Attending the wedding

At this point, you'll reach the point of no return where you'll have to choose a person with whom to attend the wedding: Kreyzl or Radovan. If you want to go with the blacksmith, you won't be able to do this side quest any further during the wedding. However, you'll be able to continue this later. If you want to go with the miller to the wedding though, this quest will continue at the wedding as soon as you get dressed appropriately and let Enneleyn you're ready to go.

At the wedding with Kreyzl, Ulrich will immediately notice Enneleyn, introduced under another name as a distant association with Kreyzl. Ulrich will try to dismiss you as no longer needed as he'll escort her around instead, but the rest will let you stay. Enneleyn will later leave Ulrich during the wedding, and while not revealing what he wanted her to do, she is disgusted enough she won't go back to him, meaning you'll have to find another way to get the book.

### Finding the book

If you didn't go with Kreyzl to the wedding, the quest will update after you're set to work off your punishment at the beginning of For Whom the Bell Tolls. However, you won't be able to do this until you've finished that quest as the scribe is too busy to talk to during it.

Once that main quest completes, go find and talk to Erazim about the book. He'll reveal Lord Nikvard Libak borrowed it but is long overdue to return it. Due to Nikvard's odd tendencies, the scribe thinks he lost the book and is actively avoiding him. He'll then point you to three others who might know more: the cook, Bertha, the maid, Regina, and a stableboy, Hersh. Note you can likely do this quest in tandem with Ulrich's task, Demons of Trosky, as that will give you full access to the castle without issue and prevent a little less running around for both.

### Asking around

If you talk to the cook, you'll need to either bribe her with 200 Groschen or convince her via a speech check (with the "Listen to me closely" route). If doing the speech route, all options are medium except "the secret will be safe..." which is a hard check. If successful or bribed, she'll reveal Nikvard was having digestive issues and all that entails, so he asked her to discreetly make him some digestive medication. However, one episode caught up to him too quickly so he had an issue in the privies below the guardhouse.

Regina will be a bit annoyed with the topic regarding Nikvard, revealing she has a letter he sent her, despite her not being able to read. Reading it will be rather nonsensical, but reveals he used something from within the book you need but lost said book down the privy's hole.

Hersh meanwhile won't reveal anything unless you pay him a steep fee (5,000 Groschen) or get him a longsword. Note you can lose some reputation a few times with him if you annoy him with trying to talk your way out or call him out on how much money he wants. Once given what he wants, he'll reveal Nikvard wanted him to go retrieve something he lost outside the castle, but ran off before he could tell Hersh exactly what he needed.

### Find the book

With all their information, it points to the book being somewhere outside the castle, below the guards' privies. On the map, this is roughly in the western part of the rocks around the castle. Head out there and you should find a small path that leads you up to the area right below the guardhouse to find Nikvard's body. The book, Lightbringer's secret, is further along, in the small alcove past his body.

### Talk to Kreyzl

After you obtain the book, head back to Kreyzl. Note you can choose to read the book without any consequences, and will give you insight into exactly what the miller is trying to make. Kreyzl will be delighted over getting the book (though understandably confused why it's covered in crap). After a little bit more talk, he'll request you meet him at The Lair where he'll reveal his plans.

At The Lair, you'll be pulled into a long conversation on what the group has really been working towards, with a number of dialogue options you can ask into, like more about Kreyzl's background. Eventually though, it's revealed they're trying to make black powder, or essentially gunpowder. It'll then go to a cutscene with them all trying to test out the completed formula which goes off explosively, knocking out your hearing for a little bit. You'll then automatically receive Recipe for Lead shot gunpowder.

## Oratores

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Oratores is the 24th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Zizka's men took the captive Otto von Bergow from the conquered Maleshov back to Suchdol, where he'll be interrogated. Then we'll decide what to do next.

## Walkthrough

### Interrogate von Bergow

When you are ready, go to Suchdol to meet up with your allies, you can speak with most of them at this point and they will react to what just transpired. Go inside the fortress and talk to Zizka to start interrogating von Bergow. You’ll have the opportunity to pipe up throughout the interrogation, say what you wish.

At the end of the interrogation, the plan is decided. To hit Sigismund where it hurts, you’ll need to steal his silver from the Italian Court in Kuttenberg. It so happens, that that is also where the prisoners taken at Raborsch are being held, so you can free them as well for twice the impact. To get in, you’ll need to impersonate a papal legation and then escape through the tunnels.

Henry’s first order is to get information and the key to the mint from Vavak. To get into town without causing a fuss, you’ll need to sneak in through the tunnels to Ruthard Palace.

### Get into the city

Rosa will insist on leading you through the tunnels to her home. The quest is timed at this point, and waiting too long to talk to Rosa will fail it, but you have time to talk to your allies and stock up on a few things if need be. Talk to her and you’ll travel with her automatically to Kuttenberg after your conversation.

Follow her through the underground, along the way you’ll be able to make some more conversation with her, choices only affect reputation. Eventually, you’ll come to a section where the water is deeper and you’ll have to carry Rosa across. Follow Rosa a short way more and you’ll reach the cellars of her home.

However, you’re not alone. It seems that vagrants have taken up residence in the palace since Bergow’s men ransacked it when they kidnapped Rosa. She insists they have to be killed due to their desecrating her property and the risk of them giving you away if left alive. There’s no convincing her otherwise, Rosa will climb the trellis up to her room to grab her crossbow and you’ll have to move into the courtyard to initiate combat.

There are a lot of them, but they are not well-armed and have no armour. You can lure them into a bottleneck if overwhelmed. Once they are dealt with, Rosa will call out that someone is trying to break into her room. Head inside and deal with the remaining enemies.

Note: Knocking on Rosa’s door will initiate the opportunity to romance her. If you want to loot the bodies and romance her, it’s best to do so before going to talk to her. The cutscene will clean you up and remove your helmet and gauntlets, just in case.

When ready, let Rosa know the coast is clear and she’ll let you into her room. If you romance her, you’ll automatically spend the night with her. If you do not, then you’ll go to sleep in the servants’ quarters after speaking to her.

### Rosa Romance

To romance Rosa you first must have completed her optional quest Rosa's Book. During conversation, respond:

- Either first option.

- Allies are our most valuable asset./It’s not that simple.

- I won’t let you go away!

- (Kiss Rosa)

Other responses can lock you out.

### Get help from Vavak

In the morning, the crew will have arrived. Talk to Zizka to progress in the quest. Once you speak to him the quest will stop being timed for the time being. The next step is getting the mint key from Vavak.

The quest will point you to his house in Kuttenberg, head there during the day to speak to him. As you approach, you’ll notice there are guards outside and not those in Vavak’s colours. Head around the back and get in through an easy locked door.

No one is inside, so feel free to stomp around and loot what you will. Head up the stairs in the room you entered by to find none other than Christian of Pisek. If you agreed to accept the bribe and keep carrying on the embezzlement operation, he’ll agree to help in Vavak’s stead. If you did not accept the bribe, he’ll attack you and you’ll have to defend yourself.

He will give you (or you will rob from his corpse) a Scribbled letter. In it, Vavak has left a clue as to where the key can be found. You’ll find it in the outhouse. Leave through the backdoor you entered through, and investigate the outhouse to your right.

Now that you have the key, head back to Ruthard Palace to regroup with Zizka.

### Explore the tunnels

Zizka will want to hear any information you got from Christian regarding the situation at the Italian Court. After the report, the next order of business is mapping out the route to and from using the underground, so that Brabant’s men can get in.

Since the plan was Rosa’s you’ll be directed to ask her for more details. Exhaust all questions for her, then to talk to Sam to head out. Follow him through the passageway. He’ll stop a couple of times to bring your attention to things. Upon reaching the crypt, you’ll come across some beggars. You can sneak past them, talk to them and convince them to leave, or take them out. Note that, if freed, they will be killed in the courtyard regardless.

Continue on to the end of the accessible path. Here you’ll have to knock on a section of wall that’s discoloured and stands out from the rest. Henry will mark it and then you’ll head back the way you came.

Once back above ground, go and talk to Zizka when you are ready to progress.

### Ambush the cardinal

Zizka will task you with ambushing the cardinal to gain his coerced support. Everyone save Capon, Brabant, and the women, will be heading out the next morning. In the meantime, you can do whatever you’d like including talk to your companions, or you can talk to Dry Devil to skip ahead to the appointed time and leave right away.

After a cutscene you’ll immediately be on horseback in hot pursuit as the cardinal flees. Chase after him, if he gets too far away you’ll have to try again. Once you catch up to him, he’ll die, and you’ll have to change plans. Godwin will be taking over as legate.

Note: Zizka will let you know you’re approaching the point of no return. If you’d like to do anything else before, say you’ll meet them at Ruthard Palace later. As soon as you enter, you’ll be locked in.

### Prepare to infiltrate the Italian Court

At Ruthard Palace, talk to Zizka. He’ll get you up to speed and let you know to talk to Brabant so you can learn a few Italian phrases to pass as a member of the legate’s retinue.

Once you’ve picked up some Italian, you can talk to Brabant again to learn how to compliment someone, then try to impress any or all of the romance options with it, optionally.

Then head to Rosa’s room to change clothes. Note that the disguise will overwrite one of your outfit slots, so choose whichever you’d like to swap out before interacting with the chest. You will automatically be able to switch back later in the next quest.

Note: be sure to clear as much inventory space as possible so you can grab the available loot once you get into the Court. You won't be able to transfer items to your horse once the quest begins. It's recommended to also bring several of the strongest Artemisia potion potions you can craft/find to increase your carry weight temporarily.

Once you’ve dressed and learnt some Italian, all that’s left is to talk to Godwin and let him know you’re ready to leave, ending the quest and immediately starting The Italian Job.

## Objectives

## Bugs

- In the segment Explore the Underground passage with Samuel when you need to have a talk with Samuel he may be walking outside the Ruthard Palace, however if you tell him that you are ready go to the tunnels there an invisible wall appears around the palace and you will not be able to come inside.

## Ore merchant Hermann

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Ore merchant Hermann (Czech: Rudokupec Heřman) was an assayer responsible for evaluating ore quality and determining its price at the royal mines near Horschan.

## Involvement

He was an accomplice in a scheme to embezzle king's silver, working alongside head foreman Fett. The two collaborated to underreport the amount of ore extracted and divert the unrecorded silver. Hermann was paid from the extra groschen provided by Grund's smelting works, helping to maintain the illusion of legitimate transactions. Later he insisted he was dragged into the scheme by Fett who came up to him with the idea first.

Although complicit in the fraud, Hermann was spared punishment when Christian of Pisek made sure to protect him and Fett from consequences - on the condition that they remain silent and do not alert the higher conspirators, especially Ulrich Vavak, the mint master behind the scheme.

In the end, he had to flee for his life. After the workers found Fett on the spoil tip with his neck broken, Hermann disappeared in the middle of the day. He was last seen on the road to Grund riding with haste. Christian of Pisek suggested that it was likely Hermann had told someone that the scheme had been uncovered, and Fett paid the price for it.

### Associated quest

- Via Argentum

## Original Gunslinger

Original Gunslinger is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You got four loaded hand cannons ready.

## Acquisition

The Original Gunslinger achievement is unlocked by equipping and loading four firearms available in the game at once.

- To start, you'll need a Noble's belt, which can be purchased from tailors in Kuttenberg, if you didn't have it already. This particular belt increases the number of quick-select weapon slots to four, which is essential for the achievement.

- Next, head to Hoprink, a district located just southeast of Kuttenberg's city walls. There, just south of The Hole in the Wall tavern, you'll find Master Prokop Eldris, the local gunsmith.

- Buy four firearms (or three, if you already have one), equip them all via the quick-select slots, and begin loading them one by one. After the fourth weapon is fully loaded, the achievement will unlock.

## Tips

- The type of firearm doesn't matter. Any combination will count, as long as all four are equipped and loaded.

- Before making any purchases, it's strongly advised to save your game by exiting to the main menu - there's no practical reason to own four guns during normal gameplay, so this will help avoid wasting Groschen.

## Ostraconophobia

Ostraconophobia is a hidden achievement introduced in Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Description

You were nipped to death by crayfish.

## Acquisition

The Ostraconophobia achievement can be unlocked during the Our Daily Bread quest, which must be started right after completing Anamnesis. Progress through the quest until you speak to Cellarius Julian in the monastery kitchen.

You will receive an optional objective to find a book, titled Crayfish, the poor man's salmon. It is located on the first shelf to the left as you enter the library. Read it fully to get the objective "Catch crayfish".

Afterward, continue catching crayfish until one of them finally kills Henry to unlock the achievement.

## Tips

- Crayfish will not always pinch on the first try, so drop and pick them up repeatedly.

- To speed things up, lower Henry's health by jumping from a high spot, but be careful of bleeding - he must die from the crayfish pinch to unlock the achievement. Make a save beforehand.

- You can also poison yourself with Bane poison via food or alcohol in your inventory and then cure yourself with a Digestive potion once your health is low enough

- The crayfish pinch does 8 points of damage

- The perks Revenant and Revenant II make it trickier to die to the pinch due to regenerating up to 50/75 health respectively, so drinking a Lethean water to reset these perks will make things easier

## Trivia

- Ostraconophobia comes from two Greek words: "ostrakon" (ὄστρακον), meaning shell or shellfish, and "phobos" (φόβος), meaning fear. Therefore, the term literally means "fear of shellfish."

## Our Daily Bread

Our Daily Bread is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC after Anamnesis.

## Description

As the number of sick increases, supplies are starting to run low. And the cellarius is getting stricter about rations. If the sick in the infirmary are to last, we’ll need to get more food.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Denes Latzkfi to start the quest. He'll tell you that Cellarius Julian is causing issues with supplies, as he wants to ration in such a way that disadvantages the infirmary. You'll offer to try to convince the cellarer to change his mind.

You’ll find Julian in the monastery kitchens during the day. Talk to him and he’ll explain they have about two to three weeks worth of supplies. Offer to help, and he’ll ask you to take care of some magpies and get his spectacles back from their nest. He’ll mention as well that the man who was cellarius during the outbreak of the Black Death wrote a manuscript detailing how he was able to ration effectively.

To get his spectacles back head to the garden in the cloister, you’ll have to knock the nest out of the tree in the centre there. You can do so by throwing a coin at it from stealth. Once you have them, return them to Julian for some extra supplies for the infirmary.

Head to the library, and you’ll find the book he mentioned on the lower part of the first shelf to your left, titled Crayfish the poor man's salmon. Once you read it, you should go catch some crayfish. They can be found out on the east or west grounds in ponds and hatcheries. The hatcheries are the best place to look, as you have three ponds all connected.

Get into the water and pick them up; you’ll have to wander around until you find them, as they’ll be spread about. When you get close to one, you should hear a clicking noise. To unlock the achievement Ostraconophobia, you must be pinched to death by the crayfish upon picking them up (each has a chance to pinch you, inflicting a small amount of damage). Once you have enough, hand over all the supplies to Denes, including the book, to end the quest.

## Objectives

## Overkill

Overkill is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You pulverized a rabbit with a gunshot.

## Acquisition

The Overkill achievement is awarded for killing a rabbit (technically a hare) using a firearm.

To unlock the achievement, you must use Scatter shot ammunition. Standard Lead ball will not trigger the achievement, even if it kills the target. The type of firearm used does not matter - any firearm is valid as long as Scatter shot is equipped.

While hares can be found in most deer hunting areas, one of the most reliable spots is in the woods east of Bylany, just north of the stream near the deer hunting grounds. The terrain here lacks tall grass, offering better visibility and making it easier to track and shoot hares.

## Tips

To maximize your chances:

- Arrive at the location around 10:00 AM.

- Create a manual save.

- Use the "Skip Time" function to advance time in one-hour intervals.

- When a hare appears, attempt a shot.

- If unsuccessful, wait another hour and try again.

- Repeat the process until roughly 7:00 PM. If no kill is registered by then, reload your save and try again.

Shooting accuracy is affected by terrain and stance:

- When crouching, aim slightly above the hare.

- When shooting uphill, aim higher to compensate for elevation.

- When shooting downhill, a direct center shot is more likely to connect.

## Pagan burial ground

Pagan burial ground is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Deep in the woods of Lower Semine lies an old Pagan burial ground. Though it is not known who might have been buried here, they seem to have been important figures. Around the graves grow many wildflowers including marigolds.

Each of the three graves is marked and inside the grave, stones were laid around the deceased’s head to indicate their relative importance. The goods they were buried with suggest this as well, increasing in luxury as the stones increase.

## Loot

You will need a spade to rob the graves.

### 3 stones

- Brass brooch with lettering

- Groschen x2

- Weak Mintha perfume

### 5 stones

- Dagger

- Groschen x2

- Wolf fangs

### 7 stones

- Weak Saviour Schnapps

- Groschen x2

- Devil's head die

Pagan shrine is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. There are three such points of interest.

At a nameless spring, an old pagan shrine sits in neglect having been forgotten. Only one idol still keeps its form, but it lays in the stream having broken off its base.

## Painted

Painted is a hidden achievement introduced in Brushes with Death.

## Description

But not paid for.

## Acquisition

This achievement is unlocked during the Stained Honour quest. You'll have to deface Voyta's fresco instead of getting the Lapis lazuli stone. Or you can do both.

## Tips

- During the quest, the dishonest bailiff of Pschitoky will refuse to hand over the lapis lazuli until Henry helps him first. While it is possible to pickpocket the stone right away, doing so will prevent the achievement from unlocking.

- Instead, go along with the bailiff’s scheme until you have the opportunity to speak with Adela of Mnischek. Once you do, reveal the plan and agree to her alternative. The bailiff will be furious after you beat him and refuse to hand over the stone, but Adela will reward you with a generous sum of Groschen. Afterward, you can explain that you still need the payment. She won't object to Henry stealing the stone and will even offer help - telling you that if her guard (usually stationed inside the fortress near the fresco room) gives you any trouble, you can send him directly to her.

- Now wait until nightfall, then head to the bailiff's room on the second floor to the right and "enhance" the fresco. The achievement should unlock at this point. Afterward, pickpocket the lapis lazuli from the sleeping bailiff.

- When you return to Voyta, avoid mentioning that you took the stone. If you do, he'll be upset that you both stole it and defaced the fresco. After the quest is done you're free to sell the precious lapis lazuli.

## Trivia

- The pavise was a large, square, and convex shield used during the late 14th to early 16th centuries by archers, crossbowmen, and infantry soldiers. It was usually large enough to cover the entire body. While reloading their weapons, archers and crossbowmen would crouch behind them to shelter against incoming missile attacks.

- During a siege, the pavise was often carried by a specialist pavise-bearer, who held it in place or deployed it in the ground with a spike attached to the bottom.

- The name pavise (or pavis, pabys, or pavesen) comes from the city of Pavia, Italy.

## Pasha

Pasha is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Pasha was a bandit in a band under the leadership of Karel Arrowhead. Pasha accidentally shot the arrow that lodged itself in Karel's head lending him his nickname during a raid.

Sometime later, Pasha suggested the band take on a riskier target than usual since he thought it would be easy money due to a high ratio of loot to guards. Unfortunately, the raid did not go well and Karel was killed, leaving Pasha the leader of the band.

Believing that Karel's arrow was imbued with magical protective power, Pasha wanted to have that for himself along with the symbolic passing of the torch. He went to the Devil's Den inn along with another bandit, Hare to find someone who could help them get it back from wherever Karel had been buried.

Pasha enlisted Henry to help. When Henry recovered the arrow, Pasha asked Henry to shoot him with it like he shot Karel to complete the cycle. If Henry agreed, Pasha died instantly.

### Associated quests

## Pavlena

Pavlena is the adoptive daughter of Bozhena in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Pavlena's biological mother died during childbirth with Pavlena. With her father not in the picture, Bozhena, who was the town's midwife, took the baby girl in and raised her as her own. As such, as she grew up, Bozhena would take Pavlena with her when she was called on as needed by the women in the area.

While Pavlena was still really young, one fateful night Bozhena was called on by another villager, Jakesh, to assist his wife, Ludmila, who'd been in labour for several hours already. However, he had sent for assistance too late and Ludmila ended up giving birth to a stillborn baby boy before she herself died from the exhaustion. Bozhena could only helplessly stand by but Jakesh, not realizing his son had been stillborn, accused Bozhena of having damned his son for not christening him before death, and letting his wife die. He riled up the rest of the town and they drove Bozhena out of town with Pavlena.

Bozhena was then forced to live in isolation with Pavlena in a small hut out in the forest, making due with what they could forage from the land. As Pavlena grew older, she took to making baskets to sell in town to help out, as at least the villagers didn't blame her for what happened that fateful night as she'd only been a little girl. On her first visit to Troskowitz with the baskets though, she met Roman, a local woodcutter, and the two immediately took a liking to each other. Over time, their relationship grew, though she kept this a secret from her mother, afraid Bozhena might think she was going to leave her behind. When Pavlena found out she was pregnant, she and Roman planned to run off and get married and move somewhere else, making sure that they'd bring Bozhena along.

One day as she returned home, she found two injured men, Hans Capon and Henry, with her mother, who explained how they'd been attacked a few nights ago, but Bozhena had managed to save them. The two men then set off for their destination shortly after, thanking the women for their hospitality.

A short time later, Pavlena headed to Troskowitz to sell some baskets and meet up with Roman. However, plans went awry when the two met up as some of Jakesh's hired hands ambushed them, accidentally killing Roman in the process. Not knowing what else to do, one took Pavlena captive while the other hastily tried to bury Roman.

If Henry manages to find and save Pavlena:

Thanks to Henry, Pavlena was found and reunited with her mother. However, now realizing there was still clear animosity from Jakesh against Bozhena which caused her boyfriend's death, the two women had enough and asked Henry to do something about Jakesh, as otherwise they'd never know peace.

If Henry decides not to help Bozhena and Pavlena:

Pavlena ends up being executed by hanging by Troskowitz bailiff, while Bozhena hangs herself in her hut.

### Associated quests

- Fortuna

- Bad Blood

## Pebbles

Pebbles (Czech: Šedivka) is a horse in Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance

The mare is granted to Henry by Sir Hanush of Leipa as a reward at the start of The Hunt Begins, for saving the life of Sir Hans Capon. She comes equipped with a plain saddle and a plain bridle.

### Quests

- The Hunt Begins

### Notes

- Although the quest requires you to mount Pebbles, if you already have a horse, Pebbles won't replace it, unless you want to. In this case you'll have to take it to a horse trader.

- If you decide to not make Pebbles your horse, it will remain at the Neuhof stables after the completion of the The Hunt Begins.

- If you want to go to Neuhof on your own horse, mount Pebbles, dismount again and then mount your horse. Pebbles will remain in the courtyard for the rest of the game.

- If you leave Pebbles standing in the courtyard or at Neuhof, because you already have a horse, you can still use it at a later date, but you can't access its saddle bags or call it by whistling as your own horse would react to the call.

- Even if Pebbles isn't the strongest or the fastest horse in the game, it is given to Henry for free, and is for most players their first one.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Pebbles returns as Henry's mount in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

After the group's camp is ambushed at the start, one of the bandits takes Pebbles to sell to the horse seller in Semine for a few Groschen. You can likewise happen across her in the pasture, where Henry will instantly recognize her, or by talking to the seller who'll mention several tidbits that make you aware it's your horse. You can then either try to buy her back or, for relatively low speech checks, convince him to give you Pebbles for free.

While her stats aren't the greatest, if you ride her for about 35 kilometers, you'll eventually unlock the Good Old Pebbles perk, which will greatly increase her stats.

## Trivia

- Like the other horses, Pebbles is listed as an Easter egg.

- Pebbles may refer to the real Pebbles, a famous British-bred Thoroughbred race horse.

## Penitent One

Penitent One is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You made the penitential pilgrimage.

## Acquisition

Successfully completing the Pilgrimage task unlocks the Penitent One achievement. The quest first becomes available after completing the main quest For Whom the Bell Tolls, when you gain unrestricted access to Trosky Castle.

Speak with Father Nicodemus, who offers Henry the chance to seek redemption through a penitential pilgrimage. This task involves traveling to a randomly selected shrine marked on the map, where Henry must pray to complete the task.

If you have already moved to the Kuttenberg region, any priest encountered can offer the opportunity to begin the pilgrimage.

## Tips

- It is not necessary to commit any crimes for the quest to become available. The priest will express surprise and approval at Henry's piety and will still offer the opportunity to undertake the pilgrimage, sending him to pray at a shrine regardless of his criminal record.

## Pilgrimage

Pilgrimage is an optional task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It can be used to increase your reputation in either region and is infinitely repeatable.

## Trosky

After completing the main quest For Whom the Bells Tolls and gaining access to Trosky Castle, find and talk to Father Nicodemus to request a pilgrimage. He'll then send you out to a random shrine in the area to do so.

## Kuttenberg

Speak to any priest in the region and request a pilgrimage. He will send you out to a random shrine in the region.

## Objective

Note there's only one objective given per pilgrimage, but the location can vary each time you do one

- Pray at the conciliation cross in the clearing near the stream.

- Pray at the stone conciliation cross outside Slatego.

## Pistole

Pistole is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as the ranged weapon type.

## Description

A handgonne is a firearm that uses gunpowder to shoot small pieces of metal or stone. A thick metal barrel with a handle is attached to a wooden stock, similar to a spear, for example. Fire through the powder stopper detonates the main charge in the barrel and shoots the projectile out. It is fired by a lit cord, a red-hot iron wire or in a worst case scenario, a burning stick. This handgonne has a barrel forged from iron and is therefore less durable than those cast from bronze. Any living being hit with this weapon is sure to no longer be living.

## Poet's Gut

Poet's Gut is a hidden achievement introduced in Brushes with Death.

## Description

Every strophe is a work of art.

## Acquisition

The Poet's Gut achievement is unlocked during the Source of Inspiration quest. You'll have to impress the old woman Kvyetoslava with your poetry.

## Tips

- Go along with all of Kvyetoslava's requests. Before returning her mended dress, make sure you have at least 20 levels in Scholarship and 19 levels in Charisma.

- Return the dress to her. After she puts it on, she will ask Henry to recite a poem. You must pass all four skill checks in succession to unlock a unique dialogue with her afterward.

- Don't pick the non-skill dialogues because these will void the trophy. If you fail a skill check it also voids the trophy.

## Popinjay Shoot (Quest)

For the codex entry see Popinjay Shoot.

Popinjay Shoot is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is automatically available following Striped Tonies.

## Description

Every mine shaft in Kuttenberg has been getting ready for the miners' annual popinjay competition. Foreman Vlach invited me to come watch their champion Anton Kaspar win. The competition takes place in the morning at the shooting range in Hoprink.

## Walkthrough

Immediately upon finishing Striped Tonies, this quest will appear in your journal. In the morning, head to the shooting range in Hoprink. Anton will not be able to shoot for the Tonies, so Vlach will ask you to compete for them in his stead.

What follows is a regular popinjay shooting contest. You'll have to score at least 4 to beat the competition with 9 arrows. Win or lose, the competition will end and you can gather your reward from Vlach. If you refuse the money he offers you, he will give you a unique version of the Miner's Cap.

## Objectives

## Portrait in Red

Portrait in Red is the 4th quest of the Brushes with Death DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the final quest in the Trosky region.

## Description

The painter Voyta is deeply troubled, and it seems that a killer by the name of Burkhard, who recently arrived here, is the cause. He murders people in a brutal manner, and considering that there is a bounty on his head from the Bailiff of Troskowitz, Thrush, it’s worth my while to go and deal with him. Perhaps that way, I can finally get some important answers from Voyta.

## Synopsis

Henry returns to the painter’s studio in Trosky Castle and Voyta is excited to get his opinion on a new sword he’s acquired. Henry asks why he’s even got one to which Voyta replies that he is preparing for his final work in the region – a duel to the death.

The man he wants to duel is called Burkhard; he’s a thief, a bandit, and a murderer with a bounty on his head. Henry is confused why Voyta would suddenly want to dispatch justice in the region but Voyta tells him it’s not about the region, it’s about his own sanity.

It turns out Burkhard is that very same acquaintance Voyta had mentioned needing to meet the last time he and Henry spoke. Burkhard, Voyta says, is a vile man known for beating people to death with his distinctive helmet using a special notch on it for that very purpose. When Voyta first heard he was in the area, he tried to leave, but was nearly hit by an arrow which he took as a sign he had to stay and get rid of Burkhard. The voice in his head that has been telling him to kill Burkhard refuses to be silent, so Voyta has been trying many varied remedies including the basilisk egg and visiting the shrine, but none of them have thus far worked.

Henry decides to take on Burkhard himself one way or another; Burkhard will no doubt have men along with him but since he recruits the young and vulnerable, Voyta asks that Henry spare them if at all possible. He holed up somewhere in Apollonia, though Voyta does not know exactly where he expects they should be easy to find.

Once Burkhard is dealt with, Henry returns and gives Voyta the helmet. Voyta is disappointed not to feel the relief he was hoping for, instead feeling the same emptiness as always, but he is still grateful for Henry’s help, painting Burkhard's helmet and giving it to Henry as a gift.

Henry may push Voyta for more information, but Voyta is still reluctant to talk about his past, answering only cryptically. He recognises that Henry deserves better answers, but he finds it difficult to open up so far from home. With his work in the Trosky region complete, he decides he will be heading home soon – to Kuttenberg.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Voyta in his studio to start the quest. He’ll ask you to take care of Burkhard but spare his men.

The camp is located just off the road near the south end of the search radius, essentially right where the marker is. As Voyta suggested, you should be able to hear them as you approach as the camp will be singing loudly as a group during the day.

There are a few ways to go about taking Burkhard out; you can:

- Kill Burkhard in stealth

- Kill Burkhard openly

- Challenge Burkhard to a duel to the death

- Spare Burkhard

### Kill Burkhard in stealth

Wait until nightfall, Burkhard will go to sleep and you can stealth kill him in bed. There will be sentries wandering about, but as long as you have dark, quiet clothing and a relatively decent stealth level you should be fine.

The camp is in two sections, and Burkhard will sleep near the campfire and cooking pot farthest back from the road under a lean-to of tree branches. There will be a member of his group sitting near the campfire close to him. Depending on your stealth level you may need to subdue him, Voyta would prefer you leave him alive.

### Kill Burkhard openly

You can attack head-on during the day, this will create a large fight as he has many men. If you’re lucky, you may be able to take him out first which will cause the rest of his men to flee.

### Challenge Burkhard to a duel

You can take Burkhard on in single combat to the death. Approach him at the camp during the day and talk to him. You will have to pass skill checks in order for him to agree to the duel, otherwise, the entire band will become hostile. Once you win the duel, his men will flee.

### Spare Burkhard

During the night, sneak into the camp and steal Burkhard’s helmet from a chest near where he sleeps. You can then lie to Voyta and say you killed him.

The camp is in two sections, and Burkhard will sleep near the campfire and cooking pot farthest back from the road under a lean-to of tree branches. His chest can be found opposite him on the other side of a rock. It is a medium locked chest and you can pickpocket the keys for it if need be. The item you are looking for is called Killer's helmet.

Sparing Burkhard will earn you the achievement Vengeance Solves Nothing.

### Return to Voyta

However you deal with Burkhard, take his helmet back to Voyta at Trosky. If you spared Burkhard, you will have to pass a medium speech check to lie and say you killed him. Voyta will be somewhat disappointed no matter what, lacking the relief he was hoping for.

He will then ask what you did with the gang. If you spared them, this will earn some reputation and you will lose some if you killed them. He will then paint the helmet and give it back to you turning it into the Murderer's painted helmet, ending the quest.

Voyta will mention leaving for Kuttenberg, but he will stay in the Trosky region until you leave, allowing you to still access his shield painting.

## Post Scriptum

Post Scriptum is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

Knowing how to read and write is the privilege of priests and lords. But who should a commoner turn to when he needs to write a letter? To me, for instance!

## Walkthrough

Talk to Kvyetoslav at the inn just west of Kuttenberg to start the quest. He wants you to write a letter for him and will tell you to find his office in the Miners’ Quarter of the city and to expect two of his colleagues to be there instead of him.

### Write the Letter

Head to the Miners’ Quarter and you’ll find the house as indicated, the gate to get into the yard is facing the city wall. Go upstairs and inside to find Ranyek and Myslibor who will ask for the password:

- Justice is worth more than silver

Note: Failing the password will only result in some reputation loss.

The pair will argue over how to write the letter in a cutscene interspersed with Henry’s comments. You will be given a few medium scholarship checks. You can go with whatever you wish but making them more refined/improving will gain reputation. If you keep asking, eventually they will tell you what went down with Markhold, the man to whom the letter is addressed.

Once the letter is written, the men will insist they have to kill you since you know too much. This can be prevented with a medium speech or hard intimidation check. Otherwise, they will initiate combat and need to be killed in turn.

From this point you’ll have a choice whether side with the miners, side with Markold, or report the miners to the bailiff.

### Side with the Miners

Take the letter to its addressee as advised. Markold lives between two cobblers on the street with the grocers west of the town hall. Go inside and speak to the man standing next to the stairs, if you hesitate you will be warned as a trespasser. He will give you permission to head upstairs and you’ll find Markold at the room behind the stairs.

Tell him some fellow sent you and deliver the letter. Markold will release the miners he had taken captive and tell you you can find them at the Hloushetz Gate. This gate is just north of his house. Head there and you should see the miners there, if you are too fast they should show up within an hour. Talk to them and you can travel with them to their camp, or say you’ll meet them there later.

Once at the camp, talk to Myslibor and Markold will attack. Defend the camp and once Markold and his men are defeated, speak to Myslibor to get your reward of 150 and end the quest. You can use a medium speech check to increase your reward to 225 .

### Side with Markold

Take the letter to its addressee as advised. Markold lives between two cobblers on the street with the grocers west of the town hall. Go inside and speak to the man standing next to the stairs, if you hesitate you will be warned as a trespasser. He will give you permission to head upstairs and you’ll find Markold at the room behind the stairs.

When talking to him, say you want to work together against the miners. He will bring you along to attack their camp. Once they are defeated, he’ll reward you, ending the quest.

### Turn the Miners in

To turn the miners in, simply report to the bailiff at the Rathaus and let him know of the situation. He will thank you for your duty and reward you with 100 , ending the quest.

## Potions/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Potions and poisons return in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

Potions can help across a variety of skills based on the potion, or help with healing (or even hangovers). Poisons on the other hand are meant to be used against enemies to weaken them in some manner. Some poisons are better suited for putting in cooking pots while others are better to put on one's weapon.

They come in three basic qualities: weak, regular, and strong, with stronger versions being more potent than weaker types:

- Weak occurs when a few steps may have been done incorrectly during the brewing process and/or with low quality ingredients.

- Regular can occur when all steps are done correctly but only used dried ingredients.

- Strong can only occur when steps are done correctly and at least one fresh ingredient was used.

A fourth quality, Henry's, is achievable with the perk Secret of Secrets. It is available from level 16 in Alchemy. With the perk, the fourth quality is available when all the steps are followed correctly and fresh ingredients are used.

## Prevention

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Prevention is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC after Anamnesis.

## Description

If the plague really is in the monastery, it would be wise to prepare for it.

## Walkthrough

To protect yourself as you are digging around the monastery, Zacharias suggests you make a plague mask. To do so, you'll need mint and/or sage, aromatic oil, a rope, and some leather.

The herbs can be found in the monastery gardens. Note that you'll need different herbs to make the aromatic oil, so be sure to gather some chamomile and valerian as well. If you did Maddening Pain, you may still have valerian from that.

Flax rope can be found around the construction site or workers' camp usually lying on the ground. It may be hard to find, and some false positives may happen.

Leather can be found in various places, usually in chests, also at the construction site or workers' camp. Basically, you are looking for any animal skin that would otherwise be used for blacksmithing. One pig skin is on a table to the right of the main entrance to the cloister building.

The recipe for aromatic oil can be found in the library. You can talk to Librarian Crispin and ask him for help, passing a hard speech, scholarship, or alchemy check will convince him. He’ll direct you to the stand where it can be found. It is just to his right, at the back of the room, read the book and you’ll learn the recipe for Essential oil. The recipe calls for:

- OleumOleumOil base

- Chamomile × 3

- Sage × 1

- Valerian × 1

Add the chamomile and boil for 3 turns. Grind the sage and add to the cauldron, boil for 1 turn. Grind the valerian and add to the cauldron, pour.

Once you have all the supplies, head to the alchemy room in the infirmary. Interact with the table to put them all together to make the Plague hood and end the quest. To create the hood, 8 total samples of mint and/or sage are required; any combination will work, including using solely one or the other.

## Primum Nil Nocere

Primum Nil Nocere is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

I offered to try to help Peter, the husband of the farmer Mlada from Suchdol.

## Walkthrough

Henry can pick this task up by agreeing to help Mlada's husband during The Thunderstone.

After accepting the quest and asking Mlada about Peter, go examine him. To diagnose him, pass one or more of: an Easy Strength check to examine him by touch, a Hard Vitality check, or a Hard Agility check.

Ultimately, Peter simply has anxiety, and a chamomile decoction and a good night's sleep should fix him up. Hand over the potion, and if you can pass any of the other skill checks choose those options as well (Pray, Change Diet, Cast a Spell, Advice on dealing with fear) and wait one day then talk to Mlada to complete the task and receive the Thunderstone.

## Pschitoky

Pschitoky (Czech: Přítoky) is a village located northeast of Miskowitz and west of Kuttenberg.

## Codex entry

The first written mention of the village Pschitoky dates back to 1141, according to which it was in possession of the Olomouc archdiocese. In 1249, Pschitoky was briefly held by Havel of Löwenberk, and a year later the Olomouc bishop Bruno of Schauenberk ceded the village to the Sedletz Monastery.

In the 14th century, the farmstead and part of the village belonged to various patrician families from Kuttenberg, such as Ondřej Puša, under whom a Gothic fortress was added. In 1397, Wenceslas Bartosch (Václav Bartoš) became the owner, and pledged to pay a permanent fee to the Kuttenberg almshouse from the farmstead.

After the Hussite Wars, Hanush Ferydan held Pschitoky, burdening the farmstead and fortress with many debts which he refused to pay, so in 1443 the chief Mint Master decided that Hanush and his descendants 'from now and for all time' had to pay 50 dozen groschen to the Kuttenberg almshouse every year. The last burgher to own Pschitoky was Voršila Cihelníková, who sold the estate to Václav Materna of Květnice in 1501. The Maternas rebuilt the Gothic fortress in the Renaissance style.

To this day, only the Gothic vaulted cellar remains, though in a very poor condition.

## Quarry below Trosky

Quarry below Trosky is a minor location in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

This used to be a quarry to help build Trosky Castle, but after it was completed, the quarry was abandoned. It's now used by a hunter, Bohumir, for an archery range.

## Madman's treasure

There is a nearby location, Vagrant's hut, where a madman is known to still be digging around the quarry. Speaking with the hunter will reveal that supposedly the madman and a friend of his had stashed their savings away in a secret spot in the quarry many years ago, but only the friend knew the location. Unfortunately, the friend died from an accident, leaving the madman to try and search hopelessly for his lost money.

The money itself is real: on the left side of the quarry, against the rocky walls is a ladder. Climb up it and you should see to the left a flat area with a wooden beam sticking out over the quarry. Climb over to this area and examine the leafy pile near the tree up here to find 549 Groschen. You can either choose to keep it or go speak to the madman to return it to him for some reputation.

## Quests/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Quests in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II are divided into three main categories: main quests, side quests, and tasks (known as activities in the previous game). The game features two primary regions: Trosky (the starting area) and Kuttenberg (unlocked after completing the main quest Storm), each containing distinct questlines and optional content.

The main storyline progresses through 32 sequential main quests. Side quests offer optional narratives, while activities are shorter, often repeatable, objectives. Many quests are missable, as certain side content becomes unavailable after progressing past specific points in the main questline. Notable points of no return include the beginning of Necessary Evil main quest in Trosky and Oratores main quest in Kuttenberg.

- Main quests are the quests that form the main storyline. There are 32 main quests, with 12 in the Trosky region and 20 in the Kuttenberg region.

- Side quests are optional quests, with one notable exception: three quests from the Miller questline or three quests from the Blacksmith questline are necessary to gain access to the Semine wedding. Markers for taking other quests are available when you ask an innkeep or other quest tipper about them. There are 43 side quests, with 18 in the Trosky region and 25 in the Kuttenberg region.

- Tasks are often fetch quests or fighting activities. Completing tasks generally increases your reputation. There are 54(?) tasks as of game version 1.2.4.

This page catalogues all quests in the game, organized by type. Main quests are presented in chronological order, while side quests and activities are listed alphabetically.

## Quiet as a Church Mouse

Quiet as a Church Mouse is a hidden achievement introduced in Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Description

The knights never had to escort you to the infirmary.

## Acquisition

To unlock the achievement Quiet as a Church Mouse, you must complete the entire DLC without being caught by guards and sent back to the infirmary. The trophy unlocks after the final quest, The Time Has Come, when you leave the Sedletz Monastery.

After the Anamnesis quest, the monastery is on lockdown with curfew and patrolling guards. Being spotted and escorted back will void the achievement, but being chased does not. If seen, either escape to areas not under curfew (e.g., library, monks' quarters, cellar) or reload your last save.

## Tips

- Equipping a dark outfit with low visibility can make stealth easier. Additionally, you can throw rocks to distract guards in your path.

- During the quest Seek and you Shall Find, no matter what choices you make, you will automatically be escorted back to the infirmary at the end of the quest. This is part of the story and does not affect the trophy.

## Rabstein ruin

For the codex entry, see Codex entry: Rabstein.

Rabstein ruin is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Looming over the meadows and cow pastures near Maleshov sits the ruin of Rabstein. An old, ruined fort, it has been occupied by a group of bandits and a reclusive Alchemist. Most of the structure has crumbled, only pieces of its outer wall and the skeleton of its main tower remain. The bandits are working on repairing portions of it, stripping and forming wood. The alchemist is working on esoteric experiments in his art.

## Racing the Leech

Racing the Leech is a hidden achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You won a race against the guard nicknamed Leech.

## Acquisition

The Racing the Leech achievement is unlocked by beating the guard known as Leech in a horse race during the quest Martin's Dream. It is missable since the situation can be resolved in ways that avoid the race entirely.

To challenge him, choose the dialogue path:

- "You want money from Standa?"

- "Would you take a bet for it?"

- "I'm all about racing."

- "I'm in (500)"

Then win the race to unlock the trophy.

## Tips

- Leech rides a very quick horse, so boosting your own speed is important. Use a fast mount with quality tack and keep horse armour to a minimum.

- The Aesop potion as well as the Head Start and Head Start II perks can also give you an edge.

## Ransom

Ransom is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It has two possible starting points, as a random encounter along the road to Danemark and as a marked innkeeper tipster quest at the inn west of Kuttenberg.

## Description

Jan of Suchotlesky has sent me in his name to negotiate the release of his brother, a knight who is help captive in Sigismund’s camp.

## Walkthrough

Wherever you find Jan of Suchotlesky, be it on the road or at the inn you’ll have to heal him before the quest can start in earnest. Examine his wounds and ask him about his injuries – you’ll need a medium survival check for the ribs and medium thievery to take off his boot then another medium survival check for the ankle and an easy thievery check for the toes. You’ll need a bandage for his ankle, alcohol for his toes, and Embrocation for his ribs.

Once he’s been treated he will ask you for help, starting the quest. He needs you to go to Sigismund's camp and negotiate for his brother Peter’s release. Agree to help and he will give you a letter.

### Find Peter

Head to the camp and look for Peter. In order to get a good idea of where to look, there are a few people around the camp you can ask – Father Bohumil, Musa, and Milada the bathhouse owner. Each of them will narrow down the search area a little with a speech check.

The tent that houses captives can be found on the east side of the search radius, south of the north gate. There will be guards in front of it and it is considered a private area, so you’ll have to sneak in from behind. Talk to the man inside and you’ll find out he isn’t Peter, but after giving him some meat or passing a medium presence check he’ll tell you that Peter is already dead. His body is being kept on a cart near the bathhouse.

### Find Lázsló

László can be found in his tent in the Cuman area of the camp. It is red and any Cuman in the area will direct you towards it if you ask. Whether or not you tell Lázsló about having discovered Peter, he will insist on doing the exchange as originally planned. You can try to offer neutral ground, but he will ultimately choose the area.

### Return to Jan and Prepare

Head to the inn west of Kuttenberg to talk to Jan. He’ll want to take revenge upon hearing of his brother’s death and you’ll be given an opportunity to gather allies to stand a chance against László’s forces.

You can recruit any of the following if you have already completed their associated quest(s):

- Kubyenka and Adder (The Devil's Pack)

- Arne the German (Ars Dimicatoria)

- Hog and Goliath (The Spark)

- Mercenaries from Mezholes (Burnt Mezholes)

- Jan Posy of Zimburg and Miroslav 'Tugbone' of Zimburg (Bellatores)

- Mikesh and Kozliek (Fortuna)

Once you have your allies, tell Jan you’re ready to head out.

### Fight

You can choose to side with either László or Jan at this point. The main difference is the reward after, though László may be the more difficult fight depending on your allies and how many you were able to recruit.

### Get your Reward

Depending on whom you sided with, your rewards will be different.

If you side with Jan, you’ll get Peter’s sword off the back of the cart, plus whatever you loot from enemies. Taking Peter’s shield or chest armour will result in Jan becoming upset.

If you side with László, you’ll get Peter’s sword along with his armour, plus whatever you loot from Jan.

## Recipe Book/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

The Recipe Book catalogues all the alchemical brews that Henry has learned. Each entry includes the potion’s name, its effects, required ingredients, and step-by-step brewing instructions. Recipes are automatically added after you study them for the first time. This section serves as a convenient reference at the alchemy bench, helping you craft potions accurately and efficiently.

## Aesop potion

Increases riding and dog-handling skills. If good quality, animals will take less notice of you and dogs won't bark at you.

Ingredients

- SpiritusSpiritusSpirits base

- Belladonna × 1

- Boar's tusk × 1

- Comfrey × 2

Alchemical formula

- Grind the comfrey and add it to the cauldron.

- Add the boar's tusk to the cauldron and boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the belladonna and add it to the cauldron.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Aesop potion and Recipe for Aesop potion

## Aqua Vitalis

Reduces loss of health and slows bleeding.

Ingredients

- AquaAquaWater base

- Dandelion × 2

- Marigold × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the dandelion to the cauldron and boil for 1 turn.

- Grind the marigold and add it to the cauldron.

- Boil for 2 turns.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Aqua Vitalis and Recipe for Aqua Vitalis

## Artemisia potion

Increases strength and, if good quality, reduces how much stamina it costs to attack and defend.

Ingredients

- SpiritusSpiritusSpirits base

- Wormwood × 2

- Sage × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the sage to the cauldron and boil for 1 turn.

- Grind the wormwood and add it to the cauldron.

- Boil for 2 turns.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Artemisia potion and Recipe for Artemisia potion

## Bane poison

Depletes 110 health and therefore leads to certain death. In better quality, it depletes health faster. It's better for poisoning cauldrons than applying to weapons.

Ingredients

- VinumVinumWine base

- Wormwood × 1

- Belladonna × 2

- Amanita muscaria × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the wormwood to the cauldron and boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the belladonna and add to the cauldron.

- Boil for one turn using the bellows.

- Add the fly agaric to the cauldron.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Bane poison and Recipe for Bane poison

## Bowman's Brew

Improves your archery skill and, if good quality, reduces loss of stamina while aiming.

Ingredients

- SpiritusSpiritusSpirits base

- Eyebright × 2

- St. John's wort × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the eyebright to the cauldron and boil for 3 turns.

- Grind the St. John's wort and add to the cauldron.

- Boil for 1 turn using the bellows.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Bowman's brew and Recipe for Bowman's brew

## Buck's Blood

Increases stamina and increases stamina regeneration if good quality.

Ingredients

- OleumOleumOil base

- St. John's wort × 1

- Dandelion × 1

- Comfrey × 1

Alchemical formula

- Grind the St. John's wort and add it to the cauldron.

- Add the comfrey to the cauldron and boil for 1 turn.

- Add the dandelion to the cauldron and using the bellows, boil for one turn.

- Finally, pour.

Main articles: Buck's Blood and Recipe for Buck's Blood

## Chamomile decoction

Sleep heals you faster and if good quality, energy replenishes faster while sleeping.

Ingredients

- VinumVinumWine base

- Chamomile × 2

- Sage × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the chamomile and boil for 1 turn.

- Grind the sage and add it to the cauldron.

- Finally, pour.

Main articles: Chamomile decoction and Recipe for Chamomile decoction

## Cockerel potion

Increases energy and in better qualities slows down fatigue.

Ingredients

- SpiritusSpiritusSpirits base

- Valerian × 1

- Mint × 2

Alchemical formula

- Grind the mint and add to the cauldron.

- Boil for 1 turn.

- Add the valerian and boil for 2 turns.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Cockerel potion and Recipe for Cockerel potion

## Digestive potion

Reduces the feeling of fullness after food and cures food poisoning. If good quality, cures any poisoning, as well as boosting your vitality.

Ingredients

- AquaAquaWater base

- Nettle × 1

- Thistle × 2

- Charcoal × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the thistle to the cauldron and boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the nettle and add it to the cauldron.

- Boil for 1 turn.

- Grind the charcoal and add it to the cauldron.

- Finally, pour.

Main articles: Digestive potion and Recipe for Digestive potion

## Dollmaker poison

Disables running and reduces weapon skills. In better qualities, it also reduces Health. It's better suited to applying to weapons than poisoning food pots.

Ingredients

- SpiritusSpiritusSpirits base

- Valerian × 1

- Herb Paris × 2

Alchemical formula

- Add the herb paris to the cauldron and boil for 3 turns.

- Grind the valerian and add it to the cauldron.

- Boil for 2 turns.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Dollmaker poison and Recipe for Dollmaker poison

## Embrocation

Increases Agility and in better qualities reduces how much stamina sprinting drains.

Ingredients

- OleumOleumOil base

- Eyebright × 1

- Poppy × 1

- Valerian × 1

- Boar's tusk × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the poppy and valerian to the cauldron and boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the eyebright and add it to the cauldron.

- Add the boar's tusk and boil for 1 turn.

- Finally, pour.

Main articles: Embrocation and Recipe for Embrocation

## Fever tonicum

Fever and its complications can often end in death. This tonic will relieve and soothe the fever if given in time.

Ingredients

- VinumVinumWine base

- Feverfew × 3

- Ginger × 2

- Elderberry leaves × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the feverfew and boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the elderberry leaves and add them to the cauldron.

- Add the ginger.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Fever tonicum and Recipe for Fever tonic

## Fox potion

Improves speech and speeds up reading if good quality. Also increases the amount of experience gained if best quality.

Ingredients

- OleumOleumOil base

- Nettle × 1

- St. John's wort × 1

- Belladonna × 1

- Charcoal × 1

Alchemical formula

- Grind the St. John's wort and nettles.

- Add them to the cauldron and boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the charcoal and add it to the cauldron.

- Add the belladonna and boil for 1 turn.

- Finally, pour.

Main articles: Fox potion and Recipe for Fox potion

## Hair o' the Dog

Reduces drunkenness or, in better quality, removes it completely. In better qualities it also helps with hangovers or alcoholism.

Ingredients

- AquaAquaWater base

- Sage × 1

- St. John's wort × 1

- Mint × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the sage and St. John's wort to the cauldron.

- Boil for 3 turns.

- Grind the mint and add it to the cauldron.

- Finally, pour.

Main articles: Hair o' the Dog and Recipe for Hair o' the Dog

## Lead shot gunpowder

Gunpowder used to fire lead shot that even the best plate armour can't stop at close range. For safety reasons, load only when sober.

Ingredients

- AquaAquaWater base

- Sulphur × 1

- Saltpetre × 1

- Charcoal × 1

Alchemical formula

- Grind the sulphur and saltpetre and add it to the cauldron.

- Boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the charcoal and add to the cauldron.

- Boil for two turns.

- Pour into a mortar and grind.

Main articles: Lead ball and Recipe for Lead shot gunpowder

## Lethean Water

If you want to put to rights the imprudent choices of your life, all it takes is 1 mouthful, and you can chose your perks anew. Beware, though, the procedure is irreversible and painful!

Ingredients

- SpiritusSpiritusSpirits base

- Wormwood × 2

- Belladonna × 1

- Henbane × 1

Alchemical formula

- Grind the wormwood and add it to the cauldron.

- Add the belladonna and brew for 3 turns.

- Add the henbane.

- Finally, distil.

Main articles: Lethean Water and Recipe for Lethean Water

## Lion perfume

A strong but short-lasting perfume. Substantially increases charisma for short periods, but reduces charisma if combined with another perfume.

Ingredients

- SpiritusSpiritusSpirits base

- Sage × 2

- Mint × 2

Alchemical formula

- Add the sage to the cauldron and boil for 2 turns.

- Grind the mint and add it to the cauldron.

- Finally, pour.

Main articles: Lion perfume and Recipe for Lion perfume

## Lullaby potion

Reduces energy to 0. Reduces stamina regeneration if good quality. Suitable for applying to weapons and for poisoning cooking pots.

Ingredients

- OleumOleumOil base

- Poppy × 1

- Herb Paris × 1

- Thistle × 1

Alchemical formula

- Add the poppy and boil for 1 turn.

- Add the thistle and boil for 1 turn.

- Grind the herb paris and add it to the cauldron.

- Finally, pour.

## Mandrake decoction

Heals health over a period of time. In better qualities, it increases Vitality and unblocked strikes deplete stamina less.

Gradually heals part of your health. Helps against hangover, or cures it immediately if good quality.

Alchemical formula
