## Reckoning

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Reckoning is the 30th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically following Hunger and Despair.

## Description

The situation at the fortress is unbearable, so Sam and I have to go to Jobst for help.

## Walkthrough

From the bottom of the walls, you’ll have to sneak into Suchdol village and find a horse, and Sam. You’ll also have the opportunity to speak to von Aulitz.

### Find Sam

Head across the moat and into the town, it's best to travel in stealth as initiating combat will very quickly lead to your being overwhelmed as one enemy will sound the alarm for the others. Much of the town is blocked off, you’ll have to head east through the burnt down smithy then around the backs of the houses and through the open gate and up through the barn it leads to. In front of the barn you can inspect to find Samuel's hunting sword, which will update your objective. A trail of blood will lead you in the right direction.

From the barn where you found Sam’s sword, you’ll drop down and head through a gap in the facing wall which will lead you behind the tavern. If you’d like to head in there and confront von Aulitz, you can. From behind the tavern, follow through another hole in the wall.

This will lead you into the heart of the enemy camp, so watch for sitting and patrolling Praguers. Follow the blood stains around the corner to a barn on the south-west end of the village. As you get closer, you’ll hear Brabant. Climb up the ladder and find Sam inside.

You’ll have to fight Brabant, but he will surrender and try to make a deal with you. You can choose whether to kill or spare him, then untie Sam. Sam will insist you leave without him, but you still have the option to save him by picking him up and carrying him away.

### Find von Aulitz

Von Aulitz is being house in the tavern across from the pillory. From the barn where you found Sam’s sword, you’ll drop down and head through a gap in the facing wall which will lead you behind the tavern. Two guards sit in front of the doorway to get through to the tavern proper. There's a ladder next to them that leads into the barn attic of the barn that you can use to sneak past them. Alternatively, One of them should leave to patrol, making slipping past them easier; You may have to distract them away using stones.

There is one more guard sitting by the tavern itself, he holds the tavern key if you need to pickpocket it from him, as the door will be very hard locked. Opening the inner door will unlock the achievement Face to Face.

Once you speak with von Aulitz, there’s plenty in the room to eat and also to loot.

### Leave the camp

Depending on your choices the exit will be a bit different, but outside you’ll be able to find one Praguer who will come into the yard alone. You can kill him through stealth or regular combat, take his waffenrock and blend in a little, allowing you to move with Sam mostly unmolested.

Note: If you spared Brabant, sneaking will be much harder, but not impossible. The disguise won't work, but with sufficient stealth you can slip through past the guards without alerting them.

The easiest route is to leave through the yard, go right and through the gate, then around the back until you reach the horses. They are in a stable just south-west of the yard you started in. Alternatively, leave left and follow the wall until the path is blocked, you can use the wood pile in the yard to walk over the fence and land near the horses. Once you leave, the quest will end starting Last Rites Pt. 2.

## Reforged

Reforged is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You reforged the sword you'd been searching for so long.

## Acquisition

During the main quest Storm, Henry finally recovers the sword he has long searched for. To unlock this achievement you need to successfully reforge it at any smithy.

Note: It is important to reforge the sword before starting Judgement Day, the final quest of the game. After completing the quest, Radzig's sword is renamed to Henry's longsword and although it can still be reforged afterwards, doing so will not unlock the achievement.

## Tips

- The Reforged Radzig Kobyla's sword requires the original sword as well as Toledo steel × 3.

- Forging this sword is more challenging than standard weapons, and it is strongly recommended to save the game beforehand, as there is no second chance to reforge it.

- Make sure you have high Craftsmanship and have unlocked the Martin's Secret perk.

## Regina

Regina is Otto von Bergow's personal maid in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Regina worked in Trosky Castle and at one point was noticed by Lord Nikvard Libak, who tried to court her, including writing her letters, despite the fact she couldn't read. She told Henry she would prefer someone like Hans to be interested in her and she suggested to Nikvard that it wouldn't be proper for a noble to have an affair with a maid in an attempt to get him to stop trying to court her but he instead took this to mean she thought he was too old for her.

If she's talked to for Opus Magnum:

While she hadn't seen Nikvard in awhile, she did find a letter he left her talking about how he took a potion to try and reverse his aging. However, while it appeared to work, it'd also caused some other issues, including losing the book he had used for the potion.

And talked to after finding Nikvard's body:

Regina was relieved to hear that Nikvard wouldn't be bugging her anymore.

## Remains of a Celtic oppidum

For the Codex Entry see: Gord

Remains of a Celtic oppidum is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

In ancient times, an oppidum stood here. In the time since its ruination, the former battlements have almost all worn away. Horse tracks have been laid out and it is currently used for horseback archery competitions.

### Associated Quests

- Horses for Courses

- Mounted archery

## Loot

## Codex Entry

Gords or hillforts, sometimes called Burgwalls, were fortified settlements of various sizes, established from the Neolithic period right through to the early Middle Ages. They were built using natural terrain or the protection of waterways, on islands or hills. Within the outer walls there would typically be a central fort.

These strongholds were mostly built from timber, with an outer palisade (stockade) and ditch or moat. The stronghold fulfilled a protective and strategic function in times of war and also served as a stopover on trade routes or as goods transfer stations.

Semine hillfort

Not far from the Semine fortress is the largest documented Celtic gord in the Czech lands. The hardly accessible site, in the middle of forests and rocks, above the confluence of rivers, ideally fulfilled the conditions for a strategic settlement. The Celts probably built an oppidium here - an early Medieval form of fortified settlement - or a refugium - a temporary refuge during wars.

According to research, the fortress had three ramparts and moats in addition to natural fortifications. Inside, pottery from the La Tène period and remains of masonry made of black basalt, which was also used at Trosky Castle, were found. This suggests that the hillfort may have even been surrounded by a stone wall.

According to some hypotheses, the Celts also had a sacred place here, as during the solar equinox, the sunset can be seen from the top of Semine hill between the rocks on which Trosky Castle stands.

Since 2018, a reconstruction of the hillfort has been standing on the site, where it is possible to learn about the history of Bohemian Paradise.

## Remember, Remember…

Remember, Remember… is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Did you really think it wouldn't blow up? Really?

## Acquisition

The Spark is the final quest in The Guild's questline, which begins in the Hoprink district, southeast of Kuttenberg. To start it, speak with Chenyek, he is usually found in The Hole in the Wall tavern. He may appear with a quest marker early in the game, but cannot be interacted with until you complete Into the Underworld main quest.

The Guild quest line involves three different quests:

- Feast for the Poor - After completing it, ask Chenyek if he has any other work to unlock the next quest.

- The Thieves' Code - Upon finishing this quest, you'll need to wait a few in-game days. Eventually, while fast-traveling (commonly between Miskowitz and Suchdol) a messenger will appear and inform you that Chenyek wishes to speak with you again. This encounter also requires that you've completed the main quest, Via Argentum.

- The Spark - It involves retrieving gunpowder from Sigismund's stockpile and using it to destroy the mine you previously explored during Via Argentum. Completing this mission unlocks the achievement - but only under the specific condition.

To earn the Remember, Remember… achievement, you must intentionally fail the quest by killing Goliath near the mine entrance. Once he is dead, return to the Guild's hideout, where you first met him and the other members. You'll now be able to interact with the cooking pot over the fire. Press the appropriate button to "Throw barrel into the fire", which will result in an explosion that kills Henry and ends the game. This unlocks the achievement.

Afterwards, simply reload your previous save to complete the quest properly.

## Trivia

- The achievement is a reference to the famous English rhyme: "Remember, remember, the fifth of November, Gunpowder Treason and Plot…"

- This rhyme commemorates the Gunpowder Plot of 1605, a failed assassination attempt against King James I of England by a group of English Catholics, most famously Guy Fawkes, who planned to blow up the House of Lords with barrels of gunpowder.

## Reputation

Reputation is a feature in the game series that affects how characters will treat Henry.

Common ways to raise your reputation:

- trading with merchants, innkeepers or craftspeople. This is per trade, so if you want to raise your reputation quickly, split your shopping into multiple transactions.

- Successfully haggling

- Giving merchants extra money when trading, or selling them more items than they have coin for

- Being helpful during sidequests

Ways of losing reputation

- Being rude in dialogue

- Getting caught committing crime

- Attacking that individual

High reputation with an individual makes you more likely to successfully haggle a lower price and succeed in some speech checks.

When Henry upsets an individual, be it by dialog, by attacking them, or by being caught stealing from them, Henry's reputation with that individual will fall and therefore negatively impact his reputation with the demographic that individual is a part of, which will also impact Henry's overall reputation with that village. Henry will also inadvertently offend individuals by pursuing certain quests, for example completing the activity Fat Profits for the Sasau butcher will raise Henry's reputation with the butcher but also greatly harm Henry's reputation with the monastery monks. Siding with Prochek instead of Olbram in Frogs/Mice/Battle of the Frogs and Mice will raise your reputation in Tachov but lower it in Zhelejov and vice versa.

## Game-specific reputation

-
Kingdom Come: Deliverance

-
Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2

Henry's reputation among Rattay guards is subject to the most scrutiny. If Henry is ever seen committing a crime, his reputation among the Rattay soldiers demographic will fall in great bounds as opposed to the small doses that are typical of upsetting individuals. When Henry's reputation with Rattay soldiers is low, guards will be much more likely to stop and search Henry. Henry's reputation with Rattay soldiers can be slowly increased by:

- Helping Rattay soldiers during random encounter battles with bandits.

- Performing successful speech or intimidation checks against guards that try to stop and search Henry, which will raise Henry's reputation with that individual guard and contribute to the demographic reputation.

- Impressing Captain Bernard through quest dialog will raise Henry's reputation with Bernard as an individual, and reporting success in the quest Ruin to him will greatly improve Henry's reputation with the soldier demographic.

- Advancing the main quest line and winning the battle of Pribyslavitz will provide a large boost to Henry's reputation among Rattay soldiers.

- Winning the Rattay Tourney will make Henry famous and greatly increase his reputation with all demographics within Rattay.

The icon for the Reputation section of the Player Tab

At the beginning of the game, Henry's reputation with the people of the Trosky region is, at best, neutral. Interestingly, whether you worm your way into the wedding during Wedding Crashers with Blacksmith Radovan through honest work, or with Miller Kreyzl who everyone knows is a shady character, makes almost no difference.

Since the crime system in the game is smarter than in the first and you can get punished for a crime where you're only implicated without necessarily being caught red handed, it doesn't matter for your reputation if there are witnesses to your crimes or not.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance II has two kinds of dialogue speech checks, "positive" and "mnegative," easily discerned by the colour of the icons. Negative speech checks always decrease your reputation with the target, and they are even easier to pass the lower reputation you do have. Positive speech checks are easier to pass with good reputation, and if you are successful, passing them further increases your reputation.

Other checks generally increase your reputation when passed and decrease it when failed.

Killing highwaymen on the roads is a way to increase your reputation. However, for that, you need witnesses to carry the good news into the neighbouring villages. This tends to be difficult, as the first thing highwaymen do when you attack them is that they stab the person they were originally robbing.

Reputation is separately tracked for each location and a social group within it, but it diffuses over time between neighbouring locations.

If your reputation is low, you can increase it by paying indulgences or going on a penitent pilgrimage.

## Groups tracking reputation

Word of mouth travels and villagers will tend to know that you have been up to no good at the neighbouring location.

-
Kingdom Come:Deliverance

-
Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

Reputation is currently tracked at these locations:

- Rovna

- Uzhitz

- Pribyslavitz

- Monastery

- Rattay

- Vranik

- Neuhof

- Sasau

- Ledetchko

- Talmberg

- Skalitz

- Merhojed

- Samopesh

- Kuno's camp

Four of the above locations (Rattay, Sasau, Talmberg, and Merhojed) have their reputation values split into two or more categories relating to the demographics within each area. For example, Henry's reputation in Talmberg is split between how highly the Talmberg soldiers think of him, and how well regarded Henry is among Talmberg villagers and quarrymen. Henry's reputation with a specific demographic is based on the sum of how each individual in that group feels towards Henry, while Henry's overall reputation with a village is derived from how high Henry's reputation is with each demographic from that area. The benefit to having a high overall reputation within a village is that Henry will receive bonuses to his four main stats while in the vicinity of that village, provided Henry also has the Local Hero perk.

Not every single person in a demographic needs to like Henry in order for his Reputation to reach 100, only majority popularity is required. For example: Henry's reputation in Skalitz during the prologue is at a perfect 100 at the start due to enough people from each demographic already liking Henry to provide majority popularity, even though not everybody in town likes him. However assisting Matthew in vandalizing Deutch's house will hurt Henry's reputation with Zbyshek as an individual and decrease Henry's standing among the Skalits villagers demographic, therefore hurting Henry's overall reputation within Skalitz. Also failing speech or intimidate checks on Kunesh will lower Henry's reputation with him as an individual and therefore negatively impact the reputation among the Skalitz villager demographic, while succeeding in the speech check against him will raise Henry's reputation with him as an individual and counterbalance most of any negative reputation Henry may have gained so far in the prologue.

Henry's reputation with every trader in the game as an individual person will be at a neutral 50 at the start since many of them do not know Henry yet, therefore Henry's reputation with the Rattay trader demographic will also begin at 50. Only Rattay has a separate demographic for tracking reputation with traders, as every other village has their traders condensed within the villager demographic.

Reputation in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is separately tracked for each location and each social group within it. However, word of mouth tends to travel, and if you're very helpful in one village, the neighbouring village will also have an increase of your reputation.

## Riddler Barley

Riddler Barley is a character that can be randomly encountered up to 4 times in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

When encountered, he'll offer to tell you a riddle that, if you answer correctly, he'll give a small reward, with each encounter requiring a larger and larger bet amount.

The first time, the reward depends on if you ask to check what he has on him or something more skill related. He won't say directly though which skill trait, instead making you pick between taverns or travels. Taverns will improve your drinking skill, while travels will improve your survival skill.

The remaining three times, he'll offer the monetary reward or to learn another skill, which will vary between drinking, survival, and alchemy.

## Biography

Barley doesn't reveal much about himself, though he used to have a dog that traveled with him, who he called Wags. He had Wags since he was a puppy, having saved from otherwise being killed as he was the runt of the litter. One day while they were traveling though, wolves got to Wags and despite his best efforts, Barley wasn't able to save him. Barley buried him near Wysoka before continuing his travels, though this time alone. However, when he passes through that area, he likes to stop by there to visit Wags' grave.

Wag's grave can be found close by the Water hole point of interest. You cannot interact with it, and it is not acknowledged by Henry.

## Rock and Stone!

Rock and Stone! is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You killed an enemy with a boulder dropped from the battlements. Karl would be proud!

## Acquisition

To earn the Rock and Stone! achievement, focus on the main quest The Finger of God, during the defense of Nebakov Fortress. After defeating the first wave of enemies, you will retreat to the gate. Upon arrival, a tutorial titled "Dropping Stones" will appear, instructing you how to pick up boulders and drop them down the hole above the gate onto enemies below.

Simply pick up a boulder and successfully kill an enemy by dropping it on them. Once you do, the achievement will unlock. Be sure not to miss this opportunity during the quest.

## Tips

- In the game there are two specific moments where you can kill an enemy using a boulder. During these moments, it is possible to miss the achievement if you choose to ignore the on-screen prompts (and the tutorial) and use a bow instead, which is allowed by the game - making this achievement technically missable.

## Trivia

- The achievement's title is a reference to the dwarven battle cry from the game Deep Rock Galactic, a cooperative first-person shooter released in 2020. In that game, dwarves shout "Rock and Stone!" as a rallying cheer before going into combat.

- Karl mentioned in the achievement's description is a legendary dwarf miner who is often invoked by fellow miners with the exclamation "For Karl!"

## Rocktower Pond

Rocktower Pond is a fast travel point in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

This pond is the largest body of water in the region, stretching across a wide area west of Zhelejov.

The pond lies in a hollow beneath the Trosky Castle. Its northern and western shores are gentler, lined with meadows, small groves, and a few scattered footpaths. The southern shore is wilder, with thick reeds, tangled woods, and steep rock faces.

## Roman

Roman was a woodcutter and minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Roman had lived in Troskowitz with his parents and worked as a woodcutter like his father. However, when he was barely an adult, his mother died and his father passed a few years later. Roman managed to get by though with his job and having inherited his family's home in the village.

One day he met Pavlena, who was in town to sell baskets and potions to help her and her mother, Bozhena, make end's meet, as Bozhena had a bad history with the town's residents and was subsequently run out of town. Despite this, Roman and Pavlena immediately took a liking to each other and it soon became apparent to everyone in town they were together and would often hang out when Pavlena was in town. Eventually, the young couple learned Pavlena was pregnant and the two secretly planned to get married and try to find a new place to live where nobody knew who they were so they could bring Bozhena with them.

However, one day when Pavlena visited Troskowitz as normal with her wares, she and Roman went out to a known romantic spot in the nearby woods. Roman went to the spot and was setting up food while Pavlena was at a nearby stream when he heard a commotion and ran over to investigate. When he saw two men, Straw and Ota, trying to attack Pavlena, Roman jumped in to defend her, attacking Ota. In the midst of this though, a panicked Straw grabbed a rock and bashed Roman's head in, killing him.

## Associated quest

## Root of Evil

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Root of Evil is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 9th quest in the Brushes with Death DLC.

## Description

Voyta has confided that there is a dark voice in his mind and the struggle is not going well. A potion of mandrake root, a peal of sage, which once helped, might calm his turmoil and help him complete the crucial painting.

## Synopsis

Voyta is feeling stuck in his work for Sedletz Monastery. He confides in Henry that when he mentioned earlier about the Veles shrine ‘speaking to him’ and having heard a voice in his head telling him ‘Burkhard must die’ that he meant both of those things more literally than perhaps expected. He really does sometimes feel as if someone is talking to him in his own head ranging from whispering to shouting so loud it hurts.

The feeling has gotten worse since he found out Burkhard was in the Trosky region. He was hoping the former’s death would quiet things down but they’ve only gotten louder. To treat it, Voyta has been making a concoction on the advice of a herbalist he told he was having nightmares. The treatment has mostly worked, but he’s recently run out and has neither time nor energy to make more. He would like Henry to help him by gathering the necessary ingredients and brewing some, as asking anyone in town might sully his reputation.

A couple of the ingredients are difficult to come by – mandrake root and a river pearl. The rest of the process shouldn’t be too difficult, according to Voyta. With a bit of elbow grease, Henry is able to acquire a mandrake root from the gravedigger and a river pearl from the bed north of Danemark.

With potion in-hand, Henry returns to the painter’s studio. He is grateful for the work, though admits to Henry it is more of a bandage than a cure for what ails him. He explains the voice in his head sounds like the dead Voyta’s and he believes the Devil chose it to torment him and though he’s tried all kinds of remedies from all types of sources, this potion works best.

Voyta takes the potion and thanks Henry for his hard work.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Voyta to start the quest, he will ask you for help with brewing a concoction to help quiet the voices in his head. To brew it, he needs you to find a couple of rare materials in addition to regular sage and wine – mandrake root and a river pearl.

### Find a mandrake root

Head to the church in the north of Kuttenberg. Talk to the gravedigger there, Frantishek, and ask after the root. He’ll agree to give you some in exchange for a favour.

There are some trouble makers whom he wants Henry to teach a lesson with his fists. Agree to help and time will automatically skip to midnight when the graverobbers will arrive. If you have completed the "Nail in the Coffin" quest where you defeat him, a quest you obtain after completing the 3 fighting quests in the region, you will not have to pass the "unarmed combat" dialogue test.

Run in and fight them unarmed. There are three of them, but they shouldn’t give you too much trouble being simply dressed and not well trained. You should only have to get one of them down to low health, the remaining two will run without too much injury.

Once they’re dealt with, talk to Frantishek and he’ll give you the key to where he keeps the mandrake root. The entrance to his larder is one street over to the east, it will be the second house moving south down the street. In a chest right next to the door you’ll find 5 mandrake roots.

### Find a river pearl

To get a river pearl you will need to either convince Deserter Chief Vladimir to sell or give you one, take him and his men out and loot the pearl from him, or root around until you find one yourself.

The camp can be found north-east of Danemark Mill, if you fast travel to the mill and follow the river in that direction you’ll reach them about half-way through the search radius.

To get the pearl peacefully, approach during the day. You will be warned by a patrolling guard, talk to him and ask about their leader. Vladimir will be nearby, most likely in the camp itself. Talk to him and you’ll have the ability to get the pearl from him with a hard speech check, very hard coercion check, hard intimidation check, or medium charisma.

The starting price for a pearl will be 500 groschen and can be bartered down depending on your speech, charisma, and perks.

The safest way to take out the group hunting pearls is to approach the camp during the night, taking them out by stealth. There are a fair number of them and they are well-armed, so a head-on assault may not be smart depending on your skill levels.

To find your own, in the area near the camp mussels can be found in the shallows. Loot them and you can find up to five pearls in the area. This method can also be a little risky, as the group camped in the area will warn you off and become hostile if you do not listen. Approaching at night is an option here as well, if you are not able to convince them to remain docile.

### Obtain sage

Sage can be found in many lightly wooded places. For a shortcut, you can buy some from the apothecary in Kuttenberg near Voyta’s workshop, though it will be dried. You can also obtain fresh sage from the back garden of the same apothecary.

### Brew the potion

The most easily accessible alchemy bench will be in the back of the apothecary near Voyta’s workshop. Making a high “Henry’s” quality mandrake potion will get you the achievement Nothing But the Best. For this, you will need fresh sage and the perk Secret of Secrets.

Brew the potion:

Ingredients

- Wine base

- Freshwater pearl × 1

- Mandrake root × 1

- Sage × 2

Alchemical formula

- Add the Mandrake and boil for 1 turn.

- Grind the Pearl and add it to the cauldron.

- Boil for 1 turn.

- Grind the Sage and add it to the cauldron.

- Using the bellows, boil for 1 turn.

- Finally, distil.

### Return to Voyta

Once you have the potion, return to Voyta and hand it over. He will thank you, ending the quest.

## Objectives

## Rosa Ruthard

Da mihi castitatem et continentiam, sed noli modo! (Give me chastity and continence, but not just yet!)

Rosa Ruthard (Czech: Róza Ruthardová) is a young Bohemian noblewoman, daughter of a recently ennobled wealthy burgher from Kuttenberg, Kunzlin Ruthard.

Rosa Ruthard is one of the main love interests for the protagonist, Henry.

Their relationship development depends on the player’s choices as Henry; she is intelligent, capable and has moral compass that guides her actions as well as words. Despite her noble upbringing as a lady, she isn’t afraid of using her crossbow or getting her hands dirty in politics.

## Biography

### Early life

Rosa was born to Kunzlin Ruthard as a second child, following her older brother, Ventza. Her mother died when she was young. Rosa was good friends with Anna of Waldstein growing up and the two were even called inseparable.

Rosa developed a love for reading and the pursuit of knowledge as well as a knack for crossbow shooting and horse riding thanks to her brother's tutelage. She had an inquisitive personality and an adventurous soul but was prohibited from going out into the wilderness by her father, so instead had to spend her time exploring the Maleshov fortress and spent time researching the underground passages running beneath the town of Kuttenberg through her father's administrative documents.

Her brother was killed during the siege of Kuttenberg which made Rosa her father's heir, something she endeavoured to live up to and prove even as a woman in the middle ages she can be a force to be reconned with.

### Involvement

Rosa's father was involved in a mining dispute with the Mint Master who had been appointed by Sigismund following his takeover of Kuttenberg, Ulrich Vavak. One day, Vavak's men were attempting to intimidate her father, when Rosa fired a warning shot at them and a fight broke out.

The Ruthards were aided by a young man who then introduced himself as Henry. He had come to them to seek help in freeing Hans Capon from their former estate of Maleshov, now under Otto von Bergow's control.

Rosa told Henry how to find the secret passageway that served as an escape route from the fortress, and asked him to find a book of hers that had been left there. Inside the book were some general anecdotes and a treatise she had written her own views regarding the treatment and status of women.

If Henry retrieved the book for her, she asked him to help her complete it, fleshing out the final story and bringing them closer together.

Sometime later, her father left Kuttenberg to attend a meeting of Wenceslas supporters at Raborsch, leaving Rosa in town. While he was away, von Bergow's men came to Ruthard Palace and ransacked it, taking Rosa hostage and bringing her to Maleshov. Henry would find out about her capture from Adder's scouting report of Maleshov.

Rosa was later freed when Jan Zizka and his men came to Maleshov to capture von Bergow. After being freed, she agreed to help them further, as she wanted her father freed, who was taken captive by Von Bergov at Raborsch.

She led Henry through the underground to sneak into Ruthard Palace with the intent of using it as a base of operations for Zizka's company in Kuttenberg while they tried to find a way into the Italian Court to steal the silver there at von Bergow's suggestion, and to free her father along with the other captured lords. When they arrived, Rosa was furious to find some local vagrants had set up their lair having looted her entire palace clean. She climbed into her bedroom using the trellis and grabbed her crossbow supporting Henry deal with the violent vagrants.

After clearing out the palace, Rosa and Henry can spend a night of passion together.

In the morning, the others arrived at the palace through the same underground passage and took up temporary residence there. Part of the plan to break into the Italian Court would require a way to get the silver back out unnoticed. Rosa came up with the plan of marking and clearing out the tunnels that connected Ruthard Palace to the nearby St. James Church and the abandoned mines beneath the Italian Court.

The other half of the plan was to have the coerced help of a visiting papal dignitary to allow some of the group entrance aboveground. Unfortunately, that part went awry and rather than escorting a group peacefully, they had to pretend to be the delegation. Rosa helped prepare by mending and washing the clothes that had once belonged to the delegation's guards.

Rosa went with the second group to enter the Italian Court through the tunnels. She was very happy to be reunited with her father after Henry managed to free the captured lords and went together with him and the others first to Suchdol and then to her kin in Podiebrad to send news to Jobst of Moravia that Zizka's robbery had been successful and Sigismund has withdrawn from Bohemia.

At Suchdol, she said her farewell to Henry. If his company (or himself) threatened to burn the Maleshov tower, she said her goodbye coldly. If they didn't, she wished him goodbye with a kiss on the cheek, hoping they can meet again someday.

## Codex entry

Rosa Ruthard

Rosa Ruthard is not a documented historical figure. She is inspired by Rosa/Rozina from a Kuttenberg legend, which was adapted by Czech playwright Josef Kajetán Tyl. The story intrigued us, but ultimately, we retained only her name from the tale of the daughter of a wealthy nobleman from the Ruthard family. The original legend goes like this:

Rosa was the daughter of George Ruthard, a wealthy but very stingy townsman of Kuttenberg. She was beautiful and intelligent, so she had no shortage of suitors. However, her father feared this, as the last thing he wanted was to diminish his treasure with his daughter's dowry. He secured his wealth in a very cruel manner - he had his daughter bricked up in the same cellar where he kept his riches.

Her ghost later haunted the house and its surroundings; people in the street would hear crying at night. The spirit often appeared to the house's residents and predicted terrible misfortunes. This eventually came true - in 1648, the house collapsed, burying everyone inside.

—Codex entry: Rosa Ruthard

## Rosa's Book

Rosa’s Book is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is only available during Taking French Leave and its completion is necessary in order to romance Rosa.

## Description

During my trip to Maleshov, Rosa Ruthard also asked me to get a book she desires greatly. I probably won’t get there again, so I shouldn’t forget.

## Walkthrough

Once you arrive in Maleshov Fortress during Taking French Leave, you’ll find Rosa’s book on the second floor of the tower in the room with Lady Ofka, a guest of von Bergow’s. You can knock her out or sneak past her to get the book or else speak with her. When initiating conversation, you’ll have to pass a medium intimidation or hard charisma check for her not to alert the guards.

The book is on the nook by the window to her right – called Book of Anecdotes.

Return to Kuttenberg following your escape from Maleshov and read the book. Then give it back to Rosa. She'll ask you to help her finish it. Finish the story as you see fit then speak to her again, be sure to mention you'd like to get to know her better to open the option for romance later if you are so inclined.

## Ruins of Zimburg

Ruins of Zimburg is a castle ruin located west of Danemark mill.

## Codex entry

Settlement in the area dates back to the late Stone Age (about 3000 BC). Today, however, only traces of an early medieval fortified settlement remain in the form of remnants of moats and visible ramparts.

Some historians (as well as folk legends) claim that Zimburg (Cimburk) Castle, owned by the Lords of Zimburg, once stood here and was even perhaps their ancestral home. Later, the descendants of the family built two more castles with the same name: Cimburk in Trnávka and Nový Cimburk in Koryčany.

Unfortunately nothing remains from the original castle. Hence why some historians claim that such a castle never stood here and the settlement rather got its name from the nearby mine that belonged to the Zimburg family. Nevertheless, we decided to depict it in the game.

## Samuel of Kuttenberg

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Samuel is a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

Samuel is the biological son of Sara and Henry's foster father Martin.

## Biography

### Early life

Samuel was born to Sara, the daughter of the rabbi of Kuttenberg, Jehuda. He was raised without a father, as his biological father, Martin, was not involved in his life and did not know of his birth.

His mother moved to Prague to conceal her pregnancy and she returned to Kuttenberg with Samuel when he was four years old, a sufficient amount of time for the larger community to accept his grandfather's story that his mother had been married and then widowed.

As an adult, he ran the King Solomon Tavern in the Jewish Quarter of Kuttenberg.

### Involvement

Samuel eventually found himself hiding John II of Liechtenstein in the cellar of his tavern, while also concealing the latter's whereabouts and running his spy network on the surface. This activity was the last straw for king Sigismund, who used it as an excuse for a pogrom on the Jewish population of Kuttenberg, gaining support of the gentry and funds from the looting of the Quarter.

In the quest Exodus, thanks to the efforts of Samuel, Henry and Kubyenka, a large part of the population of the Jewish Quarter was saved, though Samuel was forced to burn the quarter's synagogue himself to cover the escape. He then accompanied his people to Kolin.

After his return from Kolin, Samuel joined the Devil's Pack for a short while to exact revenge on Otto von Bergow, Markvart von Aulitz and king Sigismund. He even attempted to kill Otto in Dancing with the Devil after the successful retaking of Maleshov, but he was stopped by the rest of the pack.

With the Pack, he aided in the theft of royal silver in The Italian Job and was subsequently trapped in Suchdol with the others. Together with his half-foster-brother Henry, he volunteered for a mission to escape the besieged castle and get help from Jobst. His lust for revenge got the better of him, and he was captured in the Praguers' camp trying to find von Aulitz. Depending on the player's choice in Reckoning, he either escaped or was hanged in view of his friends in Suchdol.

If Samuel survived the finale, he can be found in the Devil's Den.

### Associated quests

- Exodus

## Sauerkraut Pepa

Sauerkraut Pepa (Czech: Zelňák Pepa) is a genial but slow-witted cabbage thief, who likes to make sauerkraut.

## Biography

Although not considered particularly bright by his mother, Pepa proved himself to be a great maker of sauerkraut. He never caused anyone harm except in a roundabout way through his stealing of cabbage which he needed for his cooking. He was not a particularly sly thief, leaving a trail of cabbages in his wake.

One day, he was happened upon by Henry who found his sauerkraut making lair and the evidence of his crimes. Pepa asked that Henry not turn him in, as he was not intending to hurt anyone and his sauerkraut was without equal

If he was found but not turned in:

Grateful for not being turned in, Pepa then offered to provide sauerkraut to Henry in exchange for cabbage.

If he was found and turned in:

Pepa understood Henry's reasoning and accepted being turned in for stealing cabbages, noting maybe he could make sauerkraut as repayment.

## Sculptor without a Future

Sculptor without a Future is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is part of the Legacy of the Forge DLC and introduces the Sinners of Kuttenberg repeatable task.

## Description

The Mole, the innkeeper from the tavern near my smithy, wants to talk to me about something, and it all seems a bit mysterious, so hopefully no trouble will come of it.

## Walkthrough

Exhaust all existing dialogue with Innkeeper Mole, though room and board are not necessary. Spots will then show up at your forge and tell you Mole has something for you, starting the quest.

Talk to Mole, and he will introduce you to a mysterious benefactor who he claims will keep you in the good graces of your poorer neighbors. They call him The Ragman, since he gives people food for their rags and is well-liked in the area. Mole will tell you to head to the Iron Eagle that evening to find him; he'll be at a corner table wearing a blue hat.

Do as he suggests and talk to Ragman. You'll find him up the stairs in the tavern at the first table. Ragman wants you to help a struggling artist called Young Damian. The artist has been unable to finish his work for the Mint. Damian wants someone to rob Adam Welvar, a man with whom he was lodging who accused him of sleeping with his wife. In his haste to get away, he left his belongings in Welvar's house. You'll have to get them back so he can finish the commission.

Ragman's only stipulation is that no one is harmed. He suggests going at night, but you can also talk to Welvar during the day without arousing suspicion. The things are upstairs in a medium locked chest near the street-facing windows. Once you have them, return to Mole at the Hole to end the quest.

## Sedletz Monastery

Sedletz Monastery (Czech: Sedlecký klášter) is a monastery just outside the city of Kuttenberg.

The monastery is not generally accessible to Henry, with the exception of the graveyard and the ossuary/undercroft of the chapel. As part of the Mysteria Ecclesiae expansion, Henry is able to gain entry to the monastery proper.

Sedletz monastery has traditionally controlled all decisions regarding religious buildings in Kuttenberg which has led the Monastery into a bitter feud with the Brotherhood of Corpus Cristi over the control of the unfinished St. Barbara's Church.

## Codex Entries

### Sedletz Monastery

The Sedletz Monastery used to be the oldest Cistercian abbey in the Czech Kingdom. Founded by the Bavarian Abbot Gerlach in 1142 , it was later abandoned and reoccupied many times in its history, either due to wars or poor financial situations.

In 1421, it was burnt down by the Hussites, only the Church of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary and St. John the Baptist survived. After the end of the war, only a few monks returned and it remained in this dismal state until the 17th century. In 1783, the monastery was completely abolished by an imperial decree.

The cemetery church of All Saints with the adjacent burial ground was originally part of the monastery, but later it began to serve as the municipal cemetery for Kuttenberg, because as records showed, burials were taking place there long before the arrival of the monks. The cemetery was at its busiest during wars and plague epidemics. In 1318 alone, 30,000 dead were buried there, and another 10,000 during the Hussite wars.

The site is shrouded in many legends. The most famous one states that the abbot of the Heidenreich Monastery brought a handful of dirt from Jerusalem on his pilgrimage to the Holy Land, which he then scattered around the cemetery and the ossuary. Thus, the cemetery ground became sacred and highly sought after, not only by the people of Kuttenberg, but also by pilgrims and those wishing to be buried there from all over Bohemia and neighbouring regions. Who wouldn't want to rest in the ground where Jesus Christ himself once walked?

Today, a cigarette factory is located on the site of the former monastery.

### Sedletz Ossuary

The ossuary is an underground chapel of the All Saints cemetery church, built in the second half of the 14th century, which originally belonged to the Cistercian abbey in Sedletz. It bears an uncanny resemblance to the underground chapels of Jerusalem where pilgrims were buried.

During the Hussite wars, the monastery was burnt down and abandoned together with the ossuary. It was not rebuilt until the second half of the 15th century. In 1511, the bones from the cemetery were exhumed and moved to the ossuary's underground, where a half-blind monk put them together into the famous pyramids and bone structures in our game, however, we decided to attribute their creation to Henry.

In its later history, the Sedletz ossuary underwent Baroque modifications and today it is one of the most popular tourist sites in the Czech Republic. The bone structures, made from the remains of more than 60,000 people, have undergone extensive renovation and, as a memento mori, are still a reminder that: dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return...

## Locations of Interest

In the southwestern corner of the wall near a stream you can find a spot marked as Hidden ladder where you can find a knocked down ladder and a chest with valuables and Map from chest by Sedletz which points to a barn marked as Love nest with some more valuables inside.

In the eastern corner, you can find broken sword in a bonfire, next to a small camp - this is a reference to the Dark Souls franchise. Nearby lies a circle of stones around a large cross and a child's grave.

## Seek and you Shall Find

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Seek and You Shall Find is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 4th or 5th quest in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC, as it is given concurrently with To Dust You Shan't Return.

## Description

Under the guise of repairs to the collapses ceiling in the monastery crypt, some workers were searching diligently for something and apparently didn’t find it. I want to uncover this mystery and find out what’s really going on.

## Walkthrough

Curious to find out what the workers were looking for in the crypt, Albich suggests you ask Librarian Crispin. The librarian recognises the name the workers gave, Boleslav Bavor, having looked into it as a novice. There’s a rumour that Bavor was buried in Sedletz Monastery with a certain relic, something rare and linked to Christ himself. Though the librarian believes it to be a fabrication.

He’ll want to report the thievery to the Abbot, but you can convince him to wait until the illness is dealt with first with a speech check. He’ll give you two books to look over. Read them and then talk to him again. Boleslav was evidently buried with a sliver of the true cross of Christ.

Crispin himself looked when he was younger, but was never able to find it. The previous Abbot came to the conclusion that it must have been a made up tale. Pass very hard checks to get some extra information and posit a few possibilities.

There is one tangible piece of Bavor’s story, a mural in one of the naves in the church. Crispin will give you an image of his family’s crest and suggest you look for him in the hidden room of the crypt.

The mural can be found in the church under construction. The shield on the mural is slightly different from the sketch, given a bit of elevation. Once you’ve looked at the mural, head down into the crypt. There will be patrol here, so sneak past them.

Bavor’s tomb is in the secret section behind the wall, just after the first winding tunnel. Open the sarcophagus to find a monk buried there. When leaving, you’ll find a murdered knight and remark that someone is following you. Follow the blood to find a killed mercenary.

Get to the library and talk to Crispin to get him up to speed. Pass a hard speech check to get him to tell you about how the monastery deals with tombs. Since there is limited space, a body with no living relatives may be moved to make space for another. Bavor was most likely moved to one of the other graveyards on the premises.

The only one you can access right now is the infirmary yard. You’re looking for Bavor’s crest on the graves, it’s on its own against the monastery wall.

Note: it is best to wait until after To Dust you Shan't Return is completed to go past this point. It can be completed, but will count as being escorted back to the infirmary by the guards for breaking the isolation. If you are trying to complete the achievement Quiet as a Church Mouse. <--- Not true apparently, although I would do To Dust you Shan't Return first anyway just to be safe.

### If done before To Dust you Shan't Return

Dig him up and take his sword. Inspect the lid of the sarcophagus and you’ll find the relic hidden inside. When you go to leave, you'll be interrupted by three mercenaries who will attack you! Do your best, but they will overwhelm you. Ludolf will then come to investigate. He’ll take you to the Abbot to defend your case, ending the quest.

### If done after To Dust you Shan't Return

Dig him up and take his sword. Inspect the lid of the sarcophagus and you’ll find the relic hidden inside. When you go to leave, Ludolf and a few of his men will intercept you. They will take you to the Abbot where you can mention Zacharias's urging, and the Abbot will allow you to keep the relic and free you of all isolation requirements, ending the quest.

## Semine

Semine is a fortress in the Trosky region, with a small village situated around it. The local lord is Jan Semine, an impoverished nobleman who lives there with his family.

## Codex Entry

Semín (Semine) is a small village lying to the west of Troskowitz. In earlier times, it included a fortress that no longer exists today, which, according to surviving records, belonged to Jan and Oldřich of Semín in the year 1365. These two brothers, and later their children, owned the fortress until 1416, but did not reside there much because they chose other places for their seats. In 1375, Oldřich's son Jan therefore assumed administration of Semín, and after him it passed to his sons Petr and Přibík.

Whether these Semín men were ancestors or relatives of the Semín of Semín line - an old Bohemian minor noble family - unfortunately can no longer be definitively proven or disproven. So far, the only discovery is that the first to bear that name was Jakub the Younger Semín of Semín, as late as 1422.

Even so, we decided to present the owner of the Semín fortress in our game as a representative example of impoverished nobility dwelling in pleasant countryside.

As for the place where the fortress is situated, the terrain bordered by steep rocky slopes, lakes, marshes and fishponds became an ideal settlement area as early as the middle of the first century BC. Remains of massive ramparts can be found here, the most prominent part being a ten-metre-high frontal rampart with a moat, which archaeological research indicates was built by the Celts.

In Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2, one also finds the Semín mill, which belonged to the lords of Semín for centuries, and it remains an important part of the picturesque landscape to this day.

## Servant Brother Karl

Servant Brother Karl is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Skill Teaching

Following a sparring session, Karl can teach the following skills:

|
Skill

Level

Price

|
Swords
Master (20 lvl)
5,000

|
Heavy Weapons
Journeyman (15 lvl)
1,500

## Biography

### Early life

Karl was dedicated to Mary by his father as a child and was sent to Marienburg to join the Order. He considered Marienburg to be the most beautiful castle in the world and would describe it to anyone who would listen, especially newer recruits who had never been there.

Growing up in the Order, he considered them to be his true family and believed in the righteousness of their cause. He trusted his commander, Ludolf with his life and considered him to be a fair, if strict, leader.

### Involvement

Karl travelled with the Order through the region to gather supplies and men in an attempt to bolster their forces. He was eager to return to Poland to fight those he considered infidels and take the lands which he considered were their due.

Along this path, the Order stopped at Sedletz Monastery, and Karl worked to train the newer recruits they had gathered through Bohemia. He enjoyed the work as a combat trainer and would spar with anyone should they prove themselves a match.

## Servant Thaddeus

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Servant Thaddeus is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Thaddeus served the von Grolle family. He pursued Jarka, who also served at the same house. However, she declined him. Mandelina von Grolle, the mistress of the household, used this to rope Thaddeus into the serial murder of women, who, like Jarka, could tempt Mandelina's son Hendl.

Depending on Henry of Skalitz's actions, Thaddeus was free to continue in this endeavor, or captured and executed by Henry or by the Kuttenberg executioner.

## Shield painting

The in-game tutorial of the shield painting

Shield painting is a gameplay mechanic introduced in the Brushes with Death DLC for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It allows players to customize Henry's shield by commissioning personalised designs from the painter Voyta.

## Overview

Shield painting becomes available during the events of the DLC, after completing the quest A Sketchy Situation. After helping Voyta during his initial quest, he invites Henry to his workshop in Trosky Castle and offers to paint his shield for free as a token of gratitude.

You can choose from a variety of shield designs, each reflecting different aspects of Henry's path, achievements, or affiliations. These designs can be applied to any shield in Henry's inventory. Not all designs are available from the start. The selection expands as you progress further in the DLC, the main storyline, and certain side quests.

## Mechanic

- Initiate dialogue: Speak to Voyta in his workshop (first in Trosky, later in Kuttenberg) and select "Paint a shield for me" or "How does shield painting work?"

- Select your shield: Choose any shield from your inventory - including previously painted shields. All shield types (kite, cuman, heater, knight, pavise) are eligible.

- Customise:

- Pattern: Base background (e.g., split, cross, heraldic field),

- Colour I & II: Two-tone colour layer selection,

- Categories & Symbols: Under different categories you will find symbols to adorn the shield.

- Confirm: Accept to finalise the design. You may return to Voyta anytime to repaint it again.

## Achievements

There are a total of 2 achievements related to Shield painting.

|

Bohemian Graffitti

10

|
You painted every type of shield.

|

Bohemians Rise Up!

10

|
You were ahead of your time and created the foundations for the state emblem of Bohemia.

## Trivia

- The design options use real terminology from medieval heraldry. For example, 'Goat Sable' refers to a black goat.

## Shields of Seasons Passing

Shields of Seasons Passing is a downloadable content pack for Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, released on 4 February 2025 alongside the base game.

Initially, it was available exclusively through the Expansion Pass and could not be purchased separately, but it has since been released as a standalone DLC.

## Description

What time is it? It's time to customise your shields with one of these four unique designs.

The DLC introduces a collection of decorative shields themed around the four seasons, which can be equipped by Henry. Each design is unique, offering a purely cosmetic addition without affecting gameplay balance.

## Acquisition

After the DLC has been downloaded, its content becomes available in the shared stash once it is unlocked. The unlock occurs after completing the introductory questline, with the final requirement being the quest Laboratores.

Players who meet this condition receive a pop-up notification. This appears either immediately upon finishing the required quest or, if the it was already completed, upon the next login after purchasing the DLC. The message displayed is:

Your premium items have been successfully added to your shared stash. Enjoy your new gear and happy adventuring!

## Content

- Shield of Spring

- Shield of Summer

- Shield of Autumn

- Shield of Winter

## Shiny

Shiny is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You won a gold badge in a game of dice.

## Acquisition

There are two types of dice games in the game: with badges and without badges. Badges act as bonus cards that can be played during the game. To unlock this achievement, you first need to acquire a gold badge. These badges can be purchased from certain innkeepers across the land, particularly in Kuttenberg. For example, the Alehouse maid at Emperor Charles Tavern in northwestern Kuttenberg sells the Gold badge of headstart.

Once you have a gold badge, you can play for someone else's gold badge under specific conditions:

- You must play with a gold badge.

- Your opponent must also have a gold badge.

- The dice game mode must be "Emperor" (300 Groschen buy-in).

- The bet criteria must specify "… and a badge."

## Tips

- Since players at most dice tables are randomized, finding an opponent who meets the specific criteria requires some luck. It is recommended to fast-forward time to refresh the player pool and use the "Save and exit" option when facing a suitable opponent, in case you lose.

- A guaranteed way to obtain a gold badge is by winning the dice tournament at the Semine wedding. This event requires beating several opponents in sequence: Chamberlain Ulrich, Blacksmith Radovan, Bailiff Thrush, Innkeeper Betty. Defeating the final opponent will award you 200 Groschen and the Gold wedding badge.

## Shrine

Shrines and conciliation crosses are locations that serve both as places of prayer and as important landmarks, common on the crossroads. In both Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, their locations are shown on the maps.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance

In the first game, each painting in a church and each shrine and conciliation cross bears a name of a person that believed in the game and supported it through one of the higher tiers on Kickstarter. Reading at least 90 out of the 131 names earns you the achievement Pilgrim. During the Woman's Lot questline of Johanka, Henry will have to repent for his sins by praying at shrines on the path from Sasau to Uzhitz.

## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II

With the perks Fundamentals of Theology and Fundamentals of Theology II, Henry can pray at any wayside shrine for a useful buff. If Henry's sins are too great to bear, he may choose to ask a priest for penance, starting the Pilgrimage quest and granting the achievement Penitent One upon first completion.

## Sigismund of Luxembourg

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

There's a fortress standing on every damned hill here. What side are their lords on?

—Sigismund (The King's Gambit)

Sigismund of Luxembourg (Czech: Zikmund Lucemburský) (15 February 1368 – 9 December 1437), also referred to as the Red Fox (Czech: liška ryšavá) by Bohemians, is King of Hungary and Croatia, Germany, Bohemia, Italy and at a later point in life the Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire. He is a son of Charles IV and younger half-brother of Wenceslas IV of Bohemia. The actions of him and his army lead to the events of Kingdom Come: Deliverance.

He serves as the overarching antagonist of Kingdom Come: Deliverance, and the DLC A Woman's Lot. He serves as one of main antagonists of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

### Kingdom Come Deliverance

Due to the continuous failures of King Wenceslas IV, who did not manage to live up to the reputation of his father Charles IV and preferred frivolous pursuits over political affairs, the Czech nobility looked for someone more suitable to the throne. Their choice fell on King Wenceslas' half-brother: King Sigismund of Hungary.

Sigismund opted for a radical solution: with the support of the nobility, he kidnapped King Wenceslas and forced him to abdicate, in order to gain the crown for himself. Then, at the head of a massive army composed mostly by Cuman mercenaries and commanded by his trusted general Sir Markvart von Aulitz, he invaded the kingdom of Bohemia, defeating all the nobles who remained loyal to Wenceslas.

In December of 1402, Sigismund conquered and sacked the city of Kuttenberg, stealing a large amount of silver. This allowed him to expand his already powerful army. Later, in 1403, Sigismund attacked the settlement of Silver Skalitz, in order to take control of the rich silver mines and to kill Sir Radzig Kobyla, the local Lord who remained loyal to Wenceslas. Although Sigismund managed to conquer the mines and destroy Skalitz, Sir Radzig escaped. Sigismund and his lieutenant Markvart searched for him throughout the local region, heading first toward Talmberg, from where however they returned empty-handed.

Sigismund's attack on Skalitz would result in the destruction of Henry's home, as well as the death of his parents and many of his friends. This is turn would spark his desire for vengeance.

### Kingdom Come Deliverance II

## Codex entry

14.2.1368 - 9.12.1437

Sigismund of Luxembourg, son of Charles IV, was King of Hungary and Croatia from 1387, King of Germany from 1411, King of Bohemia from 1419 and King of Italy from 1431. He was also Prince of Silesia, from 1419 Margrave of Lusatia and most notably Holy Roman Emperor between 1433 and 1437.

At an early age, he was sent to be educated at the Hungarian court, quickly mastering the tough conditions of politics. Like other members of his family, he was abducted at least once (in his case by the Hungarian nobility). Having lost faith in the Hungarian nobility, he turned his attention to Bohemia and became engaged in hostilities with his half-brother, Wenceslas. Some of the Bohemian nobility welcomed Sigismund, hoping he would rid them of their ineffective monarch, while others sided with Wenceslas, resulting in long-lasting wars, in the course of which Sigismund and his Hungarian army (consisting in no small part of Cuman mercenaries) repeatedly pillaged Bohemia, often with the help of Bohemian - and especially Moravian - lords themselves. Sigismund fought not only to seize his brother's throne, but also against the Hussites with the aim of seizing the Imperial crown. He regarded himself as the defender of Christianity and in 1409 even founded the Order of the Dragon to wage war against all enemies of the Christian faith. (One of the later members of the order was the infamous Vlad the Impaler, inspiration for the fictional Dracula).

After the death of Wenceslas, Sigismund brought to Bohemia four unsuccessful crusades against the Hussites. He died soon after the signing of the Compacts – a set of agreements with the reformers guaranteeing freedom of religious belief to every inhabitant of the lands of Bohemia and Moravia.

## Silence is Golden

Silence is Golden is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Thanks to you the raid on Semine didn't happen.

## Acquisition

The Silence is Golden achievement is tied to the events of the main quest involving Otto von Bergow and the raid on Semine. All you have to do is avoid revealing the incriminating information to von Bergow. If he learns of it, he will order the raid, which prevents this achievement from unlocking.

## Tips

- To unlock the achievement, you must successfully convince von Bergow that "Nobody helped the bandits here." This dialogue option appears when you report to von Bergow after interrogating the prisoner. If you did not mention Olda Semine's disappearance from the wedding during your earlier meeting with him in the previous quest Back in the Saddle, the persuasion will be easier. However, if you did report Olda missing, von Bergow will be aware of the connection, and you'll need a high Persuasion stat to succeed.

- To pass the "Very Hard" skill check, increase your Charisma and Speech using gear, perks, and potions. The strong Lion Perfume (+7 Charisma for 5 minutes) can help significantly.

- Additionally, the following perks offer notable bonuses:

- Jack of All Trades (Speech lvl 10) +2 to all skill checks.

- Local Hero (Main lvl 10) +2 to all stats in regions where you have high reputation.

- Burgher (Main lvl 10) +1 to Strength, Agility, Vitality, and Speech in towns.

- Flower Power (Survival lvl 8) +2 Charisma when carrying a large number of fresh herbs.

- With sufficient stats, select "Nobody helped the bandits here" and follow up with "I must have made a mistake." If successful, von Bergow will reply: "Hmm… I have never suffered from that, but I have heard such things. That is plausible. Very well." At this point, the achievement should unlock.

## Silent Partner

Silent Partner is a hidden achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You handed over the evidence from the underground and no one died.

## Acquisition

To earn the Silent Partner achievement, you must complete the In the Service of the Guild – Silent Partner activity for Klaus Eichner.

- Follow Klaus to his younger brother, Olbert, and search an abandoned mine shaft for evidence.

- Retrieve the proof without killing the guards (knocking them out is fine).

- Return the dagger to Klaus Eichner and the achievement will unlock.

## Tips

- Make a save after unlocking the yard door and before entering the area to prevent losing the achievement if a guard is accidentally killed.

- Loot the two chests in the storage area of the mine to obtain the Sketch for armourer I and Sketch for caster II, required for the Innovator achievement.

## Silent Witnesses

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Silent Witnesses is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 3rd quest in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC.

## Description

Where did the illness in the Sedletz Monastery come from? The trail leads to the crypt beneath the church.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Albich and Zacharias to figure out your next move. Albich wants you to search the crypt whether or not the Abbot gives permission.

Since the monastery is officially on lockdown now. Any formerly public areas of the monastery will be considered private and you will be warned with escalating consequences for being caught. You’ll have to sneak to avoid the patrolling guards and talk to the workers to see if they have any insights on what may have been unleashed by their construction.

Zacharias will suggest you get a plague mask to avoid breathing in foul air. You’ll need mint, a rope, and some leather to make one, starting Prevention.

The construction site is under surveillance, so you’ll have to sneak past the knights on-guard to get close to the crypt and the workers. Speaking to any of them will direct you to one called Workman Loyza

Tell Loyza you’ll scratch his back and he’ll ask you to get him some booze, due to the plague of course. Get him some and he’ll answer your questions. There are two main groups of workers, those who work above-ground and those who work in the crypt.

The crypt workers have their tents by the monastery walls. Search a chest there to find a golden cross.

To get into the crypt, you’ll have to either unlock the very hard lock on the door or find a key. The main outside door to the church will have a worker standing guard, if you talk to him you can convince him with an easy intimidation or hard speech check to let you in and he’ll give you the key. There will also be labourers around who you can pickpocket or rob to get monastery keys if need be. Once inside, you'll remark on the pit. There will be a couple of labourers talking inside, so tread lightly as this is a trespassing zone.

Head down the ladder or leap to enter the crypt itself and the game will autosave. Soon, it will become clear that the graves are being robbed. Find a map of the crypt on an open tomb to your right. At the far end of the room is a table with a note on it. Pick it up and the door will close behind you, labourers having locked you in.

The door is locked by a very hard lock you can pick or you can escape through the wall to the left of the table where you found the parchment. Follow the tunnel and you’ll come back to where you started. Either way this will lead to an altercation with Foreman Ondra. He’s looking for a man called Boleslav Bavor whom he believes you’ve found. They will initiate combat and you’ll have to kill them to leave.

Head back to Albich in the infirmary and find his room has been ransacked and robbed. Albich believes the thieves were after his copy of notes regarding King Wenceslas’s health and treatment history. No one knows who might have done it, but Zacharias suspects the Abbot.

Albich will send you to see if Benedict or Denes noticed anything. Benedict didn’t see anything but Denes thinks he saw a monk go in, though he can’t say which one. Head back to Albich and catch him up to speed on the crypt situation, ending the quest.

## Objectives

## Sinners of Kuttenberg

Sinners of Kuttenberg is a repeatable task in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. After completing Sculptor without a Future, Innkeeper Mole will occasionally offer these tasks in the daily rotation.

## Description

All people are sinners, the rich think they can do anything, and the poor often have nothing left to lose. A person should therefore try to help where it makes sense, perhaps then the world will become a better place.

## Repeatable Task

### Debt Notes

Walkthrough

Go to the indicated location and steal the requested item(s). Although this quest is somewhat procedural and may not follow the exact description given here, Mole will always tell you where to go and which floor the item(s) will be on. Quest items are usually in chests, although they must sometimes be pickpocketed. Once you have the item(s), return to Mole to complete the task.

## Sinners of Kuttenberg - Fake Will

### Walkthrough

You'll get this quest directly from Ragman this time. He usually hangs out at the All Saints' Tavern during the day. If you talk to him there, he'll ask you to meet him at the Iron Eagle in the evening. Talk to Ragman at the Iron Eagle in the evening (as early as 8pm). He will be in the same seat from Sculptor without a Future.

He needs you to exchange a will that can be found in the fortress at Pschitoky. Once you accept this quest, it becomes timed and must be completed during the same night. Head to Pschitoky and go over to the fortress. Depending on the time of night you arrive, the guards will be quite active. It is best to wait until midnight when the guards inside will have gone to sleep.

The safest way in is around the side over the scaffold. The lectern is in the tower, up the stairs behind an easy locked door. There will be a guard posted right at this door if it is too early. Once in the tower, go to the hard locked door on you left behind the stairs. Here you'll find there are two documents out, compare the documents on the table to the one in your inventory and swap the one that has matching names.

With that done, return to Ragman to end the quest.

### Objectives

## Sinners of Kuttenberg - Ragman's Dream

### Walkthrough

Ragman needs your help; his documents have been stolen and he's being blackmailed. He's been gathering rags for so long in the aim of using them to start producing paper. He needs you to deliver the ransom to keep his future business dealings afloat.

The handoff is to happen by Kurzhim gate (the western one), and you're to look for a man with red hair and a green hood. You'll find him (helpfully named Blackmailer) leaning against a wagon near his associate. Agree to pay the ransom, and they'll tell you to pick up the documents from the almoner who just went into town.

The monk is walking around the search area, so you'll have to keep an eye out for him, but he's dressed all in white with a red hat. To get the documents from him, pass a very hard speech or medium intimidation check. This part of the quest is timed; if you do not find the almoner in time, the activity will fail.

Head back to Ragman to end the quest. He'll give you Liber Razielis Archangeli (only if you choose the dialogue option "If only that dream of mine made more coin."), Sketch for armourer II, Sketch for caster I, and Sketch - Kilij, Lion's roar.

## Skeleton in the Closet

Skeleton in the Closet is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is available following the side quest Bellatores.

## Description

Jan Posy and Miroslav Tugbone need help with the Cumans, who have stolen their chest. I have no idea what’s in it but Posy really wants it. The Cumans probably still have it.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Posy to start the quest. Now that he and Miroslav are settled in the ruins of their family’s ancient castle, they need your help recovering the mysterious item they have been looking for.

You’ll ride with them to a location housing a Cuman camp in some woods. You’ll have the opportunity to either go in and deal with stealth or do a frontal attack, as in Bellatores. The easiest and safest way to deal with the Cumans is to opt for stealth, as they are quite numerous even for three fighters to handle.

There will be a guard post near the edge of the forest where a few of the Cumans will wander one at a time. Take them out one-by-one and be sure to place their bodies outside the range of sight of the next. Once they stop coming to that area, sneak around behind the camp to find a second post where Cumans will come to sit on a log and work on some carpentry. Take them out until they stop coming over.

All that should be left at this point is the guard in the camp and their leader, Sharkan, who will stay in his tent unless alerted. Take them out and return to Posy to tell him the good news.

He will ask you to locate the stolen chest. You’ll find it in the locked chest in the red tent, where the Cuman leader was. You can loot the key for it from his body. Loot the Zimburg reliquary from the chest and return it to its rightful owners, ending the quest.

## Objectives

## Trivia

According to the game files, the working name of this quest was Brothers from Zimburg,

## Slavek of the Order

Slavek of the Order is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Slavek joined the Order as Ritterbrüder Ludolf was travelling through Bohemia. Along the way, the Order stopped for shelter at Sedletz Monastery and set up camp there temporarily. While there, he sparred with another recent recruit, Jeshek, and the two were mutually injured.

Slavek claimed that Jeshek pounced on him out of nowhere and he had to defend himself. Meanwhile, Jeshek claimed that Slavek had been running his gob, insulting Jeshek’s mother, and so Jeshek lost his temper a little and jabbed him – politely – in the shoulder. Slavek went high and smacked Jeshek on the head while Jeshek went for Slavek’s legs and ribs.

When being carried to the infirmary, Slavek lost his purse when it got snagged on a bush.

The two spent most of their time in the infirmary recovering from their injuries engaged in banter with each other over who was at fault for the injuries and whether it was fair.

When Henry came over to check on them, they asked for him to settle their dispute – happy to have his opinion as the tiebreaker. They wanted him to know there were not really any hard feeling between them. Despite their heated exchange, they were glad to be in the infirmary together and thus didn’t have to deal with Ludolf. They also requested that Henry tell Servant Brother Karl no harm was done and they were not seriously injured, if Henry happened to see him.

## Inventory

## Slip the Noose

Slip the Noose is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You managed to talk your way out of an execution.

## Acquisition

To unlock the achievement, you must be sentenced to execution and then successfully talk your way out of it. This requires first committing a serious crime like murder and accepting to be branded, which imposes a 48-hour penalty. During this period, you must commit another serious crime.

When surrendering, you'll have to persuade the guard to spare your life. Success depends on having around 28 Charisma, and sufficient Speech and Persuasion, ideally around 28 and 22 respectively.

You will have multiple dialogue options to avoid execution:

- Pay an 800 gold fine.

- "We can come to an arrangement."

- "Do you know who I am?"

- "Let me go or else!"

- "The law is on my side."

Choosing "We can come to an arrangement" and succeeding in a skill check usually unlocks the achievement.

## Tips

- Strong Lion perfume (+7 Charisma for 5 minutes) is a great way to ensure your Charisma is sufficiently high.

- Perks such as Flower Power (+2 Charisma when carrying fresh herbs), Burgher (+1 Speech in settlements), and Local Hero (+2 to all stats in friendly areas) also greatly improve your chances.

## Smelter Shima

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Smelter Shima is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Shima worked as a smelter in Grund under the supervision of Foreman Volkmar. He did not enjoy working as a smelter, complaining of health issues and the inevitability of becoming crippled. He had no other prospects, however, so he could not lose the job without being unable to provide for his family.

He was aware of the embezzlement and fraud operation at work, but was not actively involved. When Henry came to Grund to look into the operation, Shima was forthright with him and let him know who at the smelter was involved and to what extent.

He was, however, unwilling to speak ill of his employer, Buresh of Krakovitz, for fear of his job and life.

## Biography

Volkmar was the foreman of the smelters at Grund, working under Buresh of Krakovitz. In this role, he was intimidated and bribed into perpetuating the silver siphoning scheme his boss helped operate. When a new foreman was appointed at the Horschan mines, Buresh sent Volkmar to intimidate him in turn to continue cooking the books to keep things running.

He eventually was found out when Henry came to investigate the allegations of counterfeit groschen minting. Volkmar tried to have Henry killed, enlisting the help of Buresh's guard, Little Nary, to do so. However, Henry was able to defeat Little Nary, leaving Volkmar at his mercy.

Volkmark explained his part in the operation and provided Henry with a map that would direct him to the secret mint that Vavak was operating in the area. He then had no other option but to beg Henry for mercy which may or may not have been afforded him.
