## So it begins…

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

So it begins... is the 27th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically at the conclusion of Civitas Pragensis.

## Synopsis

The Prague army has marched on Suchdol to retrieve the silver stolen from the Italian Court.

## Walkthrough

The siege of Suchdol begins

Immediately upon completion of the cutscene, Zizka will be directing you to the walls to help repel the attack. If you don’t have one in your inventory from The Italian Job, pick up a polearm as you’ll need it shortly. The first wave will shoot out from behind the shield wall, you can take aim at them with a bow or crossbow or else wait them out.

Eventually, the enemies will turn their attention to the gate. Run over on the walls and you can drop stones on them to repel them.

Once that wave has passed, they’ll start sending ladders up. Take care to take out any enemies that make it over the walls, it is possible to get surrounded if too many succeed without being killed. There will be other defenders trying to push down the ladder as well, so if you get overwhelmed by enemies it’s fine to focus on taking them out first.

### Get your orders

With the first advance repelled, things settle into siege preparations. Godwin will tell you Zizka is waiting to give you orders at the walls, but you can speak to some of your other allies first. Follow Godwin out to the bailey and up the stairs to get your orders from Zizka. You can go and do the optional objectives first, or in tandem with Zizka’s request.

Zizka wants to make you a commander, and a commander needs men to command. You’ll have to go find your recruits and let them know they now report to you.

### Find your recruits

You’ll have to go to the members of your new company and let them know to assemble for further orders.

You’ll find Sam and Kubyenka will be in the kitchens. Where you’ll also have a chance to speak with Janosh if you haven’t already.

Wolfram is in the cellar. He’s not too happy to be involved in warfare. You can pass a very high impression check to give him a boost of morale.

Dobrosh is up by the walls practising his aim. He will offer a shooting competition with bows which you can accept for reputation.

Note: If left alive during Fortuna, Wolfram and Dobrosh will be replaced by Mikesh and Kozliek.

Old friends, Jaroslav and Janek, are sitting at the dice table near the smithy in the outer bailey.

Once you’ve spoken to everyone, you’ll find them assembled in the outer bailey, near the inner gate.

### Give your orders

Once you’ve spoken to everyone, your men will be waiting for their orders, talk to them. If you’d like you can pass a skill check to inspire them. The medium speech and hard impression checks will gain reputation and the medium domination check will lose some.

Then give your orders. Have them reinforce the night watch, this will help with the upcoming night attack and get you rep with Zizka.

If you haven’t yet, you’ll have the opportunity before going to bed to check in with your other allies around the fortress.

### Check on your allies

In the kitchens, you’ll find Janosh. Speak to him and he’ll give you your rations for the day. Once you’ve spoken to him, head across the yard to find Musa and Katherine. They’ll let you know you can come see them for treatment when necessary.

Frenzl can be found in the outer bailey at the smithy. Offer to help him and he’ll ask you to sharpen a couple old swords so they can be used. You’ll find them on the table next to Frenzl. Pick them up then head over the to nearby grindstone to sharpen them or use a blacksmith's kit. Once they are sharp, return them to Frenzl.

By the baths you’ll find a weeping housewife. You can comfort her with a medium speech check.

### Help the Nightwatch

Go to bed to trigger waiting for night watch. As you head up the stairs, you’ll be flagged down by Hans for a chat. Talk to him. You can finish with a medium scholarship check for some reputation, then tell him "you’ll manage this."

Once you speak with him, go get some sleep. You’ll be woken up by Dry Devil who’s come to the end of his shift. Your duty is to patrol and make sure everyone is doing what they should. Make sure you still have a polearm in your inventory, as the night will not be a calm one.

You can visit them all, but the one you need to check is posted on the western palisade. At the eastern wall, you’ll find Janosh who will report everything looks calm at the main camp. At the gate, you’ll find a guard asleep at his post, punch him to wake him. At the outer bailey gate, you’ll find a guard who will report all clear on their side as well.

Finally, head to the western palisade. This guard is an imposter, a Praguer who sneaked in, confront him and the night attack will start. The Praguer forces will rush forward, trying to get over the walls, push down the ladders as you can and kill the rest of the enemies. The one downside to reinforcing the watch with your men is that, save Kubyenka and Sam, they can be killed. Deal with the Praguers as quickly as possible, should any of them die, Zizka will mention it in the following scene. If you’re able to lower the ladders quickly, only a few enemies should make it over.

Once they’re dealt with, Zizka will give a speech in the outer bailey. After he’s done, talk to him and report. Then there will be a cutscene and the quest will end, starting the next, Besieged.

## Something rotten...

Something rotten… is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Innkeeper Grosch from Grund has trouble with a gang that comes to his inn and makes a mess. They’re led by a man called Eggman, and the innkeeper has it in for him.

## Walkthrough

Talk to the innkeeper in Grund and ask him how things are to start the quest. He wants you to help him be rid of a nasty group who have recently taken to patronising his inn, lead by a man called Eggman. He’ll give you a Strong Bane potion that he was originally planning to use on them the next time they stopped in and will tell you where their camp is. If you’ve completed The Magic Arrow, Henry will remark he already knows the camp.

You can take out the entire group or just Eggman. There are 7 of them, so be prepared if you choose a front-on attack. You can also work in stealth, and even make use of the poison Grosch gave you. Once Eggman is dead, loot him and take his hat then return to Grosch.

The hat, it seems, used to belong to a pilgrim who was caught by Eggman’s band and forced to walk until he died of exhaustion. You can pass a medium scholarship check to request a mass be said in that pilgrim’s honour which will earn reputation. Grosch will thank you for your service, rewarding you with 150 groschen.

## Source of Inspiration

Source of Inspiration is the 2nd quest in the Brushes with Death DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The painter has heard of a shrine of the pagan god Veles located somewhere in the area. He would like to find it and use it as inspiration for one of his paintings. However, he doesn’t know where to find where the shrine is and needs me help to find it.

## Synopsis

Henry comes by Voyta’s studio to ask if the painter has anything he could help with. Voyta thinks Henry has certainly already done enough, but he cannot refuse the offer as Voyta believes he and Henry were fated to meet. Voyta wants to create a lasting masterpiece and Henry can help him. In the Trosky region lies an old Pagan shrine to the god Veles, the only problem is that no one remembers where it is. This is where Henry comes in, being quite skilled at finding lost things.

Voyta has a lead; there’s an old woman who lives at Vidlak Pond called Kvyetoslava who knows something about the shrine. Voyta is sure of this as he was directed to her by some locals when he was looking around in the area; however, her memory isn’t what it once was.

Henry asks her about the shrine but she is distracted, mooning over her late husband and reminiscing. Henry tries to help jog her memory by bringing her the flowers she used to be brought, mending her best dress, and even reciting poetry for her. It takes some effort, but she is able to remember something, in the end – a few locations her grandmother took her as a child. She warns Henry that she thinks Voyta is bad news, having given her the impression something was terribly wrong with him when they interacted previously.

Henry searches all the places she mentioned, eventually finding the shrine near Semine. There are some bandits set up there and Henry deals with them before returning to tell Voyta what he’s found. When he hears of the bandits, Voyta asks if one of them was wearing a distinctive helmet brushing off Henry’s questions when it turns out none of them had been.

Voyta travels there to see it with Henry and sets up to start painting. While he paints, Henry falls asleep under a nearby tree. After finishing the painting, Voyta notices Henry sleeping and mischievously tosses an apple at him to wake him up. He shows Henry the finished piece and asks for his opinion.

Voyta is happy with the piece but it still isn’t quite the enduring masterpiece he wants to create. Having finished painting, Voyta has become somewhat uneasy. He says the place speaks to him, telling him the history of the shrine and its god. With his work done, Voyta heads back to the castle but not before telling Henry he has another little job for him.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Voyta in his studio to start the quest. He’ll ask you to help him with finding an old pagan shrine and will direct you to the tanner's at Vidlak Pond to speak to an old woman there called Kvyetoslava.

Note: Kvyetoslava has memory issues and will require you to do a few things for her to jog her memory. Before heading over, make sure you have a Tailor's kit to avoid a detour.

Over at the tanner’s, you’ll find Kvyetoslava nearby most likely working in the vegetable beds. Talk to her and she will mention how her husband used to bring her valerian flowers. There is plenty of valerian in the area, but the closest ones are to the north-east by the stream. Once you have enough, return to Kvyetoslava and give them to her.

Next, you’ll offer to repair her old dress. Use a tailor’s kit (repair will cost about 10) and return it to her.

Finally, compose a poem for her. This section will require skill checks and passing the following will get you the achievement Poet's Gut:

- She yearned for something more (medium scholarship)

- He brought her gifts (medium charisma)

- They were equals (hard scholarship)

- Remember Veles (hard scholarship)

Ask again after the shrine and she will tell you three places it could be located. You can visit all three, but the one you want is the one named last and located between the other two in a gorge south of Lower Semine Pond. There will be bandits here (if you haven’t cleared them out already during your travels), so be prepared.

When you reach the shrine, Henry will notice a dead man with a dagger in his head. The dagger is a Rondel dagger so worth grabbing even just to sell if you aren’t interested in using it as your primary dagger.

The bandits are nearby just on the other side of the gorge. You can deal with them however you like. They leave only one guard at night, so taking them out with stealth during the night is the least risky option. Once you’ve cleared the area, head back to Trosky to report to Voyta to end the quest.

## Speak of the Devil

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Speak of the Devil is the 14th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

"Zizka and I set out to find the Dry Devil, who is hiding somewhere around Kuttenberg and sabotaging Sigismund's efforts."

## Synopsis

Henry and Zizka head out to search for the Dry Devil. If it comes to it, Zizka is willing to stop in at every tavern they pass until some trace is found, but he wants to start at a place he’s heard is favoured by less savoury patrons – the Devil's Den.

They arrive there to find a few patrons in the middle of a disagreement. One very drunk man, is being accosted by a few others, accused of cheating at dice. Before they can kill him, Zizka intervenes - the two men, it seems, know each other. A fight breaks out and the attackers are killed. Zizka complains about having to save the drunk, Kubyenka, from another sticky situation, and introductions are made.

Kubyenka is a member of Dry Devil’s band and a fine archer, though he’s also a sodden drunk. Kubyenka explains that the Devil’s Pack has been scattered and Dry Devil was taken captive in Kuttenberg a few weeks prior, though Kubyenka can’t remember exactly how long it’s been. The only thing that’s kept Dry Devil alive this long is that everyone wants a more spectacular execution for him than just hanging or beheading. To do so, he will be brought from Kuttenberg to Sigismund's camp, giving Henry and Zizka a chance to spring him.

Zizka will have to hire men to help, but Kubyenka mentions they had some hand cannons that should still be at their old camp at least. Henry goes with Kubyenka to look for them while Zizka rustles up some men to meet them at a suitable ambush spot.

On the way to the camp, Kubyenka gets to know Henry a little, asking after how he came to be in cahoots with Zizka, and jokes with him about his own past and Henry’s attitude. Kubyenka can’t remember exactly where the hand cannons were hidden, but he has a few ideas. After a few false starts, and much grumbling from Henry, they find them.

With the hand cannons retrieved, Henry and Kubyenka can head to meet Zizka at the ambush spot. Kubyenka sings a bawdy tune as the travel, much to Henry’s chagrin. Zizka has everything just about set up at the ambush spot, having wrangled some men and a wagon to block the road.

Sometime later, the convoy approaches, with Dry Devil talking the ears off of every man who guards him. Henry and Zizka are in the road by the wagon, pretending to be its riders trying in vain to get a lost wheel back on. They light the fuses on their handgonnes and turn around, ready to blast the guards away. Their shots, however, miss, managing only to take out one of the cart horses and knock a helmet off of one of the guard’s head. One of the hired men even manages to shoot Dry Devil in the leg with a crossbow bolt.

Henry loudly proclaims that was only a warning shot, but the lead guard isn’t much too threatened. Henry may convince the guards they present a real threat or else have to fight their way into freeing Dry Devil. As the dust settles, the group put the wheel back on the wagon and leave back for the Devil’s Den with the Devil in tow.

Once back, the quartet share a drink and discuss what comes next.

## Walkthrough

Head to the Devil's Den inn to see Kubyenka getting thrown out of the building by a group of armed men threatening to kill him. Kill the men and Kubyenka will tell you that Dry Devil was captured and is being held in Kuttenberg. However, Sigismund wants to make an example out of him via an especially nasty execution, and to do so he'll be transported to Sigismund's Camp. The group decides that ambushing the guards while they're transporting Hynek is the only realistic chance they'll have at freeing him.

### Find the guns

The group agrees that hand cannons would be helpful for the ambush, and luckily Kubyenka has maybe, surely hid them in the woods nearby the ambush spot, and Henry needs to accompany him there to help find them. When you arrive at the old camp, Kubyenka won't remember exactly where the guns are, only that they buried them somewhere nearby, so you'll have to go digging (grab the spade leaning against the tent if you didn't bring one). The first spot you dig will contain only a bottle of Saviour Schnapps. At the second spot he'll ask you to grab some Moonshine out of the creek for him, which you can do if you want to see him get even drunker, otherwise it doesn't affect the quest. At the third spot you'll dig up his old friend, who you can loot for some groschen, a few lockpicks, and some cheap armour. At the fourth spot you'll find the guns, along with some ammunition and a strong Bowman's Brew. Grab everything, equip your battle gear, and head to the ambush site with Kubyenka.

### The ambush

When you arrive at the ambush site, Kubyenka and Zizka will discuss preparations for the ambush itself, and then a cutscene will play. Note: BEFORE you talk to Zizka, drink all the potions you can and poison all the weapons you'll use to give yourself the best possible chance for the fight ahead if you don't think you'll pass the skillchecks. The ambush goes comically wrong from the start, but before the fighting begins you'll be given one chance to talk your way out of it with a Charisma, Intimidation, or Speech check. All checks are Hard (25 Charisma still failed the check, so maybe they should be classed as Very Hard?), so be prepared to fight. Also note here that the fight is MUCH more difficult if you fail the Charisma check, as several of your men will run off, leaving you significantly outnumbered. Also, the fight happens even if you pass the Charisma check with no noticeable differences save for some reputation gain. The Speech and Intimidation checks, if passed, both result in some of the enemies successfully being intimidated and running away before the fight (as well as gain and loss of reputation, respectively).

### The fight

If you failed the skillchecks, you'll have to fight your way out. If you choose the Charisma check specifically and fail it, this is one of the more difficult fights in the game as you're heavily outnumbered against multiple well-armed and armoured soldiers, you can't run away, and you can't drink any potions that aren't already equipped in your belt. Your best bet here is to try and kill the enemy closest to you that Zizka is fighting with the preloaded gun you're holding, and then maybe try to quickly reload and kill the captain just behind him (assuming Zizka draws aggro on him as well). At this point all your allies will be dead or unconscious (except maybe Zizka) so you'll want to pull out a melee weapon and play extremely defensively here. Try circling around the cart continuously to keep the enemies funnelled in a line -- if you get surrounded you're dead. Alternatively, reload the game and choose any of the other dialogue options and the fight will be much easier as both sides will have roughly the same number of soldiers.

Once the soldiers are dispatched, loot as much as you like then talk to Zizka to fast travel back to Devil's Den with Dry Devil in tow. Back at the inn, the group will discuss their next move as the quest concludes.

## Spoils of War

Spoils of War is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available after Speak of the Devil, but will be prompted during The Lion's Den if not already completed.

## Description

Once I managed to get inside Sigismund's camp, I had to make it look like I belonged there. And that meant working, such as rustling up supplies from a nearby village. But should I help them?

## Walkthrough

Talk to Captain Puta before 1 p.m. and agree to go with him to requisition supplies to start the quest. After the cutscene, you’ll be given the orders to gather supplies from the townsfolk and to search for anything they might have tried to hide from the soldiers.

If you talk to Bynyek, you can convince him with an easy speech check to tell you a few locations where the villagers have indeed hidden supplies from the soldiers and with a very hard speech check his own hiding spot. There are a few ways this quest can go. You can either keep both parties alive, side with the soldiers against the villagers, or with the villagers against the soldiers.

### Gather all supplies for soldiers

Talk to Farmer Smil, and he’ll tell you his prepared supplies are next to his cottage door. His additional hidden supplies can be found inside his barn out back in a sack hidden in the hay. To the right, there is also a locked cellar. You can ask Smil about this or pick the lock, and you’ll find a stockpile of beer which you can tell Puta about.

Then talk to Farmer Fowl. His prepared supplies are in his yard next to the gate. For additional supplies, head into the barn where you can examine to notice there are cows missing. Go up the stairs and across a walkway you can make it to the top floor of his house where he’s hidden more food. To find the cows, go into the woods and follow the stream south until you hear mooing then go east, the cows will be just hidden off the path.

Talk to Willow, he’ll tell you his prepared supplies are behind the door just inside his house. You’ll find them right in front of you to the left between the two rooms inside. You’ll also find an injured man named Vitek, treating him is optional and although doing so will not gain you more supplies, you can use the information he will tell you after being treated to extort some groschen and the locations of various hidden stashes (the beer, cows, and plague graves) out of Willow.

For Bynyek’s supplies, talk to his daughter Sovka in front of their house. She’ll tell you the prepared supplies are in the house, below the window that will be in front of you as you enter. His hidden supplies can be found in the plague graves just outside the village. Dig up the grave on the left to loot the valuables inside.

Once you have everything loaded, talk to Puta to return to the camp and end the quest. It is possible to take all the hidden supplies and have a peaceful ending, however, if you extort too much from the villagers, they will revolt.

### Gather minimum supplies for villagers

It is possible to take only what the villagers set aside and still succeed. To do so, however, you will have to donate some of your own food and/or valuables to a total of about 2000 groschen.

Puta will treat anything placed in the requisition chest as having been donated by the villagers.

### Treat the wounded villager

No matter what amount of supplies you wish to gather from the villagers, you’ll have the opportunity to heal Vitek.

To do so, talk to him once you'll notice he’s too injured to speak, but this will then give you the opportunity to examine him. Pass a medium craftsmanship or thievery check to remove his bandage to find he was injured by a sword. Then pass a medium warfare or scholarship check to check the wound and determine it is infected.

For treatment, you’ll need alcohol or a Painkiller brew to stave off pain, alcohol to clean the wound, and a bandage to redress it. Redressing the wound will also require a medium craftsmanship check.

If treated, he’ll tell you he was injured by soldiers who were trying to requisition supplies - the advance Puta had sent earlier. You can then talk to Willow again to gain more information. Initially, Willow will say Vitek was injured by cutthroats, pass a medium speech, easy intimidation check, or tell him Vitek already told you the truth to learn more.

You can then choose what to do with the knowledge. Telling Puta will cause the soldiers to initiate combat with the villagers and you can then choose which side to fight on through dialogue. You can also keep quiet, or extort some groschen out of Willow for your silence. It will also give you the opportunity to squeeze him to tell you where the hidden supplies of all the villagers are. He will tell you about the beer, the cows, and the plague graves with increasing speech or intimidation checks.

Talking to Sovka and passing a medium speech check will also give you more information regarding the dead soldiers. She’ll admit the whole situation was premeditated by the villagers and that the soldiers were buried behind the village not far from where they were killed. Behind Willow’s house is a loft where you can find a bloodstain, follow it to the road where you’ll find another and then follow the cart tracks into the woods to find the dead soldiers and the broken cart.

## Stained Honour

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Stained Honour is the 6th or 7th quest in the Brushes with Death DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is given concurrently with Man Proposes.

## Description

The painter Voyta is busy with preparations for the altar in Sedletz, so he has no time to deal with his smaller commissions. Not even the completed ones that have yet to be paid for.

## Synopsis

Henry offers to help Voyta with an outstanding payment for work he did for the bailiff of Pschitoky. The situation is slightly complicated, instead of groschen, payment was arranged to be a precious stone which can be used to produce a beautiful blue pigment – lapis lazuli. However, the bailiff went back on the promise, wanting to offer groschen instead, something Voyta is unwilling to accept. If Henry can’t get the stone, then better to paint on an inscription to say they didn’t pay him for the work.

The bailiff is unwilling to be moved. When confronted, he insists the reward he offered Voyta was even better than the stone and he simply needs it more than Voyta does. The stone is a good luck charm for him. It seems, after the death of Anna of Waldstein, a friend of hers called Adela of Mnischek arrived in the region to oversee the construction and the bailiff very much wants to impress her.

Henry may convince the bailiff to duel him to impress Adela rather than using the stone which surely a lady like herself has plenty. The bailiff’s plan is for Henry to insult Adela at an agreed upon time, so the bailiff can step in and defend her honour.

Henry may go along with that plan or else let Adela know what the bailiff was doing. She is sick of the bailiff’s attention and would quite like to see him humiliated. Henry may then defeat him in a duel for Adela’s sake.

## Walkthrough

Following The Night-Mare speak to Voyta and ask if he needs help with anything else. It turns out, Voyta has an outstanding invoice with the bailiff of Pschitoky that he wants you to collect on in the form of a precious stone.

Head to Pschitoky and speak to the bailiff. You can pickpocket him and get the gem that way or you can agree to duel him. At this point, there are a few different ways you can go about things.

### Deface the Work

In the bailiff’s room in the new fortress is Voyta’s painting. Inspecting it will allow you to paint over it with an inscription insulting the bailiff. Doing this will get you the achievement Painted, but it will also end the quest, skipping most of the rewards.

The room will be guarded by Guard Yedlitchka you can pass a hard speech check to convince him to leave.

After having defaced the work, go back to Voyta and he will reward you with the Miser's cuirass, ending the quest.

Note: If you knock out the bailiff during the night, you can deface the painting and rob him of the lapis lazuli.

### Duel the Bailiff

To go with the bailiff’s plan, find Adela sitting under a tree on the road to the west during the morning. Talking to her will further allow you to choose a couple of paths. You can choose to either do as he asked, and insult her and lose the duel or tell her about his plan and then beat him.

Going along with the bailiff will get you the stone, defeating him after having told Adela the plan will get you 1050 . If you beat the bailiff, you’ll have to pickpocket the stone, as he will be too upset to want to give it to you.

Alternatively, if you want to deface the mural instead, Adela will give you tacit permission to do so and to send her guard away. If you knock out the bailiff and then paint the mural you’ll be able to rob him and do both.

### Return to Voyta

Once you have the stone, whatever method you used to get it, go back to Kuttenberg and tell Voyta the news. He will reward you with the Miser's cuirass and 225 , ending the quest.

## Standa the Fly

Standa the Fly is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II and a major character in the Legacy of the Forge DLC.

## Biography

Standa was a journeyman armourer under Master Shkoda in Kuttenberg alongside Martin in his youth. He earned the nickname 'Fly' due to his shy and quiet nature making him seem like a fly on the wall.

During his time under Shkoda, they tried to fix the Kuttenberg astronomical clock, but were ultimately unsuccessful. After Shkoda died, Standa left Kuttenberg and found work as a smith for the mines in Horschan. One day, he injured himself and was forced out of his position as smith and began working as a regular miner.

He worked that job until Henry came looking for him. With Henry's encouragement, he returned to the forge in Kuttenberg and apologised to Shkoda's widow, Magdalena, for having left her all those years ago.

Standa was able to help Henry finally complete the dream of fixing the astronomical clock.

In time, he and Magdalena grew close and began a romantic relationship together.

## Stanya

Stanya is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Stanya worked as an alemaid in the Hole in the Wall tavern. One night, she was attacked when she was coming home from the baths, where she would regularly deliver wine or beer for the girls working there. Although she managed to escape her attacker, she was traumatized from the experience and decided to run away from Kuttenberg. Since she knew one of the charcoal burners, Barton, she went to hide in the charcoal burners' camp with his help.

When Henry of Skalitz found her there during the investigation of the murders of young women in the city, she was still too scared to return to Kuttenberg. After answering Henry's questions about her attacker, she asked him to let her know when the murderer is caught so that she could finally sleep in peace and possibly even return to the city.

## Stephen Crow

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Stephen Crow is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Crow was a corporal under Ditrich Katz in the service of Sigismund. He was considered to be Katz's right-hand man and de facto second in command of the Praguer troops in the Kuttenberg region.

When Henry needed to enlist into those ranks to do reconnaissance regarding the transport of their cannon, he sought out Crow for enlistment. Crow eventually allowed him to enlist.

Crow may have been a soldier of decent rank, but he was also secretly a supporter of Wenceslas and was operating within the troops as a spy. One night, he attempted to break into the storeroom where the cannon and gunpowder was being held and was spotted by the commander of the Cumans, Chertan. An altercation ensued, and Crow stabbed Chertan, heavily injuring him.

When Chertan was brought to the infirmary, Crow poisoned the wine when the healer, Musa of Mali, left the room to gather supplies. Musa then gave the poisoned wine to Chertan, killing him.

Following the murder, Henry was given orders to investigate. Crow then may have been held accountable and killed or else let off.

If he lived, Crow later joined Zizka's forces, fighting against the Praguers in the ambush meant to capture the cannon.

After the fight he can be persuaded into helping you once more during Dancing with the Devil.

- The Lion's Den

## Steward Zdenyek

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Steward Zdenyek (Czech: Šafář Zdík) is a minor character in the Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Zdenyek worked as a steward of the monastic granges by the Sedletz Monastery. In an attempt to make money to pay his debts, he started watering down the monastery wine that was kept in the cellars. Additionally, he can be overheard unsuccessfully asking one of the hired hands for a loan, mentioning his fear of getting beaten up or worse if he fails to pay up.

However, Zdenyek's wine-watering scheme was discovered by one of the women working at the grange, Blazhena, who caught him in the act one night. To ensure that nobody would believe Blazhena in case she decided to rat him out, Zdenyek started spreading rumors about her stealing to plant seeds of doubt in her coworkers. Despite his efforts, none of the people working in the granges seemed to trust his claims, with Blazhena's friend Valerie fiercely defending Blazhena's reputation when Henry questioned her.

## Stop Licking That!

Stop Licking That! is a hidden achievement introduced in Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Description

You tasted flour… from the hair of a dead person.

## Acquisition

The Stop Licking That! achievement can be earned during the quest To Dust You Shan't Return, specifically during the objective "Inspect the recovered bodies." For this objective, you need to sneak into a barn where the bodies are kept.

When examining the younger body, select the following options:

- Examine the head.

- Inspect the hair.

- Taste it.

## Trivia

- The achievement, particularly its technical name, is likely a reference to a scene in Baldur's Gate 3, where the player character has the option to taste rotting spider meat, prompting Gale Dekarios to yell: "Stop licking the damn thing!"

## Storm

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Storm is the 12th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

I'm back at Trosky and back in the dungeon. But this time without Sir Hans, who's been taken God knows where by von Bergow. We have to escape, but first we have to find out what von Bergow is up to.

## Synopsis

In the bowels of Trosky Castle, Henry and Zizka are strung up in the middle of torture. Godwin, though also present, is seated on the floor. Istvan Toth interrogates them, alongside Executioner Ernest and Scribe Erazim, thus far unsuccessfully. Henry regains consciousness and Toth continues interrogating Zizka, saying Henry will get his soon. What Toth wants to know most is the location of Jobst and Liechtenstein and what they were doing in Rattay, something Zizka refuses to tell him.

When attention turns to Henry, he is equally reticent, though he may antagonise Toth and threaten Erik. Each new question sent his way is met with much of the same, silence, jokes, or misinformation. He may also break under pressure and hand over the relevant information. Eventually, if Henry stays silent, Toth tells Ernest to continue torturing Henry with no care as to whether he survived and Godwin cracks, telling him that Jobst is in Brandenburg, looking for allies against Sigismund while Liechtenstein is in Kuttenberg. With the information he needed, Toth leaves the prisoners for the night, asking Scribe Erazim to find Erik, so that Erik can send word to von Bergow of what they’ve learnt so far.

The trio are left alone, Henry feeling like they’ve betrayed their allies despite Zizka insisting anyone would have broken. Sounds are heard from the other side of the door, cheering from the guards happy for something to drink followed by struggling and the turning of a key before the door opens to reveal Katherine, just having killed the guards outside.

She and Zizka banter as she lets him down, confirming they really do know each other well. She asks after their well-being, and they all confirm they’re at least well enough to be out of real danger. Katherine wants to lead them to a secret passageway under Trosky that will take them out into Apollonia, allowing them to escape undetected. The only drawback is it requires a key, one that is kept in possession of the lord of the castle, currently Toth who will most likely be in his chambers at the top of the Crone.

Thankfully, the castle is mostly empty with many of its inhabitants having left with von Bergow. Those who remain are indoors due to an oncoming storm. Henry volunteers to take care of Toth and get the keys while Godwin initially protests his going alone, he concedes and agrees to search the Maiden for the orders from Sigismund.

Katherine tends to Zizka’s wounds and Godwin prays over the dead guards as Henry prepares to head up into the castle. In the courtyard, Henry watches as Toth bids farewell to Erik, sending him off with an embrace and a message for von Bergow. Lightning flashes and the storm begins.

Henry makes his way up the tower in pursuit of Toth. He finds him at the top, staring out of the window into the storm. Toth laughs, praising Henry for his tenacity, saying it reminds him of himself. Henry is offended by the comparison and Toth admits it has its limits, Henry is much more lenient than he is, something that comes back to bite him.

Henry may talk with Toth before ending things or else take him out in a duel or without regard for honour. Should they talk, Henry learns about many aspects of Toth’s life including - his past with Erik, having taken him in following a raid in Moravia where he was orphaned, his reason for following Sigismund, having lost his own family in a raid and saving Sigismund’s life during the battle of Nicopolis, and more of his reasons for thinking he and Henry are alike.

Regardless of how Henry approaches dealing with Toth, he wins, running him through and pushing him out the window. Henry watches as Toth falls down the side of the tower before picking up his true prize – Radzig’s sword.

He then heads up to check Toth’s chambers for the orders, finding only the key to the castle and the group’s belongings. He heads back to check in with Godwin in the Maiden and finds him trying to no avail to get into von Bergow’s chambers. With the keys, the door opens with no problem, allowing Henry and Godwin to search for the orders. Once the orders are found, it’s time to make a break for it.

Back down in the dungeons, Katherine is able to unlock the passageway and everyone makes their escape. Although no one is familiar with the tunnel, Katherine expects it shouldn’t be too long; some men are waiting for them on the other side at an old poachers camp.

At the other end, everyone is glad to be back above-ground, but it soon becomes apparent that their departure has not gone unnoticed. All the available guards of Trosky are out searching the area for them. Zizka is in no state to go much further, and asks to read the orders from Sigismund before making any next steps. The orders are for all the king’s allies to mass in Kuttenberg, a sign he is losing patience and ready to take decisive action in Bohemia. A friend of Zizka’s, on Hynek of Kunstadt is staying at Suchdol fortress, near Kuttenberg, and so he and their other allies in the area need to be warned.

In order to do so, the four have to make it there first. Henry volunteers to go get the men from the nearby camp and come back with horses so they can travel out. The man he’s meant to meet, Mika, is being held captive by a patrolling guard who suspects he may have something to do with the escapees. Henry deals with the guard and frees him, letting him know the situation. The wagon and horses are further out; the men minding it will only wait until daybreak, though the guards aren’t likely to give up before then, so they have to be brought into the loop on the situation.

All allies are able to reconvene, Zizka is laid on the wagon, and Henry, Katherine, and Godwin head out towards Kuttenberg. Along the way, Godwin leaves the group to report back to Radzig and Hanush. As a token of farewell, Godwin gives Henry a ring of his and tells him if he ever needs help he can show that ring to Oderin of Raborsch.

Henry falls asleep on his horse, exhausted from the ordeal of the last few days, and dreams of his father Martin asking how he feels about finally having achieved his revenge. As he gets closer, however, he notices it’s actually Toth himself doing the asking. He rushes to attack and finds himself pushed out the window of the Crone, waking after having fallen from his horse.

## Walkthrough

Henry and his allies are captured by von Bergow’s army and dragged to the dungeons beneath Trosky Castle, where Istvan Toth begins interrogating him, Godwin Oderin and Jan Zizka.

No matter what Henry says—or refuses to say—the outcome is the same. If you stay silent through the questioning, Godwin eventually gives in, revealing key information to protect Henry’s life. He gives up details about Jobst of Moravia and Liechtenstein, including where they went and why they met with Radzig Kobyla.

If Henry succeeds in resisting the interrogation, you will avoid a debuff which makes the stealth and combat sections later much easier, and can later say that he never cracked. There's no major impact, but it's a small moral victory.

After the interrogation, Henry is unexpectedly rescued by Katherine, a spy loyal to Zizka. She tells him there's a secret passage out of the castle, but it’s sealed behind a locked gate. You will need to retrieve the key from the Crone Tower. There, you’ll also come face-to-face with Istvan and possibly uncover a letter with Sigismund’s orders.

You can loot the body of Guardsman Kroupa nearby to claim a Military sword and some armour. However, disguises won’t work as everyone here knows who Henry is. Note: armour and a weapon are not necessary to complete the quest, but may make some sections easier.

You can go up to the kitchen to find a strong Marigold decoction on the table by the stairs. You will need your health up for later.

The next section plays out as stealth, but it’s optional. There are only a few guards patrolling. You can sneak around, throw rocks to distract them, or take them out with stealth takedowns, or choose the direct route and fight your way through.

### Search for the orders in the scribe’s chambers

Sneak upstairs and move across the battlements above the courtyard, as the courtyard is conveniently blocked off from the ground. A cutscene will trigger, showing Istvan sending Erik to Kuttenburg. Afterward, continue across the battlements and enter the Crone Tower.

Go up the stairs onto the next floor. You’ll spot two guards sitting at a table. You can sneak around them and head further up, as long as you're quiet, they won’t notice you, or simply rush them and kill them.

At the top, enter the scribe’s chamber and search all containers inside:

- The desk

- The shelf next to the door

- The two chests by the bed

- The shelf near the fireplace

The letter with Sigismund’s orders won’t be found, but your objective will update upon searching everything.

### Kill Istvan

From the scribe’s chamber, head up two more floors (one floor above the alchemy bench). A cutscene will trigger as you come face-to-face with Istvan Toth.

You’ll have a choice, confront him honourably in a duel, or dispose of him dishonourably.

Before choosing how to deal with Istvan, Henry can engage him in dialogue, uncovering more about his motivations and past.

Henry can ask:

- His relationship with Erik – Istvan reveals a close bond with Erik, showing genuine concern. If Henry threatens Erik’s life, Istvan begs Henry not to harm him, asking that Henry take revenge on him alone. If threatening Erik fails, Istvan will automatically initiate combat.

- Why he thinks they’re alike – Istvan explains they were both made orphans by war. Henry, however, pushes back, saying he fights to end the war, while Istvan profits from it.

- Why Istvan joined Zizka – Istvan admits he once believed in Zizka’s cause but now sees him as weak and unwilling to do what’s necessary. He regrets not seizing control of the group when he had the chance. Istvan denounces Wenceslas, claiming Sigismund is the stronger, more capable king. He accuses Radzig of using Henry in a political game and says Henry is blind to it.

-
Honourable Duel

-
Dishonourable Kill

Henry challenges Istvan Toth to an honourable duel. Henry starts wounded and low on health from earlier torture (if the skill checks failed). The fight can be extremely difficult. Istvan, though unarmoured, can take hits and will attempt to disarm Henry during the duel. Note, if Henry agrees to the honourable duel while unarmed, Istvan will give him a Common longsword to use (the one hanging on the wall which can be looted after the fight).

To succeed, you must parry and riposte perfectly, and make use of any potions brewed beforehand (such as Chamomile Brew) at the nearby alchemy bench, or the marigold decoction found in the kithcen.

After disarming Istvan, Henry will impale him and then push him out the window to his death.

Henry then reclaims Radzig's sword.

A quicker and easier route as it skips the fight entirely, though morally questionable. Would Henry really stoop that low?

If Henry chooses the dishonourable route, he will stab Istvan in the gut with a dagger and throw him out the castle window, his body plummeting down the mountain below.

Henry then reclaims Radzig's sword, ending their long-standing conflict in brutal, dishonourable fashion.

### Get back your confiscated items

From where you kill Istvan, head upstairs to the top floor of the tower and search Istvan’s room. In the chest at the foot of the green bed, you’ll recover all your gear along with the castle keys. Make sure to also loot the other chests in the room—this completes all three objectives for this section.

If Henry was tortured during interrogation, you'll have a reduced strength debuff, limiting your carry capacity. This can lead to overencumbrance, forcing Henry to move slowly. Additionally, your horse won’t spawn, and the storage chest in the courtyard is inaccessible, meaning the only way to keep your gear is to carry everything until the quest ends.

### Search for King Sigismund’s orders

Search for King Sigismund’s orders in von Bergow’s chambers located in the Maiden Tower, where the quest originally began. His chambers are one floor above the Knight’s Hall. You’ll find Father Godwin waiting outside the door.

Once inside, search all chests, shelves, and containers until you find the orders and the quest objective updates. Since you're likely overencumbered from recovering your gear earlier, you might as well loot everything useful before moving on. Then, follow Godwin to continue the escape.

Note: a unique dagger, Ockham's Razor, can be found on a table in the room adjacent to the room where you find the orders.

### Talk to Godwin about leaving

Godwin will head into the corridor—speak to him to continue. You’ll only have one dialogue choice here, so pick whichever fits your Henry.

Follow him down into the passage beneath the jail. In the tunnels below, you’ll regroup with Zizka, Katherine, and Godwin. You can briefly talk about killing Istvan—the dialogue options are mostly flavour, so choose whichever one you like.

### Accompany Zizka, Katherine and Godwin

Walk through the tunnels—just keep heading straight until you reach the end, then turn right. If you’re unsure of the path, you can let the others lead; they’ll show the way. And if you get separated, just follow their markers on your compass to catch up. A cutscene will trigger once you reach the exit.

### Meet Mika in the abandoned camp

Head to the waypoint south of where you exit the passageway. You can stick to the path above the road to avoid detection. Watch out for enemies with torches—they’re searching for you.

At the camp, there’s one guard standing near Mika. The easiest method is to toss a rock to distract the guard, then sneak behind and untie Mika. You can also talk to Mika—the guard will eventually walk away on his own. Alternatively, you can stealth kill the guard, or just fight him if you’re spotted.

After freeing Mika, he’ll tell you to find the wagon for your escape.

Go south to the double rock with the broken cart

Follow the path south toward the next waypoint. Guards are still searching, so try to avoid detection. Wearing dark-coloured, low-visibility clothing helps. Adjust your gear to lower your visibility as much as possible. Stick to trees and bushes for cover when enemies get close.

Go uphill between the rocks

When you reach the destination, the objective will update. Head uphill between the rocks to continue.

### Continue south until the edge of Apollonia

Continue forward to the next waypoint, where you’ll enter a search area. Walk through it until a cutscene triggers, ending the quest.

This marks the end of the Trosky region storyline and the beginning of the Kuttenberg arc. You’ll unlock the New Horizons achievement for reaching Kuttenberg. You can still fast travel back to Trosky later using caravans.

## Striped Tonies

Striped Tonies is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is available after completing Yackers 'n' Fash.

## Description

The Striped Tonies invited me to a traditional procession with a ceremonial minder’s standard. The consecration of the miners’ banners always precedes the famous shooting competition of the Kuttenberg miners. A nice leisurely stroll. What could happen?

## Walkthrough

Talk to Foreman Vlach at the Black Horse tavern in the evening to start the quest. From the time you speak to him the quest will become timed. You’ll have to head to the Hoprink Church the next morning.

If you head by the church too early, there will be a prompt to wait for Anton and Franzi – they will arrive around 8am. Talk to them and they’ll explain how the day will go. You’ll go from church to church and get the standard consecrated at each one, ending with Anton's taking of the pitman's oath to bless him for the upcoming shoot.

Anton and Franzi will begin the procession, follow them and chat along the way. Upon arriving at the first stop, the priest will be nowhere in sight. Talk to Anton and for the achievement Under a Brown Flag, agree to hang the braies up in the All Saints Tavern. Note that the whole tavern will count as a private space for this section.

Head upstairs at the tavern, to your right at the top of the stairs, through the next room then to your right again to find a ladder against the wall which will take you up to where the pole is. The tavern is busy and full of guests and workers alike, make sure to buff your stealth if need be. Once the braies are hung, return to Franzi outside to continue.

Anton will be ready to head to the next stop so start following the pair again. They’ll want to stop at the Black Horse for a drink and won’t be convinced otherwise, since it’s on the way. Before you can get there though, you’ll be stopped by a group of All Saints looking for a brawl. Chances are the guards will be flagged, so you’ll have to deal with them first if you aren’t fast enough in scarpering after the brawl. Anton will run to the Black Horse, so head there to continue.

It turns out Anton has forgotten it’s also his girlfriend Tess's birthday. To right this wrong, you’ll have to source a couple of gifts for her on Anton’s behalf – roses and perfume.

The roses can be found in the east end of Kuttenberg, across from the fisherman, inside a locked garden. To get in you can either pick the hard lock to the southern door or else climb in using some barrels on the north side from the adjoining property. You won’t be alone in the garden, there is a guard dog and a sleeping gardener. The roses will be near the gardener, so buff stealth if necessary. Once you have them, you can leave the garden to the south climbing over some more barrels.

The perfume you'll have to get from Tess's friend, Else. She can be found in the workshop at the cobbler’s behind the shop front. To get the perfume from her you’ll have to pass one of the available skill checks. The first is a hard alchemy check, the next two are hard speech and hard charisma checks.

With the gifts, head back to the Black Horse to find that Anton has overdone it on the drink and can’t stay vertical. With no other options, Henry will offer to carry Anton to the church. Pick Anton up and follow Franzi to St. George.

Anton is declared inept and you’ll have to say the oath for him. He’ll tell you each line and you’ll have to repeat it in a more formal manner. The selections are timed, select the following:

- We swear before God, that we will open the shafts without malice and mine the vein honestly according to the law of God.

- We vow to work hard, listen to the foreman and duly hand over the ore.

- We swear to not mine silver on the feast day and give a few groschen to the church.

Once you take the oath, Tobias will bless you, ending the quest and starting the task Popinjay Shoot.

## Suchdol

Suchdol is a fortress located at westernmost part of the map, northwest of Wysoka.

## Codex entry

The Gothic fortress probably originated in the 13th century, commissioned by one of the Kuttenberg patricians. It had a square layout with the corners facing the cardinal points and was surrounded by walls, a moat and a rampart. From the northeast, the entrance to the fortress was secured by a bridge and a double gate protected by the main tower.

Inside the fortress, a single-story palace ran adjacent to the wall, with a smaller tower and a single-story outbuilding.

Today, a castle stands on this site, which retains only parts of the perimeter masonry, part of the gate portal and the stone seats on the ground floor of the former tower, as a reminder of the fortress.

## Survivor

Survivor is a hidden achievement introduced in Mysteria Ecclesiae.

## Description

You listened to all of Brother Vojta's jokes… and survived.

## Acquisition

The Survivor achievement can only be earned during the Anamnesis quest, specifically during the objective "Search the hidden room in the cellar."

For this objective, you must get into a locked room in the cellar, where you will meet Monk Vojtiech. Listen to all of his jokes to unlock the achievement.

## Tips

- You must keep choosing "Tell me another joke" until Vojta has no more jokes to tell.

- The achievement will not unlock immediately, but only after you finish the conversation with him.

## Svatya Thrush

Svatya Thrush (Czech: Sváťa Drozd) is a guard in Troskowitz in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Svatya was the son of the town's bailiff and older brother to Agnes. He was also best friends with Vitek, though he also occasionally hung out with Vuytek.

Svatya became involved in a verbal altercation with Sir Hans Capon, following the noble's disgraced entrance in Troskowitz, which quickly escalated into a brawl. Henry intervened to defend him, but they themselves outnumbered. The fight was broken up by the town guard and Henry and Capon were deemed responsible and sentenced to a public pillory punishment, while Svatya and his allies faced no repercussions.

Svatya bore no ill will from the incident, referring to it as "water under the bridge," and acknowledged Henry’s bravery in fighting despite the odds.

After his sister's wedding, Svatya rebuffed any attempt Henry might have made to apologise for the altercation, instead saying he found it amusing and a great way to end the event.

### Associated quests

- Laboratores

- Wedding Crashers

## Sword of Sir Valentine

Sword of Sir Valentine is a melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a shortsword.

Note: Sword of Sir Valentine can be crafted.

## Description

A perfectly authentic replica of the sword with which the knight Valentine once accompanied the Abbot of Sedletz to the Holy Land.

## Crafting

Main article: Sketch - Sword of Sir Valentine

- Coin sword pommel × 1

## Tachov

Tachov is a small village in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex entry

A small village 1.5 km north of Troskowitz, first mentioned in sources in 1388. A nameless stream flows through it, emptying into the Krčák pond, forming cascades along the way and a waterfall about 10 metres high.

Today, the village is part of a protected area and the 'Golden Trail of the Bohemian Paradise' passes through it.

## Amenities

- Lodgings

- Storage chest

- Blacksmith

- Sharpening wheel

- Tavern

- Dice table

- Grocer

- Herb garden

- Smokehouse 2x

- Drying rack 2x

## Residents

- Blacksmith Radovan

- Dice Player Jenovefa

- Drunkard Maresh

- Henik

- Herdsboy Alshik

- Hired hand Zdenyek the Mouth

- Innkeeper Prochek

- Innkeeper Voyka

- Manka

- Radovan's wife Milena

## Tachov waterfall

Nice… And peaceful. A perfect place for a little nap.

—Henry's comment

Tachov waterfall is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The waterfall is located at the edge of a forested area south of Tachov. It can be reached by following a narrow path that branches off the main road, leading through woodland.

The falls mark the point where a stream cascades over a rocky ledge into a shallow pool below. At the foot of the waterfall stands a small pier, where villagers are often seen washing laundry.

A trail leads to the top of the waterfall, where signs of a recent visit can be found. A bedroll lies near a picnic basket, with empty bottles of Schnapps scattered about. Inside the basket is the Scholarship skill book, Basics of Philosophy.

## Loot

- Basics of Philosophy

- Apple × 3

- Bacon × 3

- Bread

- Onion × 2

- Schnapps

- Groschen × 12

- Soap

## Tailor Bartoshek

Tailor Bartoshek (Czech: Krejčí Bartošek) is a craftsman who owns the Troskowitz tailor's shop.

As one gets closer to attending the wedding, he can also be asked if your current outfit will work and he'll give advice on what to fix or if it's good.

## Biography

Bartoshek lives and works in the village of Troskowitz.

According to merchant Jürg Thömel, Bartoshek - along with the apothecary Emmerich and the scribe Gaibl - often studies some Latin tractcs (although Thömel doesn't believe any of them, apart from Gaibl, can actually read Latin).

Bartoshek dyes his own fabrics, a technique which he is happy to tell Henry all about during the Mice quest - if Henry listens to all he has to say, Bartoshek will give him the Bull paint for free. He also seems to have an understanding for pranks as he only laughs about Henry's plan to paint Old Olbram's bull and promises not to spoil his fun.

He made the wedding clothes for Olda Semine (but not for Agnes Thrush, although he mentions he would have liked that). At the wedding itself, Bartoshek fights Groom Ballatay during the swordfighting competition. In the late stages of the wedding (after the ceremony, when Henry is looking for the newlyweds to congratulate them), Bartoshek can be found drunk and lying on the ground near the fire.

### Associated quests

- Wedding Crashers

- Mice

- A Sinful Soul

## Taking French Leave

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Taking French Leave is the 18th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins immediately following the conclusion of Via Argentum.

## Description

I've managed to uncover the crimes of Mint Master Vavak, fulfilling my side of the agreement with Sir Kunzlin Ruthard. For that he promised to help me get to Maleshov, where Sir Hans Capon is imprisoned.

## Walkthrough

### Kuttenberg phase

Go back to the Ruthard Palace and speak with Ruthard himself. After that, Vavak walks back into the courtyard to confront you.

Note: If you accepted Christian of Pisek's deal during Via Argentum, choose the dialogue option about stealing silver and not the one about the secret mint. Also don't mention Christian in the dialogue choice after that. After a lot of research I can conclude that this specifically is how you keep Christian's secret so he wont attack you during Oratores later on.

If you succeed any check, he's willing to settle the matter peacefully. Failure triggers combat. Whether it's due to the silver of your tongue or the steel of your sword, you're holding Vavak by his jewels. Ruthard is happy about that and informs you that Rosa will explain the secret passage to the Maleshov fortress to you, and provide two maps: the Map of Maleshov tower and the Maleshov fort map. Offering to pick up the book for Rosa triggers the task Rosa's Book wherein the successful retrieval and return of the book are one of the conditions for romancing Rosa. The book is a unique item available only during this quest.

Rosa instructs you to go to a wayside shrine, from which you see the remains of a church. Through a window, you catch a glimpse of ruins, in which there's a cross, with its top pointing in the direction of another cross, which similarly to the first one points to the correct direction of the final destination, a suspiciously flat area overlooking the spring.

### Countryside phase

Talk with Hashtal in order to persuade him to lend you horses for a quick getaway. There are likely no consequences in telling him or refusing to tell him about the location of the secret passage. Follow the directions given by Rosa: return from Hashtal's onto the main road, turn right, and walk towards some boulders. Notice a window behind those boulders, press your interact button or crouch to look through it and see the ruins on the other side of the small valley. There's a stash of some hunting gear at the ruins. On their front side and to the left from the POV of the window, you'll find a white cross on the ground with its tip pointing down towards the spring. Follow it and find the next cross somewhat next to the spring, which will again point you with its tip in the direction of the correct spot. This is a good place to change into your dirty clothes if looks matter to you, because your items will get muddy during the dig. Mutt will automatically be dismissed for the remainder of this quest. Walk through the tunnel.

### Maleshov phase

Emerging out of the tunnel and walking up, you trigger a cutscene where you overhear von Bergow, von Aulitz, and Erik. Quickfinger is very useful here.

Hans Capon is in the tower in the middle of the courtyard. All the locks on your way should be possible to lockpick at this point, but if not, walk into the kitchen on the far side of the courtyard, and pickpocket or knock out the cook to take her keys. In the highest room of the tallest tower you'll find Hans - be especially careful right at the entrance to the tower,taking the right, and waiting for the two guards to sit down at the main room. You don't have to knock them out, simply avoid them. They will be asleep on your way out.

On the next floor, in the room with Lady Ofka, is Rosa's red book on the windowsill with the seat. The book is labelled as Book of Anecdotes. You can knock the woman out, sneak behind her by walking on the bed, or talk to her. If speaking to her, you'll have to pass a hard charisma or medium intimidation check to prevent her from alerting the guards. Attempting to bribe her will not work.

You can ask her about Hans's whereabouts and she can tell you where to find keys if you are unable to pick hard locks. In the room with her are also a couple of swords you can grab to give to Hans and Brabant.

Walk up the stairs and either unlock the doors, or lockpick them to trigger a cutscene where you reunite with Hans. During the dialogue, taking any other option than "We'll manage it together" locks you out of later romancing Hans.

### Getting out

Hans insists on not walking through the tunnel. That leaves you three options:

- knock him out and sneak with Brabant towards the tunnel entrance at the back of the tower

- fight your way out - don't forget to give Brabant and Hans swords. If they die, it's a game over.

- knock out/kill every guard that could catch you, walk to the stables, and light a torch there to signal that the way is clear.

If combat ensues, Hans and Brabant will help you, but you will get a game over if either dies. Whichever option you take, you get a timeskip to the three of you on horseback in the forest. The options you choose in the discussion are just flavor text and have no bearing on your reputation with the other two men. After a while, a cutscene plays where you meet back with Radzig, Hanush and Godwin. No matter what dialogue options you choose here, you are tasked with spying on the council meeting in Kuttenberg and the quest The King's Gambit starts.

## Tales of Kuttenberg

Tales of Kuttenberg is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You helped Rosa finish her book.

## Acquisition

The main quest Taking French Leave, tasks Henry with rescuing Sir Hans Capon from Maleshov, which is now owned by Otto von Bergow and occupied by his troops. Before leaving Ruthard's Palace in Kuttenberg, Henry must speak with Rosa, Kunzlin Ruthard's daughter, to learn about a secret entrance into the fortress.

During this conversation, if Henry expresses willingness to help, Rosa will request that he retrieve a book for her, initiating the side quest Rosa's Book.

The book is located in the central tower of the fortress, one floor below where Sir Hans is held captive. It is a distinctive red and gold-bound volume resting on the window seat in Lady Ofka's quarters. Although Lady Ofka may be present, Henry can quietly knock her out to avoid raising an alarm and safely obtain the book.

Afterward, return to Rosa and agree to help her finish the book when prompted. Completing this task unlocks the achievement.

## Tips

- You'll have no other chances to complete Rosa's Book quest, as access to Maleshov is limited to this single opportunity during the main quest Taking French Leave.

## Tankard

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Tankard (Czech: Pivec) was a soldier in the service of Hanush of Leipa.

He, alongside Oats, Konrad, Nicholas, and Henry of Skalitz, was assigned to accompany Hans Capon in delivering a message from loyalist lords to Otto von Bergow.

## Involvement

Tankard rode out of Rattay as part of Hans Capon's escort. A troublemaker and gambler who was handy with a bow, he appears to have been an old friend of Konrad, even though that did not stop him from cheating when they played together. The two ended up in a spat with some locals at the last tavern where the group stopped, after Tankard, drunk and having squandered all his coin, tried his luck with the innkeeper's daughter.

He was not especially optimistic about the mission, noting that even he and Konrad could not agree on who would take the night watch, so what hope was there for the nobles.

During their stay at the Rocktower Pond campsite, he set up a dice table he had found in a nearby crevice and was pestering Konrad to play with him. Henry can wager with him for the silver ring that Tankard had won off Oats the previous day. If Henry lost, he would have had to pay for everything Tankard ordered in the next tavern.

After the letter had been delivered, Tankard hoped Capon would allow the men some free time before returning to Rattay. He had planned to go with Konrad to the Troskowitz tavern to fleece the locals, but he was killed along with the rest of Capon's men in the bandit ambush.

## Taras Mura

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Taras Mura is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Taras Mura is a knight who once committed grave misdeeds and later sought absolution from Father Martin at Old Kutna in the Kuttenberg region several years ago. He swore a contractual oath to guard a rumored entrance to hell within an abandoned mine west of the settlement. He filled the tunnels with crosses and served as a bulwark against demonic forces, cleansing himself of sin, until his death or when relieved by another knight. Prolonged isolation in the dark mines affected his mental well-being, though he could be reasoned with.

Although Father Martin promised the locals that they would provide ongoing food and water, he kept the terms of the arrangement secret. He did not tell the villagers about Taras Mura or the true purpose of sending provisions into the mines, causing speculation. After Father Martin's death, only Taras Mura knew about the contract. The locals, who believed their offerings placated devils, eventually stopped delivering supplies, triggering Taras Mura to lash out by killing their cattle.

Taras Mura can be freed from his oath if the player explains the situation to Father Marian and Vladimir after reading the Knight's contract and convincing him to exit the mine. Taras escorts the pair to Old Kutna, where he mounts a horse. He travels slowly along an irregular route to just east of Grund, then steers north-northwest and walks off the map. His journey takes approximately 30 minutes.

## Associated quest

- The Mouth of Hell

## Target on a tree

Target on a tree is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Near the crossroads between Troskowitz and Tachov, a small wooded area opens where two narrow paths converge at a large tree surrounded by a ring of lepiota mushrooms. Someone fastened a target to the trunk, and a straw dummy stands nearby, both riddled with arrows, indicating the spot once served as a makeshift archery range. A sitting log rests close to the tree, with a basket filled with the same mushrooms placed beside it.

Behind the tree, a bow leans against the trunk near a small stash of supplies. Inside the sack is the Marksmanship skill book, Aim and Fire! I.

## Teeth in the Bag

Teeth in the Bag is an activity in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. Henry can start the quest by speaking to Innkeeper Mole at The Hole in the Wall tavern in Hoprink, Kuttenberg.

## Description

In the worst dive in Kuttenberg, they host fighting matches. It's not exactly high-quality entertainment, but I could earn some extra money there.

## Walkthrough

After accepting the quest, walk to the barn next to The Hole in the Wall and challenge Beggar Damian to a fight. Damian isn't a particularly difficult opponent, just bash him and you should win quickly.

After that, challenge Drunkard Zavish who should be standing just outside the ring. You'll need to get him drunk before he'll agree to fight - 2 of any kind of alcoholic beverage should do the trick. If you pass a hard drinking check, he will pay you 5 for the booze. Zavish is a significantly tougher opponent than Damian - he's able to use unarmed master strikes and will throw combos at you, so play defensively.

Once he's beaten, it's time to challenge Goliath. Fight him the same as you did Zavish, focusing on feints and your own combos to avoid his master strikes. Once Goliath is defeated, return to Innkeeper Mole for your reward. After talking to him, the quest is complete.

## The Blacksmith's Son

The Blacksmith's Son is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It's given by Radovan if he's sought out for assistance to gain access to the wedding and acts as the blacksmithing tutorial in the game.

## Description

The Tachov blacksmith could use the help of an experienced hand. This kind of work would certainly pay off.

## Synopsis

Henry arrives at the village of Tachov, as directed by Betty, and speaks to the blacksmith there, Radovan to see if there is any way he can help Henry get into the wedding. Radovan wants to test Henry’s mettle before making any promises – blacksmithing isn’t for everyone, after all.

Radovan is intrigued by Henry’s upbringing, since he has been commissioned to forge a sword for Young Semine as a wedding present. He asks Henry to forge a hunting sword for him and if he does a decent enough job on that, Radovan will let him help with the wedding sword.

Henry’s skills impress Radovan, earning him a blacksmith’s respect and more importantly, a job and a bed.

## Walkthrough

This quest serves as the blacksmithing tutorial. Radovan will give you all the supplies you need, so just pick up the supplies from his chest and get smithing. The chest can be found to your left, at the edge of his house inside the forge area.

Follow his instructions to forge and the quest will end with some new lodgings.

## The Collector

The Collector is a missable task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It becomes available during the main quest The Devil's Pack. The task can be started either before or after meeting Matthew the Collector.

## Description

A hefty reward has been offered for Matthew the “Collector”… Should I bring him to justice or leave him be?

## Walkthrough

There are two ways to learn about the bounty on Matthew the Collector.

### Before meeting Matthew

Talk to the Miskowitz bailiff and ask him about Matthew the Collector. If you want to get Janosh out the honourable way, you will have to treat Loyza before leaving to look for Matthew. The bailiff will tell you to look for him on the road between Miskowitz and Suchdol and that there is a bounty on him, if you can return the book he stole from Sedletz Monastery.

### After meeting Matthew

If you have already encountered Matthew, you can still start the task. Talk to the innkeeper Zdeslav and ask him what is going on around the area. One of the dialogue options concerns Matthew the Collector and the fact that the bailiff in Miskowitz is looking for him.

After learning this, go to Bailiff Crux and explain that you have already met the Collector. You can then hand over the book you obtained from Matthew, whether you acquired it through the peaceful encounter or took it after killing him.

### Finding Matthew

Matthew can be found on the road to Suchdol, as promised. It is possible to claim his bounty and keep him alive, but it will require convincing him to give you the book (or stealing it from him).

If you ride past him without stopping quickly enough, he will initiate combat. You will notice a scene of carnage just before where he is waiting near the woods with him men, which will give you time to approach on foot.

### Resolving the encounter peacefully

It is possible to obtain the book and claim the bounty without killing Matthew. To avoid a fight, you can either pay his requested “duties” of 1,000 groschen or pass a persuasion check.

The available dialogue options are:

- “The Devil will have his revenge!” (Hard)

- “Did you know there’s a bounty on your head?” (Medium)

- “I’m not giving you anything!”

If you convince Matthew not to attack, he will offer to teach you skills and tell you where his group is camped. You can then try to obtain the book from him, either by convincing him to hand it over or by stealing it.

If you cannot obtain the book peacefully, you will have to fight Matthew and his men to recover it.

### Returning the book

Once you have the book, return to Bailiff Crux in Miskowitz and hand it over to complete the task. This also works if you met Matthew before learning about the bounty, provided you obtained the book.

If you spared Matthew, you can conceal the fact that he is still alive when speaking to the bailiff. The bailiff will accept the book and pay the promised reward.
