## The Devil's Pack

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Devil's Pack is the 15th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

We freed the Dry Devil. Now he needs me to get his old band back together.

## Synopsis

Now that the Dry Devil is freed, it’s time to bring his band back together. They’ll use the Devil's Den as an aptly named homebase, and make use of its reputation to hire passers-by for dirty work. Henry is tasked with finding those who survived their botched job and seeing if they would return to the fold now that their leader is free again. Among those whom Kubyenka knows survived include Adder, Janosh Uher, Bohuta, Matthew, and Ranyek.

Kubyenka is only certain of where to find Bohuta, and maybe Matthew, but he’s willing to take some guesses. Bohuta, following the loss of his brother Slavek, fled to the rectory in Grund to find comfort in a life of prayer. Kubyenka isn’t confident he’ll be able to be swayed, but it’s worth a try, since the Devil is back. Matthew meanwhile is set up robbing on the roads in the guise of a tax collector. The last Kubyenka heard, he was on the roads near Miskowitz, so Henry can start by asking the Bailiff for more details.

Kubyenka isn’t sure where to find the other three, but he offers Henry some information on them. Adder, so called because he can’t keep his snake in his pants, will no doubt be nearby Janosh as the two are all but inseparable, so if Henry can find one he’s likely to find the other. Janosh, for his part, is the band’s cook. Ranyek is a master archer with a distinctive bow that he won playing dice. Unfortunately for him, that was the only time luck at dice went his way even though he is an avid gambler. Kubyenka suggests asking around where dice is played, as he’s likely to be near a table.

Bohuta, it turns out, is not willing to come back no matter what. He feels his brother’s death was a wake up call and wants to do everything in his power to avoid eternal damnation if he can. He does, however, have some information regarding Ranyek. A few days prior, he told Bohuta he had a game arranged in Pschitoky. Before he lets Henry go, Bohuta wants to pray over the Devil. He leads Henry to his brother’s grave and explains to Henry that he found clemency from the priest and swore on his brother’s grave never to harm another again. His heart is in the right place, but his knowledge of prayers is somewhat lacking; he is only able to deliver an approximate version of the prayer he attempts.

Henry may go along with his earnest attempt at prayer or else correct or insult him. When insulted, Bohuta is quick to bring out his fists, after which he blames Henry for being cut from the same cloth as the Devil. Either way, he is stalwart in his decision to stay away from his former band.

With Bohuta’s hint, Henry heads to Pschitoky. The innkeeper there tells him that Ranyek had been there the day before with a Pole causing all sorts of trouble. Ranyek, it seems, left for Bylany with some men who paid his gambling debts while Adder made off with the local butcher’s wife, Eva.

Eva tells Henry that, although she swears it was nothing, her husband thinks something untoward happened between her and Adder and thus has decided to deal with Adder in his own way, by hanging him from a large tree nearby. Henry rushes to Adder’s aid and finds the locals attempting to kill him by tying him to a noose and seating him on a cow. Henry may talk down the locals or fights them, freeing Adder.

Adder is impressed by Henry’s show, though Henry does not understand most of what he says. Adder is happy to hear the Devil made it out and he wants to know how Janosh is, having left him. Henry explains and Adder heads for the Devil’s Den.

In Bylany, Henry comes across the dice players who were seen with Ranyek. They greet him warmly, speaking fondly of Ranyek and anyone associated with him. Unfortunately, Ranyek died after trying to escape from his debts by crawling out the wrong end of the latrines. With that sad ending, Ranyek won’t be coming back to the Devil.

In Miskowitz, Henry finds none other than Janosh in the pillory having been put there following a botched robbery that lead to him badly injuring a resident of the village. Henry is able to free him through noble or ignoble means and he’s just as happy as Adder to rejoin the Devil.

The Bailiff there also mentions to Henry that Matthew has been causing a great disturbance on the road to Suchdol through his fraudulent customs collections. Henry heads that way and finds Matthew. Matthew is tired of working for others, having found a much better gig robbing travelling merchants. Henry may then deal with him peacefully or forcefully. Either way, Matthew is not keen on returning to the Devil and cannot be convinced.

With every lead tracked down, Henry returns to the Devil’s Den to update said Devil on how he fared. The Devil is quite happy to have two of his members back, insisting they party to celebrate. The group banter and joke with each other before drinking themselves into oblivion, toasting to Henry for his efforts in bringing them all back together.

In the morning, hungover and tired, Henry talks to him again to get the low-down on what is expected next.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Kubyenka, and he’ll tell you some details about where to start looking for the missing members of Dry Devil’s band, be sure to exhaust all options. You can follow them in any order, they will only have minor effects on each other. Here, they will be listed in order of how close they are to the Devil’s Den.

### Find Bohuta

Head to Grund and find Bohuta near the church during the day or at the rectory in the evening. Talk to him and he’ll refuse to return to the fold. He will, however, give you a lead that Ranyek was in Pschitoky a few days ago.

Bohuta will ask you to join him in praying for the Devil’s soul over his brother's grave. On the way to the grave, he’ll ask you about your background a bit and Henry will respond automatically. He asks what Henry thinks of the Devil and you can respond however you wish.

He will go into a botched version of the Lord’s Prayer and you can either go along with it or correct him. Correcting him requires a hard scholarship check and will lose reputation with him while going along with it will gain reputation and a treasure map. Note that failing or insulting him will offend him and cause him to attack you unarmed.

Regardless, he will still refuse to return, so it’s off to the inn near Pschitoky.

### Find Adder

Talk to the innkeeper at Pschitoky and he will narrow down the search for you, directing you to the butcher’s wife, Eva. Talk to her, and she’ll direct you to a tree from which her husband wants to hang Adder. Note: if you exhaust dialogue options with Eva you will learn her husband hit her, which can be used in the next portion as a Might persuasion option. Head over there as quickly as you can and interrupt the attempted execution.

Pass a skill check to resolve things peacefully. If you did not find out from Eva that her husband hit here, there will be a medium speech, one hard intimidation, and a medium charisma check. Each check will fail save for the charisma check which you will need at least 10 to pass:

- He belongs to the Lord of Suchdol.

Once the vigilantes are dealt with, cut Adder down, untie him, and talk to him. If the townspeople are alive, he will ask you for a sword and if you give him one, he will use it to kill the butcher. He will also give you a hint for where to find Janosh if you haven’t already, Miskowitz.

### Find Ranyek

Head to the inn at Pschitoky and talk to Innkeeper Wolfram Raus. Tell him you’re looking for Ranyek and he’ll tell you Ranyek was there the day before with some Pole drinking and dicing and carrying on. If you haven’t found him, ask after Adder and Ranyek and the innkeeper will give you a lead for each of them.

Adder: talk to the butcher’s wife in Pschitoky.
Ranyek: head to Bylany.

In Bylany, talk to the dice players there. Pass a medium speech check and they will tell you what happened to Ranyek, namely that he literally drowned in shit while trying to escape his debts. If you cannot pass that check or miss it, they will lead you to the cesspit and force you to either pay Ranyek’s debt of 700 groschen or else retrieve him and his bow from the pit as payment.

Either way, head into the waste and find Ranyek, if you settled things with the dicers through the earlier speech check or paying back the debt, then you can keep Ranyek’s bow without trouble. Otherwise, you will have to hand it over or else deal with the dicers through force or by running away until they lose you.

### Find Janosh

In Miskowitz, you’ll find Janosh in the pillory for having gravely injured a resident called Loyza. There are many ways to free him. Note: once you talk to the bailiff regarding why Janosh is being held, the quest becomes timed and will fail after a few in-game days.

The quickest way, is simply to pick the lock on the pillory or steal the key from the guard or Bailiff and set him free at night.

The honourable way, involves helping the townspeople. Talk to the Bailiff and he’ll let you know that Loyza is in danger. You can treat him with a medium craftsmanship and medium alchemy skill check. You’ll have to give him a bandage and either a Marigold Decoction (Jahosh really fucked him up) or a Buck's Blood Potion (Jahosh broke his ribs with that strike). Once he’s been mended, the Bailiff will let you buy Janosh’s freedom for 500 groschen, though you may be able to haggle for slightly less.

Free Janosh and he will thank you and run off to rejoin the Devil.

### Find Matthew

Talking to the Miskowitz Bailiff about Matthew will start the task The Collector.

Matthew can be found on the road to Suchdol. You may be able to deal with him peacefully, if you are able to do so he will become a skill trainer; however, if you’d like to complete his attached task, then you’ll want to take him on. It is possible to claim his bounty and keep him alive, but it will require convincing him to give you the book.

If you ride past him without stopping quickly enough, he will initiate combat. You will notice a scene of carnage just before where he is waiting near the woods with him men, which will give you time to approach on foot.

To resolve things peacefully, you can either pay the requested ‘duties’ of 1000 groschen or else pass a persuasion check:

- The Devil will have his revenge! (Hard)

- Did you know there’s a bounty on your head? (Medium)

- I’m not giving you anything!

If you are able to convince him not to attack, Matthew will offer to teach you skills and tell you where they are camped.

If you want his bounty and you cannot convince him to give you the book, then you’ll have to take him on. Be prepared, as he has a fair number of men under his command.

### Talk to Dry Devil

Once every avenue has been exhausted, you’ll be prompted to return the Devil’s Den and talk to the Devil himself. Once you do he’ll insist you all drink to celebrate being reunited. There are a couple drinking checks here, but nothing that affects more than reputation. In the morning, you’ll realise you still never really talked to Dry Devil, so you’ll have to go talk to him again for real this time.

Depending on the order you have done the quests up to this point, the conversation will be slightly different. Either way simply talk to him to end the quest.

## The Dirty Seven

The Dirty Seven is a hidden, main story related achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You found all of Dry Devil's comrades-in-arms.

## Acquisition

Complete the The Devil's Pack main quest. The Dirty Seven achievement is tied directly to the quest's conclusion and therefore cannot be missed.

## Tips

- When you arrive in the Kuttenberg region, one of your first tasks will be to rescue a man known as the Dry Devil. This occurs during the main quest, The Devil's Pack. As part of the quest, you'll need to track down the Devil's former companions: Matthew the Collector, Bohuta, Ranyek, Janosh, and Adder. Once all five have been located, return to the Dry Devil. Completing this objective will unlock the achievement.

## Trivia

- The achievement title is a nod to the 1967 war film The Dirty Dozen, which follows a ragtag group of convicts recruited for a dangerous mission during World War II. It has become iconic for its portrayal of morally grey, outcast soldiers forced to work together.

- It may also reference the 1972 Italian war film The Dirty Seven, directed by Bruno Fontana. While lesser-known, it shares similar themes.

- The achievement icon is based on the Seven of Swords tarot card, which traditionally symbolizes deception, trickery, and operating outside the rules.

## The Executioner's Pride

The Executioner's Pride is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It can be tipped by Innkeeper Mole at The Hole.

## Description

Heinz, Kuttenberg’s executioner, has been down on his luck lately and wants to break the curse by having a new executioner’s sword made using various lucky charms. Naturally, I am to find them all and then forge the blade.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Executioner Heinz outside the walls in Kuttenberg and he will ask you to forge a sword to recover his luck since an execution in Rattay went terribly for him not too long ago and he's lost his confidence. He’ll want you to gather some talismans to craft a lucky sword.

### Hanged man’s noose

You’ll find a hanged man’s noose just outside Sedletz Monastery. When you get there, someone will already be trying to loot the body. You can fight him or else convince him to leave and loot the noose from the dead man.

### Ghostly horseshoe

A ghost horse has been spotted in the Burnt down forest west of Kuttenberg. The horse will appear after midnight, simply follow it through the night until it will bring you to its dead master. At this point, you can interact with the horse to take its shoe.

You can also saddle the horse and make it your own, if you are interested.

### Bezoar

In-game, bezoars are crafting materials used for blacksmithing. It is possible you may have already acquired one by this point. If not, you can purchase one from the apothecary in Kuttenberg.

### Hare pelt

A Hare pelt can be obtained in many ways. Enemies will often have one and they can often be found in chests as well when stealing.

You can also purchase one from a butcher in Kuttenberg.

### Forge the sword

Once you have all the materials, you’ll need to use them to forge the lucky sword. You can use any anvil, just head to the closest one and forge away.

Make sure the materials are all from your inventory - you can still craft the sword if the pelt and the bezoar are in your chest, but the crafted sword will disappear.

Head back to Heinz to get your reward and end the quest. He will suggest cutting you using the sword for more luck, which you can accept or deny.

## The Feast

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Feast is the 20th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins automatically at the conclusion of The King's Gambit.

## Description

After difficult but successful negotiations, Jobst and the Rattay lords left Raborsch. Those who remained in the stronghold began to celebrate the new alliance and the hope of a better future without Sigismund.

## Walkthrough

The quest begins immediately following The King's Gambit, dropping you back in the feet of Godwin deep in your cups.

If you’d like to celebrate before moving on to Liechtenstein, you’ll find Brabant, Dry Devil, and Botschek of Kunstadt marked on the map. Brabant is immediately to your left, talking with Samuel. The other two are both down in the courtyard. Play Dry Devil at dice and if you don’t wager for money he’ll wager a carrot, though you’ll still have to put up 20 groschen. Botschek is in the corner, talking to Anna of Waldstein. You can also find many conversations to observe and a dice table set up in the yard, where you can play.

Once satisfied, talk to Liechtenstein in the same room you started in. He wants to toast, but there’s no good wine except what Oderin has hidden away. The wine is in the cellar below the kitchen. You can ask Maid Elishka for a hint of where to find the wine, but she won’t be able to help you and will direct you to her mother, Cook Madeleine. Godwin remembers her from her childhood and can reminisce a bit before asking after the wine. Once you find the wine, you’ll have to pick either the red or white, it won’t make a difference which you choose.

As you walk up the stairs with the wine, a cutscene will start, leading into battle.

Note: For the achievement Die Another Day, make sure you stay close to Christopher Oderin and keep him alive for the remainder of the quest, he should be right near the bottom of the stairs.

Once most of the enemies are dealt with you’ll switch back to Henry.

As Henry, ride into Raborsch and help out in the fight. You’ll start the quest in your waiter outfit, so be sure to change back into armour before approaching. Following the fight, feel free to take your time and loot as much as you please before talking to Jehuda and Liechtenstein. Once you agree to go, the quest will end and start on the next, Exodus.

## The Fifth Commandment

The Fifth Commandment is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. You can talk to Katherine after completing Into the Underworld to receive the quest.

## Description

Katherine needs help with a murder investigation. She’s afraid her cover has been blown and someone has started killing her contacts.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Katherine at the Hangman's Halter Tavern to learn that an informant of hers named Alice has been brutally murdered, and she wants Henry to investigate. The first step is to examine the body and talk to the gravedigger to find out more. You’ll find both at the church in the north end of Kuttenberg.

### Start the Investigation

Gravedigger Frantishek, with an easy speech or medium charisma check, will tell you Alice was not the first woman to be murdered in the way she was and probably won’t be the last. A man, Lumir, was investigating other similar cases. He can also tell you that the scene of the crime was near the Hole and a friend of Alice’s, Barbora, has been mourning her. The body is nearby in the morgue. Once you talk to Frantishek, the aforementioned Barbora should be there as well.

Examine the body to note her wounds. She was torn open, most likely by a sword, both her breasts were cut off. Although her face was not gravely injured, she was strangled and her hair was hacked like her body.

Barbora will tell you that she and Alice worked together in the same house, that Alice had a rich suitor whose name she promised not to tell, and that Lumir appears to be a bit of a drunk.

Lumir should be nearby, though do note that being able to talk to him will remove the need for you to check out the crime scene. If you’d like to do that, go there first, though there isn't much to find. Lumir’s too hungover to talk so you’ll have to provide him with more booze or a Hair o' the Dog potion. Hair o' the dog is the best option, if you have one on you, you can also run and get one from an apothecary or make one if need be.

Once Lumir is sobered up, you’ll need to pass a hard presence, very hard persuasion, or hard scholarship check to get him to agree to tell you more. He’ll tell you all the victims were brunettes and killed in the same manner as Alice. There are two missing girls that Lumir believes to have been killed but not yet found.

Exhaust his dialogue to learn about the victims and where to continue the investigation. The first two victims have no one left who can help shed light on their situations, so you’ll be looking into the remaining three – Stanya, Zdena, and Jarka.

### Investigate the Previous Victims

Jarka’s information is closest, as you can find Father Prokop at the graveyard church during the day. Jarka served the von Grolle family. A hard speech and easy intimidation check will reveal she was pregnant. Father Prokop believes a man called William must have gotten her pregnant and killed her. A hard scholarship or very hard domination check will reveal that Father Prokop hates Lumir because Lumir accused him of the murder.

The other two leads both start from the Hole. Talk to the innkeeper, Mole, and ask after Stanya. He’ll give you some initial information for 10 – Stanya’s room was ransacked and the only trace were bloody footprints. After this, Mole will want more money either pay 50 or pass an easy speech check to convince him to give you more information for free. It turns out Stanya was also friendly with the bard, William, and a charcoal burner called Barton.

Since you’re at the Hole, talk to Strnad about Zdena as well. To get information out of him either fight him or pass a hard charisma check then pay 30 for the honour. With the charisma check, he mistakes you for a lord she robbed, but either way he’ll tell you she had some unfinished business with a man called Pint at Rabstein Mill. He will also mention Father Prokop having come to see her once and that she was also hanging around the bard William.

Head down to the charcoal burners’ camp south of Kuttenberg to follow Stanya’s thread. Barton doesn’t wear a hat so he should stand out from his peers. Pass a hard speech or charisma check to find out that Stanya is alive and hiding out in a cottage at the camp, traumatised from her attack. If you fail the skill checks with Barton, you can lockpick (easy) the door of the hut where he is hiding Stanya (south part of the camp, eastern hut). Talk to her and she’ll tell you her whole story. She was attacked one night and barely escaped, the ransacking of her room was her own doing in her haste to gather her things. She ran immediately to the charcoal burners where she’s been hiding ever since. Although not many rich people frequent her former place of employment, she does mention that young von Grolle used to go there sometimes and that he was friendly with her, but gave most of his attention to a ‘thieving wench’ instead. When his servant tried to shoo the thief away, von Grolle stopped bringing him.

Eventually, when you ask what she remembers about the attacker, she’ll mention he swore in German. With a medium Persuasion check you can persuade her to keep trying to remember, she heard someone talking in a side street before she was grabbed, two voices conversing, the man’s grip around her neck was also quite strong most likely a miner or a swordsman. When it comes to suspects however, unlike the other people so far questioned, she doesn’t believe William could have done it. As you leave, she’ll ask you to let her know when you’ve caught the killer.

Next is Zdena, head west south-west to Rabstein mill. Talk to Pint and he’ll tell you she had a hideout nearby and in her last haul was a signet ring she insisted on keeping as a luck token. The last time they spoke she told him she thought someone was following her on horseback. He’ll direct you to a back road she wanted to take to avoid being followed.

You can request he give you her scarf which can be used by Mutt to track. You can follow his directions or use the dog, but there is a waypoint as well to the east. Once there, it will open up into a search radius. At the ford itself, you’ll find the basket Pint mentioned with Zdena’s silver in it. There is a trail of blood leading down the road south then into the woods. Soon, you’ll find a fallen log and next to it, Zdena.

Examine her body. She’s not been as heavily mutilated as the others, but her head has been smashed in. There are signs someone was searching her for something and her right hand has been broken. The signet ring she stole was inside of her though it’s unclear by whose doing.

Go back to Kuttenberg and finally question William. He can generally be found at the Black Horse tavern near the fountain. Pass a hard coercion or easy intimidation check to get him to talk. Interrogate him and he will insist he had nothing to do with any of the murders, but he will mention that Zdena had her eyes on von Grolle.

### Investigate the Suspect

With all the information you can get, go back to Lumir. First, he’ll send for Katherine since she came asking around just as you did. Then you’ll get to trying to put things together. Katherine thinks it was Prokop, Lumir thinks it was William. It is possible to end the quest here by reporting either one to the bailiff (he will refuse to arrest Prokop), There’s one other person who connects all the victims – von Grolle. Jarka served the von Grolle family, Stanya was flirting with Hendl von Grolle, and Zdena was robbing him. When asked who you think did it, reply it was one of the von Grolles.

Suspicions aren’t enough, you’ll need to search the von Grolle house to look for evidence. Katherine and Lumir will suggest a couple of ways you might be let into the house without having to sneak around. The patriarch of the family is invalid and needs a healer while the son wants to learn sword fighting.

Enter as a Healer

Approach the house during the day and speak to the servant outside, Thaddeus. Pass an easy survival, easy alchemy, or medium scholarship check to pass yourself off as a healer. Alternatively, if you have the Thunderstone in your inventory you can offer that as well.

He’ll suggest you speak to the lady of the house, Mandelina, to learn more about old von Grolle’s situation. She’ll tell you about his symptoms and his general state and that you can find him upstairs, in bed. With a hard speech check, she’ll confirm her husband slept around and she’s willing to do anything to keep her son from doing the same.

Examine Gotzlin von Grolle with an easy survival, medium scholarship, and hard speech check. If you exhausted dialogue with Mandelina, you can also examine his stool. In the kitchen on the same floor, speak to the cook and ask what he eats.

In the end, what he needs is a Digestion potion, Painkiller brew, and pass a very hard speech check to offer some comfort. If you have the thunderstone you can also pass a hard speech check to leave it with him, but you will lose it forever.

Talk to Mandelina again and she’ll give you 225 for your trouble.

Discreetly duck into Hendl’s room, just in front of the stairs. His room is considered a red trespassing area, so be careful. With Mandelina sitting right in front of the stairs, you’ll have to use a bit of stealth. Inside, check the hard locked chest by his bed to find locks of hair from various girls.

Enter as a Trainer

Approach the house during the day and speak to the servant outside, Thaddeus. If you have already completed Ars Dimicatoria, you’ll have a special option here that will allow you right in using Menhard’s name.

Thaddeus will direct you to the courtyard where you’ll find Hendl. Speak to him and he’ll mention how his mother has been on him about going out too much and trying to keep him from seeing girls. He’ll immediately segue into wanting to test your skills, lending you a wooden sword and starting a duel.

He’s not very difficult to beat, and once you do he’ll be agreeable. You can ask him questions about weapons and the like and he’ll mention a hunting sword that belonged to his father has disappeared but otherwise doesn’t have anything enlightening to say.

Tell him to practise some sword forms and this will keep him busy for a while, allowing you to sneak back into the house. Head to his room upstairs right across from the stairs discreetly. His mother sits at the top of the stairs and his room is considered a trespassing area, so it may still require some stealth. Inside, you’ll find hidden in a hard locked chest by his bed locks of hair from various girls.

### Return to Lumir

With the evidence in-hand, leave the house and go see Lumir. Katherine will volunteer to pretend to have been knocked up by von Grolle to set a trap. It turns out, the killer is actually Mandelina and Thaddeus working together to get rid of any woman involved with Hendl, without his knowledge.

You’ll immediately be in combat with Thaddeus, take him out and then talk to him. He’ll explain the motive and you’ll have the choice to spare or kill him.

Head downstairs and Katherne will be holding Mandelina at knife-point. You can question her further to get the full story if you’d like. You’ll have the choice to support Lumir in handing her over to the bailiff or Katherine in killing her then and there.

You’ll head over with Katherine to recap with Lumir, he'll reward you with a Kuttenberg knight shield and 150 , ending the quest.

## Objectives

If entering as a trainer:

Main

## Trivia

- The name of the quest is inspired by the Ten Commandments contained in Exodus, a part of the Torah and the Bible. Depending on who you ask, the fifth is either Thou shalt not kill, or Honour thy father and thy mother.

- The game files have the quest under the working Czech name Kuba Páralů, literally Jack (the) Ripper.

## The Finger of God

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Finger of God is the 11th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Following an exhausting day full of twists and new alliances, a peaceful evening has arisen. Zizka is recovering from his injuries and his band is about to leave the estate of Sir Otto von Bergow in the morning.

## Synopsis

Having helped Zizka with his eye, Godwin and the others leave the tower. Michael meets them and informs everyone they’ll be moving out in the morning before von Bergow has time to retaliate. He gives Henry a few tasks he could do to keep busy but otherwise only asks that everyone go to bed early, refrain from fighting, and that Hans keep his grubby hands off of Klara.

Before they do anything else though, Godwin wants to lay the dead to rest. Hans begs off this duty, citing his head injury, but Henry is eager to help. On the way there, Godwin asks Henry why von Bergow didn’t join the attack. All Henry knows is that von Bergow was expecting an important visitor from Prague – something Godwin assumes must be unrelated.

Henry digs graves and buries the men while Godwin prays for them. Henry wants to sleep, but Godwin says he has something that’ll wake him back up and insists he come see at the moat before heading to bed.

Henry goes to see Godwin as promised. It turns out Godwin wants to show him handgonnes, the deadly arms that Zizka’s band used during the ambush in the ravine. Henry and Godwin give them a whirl, shooting at targets for a while before Henry is given his own pistole, one its previous owner no longer has need of.

At this point Henry may help various inhabitants around the fortress, carrying sacs, finding horseshoes, mending armour and weapons. When he walks through the gate, Hans calls to him asking him to come watch the sunset; Henry may accept and Hans will reflect on the long day they’ve had and his own rotten luck so far before asking Henry to play dice.

Klara is arguing with the guards outside the dungeons; she wants to tend to their wounds, but the guards don’t believe they should be helped. Henry may intervene and help her tend to the two prisoners – Hermann Littlehead and Black Bartosch. Henry may speak with them and they’ll be surprised to see him not only well but free. Bartosch holds no grudge and wishes Henry the best, though he is disappointed they find themselves on opposite sides. Klara also asks Henry for help with three wounded men which he may also provide, diagnosing and treating their ailments. Klara may then ask to spend the night with Henry, seeking comfort.

During the night, Henry has a nightmare featuring Markvart von Aulitz and the following morning, he is woken by the sounds of battle preparation – von Bergow is already here! It turns out, his important visitor was none other than von Aulitz and he has brought the force of the Prague militia with him along with Istvan Toth, Erik, and Jaromier Nebak. Toth opens a parley, but the talk goes nowhere, neither side is willing to give up, so an attack begins.

Zizka’s band fend of the Praguers for a while but are eventually overpowered, those who are able seeking refuge in the tower. Here, they should be able to hold out for longer until the Prague forces are worn down and more willing to negotiate. However, von Bergow has an ace up his sleeve – the Finger of God – a cannon. With one blast, the tower is demolished, Michael is killed in the blast and Zizka, Godwin, Hans, and Henry are taken captive.

Bergow takes Hans with him and splits from the group, wanting to keep him as a useful hostage, while the others are left in Toth’s care to be brought back to Trosky Castle and interrogated for information concerning their allies.

## Walkthrough

When the quest starts, you will be playing as Henry again. Immediately after Godwin helps with Zizka's injured eye, Michael will be informed about the captain's status. He'll then recommend everyone refrain from fighting and to get a good night's sleep as they'll be leaving first thing in the morning before Otto von Bergow retaliates.

Note that time does not progress during this section.

### Helping Godwin

While Michael will note you can help Bluster out with loading carts, Godwin will pull you away to assist him first with burying the dead. Follow him out past the paddocks as you discuss the situation a bit. You'll then reach three bodies that need to be buried. Dig the three marked out graves and drop a body in each one, making sure to interact with each grave to then bury them. Talk to Godwin afterwards, where you can ask him about other things as well, before letting him know you've finished the task. He'll then have you follow him back towards the fortress to introduce you to a new weapon with Hertel: the pistole. After a quick rundown of what it is, you'll then get to practice shooting with it at the nearby targets before you're given your own and 10 Lead ball to start with.

### Try to get new allies (Optional)

You can now explore Nebakov and complete side tasks to gain allies, or simply go to sleep. These allies can help defend the battlements or gate in the upcoming battle, making things easier. Completing Klara’s task also unlocks her romance scene and a skill buff.

Load supplies on the cart (Optional)

At the stables you find a cart. Talk to Hired Hand Bluster there. If you ignore him or fail the skill check he will start fistfighting you. Then pick up the 5 sacks next to him and load them onto the wagon behind him. He then thanks you and you say “Agree”. This makes him an ally.

Find Horseshoes for Peltzel (Optional)

Talk to Groom Peltzel at the stables near the archery range, just across from Bluster and the cart. He asks for 3 horseshoes, and also talks about the ravine raid and how he almost shot Henry. He also reveals that Steer, their blacksmith died at the raid and his brother Bull is not a good replacement.

You’ll need to forge them yourself at the blacksmith or already have some. Each horseshoe requires 1 iron, which you can find in the barrel in the left corner of the forge (the same one used for the blacksmith's sword task). Interact with the Anvil and select horseshoes. Forging all three takes about 10–15 minutes.

Bring the finished horseshoes to Peltzel. He’ll reward you with 55 Groschen, 1 Cockerel potion, and 8 Lead Balls (rifle ammo).

Play dice with Hans (Optional)

As soon as you head back into the fortress for the first time, Hans will call out for you to join him above the gate. Talk to him a bit, where you can gain some reputation for saying he did what he could. He'll then ask if you want to play dice against him. Nothing is really gained reward wise here (other than the 50 groschen he'll give you if you answer "Some money wouldn't hurt" when asked if you have anything to bet), though you get to talk and joke with him a bit afterwards.

Help Bull in the Forge (Optional)

Talk to blacksmith Journeyman Bull. Pass the skill check or he’ll try to fistfight you. If you had previously met his brother during Back in the Saddle Henry can mention it. Afterward, he’ll ask you to sharpen some weapons.

Loot the barrel in the corner to get three damaged weapons: a Common longsword, Military sword, and Bearded axe. Use the Sharpening Wheel to repair each one to 100% (look for the full heart icon). Henry will make a comment once each is fully sharpened.

Return to Bull and select “I repaired the weapons”. He won’t accept them unless they’re fully sharpened.

As a reward, he gives you 24 arrows and 8 scatter shot projectiles. While at the forge, you might as well make 3 Horseshoes for the next task.

### Help Klara

Klara will be arguing with some guards outside the prison—she wants to treat a few captives who were injured. Intervene to learn that one of the prisoners is Hermann Littlehead. If you choose to help, push for them to receive treatment and you’ll be given a medium speech check. Any successful option will work, though Klara will be irritated if you suggest treating the wounds yourself.

If successful, the guards will let you in, and you can follow Klara inside to find both Hermann and Black Bartosch.

Note: This interaction is missable. If Henry doesn’t witness Klara’s argument with the guards, the scene won’t trigger and the guards will eventually go to bed and Klara will go back to her shack. However, you can still visit the jail on your own and speak with the prisoners.

Make sure to also talk to Klara further to see how you can further assist and she'll point you to 3 others that also need assistance. You can also ask what you should and shouldn't do based on one's injuries, which you should pay attention to as the game will not remove incorrect choices later.

Regarding the captives, you can talk to them for a short bit, but will then be put on the spot to either lie about how you got out or reveal the truth that you joined Zizka's group (the latter will cause some reputation loss). You can then also inform them you got the guards to agree to let Klara treat their wounds, which will gain some reputation.

To treat the three men, you'll need to have on hand some needed items and be able to pass the required skill checks. For the items, grab the Schnapps from in the kitchen (on the shelf there), then go into Klara's hut and loot the chest in the loft for all items here. You can also loot additional items from the table inside the hut (like more potions and bandages).

Mark

Mark is awake, but notes he only has a headache and is just tired, which should be a warning flag as he likely has a concussion. Examine him completely and if successful, you should see the right option: clean his wounds but he cannot fall asleep. At this point then, do the following:

- Clean the wound (preferably with Schnapps)

- Dress the wound

- Give him a Painkiller brew (like the Weak Painkiller version that was in the chest)

Do not give him alcohol to drink, as he needs to stay awake.

Kozliek

Kozliek will only appear if Henry didn't kill him during Fortuna. He is unconscious, so you can't ask him anything, but you can still examine him. Examine everything you can and make the suggestion about a potion. If you succeed, Henry will note he has a fever and that the wound needs to be cleaned, cauterized, and bandaged. In this case, you'll then need to:

- (Optional) Clean his wound (preferably with Schnapps or moonshine, but water does in a pinch)

- Cauterise the wound with a gunpowder (a lead ball)

- Change his bandage

- Give him a potion for the fever - like the Weak Aqua Vitalis that you can grab on the table near Klara Fever tonicum is best, but if you don't have one, a Marigold decoction or Painkiller brew should also work)

Zwerk

Zwerk is downstairs, lying on a cot. He's got some wounds and a swollen ankle, but otherwise no serious injuries. For him:

- Clean his wound (preferably with Schnapps)

- Sew up his wounds (requires the Tailor's kit)

- Dress his wounds

- Rub Chamomile decoction or Buck's Blood on his ankle

If you want, you can also provide him something to drink, but you'll need to provide him four alcoholic drinks to do so, for some reputation gain.

After they're all taken care of, let Klara know and she'll reward you with some strong potion variants and a bandage. If you were successful and wish to pursue a quick romance with her, pass the medium speech check to get a drink with her. She'll decline but instead suggests she'll meet you in bed tonight. Otherwise, you can just end the conversation after you confirm with her that you treated the patients.

### Go to Sleep in the Cabin

Note: Before sleeping, make sure to equip your best armour and weapons—a major battle is coming, and you won’t be able to change gear during combat.

Once you’ve completed all tasks and are geared up, head to the cabin marked by the red waypoint on your compass and go to sleep.

If you helped Klara treat the wounded and passed the skill check during your conversation, you'll unlock an optional romance scene where she spends the night with you. This grants the "Time Well Spent" buff, increasing Strength, Agility, and Vitality by +1 for the upcoming battle.

### Defend the castle!

Henry awakens to the sound of preparations—a siege on Nebakov is happening. On the horizon, Otto von Bergow arrives with Istvan Toth, Erik, Nebak, and Markvart von Aulitz, leading an army of the Prague Militia. They demand Jan Zizka's surrender, promising to spare his allies. Father Godwin suggests sneaking away, but Zizka refuses, saying escape would be futile. Henry, filled with resolve, declares he will no longer run from von Aulitz. Hans then shouts defiantly at the attackers: "Kiss our asses!" Zizka plans to hold the castle in the hope that the attackers eventually parlay.

Knock down the ladders!

Stay on the battlements where the attack begins and enemies will raise ladders and Henry must knock them down. There are two on the sides and two at the front. Act fast to stop enemies from climbing up. If you don't, your allies will knock the ladders down. If enemies get in they will kill some of the men.

Repel the attack on the gate

Once this objective appears, rush to the main gate. It's opposite the blacksmith, up the stairs where Capon is. Henry can fire arrows at the attackers from here. You’ll also find boulders ready to drop. Pick one up, move to the hatch above the gate, then drop it to crush enemies below.

If you managed to defend the gate, talk to Zizka in front of the gate. He tells us the lower fortress has been breached so we must head there next.

Repel the Reserve Attack!

This objective triggers only if you successfully defended the gate. If the gate was lost, it skips straight to the courtyard battle.

Climb down the ladder to the lower fortress, where your allies are engaged in heavy combat. Flank the enemies from behind for easier kills. Once cleared, a short dialogue with Jan Zizka will follow who mentions they have to go back up top quickly.

Help Godwin in the Courtyard

The battlements will eventually fall—this part is unavoidable. Head to the courtyard, where enemies will rush in. You can fight a few of them but soon a cutscene will trigger.

The allies retreat to the tower as enemies continue to swarm the castle. Jan Zizka remains confident, believing the enemy will try to parlay, knowing that taking the tower by force won't be easy. But that hope fades when the Prague soldiers suddenly fall back—and a cannon is brought forward.

As Father Godwin prays, the cannon is fired, blasting a massive hole into the tower. The impact causes a pillar to collapse on Henry, while Hans Capon cries out, pinned under debris. The battle is lost—they've failed.

In the aftermath, Henry, Capon, Godwin, and Zizka are shown imprisoned in the back of a wagon, taken away as captives. Otto von Bergow orders Istvan Toth to interrogate and torture them to uncover any plans involving Jobst of Moravia and the League of Lords. Meanwhile, von Bergow rides off to meet with Sigismund of Luxembourg, taking Capon with him as leverage in case Hanush of Leipa attempts to retaliate.

This will complete the quest and immediately begin the next, Storm.

## The German's Treasure

The German’s Treasure is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The Guild wants to show it has long arms, long enough to reach Kuttenberg innkeeper Beikovetz, who supports King Sigismund.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Rat at the Hole and ask if she has any work for you. She’ll ask you to steal everything you can get your hands on from a local innkeeper, Beikovetz, who made his money from banditry and supports Sigismund.

He runs the All Saints Tavern, near the large church on the south end of Kuttenberg. If you already completed Yackers 'n' Fash you may have a key to the cellar there, allowing you to slip down any time. If you do not have a key you can sneak in during the night so you have time to pick the lock or you can approach the cellar from the Kuttenberg Underground. Be careful, as the All Saints spend most of their time in this cellar as well. If you stay in the rooms closest to the underground entrance, with a decent stealth skill you should be fine even if one of the miners is in the adjoining room.

However you get there, in a hard locked chest near the underground entrance you’ll find a Bloodied wedding dress which Henry will remark on. Head through the doorway south-west to find a wall you can take down wherein you’ll find an Old rusty sword and two maps – Footpad’s hideout map and Old hideout map. There is a very hard locked chest in this room as well that has an Old painted statuette inside.

Once you have everything, head to the inn just west of Kuttenerg to hand over the goods.

Note: the maps you found do, in fact, lead to valuable treasure so consider reading and finding their caches. You also have the opportunity to confront Beikovetz with the things you have found, though this will only result in a reputation loss with him.

Give the innkeeper the password I’ll have a big-eyed monkey and trade for the goods. They aren’t worth much beyond the sentimental value they no doubt held for Beikovetz, but you can pass a medium speech check to sell them, ending the quest.

Note: You can haggle for maximum value by first purchasing anything you find useful from the innkeeper (to increase their total groschen), and then you can sell them the goods

## The Heirloom

The Heirloom is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

In a forest near Bylany, there’s a family of refugees who escaped the destruction of Mesoles living in an abandoned hut. The head of the household, a tailor named Mikush, did not return from Bylany, where he works. I’ll set out to look for him.

## Walkthrough

Speak to Svatava Mikush to start the quest. She and her daughter, Mikush's Vendula can be found at the Huntsman's lodge point of interest along the river west of Bylany. Her husband, Mikush went to Bylany and hasn’t returned and she would like you to look for him. Her best lead is that you should ask around the tavern in town.

### Ask around Bylany

At the dice tables you’ll find Chernik, he has some information but will only divulge it over a game of dice – or a hard speech or medium intimidation check. If you completed The Master's Game - Special Badge this won't be needed.

After a night of dice, Mikush left the tavern with a man called Drat who Chernik mentions may be involved with bandits. Drat will be nearby, just north if the tavern. Hard speech, medium intimidation, medium charisma to get him to speak. He didn’t do anything but a friend of his, Hanka, also from Mesoles was upset upon finding out another person survived the razing.

To get more information, hard speech checks will keep coming revealing Hanka and Mikush quarrelled over an inheritance and Hanka asked Drat to arrange a meeting between them. Drat took Mikush to a crossroads near Mesoles and ran off as Hanka and the bandits took him away.

### Find Mikush

Go to the crossroads Drat described, it’s the area south-west of Bylany that makes an X on the map. Once there, it will expand into a search radius. Head west along the road until you find some blood to inspect. Follow the trail off the road, south into the woods. A few steps in you should find Mikush's cap. Keep following the tracks south-west and you’ll see some tents in the forest – the bandits’ camp.

There’s no negotiating here, so run in and kill the two bandits standing over Mikush. To treat him, you’ll need to pass a medium craftsmanship, medium alchemy, and medium survival check. Clean the wound with alcohol, preferably Schnapps (there is one near the campfire), then treat it with herbs, preferably Feverfew (there is a patch nearby behind the camp to the west), then give him a potion, preferably a Strong Marigold decoction or Aqua Vitalis, then last but not least bandage the wound. You can also pray if you like following a medium scholarship check.

Mikush told Hanka that the only person who knows where the inheritance is buried is Svatava. Hanka then took his men and headed out to the place the family has been staying.

### Get back to the cabin

Get back there on the double to confront Hanka. He is holding Vendula hostage and the next responses will be timed. Tell him to negotiate, then pass a couple of medium speech checks and he’ll let her go. Then you can confront him normally. If you learnt about him from Drat, you’ll be able to gain reputation by telling him there’s still hope for him to find a partner.

You can treat him nicely and ask that he reconcile, in which case he will leave peacefully, or you can entice him to fight. Either way, once he’s dealt with, speak to Svatava in the hut. She’ll think she hears more bandits and ask you to check the door.

### Find the heirloom

Thankfully, it’s not bandits, but Mikush returned. Once the family reunites, talk to Svatava again and she’ll ask you to find the very inheritance that caused this mess. She’ll give you directions to follow, head to the centre of Burnt Mesoles then south along the trees until you find the handcart and a dig spot. Take everything from inside and return to Svatava to end the quest.

## The Hermit

The Hermit is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

This quest is only given if you went to the blacksmith Radovan in Tachov for his help to attend the wedding. After assisting him by completing The Jaunt, he'll then bring up the sword he wants to make for the wedding, starting this quest.

## Description

The Tachov blacksmith, Radovan, has one bad character trait... Well, two actually: bragging and boozing. This time, though, his drunken bragging has put him in a tight spot. He has to forge a superb sword out of Damascus steel. Luckily, the blacksmith has a clear plan.

## Synopsis

Radovan has been commissioned to forge a sword for the upcoming wedding at Semine. In order to make a top class sword, one needs top class materials. He’s heard a story of a hermit called Ambrose living in Apollonia who had been in Andalusia fighting in a crusade. Word around town is he has a very interesting broken sword in his hut, one that could be a genuine Toledo blade which Radovan could reforge into the gift.

Other rumours surrounding him abound, he used to see travellers and now sees no one, he may have made a pact with the devil, and a demonic apparition was spotted recently in the area. It’s up to Henry to ask around the womenfolk in Troskowitz to find out more.

Betty believes the hermit really did sell his soul, how else could they explain his miraculous return to health and the apparitions in the area? Nothing has been done about it, since Bailiff Thrush has been keeping it quiet. Betty tells Henry that four strangers were by the day before and they took great interest in tales of the spirit, she says they looked like monks but were armed with daggers, another bad omen.

If Henry insists, Betty will direct him to two witnesses, Gerda and Stanislav. Stanislav claims to have seen a rider from hell and Gerda saw its destruction, a crooked conciliatory cross marking the place of death of a suicide some years ago. On the way back from gathering some roots, Gerda saw a hellish creature all in black leap up from the darkness. Unarmed, she fled in fear before he could do anything. When she turned around, she saw a shadow flying across the field towards Apollonia. Stanislav explains that he saw a black rider with glowing eyes on a black horse flying into Apollonia. At the crossroads, he turned this way and that before making off into the rocks. He seems confident in his assessment, even though surely the devil would know which way to go.

The cross marks a cache; inside are only a few papers, some groschen, a waffenrock, and a cloak. Nothing valuable was taken, so whatever the man Gerda saw was after, he wasn’t a thief. At the crossroads in Apollonia, Henry finds the black horse though its hardly devilish. Someone may have visited the hermit, but it seems unlikely now that it was truly the devil.

When confronted with the findings, the hermit initially denies all involvement, but when pressed he admits he’s not Ambrose. The real Ambrose died a few years ago and this new hermit is Konrad – a Knight of the Cross with the Red Star. Ambrose was dying when Konrad came to see him, and Konrad took his place to fulfil his dying wish – to find his hiding place beneath the conciliatory cross – and to hide from a dispute Konrad had gotten into in Prague.

Konrad agrees to tell Henry where to find Ambrose’s grave, and his sword with it, as long as Henry will fulfil the wish Konrad could not. In the village is an old widow, Margaret, Henry needs to take her a cross and tell her that Ambrose forgives her and his brother must get what is rightfully his. As it turns out, Ambrose’s brother was buried in unconsecrated ground as a victim of suicide. However, he did not actually kill himself. Margaret’s lover killed him by accident but when the brother was found in the morning, everyone assumed it was a suicide. Margaret needs Henry to rebury him properly so his soul can rest and he can, as Ambrose decreed, get what he deserves.

When Henry returns to the hut, he finds a few Knights there. They want his help, as one of theirs was shot. Konrad, they say is a fraud and a murderer who was paid off to kill the master of their order. If Henry could distract Konrad, they stand a chance at taking him.

Henry can either help them or or Konrad. If Konrad survives, he will tell Henry where the sword can be found, as promised. When pressed, he tells Henry he has proof of the master of the order’s treachery and that the whole situation is a misunderstanding – he had to kill the master of the order in self-defence – but the other brothers refuse to see the truth. If Konrad dies, Henry can read his journal which will get him the information he needs to find the sword.

Once the sword is recovered, Henry heads back to Tachov to forge it with Radovan. Radovan is shocked to hear that Ambrose was dead, initially worried Henry might have had a hand in it. Henry makes a long story short; Ambrose really was a knight and his sword really is Toledo steel. Radovan insists Henry forge the sword on his own, his father was a swordsmith after all and Radovan really only makes horseshoes and hoes.

Henry forges the sword, and Radovan is ready for the wedding.

## Walkthrough

While you can go directly to Apollonia to locate and talk to the hermit, to really get all the information and have an easier time getting details out of him, head to Troskowitz to ask around about the hermit. Eventually, the innkeeper Betty will relent and give you two names who swear they saw something: the apothecary's wife, Gerda, and a local shepherd, Stanislav. Note though that the option to talk to the villagers won't go away until you go around and ask several others, like the merchant Jurg Thomel and Bailiff Thrush.

### Investigate

Talk to Gerda, who will think you're just there to make fun of her. If you pass the speech check though (or pay her), she'll point you to the location of a cross to the west to investigate. Head out here, where you may run into some wolves. After dealing with any dangers, dig up the grave and loot it to reveal no actual valuables were taken, meaning it wasn't some common thief that Gerda saw. Make sure to grab at least the Crusader cloak, the book, and letter and read them.

For Stanislav, he's located east of the graveyard. If you pass the speech check, he'll also reveal more information, mainly how the horse and rider he saw appeared to not know exactly which way they needed to go, further confirming it's not an apparition or devil. If you also already helped out Siegfried earlier during Sheep among Wolves, Stanislav will also give a separate task involving a familiar ram, but you can complete that later.

If you're wanting to piece everything together, before going to the hermit, head over to the area marked to explore in Apollonia, where you should see an abandoned hut with a small paddock with a black horse. Investigate the horse to confirm this is likely the horse the others saw.

### Find the hermit

Now with everything in hand, go to the hermit, who's across the road, in the rocky area of Apollonia. Talk to him and after you've pointed out a few indicators you discovered, you can then directly confront him. However, he'll reveal he's not Ambrose, but rather was a friend of his. The real hermit, Ambrose, had died some time ago, but before he did he had asked that Konrad help him settle his affairs. When Konrad made it there though, Ambrose soon passed away before he could complete everything.

Konrad will then request you help with Ambrose's final wish: to deliver a cross to a widow named Margaret in Troskowitz, telling her that Ambrose forgives her but his brother must get what is rightfully his, giving the task A Sinful Soul.

After you complete the task, go back to Konrad, only to discover some knights from the Cross with the Red Star have shown up, looking to kill Konrad just as Konrad was about to run away. If you talk to Arn, he'll tell you that Konrad isn't the hermit, but a fraud and murderer, claiming that the Inquisition hired Konrad to kill their Grand Master in Prague. You can then say you don't want to get mixed up in this or help. Note that even if you agree to help, you can still side with Konrad. If you still want to side with him, agree to help Arn, but then head into the hermit's area just enough for the prompt to look at Konrad appears, who'll tell you not to move any further. Try to get answers from him and then note you're not his enemy. Some reputation is lost but he'll allow you to come closer to talk. You can then confront him with timed responses to ask where the sword is and he'll tell you and, if you want, to ask about the killings, which he'll note he had proof of the Grand Master's treachery (which lines up with the earlier letter) but the others refused to believe it.

After that, your only options are either to attack and kill Konrad, or help him fight against the three knights. If you agree to help, the knights will soon come in. Note with the tight spacing in the tunnel and all the bushes near it, this can make fighting in this area difficult unless you draw them out into the clearing or have Mutt to help provide distractions.

If you chose to attack Konrad, you'll need to look for his journal to learn roughly where the sword is instead. The journal itself is hidden upstairs, behind 3 movable sacks. Note that if you help Konrad, this journal will disappear after Konrad leaves the area so if you want to read it, you'll need to find a way to secretly steal it before he does so.

At the grave itself, the sword is planted at the head of grave. Note that while you can dig up the grave, there's nothing to loot.

You can return to Gerda and tell her what really happened at the cross to receive the skill book, On the Composition of Alchemy II.

## The Hydra's Heads

The Hydra's Heads is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

All three commanders are dead, and the powder magazine's been taken care of.

## Acquisition

During the main quest, The Lion's Den, Henry conducts reconnaissance at Sigismund's camp in the Kuttenberg region. Here, you learn that Sigismund's forces are commanded by three key figures:

- Grozav of Borumlaca, the nobleman

- Chertan, the Cuman commander

- Ditrich Katz, from the Prague artillery regiment

To unlock the achievement, you must ensure they all end up dead by the end of the quest.

## Tips

- Your objective is to eliminate all three commanders. As part of the quest, Chertan is killed during the story progression. Katz, whose trust you have earned, will then ask you to investigate the murder.

- During the investigation, you discover that the Corporal Stephen Crow is the culprit behind Chertan's poisoning. Grozav is innocent, but at the hearing, you can falsely accuse him, leading to his execution.

- After these events, while traveling with the bombard, a large explosion occurs at the camp. You then fight off guards at the ambush site. To complete the achievement, you must find and kill Katz, who rides out to escort the bombard with you.

- Once all three commanders are dead the achievement will unlock.

## The Italian Job

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Italian Job is the 25th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins immediately upon the conclusion of Oratores.

## Synopsis

We are going to steal royal silver from the Italian Court.

## Walkthrough

You’ll be in Godwin’s shoes at first. The first order of business is to walk through town and approach the Italian Court, then enter without raising suspicion.

Note: For the achievement True Cardinal, you’ll have to make specific choices in the following sections, as noted. Asking too many questions can raise suspicion, and many segments are timed, so feel free to save often.

### Stroll Through Kuttenberg

As you walk through town, some street vendors will call out to you. Talk to them and look through their goods. None are worth buying save one, the Statuette of St. Barbara, haggle to get the price down to 50 groschen. This figurine can be used later on during the council for an easier ending.

If you purchase the figurine, be sure not to mention it to anyone at the council later.

Keep walking towards the Court. At the gates you’ll be greeted by Kuttenberg city councillor, Jerome Naaz. He will recognise Henry, but not be overly suspicious. When talking to him, bow then evade. Naaz will then lead you through the Court. Avoid replying to him while walking to keep things from getting awkward.

Eventually, you’ll approach the hall where the council is being held. Here, you’ll come face to face with an Italian guard, Giuseppe Cabrini, and have to partake in a little conversation with him. If your scholarship is high enough attempt to speak Italian and reply:

- Cordial greeting in Italian.

- How is life here?

- Why did you stay here?

- How many guards are under your command?

- Say goodbye and move on.

- Come, enter the council.

Otherwise, it is better to move on without the attempt. The check is very high, so at least 25 is required.

Once you’ve spoken with him, the council will begin.

### The Council

Godwin needs to maintain a certain level of drunkenness to be able to speak Latin with ease. After the cutscene, continue formally, then state the pope has not yet reached a decision, that’s what you’re here for.

When you’re free to move around, head to the keg to your left and take a drink. Now that the council has begun in earnest, you’ll have a couple of things to balance. The most important, and necessary for the trophy, is to hear out both sides of the church dispute. When talking to them, do not ask too many questions and answer neutrally to keep up the highest reputation. The other, is to help Henry and the others down in the kitchens with their infiltration. To do this, talk to Janosh for some ideas. If he agreed to help, Christian of Pisek will be here as well to offer support.

First, talk to Janosh, he will suggest asking for more wine to thin out the guards as they’ll have to head into town to fetch some. Once wined up, talk to Naaz and make the request.

Talk to Christian and he'll suggest using the statuette to claim it was a gift from the pope, so long as you don't tell anyone you bought it on the streets of town.

Then, hear out some of the arguments. Talk to Albich of Uniczow, reply:

- I do not remember you.

- Keep quiet

- What do you think about the dispute.

- Leave

Talk to Janosh again, paying attention to your drunkenness, if it slips into the debuff or Godwin mentions being thirsty, drink some wine. His next idea is to call for the cook. Eat some of the food, then speak to Naaz again and request to see the cook.

Head back and talk to Father Anthony, next to Albich. Reply:

- What are the brotherhood’s demands?

- I understand.

- Leave

By then, the cook, Venda, should have arrived from the kitchens. Make sure you have tasted some of the food, then talk to him:

- Praise the food

- Everything

- Leave

Talk to Janosh again for another idea. He’ll suggest something with the guards but is unsure of what exactly. To call the guards, talk to the burghers, either Andrew Polner, Wenceslas Vorsucher, or Franz Rosenthal, they act as one conversation, reply:

- What is your opinion on the dispute?

- Why are the guards here?

- Leave

Then follow up with Naaz:

- Discuss the guards.

- Is there enough of them?

- Leave

Talk to Musa, reply:

- What is your opinion about this Council?

- Leave

Talk to Abbot Jan III, reply:

- What are the monastery’s demands?

- I understand.

- Leave

Then, you should be ready to make your decision as legate. Talk to Janosh and let him know you’re ready. You can choose to side with either side, but if you purchased the St. Barbara figurine and did not tell anyone about it, you can use that to force both sides to compromise. If Christian of Pisek is not there, you will not be able to use the statuette, but you can still follow the options below to find a compromise:

- Musa is right

- You need to understand each other.

- Calm down

With the speech given, you’ll head back to controlling Henry.

### Infiltrate the Italian Court

In the kitchens, review your order of attack with the others. Once the cutscene ends, you’ll be able to restore your previous outfit if you’d like by accessing the inventory.

You’ll have to take out the remaining guards to control the Court. If you did everything to help as Godwin, there will be fewer of them. Stealth is not necessary, but it is possible. Go out the door to the right of the kitchen to enter the courtyard, if you find yourself in the outer bailey, turn around. Take out the guards on the wall.

Once they’re dealt with, check on Brabant who should be crouching nearby under the same walls. His job was to secure the west gate, but he needs your help since there are two guards. Talk to him and Hans will approach as well. You can choose to take both guards out yourself or alongside Hans.

Once those last two are dealt with, talk to Hans by the well. Adder is missing, so you’ll need to look for him. You’ll find him back where you started, in the kitchens, having some fun with the cook. Her husband will come in and you can choose then to kill him or calm him down. To calm him reply:

- Calm down

- Pretend to be Italian

- Use Brabant’s phrases

- Fatta la legge, trovato l’inganno

Talk to Adder in the courtyard, then follow the others to check on the hidden passageway. Down in the cellar, interact with the wall to trigger a cutscene and the entrance of your reinforcements. You'll know it's the right one when you hear knocking from the other side. Once they arrive, you can focus on freeing the captive lords.

### Free the Lords

When the possibility presents itself, say you want to free the lords, then go with Janosh and Adder. Once free, head up the tower with the spiral staircase with the others. At the top, you’ll meet the jailer, Csaba Molnár. You can fight him or deal with him peacefully. For the peaceful option, reply:

- Skill check you are most likely to succeed at

- We beat you

- A new life awaits you!

- I understand (let him go)

Once the lords are free, all that’s left is to talk to Zizka. Doing so will trigger the end of the quest, so feel free to look around and loot before you do.

You have a key to the armoury which you can use to find good loot and there are chests and bodies to loot as well. Rosa will suggest checking out the library while Samuel can also give you some hints on where to look for loot. The armoury can be found above the kitchen, while the library is in the tower where the lords were being held. You can also loot some items from the treasury and the various minting forges that line the courtyard.

When you’re ready, talk to Zizka, and a fight will break out. You can fend off the onslaught with a polearm to keep the ladders down. After some time, you’ll move to the courtyard. Fend them off for a little while longer and eventually a cutscene will trigger.

### Return to Ruthard Palace

Once the cutscene is over, you’ll head through the tunnels back to Ruthard Palace. You can talk to Hans in the crypt if you’d like, then head out to the palace.

Another cutscene will trigger, revealing that Brabant is trying to betray you and appropriate the silver. Fight off his men, then you’ll ride off to Suchdol with the silver. In the morning, Sigismund's army will retreat, facing mutiny back in Hungary and a lack of funds due to your successful robbery, ending the quest and starting Civitas Pragensis.

## The King's Gambit

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The King's Gambit is the 19th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It begins immediately after your escape from Maleshov Fortress in the previous quest, Taking French Leave. This is a timed quest.

## Synopsis

No sooner had I reunited with Capon than another friendly encounter awaited us. However, right after that we had to split up again and go about our important tasks. I'll go to Kuttenberg to attend the City Council with King Sigismund, the others to Raborsch for a meeting of King Wenceslas' supporters.

## Walkthrough

### Kuttenberg

Once you are free to move, go to Kuttenberg. This quest is timed and Henry will remark on the approaching council if you are off doing other things. You need to speak to Vavak to get an in, you can find him in the town hall during the day, telling the guard you have an appointment will get you entry, or around town in the evenings.

He can get you in as a servant since his cook’s son, Franta, is meant to be working the event, and you may be able to convince him to let you sit in instead. You’ll need a certificate and livery.

The certificate you can get from Franta who can be found around town during the day and at the Iron Eagle in the evenings. You can steal the items from him or convince him to give it to you with a medium impression or hard charisma check, or else a bribe of 1000 groschen. Depending on your timing he may also give you the livery.

If Franta doesn’t have the livery yet, you’ll find it with tailor Schneider in the market near the fast travel point for the town hall.

Once you have everything, head to the town hall and equip the livery. Talk to the Majordomo who will be sitting inside. This will fast track you to the meeting.

Council meeting seating chart

|

Adam of Zarzitz

Peter Mailer

Jerome Naaz

Andrew Polner

Franz Rosenthal

Master Tuchmacher

Master Prokop Eldris

|
Fridusch Kumel

Master Nicholas Krondel

|
Ulrich Vavak

Master Enderlin

|

Innkeeper Havel

|
Food and wine

The king's table

Bailiff Andreas Plümel

As a waiter, you’ll have to pour wine for the councillors. Serving them incorrectly or not at all will result in a game over. There are two wines: Tokaji, the white, and Monastery, the red. Do not serve any to Adam of Zarzitz and tell him you are forbidden if he complains. Everyone will be speaking over each other, when a councillor orders he will prompt an option to look.

Plümel will call you over and ask you to get him a goblet he confiscated from a thief before anyone notices. Head up the stairs and find the stolen cup on the table then head back to hand it over.

Rosenthal will call you over next and ask you to get his gloves from the chapel and to count how many of the figures there have wings. The gloves are on a lectern, and there are 24 winged creatures. After returning his gloves and giving the correct answer, he will give you a groschen.

After some time, Sigismund will appear and the meeting will start in earnest, switching you over to Godwin.

### Raborsch

As Godwin, your first order of business is to socialise. Talk to Brabant, Rabbi Jehuda and Samuel first, the former is in the room to your left and the latter in the main room with you. After that, you’ll be talking to Liechtenstein.

He’ll then suggest you talk to Anna of Waldstein, Haman Alder, and Botschek of Kunstadt to gain their support for Jobst’s proposal.

Anna is nearby next to Jehuda and Samuel. To gain her support, you’ll have to swap out some documents from Alder’s horse. Talk to the stable master by the horses and pass a medium domination check and he’ll let you into the shed. You can also offer to play dice with him and wait for him to leave, or simply enter the shed anyway and pass a scholarship check when he protests, leading to a hilarious confession scene. Return to Anna and she’ll pledge her support.

Next is Alder himself, he can be found talking to Martin Oderin and Kunzlin Ruthard in the room with Brabant. After some awkward conversation with your father, Christopher will arrive and challenge you to a duel. Win or lose, talk to him after and he’ll offer to handle Alder for you.

Last but not least, you’ll need Botschek’s support. He can be found drinking with Zizka on on the second floor. What he wants is a marriage betrothal for his niece, Jitka. You can make suggestions but the only one he’ll accept is Capon.

Head outside and give Hanush the news, he’ll be elated in the end but forbid you from telling Hans as he wants to tell him himself. Return to Botschek to let him know things are decided and he’ll pledge his support.

With everyone’s support, return to Liechenstein. This will kick off the next phase, sending you back to Henry.

### Sigismund

After dismissing the council, Sigismund will ask you to stay and serve him wine as he talks with von Aulitz. Eventually, he will ask for the red. Keep holding it as he’ll ask for it again. The third time he asks, he’ll ask for white. He’ll then ask you to drink, answer as you wish.

After the toast, the quest will end, immediately starting The Feast.

## The Last Step

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Last Step is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 7th and final quest in the Legacy of the Forge DLC.

## Description

I'm trying to finish repairing the astronomical clock with the help of two unexpected collaborators.

## Walkthrough

After completing Old Plans, talk with Standa the Fly. He will direct you to talk to Mole the Innkeeper at The Hole in the Wall to learn more about the goldsmith's apprentice that worked on the original clock, Volf, since he will be crucial to the repair. Volf is now apparently an especially dirty vagrant and drunkard, so you'll have to go find him in the beggars' camps around Kuttenberg.

Mole will suggest you talk to Ragman who will tell you which camp specifically that Volf should be in, narrowing your search radius, as well as give you more insight into what happened to him.

### Find Volf

Head to the beggars' camp in the northeastern corner of the city, by the walls in the Cobblers' Quarter. You will notice him when a prompt appears to look at the source of an especially foul smell, which, naturally, is Volf. Volf is hammered, so you'll need to give him a Hair o' the Dog potion to sober him up (you'll need 2 of them if they are not strong).

Once he sobers up, you'll need to convince him to go with you to talk to Fabrizio 'de Dondi about the clock, despite Volf's dislike of Italians. You'll also need to convince him to head to the baths with you so he doesn't embarrass you both.

Just outside the baths, Volf will panic and run off - simply give chase for a few seconds till you corner him under a bridge just outside the walls. Convince him once again to go to the baths, and this time he will without issue. You'll need to acquire some clothes for him while he's bathing - a tunic or coat, hose, and shoes, as well as, optionally, a hat for extra reputation gain.

### Meet with Fabrizio

With a freshly cleaned and dressed Volf in tow, you'll head to talk to Fabrizio over dinner at his house. Ask for water instead of wine when offered and interject as necessary to keep the discussion civil (or don't), and ultimately Fabrizio will invite Volf to stay at his house while the two work on the clock.

The following waiting period depends on how the dinner went - if it went well, it will take two. Otherwise, it may take up to eight in-game days.

When they're finished, both will appear outside your forge with news - they've broken the crankshaft and need Henry to forge a new one. The crankshaft is simple to forge (it's essentially just a shortsword and uses the same model when forging), you'll just need 1 Frankfurt steel and 1 Toledo steel. Once the crankshaft is done, go talk to both Volf and Fabrizio and ask each to return to the forge. Talk to everyone one last time, then go speak to the bailiff and tell him everything's ready.

Once you speak to the bailiff, a long cutscene will play. Dialogue options here don't seem to matter, ultimately Volf will succeed and the clock will be restored! This concludes the Legacy of the Forge questline.
