## The Last Wish

The Last Wish is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC after Anamnesis.

## Description

Not all monks hold the Abbot’s orders as sacred. One such is the old Constantine.

## Walkthrough

There are two ways to start this quest, with a few differences depending on how it is started. It can be started by speaking to either Monk Athanasius or Constantine (who is only called "Monk" in-game).

### Talk to Athanasius

In the dorms, you’ll find a monk named Athanasius. Talk to him and he will express his worry for another monk, Constantine, whom no one in the dorms has seen since the monastery was locked down. He will then ask you to find Constantine. He suggests looking in the gardens, as Constantine loves spending time there. Head to the gardens east of the infirmary, and head north. By the wall will be an older monk with spectacles, fitting Athanasius’s description. You can also talk to Herbalist Joachim and ask after Constantine’s whereabouts, which he will divulge with a speech check.

Talk to him and exhaust his dialogue. He would much rather enjoy the splendour of nature than be cooped up indoors. He wants you to relay his good health to Athanasius, but can be convinced to return with a very hard speech check. If you are unable to convince him immediately, return to Athanasius who will then insist you go back and get Constantine to return himself.

Head back to the garden and let Constantine know of Athanasius’s response. You will have the option to either further convince him to return to the dormitory or let him stay in the garden. Either option will end the quest.

### Find Constantine

In the garden, along the eastern wall in the northern section, you’ll find a Monk sitting on a bench. Talk to him and he’ll reveal that he went to the garden to be with nature and does not want to be cooped up inside.

He will ask you to deliver a message to another monk, Athanasius, who may be worried about him. You’ll find Athanasius in the dormitories with the other monks. Talk to Athanasius and let him know that Constantine has requested to stay in the gardens, which will end the quest.

## The Lion's Crest

This article is about the DLC. For the quest walkthrough, see The Lion's Crest (quest).

The Lion's Crest is a pre-order downloadable content pack released alongside Kingdom Come: Deliverance II on 4 February 2025. It has since been made available for purchase as a standalone DLC.

## Description

Experience a unique questline that, once completed, will reward you with the legendary armour and weapon set of the famous Knight Brunswick: The Lion's Crest.

Stand out from the crowd with a polearm for long distance combat, a dagger when you want to get up close and personal, a full set of plate armour for your good self and a full caparison (a protective and decorative cloth covering) for your noble steed.

This set comes replete with a Bohemian coat of arms, with burgundy and gold trim in abundance. Because no one said you can’t look classy on the battlefield.

## Overview

After downloading the DLC, Brunswick armour set including two weapons can be acquired by finishing the quest The Lion's Crest - it can be started after finishing a few of the introductory quests, the last one being Laboratores. You will at that moment have full access to the open world, where you can start this quest by talking to the local scribe near Trosky Castle. The quest will then be marked on the map with a special DLC symbol.

## Content

- Brunswick's dagger

- Brunswick's poleaxe

- Brunswick's bascinet

- Brunswick's brigandine

- Brunswick's caparison

- Brunswick's chainmail coif

- Brunswick's gauntlets

- Brunswick's plate leg armour

- Brunswick's plate sleeves

- Brunswick's map I

- Brunswick's map II

- Brunswick's map III

- Brunswick's map IV

## The Lion's Den

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Lion's Den is the 22nd main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. You can begin the quest anytime after completing Exodus by talking to Zizka at Devil's Den.

## Synposis

Sigismund and his henchmen have thwarted our plans. We have to prepare to strike back.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Zizka at the Devil’s Den to start the quest. If you are fast enough and Samuel has not returned from Kolin, you’ll have to wait for him to do so to move forward. To hit back at von Bergow, you’ll need his cannon, only someone will have to infiltrate the Praguers and send word of when they’re moving it. As usual, it’s up to Henry.

If you’d like, you can speak to Hans to go on a little hunting jaunt with him, starting the quest Like Old Times.

### Entering Sigismund's Camp

You'll need to simply talk to the guard at the entrance and cough up 500 to get in. You'll be allowed permanent access from this point on though. If you have previously entered the camp, then you’ll be able to walk in like normal.

### Meet with Katherine

Katherine is now working at the camp as a bathmaid, you’ll be able to find her in the area that houses the baths. On your way there you may be able to observe and argument over unpaid work between Grozav of Borumlaca, the leader of the camp, and a blacksmith as well as Chertan and Milada over the conduct of the latter’s men at the baths.

Once at the baths, talk to Katherine and ask her about the situation in camp regarding the cannon and how best to infiltrate the ranks of the Praguers. Exhaust all dialogue with her and she’ll direct you to a man called Stephen Crow who may be able to get you recruited. She will also mention that there is talk of a spy in camp, though it clearly isn’t her they’re suspicious of, so Henry should be careful poking around.

Speak with Katherine a second time to start the quest The Stalker. You’ll have a second opportunity to start this quest later as well, but it is available right after speaking to her the first time.

### Get enlisted

To get enlisted, you’ll have to speak to Crow. He can be found near the archery range. To convince him to let you join, you’ll have to attempt a few skill checks. Eventually, Crow will say your insistence on joining is suspicious and you can choose from any of the options as they will all satisfy him and he’ll take you to the commander of the Prague force, Ditrich Katz.

Katz wants to give you a test. A group of men disappeared between Miskowitz and Rabstein - he wants you to find out what happened to them and retrieve the painted chest containing an important charter for him.

He’ll direct you towards the infirmary, as one of the soldiers from the lost group returned and is being treated there. He’ll also tell you to speak to the leader of the mercenaries Captain Puta and ask him for supplies, speaking to Puta will start the quest Spoils of War if it has not already been completed.

### Talk to Musa and Heal Myshek

You’ll find Musa in the infirmary. He’ll tell you that Myshek, the injured soldier, had been rambling about a place called Lhota and a wagon. To get more information out of him, you’ll need to wake him up as there’s not enough time to wait for him to come around on his own.

Pass a Hard Alchemy check to suggest making him something with mint, Musa will then suggest a very strong Cockerel potion. If you do not already have the recipe, Musa will give it to you.

It is important that it be at least Strong, anything weaker will kill Myshek. This means you’ll need fresh Mint and Valerian. The closest sure location to find mint is at the herb garden in Raborsch. Valerian can then be found by the laundry spot south of there. This is close enough to grab and return to Sigismund’s camp to brew.

Give the potion to Myshek and if it is strong you’ll be able to ask him about his missing comrades. He was injured when the deserters tried to shut him up as he had been against deserting himself. They had mentioned Lhota in the past and he thinks that’s the best bet for finding them.

### Find the Lost Charter at Old Lhota

Old Lhota is where you’ll be headed next. The soldiers are holed up in the building directly in front of the fast travel spot, head around the side and if you approach peacefully you’ll be able to talk to the posted guard.

Remain cordial and promise not to report them to get the charter peacefully. The guard will tell you where to find it and give you the key to its chest. It is up in the loft in the painted chest. Unless you take something more than promised or initiate combat, the deserters will not become hostile.

If you would rather take it by force, there are six of them. Attacking at night will let you take out some of them while they sleep, conveniently right in the loft near the charter. If you take out the ones in the loft, stay by the stairs and the rest will be easy pickings as they can be killed immediately upon getting off the ladder one at a time.

Note: Once you hand over the document, the quest will become timed.

Once you have the charter, return to camp to hand it over to Katz, you can choose whether to tell him about the soldiers if you did not kill them. He will reward you with 250 (500 if you chose to kill the soldiers) and a Praguers' hemmed waffenrock and then offer to drink and play dice with you to celebrate. If you’d like to play, he’ll wager 300 .

After a cutscene, your merrymaking will be interrupted by an attack on the commander of the Cumans, Chertan. He succumbs to his wounds and it’s up to Henry to find the perpetrator lest Musa be held accountable.

### Investigate the Murder

The first order of business is to search the crime scene. There are seven pieces of evidence you can find, though the objective will update after you have found three of them:

- The bloodstain

- The broken lock

- The cannon

- The spilled gunpowder

- The bloody tub

- Lord Borumlaca's bond

- The guard tower

- Grozav's lucky die

The bloodstain is right in front of you, where Chertan had just been lying. To your right is the shed with the broken lock housing the cannon and the gunpowder on the floor. The tub is behind Chertan’s tent, the green one to the east of Katz’s, and the bond can be found inside hidden in a hard locked chest. You can read it to reveal that Grozav owed Chertan money. (Note: The key to the chest can be found under Chertan's bed.) The guard tower is at the back of the camp. You can also question both guards that where on duty.

Once you’ve found the evidence, return to Katz and let him know what you discovered. After doing so, you’ll go to check on Chertan who has since died. Grozav accuses Musa of having done him in. Your answers in the following conversation can affect your reputation with all involved parties but not the outcome of the quest. Musa will confirm, however, that Chertan was indeed poisoned. For the best reputation, avoid incriminating Musa.

In order to save Musa, you will have to find the real murderer. Part of this will mean talking to Musa despite his being under lock and key. You’ll need to distract the guard, pick the option ‘a girl from the baths will help’ to unlock the objective to ask Katherine to help you. If you help Katherine with The Stalker then she will lure the guard away from his post.

Otherwise, you can either sneak around behind the infirmary or pass a speech or intimidation check to get the guard to leave yourself.

Once he’s gone, you can go inside and talk to Musa. Exhaust all his dialogue and he’ll suggest you figure out what poison was used. With that knowledge, finding the ingredients should cast enough suspicion. Pass a very hard alchemy check to gain Musa’s confidence.

### Examine the Body and Identify the Poison

The body and book on poisons are both in the same room of the infirmary. Examine the body thoroughly, the clues that will help you identify the poison are:

- Puked and defecated

- Lesions on his hands/reddened skin on face

- Spasms

With that information, read the book of poisons. Henry will want to check with Musa to confirm, but the poison you are looking for is Kiss of Death. Musa will then ask why a man with your skills would join as a mere foot soldier. Being honest with him will gain reputation.

### Look into the Suspects

Now that you know how Chertan was killed, it’s time to look into the possible suspects. Musa is ruled out, so that leaves Grozav, Stephen Crow, and the two guards, Adalbert and Radovan.

Since you are already in Musa’s tent, start there. The items you’ll need to examine are the vessel, the valuables, the potions, and the prayer rug.

With Musa ruled out, the next closest suspect to look into will be Grozav. The items you’ll need to examine are the herbs or the wine. You can also talk to him to interrogate him, pass a hard speech or very hard domination check to convince him to answer your questions.

Next, head around towards the archery range to look into Crow and the guards. Start with the guards, examine the alcohol, broom, bed, and take a peek in their chest, nothing of interest. For Crow, the items you’ll need to examine are the water, the oak wood, and the nails – all ingredients for Kiss of Death. You can also find 1000 groschen in his chest and a strange note if you pickpocket him. You can interrogate him the same as Grozav without a required check.

With all the evidence gathered, return to Katz to start the trial.

### The Trial

Note: Be mindful, three incorrect deductions will lead you to the gallows and a game over. You can choose whether to accuse Crow or Grozav. Indicting Grozav is needed for the achievement The Hydra's Heads.

Once you have all the evidence, you'll need to accuse someone at the trial with the justiciar. At this point you should've deduced that Chertan was killed with the Kiss of Death poison and that Stephen Crow is clearly the murderer as he had all the required ingredients in his tent, 1000 groschen in his chest (as payment for the sabotage/murder), and the Strange message on his person. It stands to reason that Crow was in fact the spy Katherine mentioned earlier. If he is not accused, Crow will turn on his comrades during the ambush to steal the cannon.

To indict Crow:

- Stay silent

- Stay silent

- He was with us at the time of the stabbing.

- Corporal Stephen Crow.

- Chertan caught Crow stealing powder.

- There was powder scattered all over the storeroom.

- Crow poisoned the wine while Musa wasn’t looking.

- You brewed a poison called Kiss of Death.

To indict Grozav:

- Stay silent

- Stay silent

- He was with us at the time of the stabbing.

- Lord Grozav of Borumlaca.

- Grozav didn’t want to pay his debts.

- I found a promissory note.

- Grozav poisoned the wine before we arrived.

- Mention the found herbs.

Regardless of who is accused, they will refuse the punishment and initiate combat. Once you kill them, Katz will tell you the Praugers are finally moving out!

### The Ambush

After the trial, go talk to Katherine - who will leave to go alert Zizka that the cannon is about to be moved.

Then equip your combat gear and go talk to Katz when you're ready to leave. A short cutscene will play as the ambush occurs, then you simply need to fight the Praguers. After the fight is won, you can choose to either let Katz go or fight him honourably to the death.

Note: If you had Grozav killed then you must kill Katz here which will earn the achievement The Hydra's Heads.

You can also go talk to Crow and ask him what he's up to. With a very hard speech check you can convince him to help in Maleshov during Dancing with the Devil.

Talk to Zizka when you're ready and you'll fast travel back to Devil's Den to end the quest and immediately start the next, Dancing with the Devil.

## The Lord Taketh Away

The Lord Taketh Away is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You've lost ten thousand groschen.

## Acquisition

This achievement unlocks when you lose a significant amount of Groschen. In this context, "lose" refers to losing money through betting or paying fines, not just spending (this is what Groschen Must Flow achievement is for).

The achievement is also cumulative, so frequent gamblers or those who repeatedly pay fines may unlock it naturally.

## Tips

The quickest way to unlock this achievement is to deliberately attract fines. For example:

- Save your game before attempting.

- Travel to Kuttenberg and kill several civilians.

- When guards approach, use the surrender option.

- Accept the hefty fine (something over 11,000 Groschen).

The achievement will unlock upon paying the fine.

## The Magic Arrow

The Magic Arrow is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

I met some bandits at the Devil’s Den tavern. They need some help with obtaining a magic arrow, which, unfortunately, is stuck in their leader’s head, and he’s dead and buried. Looks like a pretty dirty job.

## Walkthrough

Speak to Pasha at the Devil's Den to start the quest. Head to the Sedletz gravedigger Lenek’s house just north of the monastery.

Talk to him and ask about Karel. You’ll have to pass an easy skill check to get him to tell you anything. He’ll let you know the grace is not in the graveyard, as Karel was taken as a sorcerer, but buried behind a large willow next to the cemetery.

The willow is on the north end of the cemetery, just outside the outer wall. Head over there to find a fresh grave. Inspect and interact with it to dig Karel up. Remove the arrow carefully and return to the Devil’s Den.

When you get there, Pasha won’t be there, so talk to Hare. Agree to go with him and he’ll lead you towards their camp. On the way there, he’ll stop and ask you to give him the arrow. You can do so, ending the quest, or you can refuse and insist on delivering it to Pasha. He will give you no reward for the arrow, but insist you've saved the lives of the remaining men in the band and he hopes to repay you someday.

If you insist, he’ll try to attack you and you’ll have to pass a hard speech, hard coercion, very hard presence or hard intimidation check to convince him not to attack you. Otherwise, he will become hostile and you’ll be forced to kill him.

The camp you are looking for is on the map as an enemy encampment, if you did Arrow-head previously it will be marked clearly. Make a beeline for Pasha, as the others will react as regular bandits and become hostile if you are not quick.

Pasha will ask about Hare, you can tell him what you want and it will have little effect. Henry will hand over the arrow and Pasha will ask you for one last favour – shooting him with it as he shot Karel in the past, lodging the arrow in the first place.

You can get out of shooting him with a hard speech check, ending the quest, or you can agree. He’ll give you a crossbow. If you miss, he’ll sic his men on you, so aim carefully. The arrow will do what arrows to the head tend to do and his men will run off, ending the quest.

Your reward for refusing to shoot him will be 30 . Along with the knowledge he might live to see another day.

Your reward after shooting him will be everything you can loot from him and the camp. There is a medium locked chest with 178.5 and Brocade.

## The Master's Game

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Master's Game is the 3rd quest in the Legacy of the Forge DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It will transition to a repeatable guild task in the daily rotation once Henry is fully integrated in the blacksmiths' guild.

## Introductory Quest

### Description

I'm supposed to play a game of dice with Boris of Brod.

### Walkthrough

Magdalena will suggest that you play some dice with Master Boris of Brod as a way to socialize and improve your standing with the other guild members and possibly learn more about Martin.

You can find Boris's shop in the central part of Kuttenberg, near many of the other armoursmiths and weaponsmiths. He can be challenged to any game of dice with or without badges.

Regardless of whether you win or lose, Boris will give you a tin badge after the game and send you on your way. This will complete the quest and automatically begin the next, Klaus' Introduction. You will also now receive daily repeatable tasks to play dice at various locations in the city to build the blacksmiths' guild's prestige, as described further below.

### Objectives

## Repeatable Task

### Description

I'm spreading the glory of the Kuttenberg Blacksmiths' Guild among the dice players.

### Walkthrough

Various dicers around Kuttenberg want to play dice for the glory of their groups. Go to where the small orange shield shows and ask them to play. You can play at any level, with or without badges.

### Objectives

## The Master's Game - Special Badge

### Description

I'm spreading the glory of the Kuttenberg Blacksmiths' Guild among the dice players.

### Walkthrough

Talk to Dicer Ludva in Kuttenberg. He'll ask you to get a badge belonging to Chernik in Bylany. Head to Bylany and challenge him. You'll find him at the inn there, and you can challenge him to a game for the badge.

Once you've won it, return to Ludva in Kuttenberg and either hand over the badge or lie and keep it for yourself. As a reward, he'll offer you 450 or badges.

### Objectives

## The Master's Game - Die Thief

### Description

I'm spreading the glory of the Kuttenberg Blacksmiths' Guild among the dice players.

### Walkthrough

Head to Pschitoky Wagoners' Inn to meet with Dicer Kazimír. When you get close, you'll notice he's being robbed! Run after the thief. If you're unable to catch him, he'll hide in the nearby copse. You'll find him crouched next to a tree south of the quest indicator near the western edge of the search radius.

Confront him and pass a hard speech, medium charisma, or very hard intimidation check to get the die back. Alternatively, you can request he bribe you and keep the die, or if all skill checks fail, you can fight him for it.

Return to the inn and hand the die back over to Kazimir. He'll give you 150 and a Painted die, and you'll earn some blacksmith prestige. You may also keep the die for yourself if you prefer.

### Objectives

## The Master's Game - Drunkard

### Description

I'm spreading the glory of the Kuttenberg Blacksmiths' Guild among the dice players.

### Walkthrough

Head to the inn west of Kuttenberg. Once there, talk to Dice player Halama. Agree to drink, and you'll get nice and soused and play dice with him. Once you win, he'll pass out, and his wife will appear.

She'll ask for a chance to win his money back. Once you play her, if you win, she'll ask you to return some of the money to her. You can give the whole stake, just her bet, or a pittance as alms; the more you give, the more blacksmith prestige you'll earn. You can also simply give her your winnings without playing her, in which case she'll reward you with a Gold Emperor's badge, which you can either return, pay her 300 for, or keep without paying.

## The Mouth of Hell

The Mouth of Hell is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Something very strange is afoot in the abandoned mines near Old Kutna.

## Walkthrough

The quest can be obtained while passing by Old Kutna on the main road, where you'll see a group of villagers arguing with Father Marian around several slaughtered cattle. Once the conversation ends, Henry will be tasked with delivering an offering to the abandoned mine that the "monster" escaped into. The mine entrance is just to the west of Old Kutna.

### The mine

When you arrive at the mine and begin to climb down, a cutscene will play. Henry will be knocked out and wake up naked somewhere inside the mine.

Once you wake up, walk forward and follow the knight to the left at the first turn. Keep walking until you come to a room with a hunting sword and a note on a table on your left. There are also two locked chests on your right and one lockpick in the basket next to the matress. Keep walking forward, hugging the walls so you can see something. You'll eventually come to a ladder and the knight will be at the top, and ask who you are. On the table behind the ladder is another lockpick. Climb the ladder once the knight turns and walks away. At the top of the ladder, turn left and follow the tunnel. The knight will turn around in the tunnel directly ahead of you, so wait until he about faces and walks down the tunnel to the left. You can follow him here and knock him out from behind. Note: if he turns and sees you he'll attack immediately, and the fight won't be especially easy since he's fully armoured and you'll be naked at this point with only a hunting sword. His helmet's stuck so you can't identify him. Loot him for a few decent pieces of armour that are worth selling. Keep walking down the tunnel and you'll eventually come to a lit room with a chest containing all your things, as well as more notes from the knight. After this, it's time to get out of the mine. Follow the path to the right of your chest (with wooden planks along the wall) and eventually you'll come to the ladders at the entrance you fell down in originally. Climb out to trigger a cutscene.

### Out of the mine

There will be several guards waiting for you, as well as Father Marian. (If only previously knocked out and not killed in the mine, the deranged knight will follow you out a few moments later. It doesn't matter if you took his items - he'll still be wearing them here. You will have to fight him again but it should be easier as it's 4v1.) Talk to Father Marian to receive your reward: some reputation and 225 .

### Alternative ending

If you open the medium locked chest in the room with the hunting sword, you will find a Knight's contract letter and some money. If you read it you will be able to talk with Taras Mura and convince him to climb out of the mine. The cutscene will start of Henry climbing out of the mine and the knight following him. If you use the first dialogue option Henry will explain everything and show the contract letter. Later in dialogue you will have to pass one of the two skill checks: either Persuasion or Impression. Passing either of them will result in good ending, Father Marian will give you 475 and Taras Mura will end his duty in the mine.

## The Night-Mare

The Night-Mare is the 5th quest in the Brushes with Death DLC in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the first quest in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

Voyta’s opus magnum is supposed to be a painting for the altar at Sedletz. However, after many years, his old friend Bellissimo reappeared in Kuttenberg, someone with whom he has unresolved issues from the past. Bellissimo is also interested in the project and seems to have struck a deal with the abbot to his own advantage. This is bad news for Voyta, who believed the commission was secure. How can Bellissimo be deterred? And how did he manage to get the commission?

## Synopsis

Henry meets Voyta at his workshop in Kuttenberg. Voyta is quite pleased to see him, and wants to show him his current project. It is in its early stages, only a sketch, but Voyta truly believes he’s on his way to creating his masterpiece – an altar for the chapel of Sedletz Monastery.

As Voyta is explaining the commission, he is interrupted by a man who insults him. This man first identifies himself as an old friend saying they haven’t seen each other in nearly twenty years. His name is Bellissimo and he studied together with Voyta some time ago. He’s come to let Voyta know that his services will no longer be required for the monastery job, as Bellissimo has been tasked with taking on the whole lot.

With this turn, Voyta is despondent. He feels he only has two options, give up or get rid of Bellissimo. Henry suggests that since giving up is not an option, he’ll help Voyta get rid of Bellissimo. He may then simply kill him or convince him to leave.

Convincing him to leave finds Henry looking into how he managed to get the commission out from under Voyta. At the bathhouse where he rents a room, the matron there is sure Bellissimo is up to something, as he’s suddenly started praying all the time, unlike him. She tells Henry he has a room upstairs and spends most of his time in the garden across from the baths for his work. He’s apparently a terrible drunk and tries all sorts of nasty things with the girls at the bathhouse when soused.

In Bellissimo’s workshop, Henry finds a list of horrid sins Bellissimo has committed in the past and in his room, he finds a letter from the abbot. It turns out Bellissimo agreed to do the work for free in exchange for the forgiveness of his sins.

Since those sins weigh so heavily, and he’s so afraid of hell, Voyta suggests they convince Bellissimo the Devil himself has come for his soul. In order to do that, Henry will have to disguise himself as the Prince of Hell and confront Bellissimo one night after he’s been kicked out of the baths for being too drunk and tell him if he wants to save his soul, he’ll have to leave Kuttenberg and beg for forgiveness from the Pope himself, both of them even.

Henry and Voyta make a disguise and go through with the plan to scare Bellissimo. Unable to handle being confronted by the Devil himself, Bellissimo crumbles and runs away in fear. Henry returns and tells Voyta the good news.

## Walkthrough

In Kuttenberg, talk to Voyta and he’ll direct you to the bathhouse. Once there, talk to Beata and ask after Bellissimo. You can get the information you need from here with either a 50 groschen bribe, a very hard speech check, or lying and saying he robbed a friend.

She will tell you Bellissimo has a room upstairs and spends most of his time in a garden across the street from the bathhouse. You can kill him and complete the quest right away or you can dig deeper.

### Kill Bellissimo

If you want to kill Bellissimo, be aware it will lock you out of a unique outfit later. Otherwise, it will have no major implications for the DLC.

Bellissimo spends the entire day sitting on a bench in the garden across from the bathhouse. No one else is around, so you can sneak up behind him and do a stealth kill. You could also take him out while he sleeps, but this will require breaking into his room and carries a larger risk of being found out.

Once he is dead, return to Voyta and talk to him to finish the quest. Henry will not inform Voyta that Bellissimo has been killed, so your relationship with him will not be affected.

### Torment Bellissimo

In order to deal with Bellissimo without killing him, you’ll need access to his room. The bathhouse is busy and many people walk past the door at all hours, so it is easiest if you pickpocket the key from Bellissimo first.

He spends the entire day sitting on a bench in the garden across from the bathhouse. No one else is around, so you can sneak up behind him and pickpocket him to get the key to his room. Also in the garden is a shed that doubles as Bellissimo’s workshop, inside it you will find a chest with a List of Bellissimo’s Sins inside. Read it and it will reveal he has committed adultery with the wife of a client, shat in a church, slept with nuns, and vomited on a priest. Revealing these past sins will help you convince him to leave the city later. You will also be able to look this list later in the quest, should you prefer.

Alternatively, if you have the Master Thief perk, you can unlock his room using that and enter as you will.

With the keys, you can head into his room unnoticed. There will be a dresser with a letter on it for you to read which will reveal how Bellissimo got the job.

Once you’ve done that, head back to Voyta and update him. Voyta will suggest Henry scare Bellissimo by making him think the Devil is after him. To make a suitably devilish disguise, you’ll need a helmet with a bascinet, three torches, and five eggs. A helmet with a bascinet can be purchased from most armourers (or stolen from them), torches can be found on almost any person as well as from general traders, and eggs can be stolen from hen houses or else purchased from a grocer. Once you have everything, head back to Voyta again and he will exchange those items for the disguise.

To give Bellissimo the fright of his life, first you have to steal the schnapps from his room. Simply take all the schnapps in his bedside chest. Next, you’ll have to find Bellissimo at night and get him drunk. There will be skill checks during your conversation, but they will not have an impact on the outcome. Once Bellissimo has passed out, pick him up and carry him into the shed where you previously found the list of his sins and drop him there.

At this point, Henry will change into the disguise, overwriting whatever outfit you have equipped, and Bellissimo will wake to find the Devil putting him on trial for his sins. If you read the list, you can use that by telling him about them. Henry will tell him to leave the city and he will run away in fear. If you did not read the list and you fail the skill checks, Bellissimo will realise you are a fake and will initiate combat. Simply beat him unarmed and he will run off all the same.

Return to Voyta one last time and let him know Bellissimo has left town, ending the quest.

## The Peasants' Revolt

The Peasants' Revolt is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is tipped by Kubyenka at the Devil's Den.

## Description

The peasants from around Miskowitz are resisting the oppression of Sigismund’s army, and they need all the help they can get.

## Walkthrough

To acquire the tip for the quest, talk to Kubyenka. He'll direct you to Herbwoman Vlasta and give you the password to say to her. When speaking to her, give her the proper password (The fox is in the henhouse) and any choice will convince her to let you help. She will then give you supplies to deliver to the rebel camp where the young men gather to the south-west.

When you arrive, you’ll find the camp massacred with one survivor, Otter. Talk to him and pass a medium Survival check to treat him.

Wolves will attack, fend them off, and then talk to Otter again. He’ll tell you there’s money hidden in a jug over a cliff near Miskowitz he wants you to have as payment, but there's nothing else he can do for you or the cause. This is not marked as part of the quest but will be marked on the map as a point of interest. It is along the river that flows south-east from Miskowitz, east of a roe hunting spot.

Lastly, head back to Vlasta and let her know the situation. She’ll give you two strong Aqua Vitalis, two strong Marigold decoctions, and two strong Painkiller brews as a reward.

## The Ragman's Dream

The Ragman's Dream is an achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You helped the Ragman save his dream.

## Acquisition

The The Ragman's Dream achievement can only be earned during the activity Sinners of Kuttenberg – Ragman's Dream, given by Ragman. He asks you to help him recover some stolen documents. Return them to Ragman to unlock the achievement.

## Tips

- To begin the last quest in the thievery questline, talk to Ragman at his house once the quest icon appears on the map. Ragman says some people stole important documents from him, and he need Henry to pay off a ransom to them.

- Meet the two blackmailers outside the west gate of the city. During the conversation, give them the 1,000 Groschen provided by Ragman. They will then tell you where to find the necessary documents.

- You can pickpocket the money back from them as they walk away.

- Locate the Almoner, who walks around Kuttenberg wearing white clothing and a red hat. He can often be found in the central street near several food stalls.

- During the conversation with the Almoner, select whichever dialogue options are easiest to get the documents.

- Return the documents to Ragman and the achievement will unlock.

## The Reliquary

The Reliquary is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It can be completed concurrently with the quest Thou art but dust...

A Humble Knight camping near Sedletz Monastery wants to see the sword of Sir Valentine who is buried in the church graveyard.

## Description

Location of Humble Knight's camp

Not far from Sedletz graveyard I met a knight who told me about his role model, Sir Valentine, who is said to have once made a pilgrimage to Jerusalem and brought back soil from a holy field. They say Valentine is buried in the church graveyard, and the knight asked if I could bring back him his sword.

## Walkthrough

You will find the grave of Sir Valentine in the same undercroft you are forced to explore in the side quest Thou art but dust.... The grave will be empty but Henry will be able to come up with a plan to forge the sword based on the picture on the casket.

Note: Although Henry may remark on the tomb when you see it, be sure to interact with it to have him get the idea for the sketch.

Forge the sword and bring it to the Humble Knight. He will be impressed by the work but he will also reveal that he is indeed a charlatan who sells mainly stolen and fake artifacts and will need to kill you since you know the sword is fake, you will be then forced to succeed in a hard Might speech check or engage in combat with the swindler.

If you manage to kill the charlatan you can find valuables in his body and chest although they will be flagged as stolen, he will drop the sword of Sir Valentine to the ground where you can pick it up.

## Objectives

## Bugs

- Although Henry forged the sword, it will be flagged as stolen if you get it back from the Humble Knight after killing him.

## The Royal Physician

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Royal Physician is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 1st quest in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC.

## Description

Lord Pisek tasked me with going to see Master Albich of Uniczow – a renowned physician who now lives at the house of the Tarmarian apothecary in Kuttenberg. Albich is planning a visit to the Sedletz Monastery and Lord Pisek is looking for someone to accompany him.

## Walkthrough

Speak with Peter of Pisek to begin the quest. Depending on when you initiate the quest, he can be found in different locations; he'll be marked on the map with a purple shield icon with a gold cross. He needs your help: Albich of Uniczow, a renowned physician and friend, has heard that Wenceslas IV has taken ill in Vienna. The doctor is heading to Sedletz Monastery to ask for the abbot’s intercession to allow him to treat the captive king. Pisek wants you to act as the physician’s escort to the monastery.

Pisek will give you a letter and send you to Albich’s house in Tarmark at the apothecary. Speak to the apothecary trader and he’ll tell you Albich is out. Apparently the maid two doors down is unwell and he rushed over there to help her.

At the mentioned house you’ll find Matthew Ram of Tseyle and his bodyguard banging on the door trying to get Albich to come out. He won’t speak to you and the guard will tell you to clear off so you’ll have to get in around the back.

Once inside, head into the main room and talk to the hired hand who has been trying to keep Ram out. Turns out, Ram wants Albich’s help over the maid, Manya. The hired hand will let you know Albich is upstairs. Head up there and you’ll find him working with Manya the maid to the right of the stairs.

Give him the letter and you'll explain the situation. You’ll be interrupted by Ram and Albich will send you to deal with them. Medium scholarship check will calm them down and run them off. If you are unable to convince them to leave, you’ll have to fight them.

Albich will then invite you to the monastery. He will ask you to change into simple clothes, no armour, before allowing you to go.

Note: Once you enter Sedletz, you will not be able to leave for the rest of the DLC. There will be some opportunity to gather armour later in the questline, so it is best to bring a cloth coif along if you want to have the option of wearing a helm.

Albich will head back to the apothecary and can be found either around the upstairs or outside reading, let him know when you are ready to go. Once in Sedletz, you'll talk to the abbot, ending the quest and starting Anamnesis.

## The Spark

The Spark is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It's part of The Guild's questline. It is mutually exclusive with the quest Civic Duty.

## Description

The Guild is planning its greatest diversion mission yet, I can’t miss it.

## Walkthrough

A few days after completing The Thieves' Code, a messenger will call out to Henry as he rides through any town in the Kuttenberg region. The messenger will tell Henry to go meet with Chenyek at The Hole in the Wall tavern, starting the quest.

Upon receiving the quest, head to the Hole and speak to Chenyek. He wants to take a big step and hit Sigismund where it hurts, in the coffers. To stop the flow of silver, he wants to collapse a mine. As always, he’d like you to do it without any bloodshed, if possible. To blow up the mine, you'll need some black powder.

Knuckles will offer you an alternative again as well. Fed up with Chenyek for good, he wants to report him and take over as leader with fewer ideals trapping the group down.

### Get the powder

The first step is talking to Eldris to find out where to get black powder; he can be found at his workshop in Hoprink, not far from the Hole. He will only sell the stuff to a small set of people, pass a very hard charisma, easy intimidation, or hard domination check to convince him. However, he doesn’t have any as he was recently robbed.

His rival, Whisker of Kolin, however should have some supply and Eldris wouldn’t mind if his shipment were to disappear. He will tell you that you can find Whisker north of Sigismund's camp heading there from Bohunowitz.

There will be a large search radius, you’ll find Whisker and his men along the road near where the river splits. To get there quickly, fast travel to Bohunowitz and head north on the road. The wagon is stuck in the river. Talk to Whisker and pass a medium charisma check to convince him to give it to you or else buy it from it outright. He’ll give you the Barrel chest key, allowing you to loot the barrel from the chest just in front of him.

Now that you have the powder, you can set up the explosion.

### Set the powder

The Guild members are waiting for the black powder at the Horschan mine between Horschan and Grund. Talk to Goliath, if you approach during the day you have the option to wait with him until nightfall. Once the time is right, he’ll tell you the plan, follow him to the mine entrance.

Note: for the achievement Remember, Remember..., kill Goliath in front of the mine. This will fail the quest but allow you to return to the main camp and toss the barrel onto the cooking fire there, earning you the achievement.

Head into the mine, follow the path ahead until you come to a wheelbarrow at a crossroads. Turn right there and you’ll eventually reach some platforms leading downwards, go down them and then you’ll see the beam with the reddish rag where you need to place the barrel.

Note: lighting the fuse will use up a torch. If you are worried about getting lost in the semi-darkness, it is best to bring a second one or a Nighthawk potion.

Once you place the barrel, retrace your steps to leave the mine. This section is timed, so there is a possibility that the explosion will go off if you get lost. As you approach the exit, the explosion will go off, knocking you out. While are you are unconscious, Goliath will steal whatever shoes you are wearing as well as a portion of your grochen, both of which can be pickpocketed from him after, but the shoes will be flagged as stolen if you do. If you remove your shoes before the powder explodes, he won't take them but will still steal some of your grochen. Upon waking, if you killed Knuckles after rejecting his proposal, you can leave the area immediately. If you left him alive, you’ll be confronted by a group of guards because he ratted you out. You can pass a hard intimidation check or very hard charisma check to end the situation without bloodshed. With the impact of the explosion on your cleanliness, your charisma will be negatively affected. If you are unable to pass either check, you’ll have to fight the guards.

Once the guards are dealt with, return to the Hole to update Chenyek on how things went. Talk to him and he’ll reveal that Knuckles betrayed the group and set the guards on you, so the other Guild members did away with him. Share a toast and finish out the conversation with him to end the quest and your time with the Guild.

## The Stalker

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Stalker is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is only available during the main quest The Lion's Den by talking to Katherine immediately after she gives you a bath.

## Description

It seems Katherine has caught the eye of one of the Cumans in Sigismund’s camp. At night she hears him whispering by her tent – he even stole one of her shoes. I should find him and make him leave her alone.

## Walkthrough

You’ll have a few different ways to find Katherine’s stalker. If you passed an easy houndmaster check, she’ll give you her remaining shoe which you can then give to Mutt to track. You can also wait around by her tent for the stalker to appear.

Depending on the time of day and how willing you are to wait, the simplest option is to wait by her tent. If you’d like to find her other shoe, give it to Mutt to track and he’ll lead to to the tent where it sits on a barrel inside. If the stalker is not already at the baths, a man called Chakan will be sitting outside his tent.

If waiting, after midnight Chakan will appear and start whispering as she described. In order to confront him, you have to sneak up behind him or else he’ll scarper.

He doesn’t speak Czech, but you can pass a hard speech check to avoid combat or choose to beat him in a fist fight. Passing the very hard check will also initiate a brawl. However you deal with him, talk to Katherine again to end the quest.

## The Sword and the Quill

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Sword and the Quill is the 13th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It's the first quest that takes place in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

"When fleeing from Trosky we managed to discover that Bergow was headed with Sir Hans Capon to somewhere around Kuttenberg. Fortunately, a certain Hynek of Kunstadt, known as Dry Devil, is holed up in the Kuttenberg region. He could help us rescue Sir Hans. His base is Suchdol Fortress, which belongs to Lord Peter of Pisek, and that's where we have headed..."

## Synopsis

Sometime later, Henry enters the Kuttenberg region following behind Katherine and Zizka in the wagon. Zizka asks how much longer it will be before they reach Suchdol and Katherine replies it shouldn’t be much longer. The people in the region are wary of them and Zizka understands it’s because of Sigismund causing trouble with military occupation while Katherine thinks that others, like Dry Devil, are contributing just as much regardless of whose side they’re on. Zizka is offended on his friend’s behalf, conceding he may not be a saint but he’s an ally nevertheless.

Henry doesn’t know Suchdol but Zizka informs him it’s the residence of Peter of Pisek, Mint Master to Wenceslas. The plan is to have an audience with him, but Henry wants to know what comes after that after all his priority is saving Sir Hans. Zizka mollifies Henry by saying they’ll get to that, but he isn’t entirely convinced that ransom will work, as Hanush has a reputation for being stingy. Zizka’s priority is war, meeting Sigismund head-on and not shying from conflict or giving up ground.

The trio arrive at Suchdol fortress and Zizka is surprised to find the gate open with no sentry to stop them. Lord Pisek is in the bailey, giving urgent orders to a worker to take care of some horses. Henry helps Zizka off the wagon and they walk over to greet him. Zizka introduces himself, saying they have a message for Dry Devil and for Lord Pisek, but further elaboration is interrupted by the entry of Lord Pisek’s honoured guest – Margrave Jobst himself.

Jobst tells them that Dry Devil has already left, he expresses curiosity as to what lead them to wash up at Suchdol looking worse for wear, but has no interest in hearing it now. Rather, Jobst tells them all to get some rest, any talk can be had in the morning, then he heads out.

Lord Pisek brings the trio to the banquet hall so they can have something to eat after their journey. On the way there, Zizka compliments the fortress but Lord Pisek would rather move back to the city, saying fortress life isn’t ideal for a man of his age. He invites them to eat their fill, and they, in turn, fill him in on what has just transpired and brought them to his doorstep.

Lord Pisek is grateful for the warning, vowing to stock up on supplies and prepare his men for the likely possibility of trouble on the horizon, and offers some of his best wine as payment for the message. Zizka and Lord Pisek find common ground in their mostly negative opinions towards Jobst and joke about Zizka’s rough past. He begins to tell Lord Pisek of Katherine’s past but she interrupts him immediately. Wanting to avoid the subject, she deflects by mentioning that Henry knows Jobst the best of any of them. Zizka asks after Dry Devil and Lord Pisek explains that he was at Suchdol but parted on bad terms after an argument with the Margrave.

Lord Pisek, when asked what he thinks of the current political situation, says that although Wenceslas may not be a good ruler by any means, he is the legitimate one and that legitimacy is more important than anything else. A legitimate king, in his eyes, is a guarantee of peace, and if the king truly is that bad? Well, no one lives forever. Jobst, it seems, is in the area seeking out alliances with nobles who have thus far remained on the fence in the conflict while also trying to win over some who have allied with Sigismund. As for what comes next, there is a bath and beds waiting for the visitors, as Jobst won’t be back earlier than the next day and he will surely want to talk with them.

During the night, Henry dreams, this time focused on his father Martin’s reaction to his having gotten revenge by killing Toth. Martin asks him if he feels better now and what comes next to which Henry says von Aulitz, then von Bergow… the list seems endless. Is an endless stream of more people to kill what he really wants? Henry says it is, staring down at Toth’s mangled body.

Henry is woken by Maid Zuzana, she’s come to tell him that his presence has been requested by the Margrave and Zizka. Zuzana offers Henry some breakfast, though she’s worried this is an overstep. Henry, somewhat oblivious, thanks her, though she has to prompt him to dismiss her.

In the courtyard, Henry comes across Katherine who is talking to Pisek’s captain – Frenzl. They are discussing the state of the fortress and its men. Katherine thinks the fortress is rather a dump, but Frenzl insists it doesn’t matter as his garrison is strong. He asks for Henry’s opinion and Henry may flatter him or else insult him – either possibly leading to a duel with one of Frenzl’s men, Pullcock. After which, Katherine will beg off meeting the Margrave to ready the horses, expecting they’ll be moving out soon.

Zizka is having his wounds tended to elsewhere in the courtyard. He sends Henry along to meet with Jobst first, saying he’ll follow soon after. Jobst asks for a brief recap of Henry’s plight, despite already knowing the large details, and Henry obliges. Jobst also wants to know about Zizka, how he and Henry came to travel together and who he’s working for, information that Henry may or may not provide. Jobst tells Henry that Liechtenstein has gone silent. Henry admits that under duress, von Bergow was informed that Liechtenstein was in Kuttenberg, which makes him fear that Liechtenstein may have been killed. Jobst agrees, but is not too hung up on it, saying that Liechtenstein knew the risks. Jobst thanks Henry for the information, telling him he’s free to go but there will be a group heading to Rattay soon which he is also free to join. Henry refuses, unwilling to leave without having saved Hans.

Zizka enters and conversation turns to Dry Devil. Zizka is upset that Dry Devil was refused asylum by Jobst, but Jobst counters that such a state isn’t for those who are seeking to cause trouble. They snipe back and forth at each other but when Zizka becomes too heated, Jobst mollifies him. A knock sounds on the door and the Margrave’s men enter, informing him they are ready to leave. Jobst does so, with a warning that no one should trample on the fragile truce he has brokered lest they face severe consequences.

Zizka says Henry can come with him and Katherine. He’ll help Henry get Hans back, but that will require men and information, so nothing can be promised immediately. Katherine, he sends to Kuttenberg to look for Liechtenstein, while he and Henry will look for Dry Devil and his band.

## Walkthrough

Zizka and Peter of Pisek discuss the party's arrival in Suchdol

Follow Lord Pisek and talk to him inside the Banquet Hall. Everyone will discuss the events that happened in Trosky and how you ended up in Kuttenberg (choose whichever dialogue options you like). Zizka will warn Pisek that von Bergow intends to attack those who are still supporting King Wenceslas and is currently headed to Kuttenberg with the Prague militia to meet up with Sigismund. At the end of the conversation, Peter will direct you to your quarters inside the castle and offer you a bath.

You're now free to explore the castle as much as you like, and can go to the bathhouse in the courtyard and speak with Maid Zuzana to bathe. When ready to advance the quest, go to your assigned bed to sleep and save. Your chest is directly next to your bed and now is an opportune time to unload all the gear you picked up during Storm.

### The Next Morning

Maid Zuzana will wake Henry up because Jobst wants to speak to him. Head to the courtyard and speak with Captain Frenzl. You will find him talking to Katherine near the training area. Here, you can agree to duel Pullcock to train with him. If you win, you will receive a Decorated Field Crossbow from Katherine. Afterwards, go find Zizka at the northern corner of the fortress next to the stables where Maid Zuzana is examining him.

Talk to Zizka then head to the Banquet Hall once again where you will deliver your reports to Jobst (you'll go alone regardless of dialogue options chosen with Zizka). After a while, Zizka will join you. Jobst believes that Henry should head back to Rattay, but he insists on staying in order to save Hans. As Jobst takes his leave, he reminds Zizka of his truce with Sigismund, ending the quest.

## The Thunderstone

The Thunderstone is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. In this quest, Henry is tasked with retrieving a rare and powerful Thunderstone. The stone is highly sought after for its magical properties, and players can choose how to resolve the quest for different rewards.

## Description

Thomlin Bruthans founded a fight club in Horschan. If I manage to beat the local goons, I could get a nice reward.

## Walkthrough

After discovering the village of Grund in Kuttenberg, speak with Kona by the drying racks and herb garden. She will ask for your help in retrieving a protective charm, the Thunderstone, which she believes will help with her troubles. Agree to assist her to begin the quest. You can ask more about the stone and also why she wants it, you can pass a medium speech check for her to reveal it's to protect her child after pregnancy.

### Get a Thunderstone

The Thunderstone is currently held by Thomlin Bruthans of Horschan. Track him down and challenge him to a fight (you can kill two birds with one stone here and also start and complete Fight Dirty before continuing to the next step). Defeat Thomlin to learn that the stone was stolen from him by Peter and Hensel, both of whom live in Raborsch. You can also pass a few speech/scholar checks to bypass the fight and force Thomlin to reveal what happened and where the stone is.

### Fake Thunderstone

If you decided to steal Thomlin's thunderstone by pickpocketing, you'll instead find a fake polished stone that doesn't match the description from Kona, the game will even display the description of the real thunderstone and even give you its buff in the player screen, but with no effects. If you bring this stone to Kona she will realize the stone is fake and ask you how you got it, you can either lie and say you won it from a fight with him or confess you stole it, either way she will send you back to Thomlin.

### Peter & Hensel

To learn more about the Thunderstone’s origins, head to Raborsch talk to Peter. He will direct you to a military encampment where Hensel is being held captive. Infiltrate the camp and free Hensel (or kill all the soldiers and their leader, Andrew Ramhead) to progress. After rescuing Hensel, Henry learns that Ramhead stole the stone and sold it to Mlada in Suchdol and he'd have to go talk to her.

Note: You get different dialogue, depending on whether you do this part of the quest before The King's Gambit, or after.

Hensel will tell you where he discovered the gang hid their loot after you rescue him and mark a location on your map called "Two dead trees." Just below the aforementioned trees (towards the pond) is a ram skull mounted on a stick, and right behind that in a little alcove in the cliff face is a vase containing 357 .

### Consult with Mlada

Speak with Mlada to learn that she bought the stone to help save her gravely ill husband. Agreeing to help heal the man will begin the Primum Nil Nocere task, which you'll need to complete successfully if you want to get the stone from Mlada without pickpocketing her.

### Quest Outcomes

You have several choices on how to conclude the quest:

Rewards

|
Action

Reward

|
Give to Kona

Lethean Water recipe, 100 , Alchemy skill increase, discount at Grund stud farm

|
Give to Thomlin

Unarmed combat skill upgrade

|
Keep the thunderstone

Unique permanent buff (see below)

|
Multiple turn-ins (via pickpocketing)

All of the above

## Thunderstone Effects

The Thunderstone is the only item in the game that permanently grants the following buffs (while in your inventory):

- Stamina regen: +10%

- Attack stamina regen: +5%

- Block stamina regen: +5%

- Stamina consumption: -10%

## The Time has Come

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

The Time Has Come is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 6th and final quest in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC.

## Description

The die is cast, Albich’s life hangs by a thread and time’s running like a mad sow.

## Walkthrough

Albich has been poisoned and before he’ll hand over the antidote, Zacharias wants the medical records of King Wenceslas along with the relic from Bavor for Sigismund. Pick Albich up and put him on the bed in his room. He’ll tell you the medical records are “behind the scales”.

Once Seek and You Shall Find complete, the Abbot will free you from requirements imposed by the curfew. Talk to Ludolf and he’ll offer you a cuirass and gambeson which you can pick up from inside the large tent at the knights' camp. There is also a Bell-shaped bascinet you can take with no penalty.

If you talk to Novice Benedict, he’ll suggest scales might be in reference to the Archangel Michael, who is often depicted holding them. He also mentions that Albich left the infirmary to talk to the Abbot a few days ago, giving him the opportunity have hidden the records somewhere in the cloister.

You’ll find the records behind a triptych of the Archangel Michael in the Abbot's chapel.

You can hand the real documents over to Zacharias or else forge a fake. To forge the fake, speak to Librarian Crispin to get some inspiration then head to the secret scriptorium in the cellar and use the materials there. You’ll have to choose the proper responses to make a convincing fake. Note that if you make a mistake, you can still convince Zacharias they are legitimate by passing a hard scholarship check, but to be safe the correct options to convince him outright are:

- Without addressing

- Head and stomach pain

- Less drink

- Infertility

- Healthy lifestyle

With relic and records in-hand real or fake, go to the church and wait for Zacharias near the pit. A group of heavily armed men will arrive and Zacharias with them.

The Abbot will then arrive himself with Ludolf and his company and a fight will break out. You’ll have to take on Zacharias’s men and run after him.

Follow him into the crypt and through the passageway to a now open gate, follow the trail of blood into the cellar, dealing with Zacharias’s men along the way. Eventually, you’ll trigger a cutscene and end up back on the main floor of the cloister.

Defeat Zacharias in a duel. After, the illness will be cured and the monastery reopened. Talk to the Abbot, Albich, and some of the survivors in the church. Then leave the monastery to end the quest and the DLC.

## The White Roebuck

The White Roebuck is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is available as soon as you are able to move freely about the region.

## Description

A rare white roebuck was felled by a poacher. Such a thing cannot be left unpunished.

## Walkthrough

In Suchdol Fortress, talk to Huntsman Dobrosh Pecker to start this quest. He will let you know that a rare white roebuck was recently poached in the region and he wants you to retrieve its pelt for Lord Pisek as compensation.

He will suggest starting by talking to Knacker Wolfram, as the man previous did business with poachers in the past. Pass a medium speech, medium charisma, or hard intimidation check to get him to talk. If you are unable to pass any, you can offer him a bribe of 200 groschen. He will give you a better idea of where to find the poachers, shrinking the search radius, and offer to buy the pelt from you instead of the huntsman.

At the camp, the poachers will be hostile, so take them out as you will. There are three of them and each will carry a Poacher's squirrel tail item as a signifier. On the outcropping above the poacher camp, a younger white roebuck can be found, and observing him up close will sharpen Henry's survival skills. Once the poachers are dealt with, head to the structure in the middle of the camp to find the pelt in the chest there along with a map of local hunting spots.

Now you can choose whether to hand over the hide to the huntsman or the knacker. They will pay you the same base amount for the hide of 225 but the huntsman will give you additional rewards for the squirrel tails bringing his total reward to 450 .

Hand the hide over to whichever man you choose to end the quest.

## Thomlin Bruthans

Thomlin Bruthans is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Thomlin Bruthans, also called young Bruthans, ran a farm in Horschan and a fighting ring along with it. He was known as quite the fighter and used to wager a thunderstone he found from time to time. The stone came to him following a storm and he kept it as a good luck charm ever since.

Eventually, it was stolen from him by a couple of men from Raborsch, Peter and Hensel. He made himself a fake so no one would think anything had gone wrong.

When Henry came through Horschan he may have participated in the fights and come seeking the thunderstone for a woman called Kona whose husband had tried fighting Thomlin for the stone but lost.

Henry may also have fought Thomlin and been offered the fake, though it would be found out. Henry may then have recovered the stone and chosen to give it back to Thomlin.

## Thou art but dust…

Thou art but dust… is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. This quest can be unlocked following the completion of Speak of the Devil and can be completed concurrently with the task The Reliquary.

## Description

Morticius, an old and blind caretaker of the Sedletz ossuary, asked me to tidy up the long-neglected local chapel.

## Walkthrough

At the Sedletz Monastery graveyard, talk to a monk called Brother Morticius. You will know him, as he’ll be talking to himself in rhyme. He will ask you to tidy up the mortuary.

To do so you will have to interact with the piles of bones around the area to build three pyramids and then sweep up the remaining bones into a more orderly pile. There are a decent number of bones in the main room, but once you have swept those up, head over to the trap door in the middle of the room.

You will fall through into the lower level and be able to continue in your task.

Note: if you are also completing The Reliquary at the same time, you’ll want to look for the related tomb in this lower level.

To leave, there is a tunnel that will lead back up to the surface. Follow it to find that Brother Morticius is nowhere to be seen. Speak to the nearby grave digger and he’ll be dumbfounded you did all that work, saying that Brother Morticius died many years ago.

Your only reward is a some craftsmanship experience and the knowledge of a job well done.

Note: even if you have more bones than required, they will be automatically removed from your inventory once the pyramids are built.

## Tibor

Tibor is a young Romani man and the son of the leader of the nomads who recently made camp in the Trosky region.

## Biography

Tibor appeared to have a solid relationship with both his siblings, though Marika and Gejza were polar opposites. Tibor is close enough to his sister for her to express her desire to have a permanent home and not keep travelling (something their father couldn't understand), while also getting along with his more hot-headed brother.

Unlike his brother, Tibor was known to talk his way out of trouble, keeping himself calm during intense situations. This didn't stop him from trying to avenge his family's honour when his father was insulted by villagers in Semine after the voivode tried to push for Marika's boyfriend, Bohush, to marry his daughter or pay. Not realizing Bohush didn't send the insults, Tibor and Gejza went to confront the villagers. Unfortunately, things took a turn for the worse when they ran into some woodcutters and Bohush was stabbed, Gejza was killed, and Tibor was taken captive.

## To Dust you Shan't Return

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

To Dust You Shan't Return is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 4th or 5th quest in the Mysteria Ecclesiae DLC, as it is given concurrently with Seek and You Shall Find.

## Description

A fire broke out during the night. Two bodies were found in a burnt down building. But something’s not right here – the victims might have been more of the infected.

## Walkthrough

In the night, there was a fire and two men were found dead in the burnt building, though not apparently killed by fire. Signs of illness were found on the bodies, so the Abbot had them locked in the hops store. You want to look into it, so look into it you shall.

You’ll have three main things to do, search the are of the fire, examine the bodies, and talk to the lay brother who found them. You can do this in any order.

Sneak into the hops shed to find the bodies, you’ll have to pick a hard lock to get in or else find the keys on a guard. The best route to get there is from the adjoining garden, as there will be a guard posted at the closest entrance. Once inside, it’ll be considered a trespassing area. Examine the bodies in either order, passing skill checks varying from easy to very hard to go more in-depth. Neither man died from fire, but from the same illness. It seems that someone was trying to treat them but using unorthodox methods.

Note: for the achievement Stop Licking That!, taste the flour found in the hair of the younger man. This will induce food poisoning, so if you don't have one on you, run to the infirmary to grab a Digestive potion.

Check the lay brother dorms for Elijah and one of them will let you know he is not around, but is prone to disappearing from time to time. Another will mention having seen him by the cellar door looking hellish. Check the cellars and speak to him. He will be too drunk and distraught to talk at first. To sober him up hand over either a Hair o' the Dog or a Strong broth from the kitchens. He doesn’t know too much but it’s clear the dragging injuries the dead men sustained weren’t from him.

Head to what’s left of the shed, hop into the drainage ditch and to your left will be a torch – evidence of arson. Examine some remnants of clothing and a barrel full of oil to confirm your suspicions. Back where the torch is, you’ll see some drag marks that lead out of the flour store towards the same ditch where you found the torch. Follow it to find a cart hidden in rose bushes. Follow the tracks from the cart towards a locked gate, climb up into the nearby building to get to the other side. Keep following the tracks until you come to the herbalist’s house.

Inside, two men are arguing – Herbalist Joachim and Denes. You’ll have to fight Denes, though he shouldn’t be too difficult. Once he’s dead, go back inside and talk to the injured herbalist. On the orders of Zacharias, the herbalist has been trying alternative treatments to no avail.

Head back to the infirmary to confront Zacharias, ending the quest.

## Tobias 'Darling'

Tobias 'Darling' is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Tobias, called Darling by most, lived in Grund with his aunt and helped look after her horses and dogs. As a child, he fell off a rotten ladder and hit his head, after which he was apparently never quite the same.

In Horschan, he participated in a fighting ring run by Thomlin Bruthans, along with Tuma and Stanley. He didn’t like fighting, but felt he had to beat Stanley so that Stanley would leave him alone.

Stanley would often cause trouble with Darling, making fun of him and playing tricks on him. Even once lying to him about a drink to get him drunk and telling him to go into the water to catch the moon which he was told was a silver platter, nearly drowning in the process. Stanley would also come to Grund and scare the horses as well as beating Darling’s dog, Beda, and making the dog afraid of strangers.

Darling seemed to like Tuma, however, describing him as funny and kind.

He could fight Henry when Henry came through Horschan and, if fought, would later suggest that Henry throw a fight against him so that Stanley might leave him alone. Henry could then suggest to help train Darling instead and in turn Darling would teach him about the care of animals.

### Associated quests

- Fight Dirty

- A Moment of Fame

## Toledo steel sword

Toledo steel sword is a unique melee weapon and a quest item in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a shortsword.

Note: Toledo steel sword can be crafted.

## Description

A good blade of Toledo steel created from the broken sword of a dead hermit.

## Crafting

Main article: Sketch - The Hermit's Sword

- Ambrose's broken sword × 1

- Frankfurt steel × 1

- Scrap metal × 2

## Acquisition

- Finding materials for and crafting the Toledo steel sword is part of the side quest The Hermit.

- After giving the crafted sword to Blacksmith Radovan it becomes the Sword for young Lord Semine.

- If crafted after the Wedding, Radovan will send Henry to the Nomad's Camp to bring the sword to Tomcat, whom he had a bet with. The sword is handed over but can be pickpocketed afterwards.

## Torch/KCD2

KCD

KCD2

Torch is a weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is useful for lighting dark spaces and can be held in Henry's off-hand. With the perk Arm of Beowulf, Henry can hold a torch while using a longsword. Walking without a torch in a village or city can be punished as a crime.

## Description

May it be a light for you in dark places, when all other lights go out.

## Acquisition

### Sold by

No vendors sell this item

### Carried by

Almost every NPC will carry a torch in their inventory.

## Tournament longsword

Tournament longsword is a melee weapon in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, categorized as a longsword.

## Description

A longsword for swordmasters is a noble and damn dangerous weapon. Like the tongue of a viper, it can cut the thread of life in an instant. This blade is designed primarily for tournaments, but in a more fierce battle it could quickly come to naught.

## Acquisition

- The Tournament longsword is given to Henry as part of the Kuttenberg Tournament side quest.

## Tragedy in Danemark

Tragedy in Danemark is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

The Danemark Mill was occupied by a band of cutthroats. They slaughtered the hired hands and took miller Hermann’s family captive.

## Walkthrough

During Yackers 'n' Fash, agree to help Miller Hermann’s family to start this activity. They can be found in the loft where one of the patrolling bandits will stand guard.

Take out all the occupying bandits however you choose. Once they are dealt with, return to the miller and his family to get your reward. He will reward you with 150 groschen.

If you take too long, they will go to Maleshov stud farm and can be found there.

## Troskowitz

Troskowitz is a village in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, located at the foot of the Trosky Castle roughly in the centre of the Trosky region.

As the largest settlement in the region after Trosky itself, Troskowitz functions as the administrative centre for the common folk and the seat of the region's bailiff, where the Rathaus is located.

## Description

The first mention of Troskowitz is found in 1388 in connection with the nearby castle, but the village probably existed long before that. The village got its name from the rock on which the castle was later built, as the rock resembled the ruins of a castle from a distance.

—Codex entry: Villages of the Trosky Region

## Layout

Troskowitz is built along a single main street, with the pillory standing at its centre. The village core is formed by the Troskowitz Rathaus, the residence of Bailiff Thrush. Adjacent stands the tavern, the main gathering place for villagers, and opposite it is the carpenter's workshop.

West of the Rathaus is Merchant Jurg Thömel's general store with a small field, while across from it lies Apothecary Emmerich's shop, identifiable by its herb garden. Nearby is the house of Drunkard Jezhek, the local cooper.

The eastern part of the village contains the craftsmen's workshops. Tailor Bartoshek's shop stands directly east of the pillory, while Woodcutter Dushko occupies a fenced plot on slightly raised ground with a path leading toward the forest. Butcher Bashka's shop lies along a side road at the edge of the village, with a small pond situated just west of his house and used by locals for laundry.

Several farms and homes are scattered around the settlement, including Landowner Jakesh's farm on the southern edge. A small stream runs through the village, separating some properties and supplying nearby fields.

## Trosky Castle

Tosky Castle is Otto von Bergow's residence and seat of power in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Codex Entry

Trosky Castle was built around 1380 by Čeněk of Vartenberk between two basalt rock formations of a long-extinct volcano. The castle derived its name from the shape of the rock, which resembled the ruins of a collapsed castle.

After Čeněk's death, the castle passed to King Wenceslas IV, from whom it was acquired by Otto von Bergow, who is listed as the owner since 1399.

Structurally, the castle consists of two landmarks still standing today: the Crone tower, and the Maiden tower. Between them lies an elongated castle core with two palaces, transitioning into a fortified outer bailey on the northern side. The entire castle is rugged and complex, traversing it requires covering a long distance with elevation changes.

Neither of the entrance gates were protected by moat - it was not necessary, given the other defenses. The gate leads to the eastern part, where the three-story residential palace once stood. On the western side there was a second palace primarily built of wood. On its ground floor was a forge, which was in use until 17th century.

Today the castle is accessible from spring to autumn and is one of the most visited ruins in Bohemia. The ramparts and the gate have been restored and the lower tower has a viewing platform open to the public with far-reaching view of the entire Bohemian Paradise region.

## Trosky region

The Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is one of the game's two primary explorable areas. Out in the countryside, it is made of a network of small villages, rolling hills, and wild forests.

## Codex entry

An area, also known as Bohemian Paradise, about 90 km north-east of Prague with a great number of natural and cultural monuments. The main landmarks of the region are Kozákov Mountain and Trosky Castle, while other important sites include, for example, the Prachov and Klokoči rock formations, the castles Kost, Waldstein and Sychrov, and a number of ponds.

Its picturesque landscape is mainly underscored by the ubiquitous sandstone rocks, characterised by their steep and rugged reliefs and towers.

It is an important protected landscape area and a popular destination for climbers. Nowadays the area is crisscrossed with a dense network of tourist trails, making it a haven for nature lovers and enthusiasts of historical landmarks.

In the medieval period the region was quite bustling, particularly due to the numerous castles, fortresses and fortifications, which are located almost literally on every hilltop.
