## Troubadours

This article is about the quest. For the perk in Kingdom Come: Deliverance, see Troubadour.

Troubadours is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Two lads from Zhelejov dream of being bards extolled throughout the land. But they need a helping hand…

## Walkthrough

At Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn, you'll eventually find two bards, George and Michael, arguing at a table. They apparently have rather ambitious dreams of making it big in Kuttenberg but without instruments, they can't do much. They'll then note how they heard the carpenter in Troskowitz is said to have a very nice lute just hanging in his home, but refuses to sell it. At this point, they'll ask if you can get it for them.

If you agree, there's a few ways you can go about getting the lute, though it can be tricky doing a full stealth route depending on the time of day.

- Convince the carpenter or his father to sell it

- Sneak in and steal it

- Sneak in and talk to the father and give him alcohol, leaving it unguarded to steal

Note that the lute is in an area where the father typically sits, with windows that the carpenter can typically see you through, so sneaking in to take it can be very tricky. Likewise, because of its high value, if you got seen sneaking about, even if they didn't see you take it, they'll quickly figure out you took the lute when they go to check if anything was stolen.

However you get the lute, bring it back only for another inn patron to accidentally break the strings, putting a dent in their plans once more. At this point, if you helped Vostatek already, you can mention that he owes you and seek his help. However, he doesn't have the required materials, but tells you how you can go about it (either buy from a butcher or kill a lot of game in the area to eventually find some). Once you have the sheep gut, bring them back and he'll make the lute strings for you.

Bring the repaired lute back and the two bards are all but set to go make their dreams a reality, but there's one additional snag: their bar tab. If you inquire further about it, they'll note how the innkeeper won't just let them pay even if they had the money, but rather wanted them to do certain labours around the place. Go talk to the barkeeper where you can either agree to do the tasks or convince him to let you pay so he can hire someone else to do them.

If you do the tasks, you'll have to carry 8 sacks by yourself and dig a hole for the outhouse. While you can try and get the bards to help, they will give excuses that they're artists and thus don't do manual labour. Otherwise, since you don't gain anything but getting dirty by doing the tasks, paying the innkeeper if you have money to spare is a better deal.

After you settle their tab, talk to them again and a cutscene plays out where they will sing a song to Henry with the lute. You can respond how you wish, but they'll be set in getting to Kuttenberg and the quest will complete.

## Truce

Truce is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You've helped the two quarreling villages reconcile. For now.

## Acquisition

While exploring the Trosky region, players may find themselves caught in a local land dispute between the villages of Tachov and Zhelejov. Both communities seek Henry's help to play a prank on the rival town, presenting a choice that affects the related side quests and the achievement tied to them.

There are two initial side quests connected to this conflict: Mice, which begins by speaking to Innkeeper Prochek in Tachov, and Frogs, which starts by talking to Old Olbram in Zhelejov. After finishing either or both quests, the final quest, Battle of Frogs and Mice, becomes available.

Instead of joining the escalating feud between the villages, you have to seek out Bailiff Thrush in Troskowitz and persuade him to intervene. This is the only way to bring about a peaceful resolution and help the two villages reconcile. This will require you to find truth about the disputed pasture. Report your findings to Thrush and complete the quest. He will then intervene and bring the feud to a final resolution.

## Tips

- If you move the nail marking the boundary anywhere other than the middle, the villages will not reconcile.

## True Cardinal

True Cardinal is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You made it through the church council without raising suspicion.

## Acquisition

In the main quest, The Italian Job, Henry and his allies infiltrate the Italian Court to steal Sigismund's silver reserves, aiming to cripple his ability to fund his army. The quest is divided into two parts: the first part follows Godwin attending the Church Council, and the second part involves Henry securing the perimeter and rescuing captive lords. For the purpose of unlocking the achievement, only the first part matters.

## Tips

The key to unlocking this achievement lies in how Godwin behaves during the Church Council. To ensure the achievement unlocks, follow these choices:

Approaching the Italian Court

- While walking toward the court, some traders will wave and try to talk to you - ignore them and continue walking.

- Two guards will greet you in Latin, return their greeting.

- After speaking to Jerome Naaz, he will say Henry looks familiar. Choose the "Evade" dialogue option.

- Follow Jerome as he escorts you to the court. During the conversation, select "Where are we going?"

- Just before entering, two guards wait - one is Italian and tries to greet you. Respond with "Obfuscate and move on." When Jerome asks if you want to proceed, select "Enter the council."

Inside the Council

- Select "Continue Formally."

- Select "The Pope has not reached a decision."

- You can now move freely. Speak immediately to Janosh Uher, who will share an idea and advise you not to get too drunk. Request more wine. To your right is a wine casket - drink three cups (!) to maintain a convincing level of intoxication without raising suspicion during Latin conversations.

- Approach Jerome and request more wine.

- (Optional) If Janosh calls you again while exploring, speak with him. He will suggest asking to meet the cook to assist Henry. Follow up by asking Jerome to arrange this meeting.

- (Optional) If you sided with Christian of Pisek earlier in the Via Argentum quest, you can speak to him about helping Henry. He will suggest asking Jerome for more guards. Then, request more guards from Jerome.

Speaking to Council Members

- To avoid difficult skill checks, select only the following dialogue options when interacting with factions and key NPCs.

- Approach the burghers on the right and ask for their opinion on the dispute.

- Speak with Albich of Uniczow (in green outfit). For the first option, reply "Remind me." End the conversation by asking his opinion.

- Talk to the Father Anthony from the Brotherhood (in black robes) and ask about their demands. Respond with "I understand." and then leave.

- Speak with Musa of Mali and ask for his opinion on the council.

- Approach the Abbot (in white robes) and ask about the monastery's demands. Respond with "I understand." and then leave.

Closing the Council Session

- Speak to Janosh and initiate the closing speech. When prompted, select "Musa is Right" / "Path towards reconciliation."

- When asked how the groups will reconcile, choose "You need to understand each other."

- After some back and forth, select "Calm down."

After completing the closing speech, the achievement will unlock.

## Tuma

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Tuma is the Semine guard commander in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

He is also one of the few in the area that can be asked if he's seen Hans, though he'll note he has no information regarding him.

## Biography

Tuma worked as commander of the guard at Semine fortress.

During the wedding between the Lord Semine's son Olda and Agnes Thrush, Tuma was ordered to watch the gate and chase away any beggars. Henry offered to help and Tuma suggested he bring food, as coin would only entice them to stay and ask for more. Once the beggars were dealt with, Tuma shared a toast with Henry to celebrate their success.

### Associated quests

- Wedding Crashers

- Necessary Evil (Optional)

## Tunnel in the cliffs

This page is still a stub and is in need of information. You can help us by expanding it. Click here to add more.

Tunnel in the cliffs is a minor location in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It's located in the southern part of the Apollonia region near an enemy camp. The tunnel has a few useful early start items, notably a kettle hat and dagger. A short distance away directly west in another arch-stone formation is also a Billhook and Bearded axe.

## Hidden treasure

A skeleton with two crossbow bolts in its torso can also be found sitting beneath a map carved in the tunnel wall. The map reveals the location of a hidden treasure chest, which can be found north of Trosky castle.

---

## Two Brothers

Two Brothers is a hidden achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You resolved things with Koniash without a fight.

## Acquisition

The Two Brothers achievement can be earned during the last quest in the Kuttenberg Sharpshooters questline (Two Brother's Archery Contest). Resolve the matters between Carpenter Raven and Koniash to obtain it.

## Tips

- During the conversation with Raven at his house outside the city walls, exhaust all dialogue options.

- Go to speak to Bailiff Andreas Plümel in the Rathaus (the building with the astronomical clock).

- There is no quest marker for him, and speaking with him is not highlighted in the quest objectives.

- Ask the dialogue option "Did you arrest Brada the bandit?" and exhaust all dialogue to obtain the letter that allows a peaceful resolution.

- DO NOT pick the option "I'm here to report the bandit Raven!"

- Meet Koniash at his camp in the following conversation, select "I know who turned Brada in!"

- The achievement will not unlock if you personally pay the debt, even though it resolves the situation peacefully.

## Ulrich Vavak

Sir Ulrich Vavak of Neuhaus (Czech: Oldřich Vavák z Hradce) is a wealthy nobleman and the royal Mint Master of Kuttenberg, appointed by King Sigismund.

## Biography

## Inventory

## Codex entry

Twice during his life, he was appointed Royal Mint Master, and after the outbreak of the Hussite uprising, he was one of the few representatives of the higher Czech nobility to join the rebels.

We know nothing about his life before the outbreak of the uprising, except that in the years 1402-1403 (or 1404), during King Wenceslas's absence from Bohemia, he held the office of Mint Master.

His later life is documented, during which he supported Jan Hus and complained to King Sigismund about his burning. He initiated the negotiations of the Four Articles of Prague (which defined the direction and demands of the uprising) and was elected as a representative of the nobility to the provisional government at the Congress of Tschaslau. He marched into battle alongside Jan Zizka, and in 1421, he became the Mint Master of Kuttenberg for the second time.

## Associated Quests

- Via Argentum

- Taking French Leave

- The King's Gambit

## Ulrich von Remold

Ulrich von Remold is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered at Camp by the road locations.

## Biography

Henry first encounters the German knight Ulrich von Remold camped alongside the road with an entourage of a man-at-arms and a hired hand. Despite a language barrier, Henry can speak to him and eventually suss out that von Remold would like to spar. If Henry wins, von Remold gives him the lore book "A Selection of Amorous Poetry" - a prize that amuses Henry.

If Henry has a high enough scholarship skill, he can attempt to communicate with Ulrich in German. The attempt pleases the knight and grants a small reputation increase, but otherwise has no affect on the overall conversation or sparring event.

## Undecided duel

Undecided duel is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A grievance between a mercenary and a townsman was to be settled by combat. In the end, they killed each other, leaving the winner of their duel undecided. They now lie with the rest of their village, partially obscured by long grass. From the goods on the mercenary, it seems likely the grievance was surrounding his appropriation of property.

## Under Pressure

Under Pressure is an achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You won three skirmishes while bleeding.

## Acquisition

To unlock this achievement, you must win three combat encounters while bleeding. These encounters do not have to be consecutive.

## Tips

- If Henry takes enough damage, a small blood drop icon will appear to the left of the Health and Stamina bars, indicating he is bleeding. The only way to stop the bleeding is by applying bandages.

- This achievement will likely unlock naturally during gameplay unless you are exceptionally skilled in combat. If so, allow yourself to take enough damage to start bleeding, then win three separate skirmishes before treating the wounds.

## Under a Brown Flag

Under a Brown Flag is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You hung used underwear on the tavern. Very used.

## Acquisition

This achievement is tied to the successful completion of the two side quests: Yackers 'n' Fash and Striped Tonies.

## Tips

- Begin by locating Foreman Vlach, who can be found at the Black Horse Tavern near the bathhouse during the evening hours, accompanied by his group of friends. Speak to him and agree to help recover their stang, which will initiate the side quest Yackers 'n' Fash.

- Once you retrieve the stang and return it to Vlach, the side quest will conclude. Afterwards, return to the same tavern in the evening to initiate the next quest, Striped Tonies.

- During Striped Tonies, you will be tasked with infiltrating the All Saints Pub and hanging a pair of braies on a pole as part of a prank.

To enter the pub stealthily:

- Approach the rear of the All Saints Tavern.

- Use the ladder to access the stock room.

- Inside the stock room, climb the second ladder to reach the attic.

- In the attic, interact with the stob to "hang up the braies."

Upon completing this objective, the achievement will unlock.

## Under the Straw Hat

Under the Straw Hat is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. It is only available during the side quest In Vino Veritas.

## Description

Work in the vineyard is hard and gruelling, mostly taking place in the scorching summer and for meagre pay. Not for the faint-hearted. But it gives me the opportunity to clear my mind and explore the places where the drink of kings is born.

## Walkthrough

After starting In Vino Veritas, head to the vineyard and speak to the guard at the gate. Let him know you are looking for employment and he will direct you to Jerome. Jerome will let you know what you will be expected to do and where you can sleep.

Starting first-thing in the morning at 6 a.m., you’ll have to work in the vineyard, collecting weeds and carrying sacks of collected weeds from across the vineyard to their proper dumping ground near where you sleep. There are five areas around the vineyard where sacks of collected weeds will appear, you can walk around from one to the next as part of your work.

You’ll have to keep doing this work for 12 in-game hours. You may be able to skip a little bit of time, but you run the risk of being seen slacking off.

At the end of the work day, report to Jerome. If you’ve done a good enough job he’ll not only pay you but ask you to get some wine from the cellar, allowing you entry where you can then steal an item associated with In Vino Veritas.

Either way, once you end the day and speak to Jerome the quest will complete or fail depending on the quality of your work.

## Under the bridge

Under the bridge is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The underside of bridges is often littered with trash and various cast-offs of the people who have walked over it. Below the covered bridge near the Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn is no exception to that rule, broken wheels, old pots, bits and bobs are scattered along the ground and over the stream.

Unusual, however, is the presence of a barrelfire and a man who lives there. He calls himself Karl von Unterbruck and he makes a living selling what he describes as ‘gifts from heaven’ – the very things travellers toss over the side of the bridge when wandering home inebriated after a long night of carousing.

## Resident

- Karl von Unterbruck

## Unmarked grave

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Sweet Virgin Mary… This must have been a pregnant woman.

—Henry's comment

Unmarked grave is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The unmarked grave can be found in the woods east of Vidlak Pond, at the center of a small glade. It appears clean and looked after, with a simple wooden cross marking the place. Beneath it lies the skeleton of a young pregnant woman, the remains of two unborn children still visible inside.

After the Lackey and Wedding Crashers quests, if Henry chooses to help Gamekeeper Vostatek and keep him sober during the Semine wedding, Vostatek eventually confesses that two winters prior, Otto von Bergow ordered the girl's death. She had been a servant at Trosky Castle and the lover of von Bergow's son, Jan. When it was discovered she was carrying Jan's bastard, von Bergow decided the matter needed to be handled discreetly and sent for his gamekeeper to take care of it.

Vostatek couldn't refuse an order from his lord, so he led the girl deep into the woods and killed her, burying her right there. She was no older than fifteen. Since then, he has been haunted by her memory, attempting to drown his guilt in alcohol: "She had hair like straw and blue eyes. I keep seeing her in my dreams."

## Unveiling

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Unveiling is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is the 10th and final quest in the Brushes with Death DLC.

## Description

Voyta looks more agitated than usual. That doesn’t bode well. He only needs the last figurines for the altar, which are being made by the Kuttenberg carpenters.

## Synopsis

Voyta is almost finished his altarpiece for Sedletz Monastery, all that’s left is the face of one saint and a few little details. Then he only needs to have it put together with the carpentry work and it will be complete. Speaking of those, Planck the carpenter should have been finished them long ago. Voyta thinks he should visit as soon as he’s feeling better and ask after them, but Henry offers to check on them in his stead.

Planck tries to blow Henry off, telling him to go back and let Voyta know he’ll send them over soon. When Henry offers to deliver them himself, Planck avoids the help which makes Henry suspicious. It turns out, the final figurine of the Virgin Mary has been stolen by the apprentice, Chrudrosh, who was meant to be working on it.

Planck thinks Chrudosh would have gone to sell it, as there’s a certain group which deals in such things lead by a man called Reaper. Planck has done work for them in the past making knock-off of various figures and tells Henry where he can find the usual drop-off point.

Henry follows the directions and finds Chrudosh tied to a tree in the bandits’ camp. The bandits, it seems, wanted to strong-arm him into joining them so they didn’t have to outsource their carving work. Henry is able to free Chrudosh and recover the figurine for the painter.

While Henry was away, Planck delivered the rest of the figurines and Voyta is grateful again for Henry’s help, saying he appreciates how Henry has been there for him, watching and judging him. It’s given him the opportunity for self-reflection.

This self-reflection, however, has lead to doubts. He is no longer sure why he is even trying to complete a masterwork, is it really for the dead Voyta’s memory? Or is it something the skull has planted in him? What if the Devil has been leading him? The Veles shrine, the basilisk egg, plotting Burkhard’s death, toying with Bellissimo – they all seem like infernal whisperings to him now. Everyone who has ever crossed his path, it seems, has ended up dead, insane, or forsaken by God.

Henry, however, proves to be an exception. The painter wants to ask him for one last piece of advice. His whole life and career have been coming to this moment, his grand work. If it truly has been the Devil leading his steps, should he even finish it?

Henry is able to convince him otherwise, that his work is a testament to his talent and love, so Voyta thanks him and asks that he sends for the people from the monastery. He works on the painting tirelessly from then until it is finished.

When Henry returns the next day with monks in tow, they approve of the work taking it to be assembled for the altar. With that, the work is done.

Voyta feels better, lighter, now that the work is completed and Henry was able to help him, giving him the confidence that God may still be giving him a chance. The voice has gone quiet for the time being, the painter says he can still sense something deep down, but for now it is silent.

As for what’s next in store? Voyta thinks he might travel, as that was always his most favourite part of being a painter. He wants to take inspiration from Henry and get out more, see more people, and live a little for himself.

With all said and done, Voyta has one final request of Henry – to take his painted skull and return it to its proper resting place, along the rest of the dead Voyta. Henry does as he asks, finally laying the dead Voyta to rest.

## Walkthrough

After completing Root of Evil talk to Voyta in his workshop to start the quest. He needs you to find the missing figurine for the altar for Sedletz.

You’ll find Carpenter Planck working in his workshop, he wears a pale yellow tunic and a brown bandana. Talk to him and let him know why you are there. Pass a skill check to get him to tell you right away or else beat him unarmed and wait until he wakes up when you can talk to him once more and then he will tell you.

Essentially, his apprentice Chrudosh stole the figurine and ran off with it. He’ll direct you to an abandoned shack in the woods between Maleshov and Danemark Mill. In the shack, you can find Crudosh’s chisel that you can let the dog smell. Follow the trail that leads out from behind the shack (Henry will comment on markers along the way) and eventually you’ll come to a bandit camp. The apprentice will be tied to a tree. You’ll have to free him to talk to him.

If you approach slowly, you can talk to the bandits when they warn you away and they will let you speak to their leader, Reaper. This will allow you to ransom Chrudosh for 750 .

Note: Taking out the bandits before speaking to Chrudosh may lock you out of the achievement All Fun and Games, as he might be too scared to talk to you.

Untie him and speak to him. It may be easier to approach at night, so the bandits are less likely to spot you. Once free, he will walk off, follow him until he stops and then speak to him. Exhaust all his dialogue and then he will direct you back to the camp, letting you know the figurine is in the chest near the fire pit.

The chest is hard locked, pick the lock and loot the Mother Mary statuette. If you need the key, you can pickpocket or loot it from the bandit leader. They are well-armed with high quality armour.

Before heading back to Voyta, go back to the place where you spoke with Carpenter Planck and speak to Journeyman Stihlau to unlock the achievement All Fun and Games.

Once that’s done, head back to Voyta’s workshop and speak to him. He’ll ask you whether he should complete the work or not. You have two options – convince him to finish or convince him to destroy the painting.

If you assure him the Devil isn’t leading him, he will complete the painting and then give you the dead Voyta’s skull which you can rebury for the achievement Rest in One Piece. To unlock it, travel back to Voyta’s grave and place the skull inside.

If you would rather he destroy the painting, pass a hard speech check to convince him to do so.

With that, the quest will end, ending the storyline and giving you the achievement Masterpiece.

## Urso von Morgenstern

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Urso von Morgenstern is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

### Early life

Urso was originally from Brunswick but lost considerable estates due to his relatives and battles in Eastern Prussia and afterwards led a small band of mercenaries.

In 1402, he fought in the Third Florentine–Milanese War on the Bolognese-Florentine side for Sir Muzio Sforza in northern Italy but ultimately ended up getting defeated by Alberico da Barbiano, who fought on the Milanese side.

Following his defeat, he moved to Kuttenberg and served King Sigismund but left his service due to the king's inability to pay them. Afterwards he entered the service of Vauquelin Brabant, whom he first met at the great tournament of Lorraine years prior.

### Involvement

Under Brabant’s employment, Urso and his men worked to support Zizka’s band, helping to steal a cannon from the Prague militia and make a raid on the village and adjoined fortress of Maleshov. He also provided reinforcements and helped carry the silver stolen from the Italian Court to Ruthard Palace to load it onto wagons.

Ultimately, Brabant’s plan was to have them take off with the silver and betray Zizka’s band. This ploy was found out, and a fight broke out in which Urso lost his life along with most of his other men.

### Associated Quests

- The Lion's Den

- Dancing with the Devil

- The Italian Job

## Vantage point

I have to admit, Trosky is a truly majestic castle.

—Henry's comment

Vantage point is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

The low cliff that offers a clear view on Trosky Castle and the surrounding landscape is located north of Semine Keep. A narrow path, winding through a field of valerian and thistle, leads to the point. Beneath a large tree stands a simple sitting log.

The area right below the cliff shows signs of struggle, with a patch of trampled earth, blood splattered on the rocks, and a pair of lost Farmer's horseshoes. It seems that some poor horse has been tortured there.

There is Mead as loot in the hollow tree trunk on top of the vantage point.

## Vasko

Vasko is a cuman in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Vasko's parents met on account of his father travelling a lot and eventually meeting a half-German, half-Czech woman. Together, the two had a son, Vasko, whom his mother made sure to teach Czech. The family took to travelling a lot and at one point ended up in Milan, Italy. While there, Vasko worked for a cloth trader, Muzzio, as a hired bodyguard/hitman for Muzzio's family and became smitten with Muzzio's niece, a woman named Julia. However, he didn't realize Julia had eyes on Muzzio's money. When Vasko finally learned of this and that others were trying to assist Julia to hurt her uncle, Vasko had no choice but to kill her to protect Muzzio. Despite doing this to protect his employer though, Muzzio didn't believe Vasko, leaving Vasko no option but to run away.

He then joined up with the army and at one point served under King Sigismund of Luxembourg, including taking part in the attack on Silver Skalitz. However, when the king's money started to dry up, Vasko and his group left and set off on their own. Ending up in the Trosky region where they camped alongside the Nomads there due to mutual issues with local prejudice and common understanding.

## Vauquelin Brabant

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Vaquelin Brabant is a major character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He is a braggadocio who is prone to embellishing his own reputation and involvement in his stories.

## Biography

### Early Life

Born in Brabant province, from which he got his name, Brabant claimed to come to wealth through an enterprise through which he made and sold copies of a dagger that he found following a famous duel between two knights. He also claimed to be responsible for a famous account of the event after he told the author of said account about it, though he was not upset at his story being published under another's name, as he said he was happy to help others come to success.

Later, he claimed to have become a knight following the battle of Arezzo where he allegedly single-handedly struck fear and confusion into the enemy Italian troops by ignoring the orders he'd been given and rushing directly into a head-on assault. He also claimed to have won a tactical victory for the French against the English when he accidentally set the French horses to stampede while fleeing in the night to "fetch reinforcements" which allowed the French army to retreat from an otherwise unmatched battle.

He also claimed to have saved the king of France from a medical emergency. When he arrived in court to tell the king of a victory, the king refused to see him, claiming a poor disposition. As Brabant knew his news would no doubt cheer up the king, he sneaked up the window to climb into the king's chambers where he found the king in the midst of a medical attack. Brabant was able to move him to a position which allowed recovery and for doing so earned a place at court.

His favour would not last forever, however, Brabant eventually lost favour due to a confluence of bad luck. He advised a prominent member of court to invest into maritime trade with Africa, but the ships were sunk and the influential lord lost his investment and his respect for Brabant. He also accidentally killed the horse of a prominent lady, having mistaken it for a white stag.

The loss of favour made him seek out other pastures. He then travelled for a while, in his own words gaining fame and fortune, eventually settling in Bohemia and buying the estate of Miskowitz and shares in silver mines. He led the defence during the siege of Kuttenberg, wanting to earn accolades and the respect of Wenceslas IV.

He claimed to have been sabotaged and undermined by the burghers of Kuttenberg who he saw as being too stupid and cowardly to put up a true defence. Although Kunzlin Ruthard's account was different, saying that Brabant's own poor strategy led to their defeat. Following the defeat, he found himself imprisoned in Maleshov.

### Involvement

While imprisoned at Maleshov, Brabant was joined in captivity by Hans Capon who had been taken hostage by von Bergow following the attack on Nebakov Fortress. The two spent some time together with hardly anyone else for company, exchanging stories and playing dice.

Sometime later, Henry sneaked into Maleshov to free Capon and thus inadvertently feed Brabant as well. Brabant was grateful for having been freed and came along with them to the Devil's Den, joining Zizka and the others.

He offered to gather mercenary troops for help with the subsequent attack on Maleshov to capture von Bergow. These troops answered to him specifically, and had previously been in the employ of Sigismund. At Maleshov, he manned the cannon with Kubyenka, as he claimed to have prior experience doing so. Their initial salvo missed, but the second hit its target, breaking the cannon in the process and causing temporary hearing damage to both men. When asked how he was doing, Brabant claimed his injuries were worse than they seemed and he in fact saved Kubyenka's life by pushing him out of the way to take the brunt of the blast.

After the Devil's Den was compromised, Brabant moved with the rest to Ruthard Palace where he could not resist boasting about his knowledge of the underground passages beneath Kuttenberg. When asked to put this knowledge to use, he refused, citing that he would be more useful in other pursuits.

With his command of the Italian language, Brabant was asked to teach a little to the less wordly members of the group chosen in preparation for infiltrating the Italian Court in place of the Cardinal Pozzo's retinue.

His mercenaries were assigned the role of carrying the silver from the court back to Ruthard Palace for transport.

He himself joined as one of the cardinal's guards. His role in the operation was to take out the men posted at the gate, which he refused to do. Instead, making Henry and Capon handle it. During the ensuing commotion, he slipped away.

As it turned out, Brabant had given secret orders to the mercenaries for them to take the silver and run. When Adder approached the wagons to celebrate a job well done, Brabant stabbed him, wounding him mortally, and attempted to run off with the silver. He revealed that it was him who had tipped off Erik as to the operation at the court, implying he had been a mole the entire time. Most of his mercenaries were killed, but he managed to escape empty handed.

Brabant then went to the Praguer forces and aided them in their attack on Suchdol. Following the wounding of Markvart von Aulitz and the departure of von Bergow, Brabant was de facto in charge of the forces.

Late into the siege, when Henry and Sam were sent to send word to Jobst of Moravia of their plight, Sam was captured and brought to Brabant. Henry may then have come looking for Sam and confronted him. Brabant begged Henry to spare him, mentioning that he would subsequently order the Prague forces to go easier on the besieged men.

### If Spared

Brabant immediately ran out of the building where Sam was being held and alerted the Praguer forces to Henry's presence in the camp. Fleeing himself if he was not caught and killed anyway.

## Vengeance Solves Nothing

Vengeance Solves Nothing is a hidden achievement introduced in Brushes with Death.

## Description

You let Burkhard live.

## Acquisition

To unlock the achievement during the Portrait in Red quest don't attack Burkhard. Steal the helmet off him instead.

## Tips

- At the start of the Portrait in Red quest, Henry volunteers to deal with Voyta's old acquaintance, Burkard the Bloody. Voyta asks him to bring back Burkard's helmet as proof. To get the achievement you have to bring the signature helmet without killing Burkhard.

- The tricky part is that if you try to knock him out or beat him up unarmed, he will die instantly instead of falling unconscious.

- To get the helmet, wait until everyone at the camp is asleep. Then, find Burkhard and his bunk - the helmet is usually in a nearby chest.

- The quest will not update at this point, but don't worry. Simply show the helmet to Voyta, then reload your save and deal with Burkhard. The bastard had it coming. And don't forget to collect the reward from Bailiff Thrush!

## Ventza

Ventza is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Most of Ventza's past isn't clear, though at one point he had met Gules and saved the nobleman in Kolin. Sometime later, Ventza and his cousin, Franzi, worked with Gules to see about stealing from Tachov's blacksmith. To do so, the cousins apprenticed to him and worked for about a month before they were sent with a loaded cart to take to a wedding in Semine.

However, they suddenly got the idea to try and take the goods for themselves, cutting out Gules. Gules learned of this though and managed to find the cart and cousins. Owing to Ventza having saved Gules' life though, Gules only had Franzi tied up while he confronted Ventza.

If The Jaunt is completed and Ventza surrenders:

Unfortunately for Gules and his men, the missing cart hadn't gone unnoticed and Jan Semine set out with Captain Gnarly and Henry to find it. The trio soon found and attacked Gules' bandit camp, taking Gules captive alongside the two cousins. The three were then taken to Semine, where their fates would be decided. Ventza can later be found hanged on a tree east of Semine, where his map may be looted from his body if it has not yet been obtained.

If The Jaunt is completed and Ventza is let go:

Alternatively Henry can let the crooked hired hand go. In exchange Ventza gives him a map to the loot Franzi skimmed off the cart before Gules had a chance to check it. It's up to Henry if he honors the deal or hauls him to Semine anyway.

## Via Argentum

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Via Argentum is the 17th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Who better to help free Capon than the former owner of the fortress where Capon is being held prisoner? But maybe he'll want something in return...

## Walkthrough

Approach Ruthard Palace for a cutscene, combat will initiate, so help take out the men in yellow. After being introduced to the Ruthards, there will be a few dialogue options only affecting reputation. As long as his rival Vavak is around, Kunzlin Ruthard won’t be able to help you free Hans Capon from Maleshov, so you’ll have to find a way to compromise him. There are rumours that Vavak has been making counterfeit money and embezzling silver. Thankfully, his steward, Christian of Pisek, Peter’s brother, hates Vavak as well and would be more than happy to help see his downfall.

### Talk to Christian

Christian of Pisek works at the Horschan mines and can be found there during the day at the estate between Horschan and Grund. He has nothing of note right now, but you could help him by investigating yourself. Follow Christian, he’ll lead you out around the estate building to a private spot where you can speak more candidly.

In order to crack the book cooking, Christian wants you to ask miners how much they mined on a given day – the feast of St. Petronilla. This way they can compare with what was written into the record. He’ll give you the option of a few different back stories, you can choose any one and be stuck with it as the miners will talk with each other too and find you out if your story changes.

### Investigate the Mines

Speak with the foreman of each of the three shifts. The working shift, Paul's will be down in the mines while the resting shifts, Frank's and Samko's, will be above-ground.

Samko isn’t feeling up to talking but he will offer a dice game. You can pass a medium speech or easy intimidation check to get him to speak right away. Otherwise, you can bribe him for 200 groschen or beat him in a game of dice. No matter what method you choose, he’ll tell you the amount they mined – 34 corves.

Head into the mines. The paths are more linear than they seem. You’ll find Paul praying, mourning the loss of a young miner on the very day you want to ask about. Offer condolences and pray with him then he’ll be willing to answer your questions and tell you the amount his group mined that day – 30 corves.

Frank will be in or outside the mine depending on the time of day. If he is asleep, he won’t talk to you, so you may have to wait. Frank will answer most of your questions, if unhelpfully, but he won’t initially be willing to give you the details you actually need. To get him to talk you can pass a medium check based on the story you gave or an easy intimidation check. Otherwise, he’ll request you get him some ale. He’ll direct you to an easy locked chest with 10 beers inside, get them for him. Once you have convinced him, he’ll tell you the amount his group mined – 36 corves.

Go back to Christian and let him know the numbers. The books are 10 short, meaning someone really is skimming off the top. To figure out more, you’ll have to speak to Chief Foreman Fett and Hermann the ore seller.

### Fett and Hermann

Hermann is usually right next to the mine estate building, so speak to him first. You’ll confront him immediately. Let him know he’s reporting false numbers and he’ll resist. To get him to fess up, pass a medium domination, medium speech, or easy intimidation check. He’ll tell you the plan was Fett’s idea and he’s pretty sure the smelters are in on it too, as no one blinked an eye at the ten missing corves – a much larger number than they usually take.

Fett will be wandering around the yards. Tell him it’s his error as he counts the ore. Then pass a medium speech, medium charisma, or easy presence check to get him to crack. He’ll insist he was also strong-armed into it by a stranger in Grund.

Now that you have their confessions, head back to Christian.

### Investigate the Smelter

All signs point to the smelters. You’ll have to convince the owner, Buresh, that you’re a nobleman interested in purchasing a smelter yourself in order to swindle him into giving your permission to look around the smelter itself. He is apparently quite paranoid and careful, you’ll have to dress to the nines. This means no armour and no weapons equipped. It is best to have clothing of gold quality and to make sure you are freshly bathed.

If you need to purchase clothes, head to Kuttenberg. Make sure you have a full set of charisma-heavy clothes to help. The set you wore to the Semine wedding should suffice, if you kept it. Otherwise, you’re looking for that level.

Talk to him and show interest in purchasing a smelter then ask all the questions you need. He will tell you they received ninety corves from Horschan and give you a letter of safe conduct to allow you access to the smelts.

The smelter itself can be identified by the large amount of smoke it puts off. In the yard, you can speak to some of the workers there and ask them about their jobs and if they’ve noticed any suspicious behaviour. They will direct you to Shima and the search radius will turn to a specific point directing you to him. On your way to see him, you can examine a pile of ore to which Henry will remark it must be the processed silver that goes missing.

Shima, if he’s in the yard, will immediately act suspicious and ask you to talk to him in a secluded place and to avoid the guards. Follow him if need be. When you get to talk to him, tell him you know silver is going missing then pass a medium speech, easy craftsmanship, medium charisma, or easy intimidation check to get him to tell you more. He’ll tell you it points to the head smelter Volkmar, as he is the only one among them who handles the bars once they are smelted.

### Talk to Volkmar

Before going to see Volkmar, heed Shima’s advice and re-equip yourself with your best gear. He lives by the stud farm and can usually be found leaning against the adjoining house. As soon as you talk to him, he’ll try to initiate combat with a few of his underlings. To avoid combat, you'll have to pass a timed hard presence check to demand a one-on-one duel to make things easier.

If you are able to pass the check, you’ll be up against Little Nary. He is lightly armoured but strong, fighting with a mace. If you cannot pass the check, you’ll be up against him and two others. Once they are dealt with, you can speak with Volkmar.

Note: You do not have to kill Little Nary, you can knock him out instead. This avoids a "Congratulations, you killed a family man" dialogue later. If you want to do this make sure to avoid him after he wakes back up, since he will be hostile towards you and immediately initiate combat again.

He’ll pin the blame on Buresh; exhaust his dialogue and then take the map from him. You’ll have the option to kill him or set him free. Killing him will allow you to loot him, he keeps 253.1 groschen on him as well as some lockpicks. Setting him free will net you reputation and 100 groschen if you ask him to pay for the privilege.

### Find the Secret Mint

The map points to the abandoned shafts east of Grund. As you approach, the area will be indicated as private and guards will be posted. You can circumvent them, as the entrance you are looking for can be found south. You’re looking for a hole, essentially, a shaft with a ladder leading down to it. As you approach, you’ll see a horse called Agro.

Enter the secret mint, as the horse at the top implies, you will not be alone there. You’ll come across Buresh and his men. In order to avoid fighting them, you’ll have to accept a bribe. He will offer you an array of bribes to choose from, the largest you can accept is labelled "large" he will refuse the very large one. Note that you can do so and still take out the guards, luring them away by trespassing and walking further into the old shaft can make taking them out easier, depending on the time of day they may go to sleep after you leave as well.

Otherwise, you can circumvent the room with Buresh in it by going through the adjoining tunnels. Behind the main room you’ll find a medium locked door with a couple of minters behind it. They’ll tell you the evidence you need is in a chest in the room with them, but only Buresh has the key. Thankfully for you, the chest is only locked by a medium lock. The key can be found on the table in the room where you met Buresh initially, if needed. They will also give you a Minting die if you ask about the operation which will allow you to continue it later.

Pass a medium presence or charisma check and the minters will ask you to free them. If you’ve already taken care of the guards, they’ll leave right away. Talk to them after dealing with the guards and they will thank you, giving reputation, and will leave.

Once you have the evidence, you can head back to Christian to wrap up the investigation. Hand over all the evidence, including the die you got from the minters, and he’ll suggest you keep the operation going. If you agree to do so, he’ll pay you 625 groschen. Refusing to help will only lose you that money and some reputation. Either way, once you decide what to do, the quest will end, automatically starting the next Taking French Leave.

## Victimised

Victimised is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. It is available following Damsel in Distress and Taking French Leave.

## Description

I met a vagrant named Margaret, who had it in for some bastard in Kuttenberg. I’ll try to help her and maybe I’ll get something out of it.

## Walkthrough

Talk to Innkeeper Wolfram Raus to get the tip for the quest, then go talk to Margaret who is standing around the same inn. She needs your help pulling off a blackmail scheme to get back at a rich burgher who allegedly poisoned his wife. You have the option to give her 1000 groschen, but this will bypass the quest.

Agree to help and she’ll tell you what you’ll need to pull it off. She needs a nice outfit for you and herself and a strong sleeping potion to make the burgher forget what transpired so you can convince him he slept with her. She will also give you her mother’s ring as proof she won’t just cut out on you.

### Sleeping Potion

The sleeping potion you’ll need is Lullaby. You can either brew or purchase one if you don’t have one already. Regular strength will do.

Main article: Recipe for Lullaby potion

- Herb Paris × 1

- Poppy × 1

- Thistle × 1

### Outfit for Margaret

Any high-quality women’s dress will do. These can be purchased from tailors or robbed from rich houses at night.

### Outfit for Henry

High charisma clothing is required, no armour. If you still have your outfit from the Semine wedding that should do. Otherwise, purchase or steal an outfit of that calibre. If you are unsure, you can talk to Margaret and she will let you know when your outfit is up to snuff.

Note: Be careful if stealing clothing, you should wait until it loses its stolen tag, as many of the city's merchants frequent the tavern and will notice if you are wearing their stolen merchandise.

### Put the plan into action

Margaret will suggest the two of you meet up in Kuttenberg after arriving separately. You’ll find her across from the fisherman in the evening, near the Garden of Eden point of interest. If you head there too early, you’ll be able to wait there automatically by interacting with the bench. She will then talk you through the next stage of the plan.

Your mark, the tailor Latsek, will be spending the evening at the Hangman’s Halter. Go there and you’ll find him sitting near a window. In order to convince him to drink with you you’ll have to pass a hard charisma, medium craftsmanship, or medium warfare check.

He will then get up to take a piss at which point you’ll be able to slip the Lullaby into his drink. Make sure he has walked away before you do, as the quest will fail if he spots you. Then just wait until he returns and talk to him. Keep talking to him and he’ll head out to get some fresh air, follow him and he’ll pass out just outside the tavern’s yard.

Pick him up and carry him over to Margaret. Drop him inside the building and then talk to Margaret. She’ll suggest you wait until morning and then return to divvy up the money. Take a nap and you’ll wake to a shout. Head over to the loft. It turns out, Latsek hit Margaret and ran off.

She’ll suggest taking things to him immediately, with you playing witness to his actions that he surely won’t remember anyway. Follow her and talk to her along the way. She’ll insist that you leave all the talking to her. You can do so, and she’ll successfully extort the money out of Latsek. If you speak up, it will cause issues. You can extort Margaret back with an easy intimidation check.

Once that’s done, follow Margaret again to head back to the loft. Talk to her on the way back and she’ll mention a motive that seems less self-less than she initially implied to you. Once back at the hayloft, talk to her once more and she’ll suggest paying you back with a roll in the hay.

Kissing her will lead to her stealing one fifth of your total groschen. Divvying up the money will give you the choice to give her all of it, take half as agreed upon, or take only a quarter.

Alternatively, if you speak up during the confrontation (especially during the second chance to respond), you will discover that Margaret lied to you from the beginning and Latsek is an innocent man. She will even threaten you with false accusations and play the victim. You can use the intimidation check to make her return the money back to the Latsek. After that she will run away. If you will follow her, she will go through the town around the Hole in the Wall and out of town behind the map boundary. If you manage to kill her during this journey, Henry will mention it to Latsek when you eventually go to him to apologize.

## Vidlak Pond

Vidlak Pond is a waterside location with a fast travel point in the Trosky region of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

It forms part of the interconnected pond system situated in the valley below Trosky Castle.

## Description

Vidlak is located near the center of a pond system, surrounded by hills and sandstone outcrops, with areas of boggy terrain in the vicinity. The pond is fed by several rivulets and springs, and its outflow runs southward through the lowlands. A wooden bridge crosses the outflow stream to the southeast, providing access through the valley.

Three cabins are situated along the shoreline. On the eastern shore, above the waterline, is the gamekeeper's lodge, the residence of Gamekeeper Vostatek and his family. The structure is built into a rocky slope, overlooks the pond, and is connected to the valley by a narrow footpath.

On the western shore are two timber dwellings: the house of Tanner Benesh and Kvyetoslava, accompanied by a tannery yard, and a small hut occupied by the local fisherman and his wife. The two dwellings are separated by a wooden bridge and a horse pasture.

## Residents

- Gamekeeper Vostatek

- Huntsman's son Vitek

- Kvyetoslava

- Tanner Benesh

- Vidlak fisherman

- Vidlak fisherman's wife

- Vidlak stranger

- Zlata

- Hide'n'hair

- Pike

## Amenities

- Archery range

- Bowyer

- Bee hive × 2

- Drying rack

- Fish trap × 5

- Grindstone

- Laundry

- Lodgings

- Tanner

- Smokehouse

## Real-life counterpart

The in-game location is modeled after a real pond in the Bohemian Paradise region of the Czech Republic, situated in the Podtrosecké Valley beneath the ruins of Trosky Castle. Covering an area of approximately 3.1 hectares, it borders a 3.8-hectare peat bog. The site lies within the Podtrosecká údolí nature reserve, established in 1999 to protect valuable wetland habitats and rare plant and animal species.

The pond, created in the 16th century from former wetlands fed by the Jordánka and Žehrovka streams, forms part of a network that includes Věžák, Nebák, Krčák, Hrůdka, Rokytnický, Dolský, and Podsemínský ponds. Historically, these ponds were developed as fishponds during the medieval and early modern periods to support local agriculture, with management practices involving water level regulation and wetland upkeep. Over time, traditional use declined, and the area became valued for its landscape and ecological significance, leading to its current protected status.

## Trivia

- In the game, the area west of the bridge is depicted as a horse pasture. In reality, this spot serves as a small parking lot for visitors, with a kiosk and seating nearby. The bridge itself is based on a partially reconstructed dam that spans the pond's southern outlet.

- At the southern end of the dam, a famous scene from the 1978 Czech film How to Get Dad Into Reform School was filmed. In this scene, the character of the postman, portrayed by actor Petr Nárožný, drives into the pond. This moment has become a memorable part of Czech cinematic history.

## Vitek

Vitek is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Vitek lived and worked in Bohunowitz with his father, Willow, and his mother. He was sweet on a local woman, Sovka, who was daughter of the village elder, Bynyek.

He was frustrated with the constant requisitioning of supplies from his village by the nearby soldiers in the service of Sigismund. To prevent them from wringing the village dry, Vitek spearheaded an attempt to kill a couple of soldiers when they came to tell the villagers to prepare supplies. He was grievously injured in the attempt, and brought back to his family's house to be treated.

To cover up the crime, when interrogated as to the source of his injuries, he told Henry that the soldiers he killed tried to assault his sweetheart, Sovka, and he killed them to protect her. This was corroborated by his father, but not by Sovka herself, who mentioned that it was premeditated.

## Voice of the Bell

Voice of the Bell is a hidden achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

Thanks to your generosity Old Kutna gained a new bell.

## Acquisition

The Voice of the Bell achievement is can be obtained during the Alms repeatable task in the Old Kutna.

- Talk to Father Marian and donate 2,000 Groschen for the church bell repair.

- Wait at least 3 in-game days for the repairs to be finished.

- Return to Old Kutna around noon and wait for the bell to ring.

- It usually occurs within the one-hour window from 11:30 to 12:30.

- When the bell rings, the "Look at the bell" prompt will appear. Use it to unlock the achievement.

## Tips

- The relevant task will become available only after completing the side quest The Mouth of Hell.

- Donating the lesser sum might work, but this has not been confirmed.[testing needed]

## Von Bergow's ambushed men

Von Bergow's ambushed men is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

Bandits in the area have been very active, especially targeting the local lord Otto von Bergow's men. One such ambush happened here, what appears to have been a trap sprung on a patrol as they went through the gully near Nebakov Mill.

The remains of three soldiers, along with their horses lay out in the open, riddled with arrows. One horse survived, and is grazing nearby for lack of a rider. Despite the usual motive of banditry, none of the men have been looted.

## Vuytek

Women don't want me… To… my friends I'm a joke… All that's left… is the booze. Booze… never lets you down.

Vuytek (Czech: Vůjtek) lives in Troskowitz with his parents, Apothecary Emmerich and Gerda, and his brother, Heinrich. He has a reputation as a not particularly bright troublemaker.

He is usually found working in the apothecary's yard or sitting on the bench facing the village pillory.

## Biography

### Early life

Sometime in the past, his family moved from the city (presumably Kuttenberg) after his mother inherited a house from her relatives. Since then, they have been living in Troskowitz, where Vuytek and Heinrich help their father run the apothecary's shop.

### Involvement

Henry first has a chance to encounter Vuytek after serving his time in the Troskowitz pillory. A band of Cumans arrives at the village tavern, much to the displeasure of the locals. Vuytek is the loudest among them, and after a while his patience runs thin. He instigates a fight, during which Henry can choose to support Vuytek or the Cuman leader Vasko.

After the brawl, he asks Henry to make sure the Cumans never return to Troskowitz. He becomes angry if Henry lets them go easily, but rewards him with some coin if Henry convinces him they were dealt with for good, though he does not care to hear the gory details.

At the Semine wedding, he disastrously tries to woo Myshka, the cook's daughter, to the amusement of his friends Svatya Thrush and Vitek. The girl is unimpressed with his attempts at poetry, and the pair talk Henry into trying to do better than Vuytek. Henry can instead win her favour by not doing that and telling Vuytek to bugger off instead.

If Henry does attempt to woo Myshka, he may either make a fool of himself in front of both of them, or piss Vuytek off enough to be challenged to a to a fistfight, with Myshka leaving in the meantime. Afterward, Captain Gnarly calls them both morons and points out that Myshka is not interested in either of them. Either way, Vuytek is furious at Henry for ruining his chances with Myshka, and he storms off to drown his sorrows in alcohol.

In the evening, barely able to stand, Vuytek stumbles into the hayloft where Henry, Hans Capon and Enneleyn are arguing and begins raising hell. He had apparently tried his chances with her, but she quickly found more pleasant company in a nobleman. Dejected and angry, Vuytek attempts to start another fight. If Henry convinces him to drop it, he slinks away even more miserable than before. Otherwise, the fight still doesn’t happens, as Vuytek doubles down to throw up in the next moment.

After the wedding ceremony, in search of more drink, Vuytek barges in on Henry while he is trying to comfort an upset Agnes. Drunk, he assumes Henry is making advances on the bride, drags him out and prepares to smash his teeth in, until Capon knocks him down. Thus begins the infamous brawl still talked about around the region. The brawl is interrupted by Chamberlain Ulrich with the guards in tow, who drag all three, Henry, Hans and Vuytek, in chains to Trosky Castle.

The next morning, Vuytek, like Henry, is made to work off the debt for the trouble he caused. Instead of hauling sacks, however, Henry soon finds him chatting up Magda, the local bathmaid. Vuytek boasts and embellishes the events of the wedding, as well as his reason for being at the castle. When Magda remarks that she has not seen him around before, he claims to be helping his "uncle," Blacksmith Osina, run the workshop. Whether Henry exposes the lie or takes pity on him, he ultimately tells Vuytek to stop idling and get back to work.

Eventually, he works off his punishment and returns home to Troskowitz.

### Related quests

- Invaders

- Wedding Crashers

- For Whom the Bell Tolls

## Warding Off Evil

Warding Off Evil is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region. This quest can be started by speaking with Johann Parler, who can usually be found on the upper floors of the Emperor Charles Tavern.

## Description

Builder Johann Parler is working on the Church of Saint Barbara, and he wants to protect the building form fire and lightning with a bit of magic. He couldn’t get his hands on a magical talisman or thunderstone anywhere, so he wants me to steal three protective talismans from Kuttenberg burghers, to melt them down, and forge a protective axe out of them to get rid of my evidence.

## Walkthrough

Johann Parler seeks help crafting a protective charm to ward off evil in the city. He requests your aid in collecting several specific warding items scattered throughout Kuttenberg.

### Starting the Quest

To begin, find Johann Parler at the Emperor Charles Tavern and agree to assist him in his superstitious task.

### Acquiring the Warding Items

Johann asks you to collect three unique items used in local protective rituals:

- Nail – Located in the upper floors of a house north of the Tavern. The nail can be found on a desk in the rafters. Enter quietly at night for easier access and to avoid suspicion.

- Horseshoe – Found above the doorframe in the tailor's home, just south of the Fountain on Kuttenberg's west side. Enter the first door, then look to your left at the top of the frame.

- Coin – Hidden in the basement of the Hangman’s Halter Tavern in the eastern district. Interact with the exposed bricks on the right to discover the coin.

Stealth is highly recommended—if you are caught or wait too long, city guards may confiscate your stolen items.

### Forging the Protective Axe

Once all three items are obtained, proceed to the nearest anvil. Use the items to craft the Protective Axe as requested by Johann.

### Alternative Solutions

If you possess a Thunderstone (from the side quest The Thunderstone), you may immediately offer it to Johann to complete the quest. This will skip the collection phase and count as a valid ritual object. You can also reclaim the thunderstone afterward via pickpocketing.

Alternatively, you may craft a regular Work axe and attempt to convince Johann that it is made from the proper ritual parts. With a successful speech check or persuasion, he will accept the axe and the quest will be completed.

## Warlock's Riddle

Warlock's Riddle is a hidden achievement introduced in Legacy of the Forge.

## Description

You cracked the riddle of the lost alchemist.

## Acquisition

The Warlock's Riddle achievement can only be earned during the activity In the Service of the Guild – Warlock's Riddle, which is assigned by Bushek the Elder rather than Klaus Eichner like most other Investigation activities. In this task, he asks you to deliver an item to an alchemist while also collecting payment for it.

## Tips

- Follow the objective marker to the inn on the western road leading to Kuttenberg.

- Once there, attempt to open the door and then kick it in when prompted.

- Search the room thoroughly, especially the book and the Strange Riddle parchment on the shelf to the left of the door.

- To solve the riddle, head to the crossroads slightly east of the tavern, near a tree. There is a shrine there; the alchemist's payment can be found behind it.

- Return to Master Bushek and select the following dialogue options:

- "I didn't find the alchemist."

- "I don't want anything." - Not required for this trophy, but this choice is a confirmed method to obtain the Sketch for armourer V needed for the Innovator achievement.

## Water goblin's hut

This place would be great for a water goblin!

—Henry's comment

Water goblin's hut is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

This place is, according to local legend, the home of the water goblin said to dwell in the Trosky region.

You can overhear tales and rumors about the water goblin from two sources - from Zdenyek the Mouth in Tachov or from Innkeeper Lawrence at the Zhelejov Wagoners' Inn.

The hut is located on the northern shore of Rocktower pond, partially submerged and overgrown. A path from the main road west of the pond leads toward the shoreline, where the sunken shack can be found.

Inside the hut, there's an easy-locked chest that contains the Water goblin's hose, as well as a shelf and an underwater basket (with a rock on top) with minor loot.

## Loot

- Water goblin's hose

- Crayfish × 5

- Perch × 3

- Groschen × 143

## Water goblin's treasure

Water goblin's treasure is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

There is a hidden loot cache located on the southern bank of the Rocktower pond. It is tied to the local legend of the water goblin said to dwell in the region.

The treasure is hidden inside a small clay pot, resting at the water’s edge beneath a rocky outcrop and the large willow tree.

The Drowner's map, which leads to the loot can be found at the Bathing spot on the western shore of the pond.

## Loot

- Groschen × 125

## Weapon of Choice

Weapon of Choice is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You've defeated an enemy with every type of weapon.

## Acquisition

The game features a diverse arsenal of weapons, including swords, polearms, ranged weapons, and more. The weapons are categorized as follows:

- Swords: short swords, long swords, hunting swords, and sabres

- Heavy weapons: clubs, maces, axes, and warhammers

- Polearms: spears, halberds, glaives, and poleaxes

- Ranged weapons: bows, crossbows, and handgonnes

- Other weapons: daggers

Once a kill is registered with each weapon category, the achievement should unlock.

## Tips

- Only kills against legitimate hostile targets count toward the achievement, defeating non-hostile NPCs or civilians will not contribute to its progress.

## Codex entry

Weapons

Humans have been using weapons made of wood, stone, bone, and antlers since the Paleolithic era. Initially, due to the materials used, piercing weapons like spears, knives, and arrows were the most common. Later, with advancements in metalworking techniques, slashing weapons such as daggers, axes, and swords began to be produced. Besides these two traditional types, we also know of striking, throwing, hand-held firearms, artillery, and positional weapons. In the medieval period, spears, halberds, and crossbows were common. In villages, agricultural tools were often used as weapons. From the 14th century, cannons using gunpowder (known in China much earlier) started to be used in Europe, and firearms began to spread gradually. Records of the use of hand-held firearms in Bohemia date back to the reign of Wenceslas IV, with their use documented in 1398 during the siege of the archbishop's court in Kyje near Prague.

—Codex entry: Weapons/KCD2
