## Wedding Crashers

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Wedding Crashers is the 5th main quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

A grand wedding between Olda, son of Lord Semine, and Agnes, daughter of the Troskowitz Bailiff, is going to take place at Semine. This could be the perfect opportunity to meet Lord von Bergow. I need to gain entrance into the wedding party no matter what.

## Walkthrough

To attend with Miller Kreyzl, you will have to complete his side quests:

- Materia Prima

- Forbidden Fruit

- Opus Magnum

To attend with Blacksmith Radovan, you will have to complete his side quests:

- The Blacksmith's Son

- The Jaunt

- The Hermit

Note: both lines can be followed to the end without conflict. Only once they suggest you get ready to leave will you have to make the choice.

Pick which character you want to appear with (Radovan or Kreyzl/Enneleyn) and let them know you're ready. If you're not already appropriately dressed, they'll tell you to get dressed correctly before you can go. Keep in mind that due to certain actions you may take in this quest, you may want to stock up on Saviour Schnapps for any manual saves and a couple Hair o' the Dogs.

Regardless who you pick, you'll arrive at the wedding with them and can talk a bit at the gate, including asking if Otto von Bergow will be there. If you showed up with Kreyzl and Enneleyn (using the alias "Kvyeta of Kolin"), Ulrich will immediately take notice of her and tries to send you off, but the rest will convince Jan Semine to let you stay (unless you also completed The Jaunt, in which case Jan will welcome you without prompting). You can also offer to help Jan with the beggars but he'll wave this off (but will gain you some reputation for offering).

You'll be directed to talk to Svatya, but if you want to partake in all optional objectives going on here, it's best to get those started first as completing the main objective will move the quest/time forward and lock out some side objectives as time progresses.

### First Phase

Talk to Svatya

Svatya is hanging out with his close friend, Vitek. They'll talk to you for a bit until it becomes apparent they'd been trying to watch and listen to another friend, Vuytek, trying to woo an extremely unimpressed girl, Myshka, further off. The two friends will then bet on who's likely to have a better chance appealing to her: Henry or Vuytek.

Agreeing to the bet, approach the pair to see that Myshka has no interest in Vuytek. When you butt in, Vuytek won't like this, and Myshka will get annoyed when he tries to speak on her behalf. Instead of trying to butt heads with him directly, suggest you both leave her alone, which she'll approve of. She will tell Vuytek to sod off and suggest you follow her somewhere quieter.

She'll lead you out a side door, overlooking the small pond here, and talk to you about how annoying guys like Vuytek are when she attends weddings. She'll ask a bit about you, which you can indulge, before conversation turns to her asking if you'd like to dance, which you can agree to or not. If you go dance, there's one conversation prompt, but otherwise it goes well. Afterwards, go back to Svatya and Vitek and talk a bit, before the wedding goes into the next phase. This will also create an auto-save here.

### Second and Third Phase

Talk to Jan Semine

You'll now need to talk to Jan Semine, who is right inside the courtyard with all the food. Talk to him and he'll note it's not just the beggars he needs help with, but also Jurko and the rest of his Moravian relatives. Note completing each task here (regardless of order) progresses the wedding, so don't rush both until you've done all you wanted in each phase first.

Beggars

For the beggars, talk to Tuma near the gate. He doesn't mind giving out food, but the cook, Dorothy, is very stingy. While you can try and talk to Dorothy, she'll refuse to give anything, leaving you two options : sneak into the pantry when she's not looking to get the scraps or go around the wedding and gather up 40 pieces of food. Note also this number only counts food (not drinks) in your inventory that you brought along into the wedding, so if you want you can offer that as well when you have enough. The other option is to get the scraps from the pantry. For that, you need to lure her outside by taking all the food from a single table, after which you can go back to Dorothy, and tell her a table is empty, or get her daughter Myshka to distract her. She will leave the kitchen and you may go to the pantry to obtain the scraps, which are on the left. A third unmarked option is to choke her out so she won't witness you getting into the pantry. Give Tuma the scraps or 40 food items. Note, once you provide him the food, the wedding moves to the next phase.

The Moravians

Jurko is also in the courtyard, at the table at the far end. If you dealt with him prior, he'll give you a bit of a hard time, but no hard feelings and offers to drink with you. He'll then reveal that his group gets more rowdy when they don't have their drinks vs. not and asks you to try and recover their good stuff from the cellar. Note that doing this will cause some slight reputation loss with Semine later, but he'll reluctantly agree they have been behaving relatively well so it evens out.

The cellar is behind the closed door in the courtyard with a guard, though he won't stop you from entering. The guard inside, though, will cause you issues if you try and go into the next room. Instead, talk to him and either convince him to go get a drink or offer to bring him some. If you do the latter, make sure to grab several different varieties that are around at the wedding for him. Eventually, you'll be able to access the other area without issue, with the Moravian schnaps sitting on the table inside. If you told the guard you'd get him something with more kick, you can return to him and give him Schnapps to satisfy him. When you return to Jurko and give him the drinks, the wedding progresses to the next phase.

### Fourth Phase

What happens here depends on who you arrived with. With Radovan, he'll automatically approach you as he needs help finding the wedding present as it's gone missing. If you instead arrived with Kreyzl, Ulrich will approach you. Note also that you can go talk to Semine during this phase about completing the two requests for him. He'll be upset about giving booze to his relatives, but if you note it's better this way, he'll reluctantly agree. You may also act dumb and tell him you have no idea how they obtained their booze, and receive no reputation penalty.

Radovan route

Radovan will approach and tells you he's in a dire situation: the wedding gift has gone missing, so if not found, he'll likely not be able to work in the area again. Ask him about the details and he'll eventually note he saw someone in yellow acting suspiciously. You can bump into a hired hand near the dice tables, but it's not the right person. You can also run into Scribe Gaibl who will give you a Tin badge of defence, 48 and Courtier's boots. Meanwhile, head upstairs to the barn loft to find Hans Capon, dressed in his usual yellow, with Enneleyn. He'll reveal it was the bailiff's son, Svatya, that took the sword, but right then you'll be interrupted by a drunk Vuytek, still going on about everyone taking "his girl", in this case now referring to Enneleyn. Talk to him however you want, and once he's gone, continue to talk to Hans. You'll lose reputation here if you say you don't trust him.

Confront Svatya, who's standing near the wagon right outside the barn. With an easy speech check, he'll confess he took it and you can get him to reveal where he tossed it: right into the pond outside. Thankfully, he's not a very good thrower and the sword is right at the base of the steps going into the pond. Once you turn the sword in, this will move the wedding to the ceremony itself, so make sure you wrap up anything you want to do first. You can reveal it was Svatya or note it doesn't matter who stole it and Radovan will be fine with the answer, as he got the sword back.

Note that giving him the sword back will move into the wedding ceremony, so make sure you wrap up anything else you want to do first.

Kreyzl route

Ulrich will approach you, asking if you've seen Kvyeta, as she seems to have disappeared. Ask Ulrich for some information and he'll mention and describe some fella in yellow that sounds oddly familiar. You can bump into a hired hand dressed in yellow near the dice tables, but it's not the right person. You can also run into Scribe Gaibl who will give you a Tin badge of defence, 48 and Courtier's boots. Head upstairs to the barn loft to find Hans Capon with Enneleyn. Talk to them, but while in the middle of talking you'll be interrupted by a drunk Vuytek, still going on about everyone taking "his girl", in this case now referring to Enneleyn. Talk to him however you want, and once he's gone, continue to talk to Hans and Enneleyn. However, she refuses to go back to the chamberlain on account of what he asked her to do to him, though she won't divulge what it was. She'll then give you his ring so you can give it back to the chamberlain.

Head back to the chamberlain when ready to let him know the news. You can either try to pass a medium speech check here or give him the ring. If you give the ring back, you can either claim you don't know why or insinuate you know exactly why. The conversation will then turn to where von Bergow is and Ulrich will get disgruntled about this, leading to some reputation loss.

Note that once you let the chamberlain know about Kvyeta, this will move into the wedding ceremony, so make sure you wrap up anything else you want to do first.

### Wedding ceremony

A cutscene plays out, where Semine and Ulrich discuss where von Bergow is. They will conclude he's not going to show up and they go ahead with the ceremony. The wedding will take place, though some things seem a bit off. Afterwards, as there's no meeting with von Bergow, the only other thing you can do here is wrap up any last side objectives and give your congratulations to the newlyweds. However, they seem to have disappeared. You can ask around, but eventually you find that for some reason Olda left immediately after the wedding and Agnes is crying alone in the cellar.

Talk to her and you can get her to reveal Olda has been acting really strange: even before they got married, he'd disappear a lot at night, sometimes for days. This time, a messenger not bearing any noble's colours arrived, but he didn't tell her what it was about. Eventually she'll mention needing a drink, but no matter what you choose here, the game moves on to a cutscene where Vuytek comes in and mistakenly assumes you're trying to seduce Agnes. Vuytek will then kick you outside to beat you up in front of other guests. Hans will jump in to assist you as a brawl breaks out among the guests. Ulrich will eventually arrive with his guards to take control of the situation.

### Side objectives

Help Vostatek

If you saved Vostatek, he'll be here and happy to see you. However, he has a request: he needs help staying sober and so needs you to keep him from drinking throughout the wedding. If you agree, this will have three separate times as the wedding progresses where he needs to have any drinks taken away.

- During the second phase, he's at the fighting ring

- During the third phase, he'll be near the dice competition area, next to the stairs going up to the loft

- During the fourth phase, he'll be outside by the pond (same area you went with Myshka)

Right after the wedding ceremony, find him in the courtyard with all the food, where he's talking with his wife. He’ll thank you for keeping him sober and invite you to visit him at his family's cabin after the ceremony.

If you fail to keep him away from the drinks, you will find him sitting on a heap of waste next to the place where you saw Myshka and Vuytek. You may help him sober up a bit by giving him Strong broth, which can be found at the far table in the inner courtyard. If you can't find it, or you ate it, you might talk to Zlata and apologise for not managing to keep Vostatek sober. Either one of those outcomes unfortunately locks out the option for Vostatek to open up to you about his drinking problem later.

Dice

For the dice competition, head to the barn area and to the left you'll find Bailiff Thrush. Talk to him and he'll note the reward is a gold badge, but you have to first defeat 3 opponents:

- Radovan (gives Tin badge of might)

- Ulrich (gives Tin badge of headstart)

- Emmerich

The first two can be challenged immediately in the initial phase of the wedding celebrations, while Emmerich cannot as he's busy dancing with his wife. Keep in mind that losing won't cost money, but you'll have to take a drink, which can lead to getting too drunk if you're drinking already with other guests. When the second phase of the wedding starts, you can then challenge Emmerich, who reveals he actually lost his badge, so you won't need to beat him after all. Go let the bailiff know and he'll agree to then compete against you.

Once you beat the bailiff though, he reveals he doesn't have the badge: Betty won it off him, having goaded him into playing against her earlier, so you'll have to go play her if you want the badge. However, Betty won't part with it easily: even if you helped with the Cumans during Invaders, she'll require you to cough up 50 Groschen to bet with. Winning against her will get your bet back along with the Gold wedding badge.

Swordfighting

In the barn on the right side, you'll find Gnarly running the fighting competition. However, the competitors are in phases throughout the wedding so you can only fight one at each phase. Also bear in mind they're not easy: usually 1-2 hits by them and it's considered a loss, so you'll need to either make sure of saves or effective dodging/blocking tactics here if you want to win against all of them (rushing them with a blow to the head also works wonders).

You can also bet on some of the fights with Gnarly. It is based on RNG, not guaranteed, but the better odds in the first fight are for the merchant, Capon in the second, and the tailor in the third. Also, to boost your odds, see who’s more aggressive before you bet—watch who lands the first few hits, then place your wager.

- Olda (during initial wedding phase)

- Svatya Thrush (during second phase)

- Jan Semine (during third or fourth phase)

If you win against them all, Jan and Gnarly will give you the prize: Lord Semine's necklace.
If you win against some but not all, you will earn
If you lose all the bouts, you will earn 90

Dancing with Doubravka

During the initial phase, go to the area behind the wedding arch and a woman will call out for your attention. She would like someone to ask her daughter, Doubravka, to dance as she tends to be withdrawn so doesn't get any attention. However, you can press her for the truth where, if successful, she'll reveal her daughter is clumsy and really bad at dancing. If you wish, you can agree to dance with her. Her daughter is sitting nearby at the campfire, in purple.

Approach and you can either use a speech check (hard check to not worry about the others, or medium to convince her not to sit there). Otherwise, you'll need to drink to get her to agree. Getting her to agree, you'll dance with her, and while Henry will privately remark she is indeed clumsy/stepping on his feet, no injuries are obtained. At the end, you can try to lie that it was nice with a medium speech check, or note never again. If you lied, she'll take a liking to Henry and later during the wedding will try go get his attention about sleeping together. You can opt for this or pass a speech check to convince her you're not able to give her what she wants, which she'll take in stride. If you ignore her at this phase, the drink you may choose to accept from her later on will be drugged.

If things went well with the dance, you can talk to the mother again and she'll thank you, for some small reputation.

Other guests

While not side objectives, you can gain some small reputation if you helped the following prior to the wedding and then talk to them here (with the first three asking to drink with them):

- Gules

- Olbram

- Prochek

- Manka - during second phase, she'll be on the railing overlooking the pond, crying. You can talk to her and if you offer to dance, she'll decline but earn some small reputation with her.

### Interlude: Godwin

After the fight is broken up, you'll be introduced to and play as Godwin for a small portion. Hanush of Leipa and Radzig Kobyla have come to pay a visit to him, as Hans has still not returned from Trosky. Answer how you wish (some reputation is gained/lost here based on how you respond) before it cuts back to Henry and Hans, completing this quest.

## Well

Well is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. There are a total of three such points of interest in the base game and one in the Mysteria Ecclesiae expansion.

## Description

Around Trosky, a few wells have been set up by various people there.

### North-west of Vidlak Pond

Someone has built a little well using logs and stones to block the water at the spring. A little wooden boat floats in the still pool.

Loot

- Beer

- Crayfish

### South-west of Vidlak Pond

Along the road near where Vidlak pond splits in two, an old well of water has been maintained. A natural formation of rocks trapped water as it fell and that water now feeds a large tree. Next to the well is a pagan idol where locals leave offerings.

Loot

- Trout × 3

### Apollonia

At a small, nameless spring in the wilderness of Apollonia, fallen trees have created a small well. With a nearby bucket and cups, it seems that someone frequents this place to relax.

Loot

- Beer

- Mint

- Comfrey

### Gallery

### Sedletz Monastery

|

Hey another cistern. And I still don’t know where that water is coming from. Here in the middle of the monastery

|
- Henry's comment

Description

In the cloister of Sedletz Monastery, behind the large garden a stone fountain provides drinking water. Nearby drinking vessels both empty and full wait their turn.

Gallery

## Wenzel Torwart

Wenzel Torwart (Czech: Vencl Torwart) is a master apothecary from Turnau whom Henry can meet at various campsites scattered throughout the world.

He is accompanied by a hired hand, a soldier, and a fellow townsman.

## Biography

Wenzel had an establishment in Turnau, and was visiting his brother Oswald in Kuttenberg, but then got called away on a case. When asked about the details of the case, Wenzel will explain that a young woman was believed to be murdered only to leap off the mortuary table and flee. It turns out she was poisoned by a philandering nobleman so that she appeared dead. Hearing about the case will increase Henry's knowledge in alchemy.

## Widow Margaret

Widow Margaret (Czech: Vdova Markéta) is an old woman living in Troskowitz in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Margaret grew up around Troskowitz and was childhood friends with Jan. When she got together and married Vashek though, a friend of Jan's, Jan didn't handle this well as he'd been secretly in love with Marget. Things came to a head when Jan tried to ambush Vashek one day and as they fought, Jan suddenly slipped off the cliff they were on, falling to his death. Vashek informed Margaret what happened and the two kept quiet, so when Jan's body was found at the base of the cliff, everyone else thought he'd died by suicide, with only Jan's brother, Adam, suspecting otherwise. As such, Jan's body was buried outside of hallowed ground, as deaths by suicide were not allowed to enter heaven.

Over the years, Margaret and Vashek were constantly worried over Adam seeking out revenge, believing he'd one day appear to kill Vashek for it. 30 years after that eventful day though, Vashek had since passed on while Margaret lived out her years in the village, not realizing Adam had returned to the area under a different name and just wishing to live a secluded life.

If A Sinful Soul is completed:

She was later approached by Henry, who bore a message from Adam (now known as Ambrose): that Ambrose forgave her, but his brother should get what was rightfully his. Realizing this meant burying Jan's remains on hallowed ground, she got Henry to secretly assist in digging them up and burying them on Vashek's grave.

### Associated quest

- A Sinful Soul

## Wild woman

Poor woman… All beat up. What brute could do that to her?

—Henry's commentary

Wild woman (Czech: Divoženka) was once a hermit herbalist that lived in the hut tucked away among the rocks below Semine village, between the Rocktower and Lower Semine ponds.

## Involvement

People say the Divozhenka is a wild woman of the forest, a disfigured, ugly creature. You might come across one deep in the woods or hiding in caves, where they brew ointments and gather magical herbs. Some claim they bring harm, while others insist they offer help to those in need.

Henry first can hear about the Divozhenka from Betty, the innkeeper at the Troskowitz tavern. She says it's been a few years since the woman appeared in the area. For a time, the locals tolerated her, even visited her for magical salves and decoctions.

But gossip spread that she had bewitched a married man and seduced him, and just before the son of the local lord was to be wed. The villagers of Semine feared she might cast her spell on him as well, so they "took care of her." No one was ever punished for the murder of the poor woman.

## Wild woman's hut

So this is the divozhenka's shack. Why would anyone live like this? All alone.

—Henry's comment

Wild woman's hut is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

This is the place where the so-called Divozhenka of Semine, or "wild woman", once lived. The hut is tucked away among the rocks below Semine, between the Rocktower and Lower Semine ponds.

The hut itself is little more than a crude lean-to shelter made of tree branches. Inside, there's a rough pallet fashioned from vines, a basket of potions, and a sack filled with dried herbs. A simple shelf holds a small clay pot containing a bit of silver.

Outside the hut lies the body of a young woman, beaten and abandoned, left where she fell.

## Willow

Willow is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Willow lived and worked as a farmer in Bohunowitz alongside his wife and his son, Vitek.

Their village was close to Sigismund's camp and was, as such, often accosted by said soldiers and requisitioned for supplies often to the point of hunger.

One time, his son wanted to deal with the visiting soldiers to stop their exploitation. He lured the soldiers to a hayloft and attacked them, sustaining grievous injury himself in the process. Willow brought Vitek back to their home and set to treating him as best as could be done.

When Captain Puta and his men came by in the dead soldiers' wake, Willow tried to be cooperative and to obfuscate his son's injury. He told Henry that Vitek was injured by cutthroats on the way home from Kuttenberg, though he could not come up with a good reason as to why cutthroats would mug someone so close to a military encampment.

He may have cracked under pressure and told Henry more about not just his son, but the other villagers and where they were hiding their extra supplies.

### Associated Quest

- Spoils of War

Wine wagon is a point of interest in the Trosky region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

This wagon was ambushed, went over the road, and crashed spectacularly. It now sits next to the stream on its side and in pieces, its goods having been strewn about in the aftermath. Blood and wine both soak the ground, turning it red.

## Without Protection

Without Protection is a hidden achievement in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

You broke an enemy's shield.

## Acquisition

This is an achievement that requires to break an enemy's shield during combat. While it may seem difficult, this achievement is straightforward with the right setup.

You will need the following:

- A heavy weapon that deals blunt damage, such as a mace or warhammer.

- The Shieldbreaker perk from the Heavy Weapons skill tree.

To break a shield, target the side of the enemy where the shield is equipped. Avoid using combos - simply focus repeated strikes on the shield with your heavy weapon until it breaks. Small or worn shields are ideal targets, and bandits are usually the best enemies to farm this on.

Once the shield shatters, the achievement will unlock.

## Tips

- It's recommended to attempt this achievement in Kuttenberg, where enemies tend to be better suited for heavy bashing. In contrast, Trosky region features weaker opponents, making it easier to defeat them accidentally before their shield breaks.

## Woodcutters' camp with wolves

Woodcutters' camp with wolves is a point of interest in the Kuttenberg region in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Description

An unlucky group of woodcutters met with local wolves in the clearing the were making. Most of the cutters were killed, though they fought bravely. One escaped, at least for a while, leaving a trail of blood to a cabin further south outside of which three wolves still prowl, ready to defend their former home.

In the aftermath, even a pack of wild dogs has moved in to feed on the corpses.

## Wysoka

Wysoka (Czech: Vysoká) is a village located southeast of Suchdol.

## Codex entry

It is the hill where in 1142, a memorable battle took place between King Vladislav II and Prince Conrad of Znojmo, supported by rebellious nobility. The king suffered a great loss due to the treachery of his own people.

In the 13th century, an early Gothic church dedicated to the Visitation of the Virgin Mary was built on the hill, which has survived almost unchanged to the present day.

Today, at the summit, at an elevation of 471m above sea level, stands a lookout tower with a beautiful view of the surrounding area.

## X Marks the Spot

X Marks the Spot is a task in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. The option to talk to Krizhan is tipped by Innkeeper Wolfram Raus.

## Description

In Pschitoky I was able to get a treasure map from a hired hand named Krizhan. Perhaps it will lead me to riches.

## Walkthrough

In Pschitoky, talk to Krizhan. He is usually working on the construction there. Although he cannot hire Henry to help with the work, he has a map he found behind a wall in the cellar of the fortress that’s under construction. He can’t make heads or tails of it so he wants Henry to have it, but not for free.

Buy the map from him for 100 . It shows a location north-west of Sedletz Monastery, north of Kuttenberg. When you are in the right area, Henry will remark on it. The shaft you want is off to right of the path that runs through the area north-south.

There is a group of bandits already there that you’ll have to take out. Deal with them how you will, there are only a few of them. Once they are dealt with, head into the shaft where you will find two remaining bandits digging inside, including the leader.

Note: It is possible to spare the leader and talk to him, where he will tell you his group was camping here due to the very same map.

Loot the leader’s body to find an exact copy of the same map you just purchased. Go back to Pschitoky to confront Krizhan. Pass an easy speech or intimidation check to get him to crack and admit he forged the maps to make a quick buck on the side.

After hearing his story, you have the option to demand repayment or let him keep the money. Using the speech check and letting him keep the money will make him available as a skill teacher.

## Yackers 'n' Fash

Yackers 'n' Fash is a side quest in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II in the Kuttenberg region.

## Description

A few days before the renowned shooting competition, the miners from the St. Anthony pit lost their standard. The clues surrounding the theft lead to their competitors from the All Saints pit.

## Walkthrough

### Talk to Vlach

Head over to the Black Horse tavern in the evening and you will be flagged down by Foreman Vlach, a miner, who will explain the situation. The standard for his shaft has been stolen by another shaft's group and he needs you to help retrieve it. The group who stole it are called the All Saints and they spend their time in the cellar of their tavern.

### Infiltrate the All Saints

Head to the tavern. You have three ways into the basement: pass a speech check with the innkeeper, present the Player Mark (found in the outhouse out back) to get the key, or simply pick the lock and break in. Once there, head downstairs and talk to Jeorg Preng. Unfortunately, the Saints no longer have the standard, they sold it to a merchant called Hensel who was headed to Prague.

### Find the Standard

Hensel was heading to Prague by way of Bylany, a search area will appear on the road there after speaking to Preng.

At the southward facing crossroads, inspect a bloody sack. This will prompt a new search area, head down the road until you reach a puddle where Henry will spot some wagon tracks leading off the path. Follow them until you find an abandoned cart, this is close to the western edge of the search area, and Henry will remark that the robbers can’t be far.

There is a trail of blood you can follow to the west where you’ll happen upon a few wolves eating a corpse. Kill the wolves and inspect the body to identify it as the missing merchant, sans standard.

Head to the nearby mill. NPCs here will be hostile, so it may be best to opt for stealth. You’ll find the inhabitants replaced by bandits. In a shack by the northwestern gate, go up the ladder to find the surviving mill folks. Untie them and either let them run or offer to take out the bandits first.

Offering to help will start the activity Tragedy in Danemark.

The standard can be found in a hard locked chest in the mill itself, below the stairs, near where the bodies of the mill hands were placed.

### Return the standard

Head back to Kuttenberg and talk to Foreman Vlach. He’ll be quite happy with your service and reward you with 250 .

## Zacharias

Not to be confused with: Zacharias of Prachatitz

Ah, laudetur Jesus Christus! Here you are at last, I've been waiting for you!

Zacharias (Czech: Zachariáš) is a travelling occultist and a gambler Henry can encounter at one of the campsites scattered throughout the world.

## Involvement

Upon the first meeting Zacharias immediately claims that he has been waiting for Henry. Speaking in a combination of Czech, Latin, and Arabic, it can be surmised that he has been performing a ritual to summon the devil. Henry's arrival coincides with the ritual's conclusion, leading Zacharias to believe that Henry is a messenger from hell.

Zacharias angrily demands to play chess "again," referring to an alleged previous encounter with a "demonic entity" that did not provide him with the desired outcome. Henry declines to play chess, stating that he only plays dice.

Zacharias agrees to play Henry's game of choice and reacts the same regardless of the outcome, but is surprised when Henry invokes the name of Jesus Christ, which does not appear to disrupt his perception of Henry as a supernatural being.

He doesn't have a unique response in subsequent meetings, which implies that he keeps summoning supernatural forces over and over again, but only Henry appears.

## Inventory

Note: Character inventories are divided into Equipment, which includes items currently worn or actively used, and Possessions, which can be pickpocketed. Equipment is typically stored in the character's bedside chest overnight.

## Dialogue

## Trivia

- The Latin invocation "Exorcizo te, per Deum vivum, per Deum verum, per Deum sanctum…" is part of the exorcism prayer in the traditional Roman Rite used in the blessing of salt and holy water, which contains commands expelling evil and invoking God's power.

- More specifically, it comes from the Rituale Romanum, the collection of Catholic sacramentals and rites first published in the 16th century.

## Zacharias of Prachatitz

"Take heed, curious soul!" — This manuscript reveals SPOILERS from your journey ahead.

Zacharias of Prachatitz (Czech: Zachariáš z Prachatic) is a major character and main antagonist in the Mysteria Ecclesiae expansion of KCD2.

## Biography

Zacharias originated from the town of Prachatitz (Czech: Prachatice) in Southern Bohemia but he left for Prague to pursue medical studies. He once was a student of Albich of Uniczow and at the time of the events of the game worked as a personal physician of Sigismund of Luxembourg. As an important courtier, he was also assisted and protected by Denes Latzkfi, his bodyguard.

Despite being considered a friend by Albich, Zacharias harboured certain resentment towards his old teacher, feeling like he deserved more acknowledgement for his work and wisdom that he got. This can be seen in the resentment which Zacharias has for Abbot Jan who waits for Albich's input about the illness rather than believing Zacharias' assessment.

While in Sigismund's services, Zacharias once managed to save the king's life by preventing him from drinking poisoned wine (which had suspicious color). The king, realizing that Zacharias knew a lot about poisons, started using him to get rid of his enemies, which Zacharias reluctantly agreed to do in fear of losing the king's favour.
Sigismund had, however, grown impatient with Zacharias when the latter seemed unable to help him with his big problem - infertility. After failing to help the king with this problem medically, both the King and Zacharias turned to religious relics for help. When the family of Boleslav Bavor asked the king to sponsor their search for their ancestor's grave (where a relic from the Holy Land was supposed to be hidden), the king turned them down, hoping to secure the relic for himself. Zacharias found the biography of Boleslav Bavor in Buda, where Bavor stopped on his return from the Holy Land and had his adventures penned down. Armed with this knowledge, Zacharias accompanied King Sigismund on his campaign to Bohemia to find Bavor's grave with the relic in an attempt to secure the king's fading favour.

In Sedletz, he paid workmen repairing the crypt to look through the graves there. However, when two of them got sick, he was scared of reprocussions for the grave opening and robbing and decided to keep their illnesses a secret. He forced Herbalist Joachim to take the sick men in and attempt to heal them. In the meantime, however, the illness spread throughout the monastery, forcing a lockdown. Zacharias' former teacher Albich, who happened to be at the monastery at the time to help locate and cure the mysterious disease, had with him the medical records of King Wenceslas IV which Zacharias was desperate to get his hands on, since they could help him treat Wenceslas' brother Sigismund.

## Zavish of Garbow

This article is about the character. For the Codex entry, see Codex entry: Zavish the Black of Garbow.

Zavish of Garbow is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. His arms are a black eagle spread with three rounded crosses on a split field.

## Biography

Sir Zavish of Garbow was a knight in the service of Sigismund in the Kuttenberg region. At some point he won the armour and horse of another knight called Jezhek of Holohlavy in a duel following a dispute where Jezhek tried to stop Zavish from razing a village.

His tent in Sigismund's camp was located near the field chapel, demarcated by the placement of his shield.

Henry may have duelled him to recover the belongings of Sir Jezhek or else he may have stolen them. If duelled, Zavish would fight with polearm, shield and one-handed, and longsword. After the duel, he would concede to Henry and allow him to return Jezhek's belongings to their original owner.

## Zhelejov

Zhelejov is a small village in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

Unlike most other villages, this one does not have an option to rent a place to rest.

The residents here have a constant feud with Tachov owing to both villages claiming a pasture they share belongs to their respective village. In reality, the pasture was split evenly between the two villages but the marker for this was forgotten.

## Codex entry

There are only a few mentions of Zhelejov. Notably, in 1558, the three sons of Lord Semine sold the fortress and the village to the 'Skalské panství'. The fortress was abandoned during the wars with the Swedes.

## Zich of Kaplitz

Zich of Kaplitz is a minor character in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. He can be randomly encountered at Camp by the road locations.

## Biography

Zich of Kaplitz is a burgrave serving under Sir Jiska of Dollein. Kaplitz and his men are pursuing a band of horse thieves who stole several horses from Sir Jiska's stables, and that pursuit has led them into the area around Kuttenberg. Zich has little patience for politics and supports neither Sigismund or Wenceslas, stating that his lord is still in debt from the previous war with little to show for it. He is happy to meet Henry, however, and notes that men in service such as them should enjoy each other's company when time and the war allows. To that end, he will offer to spar with Henry as the waiting makes him bored.

## Zinek

Zinek is a hired hand that works for Kreyzl in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

When he was a child, Zinek used to help stir lye at a tannery and then worked at a dyehouse. However, realizing he didn't want to work six days a week soaking his hands in lye, he set off to find another way to earn a living. When he later found his way to Lower Semine Mill though, he turned to less reputable work, but for him, as long as it got him money, he didn't care.

If you turn him in to the Troskowitz bailiff:

Bonnie, Zinek and Miller Kreyzl end up being executed by hanging. Bailiff decides to leave them swinging from the rafters in their own Lair.

### Associated Quests

- Materia Prima

- Opus Magnum

## Zlata (Vostatek's wife)

Zlata is Vostatek's wife and the mother of Vitek in Kingdom Come: Deliverance II.

## Biography

Zlata lived with her family in a cabin that was assigned to von Bergow's chosen huntsman, as her husband bears that honour. She tried to keep peace between her husband and son who often quarrelled on account of the former's near constant state of drunkenness.

### Associated quests

- Lackey

- Wedding Crashers
